### The best family's gap in ρ on odor-odor distances, read by what could close it {#gap-parts}

**The question was whether ρ on odor-odor distances can still be raised with neither the mean APL effect nor any other measure of the match getting worse, and which constraint would have to be relaxed if it cannot.** The decomposition above read the reference model. This subsection reads the best family of the later fits.

**Under those constraints the room is a few hundredths, and the gap is not APL's to close.** The family's gap is one gap in both conditions. It lies in the distances that the two conditions share, those distances follow the ORN input, and the largest single part of it is on the pairs of paa and B-myr. What would have to be relaxed is the input, or whatever sets an odor's distance from all the others before the KCs. Neither the realism bands nor the main target stands in the way.

**What was read.** The experiment, the gap in ρ on odor-odor distances read by what could close it, takes the breadth-2 APL-effect fit on the real wiring and on seven re-drawn ones, each at its own fit ([the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population)). The family is read as the mean matrix over its eight wirings, on raw spike counts. No model was changed and no simulation was run, so that neither ρ and no part of [the APL-effect loss](#apl-effect) moves. For every saved model the two ρ's on odor-odor distances were written beside its APL-effect statistics.

**The readings are bounds, not models.** For the family each ρ was computed again with the flies' values in the place of one part of its matrices at a time. Such a reading bounds what a change of one kind could gain. No mechanism puts the flies' values in one part and leaves the rest.

![The best family's two ρ's on odor-odor distances (APL on against the control flies, blue circles; APL off against APL output blocked (TNT), orange squares) and what they would be with the flies' values in one part of its matrices, beside the KC data's own yardsticks and the input. Marker: the flies' values read raw, or the family as the mean matrix over its eight wirings; line: the range over the readings at the family's scale, or over the eight wirings. 120 pairs unless stated.](results/E106_rho_gap_parts/E106_gap_readings.png)

**How the flies' values are put in.** Read raw, the flies' numbers go in as they are. The family's distances are spread differently from the flies', so that each reading is also made at the family's scale, in up to three ways: the part that is put in is rescaled to the spread of the part it replaces, the flies' matrix is first mapped onto the family's distribution of distances, or the part is multiplied by the factor that gives the largest ρ. A range in the table is over these.

ρ on odor-odor distances over the 120 pairs unless a row names fewer, on raw spike counts, with APL on against the control flies and with APL off against APL output blocked (TNT): the KC data's own yardsticks, the input, the best family, and the family with the flies' values in one part of its matrices. **Among the saved models the room is a few hundredths.** Of {{E106/archive_summary.csv:scope=all;subset=all120:n ~ .0f}} distinct saved models, {{E106/archive_summary.csv:scope=inside the bands;subset=all120:n ~ .0f}} are inside the realism bands. None of those exceeds {{E106/archive_summary.csv:scope=inside the bands;subset=all120:max_on ~ .2f}} with APL on or {{E106/archive_summary.csv:scope=inside the bands;subset=all120:max_off ~ .2f}} with APL off, and the two maxima are different models, each on a single wiring. The family's best wirings reach {{E106/conditions.csv:family=family;reading=M1;subset=all120:rho_on ~ .2f}} with APL on and {{E106/conditions.csv:family=family;reading=P2;subset=all120:rho_off ~ .2f}} with APL off, one at a time, and the number of saved models at or above both values together is {{E106/archive_summary.csv:scope=all;subset=all120:n_both_070_077 ~ .0f}}. Between its eight wirings a ρ of the family has a standard deviation of {{data:family_rho_on_sd_wirings_120 ~ .3f}} / {{data:family_rho_off_sd_wirings_120 ~ .3f}}.

**Relaxing the realism bands buys nothing with APL on, and one flagged model with APL off.** Outside the bands the largest ρ on odor-odor distances with APL on is lower ({{E106/archive_summary.csv:scope=outside the bands;subset=all120:max_on ~ .2f}}). With APL off one model outside them is higher, at {{E106/archive_summary.csv:scope=all;subset=all120:max_off ~ .2f}}: the lab's profiles of four weak odors scaled to Hallem's level ([below](#hallem-input)). It has lost the per-odor response-rate pattern (response rate ρ with APL on {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E38_hallem_input;tag=A_lab_scaled:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}}, outside the band on it), and its ρ on odor-odor distances with APL on is {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E38_hallem_input;tag=A_lab_scaled:spike_counts_cosine__dist_rho_on_all120 ~ .2f}}.

**Across the saved models a higher ρ on odor-odor distances has gone with a lower APL-effect loss.** Inside the bands the rank correlation between a model's ρ on odor-odor distances and its APL-effect loss is {{E106/tradeoff.csv:scope=inside the bands;condition=on;subset=all120;against=apl_effect_loss:rank_corr ~ .2f}} with APL on and {{E106/tradeoff.csv:scope=inside the bands;condition=off;subset=all120;against=apl_effect_loss:rank_corr ~ .2f}} with APL off. That is across experiments, where better models are better on most measures at once.

**Within one kind of change the two have traded.** The inputs searched for the pattern part of the main target ([the input side of the error common to all wirings](#input-side) and its two successors) were read on the four wirings held out of their searches. At 0.6 of their size they change ρ on odor-odor distances with APL on by {{E106/probes.csv:probe=searched_on_min;reading=main reading:script_value ~ +.3f}} to {{E106/probes.csv:probe=searched_on_max;reading=main reading:script_value ~ +.3f}}, and at full size by as much as {{E106/probes.csv:probe=searched_on_min;reading=all searched inputs, size 1 included:script_value ~ +.3f}}. The one with the lowest pattern part there on raw counts ({{E106/searched_inputs.csv:change=A2_halfA_s0.6;wiring=population:pattern ~ .3f}}, against {{E106/searched_inputs.csv:change=A2_halfA_s0.6;wiring=population:base_pattern ~ .3f}} with the lab's input) changes the two ρ's by {{E106/searched_inputs.csv:change=A2_halfA_s0.6;wiring=population:change_on_120 ~ +.3f}} / {{E106/searched_inputs.csv:change=A2_halfA_s0.6;wiring=population:change_off_120 ~ +.3f}}.

**One gap, in the distances that the two conditions share.** A matrix with APL on is the matrix with APL off plus the per-pair APL effect, so each ρ can be computed again with one of the two taken from the flies. With only its error in the APL effect left, the family would have {{E106/conditions.csv:family=family;reading=population;subset=all120:on_from_flies_off_model_effect ~ .2f}} / {{E106/conditions.csv:family=family;reading=population;subset=all120:off_from_flies_on_model_effect ~ .2f}}; with only its error in the distances of the other condition, {{E106/conditions.csv:family=family;reading=population;subset=all120:on_from_model_off_flies_effect ~ .2f}} / {{E106/conditions.csv:family=family;reading=population;subset=all120:off_from_model_on_flies_effect ~ .2f}}. With APL on the second is below the family as it is ({{E106/conditions.csv:family=family;reading=population;subset=all120:rho_on ~ .2f}}): there the family's two errors partly cancel.

**Both conditions carry the same error.** The rank residuals of the two conditions agree at ρ={{E106/conditions.csv:family=family;reading=population;subset=all120:resid_on_vs_off ~ .2f}}. The family's two matrices agree at ρ={{E106/conditions.csv:family=family;reading=population;subset=all120:model_on_vs_model_off ~ .2f}} on odor-odor distances, where the flies' two agree at {{data:rho_ctrl_tnt ~ .2f}}. A mechanism that changes only how APL acts on the pairs therefore has little room on the two ρ's.

**The gap follows the input.** The family's matrices follow the ORN matrix at ρ={{E106/input_follow.csv:input=orn_pearson;family=family;condition=on:family_vs_input ~ .2f}} / {{E106/input_follow.csv:input=orn_pearson;family=family;condition=off:family_vs_input ~ .2f}} on odor-odor distances, where the flies' follow it at {{data:rho_ctrl_orn ~ .2f}} / {{data:rho_tnt_orn ~ .2f}}. Its rank residuals follow the ORN input's own at ρ={{E106/input_follow.csv:input=orn_pearson;family=family;condition=on:resid_family_vs_input ~ .2f}} / {{E106/input_follow.csv:input=orn_pearson;family=family;condition=off:resid_family_vs_input ~ .2f}}: the family's errors are mostly its input's.

**What the KC stage adds depends on how the input is read.** Over the ORN input as this page reads it, a Pearson correlation distance, the family adds {{E106/input.csv:input=orn_pearson;subset=all120:family_gain_on ~ +.2f}} / {{E106/input.csv:input=orn_pearson;subset=all120:family_gain_off ~ +.2f}}: {{E106/input.csv:input=orn_pearson;subset=v2odors54:family_gain_on ~ +.2f}} / {{E106/input.csv:input=orn_pearson;subset=v2odors54:family_gain_off ~ +.2f}} on the 54 pairs with paa, -aPine, euc or B-myr and {{E106/input.csv:input=orn_pearson;subset=megamat66:family_gain_on ~ +.2f}} / {{E106/input.csv:input=orn_pearson;subset=megamat66:family_gain_off ~ +.2f}} on the 66 pairs among the megamat odors. Read as cosine distance, the measure of the KC matrices, the model's own input already reaches {{E106/input.csv:input=input_cosine;subset=all120:rho_on ~ .2f}} / {{E106/input.csv:input=input_cosine;subset=all120:rho_off ~ .2f}}, and the family adds nothing to it ({{E106/input.csv:input=input_cosine;subset=all120:family_gain_on ~ +.2f}} / {{E106/input.csv:input=input_cosine;subset=all120:family_gain_off ~ +.2f}}).

**paa and B-myr carry the largest part.** Without the 29 pairs of the two odors the family has {{E106/odors.csv:family=family;condition=on;odors=paa and B-myr:rho_without ~ .2f}} / {{E106/odors.csv:family=family;condition=off;odors=paa and B-myr:rho_without ~ .2f}} on the other 91 pairs, and the ORN input alone {{E106/odors.csv:family=family;condition=on;odors=paa and B-myr:rho_without_orn ~ .2f}} / {{E106/odors.csv:family=family;condition=off;odors=paa and B-myr:rho_without_orn ~ .2f}}. The gain is not one recording's. Against random halves of the recordings it is {{E106/probes.csv:probe=gain91_halves_min;reading=main reading:script_value ~ +.2f}} to {{E106/probes.csv:probe=gain91_halves_max;reading=main reading:script_value ~ +.2f}} (the 5th to the 95th percentile over halves and conditions), and it is positive against every single recording, all {{E106/probes.csv:probe=gain91_recordings_positive;reading=main reading:script_value ~ .0f}} of them.

**With those pairs at the flies' values the family gains about as much.** With the two odors' pairs at the flies' values and nothing else changed, it would have {{E106/odors.csv:family=family;condition=on;odors=paa and B-myr:at_data_raw ~ .2f}} / {{E106/odors.csv:family=family;condition=off;odors=paa and B-myr:at_data_raw ~ .2f}} read raw and {{E106/odors.csv:family=family;condition=on;odors=paa and B-myr:at_data_quantile ~ .2f}} / {{E106/odors.csv:family=family;condition=off;odors=paa and B-myr:at_data_quantile ~ .2f}} at its own scale. Every reading on paa's pairs rests on ORN input recorded a decade below the flies' concentration ([footnote](#fn-concentrations)); B-myr's input is at the flies' concentration.

**Single odors, as leads.** A single odor's share of the gap is not checked on halves of the recordings and is a lead only. Each pair counts for both its odors, so that the shares add to two and an even share is an eighth. paa carries {{E106/residuals_odors.csv:family=family;condition=on;odor=paa:share_of_gap ~ .2f}} / {{E106/residuals_odors.csv:family=family;condition=off;odor=paa:share_of_gap ~ .2f}} and B-myr {{E106/residuals_odors.csv:family=family;condition=on;odor=B-myr:share_of_gap ~ .2f}} / {{E106/residuals_odors.csv:family=family;condition=off;odor=B-myr:share_of_gap ~ .2f}}, and their shares of the ORN input's own gap are close ({{E106/residuals_odors.csv:family=family;condition=on;odor=paa:share_of_gap_orn ~ .2f}} / {{E106/residuals_odors.csv:family=family;condition=off;odor=paa:share_of_gap_orn ~ .2f}} and {{E106/residuals_odors.csv:family=family;condition=on;odor=B-myr:share_of_gap_orn ~ .2f}} / {{E106/residuals_odors.csv:family=family;condition=off;odor=B-myr:share_of_gap_orn ~ .2f}}). 2-but, the third carrier in the reference model, is at or below an even share in the family ({{E106/residuals_odors.csv:family=family;condition=on;odor=2-but:share_of_gap ~ .2f}} / {{E106/residuals_odors.csv:family=family;condition=off;odor=2-but:share_of_gap ~ .2f}}).

**The odor part and the pair part.** A matrix over the 120 pairs can be split by least squares into an odor part, one value per odor added for the two odors of a pair, and a pair part, the rest. The odor part says how far an odor is from all the others, and the pair part holds what is particular to a pair.

![Left: the share of each matrix's variance over the 120 pairs that its odor part carries, for the KC data, the family (range over its eight wirings) and the input read two ways. Right: each odor's share of the family's gap in ρ on odor-odor distances, APL on against the control flies and APL off against APL output blocked (TNT); the shares add to two, so that an even share is an eighth. Single odors' shares are leads.](results/E106_rho_gap_parts/E106_odor_parts.png)

**The family's matrices are too much a value per odor.** In the family the odor part carries {{E106/odor_pair_parts.csv:family=family;reading=population;condition=on:model_odor_r2 ~ .0%}} / {{E106/odor_pair_parts.csv:family=family;reading=population;condition=off:model_odor_r2 ~ .0%}} of the variance over the pairs, against {{E106/odor_pair_parts.csv:family=family;reading=population;condition=on:data_odor_r2 ~ .0%}} / {{E106/odor_pair_parts.csv:family=family;reading=population;condition=off:data_odor_r2 ~ .0%}} in the flies, and its spread is about twice the flies' ({{E106/odor_pair_parts.csv:family=family;reading=population;condition=on:model_odor_sd ~ .3f}} / {{E106/odor_pair_parts.csv:family=family;reading=population;condition=off:model_odor_sd ~ .3f}} against {{E106/odor_pair_parts.csv:family=family;reading=population;condition=on:data_odor_sd ~ .3f}} / {{E106/odor_pair_parts.csv:family=family;reading=population;condition=off:data_odor_sd ~ .3f}}, in units of distance). The ORN input has the same excess ({{E106/input_parts.csv:input=orn_pearson;condition=on:model_odor_r2 ~ .0%}} of its variance). The order of the odors is not what is off: the two sides' values per odor agree at ρ={{E106/odor_pair_parts.csv:family=family;reading=population;condition=on:odor_shares_rho ~ .2f}} / {{E106/odor_pair_parts.csv:family=family;reading=population;condition=off:odor_shares_rho ~ .2f}}.

**A change that acts per odor is worth about twice what had been estimated.** With the flies' odor part in the place of its own the family gains {{E106/probes.csv:probe=per_odor_worth_on;reading=main reading:script_value ~ +.2f}} / {{E106/probes.csv:probe=per_odor_worth_off;reading=main reading:script_value ~ +.2f}} read raw: an odor part of half the spread barely moves the family's ranks. At the family's scale it gains {{E106/probes.csv:probe=per_odor_worth_on;reading=matched:script_value ~ +.2f}} to {{E106/probes.csv:probe=per_odor_worth_on;reading=quantile:script_value ~ +.2f}} / {{E106/probes.csv:probe=per_odor_worth_off;reading=quantile:script_value ~ +.2f}} to {{E106/probes.csv:probe=per_odor_worth_off;reading=best:script_value ~ +.2f}}, and the best 16 values per odor, fitted to the same data, give {{E106/probes.csv:probe=per_odor_worth_on;reading=optimal:script_value ~ +.2f}} / {{E106/probes.csv:probe=per_odor_worth_off;reading=optimal:script_value ~ +.2f}}. An estimate made when this reading was planned had put such a change at {{E106/probes.csv:probe=per_odor_worth_on;reading=main reading:probe_value ~ +.2f}} / {{E106/probes.csv:probe=per_odor_worth_off;reading=main reading:probe_value ~ +.2f}} at most. It did not hold.

**The pair part carries the larger error.** With the flies' pair part in the place of its own the family would have {{E106/odor_pair_parts.csv:family=family;reading=population;condition=on:model_odor_flies_pair ~ .2f}} / {{E106/odor_pair_parts.csv:family=family;reading=population;condition=off:model_odor_flies_pair ~ .2f}} read raw, and up to {{E106/odor_pair_parts.csv:family=family;reading=population;condition=on:model_odor_flies_pair_best ~ .2f}} / {{E106/odor_pair_parts.csv:family=family;reading=population;condition=off:model_odor_flies_pair_best ~ .2f}} at its own scale, near the measurement ceiling with APL off (table).

**The other estimates made at planning held, three of them in one reading only.** The largest ρ on odor-odor distances with APL off holds inside the realism bands and not outside them. The cost of the searched inputs holds at 0.6 of their size and not at full size. The pairs of paa and B-myr at the flies' values hold at the family's scale and not read raw. The two experiments that rest on these estimates are read against the values given here (one in [the next subsection](#validation2-panel), the other in [the one after it](#paa-concentration)).

**Two changes per odor that have been run are not that handle (leads).**

- On the base with the flies' recruitment, an [oracle](#fn-oracle) in which every odor's response rates are set to the flies' ([the breadth weighting inside the models' APL](#breadth-weighting)), the family's ρ on odor-odor distances with APL on differs from that of its fits by {{diff:apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E89_apl_breadth_weighting;tag=C2_F_k2_P1:spike_counts_cosine__dist_rho_on_all120 -- E106/conditions.csv:family=family;reading=P1;subset=all120:rho_on ~ +.2f}} to {{diff:apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E89_apl_breadth_weighting;tag=C2_F_k2_P2:spike_counts_cosine__dist_rho_on_all120 -- E106/conditions.csv:family=family;reading=P2;subset=all120:rho_on ~ +.2f}} on the four wirings it was run on, and that with APL off by a hundredth at most.
- [The antennal lobe's normalization](#al-normalization) at fixed scales lowers ρ on odor-odor distances with APL on, on each of the eight wirings at the step that the flies' APL picks (on the real wiring from {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E102_antennal_lobe_normalization;tag=B_identity_real_held:spike_counts_cosine__dist_rho_on_all120 ~ .2f}} to {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E102_antennal_lobe_normalization;tag=B_inhadd1000_real_held:spike_counts_cosine__dist_rho_on_all120 ~ .2f}}).

**On the megamat pairs the family adds nothing to its input.** On the 66 pairs among the megamat odors the family has {{E106/conditions.csv:family=family;reading=population;subset=megamat66:rho_on ~ .2f}} / {{E106/conditions.csv:family=family;reading=population;subset=megamat66:rho_off ~ .2f}} and the ORN input alone {{E106/input.csv:input=orn_pearson;subset=megamat66:rho_on ~ .2f}} / {{E106/input.csv:input=orn_pearson;subset=megamat66:rho_off ~ .2f}}. [Remy's wild-type KC somata](#fn-yang-remy), a second set of flies, have {{data:rho_ctrl_remy_soma ~ .2f}} / {{data:rho_tnt_remy_soma ~ .2f}} against the same two KC matrices.

**No saved model is a lead for a mechanism there.** A saved model three hundredths or more above its input on the megamat pairs in both ρ's would have been one. There is none: even against the ORN input read as Pearson correlation distance alone, the number of saved models that far above it is {{E106/archive_summary.csv:scope=all;subset=megamat66:n_above_orn_both_003 ~ .0f}}.

**The yardsticks for "not worse".** The reading also fixes the scales by which a later change counts as a gain or as not worse. A change read on the same eight wirings is set against the spread of a near-null change over those wirings, {{data:paired_rho_off_sd_e102_weakest_step ~ .3f}} to {{data:paired_rho_off_sd_e93_fuller_input ~ .3f}} per wiring. A comparison between families is set against the spread of a ρ over wirings (above). A claim about the flies is set against resampling the recordings (a standard deviation of {{data:family_rho_on_boot_sd_120 ~ .3f}} / {{data:family_rho_off_boot_sd_120 ~ .3f}}) and against two halves of them, between which the family's ρ differs by {{data:family_rho_on_split_diff_120 ~ .3f}} / {{data:family_rho_off_split_diff_120 ~ .3f}} on average.

**Which ORN flies feed the model matters little, and the gap is not the recordings' noise.** Two populations of model flies whose inputs come from disjoint ORN flies ([the ORN input as a population of flies](#input-population)) agree at ρ={{data:e85_population_agreement_on_66 ~ .2f}} / {{data:e85_population_agreement_off_66 ~ .2f}} on odor-odor distances over the megamat pairs. Against the flies' distances with the trial noise removed the family has {{E106/robustness.csv:target=noise-free (E81);reading=family;subset=all120:rho_on ~ .2f}} / {{E106/robustness.csv:target=noise-free (E81);reading=family;subset=all120:rho_off ~ .2f}}. Against the six recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) that are alike it has {{E106/robustness.csv:target=six typical TNT recordings (E76);reading=family;subset=all120:rho_off ~ .2f}} with APL off, and the ORN input falls as far (to {{E106/robustness.csv:target=six typical TNT recordings (E76);reading=ORN input;subset=all120:rho_off ~ .2f}}).

**Limits.** Everything is on raw spike counts, with no calibrated readout, and the twelve fits read are all inside the realism bands. The correlations over the saved models are across experiments, on mostly single wirings. The readings on the 54 pairs include euc and -aPine, whose ORN input was recorded within a log unit of the flies' concentration and not at it ([footnote](#fn-concentrations)). Saved runs whose wirings were built from the connectome tables on hold are left out of every table ([footnote](#fn-derived-tables)).

**What this leaves.** A mechanism on APL's side has little room on the two ρ's, and no saved model orders the megamat pairs better than its input by a margin that would make it a lead. What is left to relax is the input: the ORN recordings of paa and B-myr, or whatever sets how far an odor is from all the others before the KCs. Neither the odors' response rates nor the antennal lobe's normalization as run supplies the second.

The first has since been read on Remy's KC recordings of the validation2 panel ([the next subsection](#validation2-panel)). paa's concentration, which this reading had named first, is not the reason for the gap at paa and B-myr: wild-type flies hold the two apart at the concentration of the ORN input, and the ORN input itself holds them close. paa's input has since been moved to the flies' concentration by extrapolation as well, and ρ on odor-odor distances does not rise by what the test asked ([paa's input at the flies' concentration](#paa-concentration)).

### The four validation2 odors in the panel their ORN input was recorded in: where the gap at paa and B-myr is made {#validation2-panel}

**The question was which of four things makes the gap at paa and B-myr.** In the panel of the main target the best family holds paa and B-myr at a cosine distance of {{E107/a_verdict_pair.csv:reading=cosine on spike counts:distance ~ .2f}} with APL on, where the control flies hold them at {{E107/a_verdict_pair.csv:source=control flies (Yang):distance ~ .2f}}, and the pairs of the two odors carry the largest part of the family's gap in ρ on odor-odor distances ([the subsection before this one](#gap-parts)). Four explanations of that gap were open:

- **paa's concentration:** the KCs of the main target got paa at 10^-3 and its ORN input was recorded at 10^-4 ([footnote](#fn-concentrations)), so that the family could be right at the lower concentration.
- **The family's KC stage:** the model's KCs collapse two odors that share their strongest glomerulus, where the flies' KCs do not.
- **The input before the KCs:** the ORN recordings of these odors, or what the flies make of them before the KCs, are not what the model is given.
- **The joining of two ORN sessions:** the ORN input of paa, B-myr, euc and -aPine comes from other flies than that of the megamat odors, and the gap belongs to setting the two sessions side by side.

**The first is excluded, the second has no support, and the result points at the input.** Wild-type flies shown paa at the concentration of its ORN input hold paa and B-myr apart, so that paa's concentration is not the reason. The ORN input itself has the two among its closest pairs and the family follows its input, so that the collapse is not made at the family's KC stage. Between the last two explanations the answer depends on how the pairs are read, and the reading fixed beforehand to carry the verdict gives the input before the KCs.

**What was read.** The experiment, the four validation2 odors in the panel their ORN input was recorded in, reads Remy's KC soma recordings of the validation2 panel, made in {{E107/a_ceilings.csv:panel=validation2;metric=cosine;set=136;subset=all:n_flies ~ .0f}} wild-type flies. It is the one panel in which the ORN input and the KC responses of the four odors were both recorded, with paa at 10^-4 and B-myr at 10^-2 as in that input. These recordings had not been read for this work before.

**The model's side.** The best family was run at fixed parameters on the validation2 ORN input, {{E107/c_realism.csv:panel=validation2;reading=fitted;member=mean of 8:n_odors ~ .0f}} odors recorded in one session: its eight wirings at their own fits ([the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population)), as fitted and with the response rate with APL on held at the control flies'. It is read as the mean matrix over the wirings, on raw spike counts. No model was changed. Her flies are wild type, so that only APL on is read, and no part of [the APL-effect loss](#apl-effect) moves.

**The yardstick within one panel is the megamat level.** The same runs were made on the megamat ORN input and set against [Remy's megamat KC somata](#fn-yang-remy). The megamat level of the ORN input alone, or of the family, is its ρ on odor-odor distances with those somata over all pairs of the megamat panel. Either of the two is said to order a set of pairs of the validation2 panel if its ρ on odor-odor distances over them is no more than {{lit:0.05 # results/E107_validation2_panel/verdict.json, rules.order_tol: the allowance below a reader's megamat level within which it counts as ordering a set of pairs, fixed before any of the distances was opened}} below its megamat level.

**The outcomes were fixed before any of her distances was opened.** A lock was first written from her lists of files and of stimuli alone, with the measure of the verdict (a cosine distance, as in the matrices of the main target) and its thresholds. The reading that carries the verdict takes her mean table, the {{E107/a_rhos.csv:panel=validation2;reader=orn;remy=table_cos;set=136;subset=all:n_pairs ~ .0f}} pairs that her manuscript reports, of the panel's {{E107/a_rhos.csv:panel=validation2;reader=orn;remy=table_cos;set=231;subset=all:n_pairs ~ .0f}}, and the family as fitted. Six partner readings change one thing each.

| explanation of the gap | what it needed | what was found |
|---|---|---|
| paa's concentration | paa and B-myr no more than {{lit:0.70 # results/E107_validation2_panel/verdict.json, rules.close: the cosine distance of paa from B-myr at or below which the two count as close, fixed before any of the distances was opened}} apart in her flies, as in the family | excluded on every reading |
| the family's KC stage | the two at least {{lit:0.85 # results/E107_validation2_panel/verdict.json, rules.apart: the cosine distance of paa from B-myr at or above which the two count as apart, fixed before any of the distances was opened}} apart; the ORN input alone orders the pairs of paa and B-myr, and the family does not | on no reading |
| the input before the KCs | the two apart; neither the ORN input alone nor the family orders those pairs | on the carrying reading and on {{lit:four # results/E107_validation2_panel/verdict.json, core.partners: the partner readings whose class is c, the carrying class (held, megamat66, fly_mean and orn_cosine)}} of its {{lit:six # results/E107_validation2_panel/verdict.json, core.partners: the partner readings (held, other_set, megamat66, fly_mean, correlation and orn_cosine)}} partners |
| the joining of two ORN sessions | the family orders the panel as it orders the megamat panel, those pairs included | on {{lit:two # results/E107_validation2_panel/verdict.json, partners_differing: the partner readings whose class is d (other_set, the 231 pairs, and correlation)}} partners, by small margins |

**Her flies hold paa and B-myr apart at the concentration of the ORN input.** The two are {{E107/a_verdict_pair.csv:reading=table_cos:distance ~ .2f}} apart as cosine distance and {{E107/a_verdict_pair.csv:reading=table_corr:distance ~ .2f}} as correlation distance (one minus the Pearson correlation across KCs), in the {{E107/c_pb_pairs.csv:odor_a=paa;odor_b=B-myr:n_flies ~ .0f}} flies that have both odors. Every reading is above the threshold for apart, and the first explanation is excluded.

The distance of paa from B-myr, and the pair's rank: the fraction of the pairs of its panel that are no further apart than this pair, among the pairs that the manuscript reports for Remy's flies and for the ORN input, and among the 120 pairs for the panel of the main target

| source | distance of paa from B-myr | rank: fraction of the pairs no further apart |
|---|---:|---:|
| KCs, Remy's wild-type flies, the validation2 panel: cosine distance | {{E107/a_verdict_pair.csv:reading=table_cos:distance ~ .2f}} | {{E107/a_verdict_pair.csv:reading=table_cos:pct_rank_136 ~ .2f}} |
| the same flies: correlation distance | {{E107/a_verdict_pair.csv:reading=table_corr:distance ~ .2f}} | {{E107/a_verdict_pair.csv:reading=table_corr:pct_rank_136 ~ .2f}} |
| ORNs, the validation2 input: Pearson correlation distance | {{E107/a_verdict_pair.csv:reading=pearson:distance ~ .2f}} | {{E107/a_verdict_pair.csv:reading=pearson:pct_rank_136 ~ .2f}} |
| ORNs, the validation2 input: cosine distance | {{E107/a_verdict_pair.csv:source=ORN input (validation2, 36 glomeruli);reading=cosine:distance ~ .2f}} | {{E107/a_verdict_pair.csv:source=ORN input (validation2, 36 glomeruli);reading=cosine:pct_rank_136 ~ .2f}} |
| the best family on the validation2 input, APL on: as fitted / response rate held | {{E107/c_pb_pairs.csv:odor_a=paa;odor_b=B-myr:family_fitted ~ .2f}} / {{E107/c_pb_pairs.csv:odor_a=paa;odor_b=B-myr:family_held ~ .2f}} | — |
| KCs, control flies, the panel of the main target: cosine distance | {{E107/a_verdict_pair.csv:source=control flies (Yang):distance ~ .2f}} | {{E107/a_verdict_pair.csv:source=control flies (Yang):pct_rank_120 ~ .2f}} |

| the best family in the panel of the main target, APL on | {{E107/a_verdict_pair.csv:reading=cosine on spike counts:distance ~ .2f}} | {{E107/a_verdict_pair.csv:reading=cosine on spike counts:pct_rank_120 ~ .2f}} |

**The two sets of flies differ in level, so that the order is read as well.** On the {{E107/a_rhos.csv:panel=megamat;reader=orn;remy=flymean_cos;set=66;subset=all:n_pairs ~ .0f}} megamat pairs that both hold, Remy's megamat somata sit {{lit:0.11 # results/E107_validation2_panel/verdict.json, level_check: Remy's megamat somata average 0.699 and the control flies of the main target 0.809 as cosine distance over the 66 megamat pairs that both hold (difference -0.110, beyond the tolerance of 0.05 fixed beforehand)}} lower than the control flies as cosine distance, more than the tolerance fixed beforehand, and the two agree at ρ={{E107/a_rhos.csv:panel=megamat;reader=yang_control;remy=flymean_cos;set=66;subset=all:rho ~ .2f}} on odor-odor distances. By rank the pair is in the middle of her pairs and in the upper part of the control flies', and near the bottom of the ORN input's and of the family's (table). Both sets of flies put the pair well above where the input puts it.

**The ORN input already holds them close, and the family follows it.** Within one ORN session and at matched concentrations, the ORN input has paa and B-myr among its closest pairs. The family on that input holds them {{E107/c_pb_pairs.csv:odor_a=paa;odor_b=B-myr:family_fitted ~ .2f}} apart, as it does in the panel of the main target. On no reading does the ORN input alone order the two odors' pairs where the family fails to (the table of readings below), so that nothing supports a collapse made at the family's KC stage.

**Within the validation2 panel the family adds nothing to its input.** Over the pairs that the manuscript reports the family has ρ={{E107/c_rhos.csv:panel=validation2;reader=family;reading=fitted;member=pop;remy=table_cos;set=136;subset=all:rho ~ .3f}} on odor-odor distances with her flies and the ORN input alone {{E107/a_rhos.csv:panel=validation2;reader=orn;remy=table_cos;set=136;subset=all:rho ~ .3f}}, against a measurement ceiling of {{E107/a_ceilings.csv:panel=validation2;metric=cosine;set=136;subset=all:ceiling ~ .3f}} from halves of her flies. Holding the response rate moves the family's value by {{diff:E107/c_rhos.csv:panel=validation2;reader=family;reading=held;member=pop;remy=table_cos;set=136;subset=all:rho -- E107/c_rhos.csv:panel=validation2;reader=family;reading=fitted;member=pop;remy=table_cos;set=136;subset=all:rho ~ +.3f}} (table).

**Single wirings split the same way.** On the carrying reading, as fitted, {{lit:five # results/E107_validation2_panel/verdict.json, core.n_wirings_same_class: the wirings of the eight whose class on the carrying reading, as fitted, is the carrying class c (real, P1, P2, M1 and P4)}} of the eight wirings give the input before the KCs and {{lit:three # results/E107_validation2_panel/verdict.json, core.per_wiring: the wirings whose class on the carrying reading, as fitted, is d (P3, M2 and M3)}} give the joining of two sessions.

**Single odors, as leads.** paa carries the largest share of the gap in the validation2 panel as well: {{E107/c_shares.csv:reader=orn;reading=-;panel=validation2;odor=paa:share_of_gap ~ .2f}} of the ORN input's and {{E107/c_shares.csv:reader=family;reading=fitted;panel=validation2;odor=paa:share_of_gap ~ .2f}} of the family's, where each pair counts for both its odors. Without paa's pairs ρ on odor-odor distances rises by {{E107/c_shares.csv:reader=orn;reading=-;panel=validation2;odor=paa:loo_delta ~ .2f}} for the ORN input alone and by {{E107/c_shares.csv:reader=family;reading=fitted;panel=validation2;odor=paa:loo_delta ~ .2f}} for the family. These shares rest on one set of flies and no held-out check, and are leads.

**euc and -aPine by concentration (a lead).** {{E107/a_by_concentration.csv:odor=euc;conc=-2;metric=cosine:n_flies ~ .0f}} of her {{E107/a_by_concentration.csv:odor=euc;conc=pooled;metric=cosine:n_flies ~ .0f}} flies with euc and {{E107/a_by_concentration.csv:odor=-aPine;conc=-2;metric=cosine:n_flies ~ .0f}} of her {{E107/a_by_concentration.csv:odor=-aPine;conc=pooled;metric=cosine:n_flies ~ .0f}} with -aPine had the odor at 10^-2, the concentration of the flies of the main target, within a log unit of the ORN input's ([footnote](#fn-concentrations)). -aPine's pairs follow the ORN input at ρ={{E107/a_by_concentration.csv:odor=-aPine;conc=-1.5;metric=cosine:rho_orn_pearson ~ .2f}} on odor-odor distances at the ORN input's own concentration ({{E107/a_by_concentration.csv:odor=-aPine;conc=-1.5;metric=cosine:n_flies ~ .0f}} flies) and at {{E107/a_by_concentration.csv:odor=-aPine;conc=-2;metric=cosine:rho_orn_pearson ~ .2f}} at 10^-2. The verdict on paa and B-myr does not rest on these two odors.

**The fits carry over to both panels.** No realism band is applied on a panel that the family was not fitted to. As fitted, {{E107/c_realism.csv:panel=validation2;reading=fitted;member=mean of 8:rate_on ~ .3f}} / {{E107/c_realism.csv:panel=validation2;reading=fitted;member=mean of 8:rate_off ~ .3f}} of its KCs respond on the validation2 input with APL on / APL off and {{E107/c_realism.csv:panel=megamat;reading=fitted;member=mean of 8:rate_on ~ .3f}} / {{E107/c_realism.csv:panel=megamat;reading=fitted;member=mean of 8:rate_off ~ .3f}} on the megamat input, against {{data:noise_ctrl_frac ~ .3f}} / {{data:noise_tnt_frac ~ .3f}} in the flies of the main target, counted in baseline-noise units. Remy's files hold distances only, so that her flies' response rates cannot be set beside these.

**The largest spike counts are higher on the validation2 input.** With APL on the largest count of a KC to one odor is {{E107/c_realism.csv:panel=validation2;reading=fitted;member=M2:max_count_on ~ .0f}} to {{E107/c_realism.csv:panel=validation2;reading=fitted;member=P1:max_count_on ~ .0f}} over the eight wirings, against {{E107/c_realism.csv:panel=APL16 (the fit's panel);reading=fitted;member=P2:max_count_on ~ .0f}} to {{E107/c_realism.csv:panel=APL16 (the fit's panel);reading=fitted;member=M3:max_count_on ~ .0f}} in the panel of the main target, to which the family was fitted.

**Limits.**

- Remy's distances rest on her own measure of a response and her own selection of cells, and her flies are wild type and not the control genotype of the main target.
- The choice between the last two explanations rests on margins against a megamat level taken on all pairs of the megamat panel, where the ORN input alone and the family sit lower than on the pairs shared with the panel of the main target. Another yardstick could move the class.
- Only APL on is read. Nothing here bears on the main target or on the matrix with APL output blocked (TNT).

**What this leaves.**

- **paa's concentration does not explain the gap at these two odors.** At the concentration of the ORN input Remy's flies separate paa from B-myr about as the control flies do a decade higher. The experiment that moves paa's input to the flies' concentration has since been classed by its own gate, as no gain ([the next subsection](#paa-concentration)).
- **The collapse is in the input, before the family's KCs.** The family keeps its input's order here as in the panel of the main target, and inherits the collapse. A mechanism at the KC stage for these two odors, such as a requirement of several active claws, is not what the result asks for.
- **What lies between the ORN input and the KCs is open.** The carrying outcome names the ORN recordings of these odors and what the flies make of them before the KCs, in the antennal lobe and at the step from ORNs to PNs. This comparison cannot tell the two apart.
- **The joining of two sessions is not excluded for the other pairs.** paa and B-myr are both odors of the validation2 session, in the panel of the main target as well, so that the joining cannot explain that pair. It could bear on the two odors' pairs with megamat odors.
- **A measurement would separate the last two explanations:** the four odors recorded in the same ORN flies as megamat odors, or a new ORN recording of paa and B-myr (with the open measurement question at the end of the page).
- **A search of the input says what such a recording should test.** The input of paa, B-myr and 2-but was searched and tested on wirings and recordings that the search did not see: both ρ's on odor-odor distances rise there, at a price in the response rate ρ ([below](#input-search-rho)).

### paa's input at the flies' concentration: whether an input extrapolated to the concentration that the KCs got raises ρ on odor-odor distances {#paa-concentration}

**The question was whether the decade between paa's ORN input and the flies' stimulus costs the best family the order of its odor pairs.** paa's ORN input was recorded at 10^-4 and the KCs of the main target got 10^-3, a caveat that every result on this page carries ([footnote](#fn-concentrations)). The experiment, paa's input at the flies' concentration, moves that input to 10^-3 by rules that take nothing from the KC data. It asks whether ρ on odor-odor distances then rises with no other measure of the match getting worse.

**It does not rise by what the test asked, and the response rates pay.** Extrapolated a decade up, paa's input raises ρ on odor-odor distances by less than the test asked with APL on, and with APL off by about that much on too few wirings and not against every half of the recordings. The response rate ρ falls in both conditions. A decade down, both ρ's on odor-odor distances fall on every wiring.

**By the outcomes fixed beforehand, the rule of extrapolation is the limit.** The model's order of the pairs depends on paa's concentration, and no rule that the lab's recordings allow for one more decade raises ρ on odor-odor distances by what the test asked. No extrapolated input is put forward for the model, and an ORN recording of paa at 10^-3 is the measurement to ask for.

**Three rules were fixed before any run.** The lab holds two ORN recordings of paa from one session, at 10^-5 and at 10^-4. The linear rule continues each glomerulus's change from the lower to the higher by one more such step, and the saturating rule lets each glomerulus approach a common ceiling. The fitted rule predicts a response from the responses at the two concentrations below it, with coefficients fitted on the lab's ORN recordings of {{E108/scores.csv:rule=X3:n_odors ~ .0f}} other single odors, each at five concentrations a decade apart.

**The fitted rule carries the verdict.** Scored with each odor's series left out of its fit in turn, it predicts the highest of three adjacent concentrations from the two below it with a root mean squared error of {{E108/scores.csv:rule=X3:rmse ~ .1f}} in the units of the model's input, over {{E108/scores.csv:rule=X3:n_triples ~ .0f}} cases. The linear and the saturating rule have {{E108/scores.csv:rule=X1:rmse ~ .1f}} and {{E108/scores.csv:rule=X2:rmse ~ .1f}}, and no change at all {{E108/scores.csv:rule=none (top = mid):rmse ~ .1f}}. All three rules were run.

**Three kinds of control.** paa at 10^-5 in the place of 10^-4 moves the input the wrong way. The linear rule's changes are moved to other glomeruli, in four permutations. And the lab's paa is scaled to the linear rule's total with its pattern unchanged.

**The reading.** Each input is read in the best family at fixed scales: its eight wirings at their own fits ([the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population)), with both response rates held and nothing fitted again. Each wiring is compared with itself at the lab's input.

**The gate was fixed beforehand.** A gain is a rise of one ρ on odor-odor distances by {{lit:0.010 # GAIN in experiments/E108_paa_extrapolation.py: the rise of one ρ on odor-odor distances that counts as a gain, fixed before any run}} or more for the mean matrix, on at least {{lit:six # GAIN_WIRINGS in experiments/E108_paa_extrapolation.py: the number of the eight wirings on which the rise has to be GAIN or more}} of the eight wirings and against each half of two splits of the recordings. Beside it, the pattern part of [the APL-effect loss](#apl-effect) may not rise by more than {{lit:0.003 # EQUAL_PATTERN in experiments/E108_paa_extrapolation.py: the most that the pattern part may rise, against all recordings and against each half}} nor the response rate ρ fall by more than {{lit:0.05 # RATE_RHO_SLACK in experiments/E108_paa_extrapolation.py: the most that the response rate ρ may fall, as the mean over the eight wirings}}, and every run has to stay inside the realism bands.

The best family with paa's input changed and nothing fitted again: ρ on odor-odor distances on raw spike counts and the APL-effect statistics through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout), for the mean matrix over the eight wirings and against all recordings; the response rates as means over the wirings, with the flies' in baseline-noise units. Here and in the text below, two values joined by a slash are with APL on and with APL off unless a row names them otherwise. No input is chosen by a correlation ([why](#fn-pattern-split))

**No rule gains.** The fitted rule raises ρ on odor-odor distances by {{E108/gate.csv:input=X3;population=all8:d_rho_on_all ~ +.3f}} with APL on, below what a gain needs. With APL off the rise is {{E108/gate.csv:input=X3;population=all8:d_rho_off_all ~ +.3f}}, but it reaches the gate's step on {{E108/gate.csv:input=X3;population=all8:n_wirings_gain_off ~ .0f}} of the eight wirings, and against two of the four halves it is {{E108/gate.csv:input=X3;population=all8:d_rho_off_A ~ +.3f}} and {{E108/gate.csv:input=X3;population=all8:d_rho_off_D ~ +.3f}} only. The linear and the saturating rule change the two ρ's by {{E108/gate.csv:input=X1;population=all8:d_rho_on_all ~ +.3f}} / {{E108/gate.csv:input=X1;population=all8:d_rho_off_all ~ +.3f}} and {{E108/gate.csv:input=X2;population=all8:d_rho_on_all ~ +.3f}} / {{E108/gate.csv:input=X2;population=all8:d_rho_off_all ~ +.3f}}, on no more wirings ({{E108/gate.csv:input=X1;population=all8:n_wirings_gain_on ~ .0f}} / {{E108/gate.csv:input=X1;population=all8:n_wirings_gain_off ~ .0f}} and {{E108/gate.csv:input=X2;population=all8:n_wirings_gain_on ~ .0f}} / {{E108/gate.csv:input=X2;population=all8:n_wirings_gain_off ~ .0f}}).

**The rise is one of the model, and too small for a claim about the flies.** A near-null change read on the same wirings has a spread of {{data:paired_rho_off_sd_e102_weakest_step ~ .3f}} to {{data:paired_rho_off_sd_e93_fuller_input ~ .3f}} per wiring, so that the mean rise with APL off is not noise of the model. It is below {{data:family_rho_off_boot_sd_120 ~ .3f}}, the standard deviation of that ρ over resamples of the recordings. With paa's pairs at the flies' values the family would have {{E106/residuals_odors.csv:family=family;condition=on;odor=paa:at_data_raw ~ .2f}} / {{E106/residuals_odors.csv:family=family;condition=off;odor=paa:at_data_raw ~ .2f}} ([the gap in ρ on odor-odor distances read by what could close it](#gap-parts)), of which the fitted rule covers a small part.

**A decade down, the order is lost.** With paa at 10^-5 the two ρ's on odor-odor distances change by {{E108/gate.csv:input=W5;population=all8:d_rho_on_all ~ +.3f}} / {{E108/gate.csv:input=W5;population=all8:d_rho_off_all ~ +.3f}}, on every wiring and against every half of the recordings. That is more than a ρ of the family differs between its eight wirings, a standard deviation of {{data:family_rho_on_sd_wirings_120 ~ .3f}} / {{data:family_rho_off_sd_wirings_120 ~ .3f}}. The model's order of the pairs therefore depends on paa's concentration; had this control lost nothing, the concentration would have been ruled out as a cause at the KCs.

**What rises with APL off is not the extrapolated pattern's.** The linear rule's changes moved to other glomeruli raise ρ on odor-odor distances with APL off in all four permutations, by {{E108/gate.csv:input=P3;population=all8:d_rho_off_all ~ +.3f}} to {{E108/gate.csv:input=P4;population=all8:d_rho_off_all ~ +.3f}}, and one permutation gains as much as the fitted rule in both conditions (table). The lab's paa scaled up with its pattern unchanged changes the two ρ's by {{E108/gate.csv:input=S1;population=all8:d_rho_on_all ~ +.3f}} / {{E108/gate.csv:input=S1;population=all8:d_rho_off_all ~ +.3f}}. A change of paa's pattern of this size thus helps a little with APL off wherever it falls, and a stronger paa alone does not.

**On paa's own 15 pairs the extrapolations do order better (a lead).** Over those pairs alone, ρ on odor-odor distances rises from {{E108/readings.csv:input=I0;unit=all8;readout=raw:rho15_on_all ~ .2f}} / {{E108/readings.csv:input=I0;unit=all8;readout=raw:rho15_off_all ~ .2f}} with the lab's input to {{E108/readings.csv:input=X3;unit=all8;readout=raw:rho15_on_all ~ .2f}} / {{E108/readings.csv:input=X3;unit=all8;readout=raw:rho15_off_all ~ .2f}} under the fitted rule, on every wiring and against every half; no permuted control raises it by more than {{E108/gate.csv:input=P1;population=all8:d_rho15_on_all ~ +.2f}} / {{E108/gate.csv:input=P4;population=all8:d_rho15_off_all ~ +.2f}}. It is a reading of one odor's pairs, so a lead, and it leaves those pairs far from the flies' order.

**The response rates pay under every changed input.** With the lab's input, paa already has the flies' response fraction in the model: {{E108/readings.csv:input=I0;unit=all8;readout=raw:run_frac_paa_on ~ .3f}} / {{E108/readings.csv:input=I0;unit=all8;readout=raw:run_frac_paa_off ~ .3f}} of the family's KCs respond to it, against {{data:noise_ctrl_frac_paa ~ .3f}} / {{data:noise_tnt_frac_paa ~ .3f}} of the flies' in baseline-noise units. The fitted rule takes it to {{E108/readings.csv:input=X3;unit=all8;readout=raw:run_frac_paa_on ~ .3f}} / {{E108/readings.csv:input=X3;unit=all8;readout=raw:run_frac_paa_off ~ .3f}}, away from the flies. The response rate ρ changes by {{E108/gate.csv:input=X3;population=all8:d_rate_rho_on ~ +.3f}} / {{E108/gate.csv:input=X3;population=all8:d_rate_rho_off ~ +.3f}} as a mean over the wirings, beyond the margin, and with APL on it falls on every wiring. With APL off every other changed input lowers it beyond the margin as well.

**The main target barely moves, and the wrong way.** Under the fitted rule the pattern part of the APL-effect loss rises by {{E108/gate.csv:input=X3;population=all8:d_pattern_all ~ +.4f}} against all recordings, inside its margin, and by {{E108/gate.csv:input=X3;population=all8:d_pattern_A ~ +.4f}} against one half of them, just outside it; the rise is in the shape part. The mean APL effect stays at the flies' (table). Little had been expected to move, paa's pairs not being among those that carry the common error. Three further constraints, on the block, on the natural-source alignment and on the structure vs wild-type somata, were applied apart, and none fails.

**Realism.** All {{lit:156 # the rows of results/E108_paa_extrapolation/variants.csv: nine changed inputs of paa and six of B-myr on the eight wirings, and the nine of paa on the four wirings of the family with the firing ceiling; in runs.csv none has a realism_flag or a realism_flag_zcrit}} runs are inside the four realism bands, with the flies' responses counted in baseline-noise units and by the recordings' own criterion. Both response rates are held at the fits' (table), and the distribution of the number of odors per KC stays {{E108/readings.csv:input=X3;unit=all8;readout=raw:run_opk_on_tv ~ .3f}} / {{E108/readings.csv:input=X3;unit=all8;readout=raw:run_opk_off_tv ~ .3f}} from the flies' under the fitted rule, for bands of {{data:noise_ctrl_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .3f}} / {{data:noise_tnt_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .3f}}.

**Where realism is weakest is the extrapolated input itself.** The fitted rule raises paa's summed input by {{lit:65 % # results/E108_paa_extrapolation/paa_inputs.csv: the sum over the 36 glomeruli of column X3 (1874.8) over that of column hi, the recording at 10^-4 (1133.3), minus one}}, its constant term adds drive in glomeruli that paa does not excite at 10^-4, and DC1 is taken to {{E108/paa_inputs.csv:glomerulus=DC1:X3 ~ .0f}}, below the lowest value anywhere in the lab's input ({{lit:−21 # results/E108_paa_extrapolation/rule.json, paa.lab_min (-20.84): the lowest value in the lab's input over all odors and glomeruli}}); no floor had been set.

**Two readings beside, which decide nothing.**

- In [the family with the firing ceiling](#firing-ceiling), on four wirings, the fitted rule changes the two ρ's on odor-odor distances by {{E108/gate.csv:input=X3;population=fc4:d_rho_on_all ~ +.3f}} / {{E108/gate.csv:input=X3;population=fc4:d_rho_off_all ~ +.3f}}. The response rate ρ falls there as well, two of the permuted controls gain about as much with APL off, and a decade down loses.
- B-myr's input, which is at the flies' concentration, was varied within the spread of its ORN flies: each of the six flies' own B-myr in the place of the lab's mean. The two ρ's on odor-odor distances then change by {{E108/readings.csv:input=B2;unit=all8;readout=raw:d_rho_on_all ~ +.3f}} to {{E108/readings.csv:input=B0;unit=all8;readout=raw:d_rho_on_all ~ +.3f}} with APL on and by {{E108/readings.csv:input=B2;unit=all8;readout=raw:d_rho_off_all ~ +.3f}} to {{E108/readings.csv:input=B0;unit=all8;readout=raw:d_rho_off_all ~ +.3f}} with APL off. A rise of a hundredth from an input rule is thus well inside what other ORN flies would give.

**Limits.**

- paa's input at 10^-3 is an extrapolation and not a recording, from two recordings of the same six flies of one session. The series behind the fitted rule are of other odors, pooled over odors and glomeruli, and no rule has a floor.
- The scales are fixed. The family was to be fitted again only with an input classed as better, and none was.
- euc and -aPine stay at their recorded concentrations, so that every statistic over the 120 pairs carries that substitution ([footnote](#fn-concentrations)).

**What this leaves.**

- **No extrapolated input is put forward for the model.** The order of the pairs depends on paa's concentration, the rule of extrapolation is the limit, and the lab's recording at 10^-4 stays paa's input.
- **An ORN recording of paa at 10^-3 is the measurement to ask for,** without a claim about what the model would do with it (with the open measurement question at the end of the page). The fitted rule raises DM1, DP1m, DM4 and DM6 with nearly every other glomerulus, where the bounded-input oracle leaves DM1 and lowers the other three ([above](#gap-pairs)), and a recording would decide between them.
- **Neither the model nor the flies ask for the extra decade's drive.** In the model the lab's input at 10^-4 already gives paa the flies' response fraction, and wild-type flies shown paa at 10^-4 already hold it apart from B-myr ([the subsection before this one](#validation2-panel)). The collapse of paa's pairs stays with its measured input or with the stage before the KCs.
- **The search of the input of paa, B-myr and 2-but started from the lab's input,** since no extrapolated input was classed as better. It raises both ρ's on odor-odor distances on held-out wirings and recordings, and the response rate ρ with APL on is the constraint that it misses ([the next subsection](#input-search-rho)).

### The input of paa, B-myr and 2-but searched for ρ on odor-odor distances: whether an input within a factor of two of the lab's recordings raises it on wirings and recordings that the search never saw {#input-search-rho}

**The question was whether a bounded change of three odors' input can raise the order of the pairs where the search did not look.** The pairs of paa and B-myr, and less those of 2-but, carry most of the best family's gap in ρ on odor-odor distances ([above](#gap-parts)). The experiment, the input of paa, B-myr and 2-but searched for ρ on odor-odor distances on held-out wirings and recordings, lets each glomerulus's response to these odors move within a factor of two of the lab's recording. It is an [oracle](#fn-oracle) on the input, so only its reading on unseen wirings and recordings counts.

**It can, and one constraint fails by a hair.** On the held-out wirings and against the unseen recordings both ρ's on odor-odor distances rise, in every search and on every wiring, and the controls gain less than half as much. The APL-effect loss does not move. The response rate ρ with APL on falls just beyond its margin in one of three readings.

**By the outcomes fixed beforehand, that is a gain at a price.** The same cost is paid by the control search and by the permuted and the inverted factors, and it is absent when the wirings' response fractions are pooled. Whether it counts as a failed constraint is an open decision. No searched input is put forward for the model.

**The search.** Four of the family's eight wirings ([the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population)) were searched at once, each at its own fit. The objective was the sum of the two ρ's on odor-odor distances of their mean matrices, against one half of the recordings of each genotype. A candidate was penalized when an odor's response fractions left a set range or the pattern part of [the APL-effect loss](#apl-effect) rose beyond a small margin.

**Six searches, each read where it did not look.** Two searches ran on each half of one split of the recordings and one on each half of a second split, all from the lab's input. Each searched input was read at {{lit:0.6 # GATE_SIZE in experiments/E83_cross_wiring_fit.py}} of its size on the four other wirings, against the half of the recordings that its search never saw, with both response rates held at the fits'. Its full size was read beside.

**Three kinds of control.** The factors were permuted among each odor's glomeruli, in four permutations per search. They were inverted. And the same search was run for 2h and 6al, two odors whose input is not in question.

**The gate was fixed beforehand.** A gain is a rise of ρ on odor-odor distances by {{E109/yardsticks.csv:name=gate_gain_on:value ~ .3f}} with APL on or by {{E109/yardsticks.csv:name=gate_gain_off:value ~ .3f}} with APL off, on at least three of the four wirings and in both directions of the split. The other ρ may not fall by more than {{E109/yardsticks.csv:name=gate_other_slack:value ~ .3f}}, the second split has to agree in sign, and each control has to gain less than half as much. The other margins are in the table.

The searched inputs on the four held-out wirings, against the half of the recordings that each search never saw: changes from the family at the lab's input, each column the mean over its two searches. ρ on odor-odor distances and the loss on raw counts are on raw spike counts, and the other APL-effect statistics through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout). The response rate ρ is each wiring's own, averaged over the four. No input is chosen by a correlation ([why](#fn-pattern-split)).

| | the three odors' searched input {span=3} | | |
| statistic | searched on half A<br>read on half B | searched on half B<br>read on half A | the second split<br>of the recordings | the control search<br>for 2h and 6al<br>on A / on B | margin |

**Both ρ's gain on every held-out wiring.** Over the two directions of the first split the mean gain is {{E109/gate.csv:which=six;carrying=True:mean_gain_on ~ +.3f}} with APL on and {{E109/gate.csv:which=six;carrying=True:mean_gain_off ~ +.3f}} with APL off, and the second split agrees (table). A near-null change read on the same kind of wirings has a spread of {{data:paired_rho_on_sd_e102_weakest_step ~ .3f}} to {{data:paired_rho_off_sd_e93_fuller_input ~ .3f}} per wiring, so the gains are not noise of the model. The inputs searched for the pattern part had lost ρ on odor-odor distances on held-out wirings ([above](#gap-parts)).

**The controls gain less than half as much.** The permuted factors gain {{lit:+0.005 # results/E109_input_search_rho/gate.csv, row which=six;carrying=True, column controls (a JSON cell): on.permuted, the mean over the 24 permuted inputs}} with APL on and {{lit:+0.007 # the same cell: off.permuted}} with APL off on average, and the inverted factors lose {{lit:0.032 # the same cell: on.inverted}} and {{lit:0.030 # the same cell: off.inverted}}. The control search for 2h and 6al gains {{E109/gate.csv:which=ctl;reference=I0:mean_gain_on ~ +.3f}} / {{E109/gate.csv:which=ctl;reference=I0:mean_gain_off ~ +.3f}}, below the gate. One permutation of the 24 gained more than its own search, so the spread among permutations is wide.

**The gain covers part of what the three odors' pairs could give.** With the 42 pairs of the three odors at the flies' values and nothing else changed, the held-out wirings would reach the last column's values. The searched inputs cover less than half of that distance in each condition (table). paa's factors sit at the limit of a factor of two on {{E109/searches.csv:search=B2:paa_n_at_bound ~ .0f}} to {{E109/searches.csv:search=D1:paa_n_at_bound ~ .0f}} of its 36 glomeruli, so for paa the limit binds.

**The main target does not move.** The pattern part of the APL-effect loss changes by less than its margin in all three readings, in its amplitude part and its shape part alike, and the mean APL effect stays at the flies' (tables). At full size the searched inputs gain a little more in both ρ's, {{E109/gate.csv:which=six;reference=I0;size=1.0:mean_gain_on ~ +.3f}} / {{E109/gate.csv:which=six;reference=I0;size=1.0:mean_gain_off ~ +.3f}}, and the loss on raw counts rises by {{E109/gate.csv:which=six;reference=I0;size=1.0:worst_d_loss_raw ~ +.4f}}, beyond its margin. Three further constraints, on the block, on the natural-source alignment and on the structure vs wild-type somata, were applied apart, and none fails.

**The price is the response rate ρ with APL on.** Taken on each held-out wiring and averaged, it falls by {{E109/gate.csv:which=six;carrying=True:dirB_d_rate_rho_on ~ .4f}} in the direction that fails, just beyond the margin, and by a little less in the other two readings (first table). With APL off the fall is inside the margin. paa's response fraction falls, away from the flies' (second table); the search held each odor's fractions within a set range of the family's.

**Every change of the input pays that price.** The control search for 2h and 6al lowers the same statistic as much in one direction (first table). The permuted factors lower it by {{lit:0.028 # the mean over the 24 permuted inputs of run_rate_rho_on on unit T (raw rows of results/E109_input_search_rho/readings.csv) minus the I0 row's; computed read-only, not a column of a table}} and the inverted by {{lit:0.041 # the same mean over the 6 inverted inputs}} on average. It reads as the cost of any departure from the input that the family was fitted to, and not as the searched pattern's.

**The pooled response fractions do not pay it.** With the four wirings' response fractions averaged per odor before the ρ is taken, the family has a response rate ρ of {{lit:0.694 # E109_input_search_rho.md, "What the price is": a read-only check of the archived response matrices; not in a results table}} with APL on and the six searched inputs {{lit:0.685 to 0.712 # the same check}}. The fall is in each wiring's own order of the odors, not in the population's.

**What carries is paa held apart from B-myr.** The searched inputs move the cosine distance between the two odors most of the way to the flies' with APL on (second table). Across all {{lit:46 # the changed inputs read on unit T in results/E109_input_search_rho/readings.csv: 38 at 0.6 of their size (six searched, 24 permuted, six inverted, two control searches) and 8 at full size}} changed inputs that were read, searched and control alike, the gain in each ρ on odor-odor distances follows the change in that distance, with a Pearson r of {{lit:about 0.8 # computed read-only from readings.csv, raw rows of unit T, each input's gain against its unseen half and its change in paa_bmyr_on / paa_bmyr_off: 0.78 with APL on and 0.83 with APL off; not in a results table}}. The inverted factors bring the two odors closer and lose.

**Wild-type flies of another panel agree (a description).** paa's and B-myr's searched factors were applied to the validation2 ORN input, where paa is at the concentration that those flies got ([above](#validation2-panel)). Against Remy's KC somata, ρ on odor-odor distances of the held-out wirings rises from {{E109/e107_reference.csv:unit=T;reading=fitted:rho_all ~ .3f}} to {{E109/step7_remy.csv:input=D1;unit=T:rho_all ~ .3f}} to {{E109/step7_remy.csv:input=C1;unit=T:rho_all ~ .3f}} over the manuscript's pairs (ceiling {{E107/a_ceilings.csv:panel=validation2;metric=cosine;set=136;subset=all:ceiling ~ .3f}}). Over the pairs of the two odors it rises from {{E109/e107_reference.csv:unit=T;reading=fitted:rho_pb ~ .3f}} to {{E109/step7_remy.csv:input=D1;unit=T:rho_pb ~ .3f}} to {{E109/step7_remy.csv:input=A2;unit=T:rho_pb ~ .3f}}. No search saw these flies; they are of another genotype and response measure, so this decides nothing.

**The glomeruli that the searches agree on are leads.** {{lit:18 # the rows of results/E109_input_search_rho/step6_entries.csv with meets True: a mean log2 factor beyond 0.5 with the same sign in at least five of the six searches}} entries recur in five of the six searches. They lower DM1 for paa and for B-myr and DP1m for paa, the glomeruli onto which the family's KCs collapse the two odors ([above](#gap-pairs)), and raise DL5 and VM7d for paa. As read, paa's VM7d is {{E109/step6_entries.csv:odor=paa;glomerulus=VM7d:read_in_flies_sd ~ .1f}} standard deviations of its ORN flies above the lab's value and the others are within about one. Single entries are leads, and the result is not a pass, so they are not a list for a measurement.

**Realism.** All {{lit:184 # the rows of results/E109_input_search_rho/runs_R.csv (the searched inputs at both sizes and the controls on the four held-out wirings); none has a realism_flag}} runs are inside the four realism bands, with both response rates held at the fits' (second table). The distribution of the number of odors per KC is {{E109/readings.csv:change=B2_s0.6;unit=T;readout=raw:run_opk_on_tv ~ .3f}} / {{E109/readings.csv:change=B2_s0.6;unit=T;readout=raw:run_opk_off_tv ~ .3f}} from the flies' for the searched input with the lowest loss, for bands of {{data:noise_ctrl_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .3f}} / {{data:noise_tnt_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .3f}}. Where realism is weakest is the input itself: about half of paa's glomeruli sit at the limit of the search.

**Limits.**

- The search is given the KC data. Only the held-out reading counts, at the size fixed beforehand, and the scales are fixed: the family was to be fitted again with a searched input only on a pass.
- The margin was missed by less than a near-null change moves a wiring. The rule was applied as written.
- paa's input is the recording at 10^-4 standing in for the flies' 10^-3, and paa is one of the searched odors, so every number here carries that substitution. euc and -aPine stay at their recorded concentrations and are in every statistic over the 120 pairs ([footnote](#fn-concentrations)).

**What this leaves.**

- **The input's side is open for the order of the pairs.** A bounded change of three odors' input raises both ρ's on odor-odor distances where it was not searched, which no earlier searched input did, and it leaves the main target where it was.
- **Whether the price is one is an open decision.** If the missed margin is read as no failure, the next step is the family fitted again with a searched input, then the family with the firing ceiling and the trial noise.
- **No searched input is put forward for the model.** The lab's recordings stay the input of the three odors.
- **A measurement would test the lead:** paa and B-myr recorded in the same ORN flies as megamat odors, at the flies' concentrations, with DM1, DL5, VM7d and DP1m as the glomeruli to look at (with the open measurement question at the end of the page).
- **The concentration is not the likely reason for the collapse.** paa's input moved to the flies' concentration did not give this gain ([the subsection before this one](#paa-concentration)), and wild-type flies separate the two odors at the concentration of the ORN input.

### Hallem's receptor data as the weak odors' input {#hallem-input}

The lab's ORN input and Hallem & Carlson's receptor data (odors at 10^-2; 16 of the model's 36 glomeruli) agree for the esters and aldehydes and disagree for exactly the weak-input odors: ms is a one-glomerulus odor in Hallem (DL1 at 258 Hz against 70 Hz in the lab's data), paa and 1-8ol peak in different glomeruli in the two datasets (DM6 against DM1; VC3 against DC2), B-myr is weak in both, and euc is not in Hallem's set.

Putting Hallem's values for ms, paa, B-myr and 1-8ol into the input (on the shared glomeruli, the lab's elsewhere) on the 70 Hz threshold model, one odor at a time, says which of the five odors' deficits the input can explain. Hallem's 10^-2 is ten times Yang's concentration for ms, paa and 1-8ol, so these inputs are upper bounds.

**By odor.** Hallem's ms recruits half the fly's ms population with APL off and Hallem's paa recruits paa at the fly's fraction, both at no cost to any other statistic; Hallem's 1-8ol over-recruits and costs the natural-source alignment; Hallem's B-myr is weaker than the lab's and changes nothing. Every ms responder recruited by DL1 has a second claw from a glomerulus ms drives weakly: one claw at 258 Hz does not fire a KC in this model, so the recruited population is narrower than the fly's with APL off (a breadth of 2.4 odors against 4.9), and the fly's single-claw ms channel, if it is one, needs a mechanism the model lacks.

**In the reference model**, which carries the 1.5× gain on DL1, VA7m and D, Hallem's ms brings ms to the fly's fraction with APL off, but APL then spares the new narrow responders (blocking APL output multiplies ms's response fraction by 1.3, against 2.1 in the fly), because breadth-weighted APL inhibits broad KCs most: a narrow channel is where that rule and the fly part.

**Level is not profile.** Scaling the lab's profiles of the four odors to Hallem's level instead over-recruits ms, paa and 1-8ol (16 glomeruli above the knee for ms instead of two) and gives the highest ρ on odor-odor distances with the APL output blocked (TNT) matrix of any model so far with the per-odor response-rate pattern destroyed: the matrix ρ rewards a weak odor's recruitment whatever its size, which is why it is read together with response rate ρ.

### The operating point: the control flies' 6.8 % instead of 5 % {#operating-point}

Every model on this page is tuned or fitted so that 5 % of KCs respond with APL on, a convention from the lab's earlier modelling, while {{data:ctrl_frac ~ .1%}} of the control flies' KCs respond (and {{data:tnt_frac ~ .1%}} with APL output blocked). Re-fitted with the response-rate target at the control flies' fraction instead, the reference model keeps everything the fit measures: the block, ρ on odor-odor distances with both KC matrices and the structure vs wild-type somata stay where they were at 5 %, response rate ρ with APL on rises slightly, and the loss without its response-rate term is no worse (the fit does it with a stronger APL↔KC loop and a weaker APL→bouton scale).

Moving only the somatic threshold to the new operating point, with every other fitted scale held, costs the 40 Hz model almost half of its block, so a threshold-only change of operating point is not neutral. What the operating point does change is the response fractions: at 6.8 % the weak-input odors respond more, and the reference model, whose gain was fitted at 5 %, now over-recruits them with APL off. Its weak odors were already too strong relative to the mean at 5 % (the absolute match there came from an overall APL-off response rate below the data's), so the gain of 1.5 on eight glomeruli is more than the data's operating point needs.

In the bouton bases tuned from 3.4 % to 10 %, ρ on odor-odor distances barely moves and the block stays at zero; the weak odors' share of the mean APL-off response rate rises from {{E44/comparison.csv:A_thr70_t0.050:weak_share_off ~ .2f}} at 5 % to {{E44/comparison.csv:A_thr70_t0.068:weak_share_off ~ .2f}} at 6.8 % in the 70 Hz base (data {{data:tnt_weak_share ~ .2f}}), a fifth to a quarter of the way, and the APL-off mean pair distance falls toward the data's as more KCs respond ({{E44/comparison.csv:A_thr70_t0.050:mean_dist_off ~ .2f}} to {{E44/comparison.csv:A_thr70_t0.068:mean_dist_off ~ .2f}}; data {{data:tnt_mean_dist ~ .2f}}). Fitting at the data's fraction costs nothing and compares response fractions with the data at the same mean; the gain is the parameter to re-fit there.

**The gain at the data's operating point.** Re-fitting the gain arms at the control flies' response rate settles three things.

- The gain is not an artefact of the 5 % convention: without it the fits keep the block but lose the APL-off to APL-on response-rate ratio and the natural-source alignment with APL off, at a much higher loss.
- At the 70 Hz per-claw threshold a smaller gain on the eight glomeruli (1.25) gives the best fit of all, keeping the block and the agreement with both KC matrices with more structure against wild-type somata; at 40 Hz the block still needs 1.5.
- And the three-glomerulus core with Hallem's ms input is the best fit at 40 Hz and the only arm whose weak odors take the data's share of the APL-off response, at its usual cost in agreement with the KC matrices.

The differences are within the spread between wiring draws, so the reference model is unchanged until a second draw.

**The operating-point fits on a re-drawn wiring.** The two best fits at the control flies' response rate, the eight glomeruli at 1.25 at the 70 Hz per-claw threshold and the DC2, DM5 and DM1 core with Hallem's ms input at 1.5 at 40 Hz, led the reference model by only 0.1–0.2 of extended loss, within what a re-drawn wiring can move a fit. Re-fitted on the second within-type claw-permutation draw (the one the replication on re-drawn wiring and the reduced gain sets on a re-drawn wiring used), both orderings hold and widen: at 70 Hz the eight at 1.25 reach {{E46/comparison.csv:thr70_wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed2_gain1.25_rate0.068_k2_cap3:loss ~ .2f}} against {{E46/comparison.csv:thr70_wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed2_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3:loss ~ .2f}} for the eight at 1.5, and at 40 Hz the core reaches {{E46/comparison.csv:thr40_wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed2_input-hallem_shared_ms_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_core3_cap3:loss ~ .2f}} against {{E46/comparison.csv:thr40_wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed2_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3:loss ~ .2f}}.

The draw again takes most of its toll on the block: the reference model keeps half of its block on the draw at 70 Hz and two thirds at 40 Hz (the latter from a second start with a lower somatic threshold and a stronger APL; from its own start it kept a third), the core two thirds, and the eight at 1.25 nearly all of it, by shifting to that lower-threshold, stronger-APL solution.

Structure against wild-type somata and the natural-source alignment fall on the draw for every model, as in the replication on re-drawn wiring, while agreement with the two KC matrices does not. So the smaller gain at 70 Hz and the core at 40 Hz are not artefacts of the real wiring, and fitting at the data's response fraction left the reference model's dependence on the real wiring unchanged; what that dependence consists of is taken up [next](#wiring-feature).

### Which feature of the wiring the fitted block needs {#wiring-feature}

Every re-drawn wiring on this page is one kind of shuffle, each KC type's claws re-assigned among that type's boutons, and every such re-draw lost part of the block once the model was fitted with the structure targets. Which feature of the real wiring the block needs was asked with four kinds of shuffle of the bouton wiring: claw permutations, which keep each KC's and each glomerulus' number of claws, and Curveball shuffles, which keep each KC's number of distinct glomeruli and each glomerulus' number of KCs, each either across all KCs or within each KC type (so that each type keeps its glomerulus repertoire).

The reference model at the control flies' response fraction (the eight glomeruli at 1.5, at both per-claw thresholds, and the eight at 1.25 at 70 Hz) was first run on five draws of each kind at its fitted APL and KC–KC scales, with only the somatic threshold re-tuned to the response fraction (it moved by at most 2 %), and then re-fitted on one draw of each kind.

At the fitted scales every kind of shuffle loses part of the block, and the draw-to-draw spread is as large as the differences between kinds, so no kind separates from the others: the within-type Curveball keeps the most for the eight at 1.5 and the claw permutations the least at 40 Hz, but the eight at 1.25 reverse that order. Agreement with the two KC matrices does not move; what the shuffles cost besides the block is the APL-on response-rate pattern and the natural-source alignment.

Re-fitted, the block comes back, but by an amount set by the draw and not by the kind of shuffle. On the first draw the two shuffles that ignore KC type made the data's block in full, on a wiring whose every claw was re-assigned at random across all KCs, and the two within-type shuffles kept the least; the follow-up on four draws each of the plain claw permutation and the within-type Curveball (the fitted block on more shuffle draws) found the two kinds indistinguishable, their means in the opposite order and both between half and three quarters of the data's block, with single draws recovering anything from none of it to all of it, none above the real wiring's value, and the four draws with the lowest loss carrying the four largest blocks.

So the fitted block does not need the hemibrain's pairing of glomeruli on KCs: a re-fit recovers it on a random wiring with these claw counts to a degree that varies from draw to draw, and the re-draws' loss of it above was the typical draw's loss (their within-type claw-permutation draws recovered what a typical draw of either kind recovers), not a sign that the block rides on the real wiring.

What every shuffle loses, re-fitted or not, is the natural-source alignment with APL off, which on the real wiring sits at the data's value and on no shuffled wiring the model was re-fitted on comes close to it; APL's effect on it (on minus off) is at or below zero on the real wiring and on the within-type shuffles, where the data's is positive, and positive only on the plain claw permutation, the one statistic that told the two kinds apart.

The structure against wild-type somata is kept by every shuffle for the eight at 1.5 and lost only for the eight at 1.25. The real wiring's own contribution to the fitted models is therefore the natural-source alignment, not the block; a block difference between two wirings means something only once several draws of each have been re-fitted.
