Which part of the wiring carries the natural-source alignment was then asked directly (the glomerulus pairs behind the natural-source alignment). Counting, for each pair of the 54 glomeruli of the claw wiring, the KCs with claws from both glomeruli against 200 draws of each kind of shuffle finds two layers of structure beyond the margins.

- Fifty-five of the 1431 pairs are over-shared against every kind, and they are the food glomeruli converging on common KCs (DM1 with DM4, DM2, DM5 and DP1m, DM2 with DM4 and DM5, VM5d with VM5v and VA3; DM1 / DM4 on 92 KCs where the margins predict 50), the convergence the connectome literature reports.
- And 76 of the 162 glomerulus x KC-type counts are far from what a type-ignoring shuffle predicts: the food glomeruli are concentrated on the α/β KCs and depleted on the γ KCs (DM2 reaches 22 % of the α/β KCs and 8 % of the γ KCs where a type-ignoring shuffle gives 14 % of each), and a second set (DC3, VA5, VA6, VL2a, DA2, D, DL1) the other way round; this is the layer the within-type shuffles keep and the type-ignoring ones destroy.

Turned into a score per odor pair (the shared-KC counts summed over glomerulus pairs, weighted by the two odors' ORN input), the type layer predicts which odor pairs the fitted real-wiring model brings closer than its shuffles do (ρ {{E52/score_correlations.csv:weighting=norm;kind=typestruct;null_class=claw_permutation;target=model_contrib_off_thr40_gain1.5:rho ~ +.2f}} with the reference model's APL-off residual minus the shuffle mean), which pairs the control flies bring closer than the ORN input predicts ({{E52/score_correlations.csv:weighting=norm;kind=typestruct;null_class=claw_permutation;target=resid_ctrl:rho ~ +.2f}}) and, less strongly, the natural-source-close pairs ({{E52/score_correlations.csv:weighting=norm;kind=typestruct;null_class=claw_permutation;target=vcf_hyp:rho ~ +.2f}}); the over-shared pairs' excess beyond type predicts chemical distance instead ({{E52/score_correlations.csv:weighting=norm;kind=excess;null_class=curveball_within_type;target=chem:rho ~ +.2f}}) and none of those ({{E52/score_correlations.csv:weighting=norm;kind=excess;null_class=curveball_within_type;target=vcf_hyp:rho ~ +.2f}} with the natural-source distance).

Lesioning only the 55 pairs' excess, by claw swaps that keep every KC's and every bouton's claw count (a tenth of the claws moved), takes the reference model's alignment with APL off at its fitted scales from {{E47/comparison.csv:A_thr40_gain1.5_real_retuned:spike_counts_cosine__off_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp ~ .2f}} to {{E52/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=lesion_targeted:spike_counts_cosine__off_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp__mean ~ .2f}}, where the within-type shuffles sit, while a control lesion of the same size on count-matched pairs leaves it at {{E52/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=lesion_control:spike_counts_cosine__off_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp__mean ~ .2f}}; the block does not move.

So the alignment the models owe to the real wiring has two carriers: the KC-type organization of the glomerular input, the larger and the one organized along the natural-source axis, and the within-type convergence of the food glomeruli, the smaller and organized by chemistry. A within-type shuffle is the right null for the first and the targeted lesion for the second; the type-ignoring shuffles lose both, which is why a model re-fitted on one loses more of the alignment than any pairwise feature accounts for.

The reference model at its fitted scales (somatic threshold re-tuned to the response fraction) on the real wiring, with the 55 over-shared pairs' excess removed, with the same excess removed from matched control pairs, and on the within-type Curveball and the plain claw permutation (mean ± sd over draws; the 70 Hz model and the eight at 1.25 are in the experiment's note).

What each layer of the wiring's co-input structure predicts about an odor pair: the Spearman ρ, over the 66 megamat pairs, between the pair's wiring-sharing score and the quantity named (the KC-type layer is a within-type shuffle's expected sharing minus a type-ignoring shuffle's; the layer beyond type is the sharing in excess of the within-type Curveball's expectation; the two together are the excess over the plain claw permutation).

| statistic | KC-type layer (what the within-type shuffles keep) | beyond-type over-sharing (what every shuffle destroys) | both together |

| natural-source distance | {{E52/score_correlations.csv:weighting=norm;kind=typestruct;null_class=claw_permutation;target=vcf_hyp:rho ~ +.2f}} | {{E52/score_correlations.csv:weighting=norm;kind=excess;null_class=curveball_within_type;target=vcf_hyp:rho ~ +.2f}} | {{E52/score_correlations.csv:weighting=norm;kind=excess;null_class=claw_permutation;target=vcf_hyp:rho ~ +.2f}} |
| chemical distance | {{E52/score_correlations.csv:weighting=norm;kind=typestruct;null_class=claw_permutation;target=chem:rho ~ +.2f}} | {{E52/score_correlations.csv:weighting=norm;kind=excess;null_class=curveball_within_type;target=chem:rho ~ +.2f}} | {{E52/score_correlations.csv:weighting=norm;kind=excess;null_class=claw_permutation;target=chem:rho ~ +.2f}} |
| ORN distance | {{E52/score_correlations.csv:weighting=norm;kind=typestruct;null_class=claw_permutation;target=orn:rho ~ +.2f}} | {{E52/score_correlations.csv:weighting=norm;kind=excess;null_class=curveball_within_type;target=orn:rho ~ +.2f}} | {{E52/score_correlations.csv:weighting=norm;kind=excess;null_class=claw_permutation;target=orn:rho ~ +.2f}} |
| KC residual around the ORN prediction, control flies | {{E52/score_correlations.csv:weighting=norm;kind=typestruct;null_class=claw_permutation;target=resid_ctrl:rho ~ +.2f}} | {{E52/score_correlations.csv:weighting=norm;kind=excess;null_class=curveball_within_type;target=resid_ctrl:rho ~ +.2f}} | {{E52/score_correlations.csv:weighting=norm;kind=excess;null_class=claw_permutation;target=resid_ctrl:rho ~ +.2f}} |
| KC residual around the ORN prediction, APL output blocked (TNT) | {{E52/score_correlations.csv:weighting=norm;kind=typestruct;null_class=claw_permutation;target=resid_tnt:rho ~ +.2f}} | {{E52/score_correlations.csv:weighting=norm;kind=excess;null_class=curveball_within_type;target=resid_tnt:rho ~ +.2f}} | {{E52/score_correlations.csv:weighting=norm;kind=excess;null_class=claw_permutation;target=resid_tnt:rho ~ +.2f}} |

The pairwise carrier was then tested against the gain (the gain and the wiring behind the natural-source alignment), since four of the eight gained glomeruli sit in the over-shared pairs. It works only through the gain. With the eight glomeruli's gain set to 1 at the fitted scales the reference model's alignment with APL off falls from {{E47/comparison.csv:A_thr40_gain1.5_real_retuned:spike_counts_cosine__off_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp ~ .2f}} to {{E54/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=nogain:spike_counts_cosine__off_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp__mean ~ .2f}} (the fit made without gain, which re-tunes every scale, reaches {{E54/comparison.csv:model=thr40_nogain;shuffle=real:spike_counts_cosine__off_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp ~ .2f}}), and under the fits made without gain the lesion of the 55 over-shared pairs changes nothing beyond draw noise.

With the gain, neither half of the over-shared pairs with ORN data moves the alignment on its own: the 15 pairs that involve a gained glomerulus leave it at {{E54/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=lesion_gained:spike_counts_cosine__off_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp__mean ~ .2f}} (their matched control pairs {{E54/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=control_gained:spike_counts_cosine__off_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp__mean ~ .2f}}), the 17 that do not at {{E54/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=lesion_ungained:spike_counts_cosine__off_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp__mean ~ .2f}} ({{E54/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=control_ungained:spike_counts_cosine__off_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp__mean ~ .2f}}), and the 23 over-shared pairs among glomeruli the model does not drive at {{E54/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=lesion_nonorn:spike_counts_cosine__off_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp__mean ~ .2f}} ({{E54/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=control_nonorn:spike_counts_cosine__off_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp__mean ~ .2f}}); the 32 pairs with ORN data lesioned together take it to {{E54/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=lesion_orn_all:spike_counts_cosine__off_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp__mean ~ .2f}} against their controls' {{E54/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=control_orn_all:spike_counts_cosine__off_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp__mean ~ .2f}}, where the lesion of all 55 had put it.

So the pairwise carrier is the food-glomerulus convergence as a whole, not the sum of its parts, and it carries the alignment only when the type-biased glomeruli within it are gained; the half that involves gained glomeruli is what costs the per-odor response-rate pattern with APL on ({{E54/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=lesion_gained:spearman_rate_on_vs_data__mean ~ .2f}} against {{E54/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=control_gained:spearman_rate_on_vs_data__mean ~ .2f}} for its controls). A re-fit of the reference model on a lesioned wiring buys the block back ({{E54/comparison.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=refit_lesion_targeted-seed0:spike_counts_cosine__block_fruity_small_iso ~ +.3f}} against {{E47/comparison.csv:A_thr40_gain1.5_real_retuned:spike_counts_cosine__block_fruity_small_iso ~ +.3f}} on the real wiring) and leaves the alignment at {{E54/comparison.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=refit_lesion_targeted-seed0:spike_counts_cosine__off_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp ~ .2f}}, with the loss at {{E54/comparison.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=refit_lesion_targeted-seed0:loss_rate_ctrl ~ .2f}} against {{E47/comparison.csv:A_thr40_gain1.5_real_retuned:loss_rate_ctrl ~ .2f}}: as on every shuffled wiring, the alignment is the statistic a re-fit cannot buy back.

| response rate ρ, APL on | ceiling {{data:ctrl_rate_rho_ceiling ~ .2f}} | {{E47/comparison.csv:A_thr40_gain1.5_real_retuned:spearman_rate_on_vs_data ~ .2f}} | {{E54/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=nogain:spearman_rate_on_vs_data__mean ~ .2f}} | {{E54/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=lesion_gained:spearman_rate_on_vs_data__mean ~ .2f}} ± {{E54/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=lesion_gained:spearman_rate_on_vs_data__std ~ .2f}} | {{E54/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=lesion_ungained:spearman_rate_on_vs_data__mean ~ .2f}} ± {{E54/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=lesion_ungained:spearman_rate_on_vs_data__std ~ .2f}} | {{E54/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=lesion_nonorn:spearman_rate_on_vs_data__mean ~ .2f}} ± {{E54/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=lesion_nonorn:spearman_rate_on_vs_data__std ~ .2f}} | {{E54/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=lesion_orn_all:spearman_rate_on_vs_data__mean ~ .2f}} ± {{E54/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=lesion_orn_all:spearman_rate_on_vs_data__std ~ .2f}} | {{E54/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=control_orn_all:spearman_rate_on_vs_data__mean ~ .2f}} ± {{E54/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=control_orn_all:spearman_rate_on_vs_data__std ~ .2f}} | {{E54/comparison.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=refit_lesion_targeted-seed0:spearman_rate_on_vs_data ~ .2f}} |

Whether the two carriers are sufficient was then asked by putting the convergence back (building the natural-source alignment back). On within-type Curveball draws (the type structure kept, the convergence destroyed) and on plain Curveball draws (both destroyed), the 32 over-shared pairs with ORN data were raised to the real wiring's shared-KC counts by claw swaps that keep every KC's and every bouton's claw count (10 to 12 % of the claws moved), with the same raises on count-matched control pairs as the control, and the reference models were run at their fitted scales with the threshold re-tuned. The answer splits by APL state.

- With APL on the convergence brings the alignment back: on the within-type draws the reference model goes from {{E47/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=curveball_within_type:spike_counts_cosine__on_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp__mean ~ .2f}} untreated to {{E57/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=curveball_within_type_transplant:spike_counts_cosine__on_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp__mean ~ .2f}} (the real wiring {{E47/comparison.csv:A_thr40_gain1.5_real_retuned:spike_counts_cosine__on_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp ~ .2f}}; the control raises {{E57/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=curveball_within_type_control:spike_counts_cosine__on_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp__mean ~ .2f}}), a rise of {{E57/paired_differences.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=curveball_within_type;kind=transplant;stat=spike_counts_cosine__on_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp:mean_diff ~ +.2f}} per draw that is positive on every draw and for all three models, to within a few hundredths of the real wiring; on the plain draws it gets about halfway ({{E57/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=curveball_transplant:spike_counts_cosine__on_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp__mean ~ .2f}} from {{E47/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=curveball:spike_counts_cosine__on_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp__mean ~ .2f}}).
- With APL off it does not move: {{E57/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=curveball_within_type_transplant:spike_counts_cosine__off_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp__mean ~ .2f}} after the transplant against {{E47/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=curveball_within_type:spike_counts_cosine__off_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp__mean ~ .2f}} untreated and the real wiring's {{E47/comparison.csv:A_thr40_gain1.5_real_retuned:spike_counts_cosine__off_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp ~ .2f}}, on either class of draw, although the lesion of exactly these counts on the real wiring had cost it ({{E54/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=lesion_orn_all:spike_counts_cosine__off_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp__mean ~ .2f}} against {{E54/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=control_orn_all:spike_counts_cosine__off_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp__mean ~ .2f}} for the control lesions).

So APL on minus off, which the KC data have at {{data:vcf_apl_effect ~ +.2f}} and the real-wiring models about level, moves on the within-type draws from {{E47/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=curveball_within_type:vcf_on_minus_off__mean ~ +.2f}} to {{E57/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=curveball_within_type_transplant:vcf_on_minus_off__mean ~ +.2f}}. The convergence as a pairwise count is what carries the APL-on side of the alignment, and with the type structure under it it is close to sufficient for that side; the APL-off side that the lesions lose is the convergence in its real-wiring arrangement, which KCs hold the pairs and what else those KCs sample, which no pairwise transplant restores.

The structure against the wild-type somata rises with the transplant above the real wiring's value ({{E57/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=curveball_within_type_transplant:spike_counts_cosine__on_spearman_resid_vs_remap_wt__mean ~ .2f}} against {{E47/comparison.csv:A_thr40_gain1.5_real_retuned:spike_counts_cosine__on_spearman_resid_vs_remap_wt ~ .2f}}), the block is not restored ({{E57/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=curveball_within_type_transplant:spike_counts_cosine__block_fruity_small_iso__mean ~ +.3f}} against {{E47/comparison.csv:A_thr40_gain1.5_real_retuned:spike_counts_cosine__block_fruity_small_iso ~ +.3f}}), and the response rate ρ with APL on rises under the control raises ({{E57/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=curveball_within_type_control:spearman_rate_on_vs_data__mean ~ .2f}}) nearly as much as under the transplant ({{E57/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=curveball_within_type_transplant:spearman_rate_on_vs_data__mean ~ .2f}}), so that statistic answers to the swaps rather than to the pairs.

Whether the whole pairwise matrix suffices was then asked (the co-input-preserving shuffle). A simulated-annealing shuffle of same-type claw swaps brought every one of the 1431 glomerulus pairs' shared-KC counts, on within-type and on plain Curveball draws, to within one KC of the real wiring's, with 97 % of the claws still differing from the real wiring and the three-way co-input among the over-shared glomeruli only partly reproduced.

On the type-preserving draws the match buys no APL-off alignment: the reference model's {{E59/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=curveball_within_type_matched:spike_counts_cosine__off_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp__mean ~ .2f}} against {{E47/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=curveball_within_type:spike_counts_cosine__off_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp__mean ~ .2f}} untreated and the real wiring's {{E47/comparison.csv:A_thr40_gain1.5_real_retuned:spike_counts_cosine__off_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp ~ .2f}}, as the 32-pair transplant bought none; on the plain draws it lifts it to {{E59/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=curveball_matched:spike_counts_cosine__off_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp__mean ~ .2f}} from {{E47/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=curveball:spike_counts_cosine__off_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp__mean ~ .2f}}, the untreated within-type level, so the pairwise matrix and the type layer are substitutes for one another and together reach no more than either. The APL-on side comes back on both backgrounds ({{E59/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=curveball_within_type_matched:spike_counts_cosine__on_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp__mean ~ .2f}} and {{E59/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=curveball_matched:spike_counts_cosine__on_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp__mean ~ .2f}} against the real wiring's {{E47/comparison.csv:A_thr40_gain1.5_real_retuned:spike_counts_cosine__on_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp ~ .2f}}), as it did with the transplant, and the block is restored by nothing ({{E59/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=curveball_matched:spike_counts_cosine__block_fruity_small_iso__mean ~ +.3f}} on the matched plain draws).

A re-fit of the reference model on a matched within-type wiring recovers everything the structure loss scores, the loss itself ({{E59/comparison.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=refit_curveball_within_type_matched-seed1:loss_rate_ctrl ~ .2f}} against {{E47/comparison.csv:A_thr40_gain1.5_real_retuned:loss_rate_ctrl ~ .2f}} on the real wiring), the block ({{E59/comparison.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=refit_curveball_within_type_matched-seed1:spike_counts_cosine__block_fruity_small_iso ~ +.3f}}) and the APL-on alignment ({{E59/comparison.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=refit_curveball_within_type_matched-seed1:spike_counts_cosine__on_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp ~ .2f}}), by doubling the KC-KC scale, and not the APL-off alignment ({{E59/comparison.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=refit_curveball_within_type_matched-seed1:spike_counts_cosine__off_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp ~ .2f}}): on every shuffled, lesioned or matched wiring so far it is the statistic a re-fit cannot buy back, and its carrier is finer than the pairwise matrix (the three-way co-input, or which KC holds which combination of glomeruli). None of these wirings moves ρ on odor-odor distances with either KC matrix beyond the draw-to-draw spread.

| | | | Curveball within type {span=3} | Curveball {span=3} |

### The per-claw threshold at low concentration {#low-concentration}

Every constraint above comes from the APL16 panel at 10^-3 to 10^-2, where the per-claw threshold that every good model carries costs nothing. Two further KC datasets of Yang's have weak input by construction: in control flies 2h and ma at 10^-7 recruit 5–6 % of KCs and farn at 10^-3 4 %, and with APL output blocked two to three times as many.

Run at their fitted parameters on those odors (ORN input within one log unit of the recorded concentration, the stronger one where the exact one is missing, so a failure to recruit is the conservative result), the fitted models recruit a half to a tenth of the KCs the flies recruit and almost none for ma, whose ORN input is exact; the matched trial noise roughly doubles the fractions without closing the gap, and with APL off the models are as far short of the flies with APL output blocked, so the deficit is in what reaches the KCs through the per-claw threshold, not in APL (whose share, the APL-off to APL-on ratio, is about the flies' for 2h and farn). The model with the lowest somatic threshold, the eight glomeruli at 1.25 at 70 Hz, comes closest.

The flies' binary mixtures recruit fewer KCs than the union of their components, mildly in control flies and strongly with APL output blocked (ma + farn fewer than either component); with the components' ORN input combined as their maximum per glomerulus the models show the mild sub-additivity and not the strong one. So the per-claw threshold, a hard rectifier at 40–70 Hz of PN input, is falsified at low concentration: a sub-threshold slope or noise through the threshold has to carry these responses, and the fitted models describe KC recruitment at 10^-3 to 10^-2 only.

A fit without a per-claw threshold has since been run on these odors: it recruits KCs for ma and for 2h at 10^-5, as many as the flies for 2h through the matched trial noise and about half as many for ma ([the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population)). The flies' side of these comparisons has since been read like for like, as three sets of flies that are kept apart and above the solvent's responders; the sets differ at ma about threefold, and the models of this table were not read again ([the KCs' response rates at the weak odors read like for like](#weak-odor-rates)).

| distance matrices: APL on, APL off and APL on minus APL off (the KC data above the model) | !button[matrices](results/apl_effect/matrices/data.png) | !button[matrices](results/apl_effect/matrices/E13_bouton_coincidence__bouton_base.png) | !button[matrices](results/apl_effect/matrices/E16_claw_saturation__bouton_thr70.png) | !button[matrices](results/apl_effect/matrices/E8_kc_kc_inhibition__breadth3_tau0.05_kckc100.png) | !button[matrices](results/apl_effect/matrices/E19_thr_breadth_kckc__thr70_k2_kckc100.png) | !button[matrices](results/apl_effect/matrices/E10_joint_fit__k2.png) | !button[matrices](results/apl_effect/matrices/E27_glomerulus_gain__oracle_g1.5.png) | !button[matrices](results/apl_effect/matrices/E25_joint_fit_structure__thr70_k2_ext.png) | !button[matrices](results/apl_effect/matrices/E28_gain_combined_jointfit__thr40_gain1.5_k2.png) | !button[matrices](results/apl_effect/matrices/E34_gain_bounded__thr40_gain1.5_k2_cap3.png) | !button[matrices](results/apl_effect/matrices/E44_operating_point__thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3.png) | !button[matrices](results/apl_effect/matrices/E36_spike_apl__spk_thr70_k2_s2.png) | !button[matrices](results/apl_effect/matrices/E67_apl_effect_fits__rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3.png) | !button[matrices](results/apl_effect/matrices/E69_kc_firing_ceiling__rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2.png) | !button[matrices](results/apl_effect/matrices/E39_gain_decomposition__thr70__only_DM1.png) |

- Two columns hold the same model at two operating points: the reference model until 2026-11-08, fitted with 5 % of KCs responding with APL on (the convention of the lab's earlier modelling), and the current reference model, its re-fit at the {{data:ctrl_frac ~ .1%}} of KCs that respond in the control flies, from which the later experiments start ([the operating point](#operating-point)).
- The third column from the end is one of [the APL-effect fits](#apl-effect-fits), the fits that put the APL-effect loss first in the loss: the first joint fit's family (breadth exponent 2, no per-claw threshold, no glomerulus gain) fitted at the flies' response rate with the calibrated readout in the loss, and scored here on raw spike counts like every other column.
- The column after it is the same fit made again with [a firing ceiling for the KCs](#firing-ceiling), a refractory period and an adaptation that bound how many spikes a KC fires to one odor, at the setting whose largest spike counts agree with whole-cell recordings of KCs and with both definitions of the model's side in the loss.

On the main target no model reaches the data, and only the fit with a firing ceiling comes near it, at about one and a half times the floor. That number is of the model's 0.5 s odor pulse. Read as the flies were recorded, at their 2 s pulse and through their response window with the indicator's kinetics as measured in the recordings, the same fit stands at {{E84/protocol_readings_measured_kernel.csv:point_id=B1_fit1;kernel=r1.29_d20.7:raw_loss ~ .3f}} with the adaptation it was fitted with and at {{E84/protocol_readings_measured_kernel.csv:point_id=B6_fit1_tau3;kernel=r1.29_d20.7:raw_loss ~ .3f}} with an adaptation that outlasts the odor ([the flies' recording protocol in the model](#flies-protocol) and [the time course of the APL effect in the flies' traces](#trace-time-course), at the end of this section).

Without a ceiling the lowest APL-effect loss in the table is more than twice the floor, and most columns sit at the bouton baseline's level: the per-claw threshold, the oracle gain, the structure targets, the interpretable bounds and KC-spike-driven APL were built for other statistics and left this one where it was, the reference model included (what its larger mean effect gains over the bouton baseline, its pattern loses). Only the first joint fit, the two APL-effect fits and the last column do clearly better inside the realism bands, all four of them (next paragraph); the 70 Hz joint fit with the structure targets does worst.

In every column APL moves the pairs apart less than it does in the flies: outside the last two columns the mean effect is below the lower end of the data's 90 % interval ({{data:apl_effect_mean.lo ~ +.3f}}), two thirds of the data's in the APL-effect fit without a firing ceiling and at most a little over half in the others. In all but four columns (the current reference model, the two APL-effect fits and the last) this shortfall, not the pattern, is the larger part of the loss.

For the first joint fit, the APL-effect fit of its family and the 40 Hz fits with the oracle gain, most of it belongs to the comparison of raw spike counts with a calcium signal and not to the models: compressed as the indicator compresses them, their counts give a mean effect inside the flies' interval, while the others, the last two columns apart, stay below it ([the main target under a compressive readout](#readout), at the end of this section); with the firing ceiling the raw counts themselves give it ([the firing ceiling for the KCs](#firing-ceiling)). That agreement is with the recordings as measured, and the models reach it with their responders alone, where a third of the flies' mean effect comes from products with values below the response criterion (same subsection).

They also reach it with more broadly responding KCs with APL off than the flies have (the row on KCs responding to eight or more odors), and in the three columns checked, the current reference model, the APL-effect fit and its re-fit with the firing ceiling, these are the many-claw KCs: about a third of the responses that removing APL adds go to the {{E72/release.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3:frac_kcs_9+ ~ .0%}} of KCs with nine or more claws. A threshold scaled to each KC's input moves the release off those cells at a cost on the main target, and a fit then makes as many broad responders from other cells ([the input-scaled KC threshold](#input-scaled-threshold), at the end of this section).

The flies' own effect rests on broadly responding KCs too: split by the number of odors each KC responds to, most of it sits in the KCs that respond to eight or more odors when APL output is blocked, and the part below the response criterion is for the most part the weaker responses of broadly responding KCs to their other odors ([the APL effect split by odors per KC](#apl-effect-by-class), at the end of this section).

Counted by the recordings' own criterion, in their z-scored units, most of the rest sits in a second kind of KC, those that respond to four to seven odors, which the models lack. With each KC's responses in baseline-noise units, the unit of the realism bands, there is no second kind: the KCs at eight or more odors carry the flies' effect alone, as they do in the models ([the data side of the main target](#data-side), further down in this section). The columns with the larger mean effects all carry breadth-weighted APL (in the breadth-weighted APL experiment the mean effect grew with the breadth exponent at unchanged response rates), though not every column that carries it has one.

The pattern is no closer. ρ on the per-pair APL effect stays well under its ceiling in every column; the per-claw threshold and breadth-weighted APL each lift it from the bouton baseline's, and the two 40 Hz fits with the gain on all eight glomeruli, the reference model among them, have the lowest values. Nor has a positive ρ lowered any loss yet: with the means removed, no column's pattern part is clearly below the data's own standard deviation across pairs ({{data:apl_effect_sd ~ .3f}}), which is what a model with the same effect on every pair would score, and in the columns with breadth-weighted APL and no firing ceiling it is well above it ({{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E34_gain_bounded;tag=thr40_gain1.5_k2_cap3:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse_centered ~ .3f}} for the reference model; {{E69/stats_variants.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse_centered ~ .3f}} with the ceiling).

There the effect is spread over the pairs more unevenly than in the flies ({{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E34_gain_bounded;tag=thr40_gain1.5_k2_cap3:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_sd_ratio ~ .1f}} times the flies' spread for the reference model, {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E69_kc_firing_ceiling;tag=rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_sd_ratio ~ .1f}} times with the ceiling; the row on the spread), and that is why a positive ρ has not lowered the pattern part: a model's pattern part falls below the score of an effect with no pattern only when its spread, as a multiple of the flies', is less than twice its Pearson r, which at the spreads of these columns would take a correlation near the ceiling ([how the pattern part is split](#fn-pattern-split)).

In every column without the ceiling some pairs move closer with APL on, which no pair does in the flies; which pairs, through which KCs, and what the breadth weighting has to do with it is taken up [at the end of this section](#apl-effect-parts). Two columns are outside the band on the response-rate ratio, both with KC–KC inhibition at 100: the inhibition that remains without APL keeps the response rate from doubling when APL is removed, as it does in the flies (the row of response-rate ratios further down), so the low loss of the breadth 3 column does not count.

The fourth band, on the number of odors each KC responds to, puts three of the fourteen model columns outside: the bouton baseline, with APL on and with APL off, and the two columns with KC–KC inhibition at 100, with APL off, which are outside the band on the ratio as well (the realism row; the three rows under it give every column's distance from the flies' distribution and the two ends of that distribution). One column is at its limit with APL on, the per-claw threshold at 70 Hz with the oracle gain ({{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E27_glomerulus_gain;tag=oracle_g1.5:opk_on_tv ~ .3f}} against {{data:noise_ctrl_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .3f}}), and of the columns inside it the first joint fit is the nearest to the limit with APL off ({{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E10_joint_fit;tag=k2:opk_off_tv ~ .3f}} against {{data:noise_tnt_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .3f}}).

Inside the band or outside it, the models' responses with APL off sit in fewer KCs than the flies': in every column close to half of the KCs or more respond to none of the 16 odors, against {{data:noise_tnt_odors_per_kc_0 ~ .0%}} in the flies with APL output blocked (TNT), and the KCs that respond to between one and seven odors are too few to match; in the current reference model and in the two APL-effect fits more KCs than in the flies respond to eight or more.

Part of this is the operating point. Eleven columns are tuned to 5 % of KCs responding with APL on, which leaves fewer responses to spread than the flies have and more silent KCs in both conditions, and this band, unlike the band on the ratio, is on the distribution itself and makes no allowance for it. The two reference-model columns are the same fit at the two operating points: the re-fit at the flies' response rate takes the distance from the flies' distribution from {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E34_gain_bounded;tag=thr40_gain1.5_k2_cap3:opk_on_tv ~ .2f}} to {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3:opk_on_tv ~ .2f}} with APL on and from {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E34_gain_bounded;tag=thr40_gain1.5_k2_cap3:opk_off_tv ~ .2f}} to {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3:opk_off_tv ~ .2f}} with APL off, inside the band at both operating points.

The rest is the model. At the flies' overall response rates the current reference model still leaves about half of its KCs silent with APL off and has a larger share responding to eight or more odors than the flies have: removing APL brings in about half as many new KCs as it does in the flies and makes more of the responding ones broad; the band, set by the most atypical recording, allows that much. Eleven columns are inside all four bands, every fitted model of the table among them, so the bands do not separate the columns that are ahead on the main target from the others: the first joint fit, the last column and the two APL-effect fits are all inside.

Without a firing ceiling the APL-effect fit has the lowest loss in the table but the last column's and that of its own re-fit with the ceiling, and the lowest of the columns without a ceiling once the two highest-firing KCs are left out (the row under the loss, which was not computed for the column with the ceiling) ([the APL-effect fits](#apl-effect-fits)). With the ceiling it has the lowest loss in the table, on raw spike counts nearly what it has under the calibrated readout, with less than half the block of the fit without it and no change in which KCs respond with APL off ([the firing ceiling for the KCs](#firing-ceiling)).

Read as the recordings themselves were made, each KC's signal in units of its own standard deviation over the session, the saved models keep nearly the order that the calibrated readout gives them, and fitted under that reading the fit without a ceiling and the fit with one end level, at the loss that the first has under the readout ([the per-KC normalization of the recordings](#per-kc-normalization), at the end of this section). Of the saved models, {{lit:423 of the 918 # counted in results/apl_effect/by_variant.csv as written 2026-11-10 18:27: rows with a non-empty realism_flag, of all rows}} scored are outside at least one band, {{lit:197 # counted in results/apl_effect/by_variant.csv as written 2026-11-10 18:27: rows whose realism_flag names only odors per KC}} of them on this band alone.

The bands also do not see where APL acts. In the breadth-2 family of the APL-effect fits, to which the third column from the end belongs, most of what APL does to the KCs' input is done at the PN boutons. On the eight wirings on which the family has been fitted ([the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population)), {{E94/a1_path.csv:wiring=P2:bouton_share ~ .2f}} to {{E94/a1_path.csv:wiring=real:bouton_share ~ .2f}} of the drive that APL removes from the claws is removed at the boutons, as a subtraction that is nearly the same for every odor, where the connectome puts a fraction of {{E94/a2_connectome.csv:set=calyx, all:share_pn ~ .3f}} to {{E94/a2_connectome.csv:set=calyx, assigned, KCs with a type:share_pn ~ .3f}} of APL's calyx synapses on PN boutons.

The family's match needs that path at about its fitted strength. Through the calibrated readout the pattern part of the mean over four wirings is {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} as fitted. It is {{E94/equal.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d0.1:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} higher with the path at a tenth of its fitted strength, the setting nearest the connectome's share, and {{diff:E94/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E94/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}} higher when the family is fitted again with the path held there, while half the fitted strength is inside the margin of an equal and a strength above the bound reads worse ([the PN boutons' share of APL's inhibition](#bouton-share), at the end of this section).

Most of the refit's cost belongs to how the family's APL weights the KCs and not to the site: with a part of the APL→KC weights that is the same on every claw, which the connectome's own weights are not, the family fitted again with the path held there is {{diff:E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}} higher than as fitted, just outside the margin of an equal ([APL's inhibition as a static threshold raise per KC](#static-threshold), at the end of this section). With weights that the connectome has in that part's place, the synapses that APL makes on the KCs outside their claws, which the model's weights leave out, the refit is {{diff:E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}} higher than as fitted, and its mean APL effect is {{E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} where the family as fitted has {{E96/readings.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} ([APL's synapses on the KCs outside the claws](#offclaw-synapses), at the end of this section).

At fixed scales, what loses the mean with counted weights is that KCs with the same number of claws get unequal amounts, which do not follow what the bouton path takes from each KC either; that a KC's amount grows with its number of claws less than in proportion loses none of it, and for the weights on the claws how the synapses lie over a KC's claws loses little of it through the calibrated readout, so that no part made of each KC's counted synapses holds the mean ([the evenness of APL's weights among KCs and over a KC's claws](#weight-evenness), at the end of this section).

A share of synapses is not a share of inhibition, so that this is a note on the family's realism beside the bands and not a band, and whether a limit on the bouton share replaces the bound on the APL→bouton scale is a choice still to be made. The share has been measured for this family only, and not for the other columns of the table.

Nor do the bands see what kind of inhibition the family's APL is. What it takes from a KC's drive is nearly the same for every odor, and with the whole APL replaced by a fixed inhibition of each KC that is present only with APL on, the mean over four wirings reads {{E95/equal.csv:variant=C2_bcko:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} to {{E95/equal.csv:variant=C1_bck:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} higher in the pattern part through the calibrated readout and, with one amount per KC, no higher on raw counts.

For the main target the family's APL is thus close to a threshold difference per KC between the two conditions, where in the flies' own responses the inhibition grows with an odor's response over all KCs ([the form of APL's inhibition in the flies' own responses](#inhibition-form)). This too is a description of this family alone, beside the bands and not one of them ([APL's inhibition as a static threshold raise per KC](#static-threshold)).

A third description comes from APL's own activity, imaged in the flies together with the KCs' dendrites in the calyx. There the flies' APL responds {{lit:3.69 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/c_x2_flies.csv (the table opens with a caveat line, which the filler does not read, so the value is entered by hand): row flies=L, reading=carrying, b_mult=0, ratio_id=r1, quantity=APL; column readings, the point estimate at pa @ -3.806, as printed there ~ .2f}} to {{lit:5.28 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/c_x2_flies.csv (the table opens with a caveat line, which the filler does not read, so the value is entered by hand): row flies=L, reading=carrying, b_mult=0, ratio_id=r1, quantity=APL; column readings, the point estimate at pa @ -2, as printed there ~ .2f}} times as strongly to pa as to ms, where the family's APL, read in proportion, responds {{E101/a3_x2_summary.csv:wiring=M2;ratio_id=r1;estimate=ms;baseline=blank:apl_linear ~ .2f}} to {{E101/a3_x2_summary.csv:wiring=real;ratio_id=r1;estimate=ms;baseline=blank:apl_linear ~ .2f}} times as strongly. The family's flatness is set before its APL, which follows the summed input to the claws: with Hallem's receptor data as the input the same fits give {{E101/c4_hallem_ratios.csv:wiring=M1;series=pa over ms;log10_conc=-4.0;cond=on;quantity=APL:linear ~ .2f}} to {{E101/c4_hallem_ratios.csv:wiring=real;series=pa over ms;log10_conc=-2.0;cond=on;quantity=APL:linear ~ .2f}}.

By the rule fixed beforehand the family is inside the flies' interval, which is wide, through the steepest readings of the indicator, and the quality of those recordings has not yet been checked by the experimenter who made them, so that this too stands beside the bands and is not one of them ([the flies' APL against their KC claws in the dual-colour recordings](#apl-vs-claws), at the end of this section).

A fourth is a verdict fixed beforehand, on recordings of APL alone. From paa at 10^-4 to paa at 10^-5 the flies' APL falls to {{E98/comparison_table.csv:comparison=V2, paa at 10^-5 from validation2/diag:flies_lo90 ~ .2f}} to {{E98/comparison_table.csv:comparison=V2, paa at 10^-5 from validation2/diag:flies_hi90 ~ .2f}} of its response (the interval over resampled flies), and the family's, read in proportion, to {{E98/comparison_table.csv:comparison=V2, paa at 10^-5 from validation2/diag:model_linear_min ~ .2f}} to {{E98/comparison_table.csv:comparison=V2, paa at 10^-5 from validation2/diag:model_linear_max ~ .2f}}: flatter than the flies on all eight wirings, under every reading that the measurement leaves open, and against recordings with the concentrations in shuffled order as well. Across odors near the panel's concentration the same recordings decide less, since the class of paa against ms turns on which estimate of ms's ORN input the model is given.

A further series of the same genotype, held out from every rule and read since, does not settle it from the flies' side: the family is inside those flies' interval under every estimate, the series of recordings disagree about how strongly APL responds to ms, and a ratio between two odors read from one pair of vials is known to no better than a factor of about one and a half, so that across odors the flies' APL does not at present say whether the family's is too even or too uneven ([the flies' APL across odors in the held-out vial series](#apl-held-out), at the end of this section).

At six weak odors the same question has been put to further recordings of APL alone, whose quality the experimenter who made them has not checked. Read in proportion the family's APL keeps {{E100/score_weak_table.csv:set=W;stimulus=4h-ol @ -6:family_linear_min_blank ~ .2f}} to {{E100/score_weak_table.csv:set=W;stimulus=farn @ -2:family_linear_max_blank ~ .2f}} of its response to paa at 10^-3 there, where the flies' APL keeps {{E100/score_weak_table.csv:set=W;stimulus=paa @ -5:flies_ratio ~ .2f}} to {{E100/score_weak_table.csv:set=W;stimulus=farn @ -2:flies_ratio ~ .2f}}. By the rule fixed beforehand the family is inside the flies' interval, through the steeper readings of the indicator and with one session's estimate of the input sufficing, so that this too is a description beside the bands ([the flies' APL at the weak odors and at the panel's concentrations](#apl-weak-odors), at the end of this section).

A weaker normalization in the model's antennal lobe is the one change read so far that moves the fall towards the flies'. Fitted again with it at the strength that the flies' APL asks for, the family pays a small price on the pattern part, its mean APL effect on raw counts comes close to the flies', and fewer of its KCs respond at low concentration ([the antennal lobe's normalization at the strength the flies' APL asks for](#al-normalization), at the end of this section). This too is a note on the family's realism beside the bands and not a band ([the strength of APL's response in the flies against the model's APL](#apl-strength), at the end of this section).

The last column holds the lowest APL-effect loss in the table among the models saved before the main target was fitted directly, and held the lowest of any model on the real wiring until then ([the APL-effect fits](#apl-effect-fits)). It was chosen as the lowest inside the three bands on the response rates, and it is inside the fourth, on the number of odors each KC responds to, as well. It is the 70 Hz fit of the reference model's family with the oracle gain kept on DM1 alone, every fitted scale held and the somatic threshold re-tuned to the fit's response rate, one of the variants of [the oracle gain decomposed by glomerulus](#gain-decomposition).

Among the columns without a firing ceiling its mean effect is the only one inside the data's 90 % interval, at the reference model's response rates, so the larger effect is not bought with the overall response rates, and its ρ on the per-pair APL effect is the highest. Its loss is then almost all pattern (a pattern part of {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E39_gain_decomposition;tag=thr70__only_DM1:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse_centered ~ .3f}} in a loss of {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E39_gain_decomposition;tag=thr70__only_DM1:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}}), and that part is within the range of the other columns with breadth-weighted APL, not below it.

What the larger effect does come with is a response with APL off that sits in fewer KCs. The same fit with the gain removed everywhere is {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E39_gain_decomposition;tag=thr70__none:opk_off_tv ~ .2f}} from the flies' distribution of odors per KC with APL off (the band is {{data:noise_tnt_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .2f}}), at a loss of {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E39_gain_decomposition;tag=thr70__none:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}}; the gain on DM1 lowers the loss and takes the distance to {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E39_gain_decomposition;tag=thr70__only_DM1:opk_off_tv ~ .2f}}, with more KCs silent and more responding to eight or more odors. In the 70 Hz family and in the 40 Hz family alike, the variant with the gain on DM1 alone has both the lowest loss of the decomposition and the largest distance from the flies' distribution with APL off. The distance stays inside the band, so the loss counts.

The rows further down the column show what it gives up: the lowest ρ on odor-odor distances of any column, with APL on and with APL off, a block under half the data's and a negative natural-source alignment with APL off. Its matrices (the button in the bottom row opens each column's APL-on and APL-off matrices and their difference, under the KC data's) show how a low loss and poor matrices go together: 2-but, paa and B-myr nearly coincide in both conditions, as [in the reference model](#gap-pairs), and a pair that is equally wrong with APL on and with APL off costs this loss nothing.

The column is also a selection after the fact, the best of the decomposition's variants on this statistic, with a gain set by hand. The same variant of the 40 Hz fit is the lowest of its family too ({{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E39_gain_decomposition;tag=thr40__only_DM1:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} against the reference model's {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E34_gain_bounded;tag=thr40_gain1.5_k2_cap3:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}}), so DM1's part is not an accident of the selection, but the column is a lead for a fit, not a result: a lead on raw spike counts only (under [the compressive readout](#readout) it is the one column whose loss rises).

It also rests on two of the model's {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E39_gain_decomposition;tag=thr70__only_DM1:n_kcs ~ .0f}} KCs: with the two that fire most with APL on left out of both conditions after the fact, nothing simulated again, its loss is {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E39_gain_decomposition;tag=thr70__only_DM1:raw__top2__rmse ~ .3f}} (the row under the loss), above the first joint fit's, which the same leave-out leaves at {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E10_joint_fit;tag=k2:raw__top2__rmse ~ .3f}}. In every other column the loss stays where it was or falls with the two KCs left out, most in the three 40 Hz fits with the oracle gain, whose mean effect a few such KCs hold down ([the high-firing KCs that survive APL](#high-firing-kcs), at the end of this section).

The fit that the column was a lead for has since been run, among [the APL-effect fits](#apl-effect-fits): with the same per-claw threshold and the gain on DM1 alone, fitted on raw counts at the flies' response rate, the model reaches {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=thr70_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplraw_k2_cap3_DM1:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} inside all four bands, the lowest loss on raw counts of those fits, by giving up the block; it rests on a few KCs as the column does, and it loses that lead once the flies' trial-to-trial noise is put into the model.

Among the models on the real wiring saved before those fits that are scored on all four bands and inside them, the column's loss is the lowest; without any glomerulus gain the lowest is {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E10_joint_fit;tag=k3:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}}, that of the first joint fit's family at breadth exponent 3, which is at the limit of the fourth band with APL off ({{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E10_joint_fit;tag=k3:opk_off_tv ~ .3f}} from the flies' distribution, the band's own value to three decimals; the first joint fit itself, at {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E10_joint_fit;tag=k2:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}}, is inside it); the APL-effect fit of the third column from the end is a little below that, well inside all four bands and without a gain ({{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}}). Breadth-weighted APL alone on the bouton baseline has about the same loss ({{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E12_breadth_apl;tag=spikes_k2:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}}) and is outside the band with APL off, as the bouton baseline is: the weighting leaves the model with APL off as it was.

A few single draws of shuffled wirings have losses inside all four bands as low as the lowest of the APL-effect fits (the lowest {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E47_wiring_features;tag=A_thr40_gain1.5_claw_permutation-seed5_retuned:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}}), below the last column's, with a larger mean effect than the real wiring gives at the same parameters ([about half of that difference is a few high-firing KCs of the real wiring](#high-firing-kcs)); they are controls, not candidate models.

The two mechanisms fix complementary things: the per-claw threshold sets the decorrelation level and the APL-off structure; breadth-weighted APL with KC–KC inhibition sets the block and the control-matrix ρ. The threshold × breadth × KC–KC grid combined them and they add: its block-first point is the first model with the data's decorrelation level, control excess profile and block together, at the cost of the response-rate ratio, the per-odor response rates and monotonicity; its balanced point (threshold 40, breadth 2, KC–KC 30) keeps the per-odor response rates and monotonicity with a smaller block. The joint fit then showed the response-rate ratio is recoverable by rebalancing APL between claws and boutons, but, so far, only without the per-claw threshold.

No model yet has the APL output blocked (TNT) matrix right (ρ on odor-odor distances at most {{E106/archive_summary.csv:scope=inside the bands;subset=all120:max_off ~ .2f}} among the saved models inside the realism bands, against a ceiling of {{data:tnt_ceiling ~ .2f}}; once the threshold is on, its non-ester pairs share too little), and these, with the per-odor response-rate pattern, are the remaining gaps. They point at the input side (the five weak-input odors analysed above) and at a stronger or differently distributed APL rather than at more KC mechanisms of the kind tested so far.

For the best family of the later fits the gap in the agreement with both KC matrices has since been taken apart ([the gap in ρ on odor-odor distances read by what could close it](#gap-parts)). Most of it is in the distances that the two conditions share and follows the ORN input, and the smaller part is in APL's effect.

### The main target under a compressive readout of the model's spike counts {#readout}

**Compressed as the calcium indicator compresses them, the best models' spike counts give the flies' mean effect.** A model's distances are cosines on raw spike counts, the flies' on a nuclear calcium signal that compresses large responses. A few high-firing KCs dominate the model's cosines with APL on and off alike (the 1 % of KCs that respond most to an odor hold {{E65/model_amplitude.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3:top1_share_on ~ .0%}} of its summed squared responses in the current reference model, {{E65/data_amplitude_summary.csv:genotype=TNT3c:top1_share_all ~ .0%}} in the control flies) and hide what removing APL recruits. The compressive readout of the model's spike counts re-scored every saved model through a saturating function, n / (n + k), with k set on its APL-on counts alone so that an odor's response is spread over the responding KCs as in the control flies, and kept for APL off.

The current reference model and the first joint fit, each on its raw spike counts and on the same counts through [the calibrated saturating readout](#fn-calibrated-readout) (half-saturation k of {{E65/key_models.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3;readout=saturating_cal_pr:param ~ .1f}} and {{E65/key_models.csv:folder=E10_joint_fit;tag=k2;readout=saturating_cal_pr:param ~ .1f}} spikes); the readout changes no response rate

Both models' mean effects move from below the flies' 90 % interval to inside it and their losses nearly halve. What remains is pattern ([taken apart by odor and by pair in the next subsection](#apl-effect-parts)): ρ on the per-pair APL effect stays far from its ceiling and neither pattern part is below the score of an effect with no pattern.

Other calibrated readouts, a power law among them, change little (a loss between {{E65/key_models.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3;readout=power_cal_pr:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} and {{E65/key_models.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3;readout=saturating_cal_pr_all:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} for the reference model). Every column of the best-models table improves except the last, whose loss rises ({{E65/key_models.csv:folder=E39_gain_decomposition;tag=thr70__only_DM1;readout=raw:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} to {{E65/key_models.csv:folder=E39_gain_decomposition;tag=thr70__only_DM1;readout=saturating_cal_pr:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}}) as its pattern worsens, and the first joint fit is the lowest of the {{E65/readout_summary.csv:readout=saturating_cal_pr:n_realistic ~ .0f}} models saved before the APL-effect fits and inside the three bands on the response rates (its family, fitted to the main target, goes lower still: [the APL-effect fits](#apl-effect-fits)).

The fourth band, on the number of odors each KC responds to, is not applied in this subsection or the next, whose counts and medians are over models inside those three. No readout would change a model's standing on it: the readout alters how much each responding KC weighs, not which KCs respond, and both models of the table are inside it with APL off, the first joint fit near its limit ({{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E10_joint_fit;tag=k2:opk_off_tv ~ .2f}} from the flies' distribution for the first joint fit and {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3:opk_off_tv ~ .2f}} for the current reference model, against a band of {{data:noise_tnt_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .2f}}).

The readout supplies these models' mean effect; it leaves the spread of their responses over the KCs with APL off as it was. Over those models the median mean effect rises only from {{E65/readout_summary.csv:readout=raw:median_mean_effect ~ +.3f}} to {{E65/readout_summary.csv:readout=saturating_cal_pr:median_mean_effect ~ +.3f}}: the lift grows with the APL-off / APL-on response-rate ratio, which the readout leaves alone (figure).

![Each saved model inside the three bands on the response rates (the band on odors per KC is not applied): its mean APL effect against its APL-off / APL-on response-rate ratio, on raw spike counts (grey) and through the calibrated saturating readout (blue; calibrated to the control flies' participation ratio, the effective share of the responding KCs that carries an odor's response). Horizontal lines: the flies' mean effect as measured, with sub-threshold responses set to 0 and corrected for trial-to-trial noise by the correction then in use (the dotted line, which is too high: without the trial noise the mean effect is hardly above the solid line of the effect as measured); vertical line: the flies' response-rate ratio.](results/E65_spike_count_readout/E65_mean_effect_vs_rate_ratio.png)

**The cost is the gain models' block.** Under the readout the block of both models, and of nearly every model built on the glomerulus gain, all but disappears, while the flies' block survives binarizing the recordings ({{lit:+0.047 # the block of the two KC matrices computed from binarized responses (trial mean > 1): kc_remapping_harness.compare_on_off on yang_mean_rdm(binarize=1.0) of the control flies and of APL output blocked (TNT), 0.0474; the KC data's binarized column of the cost table in E65_spike_count_readout.md}} against {{data:block ~ +.3f}} as measured): these models make the block with the amplitude of a few hard-driven KCs ([identified at the end of this section](#high-firing-kcs)), the flies with which KCs respond. The blocks that survive are mostly those of mechanisms acting on the response set (the breadth × shared-input APL rule, panel-general glomerulus scores, the oracle co-responder suppression), whose losses stay above these two models'. The APL-off distances and the natural-source alignment fall too.

**Below the response criterion the recordings are not empty, and what is there is mostly signal.** In the recordings a KC counts as responding to an odor when its mean over the three trials is above 1 in the recordings' z-scored units (1 z); everything at or below that is sub-threshold. A model KC without a spike reads exactly 0, on raw counts and through the readout alike, while in the control flies {{E65/data_amplitude_summary.csv:genotype=TNT3c:share_subthreshold ~ .0%}} of an odor's squared response vector lies in sub-threshold trial means, {{E65/data_amplitude_summary.csv:genotype=TNT3c:share_negative ~ .0%}} in negative ones.

The low end of the readout asked what those values are, whether a model's scores change when its readout is given the same low end, and whether the model holds such values under its spike threshold ([how each step was done](#fn-readout-low-end)). They are mostly signal, not measurement noise. Entries picked by their mean over two trials come back on the third: the weakly positive ones (0.3 to 1 z) at {{E68/data_cv_by_genotype.csv:genotype=TNT3c;band=(0.3, 1]:reproducible_share ~ .0%}} of that mean in the control flies and {{E68/data_cv_by_genotype.csv:genotype=TNT;band=(0.3, 1]:reproducible_share ~ .0%}} with APL output blocked (TNT), the negative ones (at or below −0.3 z) at {{E68/data_cv_by_genotype.csv:genotype=TNT3c;band=(-inf, -0.3]:reproducible_share ~ .0%}} and {{E68/data_cv_by_genotype.csv:genotype=TNT;band=(-inf, -0.3]:reproducible_share ~ .0%}}.

Blocking APL output nearly doubles the share of weak values, while the share of strong ones barely rises and the responders' mean amplitude does not change (the KC data column of the table of amplitudes further down). The negative values are more frequent for the odors with more responders, in the control flies and with APL output blocked (TNT) alike (a Spearman correlation across odors of {{E68/data_neg_by_genotype.csv:genotype=TNT3c:rho_within_recording_mean ~ .2f}} and {{E68/data_neg_by_genotype.csv:genotype=TNT:rho_within_recording_mean ~ .2f}} within a recording), so they are not a mark of APL's output.

A pair's cosine similarity is a sum over KCs, and each KC's part belongs to one of three terms: both of its entries responders, one a responder and the other sub-threshold, or both sub-threshold. Of the flies' mean APL effect of {{data:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}}, {{E68/data_effect_terms.csv:both__effect_mean:observed ~ +.3f}} is in the first term, {{E68/data_effect_terms.csv:one__effect_mean:observed ~ +.3f}} in the second (90 % interval {{E68/data_effect_terms.csv:one__effect_mean:lo ~ +.3f}} to {{E68/data_effect_terms.csv:one__effect_mean:hi ~ +.3f}}) and {{E68/data_effect_terms.csv:neither__effect_mean:observed ~ +.3f}} in the third; of the effect's pattern across the 120 pairs, {{E68/data_effect_terms.csv:both__pattern_share:observed ~ .0%}} is in the first. The sub-threshold values thus carry about a third of how far APL moves odors apart in the flies, and a tenth of which pairs it moves most.

**Giving the model's readout that low end leaves its scores where they were.** Two additions to the calibrated readout were tried on every saved model.

- One is measurement noise: the control flies' trial-to-trial standard deviation of non-responding entries ({{data:ctrl_trial_noise_sd ~ .2f}} z per trial) added to the readout's values, in simulated recordings of three trials.
- The other is a one-spike floor, an offset b in (n + b) / (n + b + k) for every KC with at least one spike, so that the weight of a single spike is calibrated instead of following from k.

The half-saturation k, the offset and the conversion of the readout's values to z are set together, on the model's APL-on counts through the noise, on three values of the control flies: the response rate under the recordings' criterion, the share of entries between 0.5 and 1.5 z and the participation ratio among responders. Each reading of the recordings is scored against the same reading of the model.

The additions move the reference model's loss by less than 0.01 under every reading but one, and under the target as defined they do not lower it: the noise lifts the model's mean effect a little further above the flies', the one-spike floor calibrates to a small offset ({{E68/key_models.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3;config=floor;reading=graded:floor ~ .2f}} spikes) and adds nothing, and the pattern part is where it was ({{E68/key_models.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3;config=cal;reading=graded:rmse_centered ~ .3f}} as defined, {{E68/key_models.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3;config=floor_noise;reading=graded:rmse_centered ~ .3f}} with both). The exception is the reading with negative values set to 0, where cutting away the negative half of the added noise brings the model's mean effect down to the flies'; that is the clipping, not the model.

The first joint fit moves as little under the target as defined (a loss of {{E68/key_models.csv:folder=E10_joint_fit;tag=k2;config=cal;reading=graded:rmse ~ .3f}} as defined and {{E68/key_models.csv:folder=E10_joint_fit;tag=k2;config=floor_noise;reading=graded:rmse ~ .3f}} with both). Over the {{E68/medians.csv:config=floor_noise;reading=graded:n ~ .0f}} saved models inside the three bands on the response rates in which the recordings' response rate can be reached, the median loss goes from {{E68/medians.csv:config=cal;reading=graded:loss ~ .3f}} to {{E68/medians.csv:config=floor_noise;reading=graded:loss ~ .3f}} and the order of the models by loss is largely kept (a Spearman correlation of {{E68/medians.csv:config=floor_noise;reading=graded:order_rho_vs_cal ~ .2f}} between the two orders). The readout therefore stays as defined, with no measurement noise and no one-spike floor.

**With APL off the models add strong responders where the flies add weak ones.** In the flies the products of a responder with a sub-threshold entry grow when APL output is blocked; in the reference model they do not (last row of the table below), and the membrane potential was the place to look for the missing values.

Six models, the reference model and the first joint fit among them, were simulated again at their fitted parameters with every KC's membrane potential saved (the spike counts are those of the saved runs), and the readout was given two more terms, calibrated on the control flies with APL on as the rest is: for a KC without a spike, a weight times its mean depolarization during the odor; for every non-responding KC, a weight times its mean hyperpolarization, subtracted. The weights are set so that the model with APL on has the control flies' shares of weakly positive entries (0.25 to 1 z) and of negative ones (below −0.25 z).

With APL on, the reference model read through the noise is close to the flies' amplitudes above 0.5 z (figure below). With APL off it is not. What blocking APL output adds in the flies is weak: the share between 0.5 and 1.5 z nearly doubles, and the share above 4 z and the responders' mean amplitude hardly move. What removing APL adds in the model is strong: about five times the flies' share above 4 z, and a mean amplitude more than a third higher than with APL on.

The potential terms do not supply the weak values. The depolarization term calibrates to almost nothing in four of the six models, the reference model among them: the measurement noise alone already puts more of the model's APL-on entries between 0.25 and 1 z ({{E68/partB_amplitude.csv:model=ref40;config=floor_noise:share_025_1_on ~ .1%}}) than the control flies have ({{data:ctrl_share_z_025_1 ~ .1%}}), which leaves the term nothing to supply. The hyperpolarization term gives the model the flies' negative values with APL on and, with APL off, more of them where the flies have fewer: in five of the six models removing APL makes more KCs fire, and their KC–KC inhibition hyperpolarizes the rest.

The cosine term that grows in the flies turns negative (last row), and the terms add strongly negative values that the flies do not have. Where a loss falls with the potential terms it falls with the mean effect, and in every model the same terms do as well or better with the potential shuffled across the non-spiking KCs or with the APL-on potential used for both conditions, so nothing in the potential's own pattern helps.

The missing low end is therefore not hidden under the model's spike threshold. It is missing from what the model recruits when APL is removed, in all six models: strong responses where the flies have weak ones.

What the weak values carry of the flies' APL effect sits for the most part in broadly responding KCs, as their weaker responses to their other odors, not in cells that respond weakly throughout ([the APL effect split by odors per KC](#apl-effect-by-class), at the end of this section). The realism bands hold a model to which KCs respond, not to how strongly, and do not see this; it is taken up with the pending work at the end of the page.

**The target's definition is open, and the readout's match of the mean depends on it.** How the recordings are read moves the flies' mean effect by about half of what the readout moves a model's: over the readings of the table of readings above it runs from {{data:apl_effect_thresholded_mean ~ +.3f}} with sub-threshold values set to 0 to the {{data:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}} of the recordings as measured, and without the trial noise it is {{data:noise_free_apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}} by the estimate across repeats (the {{data:apl_effect_noise_corrected_mean ~ +.3f}} of the table's fourth row comes from the noise correction then in use, which is too high: [the flies' variability across the three repeats](#repeat-structure)).

The model's mean effect does not follow: setting the sub-threshold values to 0 lowers the flies' mean effect by a quarter and leaves the reference model's where it was, because the model makes its mean effect with its responders alone. Through the calibrated readout the products of two responding entries give it {{diff:E68/variant_amplitude.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3;config=cal:term_both_off -- E68/variant_amplitude.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3;config=cal:term_both_on ~ +.3f}}, against {{E68/data_effect_terms.csv:both__effect_mean:observed ~ +.3f}} in the flies, and the products of a responder with a sub-threshold entry {{diff:E68/variant_amplitude.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3;config=cal:term_one_off -- E68/variant_amplitude.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3;config=cal:term_one_on ~ +.3f}}, against {{E68/data_effect_terms.csv:one__effect_mean:observed ~ +.3f}}; none of the nine models examined most closely gets any of its mean effect from that second term.

The calibrated readout's agreement with the flies' mean effect therefore holds for the readings that keep the sub-threshold values, the recordings as measured among them, and not for the two that drop them, and where it holds it is reached through the wrong term: with the sub-threshold values set to 0 on both sides, or with both sides binarized, the reference model's mean effect is above the upper end of the flies' 90 % interval for the reading ({{data:apl_effect_thresholded_mean.hi ~ +.3f}} and {{data:apl_effect_binary_mean.hi ~ +.3f}}) and its loss is higher (second and third rows of that table).

Whether a model is held to raw counts or to a calibrated readout, and against which reading of the recordings, is still to be decided; until then both are reported, and the best-models table and the progress plot stay on raw counts and the recordings as measured. Those raw counts are of the model's 0.5 s odor pulse: with the flies' 2 s pulse the numbers of the breadth-2 APL-effect fit get worse on raw counts and not under the readout ([the flies' pulse in the model and the remaining candidates for the common error](#remaining-candidates), at the end of this section).

Read as the flies were recorded, the family with the firing ceiling has its raw-count numbers back once the ceiling's adaptation outlasts the odor, and the family without a ceiling holds only under the readout ([the flies' recording protocol in the model](#flies-protocol), at the end of this section). With a firing ceiling in the model the first of these choices matters little, since its raw counts and the calibrated readout then give nearly the same scores ([the firing ceiling for the KCs](#firing-ceiling), at the end of this section); the reading of the recordings stays open.

A third definition of the model's side has since been taken from how the recordings themselves were made, each model KC's signal put in units of its own standard deviation over a simulated recording; it orders the saved models nearly as the calibrated readout does and not as raw counts do, and which of the three the target is held to is open as well ([the per-KC normalization of the recordings](#per-kc-normalization), at the end of this section).

### The pattern part of the main target, by odor and by pair {#apl-effect-parts}

**The pattern part is a per-odor error and a pair-specific error, and the models are at about twice the data's floor, or more, on each.** Once the readout has supplied the mean, what is left of the best models' loss is its pattern part, and the per-odor profile of the APL effect took that part apart.

Part of a per-pair effect is the sum of two per-odor terms, one for each odor of the pair (an odor's share of the effect in every pair it is in); the rest belongs to the pair alone. In the flies the per-odor terms hold {{E66/data_floor_parts.csv:data=graded;stat=measured_additive_r2:mean ~ .0%}} of the effect's variance across the 120 pairs, and an odor's share follows how much its response fraction rises when APL output is blocked (Pearson r {{E66/data_share_correlates.csv:data=graded;correlate=gain:pearson ~ .2f}} across the 16 odors).

A model's pattern error [is split the same way](#fn-apl-effect-parts): the per-odor part is the error that 16 per-odor terms account for, the pair-specific part is the rest, and their squares add up to the squared pattern part. Each has a floor of its own, from recordings drawn again with replacement, as the loss has.

The two parts are not measured equally firmly. Scored against two random halves of the recordings, on raw spike counts, the saved models keep their order on the pair-specific part (an agreement of {{apl_effect_metrics/split_half_reliability.csv:pair_specific_part:split_half_rho ~ .2f}}, where one is the same order against both halves) far better than on the per-odor part ({{apl_effect_metrics/split_half_reliability.csv:per_odor_part:split_half_rho ~ .2f}}; [the statistics compared](#fn-pattern-split)). What is said below about single odors' shares of an error is therefore a lead to be tested, not a result.

The pattern part of the APL-effect loss and its two parts (lower is better), on raw spike counts / through the calibrated saturating readout; for the KC data, the floor of each with its 90 % interval over the resampled recordings in parentheses

No saved model reaches either floor, and none comes close on both. The per-odor part is about the same in the bouton baseline, in the reference model and in the median saved model, a little over twice its floor, and somewhat lower in the first joint fit; the pair-specific part is the larger of the two in the models built on the joint fits and is what differs between models.

Across the {{E66/parts_summary.csv:readout=raw:n_realistic ~ .0f}} saved models inside the three bands on the response rates the two parts are nearly unrelated (a Spearman correlation of {{E66/parts_summary.csv:readout=raw:spearman_per_odor_vs_pair_specific ~ .2f}} on raw spike counts and {{E66/parts_summary.csv:readout=saturating_cal_pr:spearman_per_odor_vs_pair_specific ~ .2f}} under the calibrated readout), so being good on one says nothing about the other: the lowest per-odor part on raw counts ({{E66/parts_summary.csv:readout=raw:best_apl_effect_per_odor_value ~ .3f}}) is that of the 70 Hz joint fit with the gain on DC2 alone, one of the reduced gain sets, and the lowest pair-specific part ({{E66/parts_summary.csv:readout=raw:best_apl_effect_pair_specific_value ~ .3f}}) that of a claw-permuted wiring from the PN→KC wiring substrate experiment, a control and not a candidate model.
