**Setting every odor's response fraction on the flies' does not lower the loss.** If the per-odor part were the strength of APL's action on each odor, giving every odor the flies' response fraction in both conditions should remove it. [The per-odor rate oracle](#gap-pairs) had done that through the inputs, one condition at a time; here it was done through APL itself, by a second [oracle](#fn-apl-effect-parts): each odor's ORN input was scaled until its response fraction with APL off equals the flies' with APL output blocked (TNT), and that odor's APL→KC and APL→bouton scales were then multiplied by a factor of its own until its response fraction with APL on equals the control flies' (second model column).

The per-odor response rates are then the flies' in both conditions, and the loss is where it was, on raw spike counts and under the calibrated readout. Under the readout the per-odor part falls by about a quarter, still well above its floor, and the pair-specific part rises enough to leave the pattern part where it was; on raw counts neither moves.

The loss does not move either in the two 70 Hz fits of the reference model's family, in the first joint fit (where the oracle is partial: its recruitment with APL off saturates before most odors reach the flies' fraction) or in the reference model with the bounded oracle's searched weak-odor input, nor when the rate oracle's two sets of input scales are read together, one for each condition. How many KCs APL removes for each odor is therefore not what sets the pattern of the APL effect; which KCs two odors share is.

The factors do say what an APL that gave the flies' per-odor response rates would do differently from the model's: {{E66/multipliers.csv:base=thr40_gain1.5;variant=both;odor=eb:multiplier ~ .1f}} times the inhibition on eb and {{E66/multipliers.csv:base=thr40_gain1.5;variant=both;odor=ep:multiplier ~ .1f}} times on ep, half or less on paa, B-myr, euc and 1-5ol and {{E66/multipliers.csv:base=thr40_gain1.5;variant=both;odor=-aPine:multiplier ~ .2f}} times on -aPine in the reference model, less wherever an odor's response with APL off is concentrated in few KCs (a Spearman correlation of {{E66/multiplier_correlates.csv:base=thr40_gain1.5;variant=both;property=off_spike_share_top1:spearman ~ .2f}} across the 16 odors between the factor and the share of the odor's APL-off spikes in its top 1 % of KCs). Imposing that rule does not help the main target, so a per-odor APL rule fitted to the response rates is not pursued; paa's, euc's and -aPine's factors are in part corrections for [an input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations).

**The pair-specific part comes with breadth-weighted APL.** On raw spike counts it is about twice the bouton baseline's in the first joint fit and in the reference model (first table), and in the breadth-weighted APL experiment it rose with the exponent of the spike-total breadth at unchanged response rates (from {{E66/by_variant_parts.csv:folder=E12_breadth_apl;tag=k0;readout=raw:apl_effect_pair_specific ~ .3f}} without the weighting to {{E66/by_variant_parts.csv:folder=E12_breadth_apl;tag=spikes_k3;readout=raw:apl_effect_pair_specific ~ .3f}} at exponent 3). The largest pair-specific errors of the reference model are of two kinds, both through KCs that two odors share by way of one strongly driven glomerulus.

- The small esters eb and ep share with the alcohols 1-8ol and 1-6ol a few KCs, most of them driven through DM5, that keep firing with APL on and then dominate both odors' response vectors: the model's APL brings these pairs closer, where the flies' APL moves them apart by more than it does most pairs (an APL effect of {{E66/worst_pairs.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3;readout=raw;odor_a=eb;odor_b=1-8ol:model_effect ~ +.2f}} for eb / 1-8ol against the flies' {{E66/worst_pairs.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3;readout=raw;odor_a=eb;odor_b=1-8ol:data_effect ~ +.2f}}, half of it carried by {{E66/worst_pairs.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3;readout=raw;odor_a=eb;odor_b=1-8ol:n_kcs_half ~ .0f}} KCs).
- The same esters share with paa and B-myr KCs driven through DM1 and DP1m that respond only with APL off; removing APL adds them to both odors at once, and the effect is too large ({{E66/worst_pairs.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3;readout=raw;odor_a=eb;odor_b=paa:model_effect ~ +.2f}} against {{E66/worst_pairs.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3;readout=raw;odor_a=eb;odor_b=paa:data_effect ~ +.2f}} for eb / paa).

Under the calibrated readout the same pairs lead, with more KCs behind each. DM5, DM1 and DP1m carry the oracle gain, but the first kind of error leads in the first joint fit as well, which has no gain (a pair-specific error of {{E66/worst_pairs.csv:folder=E10_joint_fit;tag=k2;readout=raw;odor_a=eb;odor_b=1-8ol:pair_specific ~ +.2f}} for eb / 1-8ol against the reference model's {{E66/worst_pairs.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3;readout=raw;odor_a=eb;odor_b=1-8ol:pair_specific ~ +.2f}}): it comes with the breadth weighting, and the gain on DM5 enlarges it (among the variants of [the oracle gain decomposed by glomerulus](#gain-decomposition) for the 40 Hz fit, the pair-specific part on raw counts is {{E66/by_variant_parts.csv:folder=E39_gain_decomposition;tag=thr40__full;readout=raw:apl_effect_pair_specific ~ .3f}} with the gain on all eight glomeruli, {{E66/by_variant_parts.csv:folder=E39_gain_decomposition;tag=thr40__loo_DM5;readout=raw:apl_effect_pair_specific ~ .3f}} with DM5's removed and {{E66/by_variant_parts.csv:folder=E39_gain_decomposition;tag=thr40__none;readout=raw:apl_effect_pair_specific ~ .3f}} with none).

**Lowering the breadth exponent trades the pair-specific part against the mean effect and the block.** The breadth exponent is the power of a KC's breadth (its spike total over the 16 odors with APL off) by which breadth-weighted APL scales that KC's APL→KC weight; the reference model was fitted with 2. It was changed in the reference model at otherwise fitted parameters, the APL→KC scale re-tuned to the fitted response rate with APL on, so that the model with APL off is the same in every column (last three columns of the table).

Without the weighting the pair-specific part falls to near the bouton baseline's level, by half on raw spike counts, and on raw counts the mean APL effect and the block all but disappear with it: keeping APL off the high-firing KCs is what moves odors apart overall and makes the block, and where two odors share such KCs it is also the pair-specific error. On raw counts the trade has no good point.

Under the calibrated readout, which supplies the mean by itself, exponent 1 gives the reference model a lower loss than the fitted exponent 2, the lowest of the series, with most of the block on raw counts and the response rates unchanged; it is a one-parameter change of the fitted model and not a fit, and the two 70 Hz fits of the family gain nothing from it (figure). Taking a KC's breadth as the number of odors it responds to, instead of its spike total, raises the pair-specific part less for the same mean effect and gives the lowest loss of the series on raw counts, with a smaller block.

Removing the weighting, or weighting by the number of odors, also concentrates the response with APL on in fewer KCs, which the bands on the response rates do not see; the band on odors per KC counts responders and not their amplitudes, and with APL on every column passes it, the one without the weighting nearest its limit ({{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E66_per_odor_apl_profile;tag=C_thr40_gain1.5_spikes_k0:opk_on_tv ~ .2f}} from the control flies' distribution, against {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E66_per_odor_apl_profile;tag=C_thr40_gain1.5_spikes_k2:opk_on_tv ~ .2f}} as fitted and a band of {{data:noise_ctrl_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .2f}}; a participation ratio among responders of {{E66/parts_bc_table.csv:C_thr40_gain1.5_spikes_k0:participation_ratio_resp_on ~ .1%}} without the weighting, against {{E66/parts_bc_table.csv:O_thr40_gain1.5_untuned:participation_ratio_resp_on ~ .1%}} as fitted and at exponent 1, and {{data:ctrl_participation_ratio_resp ~ .1%}} in the control flies), and that ratio is what the readout is calibrated on.

![The breadth exponent of the APL→KC weights in the three fits of the reference model's family (blue: the current reference model; orange: its 70 Hz fit; green: the 70 Hz fit with the gain at 1.25), with a KC's breadth taken as its spike total with APL off (solid) or as the number of odors it responds to (dashed), and the APL→KC scale re-tuned to each fit's response rate with APL on. Columns: the APL-effect loss, the mean APL effect, the per-odor part and the pair-specific part of the loss; top row on raw spike counts, bottom row through the calibrated saturating readout. Dotted lines: the floor of the loss and the flies' mean effect.](results/E66_per_odor_apl_profile/E66_breadth_exponent.png)

### The main target fitted directly, on raw spike counts and under the readout {#apl-effect-fits}

**Fitted directly, the main target is matched in its mean under the readout but not in its pattern; on raw counts the lower losses are bought with the block, and through the trial noise the fit that keeps the block is the lowest, narrowly.** The APL-effect fits put the APL-effect loss first in the joint fit's loss, the response rates held as constraints, and fit its four parameters from five bases at the flies' response rate, each once under [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout) and once on raw spike counts.

Three of the five bases, each fitted under both definitions, and every fit scored under both (raw: on raw spike counts; calibrated: through the calibrated saturating readout). Three of the fits were run through the trial noise

Under the readout four bases end between {{E67/comparison.csv:kind=fit;tag=rate0.068_aplcal_k3_cap3:cal_loss ~ .3f}} and {{E67/comparison.csv:kind=fit;tag=thr70_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3_DM1:cal_loss ~ .3f}} (the current reference model at {{E67/comparison.csv:kind=fit;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3:cal_loss ~ .3f}}, from {{E65/key_models.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3;readout=saturating_cal_pr:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}}), their mean effects inside the flies' 90 % interval and their losses nearly all pattern; all four are inside the realism bands. The same family at breadth exponent 2, with no per-claw threshold and no glomerulus gain, reaches {{E67/comparison.csv:kind=fit;tag=rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3:cal_loss ~ .3f}}, against a floor of {{data:apl_effect_rmse_floor ~ .3f}} and the {{E65/key_models.csv:folder=E10_joint_fit;tag=k2;readout=saturating_cal_pr:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} of the first joint fit itself, fitted at 5 % to other targets. Its mean effect is the flies', but its pattern part, most of it pair-specific, is no lower than what an effect with no pattern would score ({{data:apl_effect_sd ~ .3f}}), although ρ on the per-pair APL effect is {{E67/comparison.csv:kind=fit;tag=rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3:cal_rho ~ .2f}}.

In the breadth-2 family the definition changes the number, not the model: fitted on raw counts, the same start ends at nearly the same parameters and scores (first two columns). The other bases come apart: fitted on raw counts they give up most or all of their KC–KC inhibition and the block for a larger mean effect, and two then go below the breadth-2 fit on raw counts, the breadth-3 family and the 70 Hz base with the gain on DM1 alone (fourth and last columns).

Through [the matched trial noise](#fn-trial-noise) the order changes. The 70 Hz base's loss rises, and it rests on a few of its KCs ([the next subsection](#high-firing-kcs)). The breadth-3 fit holds, with part of a block coming back, and the breadth-2 fit's loss falls with its block kept, so that it is the lowest of the three, but narrowly: its margin over the breadth-3 fit is about the difference between the two noise levels, on one seed of the noise.

Under the readout the family's lead needs the per-claw threshold absent and a breadth exponent near 2: it ends at {{E67/comparison.csv:kind=fit;tag=rate0.068_aplcal_k1.5_cap3_c2:cal_loss ~ .3f}} and {{E67/comparison.csv:kind=fit;tag=rate0.068_aplcal_k1_cap3_c2:cal_loss ~ .3f}} at exponents 1.5 and 1, and the 40 Hz model without the gain, whose structure differs from it only in the per-claw threshold, ends at {{E67/comparison.csv:kind=fit;tag=thr40_rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3:cal_loss ~ .3f}}, where the reference model does.

Three things remain in the breadth-2 fit: the pair-specific part of the pattern; the block under the readout ({{E67/comparison.csv:kind=fit;tag=rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3:cal_block ~ +.3f}} against the flies' {{data:block ~ +.3f}}), which a block term in the loss does not raise; and the recruitment with APL off, where {{E67/comparison.csv:kind=fit;tag=rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3:opk_off_0 ~ .0%}} of its KCs stay silent against the flies' {{data:noise_tnt_odors_per_kc_0 ~ .0%}}, and a term on odors per KC in the loss moves the distance from the flies' distribution only from {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3:opk_off_tv ~ .3f}} to {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=rate0.068_aplcalopk_k2_cap3:opk_off_tv ~ .3f}} (which KCs are released when APL is removed, and what moving the release costs, is in [the input-scaled KC threshold](#input-scaled-threshold), at the end of this section).

The fit is inside all four realism bands, at the flies' response rates and their ratio; its response rate ρ with APL on is {{E67/comparison.csv:kind=fit;tag=rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}}, against the first joint fit's {{E10:k2:spearman_rate_on_vs_data ~ .2f}}, and its other statistics are in its column of the best-models table. Its somatic threshold ({{E67/comparison.csv:kind=fit;tag=rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3:thr_factor ~ .2f}} of the baseline's) and its APL→bouton scale, near the bound, are hard to defend; each fit is a local search from one start, and the pairs with paa, euc and -aPine rest on [ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations).

Fitted again with a firing ceiling in the model, the same family scores on raw counts nearly as it does under the readout, lower than any fit of this subsection does on raw counts ([the firing ceiling for the KCs](#firing-ceiling)). Fitted again on seven re-drawn wirings, the family ends around the loss it has on the real wiring, and its mean over the wirings is lower ([the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population), at the end of this section).

### The high-firing KCs that survive APL, and what rests on them {#high-firing-kcs}

**On raw spike counts about twenty KCs of the real wiring hold the reference model's mean APL effect down.** The shortfall of the mean APL effect is the larger part of most losses in the best-models table, and at the same fitted scales the reference model's mean effect is larger on shuffled wirings than on the real one.

The pairwise co-input examined in [the wiring experiments](#wiring-feature) is not the reason: with the excess of the over-shared glomerulus pairs removed from the real wiring the mean effect stays at {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E52_glomerulus_pairs;tag=C_thr40_gain1.5_lesion_targeted-seed1_retuned:raw__mean ~ +.3f}} to {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E52_glomerulus_pairs;tag=C_thr40_gain1.5_lesion_targeted-seed2_retuned:raw__mean ~ +.3f}} over three draws, against {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3:raw__mean ~ +.3f}} untouched, and on the six shuffled draws matched to the real wiring on every glomerulus pair's count of shared KCs it is {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E59_coinput_shuffle;tag=M_thr40_gain1.5_curveball_within_type_matched-seed3_retuned:raw__mean ~ +.3f}} to {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E59_coinput_shuffle;tag=M_thr40_gain1.5_curveball_within_type_matched-seed2_retuned:raw__mean ~ +.3f}} (the flies' {{data:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}}). The experiment on the high-firing KCs that survive APL looked for the reason in single cells.

Two sets were fixed before any simulation: a model's high-firing set, its KCs with twenty or more spikes to some odor with APL off, and its survivors, those of them that also reach twenty spikes to some odor with APL on. The current reference model has {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3:n_high_firing ~ .0f}} KCs in the first set and {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3:n_survivors ~ .0f}} survivors, of {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3:n_kcs ~ .0f}} KCs.

With APL on the survivors respond to {{E70/wiring_by_class.csv:key=ref40;kc_class=survivor:n_odors_on ~ .1f}} of the 16 odors each, at {{E70/wiring_by_class.csv:key=ref40;kc_class=survivor:max_count_on ~ .0f}} spikes to their best odor on average, where the rest of the high-firing set responds to {{E70/wiring_by_class.csv:key=ref40;kc_class=high_firing_other:n_odors_on ~ .1f}} odors at {{E70/wiring_by_class.csv:key=ref40;kc_class=high_firing_other:max_count_on ~ .0f}} spikes; they hold {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3:survivor_share_sq_on ~ .0%}} of an odor's summed squared responses with APL on, the quantity a cosine is built from, so with APL on they are the KCs that two odors have in common. Taken apart by class of KC, the model's mean effect of {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3:raw__mean ~ +.3f}} is {{E70/class_parts.csv:key=ref40;readout=raw:effect__survivor ~ +.3f}} from the survivors, {{E70/class_parts.csv:key=ref40;readout=raw:effect__high_firing_other ~ +.3f}} from the rest of the high-firing set and {{E70/class_parts.csv:key=ref40;readout=raw:effect__responder ~ +.3f}} from the other responding KCs.

Eight saved models with KCs left out of both conditions after the fact, nothing simulated again: the two KCs with the largest spike counts with APL on, or the model's survivors. In the rows of the loss and of the mean effect the two values are on raw spike counts / through the calibrated saturating readout, its half-saturation set again on the KCs that are kept; the response rates and the bands are those of the model as saved

**Left out after the fact, the survivors give back about half of what the real wiring lacks on raw counts; under the calibrated readout the same cells keep the mean effect near the flies'.** With its survivors left out the reference model's mean effect on raw counts rises about half of the way to its shuffled wirings' and its loss falls a little (first model column of the table above); the same leave-out on nine shuffled draws of the model (three each of the claw permutation, the within-type claw permutation and the within-type Curveball), where the survivors hold less, moves the mean effect by between {{diff:E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E47_wiring_features;tag=A_thr40_gain1.5_claw_permutation-seed2_retuned:raw__survivors__mean -- E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E47_wiring_features;tag=A_thr40_gain1.5_claw_permutation-seed2_retuned:raw__mean ~ +.3f}} and {{diff:E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E47_wiring_features;tag=A_thr40_gain1.5_curveball_within_type-seed1_retuned:raw__survivors__mean -- E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E47_wiring_features;tag=A_thr40_gain1.5_curveball_within_type-seed1_retuned:raw__mean ~ +.3f}}.

With the whole high-firing set left out the real wiring and the shuffles no longer differ (a loss of {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3:raw__hf_all__rmse ~ .3f}} against {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E47_wiring_features;tag=A_thr40_gain1.5_curveball_within_type-seed3_retuned:raw__hf_all__rmse ~ .3f}} to {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E47_wiring_features;tag=A_thr40_gain1.5_curveball_within_type-seed1_retuned:raw__hf_all__rmse ~ .3f}} on the nine draws). Under the calibrated readout the reference model's mean effect is already above the flies'; leaving the survivors out raises it further and the loss with it. The same cells are a fault of the model on raw counts and a support under the readout.

![How few KCs the APL-effect loss rests on. Seven saved models with their highest-firing KCs (by spike count with APL on) left out of both conditions after the fact, against the number left out; stars: the model's survivors left out. Top: the APL-effect loss (lower is better); bottom: the mean APL effect; left: raw spike counts; right: the calibrated saturating readout. Dashed lines: the floor of the loss and the flies' mean effect. The model with the gain on DM1 alone is the 70 Hz reference fit with the oracle gain kept on DM1 only, tuned to 5 %.](results/E70_high_firing_kcs/E70_leave_out.png)

**Re-drawing the survivors' claws raises the mean effect in simulation, and the controls do not.** In the reference model each claw of the survivors was exchanged with a claw of a KC of the same type outside the set, so that every KC keeps its number of claws, every glomerulus its number of claws and every KC type its repertoire ({{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=B_thr40_gain1.5_surv_redraw-seed1_retuned:n_swaps ~ .0f}} exchanges; the glomerulus pairs' counts of shared KCs stay correlated with the real wiring's at {{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=B_thr40_gain1.5_surv_redraw-seed1_retuned:coinput_corr_vs_real ~ .2f}}). The fitted APL and KC–KC scales were held and the somatic threshold re-tuned to the response rate, three draws per arm; the real wiring run the same way reproduced the saved model exactly.

The mean effect on raw counts rose in each of the three draws, on average by about half of the difference between the real wiring and its within-type claw permutations (first row of the table below). Re-drawing as many high-firing KCs that do not survive, matched to the survivors in KC type and number of claws, left it where it was, as did re-drawing as many matched KCs from outside the high-firing set ({{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=B_thr40_gain1.5_ctl_outside-seed1_retuned:raw__mean ~ +.3f}} / {{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=B_thr40_gain1.5_ctl_outside-seed2_retuned:raw__mean ~ +.3f}} / {{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=B_thr40_gain1.5_ctl_outside-seed3_retuned:raw__mean ~ +.3f}}), and putting the survivors' real claws back into the three claw permutations lowered their mean effect by about as much as the re-draw had raised the real wiring's.

Few survivors form again on the re-drawn wirings, so it is the wiring of these cells, and not the inhibition at the fitted scales, that makes them. Re-drawing the whole high-firing set goes a little further on average. In the 70 Hz fit of the same model, where the difference to the shuffles is smaller, re-drawing its {{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=B_thr70_gain1.5_real_fit:n_survivors ~ .0f}} survivors takes the mean effect from {{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=B_thr70_gain1.5_real_fit:raw__mean ~ +.3f}} to {{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=B_thr70_gain1.5_surv_redraw-seed1_retuned:raw__mean ~ +.3f}} / {{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=B_thr70_gain1.5_surv_redraw-seed2_retuned:raw__mean ~ +.3f}} / {{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=B_thr70_gain1.5_surv_redraw-seed3_retuned:raw__mean ~ +.3f}} and leaves the loss where it was ({{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=B_thr70_gain1.5_surv_redraw-seed1_retuned:raw__rmse ~ .3f}} / {{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=B_thr70_gain1.5_surv_redraw-seed2_retuned:raw__rmse ~ .3f}} / {{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=B_thr70_gain1.5_surv_redraw-seed3_retuned:raw__rmse ~ .3f}} from {{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=B_thr70_gain1.5_real_fit:raw__rmse ~ .3f}}; all inside the realism bands).

**The gain is all in the mean part, and the block goes with the cells.** The loss barely moves: what the mean part gains, the pattern part loses (second and third rows of the table above), and under the calibrated readout, where the real wiring's mean effect is already above the flies', the loss rises in every draw.

The fruity × small-ester block, which the reference model has at the data's size on the real wiring, falls to half or less with the survivors re-drawn and keeps most of its size in all but one draw of the controls ({{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=B_thr40_gain1.5_ctl_outside-seed1_retuned:raw__block ~ +.3f}} / {{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=B_thr40_gain1.5_ctl_outside-seed2_retuned:raw__block ~ +.3f}} / {{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=B_thr40_gain1.5_ctl_outside-seed3_retuned:raw__block ~ +.3f}} with the matched KCs from outside the high-firing set re-drawn); put back into the claw permutations, the survivors' claws bring part of it back in two of the three. APL's effect on the natural-source alignment (APL on minus APL off), of the wrong sign on the real wiring, moves further from the flies' when the survivors are re-drawn and toward it when their claws are put back.

The cells that hold the mean effect down on raw counts are therefore the ones that carry the reference model's block, and on raw counts the two statistics pull against each other through the same twenty KCs. None of this costs a realism band: the re-drawn models stay at the flies' response rates, and the distance of the odors-per-KC distribution from the flies' with APL off, inside its band on the real wiring, shrinks.

**More inhibition on these cells does not silence them.** With the wiring left as it is and the survivors' APL→KC weights multiplied by two and by four on top of the breadth weighting (an oracle, at weights no connectome supports), {{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=B_thr40_gain1.5_surv_apl_x2:n_survivors ~ .0f}} and {{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=B_thr40_gain1.5_surv_apl_x4:n_survivors ~ .0f}} of the {{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=B_thr40_gain1.5_real_fit:n_survivors ~ .0f}} still reach twenty spikes with APL on, and the mean effect does not rise ({{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=B_thr40_gain1.5_surv_apl_x2:raw__mean ~ +.3f}} and {{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=B_thr40_gain1.5_surv_apl_x4:raw__mean ~ +.3f}}, from {{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=B_thr40_gain1.5_real_fit:raw__mean ~ +.3f}}; both runs, like the reference model itself, are inside all four realism bands). Their drive is too far above threshold for inhibition aimed at them to be the remedy; a mechanism that removes them has to cap their output or lower their drive.

**Most of the reference model's survivors are the cells through which the oracle gain lifts euc and -aPine, and they are not realistic KCs.**

On the real wiring the survivors' claws are concentrated on fewer glomeruli than those of the rest of the high-firing set ({{E70/wiring_by_class.csv:key=ref40;kc_class=survivor:max_claws_one_glomerulus ~ .2f}} claws from their most-sampled glomerulus against {{E70/wiring_by_class.csv:key=ref40;kc_class=high_firing_other:max_claws_one_glomerulus ~ .2f}}, {{E70/wiring_by_class.csv:key=ref40;kc_class=survivor:n_glomeruli ~ .1f}} distinct glomeruli against {{E70/wiring_by_class.csv:key=ref40;kc_class=high_firing_other:n_glomeruli ~ .1f}}); they have twice the claws from DP1m ({{E70/wiring_by_class.csv:key=ref40;kc_class=survivor:claws_DP1m ~ .2f}} against {{E70/wiring_by_class.csv:key=ref40;kc_class=high_firing_other:claws_DP1m ~ .2f}}), more from the eight glomeruli that carry the oracle gain ({{E70/wiring_by_class.csv:key=ref40;kc_class=survivor:claws_gained8 ~ .2f}} against {{E70/wiring_by_class.csv:key=ref40;kc_class=high_firing_other:claws_gained8 ~ .2f}}) and less APL→KC weight from the connectome ({{E70/wiring_by_class.csv:key=ref40;kc_class=survivor:apl_weight_connectome ~ .2f}} against {{E70/wiring_by_class.csv:key=ref40;kc_class=high_firing_other:apl_weight_connectome ~ .2f}} of the mean weight), and the KC–KC inhibition they receive is no different from the other KCs'. {{lit:14 # survivors of the reference model whose largest APL-on count is to euc (10) or -aPine (4), counted in results/E70_high_firing_kcs/survivors.csv, key ref40, column top_odor_on}} of the {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3:n_survivors ~ .0f}} fire most to euc or -aPine ({{lit:21 # survivors of the 70 Hz reference fit whose largest APL-on count is to euc (14) or -aPine (7), counted in results/E70_high_firing_kcs/survivors.csv, key ref70, column top_odor_on}} of {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr70_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3:n_survivors ~ .0f}} in the 70 Hz fit), and all of the survivors of the two fits with the gain on DM1 alone fire most to paa.

euc and paa are among the weak-input odors that the oracle gain was introduced to lift, and -aPine is carried by the same gained glomeruli as euc (DP1m and VC1); the survivors are how the gain lifts them, through a few over-driven KCs where the flies have many moderately driven ones. euc, -aPine and paa are also the three odors whose ORN input is taken from another concentration than the KC recordings' ([the concentrations](#fn-concentrations): euc's and -aPine's from a higher one, paa's from a lower one), so how many such cells a model has depends on an input that is not the recordings'.

The cells themselves are far from recorded KCs: with APL on the reference model's survivors fire up to {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3:max_count_on ~ .0f}} spikes to one odor, and with APL off {{E70/wiring_by_class.csv:key=ref40;kc_class=survivor:max_count_off ~ .0f}} on average and up to {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3:max_count_off ~ .0f}}, against a bound of about {{lit:14 # the bound the firing ceiling for the KCs (E69) takes for a KC's response with APL on: the mean plus three standard deviations of the 4.9 ± 3.0 spikes per 0.5 s response of α′/β′ KCs in Turner, Bazhenov and Laurent (2008), as quoted in E70_high_firing_kcs.md, Realism; not re-derived for this page}} spikes that [the firing ceiling for the KCs](#firing-ceiling) takes from recordings of KCs (the mean plus three standard deviations of the counts in Turner, Bazhenov and Laurent, 2008). The realism bands hold a model to which KCs respond, not to how hard they fire, and do not see them.

**The lowest losses on raw spike counts rest on two to six KCs of the real wiring; the lowest under the calibrated readout rests on none in particular.** The 70 Hz reference fit with the oracle gain kept on DM1 alone, which held the lowest loss on raw counts of the models on the real wiring before the APL-effect fits ([the oracle gain decomposed by glomerulus](#gain-decomposition)), has {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E39_gain_decomposition;tag=thr70__only_DM1:n_survivors ~ .0f}} survivors, and with its two highest-firing KCs left out its loss on raw counts goes from {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E39_gain_decomposition;tag=thr70__only_DM1:raw__rmse ~ .3f}} to {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E39_gain_decomposition;tag=thr70__only_DM1:raw__top2__rmse ~ .3f}}, above the first joint fit's, which the same leave-out barely moves (first table of this subsection; the best-models table carries the same leave-out as a row for every column without a firing ceiling).

[The APL-effect fits](#apl-effect-fits) arrived at the same kind of model as their best fit on raw counts, the 70 Hz base with the gain on DM1 alone fitted on raw counts at the flies' response rate, and it rests on its {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=thr70_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplraw_k2_cap3_DM1:n_survivors ~ .0f}} survivors in the same way (last column of the first table). Re-drawing those survivors' claws in simulation, at the fit's scales and with three draws per arm as above, takes its mean effect from {{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=C_e67-thr70_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplraw_k2_cap3_DM1_real_fit:raw__mean ~ +.3f}} past the flies' to {{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=C_e67-thr70_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplraw_k2_cap3_DM1_surv_redraw-seed1_retuned:raw__mean ~ +.3f}} / {{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=C_e67-thr70_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplraw_k2_cap3_DM1_surv_redraw-seed2_retuned:raw__mean ~ +.3f}} / {{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=C_e67-thr70_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplraw_k2_cap3_DM1_surv_redraw-seed3_retuned:raw__mean ~ +.3f}} and its loss from {{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=C_e67-thr70_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplraw_k2_cap3_DM1_real_fit:raw__rmse ~ .3f}} to {{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=C_e67-thr70_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplraw_k2_cap3_DM1_surv_redraw-seed1_retuned:raw__rmse ~ .3f}} / {{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=C_e67-thr70_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplraw_k2_cap3_DM1_surv_redraw-seed2_retuned:raw__rmse ~ .3f}} / {{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=C_e67-thr70_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplraw_k2_cap3_DM1_surv_redraw-seed3_retuned:raw__rmse ~ .3f}}, where re-drawing as many matched high-firing KCs that do not survive leaves the loss at {{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=C_e67-thr70_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplraw_k2_cap3_DM1_ctl_hf_nonsurv-seed1_retuned:raw__rmse ~ .3f}} / {{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=C_e67-thr70_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplraw_k2_cap3_DM1_ctl_hf_nonsurv-seed2_retuned:raw__rmse ~ .3f}} / {{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=C_e67-thr70_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplraw_k2_cap3_DM1_ctl_hf_nonsurv-seed3_retuned:raw__rmse ~ .3f}}.

On three untreated within-type claw permutations the fit's scales give a mean effect of {{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=C_e67-thr70_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplraw_k2_cap3_DM1_cpwt_untreated-seed1_retuned:raw__mean ~ +.3f}} / {{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=C_e67-thr70_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplraw_k2_cap3_DM1_cpwt_untreated-seed2_retuned:raw__mean ~ +.3f}} / {{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=C_e67-thr70_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplraw_k2_cap3_DM1_cpwt_untreated-seed3_retuned:raw__mean ~ +.3f}} and a loss of {{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=C_e67-thr70_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplraw_k2_cap3_DM1_cpwt_untreated-seed1_retuned:raw__rmse ~ .3f}} / {{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=C_e67-thr70_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplraw_k2_cap3_DM1_cpwt_untreated-seed2_retuned:raw__rmse ~ .3f}} / {{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=C_e67-thr70_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplraw_k2_cap3_DM1_cpwt_untreated-seed3_retuned:raw__rmse ~ .3f}}. The fit found scales at which a handful of paa cells of this wiring hold the mean effect at the flies' level; without those cells the same scales overshoot, and on the real wiring the loss is then about the first joint fit's. Every run of these arms is inside the realism bands.

The best fit under the calibrated readout, the first joint fit's family at breadth exponent 2, with neither the gain nor the per-claw threshold, has about as many survivors as the reference model and does not rest on them: with up to twenty of its highest-firing KCs left out its loss moves by at most {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3:raw__max_change_k20 ~ .3f}} on raw counts and {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3:cal__max_change_k20 ~ .3f}} under the readout.

**Strong KC–KC inhibition makes more of them.** The fit with the block term on the batched proxy, which raised the KC–KC scale and lowered the somatic threshold, has more than twice its seed's survivors, holding half of an odor's summed squared responses with APL on, and with KC–KC inhibition held at 45 there are several times more (the three columns of that family in the first table). With them left out, the mean effect of the fit on the proxy is above its seed's as saved.

In this family the inhibition that spreads the responses over more KCs with APL off, and brings the number of odors per KC to the flies', also leaves a class of KCs that APL does not stop, and the regime's cost on the main target runs through them. Over the {{E70/archive_relations.csv:operating_point=6.8 %;x=survivor_share_sq_on;y=raw__mean:n ~ .0f}} saved models tuned to the flies' response rate, shuffled wirings and controls included, the larger the survivors' share of the APL-on responses, the smaller the mean effect on raw counts (a Spearman correlation of {{E70/archive_relations.csv:operating_point=6.8 %;x=survivor_share_sq_on;y=raw__mean:spearman ~ +.2f}}) and the larger the loss ({{E70/archive_relations.csv:operating_point=6.8 %;x=survivor_share_sq_on;y=raw__rmse:spearman ~ +.2f}}); under the calibrated readout the two correlations are {{E70/archive_relations.csv:operating_point=6.8 %;x=survivor_share_sq_on;y=cal__mean:spearman ~ +.2f}} and {{E70/archive_relations.csv:operating_point=6.8 %;x=survivor_share_sq_on;y=cal__rmse:spearman ~ +.2f}}.

What separates the KCs that stay silent with APL off from those that respond to eight or more odors is input and not inhibition: the number of claws on the eight gained glomeruli tells the two groups apart almost completely (the chance that a KC of the second group has more such claws than one of the first is {{E70/opk_features.csv:key=ref40;feature=claws_gained8:auc_8plus_vs_silent ~ .2f}} in the reference model, where one half is no separation), the KC–KC inhibition received not at all ({{E70/opk_features.csv:key=ref40;feature=kckc_received_off:auc_8plus_vs_silent ~ .2f}}).

**One fly is about as far from the other flies as the best models are from the data.** Scored as a model is, one control recording paired with one recording with APL output blocked (TNT), against the mean of the remaining recordings, has an APL-effect loss of {{lit:0.111 # median of column rmse over the 88 pairs of one control recording and one recording with APL output blocked (TNT) in results/E70_high_firing_kcs/yardstick.csv}} (the median over the pairs; {{lit:0.074 # minimum of column rmse in results/E70_high_firing_kcs/yardstick.csv}} to {{lit:0.263 # maximum of column rmse in results/E70_high_firing_kcs/yardstick.csv}}) and a pattern part of {{lit:0.092 # median of column rmse_centered in results/E70_high_firing_kcs/yardstick.csv}}, measurement noise included; the floor of {{data:apl_effect_rmse_floor ~ .3f}} is that of the mean over all recordings. The best fits on one wiring score no worse than a typical single pair of recordings does.

Averaging a model over shuffled draws of its wiring lowers its pattern part only modestly (for the reference model on five claw permutations, {{E70/yardstick_models.csv:model=ref40;what=mean over the claw permutation draws;readout=raw:per_draw_pattern_mean ~ .3f}} per draw on average and {{E70/yardstick_models.csv:model=ref40;what=mean over the claw permutation draws;readout=raw:rmse_centered ~ .3f}} for the mean over the draws), so most of a model's pattern error is common to the draws and not one wiring's accident. The model's own single pseudo-recordings through the matched trial noise could not be scored the same way here (the pipeline saved only their means); scored since, a single pseudo-recording pair of the breadth-2 fit is closer to the data's mean than a single pair of recordings is ([the input-scaled KC threshold](#input-scaled-threshold), at the end of this section).

**What follows for the definition of the target, the block and the realism of the models.** On raw spike counts the shortfall of the mean effect in the models with the oracle gain is in good part the amplitude of about one in a hundred of their KCs, the least realistic cells they have.

The calibrated readout takes that amplitude away without choosing cells, which is how it supplied these models' mean effect ([above](#readout)), and a firing ceiling in the model takes it away at the source ([the next subsection](#firing-ceiling)); under the readout the same cells support the mean effect, so in a model without a ceiling whether they count against it depends on the definition that is still open. Three things do not depend on it.

- The order of the best models on raw counts turns on two to six cells of one wiring, and the order under the calibrated readout does not, which favours the first joint fit's family over the fits with the gain on DM1 alone under either definition.
- The reference model's block is carried by its survivors, so whatever removes them, re-wiring here and the readout's compression before, removes the block with them; a model that is to have the block together with the flies' mean effect needs a carrier of the block that is not a few over-driven cells, which is what the mechanisms acting on the set of responding KCs are.
- And the weak-input odors have to reach their response rates through many moderately driven KCs: the ORN input of euc, -aPine and paa scaled toward the recordings' concentrations, or a gain kept off the glomeruli that give the survivors most of their claws, is the place to start.

### A firing ceiling for the KCs, and the two definitions of the main target {#firing-ceiling}

**With a ceiling on how many spikes a KC fires to an odor, the model's raw spike counts score on the main target as the calibrated readout does, inside the realism bands; the block is lost as it is under the readout, and which KCs respond with APL off does not change.**

Until this experiment the model's KCs had neither a refractory period nor adaptation: after a spike the potential was reset and integration went on at once. The hardest-driven KC of the current reference model fires {{E69/stats_variants.csv:ref40_base:max_count_on ~ .0f}} spikes to one 0.5 s odor with APL on and {{E69/stats_variants.csv:ref40_base:max_count_off ~ .0f}} with APL off, where a reading of whole-cell recordings of KCs puts the bound at about {{lit:14 # the bound on a KC's spike count to one odor with APL on that the firing ceiling for the KCs takes from whole-cell recordings: the mean plus three standard deviations (4.9 + 3 x 3.0 = 13.9) of the spikes per response of α′/β′ KCs to a 500 ms odor in Turner, Bazhenov and Laurent (2008); E69_kc_firing_ceiling.md, Design (part B) and Caveats}} spikes (the mean plus three standard deviations of the counts of the α′/β′ KCs in Turner, Bazhenov and Laurent, 2008).

The firing ceiling for the KCs adds both to the model ([how it works and how its settings were chosen](#fn-firing-ceiling)): a refractory period of 3 ms, and an adaptation that raises a KC's threshold by a fixed fraction of itself at every spike and decays over 1 s, longer than the odor, so that within one odor it acts as a budget of spikes. It was applied first at fixed scales, to the current reference model and to the best APL-effect fit under each definition of the model's side ([the APL-effect fits](#apl-effect-fits)), with both response rates held at each model's own by re-tuning the somatic threshold and the APL scales, so that nothing is bought with the response rates.

The breadth-2 fit was then fitted again under the APL-effect loss, with the ceiling fixed and both definitions in the loss, at two strengths of the adaptation: the literature setting ({{E69/stats_variants.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2:kc_adapt_inc ~ .0%}} of the threshold per spike), at which its largest count with APL on is nearest the recordings' bound, and a stronger setting ({{E69/stats_variants.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:kc_adapt_inc ~ .0%}}), the weakest at which the calibrated readout has nothing left to compress. The reference model was fitted again at the stronger setting, where its own largest count with APL on is at the recordings' bound.

The breadth-2 APL-effect fit and the current reference model, each without a firing ceiling and fitted again with one. Where a row gives two values without naming conditions, they are on raw spike counts / through the calibrated saturating readout, its half-saturation set again on each model's own APL-on counts; at the stronger setting it runs to the upper end of its range, where the readout changes nothing. The fit without a ceiling and the two fits of its family with one went through the matched trial noise

**The raw counts now give what the readout gave.** On raw counts the loss of the breadth-2 family falls by a third at the literature setting and by nearly half at the stronger one, and the reference model's halves (first row).

The mean APL effect, below the flies' 90 % interval on raw counts without a ceiling, is inside it in every fit with one, and the two definitions come together: at the stronger setting they give one number, and at the literature setting they are about a tenth as far apart as without a ceiling. The calibrated readout was standing in for firing that the model did not bound, and with a ceiling of this kind the choice between raw counts and the readout matters little.

Most of this is there before any fitting: at fixed scales, with both response rates held, the breadth-2 fit goes from {{E69/stats_variants.csv:e67cal_base:apl_raw_rmse ~ .3f}} on raw counts to {{E69/stats_variants.csv:e67cal_r3_a1_t1000:apl_raw_rmse ~ .3f}} at the literature setting and {{E69/stats_variants.csv:e67cal_r3_a2_t1000:apl_raw_rmse ~ .3f}} at the stronger one. The best fit on raw counts without a ceiling, the 70 Hz base with the gain on DM1 alone, gets worse with one ({{E69/stats_variants.csv:e67raw_base:apl_raw_rmse ~ .3f}} to {{E69/stats_variants.csv:e67raw_r3_a1_t1000:apl_raw_rmse ~ .3f}} and {{E69/stats_variants.csv:e67raw_r3_a2_t1000:apl_raw_rmse ~ .3f}} at the two settings) and was not fitted again; its lead rested on a few high-firing KCs ([above](#high-firing-kcs)).

The data are not reached. The fit at the stronger setting has the lowest loss of any model on the real wiring inside all four realism bands, under either definition, and is still a third above the floor, nearly all of it pattern: ρ on the per-pair APL effect stays well under its ceiling, and the per-odor and the pair-specific part of the loss are {{E69/stats_variants.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:apl_raw_per_odor ~ .3f}} and {{E69/stats_variants.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:apl_raw_pair_specific ~ .3f}}, against floors of {{E66/data_floor_parts.csv:data=graded;stat=apl_effect_per_odor:mean ~ .3f}} and {{E66/data_floor_parts.csv:data=graded;stat=apl_effect_pair_specific:mean ~ .3f}}.

Through [the matched trial noise](#fn-trial-noise) both fits with the ceiling stay below every APL-effect fit without one on raw counts (the fourth row here and the same row of the table of [the APL-effect fits](#apl-effect-fits)), and the stronger setting's lead over the literature setting is gone, so the setting that agrees with the recordings loses nothing. All of these are numbers of the model's 0.5 s odor pulse.

At the flies' 2 s pulse, with parameters fitted at 0.5 s, the loss on raw counts rises in both families, by a fifth with the ceiling at its stronger setting and by more than half without a ceiling, so the ceiling's gain on raw counts stays and its level does not ([the flies' pulse in the model and the remaining candidates for the common error](#remaining-candidates), at the end of this section).

The level comes back with an adaptation that outlasts the odor: with it decaying over 3 s in place of 1 s, the fit at the stronger setting, the literature setting as a mean over four wirings and a fit made at the flies' pulse all read through the flies' response window what they read at 0.5 s ([the flies' recording protocol in the model](#flies-protocol), at the end of this section).

**The ceiling costs what the readout costs, and it does not change which KCs respond.** In the breadth-2 family the block falls to about two thirds of the flies' at the literature setting and a third at the stronger one, and the reference model's is all but gone; the natural-source alignment with APL on falls at the stronger setting, and the mean distances fall below the flies' in both conditions. The APL-effect loss scores none of these, and the calibrated readout costs the same, as expected if the two do the same job: on raw counts the block and the alignment were carried by the strong responders ([the high-firing KCs that survive APL](#high-firing-kcs)).

With the ceiling no KC of the reference model reaches twenty spikes with APL on, so none of its survivors is left, and its mean effect on raw counts comes to the flies', further than re-drawing the survivors' claws had brought it ({{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=B_thr40_gain1.5_surv_redraw-seed1_retuned:raw__mean ~ +.3f}} / {{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=B_thr40_gain1.5_surv_redraw-seed2_retuned:raw__mean ~ +.3f}} / {{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=B_thr40_gain1.5_surv_redraw-seed3_retuned:raw__mean ~ +.3f}} over the three draws): the shortfall of the mean on raw counts was the strong firing of many KCs, not of those few alone.

What the ceiling gains in realism is the spread of an odor's response over its KCs, which comes to the flies' (the row on the top 1 % of KCs), with APL on at the literature setting and with APL off at the stronger one. What it leaves is which KCs respond.

The distance of the odors-per-KC distribution from the flies' with APL off hardly moves, close to half of the KCs stay silent to all 16 odors with APL off against {{data:noise_tnt_odors_per_kc_0 ~ .0%}} in the flies, and the reference model stays where it was inside that band with the ceiling as without it, also when a term on odors per KC is added to the loss of its fit ({{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E69_kc_firing_ceiling;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplbothopk_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:opk_off_tv ~ .3f}}, from {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E69_kc_firing_ceiling;tag=ref40_base:opk_off_tv ~ .3f}} without the ceiling and against a band of {{data:noise_tnt_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .3f}}): the breadth of its recruitment with APL off belongs to the gain and the 40 Hz per-claw threshold, not to the firing.

Nor do the amplitudes come to the flies' in both conditions. Read in the recordings' units as in the table of amplitudes [above](#readout), the responders of the fit at the literature setting average {{E69/stats_variants.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2:z_floor_noise_resp_amp_mean_on ~ .2f}} z with APL on and {{E69/stats_variants.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2:z_floor_noise_resp_amp_mean_acute_off ~ .2f}} z with APL off, where the flies' average {{data:ctrl_resp_amp_mean_z ~ .2f}} and {{data:tnt_resp_amp_mean_z ~ .2f}}: the ceiling lowers both together. It sets how much the strong responders fire; which KCs are recruited when APL is removed needs a mechanism of its own, and the one tried changes them at a cost on the main target ([the input-scaled KC threshold](#input-scaled-threshold), the next subsection).

**Other wirings, and a strength that is a reading.** Under the readout, one draw of the wiring moves this family's loss by more than the fits with a ceiling differ from the fit without one. The same family fitted without a ceiling on seven re-drawn wirings (four within-type claw permutations and three shuffles matched to the real wiring on every glomerulus pair's count of shared KCs; [the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population), at the end of this section) ends between {{E72/stats_variants.csv:wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed3_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3:cal_loss ~ .3f}} and {{E72/stats_variants.csv:wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed1_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3:cal_loss ~ .3f}} under the readout, the real wiring's {{E72/stats_variants.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3:cal_loss ~ .3f}} among them, and between {{E72/stats_variants.csv:wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed3_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3:raw_loss ~ .3f}} and {{E72/stats_variants.csv:wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed2_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3:raw_loss ~ .3f}} on raw counts.

Under the readout the fits with a ceiling are therefore as good as the fit without one, not better; on raw counts they are below the fit of every one of those wirings, and the gain holds through the trial noise. The ceiling at the literature setting has since been fitted on three of those wirings as well, each beside the fit without a ceiling on the same wiring: on raw counts the loss changes by between {{E72/partG_paired.csv:wiring=P2:raw_loss_diff ~ +.3f}} and {{E72/partG_paired.csv:wiring=P1:raw_loss_diff ~ +.3f}} on the three, as by {{E72/partG_paired.csv:wiring=real:raw_loss_diff ~ +.3f}} on the real wiring, and under the readout by no more than {{E72/partG_paired.csv:wiring=P2:cal_loss_diff ~ .3f}} on any of the four, so the gain on raw counts is the family's and not the hemibrain wiring's.

The stronger setting has been fitted on the real wiring only. Its strength is a reading of the recordings, not a measurement: they give the mean and the standard deviation of the spike counts per response ({{lit:4.9 ± 3.0 # spikes per response of α′/β′ KCs to a 500 ms odor (mean ± standard deviation, whole-cell recordings, APL intact), Turner, Bazhenov and Laurent (2008), as quoted in E69_kc_firing_ceiling.md, Design (part B), Realism and Caveats}} for α′/β′ KCs and {{lit:2.2 ± 1.2 # spikes per response of α/β KCs to a 500 ms odor (mean ± standard deviation, whole-cell recordings, APL intact), Turner, Bazhenov and Laurent (2008), as quoted in E69_kc_firing_ceiling.md, Realism and Caveats}} for α/β KCs, to other odors and concentrations than the KC data's) and no largest count, and the stronger setting, at which no KC of the breadth-2 fit fires more than {{E69/stats_variants.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:max_count_on ~ .0f}} spikes with APL on, allows the α′/β′ KCs less than they show.

Both fits of the breadth-2 family also ended with more KCs responding with APL off than they started with (a response rate {{E69/stats_variants.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2:rate_ratio_off_over_on ~ .2f}} and {{E69/stats_variants.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:rate_ratio_off_over_on ~ .2f}} times that with APL on, from {{E69/stats_variants.csv:e67cal_base:rate_ratio_off_over_on ~ .2f}}; the flies' {{data:rate_ratio_fraction ~ .2f}}, 90 % interval {{data:rate_ratio_fraction.lo ~ .2f}} to {{data:rate_ratio_fraction.hi ~ .2f}}), which by itself raises the mean effect, so part of what the fits add to the runs at fixed scales may be bought that way; the ratio was not held in the fits. As everywhere, the pairs with paa, euc and -aPine rest on [ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations).

### The input-scaled KC threshold: which KCs are released when APL is removed, and what moving the release costs {#input-scaled-threshold}

**A somatic threshold that scales with each KC's input moves the release of KCs, when APL is removed, off the many-claw cells, as the flies' numbers of odors per KC ask, and in every family the main target pays for it; fitted again, each family gets the mean effect back with as many broadly responding KCs as before, drawn from other cells, and loses on the pattern.**

In the model every KC has the same somatic threshold, apart from a term proportional to its spontaneous input, so a KC with many claws crosses it for more odors than a KC with few. Breadth-weighted APL inhibits the broadly responding KCs most, so when APL is removed they are the ones released.

In the breadth-2 APL-effect fit ([the APL-effect fits](#apl-effect-fits)) the KCs that respond to eight or more odors with APL off have {{E70/opk_features.csv:key=e67__rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3;feature=n_claws:mean_8plus_off ~ .1f}} claws on average and the silent ones {{E70/opk_features.csv:key=e67__rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3;feature=n_claws:mean_silent_off ~ .1f}}, and the {{E71/input_readouts.csv:c2_base:rel_g9plus_n_kcs ~ .0f}} KCs with nine or more claws, of {{E71/input_readouts.csv:c2_base:n_kcs_on ~ .0f}}, take a third of the responses that removing APL adds. More of its KCs stay silent than in the flies, more respond to eight or more odors, and the number of odors per KC is spread more widely than in any recording.

With every KC × odor entry counted only as a response or none (binarized: two or more spikes in the model, a trial mean above 1 in the recordings), removing APL then adds more overlap between odors than it does in the flies, although under the calibrated readout the fit's mean APL effect is the flies' (first model column of the table below). The low end of the readout found the same from the amplitudes ([above](#readout)): with APL off the models add strong responses where the flies add weak ones, and what the weak ones carry of the flies' APL effect is for the most part the weaker responses of their broadly responding KCs to their other odors ([the APL effect split by odors per KC](#apl-effect-by-class), further down in this section).

[The firing ceiling for the KCs](#firing-ceiling) changes how much the released KCs fire and not which KCs they are, and KC–KC inhibition strong enough to spread the release brings the silent share below the flies' ({{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E53_kckc_held_block;tag=thr70_gain1.25_rate0.068_kckc45_k2_cap3:opk_off_0 ~ .0%}} in the 70 Hz model with the gain at 1.25 and KC–KC held at 45, against {{data:noise_tnt_odors_per_kc_0 ~ .0%}}) at a mean APL effect of {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E53_kckc_held_block;tag=thr70_gain1.25_rate0.068_kckc45_k2_cap3:raw__mean ~ +.3f}} on raw counts and {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E53_kckc_held_block;tag=thr70_gain1.25_rate0.068_kckc45_k2_cap3:cal__mean ~ +.3f}} under the readout. The one earlier test of thresholds by claw count, in the KC heterogeneity experiment, had not applied them.

The release through the many-claw KCs belongs to the family and not to the hemibrain wiring. Fitted on seven re-drawn wirings ([the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population), the next subsection), the breadth-2 family gives the KCs with nine or more claws, {{E72/release.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3:frac_kcs_9+ ~ .0%}} of the KCs, between {{E72/release.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;tag=wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed4_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3:share_added_9+ ~ .0%}} and {{E72/release.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;tag=wiring-curveball_within_type_matched-seed2_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3:share_added_9+ ~ .0%}} of the added responses, against {{E72/release.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3:share_added_9+ ~ .0%}} on the real wiring, and over the eight wirings the squared coefficient of variation of the number of odors per KC with APL off is between {{E72/release.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;tag=wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed2_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3:opk_cv2_off ~ .2f}} and {{E72/release.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;tag=wiring-curveball_within_type_matched-seed3_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3:opk_cv2_off ~ .2f}}, above every recording's (the fourth row of the table below). With the per-claw threshold at 40 Hz and no glomerulus gain the share is as large, between {{E72/release.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;tag=thr40_wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed2_rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3:share_added_9+ ~ .0%}} and {{E72/release.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=thr40_rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3:share_added_9+ ~ .0%}} over five wirings.

The input-scaled KC threshold multiplies each KC's threshold by a power of the KC's summed claw weight relative to the mean over KCs, the same with APL on and with APL off, so that it is a property of the cell and not of APL; with the power at zero it is the model as it was. Through the spontaneous-input term the threshold of the breadth-2 fit already grows with a KC's summed claw weight, with a log-log slope of {{E71/input_readouts.csv:c2_base:thr_loglog_slope_W ~ .2f}}; a power of 0.5 brings the slope to {{E71/input_readouts.csv:c2_a0.5:thr_loglog_slope_W ~ .2f}}, a threshold about proportional to the input.

The power was swept at fixed scales, from 0.25 to 1 and at −0.5 as a control of the sign, on three models: the breadth-2 fit, the same fit with the firing ceiling at its literature setting, and the current reference model. At every setting both response rates were held at the model's own by re-tuning the somatic threshold on the APL-off response rate and then the APL→KC and APL→bouton scales together on the APL-on one, so that no change is bought with the response rates, and the per-KC breadth behind the APL→KC weights was computed again with the scaled thresholds, the weights forming on the cells as they then are.

For each model the power kept is the one that brings the number of odors per KC with APL off closest to the flies' among the settings that stay inside the bands on odors per KC and on the response rate ρ with APL on, a choice that involves no distance between odors. Each of the three was then fitted again under the APL-effect loss with that power fixed, both definitions in the loss and the usual four parameters free.

The three models at fixed scales, both response rates held: without the scaling and at the power kept for each. **At fixed scales the release moves the way the flies' numbers ask.** With the power at 0.5 the few-claw KCs of the breadth-2 fit take over the responses that removing APL adds (first row), and with APL off a KC with nine or more claws then responds to fewer odors than a KC with one to four ({{E71/input_readouts.csv:c2_a0.5:rel_g9plus_opk_off ~ .1f}} against {{E71/input_readouts.csv:c2_a0.5:rel_g1_4_opk_off ~ .1f}} on average, from {{E71/input_readouts.csv:c2_base:rel_g9plus_opk_off ~ .1f}} against {{E71/input_readouts.csv:c2_base:rel_g1_4_opk_off ~ .1f}}). The distance of the odors-per-KC distribution from the flies' with APL off falls by more than a quarter, and the binarized mean APL effect and its loss come down toward the data's.

The other two models move the same way, and the reference model, inside the band on odors per KC with APL off as it stands, comes to a third of its distance from the flies' distribution with the scaling. The flies' distribution is not reached: about four KCs in ten still respond to none of the odors with APL off, a little more than the flies' {{data:noise_tnt_odors_per_kc_0 ~ .0%}}, and in the breadth-2 fit, with or without the ceiling, the spread of the number of odors per KC stays above every recording's (the reference model's comes inside their range).

The control of the sign moves the release the other way: at a power of −0.5 the KCs with nine or more claws take {{E71/input_readouts.csv:c2_a-0.5:rel_g9plus_share_added ~ .0%}} of the added responses, the distance with APL off rises to {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E71_input_scaled_threshold;tag=c2_a-0.5:opk_off_tv ~ .3f}}, more than twice the unscaled fit's and near the band's limit of {{data:noise_tnt_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .3f}}, and the binarized mean APL effect rises to {{E71/input_readouts.csv:c2_a-0.5:apl_bin_mean ~ +.3f}}. Beyond the power kept the few-claw KCs become the over-driven ones: at a power of 1 the largest spike count of the breadth-2 fit with APL on is {{E71/input_readouts.csv:c2_a1:max_count_on ~ .0f}} and the distance with APL off is above the unscaled fit's again ({{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E71_input_scaled_threshold;tag=c2_a1:opk_off_tv ~ .3f}}).

**The graded APL effect falls with it.** Under the calibrated readout the mean effect of the breadth-2 fit, the flies' without the scaling, falls by about a fifth and its loss rises by a third; on raw counts the mean effect falls to less than half and the loss nearly doubles. In the other two models the mean effect and the loss move the same way under both definitions, and only the binarized loss gains. The breadth weighting computed again on the scaled cells holds back about half of the fall: with the breadth left as fitted, the mean effect of the breadth-2 fit under the readout is {{E71/input_readouts.csv:c2_a0.5_kb:apl_cal_mean ~ +.3f}} at the same power. ρ on odor-odor distances with APL on falls in the breadth-2 fit as well.

The three families fitted again under the APL-effect loss with the scaling fixed, each beside the same family without it. Two values without named conditions are on raw spike counts / through the calibrated saturating readout, its half-saturation set again on each model's own APL-on counts. The columns without the scaling are the breadth-2 APL-effect fit, the fit with the firing ceiling at its literature setting, and the current reference model, which was fitted to other targets (the fits of its set under the APL-effect loss are given in the text)
