**Fitted again, every family gets the mean effect back and loses on the pattern.** In the two families of the first joint fit the mean APL effect is where it was without the scaling under both definitions (second row), and in the reference model's set it is at the level of the set's fits under the APL-effect loss ({{E67/comparison.csv:kind=fit;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplraw_k2_cap3:raw_mean ~ +.3f}} on raw counts in its fit on raw counts and {{E67/comparison.csv:kind=fit;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3:cal_mean ~ +.3f}} under the readout in its fit under the readout, [the APL-effect fits](#apl-effect-fits)).

The loss is higher in all three, through the pattern part (third row). Under the readout the breadth-2 family at a power of 0.5 ends {{diff:E71/fits.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_thrin0.5_k2:fit_apl_cal_rmse -- E71/input_readouts.csv:c2_base:apl_cal_rmse ~ .3f}} above the fit without the scaling and the family with the firing ceiling {{diff:E71/fits.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_thrin0.25_k2:fit_apl_cal_rmse -- E69/stats_variants.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2:apl_cal_rmse ~ .3f}} above the same ceiling's fit; on raw counts the two end {{diff:E71/fits.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_thrin0.5_k2:fit_apl_raw_rmse -- E71/input_readouts.csv:c2_base:apl_raw_rmse ~ .3f}} and {{diff:E71/fits.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_thrin0.25_k2:fit_apl_raw_rmse -- E69/stats_variants.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2:apl_raw_rmse ~ .3f}} above. The reference model's set ends {{diff:E71/fits.csv:thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplboth_thrin0.75_k2:fit_apl_cal_rmse -- E67/comparison.csv:kind=fit;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3:cal_loss ~ .3f}} above its fit under the readout ({{E67/comparison.csv:kind=fit;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3:cal_loss ~ .3f}}) and above the reference model as it stands; on raw counts it is about where the set's fit on raw counts is ({{E67/comparison.csv:kind=fit;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplraw_k2_cap3:raw_loss ~ .3f}}).

Under the readout the costs are two to four times the standard deviation of the breadth-2 family's loss over the eight wirings it has been fitted on ({{E72/spread.csv:readout=cal:sd_single ~ .3f}}), so they are not one wiring's accident, although the scaling itself was run on the real wiring only; on raw counts, where that standard deviation is {{E72/spread.csv:readout=raw:sd_single ~ .3f}}, the two costs are little more than one.

The fits reach the mean effect with less KC–KC inhibition, all but off in the breadth-2 family and in the reference model's set, with a higher common threshold in its place (last row), and with more KCs responding with APL off: the response rate with APL off is {{E71/fits.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_thrin0.5_k2:rate_ratio_off_over_on ~ .2f}}, {{E71/fits.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_thrin0.25_k2:rate_ratio_off_over_on ~ .2f}} and {{E71/fits.csv:thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplboth_thrin0.75_k2:rate_ratio_off_over_on ~ .2f}} times that with APL on in the three fits, in the order of the table, from {{E69/stats_variants.csv:e67cal_base:rate_ratio_off_over_on ~ .2f}}, {{E69/stats_variants.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2:rate_ratio_off_over_on ~ .2f}} and {{E69/stats_variants.csv:ref40_base:rate_ratio_off_over_on ~ .2f}} without the scaling (the flies' {{data:rate_ratio_fraction ~ .2f}}, 90 % interval {{data:rate_ratio_fraction.lo ~ .2f}} to {{data:rate_ratio_fraction.hi ~ .2f}}), which by itself raises the mean effect; the ratio was not held in the fits.

With the scaling the block on raw counts is about two thirds of the flies' in the breadth-2 family and half in the other two, the natural-source alignment with APL on is lower than without the scaling in all three, and ρ on odor-odor distances is lower in the two families of the first joint fit and about unchanged in the reference model's set.

**The release stays off the many-claw KCs, and the broad responders come back from other cells.** In all three fits the KCs with nine or more claws take a fifth or less of the responses that removing APL adds, where they took a third (the row on who is released), and the spread of the number of odors per KC with APL off comes inside the recordings' range (the row under it).

But between {{E71/fits.csv:thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplboth_thrin0.75_k2:fit_opk_off_8plus ~ .0%}} and {{E71/fits.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_thrin0.25_k2:fit_opk_off_8plus ~ .0%}} of the KCs again respond to eight or more odors with APL off, about as many as without the scaling and against the flies' {{data:noise_tnt_odors_per_kc_8plus ~ .0%}}, and with the power at 0.5 or 0.75 they are now KCs with few claws: the KCs of the breadth-2 family that respond to eight or more odors with APL off average {{lit:5.0 # computed from the archived response matrices of this fit (data/model_outputs/E71_input_scaled_threshold/, tag rate0.068_aplboth_thrin0.5_k2) and the claw counts of data/model_outputs/inputs/wPNKC_bouton_base.parquet, as release_stats in E71_input_scaled_threshold.py does for part A (the same computation reproduces part A's cells of input_readouts.csv); unrounded 4.96; not in a results table}} claws, from {{E70/opk_features.csv:key=e67__rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3;feature=n_claws:mean_8plus_off ~ .1f}} without the scaling, and those of the reference model's set {{lit:5.1 # computed from the archived response matrices of this fit (data/model_outputs/E71_input_scaled_threshold/, tag thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplboth_thrin0.75_k2) and the claw counts of data/model_outputs/inputs/wPNKC_bouton_base.parquet, as release_stats in E71_input_scaled_threshold.py does for part A (the same computation reproduces part A's cells of input_readouts.csv); unrounded 5.09; not in a results table}}, from {{E70/opk_features.csv:key=ref40;feature=n_claws:mean_8plus_off ~ .1f}}. The binarized mean APL effect returns with them, to between {{E71/fits.csv:thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplboth_thrin0.75_k2:responses_cosine__apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}} and {{E71/fits.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_thrin0.25_k2:responses_cosine__apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}} against the flies' {{data:apl_effect_binary_mean ~ +.3f}}, where the settings at fixed scales had brought it to between {{E71/input_readouts.csv:c2_a0.5:apl_bin_mean ~ +.3f}} and {{E71/input_readouts.csv:ref40_a0.75:apl_bin_mean ~ +.3f}}.

The breadth-2 family's distance from the flies' distribution of odors per KC with APL off is therefore back where it was (sixth row), with other cells as the broad responders. The other two families also leave fewer KCs silent and come closer to the flies' distribution, the reference model's set to about half the distance of its earlier fits, which were inside the band as well: its fits under the APL-effect loss were {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplraw_k2_cap3:opk_off_tv ~ .3f}} and {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3:opk_off_tv ~ .3f}} from the flies' distribution, and its fits with a firing ceiling {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E69_kc_firing_ceiling;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:opk_off_tv ~ .3f}} and {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E69_kc_firing_ceiling;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplbothopk_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:opk_off_tv ~ .3f}}.

In this family the flies' graded mean effect is reached through a response-set term that overshoots, carried by KCs that turn into broad responders when APL is removed; the scaling changes which cells those are, and a fit of the main target makes them again. The flies' own effect is not of another kind. Split by the number of odors each KC responds to ([the APL effect split by odors per KC](#apl-effect-by-class), further down in this section), it also rests on KCs that respond broadly when APL output is blocked, and the third of the mean effect that comes from products with values below the response criterion ([above](#readout)) is those KCs' weaker responses to their other odors.

Counted by the recordings' own criterion, in their z-scored units, the flies have two kinds of such KCs, a few that respond to eight or more odors and many that respond to four to seven, where the models have the first kind alone. That difference belongs to the unit: with each KC's responses in baseline-noise units the KCs at eight or more odors carry the flies' effect alone, as in the models ([the data side of the main target](#data-side), further down in this section). In either unit the flies have no route through amplitudes in place of broad responders.

**Read as the recordings are, the scaling is nearly free in the family with the firing ceiling.** The per-KC normalization of the recordings ([further down in this section](#per-kc-normalization)) reads every saved model as the KC data are produced: each KC's signal is put in units of its own standard deviation over the whole recording, and an odor's response is taken relative to the frames before it, so that a KC that responds to many odors has every one of its responses scaled down.

Read that way (the two rows of the second table that carry this reading) the breadth-2 family and the reference model's set lose as much with the scaling as under the calibrated readout, or more; under the recordings' own response criterion the reference model is itself inside the band on odors per KC with APL off, and its set with the scaling is further inside. The family with the firing ceiling loses {{diff:E73/by_variant.csv:folder=E71_input_scaled_threshold;tag=rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_thrin0.25_k2;reading_def=zcell_saturating;reading=graded:rmse -- E73/by_variant.csv:folder=E69_kc_firing_ceiling;tag=rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2;reading_def=zcell_saturating;reading=graded:rmse ~ .3f}}, a small part of what the loss varies by over wirings under the same reading ({{E73/by_variant.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;tag=wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed3_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;reading_def=zcell_saturating;reading=graded:rmse ~ .3f}} to {{E73/by_variant.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;tag=wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed2_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;reading_def=zcell_saturating;reading=graded:rmse ~ .3f}} over the seven re-drawn wirings of the breadth-2 family, fitted without a ceiling), and its distance from the flies' distribution of odors per KC with APL off is the smallest in the table.

If that reading becomes the definition of the model's side of the target, the firing ceiling together with the input-scaled threshold at a small power is the combination to fit under it. That fit has been made ([the APL effect split by odors per KC](#apl-effect-by-class)): under the reading it ends level with the fit without the scaling, but it gets there by weakening APL and KC–KC inhibition until its response rate at two or more spikes with APL on is {{E74/fits.csv:zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcell_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_thrin0.25_k2:rate_on ~ .3f}}, twice the flies' response rate and outside the band, so it is a measurement and not a candidate base; the question is open again with the fits' operating point held on two spikes.

**A single pseudo-recording of the breadth-2 fit is closer to the data's mean than a single pair of recordings is.** The comparison that [the high-firing KCs that survive APL](#high-firing-kcs) left open was made here, the trial-noise pipeline now saving every pseudo-recording.

One pseudo-recording with APL on paired with one with APL off (three trials each through [the matched trial noise](#fn-trial-noise), {{E71/partC_summary.csv:reading=matched_each:n ~ .0f}} pairs), scored against the KC data's mean per-pair effect as a model is, has a median APL-effect loss of {{E71/partC_summary.csv:reading=matched_each:rmse_median ~ .3f}} ({{E71/partC_summary.csv:reading=matched_each:rmse_min ~ .3f}} to {{E71/partC_summary.csv:reading=matched_each:rmse_max ~ .3f}}) and a median mean effect of {{E71/partC_summary.csv:reading=matched_each:mean_median ~ +.3f}}. One control recording paired with one recording with APL output blocked (TNT), scored against the mean of the remaining recordings, has {{E71/partC_summary.csv:model=KC data (E70 yardstick):rmse_median ~ .3f}} ({{E71/partC_summary.csv:model=KC data (E70 yardstick):rmse_min ~ .3f}} to {{E71/partC_summary.csv:model=KC data (E70 yardstick):rmse_max ~ .3f}}) and {{E71/partC_summary.csv:model=KC data (E70 yardstick):mean_median ~ +.3f}}.

The model's pairs vary far less than the flies': they have the trial noise, but one wiring and no differences between flies. The best fit on one wiring is therefore already as close to the data's mean as a single pair of recordings is, and what separates it from the floor is no more than single recordings show.

Averaged over four wirings and read through the same noise, as the data's mean is an average over flies and trials, the breadth-2 family has a loss on raw counts of {{E72/partE_noise.csv:group=population;level=match_on;transform=graded;distances=raw:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} with the noise matched to the control flies and {{E72/partE_noise.csv:group=population;level=match_off;transform=graded;distances=raw:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} with the noise matched to APL output blocked (TNT), against {{E71/input_readouts.csv:c2_base:apl_raw_rmse ~ .3f}} for the one wiring without noise ([the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population), the next subsection). The fit with the scaling was not put through the noise, being worse than the fit without it under both definitions.

**What the scaling gains is realism, and what it costs is the main target.** Every setting kept and every fit with the scaling is inside all four realism bands, the reference model's set comes to half its distance from the flies' distribution of odors per KC with APL off, and the spread of the number of odors per KC with APL off is inside the recordings' range in all three fits, which none of the three families is without the scaling.

The fit of the reference model's set has a common somatic threshold and APL scales within about a fifth of the baseline's and KC–KC inhibition all but off (last row of the second table). The fit with the firing ceiling keeps a common somatic threshold under half the baseline's, as the breadth-2 fit has, which is hard to defend, and at a power of 0.5 the scaling itself asks for thresholds from {{E71/fits.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_thrin0.5_k2:kc_thr_input_factor_min ~ .2f}} to {{E71/fits.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_thrin0.5_k2:kc_thr_input_factor_max ~ .2f}} times the common value; whether the thresholds of KCs vary that much with their claw input is a question for the physiology.

Without a firing ceiling the scaling at fixed scales makes few-claw KCs the highest-firing cells of the breadth-2 fit (the row of largest spike counts in the first table), which the fits undo (the same row of the second). Each fit is a local search from one start on the real wiring, the scaling has one functional form, a power of the summed claw weight, and as everywhere the pairs with paa, euc and -aPine rest on [ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations).

**What follows.** The input-scaled threshold does not join the base model under the present definitions of the target: it puts the release with APL off on other cells, as the flies' numbers ask, at two to four times what a draw of the wiring moves the loss under the readout. Its fit of the reference model's set is kept as that set's realism reference, not as a best model.

The best-models table is to be read with this result: the columns that match the flies' mean effect, under the readout or with the firing ceiling, do it with more broadly responding KCs with APL off than the flies have, their many-claw KCs, and when the release is moved off those cells a fit of the main target makes as many broad responders from others. What is taken up from here is with the pending work at the end of the page.

### The APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings: the model as a population of flies {#wiring-population}

**The breadth-2 APL-effect fit owes its standing to its family and not to the hemibrain wiring: fitted again on seven re-drawn wirings it ends around the same loss. One wiring's loss carries a draw term as large as the margins between recent fits, and the mean over wirings, the counterpart of data that are a mean over flies, has a lower loss, the whole gain in the pattern part. What is left is the same on every wiring: too little APL effect among the esters, where the flies have the block.**

Every loss by which the models above are ranked is one wiring's. A model has the hemibrain wiring with APL on and with APL off, while the data's per-pair APL effect is the mean over {{data:n_recordings_ctrl ~ .0f}} control recordings minus the mean over {{data:n_recordings_tnt ~ .0f}} recordings with APL output blocked (TNT), from different flies, so that what is particular to one fly's wiring is averaged out of the data and kept whole in the model.

The APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings fitted the best family of [the APL-effect fits](#apl-effect-fits) (breadth exponent 2, no per-claw threshold, no glomerulus gain; both definitions of the model's side in the loss, which on the real wiring scores as the fit under the readout does) again on seven re-drawn wirings, each from the real wiring's fitted parameters: four within-type claw permutations, and three shuffles matched to the real wiring on every glomerulus pair's count of shared KCs ([the wiring experiments](#wiring-feature)). The model's counterpart of the data's mean over flies is a mean over wirings: the pair distances are averaged over the wirings in each condition, and the APL effect and its loss are taken from the averages.

Solid line: the mean over the eight wirings. Dashed and dash-dotted lines: one shared parameter set, as the mean over the four wirings it was fitted to and over the four it never saw. **The standing is the family's, and one wiring is a noisy reading of it.** The eight wirings end between {{E72/spread.csv:readout=cal:min_single ~ .3f}} and {{E72/spread.csv:readout=cal:max_single ~ .3f}} under the readout, the real wiring ({{E72/spread.csv:readout=cal:real_single ~ .3f}}) in the middle, and between {{E72/spread.csv:readout=raw:min_single ~ .3f}} and {{E72/spread.csv:readout=raw:max_single ~ .3f}} on raw counts, where the real wiring ({{E72/spread.csv:readout=raw:real_single ~ .3f}}) is among the higher ones (the figure, and the first column of the second table). The hemibrain's exact wiring holds no special share of the match, so the family is the model to build on.

The standard deviation of the loss over the eight wirings, the draw term in what follows, is {{E72/spread.csv:readout=cal:sd_single ~ .3f}} under the readout and {{E72/spread.csv:readout=raw:sd_single ~ .3f}} on raw counts, as large as the margins by which the recent fits were ranked on the real wiring. A difference of about that size between two fits on one wiring does not tell them apart: such comparisons need both fits on the same re-drawn wirings, as the two comparisons further down were made.

**Averaged over wirings the loss is lower, and the gain is in the pattern.** Under the readout one wiring scores {{E72/curve.csv:n=1;readout=cal;stat=loss:mean ~ .3f}} on average, two wirings averaged {{E72/curve.csv:n=2;readout=cal;stat=loss:mean ~ .3f}}, four {{E72/curve.csv:n=4;readout=cal;stat=loss:mean ~ .3f}} and all eight {{E72/curve.csv:n=8;readout=cal;stat=loss:mean ~ .3f}}, which only one of the single wirings is below; on raw counts the same steps are {{E72/curve.csv:n=1;readout=raw;stat=loss:mean ~ .3f}}, {{E72/curve.csv:n=2;readout=raw;stat=loss:mean ~ .3f}}, {{E72/curve.csv:n=4;readout=raw;stat=loss:mean ~ .3f}} and {{E72/curve.csv:n=8;readout=raw;stat=loss:mean ~ .3f}}, below every single wiring. Most of the gain comes with the first few wirings.

The mean APL effect does not change with the averaging, so the whole gain is in the pattern part, and most of it in the pair-specific part: under the readout that part falls from {{E72/curve.csv:n=1;readout=cal;stat=pair_specific:mean ~ .3f}} for one wiring to {{E72/curve.csv:n=8;readout=cal;stat=pair_specific:mean ~ .3f}} for the eight and the per-odor part from {{E72/curve.csv:n=1;readout=cal;stat=per_odor:mean ~ .3f}} to {{E72/curve.csv:n=8;readout=cal;stat=per_odor:mean ~ .3f}}, and ρ on the per-pair APL effect rises (fifth row).

The data's mean is also a mean over trials. Four of the wirings (the real one, two claw permutations and one matched shuffle) read through [the matched trial noise](#fn-trial-noise) and then averaged have a loss on raw counts of {{E72/partE_noise.csv:group=population;level=match_on;transform=graded;distances=raw:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} with the noise matched to the control flies and {{E72/partE_noise.csv:group=population;level=match_off;transform=graded;distances=raw:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} with the noise matched to APL output blocked (TNT), against {{E72/partE_noise.csv:group=population;level=match_on;transform=graded;distances=det:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} for the same four without noise and {{E72/spread.csv:readout=raw:real_single ~ .3f}} for the real wiring alone, the number the family had been judged by (last column of the second table).

The two steps add: the noise raises the mean effect (from {{E72/partE_noise.csv:group=population;level=match_on;transform=graded;distances=det:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}} to {{E72/partE_noise.csv:group=population;level=match_on;transform=graded;distances=raw:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}} and {{E72/partE_noise.csv:group=population;level=match_off;transform=graded;distances=raw:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}} at the two noise levels; the flies' {{data:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}}) and the averaging lowers the pattern part. The noise of this reading is all shared between the odors of a trial, where only part of the flies' is; with the noise re-specified to the flies' shares the same four read {{E81/populations.csv:group=breadth-2 four;readout=raw;unit=z;kind=mix:loss ~ .3f}} ([the flies' variability across the three repeats](#repeat-structure)).

The mean over wirings is still not the data's design in one respect: each model wiring has both conditions, while the flies with APL on and those with APL off are different animals, and APL on from one wiring paired with APL off from another scores worse than a single wiring does. In one further respect the mean over wirings has since been made the data's: every wiring here has one input, the average over the ORN flies, where each fly behind the KC data had its own.

With each of nine ORN flies' own input on each of the eight wirings, the mean over the 72 model flies has a pattern part of {{E85/populations.csv:group=B1;unit=all;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} under the readout against {{E85/populations.csv:group=lab;unit=all;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} for the eight wirings at the averaged input, so the averaged input stands for the flies' inputs on the main target; what the input flies add is that single model flies then differ from one another about as much as single recordings do ([the ORN input as a population of flies](#input-population)).

![Left: the error common to the eight wirings, per pair: the per-pair APL effect of the mean over the wirings minus the KC data's, both means removed, under the calibrated readout (blue: the model's effect is too small; red: too large). Right: the correlation over the 120 pairs between each wiring's per-pair error and the common error.](results/E72_wiring_population/E72_common_error.png)

**What remains is common to the wirings, and it sits where the block is.** The pattern error of the mean over the eight wirings is what every wiring shares, and each wiring adds a smaller remainder of its own. Under the readout the per-pair errors of any two wirings correlate between {{E72/error_corr_cal.csv:P1:P3 ~ .2f}} and {{E72/error_corr_cal.csv:M2:M3 ~ .2f}} over the 120 pairs (on raw counts between {{E72/error_corr_raw.csv:P3:P4 ~ .2f}} and {{E72/error_corr_raw.csv:real:M1 ~ .2f}}).

In the common error the model's APL effect is too small on every pair among 2h, IaA, pa, eb, ep and ms (the largest, 2h with IaA, by {{E72/common_error_pairs.csv:odor_a=2h;odor_b=IaA:abs_common ~ .3f}} once the means are removed) and on eb with 1-8ol and 1-6ol, and too large on every pair among 1-8ol, 1-5ol, 1-6ol and 6al. These are the pairs of the block and around it: under the readout the flies' APL separates these esters from one another more than the model's does on every one of the eight wirings.

The block itself is smaller in the mean over wirings than on the real wiring (sixth row of the first table), whose block is the second largest of the eight; six of the seven re-drawn wirings have less, as shuffled wirings had in [the wiring experiments](#wiring-feature). No draw of the wiring removes this error, and averaging over wirings cannot: it is what a further mechanism has to supply.

The one rule about which KCs APL acts on that is the same on every wiring, a profile of APL's weight over the glomeruli, has since been tried and does not supply it ([the glomerulus profile of APL inhibition](#glomerulus-profile), at the end of this section), and neither does a fixed change of what reaches the KCs ([the input side of the error common to all wirings](#input-side)). Searched on several wirings at once, neither kind of change passes its test on wirings and recordings it was not fitted to, and what holds there is a small part of the error ([the input and APL's glomerulus profile fitted on several wirings at once](#cross-wiring-fit)).

**One parameter set serves every wiring.** One set of the four fitted parameters (the somatic threshold, the APL→KC and APL→bouton scales and the KC–KC scale) was fitted to the mean over four wirings (the real one, two claw permutations and one matched shuffle) and then run, nothing fitted, on the other four. On the wirings it never saw it costs {{diff:E72/partD_populations.csv:group=held-out wirings;variant=one shared set:raw_loss -- E72/partD_populations.csv:group=held-out wirings;variant=each wiring fitted alone:raw_loss ~ .3f}} on raw counts and {{diff:E72/partD_populations.csv:group=held-out wirings;variant=one shared set:cal_loss -- E72/partD_populations.csv:group=held-out wirings;variant=each wiring fitted alone:cal_loss ~ .3f}} under the readout against a fit of each wiring (last two columns of the first table), and on the wirings it was fitted to {{diff:E72/partD_populations.csv:group=fitted wirings;variant=one shared set:raw_loss -- E72/partD_populations.csv:group=fitted wirings;variant=each wiring fitted alone:raw_loss ~ .3f}} and {{diff:E72/partD_populations.csv:group=fitted wirings;variant=one shared set:cal_loss -- E72/partD_populations.csv:group=fitted wirings;variant=each wiring fitted alone:cal_loss ~ .3f}}: less than half of what one draw of the wiring moves the loss, inside all four realism bands.

Three of its parameters lie inside the range of the eight per-wiring fits and the APL→bouton scale just above it. The spread of the per-wiring fits, the KC–KC scale from {{E72/stats_variants.csv:wiring_label=P2:kc_kc_inh ~ .0f}} to {{E72/stats_variants.csv:wiring_label=P4:kc_kc_inh ~ .0f}} and the somatic threshold from {{E72/stats_variants.csv:wiring_label=P3:thr_factor ~ .2f}} to {{E72/stats_variants.csv:wiring_label=M2:thr_factor ~ .2f}} of the baseline's, is therefore how far a parameter can move on one wiring at nearly the same loss, not a different physiology for each wiring.

The APL-effect loss of the family on each wiring, on raw spike counts / through the calibrated saturating readout (lower is better): as fitted above, with a per-claw threshold of 40 Hz, and with the firing ceiling at its literature setting, each fitted on the same wiring and beside its difference from the fit without it. Last column: the fits of the first column on raw counts through the matched trial noise, the noise matched to the control flies / to APL output blocked (TNT). P and M are the claw permutations and the matched shuffles of the figure; a mean over wirings is the loss of the mean over those wirings

**The per-claw threshold costs on every wiring.** Among [the APL-effect fits](#apl-effect-fits) the family's lead needed the per-claw threshold absent, on the real wiring. The same family with a 40 Hz per-claw threshold, fitted on the four claw permutations as well, has a higher loss than the family without it on all five wirings and under both definitions, on each by more than the draw term, and in the mean over the five (second and third columns; the 40 Hz fits had the readout alone in their loss, so the like-for-like difference is the one under the readout).

What the threshold buys is the number of odors per KC, which moves toward the flies' in both conditions: in the mean over the five wirings the distance from the flies' distribution, both counted by the recordings' own criterion, is {{E72/partC_population.csv:family=40:opk_on_dist ~ .3f}} with APL on and {{E72/partC_population.csv:family=40:opk_off_dist ~ .3f}} with APL off, against {{E72/partC_population.csv:family=none:opk_on_dist ~ .3f}} and {{E72/partC_population.csv:family=none:opk_off_dist ~ .3f}} without it. It comes with a lower response rate ρ with APL on ({{E72/partC_population.csv:family=40:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}} against {{E72/partC_population.csv:family=none:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}}) and without the block on raw counts ({{E72/partC_population.csv:family=40:raw_block ~ +.3f}} against {{E72/partC_population.csv:family=none:raw_block ~ +.3f}}). Read as the recordings are produced ([the per-KC normalization of the recordings](#per-kc-normalization), the next subsection), the cost is less uniform: the threshold costs on four of the five wirings, by up to {{diff:E73/by_variant.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;tag=thr40_wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed3_rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3;reading_def=zcell_saturating;reading=graded:rmse -- E73/by_variant.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;tag=wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed3_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;reading_def=zcell_saturating;reading=graded:rmse ~ .3f}}, and on one the fit with it is lower by {{diff:E73/by_variant.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;tag=wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed2_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;reading_def=zcell_saturating;reading=graded:rmse -- E73/by_variant.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;tag=thr40_wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed2_rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3;reading_def=zcell_saturating;reading=graded:rmse ~ .3f}}.

**The firing ceiling's gain on raw counts holds on every wiring.** [The firing ceiling for the KCs](#firing-ceiling) had been fitted on the real wiring only. Fitted at its literature setting on three of the re-drawn wirings, each from that wiring's own fit, it leaves the loss under the readout where it was, to within the draw term, and lowers the loss on raw counts by about twice the draw term or more, on all four wirings, so that raw counts and the readout give nearly the same scores on each (fourth and fifth columns). The gain is the family's and not the hemibrain wiring's.

The mean over the four wirings with the ceiling scores on raw counts what it scores under the readout, and without any noise is below the mean of the same four without a ceiling read through the trial noise (last row). Read through the trial noise itself it is level with that mean ([the glomerulus profile of APL inhibition](#glomerulus-profile), at the end of this section). As on the real wiring, the fits with the ceiling end with more KCs responding with APL off (a response rate {{E72/partG_population.csv:family=40:ratio ~ .2f}} times that with APL on in the mean over the four, from {{E72/partG_population.csv:family=none:ratio ~ .2f}}; the flies' {{data:rate_ratio_fraction ~ .2f}}), which by itself raises the mean effect, and with about half the block on raw counts ({{E72/partG_population.csv:family=40:raw_block ~ +.3f}} against {{E72/partG_population.csv:family=none:raw_block ~ +.3f}}).

**Without a per-claw threshold the family responds to the weakest input.** The models with a per-claw threshold recruited a half to a tenth of the KCs the flies recruit at low concentration, and almost none for ma, whose ORN input is at the recorded concentration ([the per-claw threshold at low concentration](#low-concentration)).

- The breadth-2 fit, run on the same odors at its fitted parameters, recruits KCs for ma: about a third of the control flies' fraction without noise and half through the matched trial noise, three times what the same family has with the 40 Hz per-claw threshold, and with APL off about half of the fraction of the flies with APL output blocked (TNT) without noise and three quarters through it.
- For 2h at 10^-5, the other odor with input at the recorded concentration, it has about half of the flies' fraction without noise and the flies' fraction through the noise.
- For 2h at 10^-7 and farn at 10^-3, whose input is from a concentration ten times higher, it stays at a third to a half of the flies' fractions without noise, no better than the best of the models with a per-claw threshold.

The silence at the weakest input therefore belonged to the per-claw threshold, and neither the match to the 16-odor panel nor a response at low concentration needs one. What is left there is a shortfall of recruitment, by a factor of two to three for ma, which a change to the per-claw transfer would have to make up by adding drive at low input, not by softening a threshold. Read like for like since, that shortfall turns on the session's estimate of the input, on the set of flies and on how a response is counted ([the KCs' response rates at the weak odors read like for like](#weak-odor-rates)).

**Nothing here is bought with realism, and what the bands do not see is the same on every wiring.** Every fit of the experiment, on every wiring, and every mean over wirings is inside all four realism bands (the lower rows of the first table give the odors-per-KC distances by the recordings' own criterion, the bands' until 2026-11-10; by the present one every fit is inside as well): averaging over wirings changes the comparison and not the model, and the shared parameter set is as realistic as the per-wiring fits.

Beyond the bands the wirings agree with the real one. On each of the eight the KCs with nine or more claws take between a quarter and a third of the responses that removing APL adds, the number of odors per KC with APL off is spread more widely than in any recording ([the input-scaled KC threshold](#input-scaled-threshold)), and more KCs stay silent and more respond to eight or more odors than in the flies (last row of the first table).

The somatic threshold is under half the baseline's on every wiring and the APL→bouton scale near its bound, which are hard to defend (what that scale does in these fits, and what a smaller one costs, has been measured since: [the PN boutons' share of APL's inhibition](#bouton-share)), and as everywhere the pairs with paa, euc and -aPine rest on [ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations).

The release through the many-claw KCs is thus the family's and survives every draw, and a stricter reading of realism, one that also held the spread of the number of odors per KC to the recordings' range, would put every one of the eight wirings outside. What is taken up from here is with the pending work at the end of the page.

### The per-KC normalization of the recordings: the models read as the KC data are made {#per-kc-normalization}

**The KC data are each KC's fluorescence trace z-scored over its whole recording, so every response in them is measured against that KC's own spread.** Read through the same steps, the saved models keep nearly the order by APL-effect loss that the calibrated readout gives them, not the order of raw counts; fitted under that reading the best family ends where it stood under the readout, and the pattern part of its loss does not move. What the normalization had hidden is that the flies' responses grow with the number of odors a KC responds to much more than the models' do.

The per-KC normalization of the recordings started from the recorded values alone. If a KC's trace is divided by its standard deviation over the whole recording, the mean of the KC's squared responses over the recording's 51 presentations (the 16 odors and the solvent, three times each) cannot pass a bound set by the share of the recording that the response windows take up, however strongly the KC responds.

The recordings stop at such an edge, in all {{data:n_recordings_ctrl ~ .0f}} recordings of control flies and all {{data:n_recordings_tnt ~ .0f}} with APL output blocked (TNT): the largest per-KC mean square is {{data:ctrl_zcell_edge ~ .1f}} z² in the control flies and {{data:tnt_zcell_edge ~ .1f}} z² with APL output blocked (TNT), means over recordings, and the 99.9th percentile of a recording's KCs is only {{data:ctrl_zcell_edge_gap ~ .1f}} and {{data:tnt_zcell_edge_gap ~ .1f}} below it.

Synthetic cells with the recordings' trial structure show the edge only when the whole trace is z-scored: a z-score within each trial caps single trials well below the largest that the recordings hold, and a z-score against the frames before each odor leaves a long tail in place of an edge. Yang, who made the recordings, then confirmed the definition: each KC's trace z-scored over the whole recording, a response being the mean from 2 to 8 s after odor onset minus the mean over the 5 s before ([the footnote on baseline-noise units](#fn-baseline-noise-units) has it in full, with what it does to a KC's unit).

**Read the same way, the models are ordered as under the calibrated readout.** To read a model as the recordings were made, each model KC's spike counts are passed through a saturating map and placed in a simulated recording of the same 51 presentations, each response confined to its window, with frame noise and a slow drift (the drift set from the flies' KCs that respond to no odor). The trace is divided by its standard deviation over the session, a response is taken against the frames before it, and it counts as a response when its three-trial mean is above 1 z, as in the recordings; this is the per-KC reading.

Three numbers are set for each model on its counts with APL on and kept for APL off, so that the APL effect stays a prediction: the frame noise, so that the response rate is the control flies'; the map's half-saturation, so that the responders' mean amplitude is the control flies' {{data:ctrl_resp_amp_mean_z ~ .1f}} z; and the measurement noise of a response, so that a non-responding entry varies from trial to trial as in the control flies.

Every saved model with both conditions ({{E73/order.csv:reading=graded;present=present_cal:n_variants ~ .0f}} variants) was read this way and scored against the KC data as measured. Across them the APL-effect loss under the reading follows the loss under [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout), with a Spearman correlation of {{E73/order.csv:reading=graded;present=present_cal:rho_all ~ .2f}} between the two and a median change of the loss of {{E73/order.csv:reading=graded;present=present_cal:median_change_loss ~ +.3f}}, and not the loss on raw counts ({{E73/order.csv:reading=graded;present=present_raw:rho_all ~ .2f}}). The readout was a fair stand-in for the recordings' normalization; raw counts were not.

The lowest loss under the reading of any fit saved until then is that of [the firing ceiling for the KCs](#firing-ceiling) at its stronger setting ({{E73/key_models.csv:folder=E69_kc_firing_ceiling;tag=rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2;reading_def=zcell_saturating;reading=graded:rmse ~ .3f}}, with the flies' mean effect, {{E73/key_models.csv:folder=E69_kc_firing_ceiling;tag=rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2;reading_def=zcell_saturating;reading=graded:mean ~ +.3f}}). The breadth-2 APL-effect fit, the best fit under the readout without a ceiling, has a higher loss under the reading than under the readout because its mean effect is smaller there (first, third and sixth rows of the table below; its mean effect under the readout is {{E67/comparison.csv:kind=fit;tag=rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3:cal_mean ~ +.3f}}): part of the mean effect that the readout gave it came from the readout's compression of its strongest responders, which the per-KC normalization does not repeat.

The breadth-2 APL-effect fit and the current reference model, beside three fits made with the per-KC reading in the loss, each from its family's earlier optimum: the breadth-2 family, the same family with the firing ceiling at its literature setting, and the reference model's set with the firing ceiling at its stronger setting. A loss under the per-KC reading is the model's expectation over the reading's measurement noise, scored against the KC data as measured; raw is on raw spike counts and calibrated through the calibrated saturating readout

**Fitted under the reading, the best family ends where it stood under the readout.** Three fits were then made with the reading in the loss, in the APL-effect term and in the response-rate terms alike.

The breadth-2 family and the same family with the firing ceiling at the literature setting end level, each a little below its start (first two rows of the table), at the loss that the breadth-2 fit has under the readout; the reference model's set with the ceiling does not move and stays behind. The pattern part is where it was (fourth row; {{E67/comparison.csv:kind=fit;tag=rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3:cal_pattern ~ .3f}} for the breadth-2 fit under the readout), far above its floor, and ρ on the per-pair APL effect is no nearer its ceiling.

What differs between the two fits of the family is how they hold under the other definitions. The fit without the ceiling got its loss with a somatic threshold still further below the baseline's ({{E73/fits.csv:zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcell_k2_cap3:thr_factor ~ .2f}} of it, from {{E67/comparison.csv:kind=fit;tag=rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3:thr_factor ~ .2f}}) and a stronger APL→KC ({{E73/fits.csv:zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcell_k2_cap3:apl_factor_vs_e3 ~ .2f}} times the baseline's, from {{E67/comparison.csv:kind=fit;tag=rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3:apl_factor_vs_e3 ~ .2f}}), and it is worse than its start on raw counts and under the readout; the fit with the ceiling scores about the same under all three definitions (sixth row).

Through [the matched trial noise](#fn-trial-noise), the trials read through the reading, the order turns (seventh row). The fit without the ceiling improves, at the noise matched to APL output blocked (TNT) as well ({{E73/partB/zcell_noise.csv:model=E73-zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcell_k2_cap3;level=match_off;reading=graded:rmse ~ .3f}}), and the fit with the ceiling worsens ({{E73/partB/zcell_noise.csv:model=E73-zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcell_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2_cap3;level=match_off;reading=graded:rmse ~ .3f}} there), because the noise lowers its mean effect, as it does for the fit with the ceiling made before ({{E73/key_models.csv:folder=E69_kc_firing_ceiling;tag=rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2;reading_def=zcell_saturating_trials;reading=graded:rmse ~ .3f}} through the noise, from {{E73/key_models.csv:folder=E69_kc_firing_ceiling;tag=rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2;reading_def=zcell_saturating;reading=graded:rmse ~ .3f}} without it). The margin between the two is about twice what one draw of the wiring moves this family's loss under the readout ({{E72/spread.csv:readout=cal:sd_single ~ .3f}}), on one seed of the noise and on the real wiring only.

Under the reading the firing ceiling is thus no better than the family without it, and its case for joining the base model rests on raw counts and on realism (bounded spike counts, the spread of an odor's response over its KCs), not on this reading. On raw counts the case has since narrowed to single wirings and to the model without noise: as a mean over wirings read through the trial noise the two families are level ([the glomerulus profile of APL inhibition](#glomerulus-profile), at the end of this section).

**What the normalization had hidden.** In the flies a KC's unit grows with the number of odors the KC responds to ([the footnote](#fn-baseline-noise-units) has the ratios), so that the responders' mean amplitude, about {{data:ctrl_resp_amp_mean_z ~ .0f}} z whatever the KC's breadth, is in baseline-noise units nearly twice as large in the control flies' KCs that respond to eight odors as in those that respond to one (the last row but one of the table; few KCs respond to exactly eight odors with APL on, in the flies and in the models, so the values at eight are rough). The flat amplitude in z is strongly growing responses compressed by the normalization.

The models' responses grow much less: read the same way, their responders' amplitudes in baseline-noise units start lower and rise by a half to two thirds, their units hardly grow (the row above it), and with the firing ceiling both are lower still. The models' responses fill their sessions much less than the flies' do, so in the amplitudes the models are further from the flies than the comparison in z had said ([the low end of the readout](#readout) made it in z). The realism bands hold a model to which KCs respond, not to how strongly, and do not see this.

**The response criterion, and the realism bands.** Read this way a model is held to the flies' own criterion, a response above 1 z in a unit that belongs to each KC, in place of two or more spikes. Every model of the table then has fewer responses with APL off than it has at two spikes (the two rows on the response rates), and its distribution of odors per KC with APL off is nearer the flies' (the three rows on odors per KC).

The current reference model and its set with the ceiling, outside the band when their two-spike responses are set against the flies' responses above 1 z, are inside it once both sides are counted above 1 z: the flag had belonged to the comparison, a fixed criterion on one side against one that grows with how much a KC responds on the other, and not to the models. That was the comparison of the realism bands. They now count the flies' responses in baseline-noise units and the models' at two or more spikes, a fixed unit on each side, and the per-KC reading is reported beside them without deciding any, because its calibration sets the response rate with APL on whatever the model's firing ([the footnote on baseline-noise units](#fn-baseline-noise-units) has the change, the reasons for it and what it does to the flies' values).

**Realism, and the limits of the reading.** The three fits are inside all four realism bands (last row). Their response-rate terms were under the reading, whose calibration sets the response rate with APL on at every evaluation, so nothing in the loss held the number of KCs that fire. These fits moved their two-spike response rates little (the fit without the ceiling ends with {{E73/fits.csv:zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcell_k2_cap3:rate_ratio_off_over_on ~ .2f}} times as many responses with APL off as with APL on, inside the band, against the flies' {{data:noise_rate_ratio_fraction ~ .2f}}), but [a later fit made the same way left its operating point](#apl-effect-by-class), and fits now keep their response-rate terms on the two-spike count.

The reading has no calcium kinetics: a model's response is confined to its window, {{data:zcell_q_window ~ .0%}} of the recording, where the recordings' own edge implies {{data:zcell_q ~ .0%}}, the responses outlasting their windows. At that share the breadth-2 fit's loss under the reading is {{E73/key_models.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3;reading_def=zcell_saturating_q0.180;reading=graded:rmse ~ .3f}} in place of the first row's value, and the fit with the ceiling made before hardly moves ({{E73/key_models.csv:folder=E69_kc_firing_ceiling;tag=rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2;reading_def=zcell_saturating_q0.180;reading=graded:rmse ~ .3f}}, from the second row's {{E73/key_models.csv:folder=E69_kc_firing_ceiling;tag=rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2;reading_def=zcell_saturating;reading=graded:rmse ~ .3f}}). The drift and the measurement noise are one value for every model KC, where they differ between the flies' KCs.

The criterion does not account for the missing responses at [low concentration](#low-concentration) either: read within the session of its own panel, the current reference model has {{E73/low_conc.csv:model=ref40_68;map=saturating;panel=diag_mix;condition=on;odor=ma @ -7:frac_zcell ~ .1%}} of its KCs responding to ma @ -7 with APL on, as at two spikes, against {{E73/low_conc.csv:model=ref40_68;map=saturating;panel=diag_mix;condition=on;odor=ma @ -7:frac_data ~ .1%}} in the flies. As everywhere, the pairs with paa, euc and -aPine rest on [ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations). What is taken up from here is with the pending work at the end of the page.

### Which KCs carry the APL effect: the effect split by the number of odors each KC responds to {#apl-effect-by-class}

**Split by how many of the 16 odors a KC responds to, with a response counted as the recordings count it, above 1 z, the flies' APL effect rests on broadly responding KCs of two kinds, the few that respond to eight or more odors when APL output is blocked and the many that respond to four to seven.** The models make theirs with the first kind alone, in every best fit and on every wiring.

The difference belongs to that unit: with each KC's responses in baseline-noise units the flies' effect, too, sits in the KCs at eight or more odors alone (the data side of the main target, at the end of this section). In the z-scored units it is real, and it is not where the pattern error is: across the saved models a split closer to the flies' does not go with a lower pattern part, and a fit that is asked for the flies' split pays for it on the total.

[The input-scaled KC threshold](#input-scaled-threshold) left open which KCs carry the effect, in the flies and in the models. A pair's cosine similarity is a sum over KCs (the sum that [the low end of the readout](#readout) divided by whether its two entries are responses), so the per-pair APL effect can be divided among groups of KCs.

The APL effect split by odors per KC put every KC, in each condition, in one of the five groups of the realism band on odors per KC, by the number of the 16 odors it responds to in that condition (none, one, two or three, four to seven, eight or more; one to three are shown together below), and took each group's part of every pair's similarity. A class's APL effect is its part of the similarity with APL off minus its part with APL on, and the classes' effects add up to the pair's APL effect.

A KC can change class between the conditions, so the split says how much of each condition's similarity sits in KCs of a given tuning width; it needs no pairing of cells between the conditions, which the recordings cannot give, the control flies and the flies with APL output blocked (TNT) being different animals. In the recordings a response is a trial mean above 1 z, each genotype's class parts are averaged over its recordings, and the 90 % intervals are over recordings drawn again with replacement.

Every archived model with both conditions saved ({{E74/rank_correlations.csv:reading=zcell;subset=all variants:n ~ .0f}} variants) was read in two ways: through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout) with a response at two or more spikes, and as the recordings are produced, each KC in units of its own standard deviation over the session (the per-KC reading of [the subsection before this one](#per-kc-normalization)), with the recordings' criterion and through that reading's measurement noise, as ten pseudo-recordings of three trials, so that a model KC enters a class as a recorded KC does.

The per-pair APL effect of the KC data split by the number of odors a KC responds to in each condition. A class's share of the variance is the covariance of its effect with the whole effect across the 120 pairs over the variance of the whole effect, so the shares add up to 1; the similarity a class carries is its part of the cosine similarity between two odors, averaged over the 120 pairs

**By the recordings' own criterion the flies' APL effect rests on broadly responding KCs of two kinds.** The KCs that respond to eight or more odors, {{data:tnt_odors_per_kc_8plus ~ .1%}} of the KCs with APL output blocked (TNT) and almost none in the control flies, carry most of the mean effect and about half of its variance across pairs. Those that respond to four to seven odors, {{data:tnt_odors_per_kc_4_7 ~ .1%}} of the KCs with APL output blocked (TNT) against {{data:ctrl_odors_per_kc_4_7 ~ .1%}} in the control flies, carry the rest and a third of the variance.

The KCs that respond to one to three odors, two fifths of the KCs in either genotype, add nothing, and those that respond to none take a little away. The third of the mean effect that [the low end of the readout](#readout) found in products of a responder with a sub-threshold entry sits in the same broad KCs (third row): it is their weaker responses to their other odors, not the responses of weakly responding cells.

With the response criterion at 0.75 or 1.25 z in place of 1 z the class at four to seven carries {{data:apl_class_effect_4_7_z0.75 ~ +.3f}} or {{data:apl_class_effect_4_7_z1.25 ~ +.3f}} and the class at eight or more {{data:apl_class_effect_8plus_z0.75 ~ +.3f}} or {{data:apl_class_effect_8plus_z1.25 ~ +.3f}}: how the effect divides between the two kinds moves with the criterion and neither changes sign, so a model is compared with the flies at a matched criterion only. The flies therefore do not make the effect through the amplitudes of weak responses in place of broad responders, as the input-scaled KC threshold had read them: flies and models both make it through broad responders, the flies, by this criterion, through two kinds.

The second kind belongs to the criterion and its unit. With each KC's responses in baseline-noise units and the one threshold of the realism bands, the KCs at eight or more odors carry {{data:noise_apl_effect_class_8plus ~ +.3f}}, more than the whole mean effect of {{data:noise_apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}}, and those at four to seven {{data:noise_apl_effect_class_4_7 ~ +.3f}} ({{data:noise_apl_effect_class_4_7.lo ~ +.3f}} to {{data:noise_apl_effect_class_4_7.hi ~ +.3f}}): there the flies, like the models, make the effect with the broadest KCs alone ([the data side of the main target](#data-side), at the end of this section). What the rest of this subsection says about the class at four to seven is a comparison in the recordings' z-scored units, with both sides counted above 1 z.

A model's split is scored by the class-resolved loss: the root mean square, over the five classes and the 120 pairs, of the model's per-class effect minus the flies' (lower is better). Its floor, a resampled set of recordings scored against the measured one, is {{data:apl_class_rmse_floor ~ .3f}} ({{data:apl_class_rmse_floor.lo ~ .3f}} to {{data:apl_class_rmse_floor.hi ~ .3f}}), and one control recording paired with one recording with APL output blocked (TNT), scored against the mean of the others, has a median of {{data:apl_class_rmse_yardstick ~ .3f}}.

**Counted above 1 z, every best fit lacks the middle class, on every wiring.** In every model of the table but the one with the input-scaled threshold, the KCs at four to seven odors carry between a quarter and three fifths of what they carry in the flies, below the lower end of the data's interval; the KCs at eight or more odors carry the model's whole effect and more, and the KCs at one to three odors take away from it, where in the flies they add nothing. About half of the variance of the fits' pattern error across the pairs is in the class at four to seven, less in the reference model (the row on the pattern error, and the right panel of the figure).

Through the calibrated readout, with a response at two or more spikes, the same holds more strongly: in the breadth-2 fit the class at four to seven has an effect of {{E74/by_variant.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3;reading=cal2:eff_4_7 ~ +.3f}} and the class at eight or more {{E74/by_variant.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3;reading=cal2:eff_8plus ~ +.3f}}, at a class-resolved loss of {{E74/by_variant.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3;reading=cal2:class_rmse ~ .3f}} (left panel of the figure). The shortfall belongs to the family and not to the hemibrain wiring: fitted on each of the eight wirings of [the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population), the breadth-2 family has the class at four to seven between {{E74/by_variant.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;tag=wiring-curveball_within_type_matched-seed1_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;reading=zcell:eff_4_7 ~ +.3f}} and {{E74/by_variant.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;tag=wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed2_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;reading=zcell:eff_4_7 ~ +.3f}} under the per-KC reading, and at {{E74/wirings.csv:group=c2;reading=zcell:eff_4_7 ~ +.3f}} in the mean over the wirings.

**The models' moderately broad KCs are too broad already with APL on.** Under the per-KC reading the similarity that the class at four to seven carries with APL off is within a tenth of the flies' in every model of the table but the one with the input-scaled threshold, and with APL on it is two fifths to three fifths above the control flies', whose 90 % interval is {{E74/data_by_class.csv:criterion=1.0;quantity=level_on;class=4_7;term=total:lo ~ .3f}} to {{E74/data_by_class.csv:criterion=1.0;quantity=level_on;class=4_7;term=total:hi ~ .3f}} (the row on the similarity carried).

The class's shortfall in the APL effect is thus an excess with APL on: the KCs that respond to four to seven odors while APL is working carry more of the overlap between odors in the models than in the flies, so that removing APL adds less to them. The class at one to three odors is over with APL on in the same way. Through the calibrated readout the excess with APL on is there as well, and the class is short with APL off besides.

**A split closer to the flies' does not go with a lower pattern part.** If the missing class were what the pattern part of the APL-effect loss is made of, the archived models with a split nearer the flies' would be the ones with a lower pattern part. They are not: across the {{E74/rank_correlations.csv:reading=zcell;subset=all variants:n ~ .0f}} variants the Spearman correlation between the class-resolved loss and the pattern part is {{E74/rank_correlations.csv:reading=cal2;subset=all variants:rho_class_vs_pattern ~ +.2f}} through the calibrated readout and {{E74/rank_correlations.csv:reading=zcell;subset=all variants:rho_class_vs_pattern ~ +.2f}} under the per-KC reading, and across the {{E74/rank_correlations.csv:reading=zcell;subset=inside the two-spike bands:n ~ .0f}} of them inside the realism bands {{E74/rank_correlations.csv:reading=cal2;subset=inside the two-spike bands:rho_class_vs_pattern ~ +.2f}} and {{E74/rank_correlations.csv:reading=zcell;subset=inside the two-spike bands:rho_class_vs_pattern ~ +.2f}}.

In the whole archive, under the per-KC reading, the class at four to seven reaches the flies' interval only in models with a per-claw threshold, the claw coincidence rule or the input-scaled KC threshold, and where such a model can be set beside the same family without it, the pattern does not come with the class. The breadth-2 family with a 40 Hz per-claw threshold was fitted on the same five wirings as the family without it ([above](#wiring-population)). Under the per-KC reading it has the class at four to seven higher on every one of them, between {{E74/by_variant.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=thr40_rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3;reading=zcell:eff_4_7 ~ +.3f}} and {{E74/by_variant.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;tag=thr40_wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed4_rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3;reading=zcell:eff_4_7 ~ +.3f}} against {{E74/by_variant.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;tag=wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed1_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;reading=zcell:eff_4_7 ~ +.3f}} to {{E74/by_variant.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;tag=wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed2_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;reading=zcell:eff_4_7 ~ +.3f}}, through less of the class's similarity with APL on, and a higher pattern part on every one, between {{E74/by_variant.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;tag=thr40_wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed3_rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3;reading=zcell:apl_pattern ~ .3f}} and {{E74/by_variant.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;tag=thr40_wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed1_rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3;reading=zcell:apl_pattern ~ .3f}} against {{E74/by_variant.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;tag=wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed3_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;reading=zcell:apl_pattern ~ .3f}} to {{E74/by_variant.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;tag=wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed1_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;reading=zcell:apl_pattern ~ .3f}}.

**Asked for the flies' split, the family pays on the total.** The family with the firing ceiling was fitted again from its optimum under the per-KC reading (third model column) with the class-resolved loss added to its loss, weighted so that a fall in it counts about as much as an equal rise in the APL-effect loss (fourth column).

The class-resolved loss falls by a fifth, mostly because the class at eight or more odors comes down toward the flies'; the class at four to seven hardly moves, the mean APL effect moves away from the flies', the APL-effect loss rises by {{diff:E74/by_variant.csv:folder=E74_apl_effect_by_odors_per_kc;tag=zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcellclslin_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2_cap3;reading=zcell:apl_rmse -- E74/by_variant.csv:folder=E73_per_kc_normalization;tag=zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcell_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2_cap3;reading=zcell:apl_rmse ~ .3f}} and its pattern part stays where it was. No evaluation along the fit lowers the class-resolved loss without raising the APL-effect loss.

The family's good totals rest on class errors of opposite sign, too much effect in the KCs at eight or more odors and a loss of effect in those at one to three, that cancel pair by pair, and moving one class toward the flies' unbalances the other. The rise is about what one draw of the wiring moves the loss ({{E72/spread.csv:readout=cal:sd_single ~ .3f}} under the readout) and the fit was made on the real wiring only, so its size is a single reading; that the pattern part does not fall is what the archive says as well.

**With the input-scaled threshold the family reaches the middle class only by leaving its operating point.** The same experiment made the fit that the input-scaled KC threshold had left as the one to try ([above](#input-scaled-threshold)): the family with the firing ceiling and the threshold scaled at a power of 0.25, fitted under the per-KC reading (fifth model column).

Under that reading its APL-effect loss ends {{diff:E74/by_variant.csv:folder=E73_per_kc_normalization;tag=zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcell_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2_cap3;reading=zcell:apl_rmse -- E74/by_variant.csv:folder=E74_apl_effect_by_odors_per_kc;tag=zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcell_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_thrin0.25_k2;reading=zcell:apl_rmse ~ .3f}} below the fit without the scaling, within a draw of the wiring; its class at four to seven is inside the flies' interval; the KCs with nine or more claws take {{E74/released_by_claws.csv:model=fit S;reading=zcell;group=9+:share_added ~ .0%}} of the responses that removing APL adds, where they take {{E74/released_by_claws.csv:model=reading ceiling;reading=zcell;group=9+:share_added ~ .0%}} without the scaling; and under the recordings' criterion its distribution of odors per KC with APL off is {{E74/fits.csv:zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcell_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_thrin0.25_k2:fit_zcell_opk_off_tv ~ .3f}} from the flies', against {{E73/fits.csv:zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcell_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2_cap3:fit_zcell_opk_off_tv ~ .3f}}. It gets there by leaving the model's operating point.

In the fits under the per-KC reading the response-rate terms of the loss were computed under the recordings' criterion, and the reading is calibrated at every evaluation to the flies' response rate with APL on, so the number of KCs that fire was free. This fit used the freedom. It weakened the inhibition, APL→KC from {{E71/fits.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_thrin0.25_k2:apl_factor_vs_e3 ~ .2f}} to {{E74/fits.csv:zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcell_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_thrin0.25_k2:apl_factor_vs_e3 ~ .2f}} and APL→bouton from {{E71/fits.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_thrin0.25_k2:aplpn_factor_vs_e3 ~ .2f}} to {{E74/fits.csv:zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcell_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_thrin0.25_k2:aplpn_factor_vs_e3 ~ .2f}} times the baseline's and the KC–KC scale from {{E71/fits.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_thrin0.25_k2:kc_kc_inh ~ .1f}} to {{E74/fits.csv:zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcell_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_thrin0.25_k2:kc_kc_inh ~ .1f}}, at a common somatic threshold that stayed near {{E74/fits.csv:zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcell_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_thrin0.25_k2:thr_factor ~ .2f}} of the baseline's, until its response rate at two or more spikes with APL on is {{E74/fits.csv:zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcell_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_thrin0.25_k2:rate_on ~ .3f}}, from {{E71/fits.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_thrin0.25_k2:rate_on ~ .3f}} at its start and against a band of 0.045 to 0.085.

Through the calibrated readout and on raw counts it is {{diff:E74/fits.csv:zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcell_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_thrin0.25_k2:fit_apl_cal_rmse -- E73/fits.csv:zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcell_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2_cap3:fit_apl_cal_rmse ~ .3f}} and {{diff:E74/fits.csv:zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcell_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_thrin0.25_k2:fit_apl_raw_rmse -- E73/fits.csv:zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcell_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2_cap3:fit_apl_raw_rmse ~ .3f}} worse than the fit without the scaling, its class-resolved loss is the highest of the table, and its class at four to seven is the difference between two levels that are both above the flies' (the row on the similarity carried). It is a measurement of what that freedom allows, not a candidate base.

Fits now keep their response-rate terms on the two-spike criterion, and the per-KC reading is reported beside the realism bands without deciding them ([the footnote on baseline-noise units](#fn-baseline-noise-units)), so the fit that was asked for the flies' split, made under the same rule though inside the bands at its optimum, is likewise a measurement and not a candidate for the best-models table.

**Realism.** The split itself changes no model. Of the two fits made here, the one asked for the flies' split is inside all four bands at its optimum (the last two rows of the table), with a common somatic threshold of {{E74/fits.csv:zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcellclslin_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2_cap3:thr_factor ~ .2f}} and an APL→bouton scale of {{E74/fits.csv:zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcellclslin_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2_cap3:aplpn_factor_vs_e3 ~ .2f}} times the baseline's, as hard to defend as in the fits it starts from; the one with the input-scaled threshold is outside three of the bands, as described. The only fit that reached the flies' middle class thus did it outside the bands, and the fit that was asked for the split stayed inside them and paid on the main target.

The split counts the flies' responses by the recordings' own criterion of 1 z, and the models' under the per-KC reading by the same criterion, not in the [baseline-noise units](#fn-baseline-noise-units) in which the realism bands count the flies' responses, and in those units the flies have no middle class for a model to reach, their KCs at four to seven odors carrying none of the effect ([the data side of the main target](#data-side)); as everywhere the pairs with paa, euc and -aPine rest on [ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations).

**What follows.** Which KCs carry the effect becomes a statistic of its own, reported for later fits beside the realism bands, and in both units of the flies' responses: counted above 1 z the flies' effect sits in two classes of broadly responding KCs, and a model that has the total right with one of them has it by cancellation, while in baseline-noise units it sits in the broadest class alone, in the flies as in the models ([the data side of the main target](#data-side)). It is not a route to a lower pattern part.

What is left of the pattern is looked for pair by pair, in the errors that remain whatever the classes do. A mechanism that makes moderately broad KCs less broad with APL on at no cost on the total, which nothing in the archive does, is wanted only if the main target stays in the recordings' z-scored units. What is taken up from here is with the pending work at the end of the page.

### The glomerulus profile of APL inhibition: whether APL's weight by glomerulus carries the error common to the wirings {#glomerulus-profile}

**The error that every wiring shares is in almost every saved model, and least in a few that change what reaches the KCs, whose own errors are no smaller.** A profile of APL's weight over the glomeruli, the one rule about which KCs APL acts on that is the same on every wiring, does not carry it: one glomerulus at a time moves the per-pair APL effect little, and a profile over all of them, built from those single changes, lowers the loss on the real wiring and raises the block to the flies' but does not predict the pairs of an odor it was built without. Read as a population of wirings through the trial noise, the family with the firing ceiling is level on raw counts with the family without it.

[The APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population) left an error that no draw of the wiring removes, the common error: under the calibrated readout the APL effect of the breadth-2 family is too small among 2h, IaA, pa, eb, ep and ms and too large among 1-8ol, 1-5ol, 1-6ol and 6al, on every wiring. A draw changes which KC has which claws and keeps the glomeruli, so a rule written per glomerulus is the one way to say which KCs APL acts on that is the same on every wiring. The glomerulus profile of APL inhibition asked whether such a rule carries the common error.

A profile is one score per glomerulus by which APL's weight is multiplied, at one of three sites: the cell (a KC's whole APL weight, once for each claw it has from the glomerulus), the claw (the weight on the claws from the glomerulus) or the bouton (the weight on the glomerulus's boutons), with the mean factor held at 1.

Everything was run on the breadth-2 APL-effect fit on the real wiring (the first model column of the first table [above](#wiring-population)), at its fitted parameters. At every point the APL scale was set again so that the number of responses with APL on stayed the fit's, and the run with APL off is the fit's own, since APL's weights do nothing there. Values are through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout) unless raw counts are named: under it the fit has the flies' mean effect, and its loss is nearly all pattern.

**The common error is in almost every saved model.** For each of the {{E75/report_scalars.csv:archive_n_variants:value ~ .0f}} saved variants with both conditions, the part of its own pattern error that lies along the common error was measured as a projection: 1 if the variant has as much of the common error as the mean over the eight wirings has, 0 if it has none. Under the readout the median is {{E75/report_scalars.csv:archive_median_cal_proj_common:value ~ .2f}} (on raw counts {{E75/report_scalars.csv:archive_median_raw_proj_common:value ~ .2f}}): the error is older than the best family and belongs to nothing particular to it.

Only {{E75/report_scalars.csv:archive_n_cal_proj_below_0.5:value ~ .0f}} of the {{E75/report_scalars.csv:archive_n_variants_cal:value ~ .0f}} variants scored under the readout carry less than half of it. Two are settings of the oracle co-responder suppression, which is told which KCs to take out. The others change what reaches the KCs: four settings of a weaker antennal-lobe normalization, which passes more of the ORNs' contrast on to the PNs, on the early hemibrain model with one unit per KC and no separate claws (down to {{E75/archive_vs_common_error.csv:folder=E3_drive_dependent_gain;tag=hemibrain-wd20_inhadd10000:cal_proj_common ~ .2f}}; that model as it is carries {{E75/archive_vs_common_error.csv:folder=E3_drive_dependent_gain;tag=hemibrain-wd20_inhadd31.4088:cal_proj_common ~ .2f}}); Hallem's receptor data alone as the input for ms, paa, B-myr and 1-8ol ({{E75/archive_vs_common_error.csv:folder=E38_hallem_input;tag=B_thr70_gain1.5_k2_cap3_hallem_only:cal_proj_common ~ .2f}}); the lowest two of the random wirings of that early model ({{E75/archive_vs_common_error.csv:folder=E4_substrate;tag=uniform_sp0.05_seed9:cal_proj_common ~ .2f}} and {{E75/archive_vs_common_error.csv:folder=E4_substrate;tag=hemidraw_sp0.05_seed4:cal_proj_common ~ .2f}}); and a 130 Hz per-claw threshold followed by a cap on each claw's input ({{E75/archive_vs_common_error.csv:folder=E16_claw_saturation;tag=bouton_thr130_tanh50:cal_proj_common ~ .2f}}).

APL's inhibition of the PN boutons scaled down or up, by contrast, leaves the common error where it was ({{E75/archive_vs_common_error.csv:folder=E3_drive_dependent_gain;tag=bouton_pnapl_x1:cal_proj_common ~ .2f}} to {{E75/archive_vs_common_error.csv:folder=E3_drive_dependent_gain;tag=bouton_pnapl_x2:cal_proj_common ~ .2f}}). None of these eight has a smaller pattern part than the breadth-2 fit ({{E75/archive_vs_common_error.csv:folder=E3_drive_dependent_gain;tag=hemibrain-wd20_inhadd10000:cal_err_rms ~ .3f}} to {{E75/archive_vs_common_error.csv:folder=E16_claw_saturation;tag=bouton_thr130_tanh50:cal_err_rms ~ .3f}}, against {{E75/sensitivity_map.csv:base:cal_pattern ~ .3f}}): they carry a different error, not a smaller one.

**One glomerulus at a time moves little.** With APL's weight doubled on one glomerulus, for each of the 36 glomeruli with ORN input at each of the three sites, the loss stays between {{E75/report_scalars.csv:map_x2_cal_loss_min:value ~ .3f}} and {{E75/report_scalars.csv:map_x2_cal_loss_max:value ~ .3f}}; with the weight halved, on the eight glomeruli per site whose doubling had moved the effect most, between {{E75/report_scalars.csv:map_half_cal_loss_min:value ~ .3f}} and {{E75/report_scalars.csv:map_half_cal_loss_max:value ~ .3f}}. The fit's own loss is {{E75/sensitivity_map.csv:base:cal_loss ~ .3f}} and the floor {{data:apl_effect_rmse_floor ~ .3f}}, so the best single change gains {{diff:E75/sensitivity_map.csv:base:cal_loss -- E75/report_scalars.csv:map_half_cal_loss_min:value ~ .3f}}. Nor do glomeruli changed together add up: a set of four or eight changed at once moves the per-pair effect by well under the sum of its members' single changes.

**A profile fitted through the single changes fails the test set for it.** For each site, scores for all 36 glomeruli (ridge-penalized, no factor beyond four either way) were fitted so that the single changes, added up, cancel the common error. The test was fixed before the fit and had two parts. Fitted without one odor, a profile had to remove 15 % or more of the common error's squared sum on that odor's 15 pairs. Fitted to the effect of one half of the recordings, it had to lower the error against the other half in 90 of 100 random splits.

The profiles fitted through the single-glomerulus changes, by the site at which they act: the share of the common error's squared sum that the added-up changes remove, and the splits of the recordings won

| statistic | cell | claw | bouton | cell and claw<br>together |

No site passes both parts. The claw and the bouton fail both. The cell, alone or with the claw, passes the first and fails the second, and that failure is in the recordings: two of the {{data:n_recordings_tnt ~ .0f}} recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) have much lower distances than the other six, and the cell profile wins {{E75/report_scalars.csv:split_cell_apart_won:value ~ .0f}} of the {{E75/report_scalars.csv:split_cell_apart_n:value ~ .0f}} splits that put those two in different halves and {{E75/report_scalars.csv:split_cell_together_won:value ~ .0f}} of the {{E75/report_scalars.csv:split_cell_together_n:value ~ .0f}} that put both in one. A half with both and a half with neither are different targets, so this part of the test measured the recordings more than the profile; what the two recordings do to the target is in [the data side of the main target](#data-side), the next subsection: they are stronger than the other six and not different in pattern, and the mean over all eight stands.

**Simulated, the cell profile helps the real wiring and not a left-out odor.** By the plan a failed test closed the experiment. Because the failed part had read the recordings, and both parts rested on single changes that do not add up, the cell profile was simulated all the same, as a diagnostic in stages that kept the test's thresholds.

Of the strengths tried, half its scores (every factor at its square root) is the one at which its change takes away the largest share of the common error: were the change it makes on the real wiring the same on every wiring, {{E75/report_scalars.csv:d2_stage1_transfer_x0.5:value ~ .0%}} of it (15 % was asked), where the same scores permuted across the glomeruli would add to the error (two draws).

The next stage failed. The sixteen profiles each fitted without one odor, simulated at the same strength and scored on that odor's pairs, remove {{E75/report_scalars.csv:d2_stage2_pooled_heldout:value ~ .1%}} of the common error there, pooled, against the 15 % asked and the {{E75/profile_cv.csv:profile=cell;variant=ridge:loo_odor_reduction ~ .1%}} that the added-up changes had predicted. They help most for B-myr, IaA, pa and paa ({{E75/report_scalars.csv:d2_stage2_fold_B-myr:value ~ .0%}} of the common error on B-myr's pairs) and add to the error for 6al, t2h, 2-but and -aPine. The splits of the recordings with the two recordings kept apart did not run, and neither did the fits with a profile on several wirings, for which the test was the gate.

A fixed profile of APL's weight over the glomeruli, found by adding up single-glomerulus changes, therefore does not carry the common error. The result goes no further than that: scores fitted directly in simulation, on several wirings at once, were not tried here (they have been since, and carry a small part of the common error to wirings and recordings they were not fitted to, short of the test set for them: [the input and APL's glomerulus profile fitted on several wirings at once](#cross-wiring-fit)), nor was APL inhibition that depends on the odor at the scale of a bouton (one form of it, inhibition that grows with a bouton's or a claw's own input, has since been emulated and does not lower the pattern part: [the input side of the error common to all wirings](#input-side); another, inhibition that follows the calyx space that glomeruli share, has since been tested as a proxy on the input, from connectome tables whose use is on hold, and its reading is withheld: [the APL calyx maps against the connectome](#apl-calyx-maps)).
