**On the real wiring the profile lowers the loss and makes the block.** At half its scores the cell profile lowers the fit's loss by {{diff:E75/sensitivity_map.csv:base:cal_loss -- E75/report_points.csv:D2s1_cell_ridge_x0.5:cal_loss ~ .3f}}, about what one draw of the wiring moves this family's loss ({{E72/spread.csv:readout=cal:sd_single ~ .3f}}), and all of it in the pattern part: ρ on the per-pair APL effect rises, both group errors shrink, and the block under the readout, which a block term in the loss had not raised in this fit ([the APL-effect fits](#apl-effect-fits)), comes to the flies' (first six rows). The same scores permuted leave the loss where it was or raise it ({{E75/report_points.csv:D2s1_cell_perm1_x0.5:cal_loss ~ .3f}} and {{E75/report_points.csv:D2s1_cell_perm2_x0.5:cal_loss ~ .3f}}). The mean effect falls a little, and on raw counts, where it was short already, the loss rises (seventh row).

At the full scores the loss is the same ({{E75/report_points.csv:D2s1_cell_ridge_x1:cal_loss ~ .3f}}), with a lower pattern part ({{E75/report_points.csv:D2s1_cell_ridge_x1:cal_pattern ~ .3f}}), a larger block ({{E75/report_points.csv:D2s1_cell_ridge_x1:cal_block ~ +.3f}}) and a smaller mean effect, and at twice the scores it is above the fit's ({{E75/report_points.csv:D2s1_cell_ridge_x2:cal_loss ~ .3f}}). The doubled four do half as much for the loss and as much for the block.

These are gains on one wiring. Neither change was run on a re-drawn wiring here (run on the seven since, the two lower the pattern part of the mean over them by {{E83/existing_changes.csv:change=A1_ridge_x0.5;unit=draws7:z8_gain ~ .4f}} and {{E83/existing_changes.csv:change=A1_C2_four_x2;unit=draws7:z8_gain ~ .4f}}, where they gain {{E83/existing_changes.csv:change=A1_ridge_x0.5;unit=real:z8_gain ~ .4f}} and {{E83/existing_changes.csv:change=A1_C2_four_x2;unit=real:z8_gain ~ .4f}} on the real wiring: [the input and APL's glomerulus profile fitted on several wirings at once](#cross-wiring-fit)), and the left-out odors say what the profile's gain is: 36 scores fitted to these 120 pairs, not a rule that holds for the pairs of an odor it was fitted without.

**With flies and trials both in the model, the firing ceiling's lead on raw counts is gone.** The same experiment made the check that the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings had left open ([above](#wiring-population)): the family with the firing ceiling at its literature setting, on the four wirings it has been fitted on (the real one, two claw permutations and one matched shuffle), read through [the matched trial noise](#fn-trial-noise) and then averaged over the wirings, as the family without a ceiling had been.

The breadth-2 family without and with the firing ceiling as a mean over the same four wirings, each wiring with its own fit, on raw spike counts: without noise, and through the trial noise matched to the control flies / to APL output blocked (TNT)

| statistic | KC data | the breadth-2 family<br>no firing ceiling | the same family<br>firing ceiling<br>literature setting |
|---|---|---|---|
| APL-effect loss, without noise (lower is better; KC data: the floor of the loss) | {{data:apl_effect_rmse_floor ~ .3f}} | {{E72/partE_noise.csv:group=population;level=match_on;transform=graded;distances=det:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} | {{E75/partE_noise.csv:group=population;level=match_on;transform=graded;distances=det:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} |
| APL-effect loss, through the trial noise (lower is better; KC data: the floor of the loss) | {{data:apl_effect_rmse_floor ~ .3f}} | {{E72/partE_noise.csv:group=population;level=match_on;transform=graded;distances=raw:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} / {{E72/partE_noise.csv:group=population;level=match_off;transform=graded;distances=raw:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} | {{E75/partE_noise.csv:group=population;level=match_on;transform=graded;distances=raw:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} / {{E75/partE_noise.csv:group=population;level=match_off;transform=graded;distances=raw:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} |
| mean APL effect, without noise | {{data:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}} | {{E72/partE_noise.csv:group=population;level=match_on;transform=graded;distances=det:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}} | {{E75/partE_noise.csv:group=population;level=match_on;transform=graded;distances=det:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}} |

Without noise the mean over the four wirings with the ceiling is far below the mean without it; through the noise the two are level, apart by well under what one draw of the wiring moves the loss on raw counts ({{E72/spread.csv:readout=raw:sd_single ~ .3f}}). The noise raises the mean APL effect of the family without the ceiling and lowers that of the family with it, to nearly the same value, short of the flies' (third and fourth rows), and the pattern parts are the same (last row).

On each of the four wirings singly the fit with the ceiling is still the lower one through the noise (between {{E75/partE_noise.csv:group=E72-wiring-curveball_within_type_matched-seed1_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2_cap3;level=match_on;transform=graded;distances=raw:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} and {{E75/partE_noise.csv:group=E72-wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed1_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2_cap3;level=match_on;transform=graded;distances=raw:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} at the noise matched to the control flies, against {{E72/partE_noise.csv:group=E72-wiring-curveball_within_type_matched-seed1_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;level=match_on;transform=graded;distances=raw:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} to {{E72/partE_noise.csv:group=E72-wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed2_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;level=match_on;transform=graded;distances=raw:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} without it, the last column of the second table [above](#wiring-population)): averaging over wirings helps the family without the ceiling more. Read as the data are made, a mean over flies and over trials, the ceiling thus gives no clear gain on raw counts, as it gave none under the per-KC reading ([above](#per-kc-normalization)); its lead there belongs to the model without noise and to single wirings, and what it adds beyond that is realism, bounded spike counts and the spread of an odor's response over its KCs.

The trial noise of this reading is all shared between the odors of a trial, where only part of the flies' is. Re-specified to the flies' shares it gives {{E81/populations.csv:group=breadth-2 four;readout=raw;unit=z;kind=mix:loss ~ .3f}} without the ceiling and {{E81/populations.csv:group=firing-ceiling four;readout=raw;unit=z;kind=mix:loss ~ .3f}} with it, apart by less than one draw of the wiring moves the loss, so the reading holds ([the flies' variability across the three repeats](#repeat-structure)).

**Realism.** A profile acts only with APL on, and every point keeps the fit's number of responses there, so the response rates, their ratio and everything with APL off are the fit's own; what a profile can change is which odors keep their responses with APL on. With the half-strength profile and with the doubled four the response rate ρ with APL on rises and the distribution of odors per KC stays where it was, and both are inside all four bands, counted as the bands count now and as they did until 2026-11-10 (lower rows of the table on the real wiring).

The profile's scores stay well inside the factor of four allowed. One point of the single-glomerulus runs left a band: four times the weight at the boutons of the eight glomeruli of the block-specific set of the breadth × shared-input APL rule took the response rate ρ with APL on to {{E75/report_points.csv:bouton_E15_eight_x4:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}} (by the recordings' own criterion; its responses were not saved), and no later stage used it.

Which KCs carry the effect does not change either: through the calibrated readout, with a response at two or more spikes, the mean per-pair APL effect carried by the KCs that respond to four to seven odors is {{E75/report_points.csv:D2s1_cell_ridge_x0.5:class_eff_4_7 ~ +.3f}} with the half-strength profile and {{E75/sensitivity_map.csv:base:class_eff_4_7 ~ +.3f}} without it ([the APL effect split by odors per KC](#apl-effect-by-class)). What the bands do not see is the fit's as well: the release through the many-claw KCs when APL is removed, a somatic threshold under half the baseline's and an APL→bouton scale near its bound ([above](#wiring-population)). As everywhere, the pairs with paa, euc and -aPine rest on [ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations), so the scores of the glomeruli that mainly carry those odors are in part scores for a mismatched input.

**What follows.** The common error stays the target. APL's fixed targeting by glomerulus is left without support as its source in this family, though not excluded, and the per-odor APL oracle had already shown that how many KCs APL removes for each odor does not set the pattern ([above](#apl-effect-parts)).

The few saved models with little of the common error all change what reaches the KCs. They carry a different error, not a smaller one, so they say where to look and not what works, and that is where the next mechanisms were looked for: in the best family no fixed change of the input carries the common error either ([the input side of the error common to all wirings](#input-side), at the end of this section), and searched on several wirings at once neither a profile nor an input passes its test, a profile carrying a small part of the error to wirings and recordings it was not fitted to ([the input and APL's glomerulus profile fitted on several wirings at once](#cross-wiring-fit)). What is taken up from here is with the pending work at the end of the page.

### The data side of the main target: the unit of the flies' responses, the recordings one by one, and fits to the effect in baseline-noise units {#data-side}

**The unit in which each KC's responses are taken moves the mean of the flies' APL effect and not its pattern.**

- In baseline-noise units, the unit of the realism bands, the mean effect is about a third larger than in the recordings' z-scored units, the pattern across pairs is the same within its floor, and the saved models keep their order on raw counts. In those units the KCs that respond to eight or more odors carry the flies' effect alone.
- The two recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) that stand apart from the other six are stronger and not different, so the mean over all eight stands as the target, and neither a weaker APL nor a shifted somatic threshold makes their state in the model.
- Fitted to the effect in baseline-noise units, the family with the firing ceiling raises its mean effect by more than half of what was missing, at a cost on the pattern and with more broad responders, and read through the trial noise it keeps little of the gain.

Every loss elsewhere on this page is against the flies' per-pair APL effect computed from the recordings as they were made, each KC's trace z-scored over its whole recording. That unit grows with how much a KC responds, which is why the realism bands now count the flies' responses in baseline-noise units ([footnote](#fn-baseline-noise-units)); the target itself stayed on the z-scored values, and what the choice of unit does to it was not known. Nor was it known what the target owes to two of the {{data:n_recordings_tnt ~ .0f}} recordings with APL output blocked (TNT), whose distances are much lower than those of the other six and through which a test on split halves of the recordings had failed ([the glomerulus profile of APL inhibition](#glomerulus-profile)).

The data side of the main target measured both from the recordings and the saved models: the effect in every unit the recordings allow, every saved model scored against it, and the recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) taken one by one. It then moved the model along its own two axes, the strength of APL's output and the somatic threshold, to see whether either makes what sets the two recordings apart, and fitted the best family to the effect in baseline-noise units.

**The unit moves the mean and not the pattern.** The per-pair APL effect was computed again with each KC's trial means in baseline-noise units, as the raw change of the KC's signal, and as that change divided by the KC's mean fluorescence, by its mean signal or by each trial's signal before the odor. Every one of these units gives a larger mean effect than the z-scored values, between {{E76/data_units.csv:unit=dff_fcmean;values=graded:mean ~ +.3f}} and {{data:noise_apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}} against {{data:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}} (figure, left): the z-score divides a KC's responses by a spread that its own responses enlarge, and the KCs that respond most carry the effect.

The pattern hardly moves. Across the 120 pairs, ρ on the per-pair APL effect between each of these units and the z-scored one is {{E76/data_units.csv:unit=dff_fctrial;values=graded:rho_ref ~ .2f}} to {{E76/data_units.csv:unit=dff_fcmean;values=graded:rho_ref ~ .2f}}, and with both means removed the two effects differ by a root mean square of {{E76/data_units.csv:unit=dff_fcmean;values=graded:pattern_diff_ref ~ .3f}} to {{E76/data_units.csv:unit=dff_fctrial;values=graded:pattern_diff_ref ~ .3f}}, less than the floor of the pattern part (figure, middle).

In every unit the pairs among 2h, IaA, pa, eb, ep and ms have a larger effect than the mean over all pairs and the pairs among 1-8ol, 1-5ol, 1-6ol and 6al a smaller one, the two groups of the common error. The floor of the loss, the floor of its pattern part and the ceiling on ρ on the per-pair APL effect are nearly the same in the two units (table).

The saved models follow: scored on raw counts against the effect in baseline-noise units, the {{E76/rank_correlations_units.csv:readout=raw;unit=noise;part=loss;variants=all:n ~ .0f}} saved variants with both conditions keep the order they have against the z-scored effect, with a Spearman correlation of {{E76/rank_correlations_units.csv:readout=raw;unit=noise;part=loss;variants=all:spearman ~ .2f}} between the two losses and {{E76/rank_correlations_units.csv:readout=raw;unit=noise;part=pattern;variants=all:spearman ~ .2f}} between the two pattern parts. What changes is the mean part, which grows for every model, since no saved model's mean effect on raw counts reaches the flies' in these units. Under [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout), calibrated again in the same units, the pattern parts keep their order as well ({{E76/rank_correlations_units.csv:readout=cal;unit=noise;part=pattern;variants=all:spearman ~ .2f}}) and the losses less closely ({{E76/rank_correlations_units.csv:readout=cal;unit=noise;part=loss;variants=all:spearman ~ .2f}}). The mean part of the APL-effect loss is thus set by a choice on the data's side, and the pattern part is not.

**In baseline-noise units the broadest KCs carry the effect alone.** The split of the effect by the number of odors a KC responds to ([above](#apl-effect-by-class)) does depend on the unit, because the unit decides what counts as a response.

With a response counted above 1 z the flies' effect sat in two classes, the KCs that respond to eight or more odors and those that respond to four to seven. With a response counted above the one threshold of baseline-noise units, the first class carries the whole effect and a little more, and the second carries nothing, its 90 % interval holding zero (seventh and eighth rows of the table; figure, right). The two kinds of broad responders of that subsection are therefore a reading in the recordings' z-scored units, in which a KC's unit grows with how much it responds.

In the units the realism bands use, the flies make the effect as the models do: read through the calibrated readout with a response at two or more spikes, the breadth-2 APL-effect fit has {{E74/by_variant.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3;reading=cal2:eff_8plus ~ +.3f}} in the class at eight or more odors and {{E74/by_variant.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3;reading=cal2:eff_4_7 ~ +.3f}} in the class at four to seven. What still differs is below the broadest class: the model's classes at four to seven and at one to three odors both take from its effect (the second {{E74/by_variant.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3;reading=cal2:eff_1_3 ~ +.3f}}), where the flies' class at four to seven carries nothing and their KCs at one odor and at two or three odors carry {{data:noise_apl_effect_class_1 ~ +.3f}} and {{data:noise_apl_effect_class_2_3 ~ +.3f}}.

**In their distances the two strongest recordings are stronger, not different.** The recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) differ among themselves in level far more than the control flies' do. In the z-scored units, as in the rest of this paragraph unless the other unit is named, two of them have mean distances of {{E76/recording_ranges.csv:genotype=TNT two:mean_dist_z_min ~ .2f}} and {{E76/recording_ranges.csv:genotype=TNT two:mean_dist_z_max ~ .2f}}, where the other six have {{E76/recording_ranges.csv:genotype=TNT six:mean_dist_z_min ~ .2f}} to {{E76/recording_ranges.csv:genotype=TNT six:mean_dist_z_max ~ .2f}} and the control recordings {{E76/recording_ranges.csv:genotype=TNT3c:mean_dist_z_min ~ .2f}} to {{E76/recording_ranges.csv:genotype=TNT3c:mean_dist_z_max ~ .2f}}, and the effect computed against the two alone is more than twice the effect against the six (tenth row).

A first look had found that the step from the six to the two has another pattern across pairs than the step from the control flies to the six, the ρ between the two steps being near zero. Set against the other ways of splitting the recordings, that is not a difference.

Any split of the eight into six and two pulls this ρ negative, because the six's mean enters the two steps with opposite signs; the actual split ranks {{E76/axis_tests.csv:reading=z;genotype=TNT:rank_rho_steps ~ .0f}} of the {{E76/axis_tests.csv:reading=z;genotype=TNT:n_splits ~ .0f}} splits, counted from the lowest, and the two recordings' own steps from the six agree with each other more than two recordings do in most splits (eleventh and twelfth rows; figure below). The same holds in baseline-noise units and with each recording's cosine corrected for trial-to-trial noise (by the correction then in use, which is too low in the level of the distances: [the flies' variability across the three repeats](#repeat-structure)).

The two are unusual in their level alone, and what makes them strong is the pairs among 2h, IaA, pa, eb, ep and ms, which blocking APL output brings far closer in them: the effect over those 15 pairs is {{E76/subset_floors.csv:unit=z;subset=two:ester ~ +.3f}} against the two and {{E76/subset_floors.csv:unit=z;subset=six:ester ~ +.3f}} against the six. Of what was looked at then, nothing recorded with the flies sets the two apart beforehand, neither the time since the toxin was induced nor the number of KCs. Within the session one thing does: the response rates of the other six run down over the three repeats and those of the two do not ([the flies' variability across the three repeats](#repeat-structure)).

The frame-by-frame traces have since added two things: the responses of the two decay about three times faster than those of every other recording, and the stimulus record of one of them says that APL was not labelled, so that whether the two were measured like the others is a question for the experimenter ([the time course of the APL effect in the flies' traces](#trace-time-course)). Until it is answered the mean over all eight stands as the target, with the six given beside it, and the failed test on split halves is as it was read, a half with both of the two recordings and a half with neither being different in level.

The common error is not made by the two either: against the six alone it has the root mean square it has against all eight ({{E76/common_error_subsets_summary.csv:target=six_z:rms ~ .3f}} and {{E76/common_error_subsets_summary.csv:target=eight_z:rms ~ .3f}}) and the same sign in both groups of pairs, with about half of its part among 1-8ol, 1-5ol, 1-6ol and 6al gone ({{E76/common_error_subsets_summary.csv:target=six_z:err_alcohol ~ +.3f}} against {{E76/common_error_subsets_summary.csv:target=eight_z:err_alcohol ~ +.3f}}), and against the effect in baseline-noise units it is as large ({{E76/common_error_subsets_summary.csv:target=eight_noise:rms ~ .3f}}).

![Each recording with APL output blocked (TNT) against the control flies' mean (Yang's z in the panels is the recordings' z-scored unit). Left: each recording's APL effect, the mean over the 120 pairs with the standard deviation across pairs (triangles: the means over the pairs among 2h, IaA, pa, eb, ep and ms and over the pairs among 1-8ol, 1-5ol, 1-6ol and 6al; orange: the two strongest recordings), in z-scored units (top) and in baseline-noise units (bottom). Right: ρ across the 120 pairs between the step from the control flies to six recordings and the step from those six to the other two, for every split of the eight recordings into six and two (top), and between the two left-out recordings' own steps (bottom); the diamond is the actual split.](results/E76_data_side_target/E76_recordings.png)

**The model's own axes do not make the two recordings.** If the two were flies in which the toxin blocked more of APL's output, or whose KCs were more excitable, a model could make their state by itself.

Two models were moved along both axes at fixed parameters, the breadth-2 APL-effect fit and the family with the firing ceiling at its stronger setting as fitted again here (second model column of the table below): APL's output to the KCs and to the boutons scaled to three quarters, a half, a quarter and an eighth with its inputs unchanged, and the somatic threshold shifted by a tenth and by a fifth either way, with APL on and with APL off.

Neither axis reaches the two. APL removed altogether is the most that a block can give, a mean effect of {{E76/model_axes.csv:experiment=E67_apl_effect_fits;readout=raw;axis=block;point=base_off:effect_mean ~ +.3f}} and {{E76/model_axes.csv:experiment=E76_data_side_target;readout=raw;axis=block;point=base_off:effect_mean ~ +.3f}} in the two models on raw counts against the two recordings' {{E76/subset_floors.csv:unit=z;subset=two:mean ~ +.3f}}, and a threshold a fifth higher or lower with APL off leaves the second model's between {{E76/model_axes.csv:experiment=E76_data_side_target;readout=raw;axis=thr_off;point=thr1.2_off:effect_mean ~ +.3f}} and {{E76/model_axes.csv:experiment=E76_data_side_target;readout=raw;axis=thr_off;point=thr0.8_off:effect_mean ~ +.3f}}. The last step of the block in that model, from an eighth of APL's output to none, agrees with the flies' step from the six to the two at ρ={{E76/model_axes.csv:experiment=E76_data_side_target;readout=raw;axis=block;point=base_off:step_rho_step2_z ~ .2f}} across the 120 pairs, as well as the two recordings agree with each other, but it ends at the level of all eight recordings and not of the two; no step along the threshold comes near it.

In baseline-noise units the six and the two have the same response rate relative to the control flies' (last row of the table above), so there the two are not further along a block at all: they have as many responses as the six and a larger effect. Read as a population of six model flies at the six's ratio of response rates and two at the two's, as the model was read as a population of wirings, the second model's pattern part hardly moves ({{E76/populations.csv:experiment=E76_data_side_target;readout=raw;unit=z;axis=block:pattern ~ .3f}} against {{E76/populations.csv:experiment=E76_data_side_target;readout=raw;unit=z;axis=block:homog_pattern ~ .3f}} for one model fly) and its loss rises ({{E76/populations.csv:experiment=E76_data_side_target;readout=raw;unit=z;axis=block:loss ~ .3f}} against {{E76/populations.csv:experiment=E76_data_side_target;readout=raw;unit=z;axis=block:homog_loss ~ .3f}}), because the six then sit at a partial block and the mean falls. The spread among the recordings is thus not a term missing from the comparison, and the two recordings' state is not one that the model reaches through a weaker APL or a lower threshold.

**Fitted to the effect in baseline-noise units, the best family stops short of the mean and pays on the pattern.** Against the effect in baseline-noise units the mean part of the loss, which the firing ceiling had nearly closed against the z-scored effect ([above](#firing-ceiling)), is open again: the family with the ceiling at its stronger setting is a third above the floor against the z-scored effect and at about twice the floor against this one (fourth and first rows of the table, first model column). Three fits asked how much of it the family can close.

The family was fitted again from its optimum, first with only the response-rate terms of its loss against the flies' rates in baseline-noise units, as the realism bands now count them, and then with the APL-effect terms against the effect in baseline-noise units as well; the reference model's set with the same ceiling, which with its larger mean effect starts level with the family against this effect, was fitted the second way from its own optimum.

- The first fit hardly moves, its loss against the z-scored effect changing by less than one draw of the wiring moves the loss on raw counts ({{E72/spread.csv:readout=raw:sd_single ~ .3f}}): the change of the bands' unit left the best fit where it was.
- The second raises the mean effect by {{diff:E76/fits.csv:nu_rate0.068_aplbothdnu_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_mean -- E76/fits.csv:nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_mean ~ .3f}} and lowers the loss against the effect it was fitted to by a quarter. It stops {{diff:data:noise_apl_effect_mean -- E76/fits.csv:nu_rate0.068_aplbothdnu_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_mean ~ .3f}} short of the flies' mean, at one and a half times the floor; its pattern part rises, its ρ on the per-pair APL effect falls (second and third rows), and against the z-scored effect it is worse than before (fourth row).
  - It makes the larger effect with more responses with APL off at the same response rate with APL on, through a higher somatic threshold ({{E76/fits.csv:nu_rate0.068_aplbothdnu_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:thr_factor ~ .2f}} of the baseline's, from {{E76/fits.csv:nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:thr_factor ~ .2f}}), a weaker APL→bouton scale ({{E76/fits.csv:nu_rate0.068_aplbothdnu_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:aplpn_factor_vs_e3 ~ .2f}} times the baseline's, from {{E76/fits.csv:nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:aplpn_factor_vs_e3 ~ .2f}}) and less than half the KC–KC inhibition (a scale of {{E76/fits.csv:nu_rate0.068_aplbothdnu_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:kc_kc_inh ~ .1f}}, from {{E76/fits.csv:nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:kc_kc_inh ~ .1f}}).
- The reference model's set makes the same move and ends at a higher loss than the family's fit, with the lowest ρ on the per-pair APL effect of the five columns, so it does not come back as a base.

**Through the trial noise little of the gain is left.** The first two fits were put through [the matched trial noise](#fn-trial-noise), ten pseudo-recordings of three trials, and scored on the three-trial means, as the recordings are.

The noise lowers the mean APL effect of both, as it does for the fits with the ceiling made before ([above](#glomerulus-profile)), and that of the fit to the effect in baseline-noise units more (seventh row). The two then differ on the loss by about what one draw of the wiring moves it (sixth row). Both are about a third short of the flies' mean effect in baseline-noise units and at more than twice the floor of the loss, where against the z-scored effect, through the same noise, they are at {{E76/partF_noise.csv:model=E76-nu_rate0.068_aplbothdnu_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2;level=match_on;transform=graded;distances=raw;unit=z:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} to {{E76/partF_noise.csv:model=E76-nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2;level=match_off;transform=graded;distances=raw;unit=z:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}}, against a floor of {{data:apl_effect_rmse_floor ~ .3f}}.

The pattern part through the noise is about where it is without it ({{E76/partF_noise.csv:model=E76-nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2;level=match_on;transform=graded;distances=raw;unit=noise:apl_effect_rmse_centered ~ .3f}} and {{E76/partF_noise.csv:model=E76-nu_rate0.068_aplbothdnu_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2;level=match_on;transform=graded;distances=raw;unit=noise:apl_effect_rmse_centered ~ .3f}} at the noise matched to the control flies). Read as the recordings are made, fitting to the effect in baseline-noise units therefore buys little: through the noise the mean part is again the larger part of both fits' loss against that effect, as it was against the z-scored effect before the firing ceiling.

**Realism.** The three fits are inside all four realism bands, as the two they start from are (last row). The fits to the effect in baseline-noise units paid for the larger mean in breadth with APL off.

At an unchanged response rate with APL on, the family has more responses with APL off, so that the ratio of the two rates moves from near the flies' toward the upper end of the flies' interval and of the band (ninth row), and more of its KCs respond to eight or more odors with APL off, where it already had more than the flies (tenth row); the reference model's set does the same. In the family the distance of the odors-per-KC distribution from the flies' with APL off grows, and in both it stays well inside its band (eleventh row).

KC–KC inhibition, which no band measures, falls to less than half in both. A fit held at the flies' ratio of response rates would likely end further from the flies' mean, so the shortfall given above is the least this family leaves open. The parts on the recordings change no model, and as everywhere the pairs with paa, euc and -aPine rest on [ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations).

**What follows.** Which unit the flies' side of the main target is held to is a choice about its mean part, like the choice of the model's readout, and it is not yet made; the mean over all eight recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) stands in either unit. The pattern part and the order of the models on raw counts do not depend on the choice, so until it is made the families are ranked on the pattern part, and the mean part is given against both effects.

If the target moves to baseline-noise units, the mean part is open again for every model, and more responses with APL off is a route that the fit has already taken, at a cost; what the flies have there and the models lack is responses that grow with a KC's breadth ([the per-KC normalization of the recordings](#per-kc-normalization)). Two later readings qualify this: weighting a fit's spike counts by the KC's breadth moves its mean effect by {{diff:E80/breadth_weighted.csv:tag=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2;p_is_flies=True;target=noise:mean -- E80/breadth_weighted.csv:tag=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2;p=0.0;target=noise:mean ~ +.3f}} at most, and the comparison of raw counts with the effect in baseline-noise units is one at the model's 0.5 s odor pulse, the same fit's mean effect on raw counts being {{E80/pulse.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held:raw_mean ~ +.3f}} at the flies' 2 s pulse against {{E80/pulse.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse0.5_fixed:raw_mean ~ +.3f}} ([the flies' pulse in the model and the remaining candidates for the common error](#remaining-candidates)), and {{E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=B2_fit0_tau3;kernel=counts:raw_mean ~ +.3f}} there once the ceiling's adaptation outlasts the odor ([the flies' recording protocol in the model](#flies-protocol)).

The split of the effect by odors per KC is given in both units from here on. The state of the two strongest recordings, the pairs among 2h, IaA, pa, eb, ep and ms far closer with APL output blocked (TNT), becomes a target for mechanisms that change what reaches the KCs, where the common error is largest (the fixed changes of the input screened in the next subsection, [the input side of the error common to all wirings](#input-side), do not lower the common error; they were not scored against the two recordings alone).

Whether the two were measured like the other recordings is a question that the traces have since raised for the experimenter, their responses decaying about three times faster ([the time course of the APL effect in the flies' traces](#trace-time-course)). What is taken up from here is with the pending work at the end of the page.

### The input side of the error common to all wirings: whether a change of what reaches the KCs carries it {#input-side}

**A change of what reaches the KCs does not carry the error that every wiring shares, as far as a fixed change of the input can tell.**

- About two fifths of the common error's squared sum is of the kind that a change acting with APL on and with APL off alike reaches.
- On the real wiring no handle the model has on its input lowers the pattern part of the APL-effect loss by more than a small fraction of what one draw of the wiring moves it, APL inhibition that grows with a bouton's or a claw's own input raises it, and every one of these changes would add to the common error if it carried over to other wirings.
- An input searched within a factor of two against half of the recordings holds for the other half on the real wiring and, at the size the search gave it, not on re-drawn wirings, and the two halves do not give the same factors; the search had overshot, and at 0.6 of its size the same input has since been found to hold on four other wirings and on the half of the recordings that it was not searched against ([the input and APL's glomerulus profile fitted on several wirings at once](#cross-wiring-fit)).
  - Its controls hold and a second draw of the search carries as much, while a search on a second split of the flies does not, so that it carries a small part of the common error, less than the test set for it asks ([the controls and the replication of the reduced searched input](#reduced-input)).
- Other input for the weak odors does not help the best family.

[The glomerulus profile of APL inhibition](#glomerulus-profile) found no fixed profile of APL's weight over the glomeruli that carries the common error, and found that the few saved models with little of it all change what reaches the KCs, each on an earlier model and with an error of its own. The input side of the error common to all wirings asked the question in the best family: whether a change of the input lowers the common error there.

Everything is on the breadth-2 APL-effect fit (the first model column of the first table of [the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population)), and values are through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout) unless raw counts are named. Under the readout the fit has the flies' mean effect and its loss is nearly all pattern, so the pattern part is what a change has to lower: {{E77/partA_fits.csv:fit=C2;readout=cal:apl_effect_rmse_centered ~ .3f}} on the real wiring and {{E72/population.csv:group=all:cal_pattern ~ .3f}} for the mean over the eight wirings, the common error, against a floor of {{E66/data_floor_parts.csv:data=graded;stat=apl_effect_rmse_centered:mean ~ .3f}}. The flies' side is the mean over all eight recordings with APL output blocked (TNT), the target that stands, with the six that are alike beside it where named ([the data side of the main target](#data-side)).

The breadth-2 APL-effect fit on the real wiring: as fitted, fitted again from its own parameters on two other inputs for the weak-input odors, and with each claw's input capped at 250 Hz, the setting with the lowest pattern part in the screen further down. **Other input for the weak odors does not help the best family.** The fit was made again from its own parameters on two other inputs: with [Hallem's receptor data](#hallem-input) for ms, paa, B-myr and 1-8ol, and with the input that the bounded oracle had searched for the seven weak-input odors on the reference model ([above](#gap-pairs)). With Hallem's data the loss is {{diff:E77/partA_fits.csv:fit=H;readout=cal:apl_effect_rmse -- E77/partA_fits.csv:fit=C2;readout=cal:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} higher and the mean effect short again (second model column). The error on the five pairs of ms with 2h, IaA, pa, eb and ep nearly doubles, from {{E77/partA_fits.csv:fit=C2;readout=cal:err_ms_pairs_z8 ~ +.3f}} to {{E77/partA_fits.csv:fit=H;readout=cal:err_ms_pairs_z8 ~ +.3f}}, with Hallem's response of DL1 to ms several times the lab's.

With the searched input the loss is {{diff:E77/partA_fits.csv:fit=S;readout=cal:apl_effect_rmse -- E77/partA_fits.csv:fit=C2;readout=cal:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} above the fit's, less than one draw of the wiring moves it ({{E72/spread.csv:readout=cal:sd_single ~ .3f}}), and what the input adds is a higher response rate ρ with APL on, which that search had raised through its penalty on the odors' response fractions (third model column). Neither input lowers the loss, so the weak odors' input is not where this family's error is, and the lab's input stays.

**About two fifths of the common error is within the reach of a change of the input.** A change of the input acts with APL on and with APL off alike: it moves a pair's distance in both conditions. If a model's distances with APL on follow from its distances with APL off by a relation of its own, such a change moves a pair along that relation, and the part of the error that it reaches in this way is the part that comes from where the model's distances with APL off differ from the flies'.

The pattern error was therefore [split into three terms that add up to it](#fn-inherited-split): the inherited part, the error a model would have if it followed the flies' relation between the two conditions exactly, starting from its own distances with APL off; the difference between the model's relation and the flies'; and the two sides' pair-by-pair departures from their own relations, the block among them.

For the mean over the eight wirings the inherited part is {{E77/inherited_parts.csv:folder=E72 members;tag=mean8;readout=cal;target=z8;data_curve_fit=insample:share_inherited ~ .0%}} of the common error's squared sum, and {{E77/inherited_parts.csv:folder=E72 members;tag=mean8;readout=cal;target=z6;data_curve_fit=insample:share_inherited ~ .0%}} against the six recordings that are alike; with the flies' relation fitted on halves of the recordings it lies between {{E77/report_scalars.csv:inherited_halves_cal_q05:value ~ .0%}} and {{E77/report_scalars.csv:inherited_halves_cal_q95:value ~ .0%}}. The departures hold {{E77/inherited_parts.csv:folder=E72 members;tag=mean8;readout=cal;target=z8;data_curve_fit=insample:share_pair_specific ~ .0%}}, and the difference between the two relations offsets a little ({{E77/inherited_parts.csv:folder=E72 members;tag=mean8;readout=cal;target=z8;data_curve_fit=insample:share_curve ~ +.2f}} as a share; the three add to one). Without its inherited part the pattern part of the mean over the eight wirings would be {{E77/inherited_parts.csv:folder=E72 members;tag=mean8;readout=cal;target=z8;data_curve_fit=insample:pattern_rms_without_inherited ~ .3f}} in place of {{E77/inherited_parts.csv:folder=E72 members;tag=mean8;readout=cal;target=z8;data_curve_fit=insample:pattern_rms ~ .3f}}.

Most of the common error is thus in what APL does to particular pairs, which a change shared by the two conditions does not reach in this way. Read since from the flies' own responses, on the spike counts of the fits, this part is not in the form of APL's inhibition either: an inhibition that grows with an odor's response over all the KCs nearly gives the flies' effect when it is applied to the flies' responses without APL, and applied to the model's responses with APL off it gives no more than the model's own APL does.

What the split assigns to particular pairs then lies, by that reading, in which KCs respond without APL and how strongly, which the distances with APL off do not show. It does not lie in how many KCs each odor recruits there alone: with that set to the flies' on four wirings the pattern part does not fall, and the same reading then puts a part of what is left on the side of the model's APL ([the form of APL's inhibition in the flies' own responses](#inhibition-form)). The split is not a bound on what a search can do on one wiring, as the last part of this subsection shows.

**Two descriptions of the common error came with the split.**

- Taken apart by odor ([above](#apl-effect-parts)), an odor's term in the common error, its share of the error on every pair it is in, follows how much more its response fraction grows in the model than in the flies when APL is removed: where the model gains more responses than the flies, its APL effect on the odor's pairs is too large.
  - Across the 16 odors the two correlate at Pearson r {{E77/report_scalars.csv:per_odor_share_gain_corr_cal_z8:value ~ .2f}} against all eight recordings and {{E77/report_scalars.csv:per_odor_share_gain_corr_cal_z6:value ~ .2f}} against the six that are alike (the flies' responses counted by the recordings' own criterion), so this is a lead and not a result, and one that leans on the two strongest recordings; the per-odor part of an error is, besides, the part that the recordings pin down less firmly ([above](#apl-effect-parts)).
- And the model's antennal lobe evens out the odors' total drive: summed over the glomeruli, the model's PN rates lie between {{E77/pn_totals.csv:odor=B-myr:pn_sum ~ .0f}} and {{E77/pn_totals.csv:odor=2h:pn_sum ~ .0f}} Hz for the 16 odors, where the summed ORN responses run from {{E77/pn_totals.csv:odor=B-myr:orn_sum_pos ~ .0f}} Hz for B-myr to {{E77/pn_totals.csv:odor=1-6ol:orn_sum_pos ~ .0f}} Hz for 1-6ol.

**No handle on the input lowers the pattern part, and each would add to the common error.** Six handles that the model has on its input were screened on the fit at fixed settings: a weaker antennal-lobe normalization; other input for the weak odors with nothing fitted again; each odor's input compressed or expanded across glomeruli at an unchanged sum; a cap on each claw's input; a more equal weight for the glomeruli, by per-glomerulus drive normalization or by each glomerulus's number of claws; and bouton vesicle depletion.

At every setting the somatic threshold and the APL scale were set again until the numbers of responses with APL off and with APL on were the fit's, with the breadth weights computed again for the changed input. Beside them ran two [oracle](#fn-oracle) emulations that act with APL on only, the run with APL off being the fit's own: APL's weight on each bouton, or on each claw, multiplied by a power of that bouton's or claw's own input to the odor. For each setting, the change it makes to the per-pair APL effect on the real wiring was also set against the common error: the transfer is the share of the common error's squared sum that the change would remove if it were the same on every wiring.

The handles on the fit's input and the two emulations, each at its setting with the lowest pattern part: the pattern part through the calibrated readout, the APL-effect loss on raw counts, and the transfer, the share of the common error's squared sum that the setting's change on the real wiring would remove if it were the same on every wiring (negative: it would add that share)

| bouton vesicle depletion (the weaker of two settings) | {{E77/screen.csv:point_id=S6_p0.03_tau1:cal_pattern ~ .3f}} | {{E77/screen.csv:point_id=S6_p0.03_tau1:raw_loss ~ .3f}} | {{E77/gate.csv:point_id=S6_p0.03_tau1:cal_transfer_all ~ +.2f}} |
| emulation, APL on only: APL's weight on a bouton in proportion to the bouton's own input | {{E77/screen.csv:point_id=L1_p1:cal_pattern ~ .3f}} | {{E77/screen.csv:point_id=L1_p1:raw_loss ~ .3f}} | {{E77/gate.csv:point_id=L1_p1:cal_transfer_all ~ +.2f}} |
| emulation, APL on only: APL's weight on a claw in proportion to the claw's own input | {{E77/screen.csv:point_id=L2_p1:cal_pattern ~ .3f}} | {{E77/screen.csv:point_id=L2_p1:raw_loss ~ .3f}} | {{E77/gate.csv:point_id=L2_p1:cal_transfer_all ~ +.2f}} |

The lowest pattern part of the screen, with each claw's input capped at 250 Hz, is {{E77/gate.csv:point_id=S4_tanh250:pattern_gain ~ .3f}} below the fit's, where one draw of the wiring moves the loss by {{E72/spread.csv:readout=cal:sd_single ~ .3f}} (last column of the first table); per-glomerulus drive normalization at half strength gains as little, and every other setting of every handle raises the pattern part. The transfer is negative at every setting, {{E77/report_scalars.csv:gate_transfer_all_max:value ~ +.2f}} at best against all eight recordings and {{E77/report_scalars.csv:gate_transfer_six_max:value ~ +.2f}} against the six that are alike: what each change does on the real wiring is not what the wirings share, and carried over to them it would add to the common error.

A weaker antennal-lobe normalization does raise the mean APL effect on raw counts, from {{E77/screen.csv:point_id=base:raw_mean ~ +.3f}} to {{E77/screen.csv:point_id=S1_inhadd1000:raw_mean ~ +.3f}} at the third of its four steps, where the loss on raw counts is {{E77/screen.csv:point_id=S1_inhadd1000:raw_loss ~ .3f}} against the fit's {{E77/screen.csv:point_id=base:raw_loss ~ .3f}}, and it pays with the pattern part ({{E77/screen.csv:point_id=S1_inhadd1000:cal_pattern ~ .3f}} against {{E77/screen.csv:point_id=base:cal_pattern ~ .3f}}). The two emulations raise the pattern part, and the loss on raw counts with it. Nothing came near what had been set beforehand for going on to fits on several wirings, so no handle was fitted.

**A searched input holds over recordings on its own wiring and, at the size searched, not over wirings.** With no handle to fit, the input itself was searched, as the bounded oracle had searched it for the weak odors ([above](#gap-pairs)). On the fit at its fitted parameters on the real wiring, the ORN response of each of eb, 1-8ol, IaA, ep, 2h, 1-6ol, pa, 6al, 1-5ol and ms, one odor after the other, was multiplied in every glomerulus by a factor between one half and two, searched for the lowest pattern part against one half of the recordings, with a penalty once the odor's response fraction left ±15 % of the fit's.

The recordings were split by fly, the two strongest recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) in different halves, and the search was run once against each half. It is an [oracle](#fn-oracle): what a corrected input could at most buy, not a measurement. Each searched input was then scored against the half it had not seen, with both response rates set again, on the real wiring and on three re-drawn wirings of [the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population) at their own fits, and as the mean over the four.

The pattern part of the APL-effect loss through the calibrated readout against the half of the recordings that the search did not see (lower is better), with the lab's input and with the searched input, and the gain (the first minus the second). Against half of the recordings every value is higher than against all of them, so what counts is the difference within a row

The search has the freedom to fit: against the half it was run on, the pattern part on the real wiring falls from {{E77/oracle_scores.csv:input=lab;wiring=real;readout=cal;target=halfA:pattern_rms ~ .3f}} to {{E77/oracle_scores.csv:input=oracle_halfA;wiring=real;readout=cal;target=halfA:pattern_rms ~ .3f}} and from {{E77/oracle_scores.csv:input=lab;wiring=real;readout=cal;target=halfB:pattern_rms ~ .3f}} to {{E77/oracle_scores.csv:input=oracle_halfB;wiring=real;readout=cal;target=halfB:pattern_rms ~ .3f}}. On the real wiring part of that holds for the half it never saw, in both directions and by about what one draw of the wiring moves the loss (first row). On the three re-drawn wirings it does not, the gains there lying between {{E77/oracle_scores.csv:input=oracle_halfA;wiring=P2;readout=cal;target=halfB:pattern_gain_vs_lab ~ +.3f}} and {{E77/oracle_scores.csv:input=oracle_halfB;wiring=P1;readout=cal;target=halfA:pattern_gain_vs_lab ~ +.3f}}, and the mean over the four wirings, the kind of mean in which the common error is defined, gains next to nothing (last row).

The factors themselves do not repeat: for each of the ten odors, the correlation over the 36 glomeruli between the factors found against the two halves, on a log scale, lies between {{E77/report_scalars.csv:halves_factor_corr_min:value ~ .2f}} and {{E77/report_scalars.csv:halves_factor_corr_max:value ~ .2f}}, with a median of {{E77/report_scalars.csv:halves_factor_corr_median:value ~ .2f}}. At the size it gives its input, a search free to set every glomerulus of every odor thus finds something that holds over recordings on the wiring it was run on and nothing that the wirings share. That reading has since been restated, because the search had overshot.

With the logarithm of every factor multiplied by 0.6 and both response rates set again, the two inputs lower the pattern part of the mean over four wirings that neither search had seen (two claw permutations and two matched shuffles), against the half of the recordings that each was not searched against, by {{E83/two_by_two_A2.csv:searched_on=A;size=0.6;unit=T;against=unseen:gain ~ .4f}} and {{E83/two_by_two_A2.csv:searched_on=B;size=0.6;unit=T;against=unseen:gain ~ .4f}}, with a lower loss on raw counts and the flies' mean effect; whole, they gain {{E83/two_by_two_A2.csv:searched_on=A;size=1.0;unit=T;against=unseen:gain ~ .4f}} and {{E83/two_by_two_A2.csv:searched_on=B;size=1.0;unit=T;against=unseen:gain ~ .4f}} there. The same search run on four wirings at once does not hold on the half of the recordings that it did not see ([the input and APL's glomerulus profile fitted on several wirings at once](#cross-wiring-fit)).

The reduced input's controls have been run since. With its factors permuted across each odor's glomeruli it gains nothing on average, and with them inverted it loses; a second draw of the search carries as much as the first, and a search on a second split of the flies does not. Over the two splits the input gains {{E86/gate.csv:change=gate:g ~ .4f}}, about half of what the test asks: it carries a small part of the common error, and how much depends on how the recordings are split ([the controls and the replication of the reduced searched input](#reduced-input)).

**Realism.** Every model of this subsection has the control flies' response rate with APL on, fitted or held, and the four columns of the first table are inside all four realism bands, with the flies' responses counted in baseline-noise units, as the bands count now, and by the recordings' own criterion, as they did until 2026-11-10 (lower rows). So are both searched inputs on each of the four wirings.

Every setting of the screen is inside the four bands as they count now; counted by the recordings' own criterion, the two compressive exponents on the input, the lowest cap, the stronger of the two bouton emulations and the stronger depletion leave a band on the number of odors per KC, and no reading above rests on them. The searched inputs are oracle inputs, each glomerulus's response between half and twice the recorded one and many of them at those bounds, which no measurement supports and on which the two halves of the recordings do not agree.

What the bands do not see is the fit's own and unchanged: the release through the many-claw KCs when APL is removed, a somatic threshold under half the baseline's and an APL→bouton scale near its bound ([above](#wiring-population)). Nothing here was bought with realism: at the size searched nothing was gained beyond one wiring, and the reduced inputs, read since on all eight wirings, are inside the four bands as well ([the input and APL's glomerulus profile fitted on several wirings at once](#cross-wiring-fit)). As everywhere, the pairs with paa, euc and -aPine rest on [ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations), and Hallem's values are at ten times the concentration of the KC recordings for ms, paa and 1-8ol.

**What follows.** No draw of the wiring carries the common error, no amount of inhibition per odor ([above](#apl-effect-parts)), no fixed profile of APL's weight over the glomeruli of the kind tried ([above](#glomerulus-profile)), and now no handle on the input and no APL inhibition that grows with a bouton's or a claw's own input.

In this family the common error as a whole is therefore not on the input side, as far as these handles and a search within a factor of two go, and it stays unexplained by the mechanisms the family has; the searched input, reduced, has since been found to remove a small part of it on wirings and recordings that it had not seen ([the input and APL's glomerulus profile fitted on several wirings at once](#cross-wiring-fit)), a part that its controls confirm and that a second split of the flies does not repeat ([the controls and the replication of the reduced searched input](#reduced-input)). Most of it lies in the two sides' pair-by-pair departures from their own relations between the conditions, which a change acting through the distances that the conditions share does not reach.

- Of the changes to what reaches the KCs, one was not among the handles, a per-claw knee near the largest PN rate; it has been run since and does not carry the common error either ([the high per-claw knee without a dead zone](#claw-knee)).
- What else is left lies outside what was screened: how APL's inhibition unfolds in time, differences between types of KCs, and inhibition that depends on the odor in another form (one such form, inhibition that follows the calyx space that glomeruli share, has since been tested as a proxy on the input, from connectome tables whose use is on hold, and its reading is withheld: [the APL calyx maps against the connectome](#apl-calyx-maps), the next subsection; the length of the odor pulse, the types of KCs and changes that a long block could have left in the KCs have been run as well, and none of these carries the common error: [the flies' pulse in the model and the remaining candidates for the common error](#remaining-candidates)).
  - The two descriptions above go with them as leads, each odor's growth in responses when APL is removed and the evening-out of the odors' total drive in the model's antennal lobe, with the caution that weakening that normalization alone cost the pattern part. The evening-out has since been set against recordings of the PN dendrites, which do not show it, while the model's distances between odors at that stage are within 0.05 of the dendrites' once the noise between flies is removed ([the model's stages against the flies' stages](#model-stages)).

The input has since been taken up again in that form, as a change fitted on several wirings at once and tested by whether two halves of the recordings give the same factors: they do not, and the fitted input does not hold on the half that it did not see (the same subsection). What is taken up from here is with the pending work at the end of the page.

### The APL calyx maps against the connectome: what APL's own activity in the calyx looks like, and whether glomeruli that share calyx space carry the error common to the wirings {#apl-calyx-maps}

**APL's activity in the calyx, imaged for three odors, is reliable and for the most part one pattern that all odors share.** The part that is an odor's own is smaller, repeats between presentations and varies over several micrometres, and pa's response lies lower in the image than ms's at equal strength. The maps of the model with local APL units are flatter and less alike between odors than the flies' at every coupling.

Two further readings, of maps predicted from where the PN boutons lie in seven connectome calyces against the measured differences between odors, and of inhibition that follows each glomerulus's neighbourhood in the calyx against the common error, rest on connectome tables whose use is on hold, and are withheld until those tables are cleared or the readings are made again from other connectome outputs. A spatially local APL at the boutons has not been fitted.

The first of the two has since been made again on three calyces of the hemibrain and the male CNS, where the predicted differences between odors beat permuted labels in few of the recordings, a description that decides nothing ([the flies' APL at the weak odors and at the panel's concentrations](#apl-weak-odors)). The second has not been made again.

[The input side of the error common to all wirings](#input-side) left the common error unexplained by the mechanisms that the best family has, and all of them treat APL as one cell that inhibits the whole calyx alike. An APL that acts locally would be a mechanism of another kind: glomeruli whose PN boutons lie in the same part of the calyx would be inhibited together, and of the six odors among which the model's APL effect is too small, the five esters (2h, IaA, pa, eb and ep) have strongly driven glomeruli in common.

Local APL units had been tried early, on a model without the later mechanisms, and had left the KCs' odor-odor distances where a single APL puts them (among what did not matter, further up), with nothing measured to say how local APL is. The APL calyx maps against the connectome took that measurement from Yang's calcium imaging of APL itself and asked two things of it without fitting a model, both fixed beforehand: whether maps of APL's activity predicted from the wiring match the measured ones, and whether the nearness of glomeruli in the calyx predicts the common error on odors it was not fitted to, by removing 15 % or more of its squared sum and more than permuted glomerulus labels remove. Only with both was a spatially local APL to be fitted in the best family.

**The maps.** The recordings are of APL in a single plane through the calyx, {{E79/E79_baseline_summary.csv:baseline=order_matched:n_recordings ~ .0f}} recordings from {{E79/E79_profile_centroid_shift.csv:pair=pa - ms;axis=y:n_flies ~ .0f}} flies. Each holds pa, paa and ms as concentration series (pa from 10^-6.8 to 10^-4.4, paa from 10^-6.3 to 10^-3.0, ms from 10^-7.7 to 10^-2), every stimulus given twice, and one map per presentation: the change in fluorescence over its baseline around the peak of the response, inside an outline of the calyx drawn for the recording.

The files do not say how the images are oriented, at what depth the plane lies or how large a pixel is. Positions are therefore given along the image's own axes, and lengths in pixels, with micrometres at an assumed 0.3 µm per pixel (the size of the hemibrain calyx against the outlines implies slightly less, if the plane cuts the calyx near its widest).

**One pattern shared by all odors, and a smaller part that is each odor's own.** The maps are reliable: the two presentations of a stimulus correlate, pixel by pixel inside the outline, at Pearson r {{E79/E79_baseline_summary.csv:baseline=order_matched:repeat_r_top_median ~ .2f}} (the median over recordings at each odor's highest concentration; {{E79/E79_baseline_summary.csv:baseline=all_pfo:repeat_r_top_median ~ .2f}} and {{E79/E79_baseline_summary.csv:baseline=first_in_block:repeat_r_top_median ~ .2f}} with two other ways of taking the baseline from the solvent presentations). Maps of different odors are almost as alike, at {{E79/E79_baseline_summary.csv:baseline=order_matched:different_odor_r_top_median ~ .2f}}, though not in every fly: in {{E79/E79_baseline_summary.csv:baseline=order_matched:n_recordings_ms_vs_pa_top_below_0p8 ~ .0f}} of the {{E79/E79_baseline_summary.csv:baseline=order_matched:n_recordings ~ .0f}} recordings the maps of ms and pa correlate below 0.8.

Most of a recording is one spatial pattern common to all its stimuli. The first singular vector of its matrix of stimuli by pixels holds {{E79/E79_model_vs_measured.csv:blur_px=2.0;mode=means kept;column=share_first_sv:measured_all_median ~ .0%}} of the summed squares at the finest smoothing (2 pixels) and {{E79/E79_model_vs_measured.csv:blur_px=20.0;mode=means kept;column=share_first_sv:measured_all_median ~ .0%}} at the coarsest (20 pixels), and {{E79/E79_model_vs_measured.csv:blur_px=2.0;mode=means removed;column=share_first_sv:measured_all_median ~ .0%}} and {{E79/E79_model_vs_measured.csv:blur_px=20.0;mode=means removed;column=share_first_sv:measured_all_median ~ .0%}} when each map's mean is removed first, so that shapes alone are compared (medians over recordings; left column of the figure).

What is left of a map without that pattern, the remainder (the residual of the figure), is what is specific to a stimulus, and it is not noise. It repeats between the two presentations at every smoothing (second column), and the remainders of the two presentations stay correlated over {{E79/E79_model_vs_measured.csv:blur_px=2.0;mode=means kept;column=resid_crossrep_len:measured_all_median_px ~ .0f}} pixels, {{E79/E79_model_vs_measured.csv:blur_px=2.0;mode=means kept;column=resid_crossrep_len:measured_all_median ~ .1f}} µm at the assumed pixel size (right column): an odor's own part of APL's activity varies over several micrometres, a small fraction of the calyx.

The two presentations of a stimulus lay in one block, so that these maps could not say whether that part belongs to the odor or to the block. A later series with three vials of one odor in separate blocks says that it is the odor's: what repeats within a block returns with another vial of the same odor and not with another odor ([the flies' APL across odors in the held-out vial series](#apl-held-out)).

![The shared and the odor-specific parts of the APL calyx maps against the width of the smoothing (Gaussian, in pixels), for each recording (grey) and as the median over recordings (black); top row with each map's mean kept, bottom row with it removed. From left to right: the share of the summed squares of a recording's stimulus × pixel matrix that its first singular vector holds, the pattern common to all stimuli; the correlation of the residual, a map without that pattern, between the two presentations of a stimulus; the correlation between the residuals of different odors, which the construction pulls below zero, since the residuals sum to zero, so that it decides nothing; and the distance over which the residuals of the two presentations stay correlated (to 1/e), with the same for smoothed white noise (dotted). The residual statistics are over each odor's two highest concentrations.](results/E79_apl_calyx_constraints/E79_shared_specific.png)

**Where pa's response lies against ms's.** Within an odor, a stronger response lies higher in the image, in every fly: the centroid of the response along the vertical axis of the image moves down with the logarithm of the response's strength in {{E79/E79_profile_centroid_adjusted.csv:axis=y;quantity=slope_per_log_mean:n_flies_positive ~ .0f}} of the {{E79/E79_profile_centroid_adjusted.csv:axis=y;quantity=slope_per_log_mean:n_flies ~ .0f}} flies. Two odors can therefore only be compared at equal strength.

At matched strength, for each recording the two concentrations at which the odors' mean responses over the calyx are closest, the centroid of pa's response lies lower in the image than that of ms's by {{E79/E79_profile_centroid_shift.csv:pair=pa - ms;axis=y:mean_shift ~ .3f}} of the outline's height (mean over flies, a fly's hemispheres averaged; 90 % interval over resampled flies {{E79/E79_profile_centroid_shift.csv:pair=pa - ms;axis=y:lo90 ~ .3f}} to {{E79/E79_profile_centroid_shift.csv:pair=pa - ms;axis=y:hi90 ~ .3f}}; lower in {{E79/E79_profile_centroid_shift.csv:pair=pa - ms;axis=y:n_flies_positive ~ .0f}} of the {{E79/E79_profile_centroid_shift.csv:pair=pa - ms;axis=y:n_flies ~ .0f}} flies), and by {{E79/E79_profile_centroid_adjusted.csv:axis=y;quantity=offset_pa_minus_ms:mean ~ .3f}} ({{E79/E79_profile_centroid_adjusted.csv:axis=y;quantity=offset_pa_minus_ms:lo90 ~ .3f}} to {{E79/E79_profile_centroid_adjusted.csv:axis=y;quantity=offset_pa_minus_ms:hi90 ~ .3f}}) when the offset between the odors is fitted at equal strength over all concentrations. For paa the shift is about half as large, {{E79/E79_profile_centroid_shift.csv:pair=paa - ms;axis=y:mean_shift ~ .3f}}, and its interval includes zero ({{E79/E79_profile_centroid_shift.csv:pair=paa - ms;axis=y:lo90 ~ +.3f}} to {{E79/E79_profile_centroid_shift.csv:pair=paa - ms;axis=y:hi90 ~ +.3f}}).

The shift of pa is small against the calyx and present in most flies. Which anatomical direction it is cannot be said without the orientation of the images.

![The response along the two axes of the image, in ten bins over the bounding box of the calyx outline: the share of pa's response in each bin minus that of ms's (top) and paa's minus ms's (bottom) at matched strength, along the vertical axis from top to bottom (left) and along the horizontal axis with left hemispheres mirrored (right). Grey: single flies; black with band: the mean over flies and its 90 % interval. Dashed: the same difference in the maps of the model with local APL units at three couplings, drawn as if the top of the image were dorsal.](results/E79_apl_calyx_constraints/E79_profiles.png)

**The model with local APL units does not make such maps.** That model divides APL into compartments defined from the connectome, each with a potential of its own, coupled with a strength that was never set from data. Its saved potentials (an early model at the conventional 5 %, at three couplings) were placed on APL's neurites in the hemibrain calyx, projected as the calyx is seen from posterior, and given the statistics of the measured maps.

The measured APL calyx maps against the maps of the model with local APL units at three strengths of the coupling between units (0: each unit by itself; 15: the strongest saved). Measured: in each recording the three maps nearest the model's input, pa at 10^-4.4, ms at 10^-3.4 and paa at 10^-4.4 (the model's input is pa and ms at 10^-3 and paa at 10^-4), as the median over recordings with the range. Both are smoothed over 2 pixels, 0.6 µm at the assumed pixel size, and the model's maps are of the whole depth of the calyx

| | | the model with local APL units {span=3} |

At every coupling the model's maps are less alike between odors than the flies' and far more even over the calyx (first and third rows): in the flies the odors share most of a map that varies strongly from place to place, and in the model each odor has a weak pattern of its own on a nearly even ground. Coupling the units evens the maps out further without making them more alike, and only the distance over which an odor's own part varies is near the measured one.

Part of the flies' shared pattern may be anatomy, the density of APL's neurites in the imaged plane, which unit potentials do not have, and pa was imaged more than one log unit below the model's pa. If local units are taken up again, how uneven a map is and how alike two odors' maps are is what their coupling would be set by.

**Two readings against the connectome are withheld.** Both questions that had been fixed beforehand were put to tables of PN boutons, of KC claws and of APL's synapses that were derived from four connectome data sets in separate work: seven calyces, the right calyx of the hemibrain and both calyces of FlyWire, of the male CNS and of BANC, with the model's own set of hemibrain boutons read beside them.

The use of those tables is on hold ([what is withheld with them, and until when](#fn-derived-tables)). No number, table, figure or verdict of either reading is therefore given here, the readings on the model's own boutons included, since they were made and reported with the others and the outline of that calyx came from the derived tables.

Neither reading is made again from the derived tables while the hold stands. The first has since been made again on the hemibrain and the male CNS, the two connectome data sets that this work now uses, as a reading beside a test on pairs of weak odors ([the flies' APL at the weak odors and at the panel's concentrations](#apl-weak-odors)). Through each of three calyces, pa minus ms and paa minus ms beat the permuted labels in at most {{E100/d_pair_shares.csv:set=2021;scoring=slabs;pair=pa-ms (2021);session=apl16:share_hemibrain_R ~ .2f}} of the {{E100/d_pair_shares.csv:set=2021;scoring=slabs;pair=pa-ms (2021);session=apl16:n_recordings ~ .0f}} recordings, which is described and decides nothing. The second has not been set up again.

What was asked stands, and is described here as the plan of the two readings ([how the maps were predicted and both tests scored](#fn-calyx-maps)). For the first question, a map of APL's activity is predicted for an odor from every PN bouton of a calyx at its position, weighted by its number of release sites and by the PN rate of its glomerulus in the breadth-2 APL-effect fit, and the predicted differences between odors, pa minus ms and paa minus ms at matched strength, are set against the measured ones.

The null is the same procedure with the glomerulus labels of the PN rates permuted, and because the orientation and the depth of the images were not known when the test was made, every orientation and depth is scored, for the prediction and for the permutations alike. Any reading of this question carries two limits of the input: every pa map was imaged more than one log unit below the pa of the model's input (10^-4.4 and lower against 10^-3), outside the one log unit within which data at another concentration stand in on this page ([footnote](#fn-concentrations)), and paa's PN rates come from ORN data at 10^-4, the substitute used throughout.

For the second question, which does not need the maps, a proxy on the model's PN rates, without simulation, inhibits each glomerulus in proportion to the activity near its own boutons, the rates of all glomeruli weighted by their co-localization with it, instead of in proportion to the odor's mean rate, as an APL that acts on the whole calyx would inhibit it. The change that this makes in the 120 pairs' input distances is scaled to the common error on the pairs of 15 odors and scored on the 15 pairs of the odor left out, against the same with the glomeruli permuted.

A spatially local APL at the boutons has not been fitted in the best family. The rule that was set beforehand stands, that one is fitted only with both readings in its favour, and nothing is concluded from the two readings while they are withheld.

**Realism.** No model was changed or fitted here, so the realism bands do not apply: the only model quantities used are the PN rates of the breadth-2 APL-effect fit, which the bands do not score, and the saved potentials of the early model with local APL units, which is not a candidate base.

**What follows.** What stands is the measurement: APL's activity in the calyx is for the most part one pattern that the odors share, the part that is an odor's own is smaller and repeats between presentations, and the model with local APL units does not make such maps. Whether an APL that acts locally at the boutons, along the calyx space that glomeruli share, has support as the source of the common error is not said here while the two readings on it are withheld; the readings on the fixed profile over the glomeruli ([above](#glomerulus-profile)) and on the inhibition that grows with a bouton's or a claw's own input ([above](#input-side)) do not rest on those tables and are not affected.

What the test of the maps needed lay with the data, and most of it has since been answered by the experimenter who made the maps: the view is from posterior with dorsal up, a pixel is {{lit:0.268 # notes/yang_apl_calyx_metadata.md: read from ThorImage's Experiment.xml of four recordings (256 x 224 pixels, 68.57 x 60 um)}} µm, where the lengths above were given at an assumed 0.3 µm and are about a tenth shorter with it, and the plane of each recording is on record. Which edge of the image is medial, and where the zero of the depth was set, are still asked. With them the prediction from the wiring is tested at one orientation and one depth, the fair test of whether the wiring predicts APL's map.

That test has since been run on three calyces of the hemibrain and the male CNS, on five pairs of weak odors and with both medial edges searched ([the flies' APL at the weak odors and at the panel's concentrations](#apl-weak-odors)). It reads on no pair: one calyx's predicted map does not carry over to a single plane of another calyx well enough for a recorded fly to be tested against it. From these tables a spatially local APL thus has no test from the wiring, and what would give one is a volume of the recorded fly's own calyx.

What is still missing among the maps is, since the common error sets 2h, IaA, pa, eb, ep and ms against 1-8ol, 1-5ol, 1-6ol and 6al, APL maps of eb or 2h against 1-6ol or 1-8ol at the 10^-3 of the KC recordings, which would show what the three odors imaged cannot, whether APL's activity differs in place between the two groups.

If a prediction from a volume of the recorded fly's own calyx then matches the maps and the co-localization at the matched depth passes the test above, the local fit is taken up. What remained for the common error on the model's side outside the calyx is in the next subsection ([the flies' pulse in the model and the remaining candidates for the common error](#remaining-candidates)); what is still open is with the pending work at the end of the page.

### The flies' pulse in the model and the remaining candidates for the common error: what the length of the odor pulse does to the model's match, and whether anything left on the model's side carries the error common to the wirings {#remaining-candidates}

**The length of the odor pulse does not change the model's match to the main target under the calibrated readout, and it does on raw spike counts.**

With the flies' 2 s pulse in place of the model's 0.5 s, the breadth-2 APL-effect fit keeps its loss under the readout, while on raw counts its mean APL effect halves and its loss rises by more than half, because the model's APL nearly silences the response after the first half second; with a firing ceiling, where raw counts and the readout give one number, that number rises as well, by a fifth. The raw-count numbers of the main target are therefore tied to the model's 0.5 s pulse at the settings of these fits; the flies' recording protocol in the model, the next subsection but one, lifts this for the family with the firing ceiling once the ceiling's adaptation outlasts the odor.

None of the candidates left on the model's side lowers the error common to all wirings, and every one would add to it: types of KCs, changes that act only with APL off, how many KCs each odor recruits, and an input shared by all glomeruli. A threshold that is lower with APL on than with APL off lowers the mean APL effect, and response amplitudes that grow with a KC's breadth do not raise it toward the flies' mean in baseline-noise units.

[The input side of the error common to all wirings](#input-side) had closed fixed changes of what reaches the KCs and named what was left on the model's side: how the response unfolds in time, types of KCs, inhibition that depends on the odor in another form, and how much each odor's response fraction grows when APL is removed. This experiment took what neither [the APL calyx maps against the connectome](#apl-calyx-maps) nor the per-claw knee ([the high per-claw knee without a dead zone](#claw-knee), the next subsection) covers, on the real wiring and with nothing fitted again: on the breadth-2 APL-effect fit and, where named, on the same family with the firing ceiling at its stronger setting (the second model column of the second table of [the data side of the main target](#data-side)).

**The pulse.** The flies were given a 2 s odor pulse, and a response in the recordings is the mean of a KC's signal from 2 to 8 s after the pulse's onset ([footnote](#fn-baseline-noise-units)). The model's odor has always lasted 0.5 s, with spikes counted until 0.25 s after it ends. Both fits were run with pulses of 1 s and 2 s, spikes again counted until 0.25 s after the pulse, with both response rates held at the fit's own, which changes little (at 2 s the breadth-2 fit needs a somatic threshold {{E80/pulse.csv:point_id=C2_pulse2_held:thr_factor ~ .2f}} times and an APL scale {{E80/pulse.csv:point_id=C2_pulse2_held:apl_factor ~ .2f}} times the fitted ones).

The breadth-2 APL-effect fit and the same family with the firing ceiling at its stronger setting, on the real wiring: at the model's 0.5 s pulse as fitted, and at longer pulses with both response rates held and nothing fitted again. Two values without named conditions are on raw spike counts / through the calibrated readout, its half-saturation set again at each pulse; in the family with the ceiling it runs to the upper end of its range, where the readout changes nothing
