**Under the readout the pulse does not matter; on raw counts it does.** Through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout) the breadth-2 fit's loss at the flies' pulse is within {{diff:E80/pulse.csv:point_id=C2_pulse2_held:cal_loss -- E80/pulse.csv:point_id=C2_pulse0.5_fixed:cal_loss ~ .3f}} of its loss at 0.5 s, less than one draw of the wiring moves it ({{E72/spread.csv:readout=cal:sd_single ~ .3f}}), with the mean effect still near the flies' and the pattern part where it was (first three rows, second values). On raw counts the mean effect falls with each lengthening of the pulse, to half at 2 s, and the loss rises by more than half (first values).

A longer pulse had been expected to raise the mean effect on raw counts; it lowers it because of when the model's KCs fire. With APL on nearly all spikes of the 2 s pulse fall in its first 0.5 s, and with APL off a third come later (sixth row): the model's APL all but silences the response that outlasts the onset.

The late spikes with APL off come from few KCs, with patterns further apart between odors than the onset's (a mean distance of {{E80/pulse_windows.csv:point_id=C2_pulse2_held;window=0.5-1:mean_dist_off ~ .2f}} in the second half second against {{E80/pulse_windows.csv:point_id=C2_pulse2_held;window=0-0.5:mean_dist_off ~ .2f}} in the first). They raise the distances with APL off toward those with APL on, which hardly move (fifth row), so the effect shrinks; the readout's saturation removes most of what the late spikes add to a KC's count, which is why its numbers hold. In the family with the firing ceiling the adaptation cuts the late spikes with APL off as well, and the mean effect falls less; but there the readout has nothing left to compress, so the one number that both definitions give rises with the pulse, to about the breadth-2 fit's loss under the readout (last two columns).

All of this is at parameters fitted with the 0.5 s pulse: what shapes a sustained response in the model (the adaptation of the PNs, KC–KC inhibition, APL) had not been fitted at 2 s (both families have been since: [the flies' recording protocol in the model](#flies-protocol)), and with APL on the response after the first half second is too sparse for a per-pair APL effect of its own ({{E80/pulse_windows.csv:point_id=C2_pulse2_held;window=0.5-1:n_pairs_defined ~ .0f}} of the 120 pairs are defined in the second half second).

**No candidate lowers the pattern part, and each would add to the common error.** Under the readout the breadth-2 fit has the flies' mean effect, so the pattern part is what a candidate has to lower: {{E80/screen.csv:point_id=base:cal_pattern ~ .3f}} on the real wiring and {{E72/population.csv:group=all:cal_pattern ~ .3f}} for the mean over the eight wirings, the common error, against a floor of {{E66/data_floor_parts.csv:data=graded;stat=apl_effect_rmse_centered:mean ~ .3f}}.

- Four candidates were run on the fit at fixed settings, with both response rates held at the fit's own where the candidate does not set them, and put to the test of [the input side of the error common to all wirings](#input-side): an input shared by all glomeruli, as lateral excitation in the antennal lobe would add; each odor's response rates put on the flies' by a threshold per odor, an [oracle](#fn-oracle) for how many KCs each odor recruits; changes that act only with APL off, as a block of APL output lasting three days could have left them in the KCs (each KC's threshold raised with the KC's own activity, or the threshold of one type of KC raised); and APL's weight on one type of KC halved or doubled.
- A fifth was read as a curve and not put to the test: a threshold that is lower with APL on than with APL off, the other form that an adaptation to the block could take, with APL made stronger until the response rate with APL on is the fit's.

The candidates on the breadth-2 APL-effect fit, each at its setting with the lowest pattern part: the pattern part through the calibrated readout, the mean APL effect and the APL-effect loss on raw counts, and the transfer, the share of the common error's squared sum that the setting's change on the real wiring would remove if it were the same on every wiring (negative: it would add that share)

The lowest pattern part of the screen is {{E80/gate.csv:point_id=B4_beta0.25:pattern_gain ~ .3f}} below the fit's, where one draw of the wiring moves the loss by {{E72/spread.csv:readout=cal:sd_single ~ .3f}}. It comes from the mildest threshold raised with a KC's activity, which gives up three quarters of the mean effect on raw counts, and every steeper step raises the pattern part.

The transfer is negative at every setting of every candidate, against all eight recordings and against the six that are alike: what each does on the real wiring is not what the wirings share, and carried over to them it would add to the common error. With each odor's response rates on the flies', the per-odor part of the pattern error stays between {{E80/screen.csv:point_id=B3_throff_z:cal_per_odor ~ .3f}} and {{E80/screen.csv:point_id=B3_thr_z:cal_per_odor ~ .3f}} (the fit's {{E80/screen.csv:point_id=base:cal_per_odor ~ .3f}}; floor {{E66/data_floor_parts.csv:data=graded;stat=apl_effect_per_odor:mean ~ .3f}}), so how many KCs each odor recruits when APL is removed, a lead of the input side, is no lever in this family.

The same handle has since been run on four wirings, where it again leaves the pattern part of the main target no lower, although it brings the model's responses with APL off a third to a half of the way to the flies' in the respect that an inhibition by the odor's strength depends on, and although an inhibition of the flies' form then makes more of those responses, on the spike counts, than the model's own APL does ([the form of APL's inhibition in the flies' own responses](#inhibition-form)); simulated in place of APL on those responses, that inhibition does far worse than the model's own APL ([the common error split into who responds and how strongly](#responder-sets)).

Nor does a type of KC stand out: read from the saved fits with the KCs of one type alone, the pattern part of the mean over the eight wirings is {{E80/type_split.csv:kc_type=a'b':pattern ~ .3f}} for the α′/β′ KCs, {{E80/type_split.csv:kc_type=ab:pattern ~ .3f}} for the α/β KCs and {{E80/type_split.csv:kc_type=g:pattern ~ .3f}} for the γ KCs, against {{E80/type_split.csv:kc_type=all:pattern ~ .3f}} with all of them, and the error among 2h, IaA, pa, eb, ep and ms and among 1-8ol, 1-5ol, 1-6ol and 6al keeps its sign and most of its size in each. Nothing came near what had been set for going on to fits on several wirings, so no candidate was fitted.

**A threshold lower with APL on lowers the mean effect.** Had the KCs raised their thresholds during the block, the control flies' KCs would have the lower ones, and a model with a lower threshold and a stronger APL in its APL-on condition was expected to have the larger mean effect. It has a smaller one.

With each KC's threshold with APL on divided by 1.1, 1.25, 1.5 or 2, the mean APL effect on raw counts falls at every step, from {{E80/b1_curve.csv:point_id=B1_identity:raw_mean ~ +.3f}} to {{E80/b1_curve.csv:point_id=B1_c2:raw_mean ~ +.3f}} in the breadth-2 fit and from {{E80/b1_curve.csv:point_id=B1_fit0_identity:raw_mean ~ +.3f}} to {{E80/b1_curve.csv:point_id=B1_fit0_c2:raw_mean ~ +.3f}} in the family with the firing ceiling, where the flies' is {{data:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}} in the recordings' z-scored units and {{data:noise_apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}} in baseline-noise units. The pattern part is above the fit's at every step (last row of the table for the mildest), and holding the response rate with APL on takes an APL {{E80/b1_curve.csv:point_id=B1_c1.1:apl_factor ~ .1f}} to {{E80/b1_curve.csv:point_id=B1_c2:apl_factor ~ .1f}} times as strong.

**Amplitudes that grow with a KC's breadth do not raise the mean.** In baseline-noise units no fit has the flies' mean effect, and what the flies have there and the models lack is responses that grow with the number of odors a KC responds to ([the data side of the main target](#data-side)). Read from the recordings and the saved fits, without simulation, the family with the firing ceiling already has the summed squared response where the flies have it: with APL off its KCs at eight or more odors hold {{E80/amplitude_by_breadth.csv:tag=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2;condition=APL off;cls=8+:share_sq ~ .0%}} of it, against {{E80/amplitude_by_breadth.csv:source=APL output blocked (TNT);cls=8+:share_sq ~ .0%}} in the flies with APL output blocked (TNT).

Weighting the fit's counts by the number of odors a KC responds to, raised to a power between 0.1 and 0.5, moves its mean effect on raw counts by {{diff:E80/breadth_weighted.csv:tag=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2;p_is_flies=True;target=noise:mean -- E80/breadth_weighted.csv:tag=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2;p=0.0;target=noise:mean ~ +.3f}} at the most, at the power that the control flies' amplitudes give ({{E80/breadth_weighted.csv:tag=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2;p_is_flies=True;target=noise:p ~ .2f}}), where {{diff:data:noise_apl_effect_mean -- E80/breadth_weighted.csv:tag=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2;p=0.0;target=noise:mean ~ .3f}} is missing, and it raises the pattern part against the effect in those units (from {{E80/breadth_weighted.csv:tag=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2;p=0.0;target=noise:pattern ~ .3f}} to {{E80/breadth_weighted.csv:tag=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2;p_is_flies=True;target=noise:pattern ~ .3f}}). The shortfall of the mean in baseline-noise units is not in how amplitudes grow with breadth.

**Realism.** With the flies' responses counted in baseline-noise units, as the realism bands count now, every setting put to the test is inside all four bands, and so are the fits at the longer pulses, whose response rates and odors per KC the pulse hardly moves (lower rows of the first table). Counted by the recordings' own criterion, as until 2026-11-10, the two largest shared inputs (the one of the table among them), the steepest threshold raised with activity, the larger step on the thresholds of the α/β and of the α′/β′ KCs, the permuted control and the control in the opposite direction leave the band on the number of odors per KC with APL off; none is near passing, and no reading above rests on them.

Of the threshold lower with APL on, the divisors of 1.5 and 2 on the breadth-2 fit and of 1.5 on the family with the ceiling leave the band on the response rate ρ with APL on as it counts now ({{E80/b1_curve.csv:point_id=B1_c1.5:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}}, {{E80/b1_curve.csv:point_id=B1_c2:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}} and {{E80/b1_curve.csv:point_id=B1_fit0_c1.5:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}}, where 0.37 or more is asked), and by the recordings' own criterion two more of its settings, on the family with the ceiling, leave a band.

What the bands do not see is hard to defend at the 2 s pulse: the hardest-driven KC of the breadth-2 fit fires {{E80/pulse.csv:point_id=C2_pulse2_held:max_count_on ~ .0f}} spikes to one odor with APL on and {{E80/pulse.csv:point_id=C2_pulse2_held:max_count_off ~ .0f}} with APL off, where the family with the ceiling stays at {{E80/pulse.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held:max_count_on ~ .0f}} and {{E80/pulse.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held:max_count_off ~ .0f}}. So are the stronger APL that the threshold lower with APL on needs, and the common threshold of {{E80/screen.csv:point_id=B4_beta0.5:thr_factor ~ .2f}} down to {{E80/screen.csv:point_id=B4_beta2:thr_factor ~ .2f}} of the fitted one that meets the steeper thresholds raised with activity. Nothing was gained here, so nothing was bought with realism. As everywhere, the pairs with paa, euc and -aPine rest on [ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations).

**What follows.** The candidates that the input side had left open on the model's side are closed for this family, as far as a screen at fixed settings on one wiring closes them, and on that side the common error was left to how a claw passes its input on, the per-claw knee, which has been run since and does not carry it either ([the high per-claw knee without a dead zone](#claw-knee), the next subsection).

The result that reaches beyond this subsection is the pulse. Every raw-count number of the main target on this page sets the model's response to a 0.5 s pulse against the flies' mean over 2 to 8 s after the onset of a 2 s pulse, and, at the settings of the fits made so far, holds for the 0.5 s pulse only: the mean APL effect on raw counts, the level that the firing ceiling reaches on raw counts ([above](#firing-ceiling)) and the comparison of raw counts with the flies' effect in baseline-noise units ([above](#data-side)) among them. The readout's numbers hold at either pulse in the family without a ceiling.

It had been set before the run that a worse match would mean repeating the main numbers at the flies' pulse before anything else. The match got worse on raw counts and not under the readout, and the repeat has been made ([the flies' recording protocol in the model](#flies-protocol), the next subsection but one): read as the flies were recorded, the family with the firing ceiling has its raw-count numbers back once the ceiling's adaptation outlasts the odor, and the family without a ceiling does not, after a fit at 2 s either, so that for it the calibrated readout stays the reading that does not depend on the pulse.

What remained for the target itself was on the data's side: which recordings make the target, which waits on the experimenter and is with the pending work at the end of the page, and when in the response the flies' APL effect is made, which means over one window cannot show and which the frame-by-frame traces have answered since ([the time course of the APL effect in the flies' traces](#trace-time-course)).

### The high per-claw knee without a dead zone: whether selecting responders at the claw holds apart the odor pairs with near-identical ORN input {#claw-knee}

**A per-claw knee near the largest PN rate holds the odor pairs with near-identical ORN input apart, as the flies' KCs do, only when a claw passes nothing below it.** That hard knee leaves ms and B-myr without responses and about doubles the pattern part of the APL-effect loss.

As soon as a claw passes a tenth of its input below the knee, the gain on those pairs is gone, and a knee set relative to each odor's strongest input does not reach them either. The per-claw transfer is therefore closed for the best family on the main target. What the hard knee does bring toward the flies is which KCs are released when APL is removed.

Six of the 120 odor pairs have nearly the same ORN input, a distance between the two odors' ORN responses below 0.25: eb with ep, 6al with t2h, IaA with pa, 2h with pa, 1-5ol with 1-6ol and 2h with IaA, none of them with an odor at a substituted ORN concentration. The flies' KCs hold these pairs apart, and more so with APL than without. The breadth-2 APL-effect fit separates them less in both conditions and has about half the flies' APL effect on them, the mean of the per-pair APL effect over the six (the KC data and the first model column of the table below). Four of the six are among the esters, where the common error has the model's APL effect too small.

On the bouton model without the later mechanisms, what holds these pairs apart is a per-claw knee near the top of the PN rates, which in the model reach {{E78/partA_scored.csv:thr130_rate0.068_aplboth_k2:top_pn_rate ~ .0f}} Hz: a knee at 130 Hz with nothing passed below it takes the six pairs' APL effect on raw counts from {{E78/archive_knee_variants.csv:bouton_thr130:base_raw_six_effect ~ +.3f}} to {{E78/archive_knee_variants.csv:bouton_thr130:raw_six_effect ~ +.3f}}, where knees at 40 to 100 Hz leave it between {{E78/archive_knee_variants.csv:bouton_thr100:raw_six_effect ~ +.3f}} and {{E78/archive_knee_variants.csv:bouton_thr70:raw_six_effect ~ +.3f}}, and it leaves 1-8ol, ms and B-myr without a responding KC. With such a knee the somatic threshold falls and a KC responds through the one or two claws that sit on an odor's strongest boutons: the responders are selected at the claw and no longer at the soma.

The high per-claw knee without a dead zone asked whether that selection holds the six pairs apart in the best family without silencing the weak odors, once the knee has no dead zone, the range of input below it that counts for nothing: a claw then passes a fraction of its input below the knee (the reduced slope that had been tried below the 70 Hz threshold of the early models, further up). The other form tried is a knee set relative to each odor's strongest input.

Everything is on the breadth-2 APL-effect fit on the real wiring (the first model column of the first table of [the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population)), scored against all eight recordings with APL output blocked (TNT), through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout) unless raw counts are named. The knee was put into the fit at fixed scales: at 70, 100, 115 and 130 Hz, with nothing passed below it (a hard knee) or with a tenth, a quarter or half of a claw's input passed below it; softened over 15 Hz at the two settings nearest the fit; and at 0.5, 0.7 and 0.85 of the odor's largest bouton rate, that level taken off every bouton's output with APL on and with APL off.

At each setting the somatic threshold and the APL→KC scale were set again until the numbers of responses with APL off and with APL on were the fit's, with the breadth weights computed again for the changed transfer. The KC–KC scale was lowered in proportion to the somatic threshold, because a knee cuts the drive to the soma several-fold and lateral inhibition, which is driven by the other KCs' spikes, does not shrink with it. Hard knees at 100 and 130 Hz were also fitted, from the fit's parameters and with its loss.

What a setting had to do before fits on re-drawn wirings would follow had been set beforehand: reduce the ester group's error by a third (the mean error of the model's per-pair APL effect over the 15 pairs among 2h, IaA, pa, eb, ep and ms, where the common error has the effect too small; the alcohol group's error is the same over the 6 pairs among 1-8ol, 1-5ol, 1-6ol and 6al, where it is too large) and raise the six pairs' APL effect by 0.03, at a loss of {{E78/gate.csv:C2_pp_knee130_g0.5:loss_limit ~ .3f}} or less, with every odor keeping at least half of its response fraction.

The breadth-2 APL-effect fit on the real wiring with a per-claw knee: as fitted, without one; with the knee put in at fixed scales and both response rates held; and with a hard knee fitted. **The hard knee holds the pairs apart, and pays with the weak odors and the pattern.** With nothing passed below 130 Hz the six pairs' APL effect on raw counts rises from the fit's {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_identity:raw_six_effect ~ +.3f}} to {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_pp_knee130_g0:raw_six_effect ~ +.3f}} at fixed scales and to {{E78/partA_scored.csv:thr130_rate0.068_aplboth_k2:raw_six_effect ~ +.3f}} fitted, against the flies' {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_identity:data_six_effect ~ +.3f}}, mostly through their distance with APL on.

The same knee turns the ester group's error from too little effect into too much, doubles the alcohol group's, leaves ms and B-myr without a responding KC in either condition and about doubles the pattern part of the loss. ρ on the per-pair APL effect falls to about half, and the mean APL effect, which the fit has at the flies' under the readout, falls by a third (third and last model columns).

At 115 Hz the hard knee takes the ester group's error to {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_pp_knee115_g0:cal_err_ester ~ +.3f}} and raises the six pairs' effect by {{E78/gate.csv:C2_pp_knee115_g0:six_raise ~ +.3f}} only, at a loss of {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_pp_knee115_g0:cal_loss ~ .3f}}; at 100 Hz, at fixed scales or fitted, it does not raise them at all (fitted: fifth model column). This is what the hard knee did on the early bouton model, and breadth-weighted APL and KC–KC inhibition change nothing in it: in this family the ester group's error and the alcohol group's are two ends of one trade, and the six pairs move only with silent odors.

**With any input passed below the knee the gain on the six pairs is gone.** With a tenth of a claw's input passed below the knee, the six pairs' APL effect is below the fit's at every knee ({{E78/sweep.csv:C2_pp_knee100_g0.1:raw_six_effect ~ +.3f}}, {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_pp_knee115_g0.1:raw_six_effect ~ +.3f}} and {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_pp_knee130_g0.1:raw_six_effect ~ +.3f}} at 100, 115 and 130 Hz), and it stays below it with a quarter and with half. The ester group's error is still more than halved with a tenth passed, at losses of {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_pp_knee130_g0.1:cal_loss ~ .3f}} to {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_pp_knee100_g0.1:cal_loss ~ .3f}}, and returns to the fit's as the fraction grows.

What comes back with the fraction passed is the fit itself. With half passed below 130 Hz, the setting with the lowest loss, the ester group's error and the weak odors' response fractions are nearly the fit's and the loss is {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_pp_knee130_g0.5:cal_loss ~ .3f}} against the fit's {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_identity:cal_loss ~ .3f}}, still above the {{E78/gate.csv:C2_pp_knee130_g0.5:loss_limit ~ .3f}} that had been set (second model column). Softening the knee changes little.

The five settings nearest the fit were repeated on the same family with the firing ceiling at its literature setting and on a re-drawn wiring (claw permutation P1), each at its own fit. With the ceiling the six pairs' effect moves by {{E78/gate.csv:fit1_pp_knee100_g0.5:six_raise_vs_start ~ +.3f}} to {{E78/gate.csv:fit1_pp_knee115_g0.5_w15:six_raise_vs_start ~ +.3f}}; on the re-drawn wiring it moves by {{E78/gate.csv:P1_pp_knee100_g0.5:six_raise_vs_start ~ +.3f}} to {{E78/gate.csv:P1_pp_knee115_g0.5_w15:six_raise_vs_start ~ +.3f}}, and the ester group's error is further from zero at each of the five.

A knee at half of each odor's largest bouton rate keeps the mean APL effect and has the highest response rate ρ of all the settings, but it leaves the six pairs' effect where the fit has it, doubles the alcohol group's error and raises the pattern part by half (fourth model column). Set higher it cannot hold the response rates: at 0.7 of the largest bouton rate the response rate with APL off stops at {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_pp_rel0.7:ratio ~ .2f}} times that with APL on, outside the band on the ratio, and at 0.85 no somatic threshold gives the fit's responses. No setting did what had been set beforehand, on any of the three fits, so no fit of a knee without a dead zone followed.

**Without the trial noise the six pairs are short by as much.** The table sets a model without noise against recordings that have it. With [the matched trial noise](#fn-trial-noise) put into the fit (the noise matched to the control flies), the distances of both sides can be estimated without their noise from single trials: one minus the cosine between trials of the two odors from different repeats, divided by the cosine between trials of one odor across the same repeats, which assumes only that the noise of different repeats is independent.

By that estimate the fit has the six pairs at {{E81/saved_trials_structure.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;model=E67-rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;level=match_on;values=graded:six_noise_free_on ~ .3f}} with APL on and {{E81/saved_trials_structure.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;model=E67-rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;level=match_on;values=graded:six_noise_free_off ~ .3f}} with APL off, an APL effect of {{E81/saved_trials_structure.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;model=E67-rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;level=match_on;values=graded:six_effect_noise_free ~ +.3f}}, and the flies at {{data:noise_free_six_ctrl ~ .3f}} and {{data:noise_free_six_tnt ~ .3f}}, an effect of {{data:noise_free_apl_effect_six ~ +.3f}} (90 % interval {{data:noise_free_apl_effect_six.lo ~ +.3f}} to {{data:noise_free_apl_effect_six.hi ~ +.3f}}). The fit thus has about half the flies' APL effect on these pairs with or without the noise, and the larger shortfall is in their distance with APL on.

The correction for trial-to-trial noise that this page used until then is not the one to read the model's six pairs by, nor the flies' ([the flies' variability across the three repeats](#repeat-structure)). It assumes that the noise of two odors is independent, and in the recordings and in the model's trial noise alike two odors of one repeat are more alike than across repeats; applied to the fit's trials it puts the six pairs at {{E81/saved_trials_structure.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;model=E67-rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;level=match_on;values=graded:six_corrected_on ~ .3f}} and {{E81/saved_trials_structure.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;model=E67-rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;level=match_on;values=graded:six_corrected_off ~ .3f}}, as if they were one odor, which is not what the model does.

**Who is released when APL is removed.** In the fit the {{E78/release.csv:C2_identity:frac_kcs_9+ ~ .0%}} of KCs with nine or more claws take a third of the responses that removing APL adds, and the number of odors per KC is spread more unevenly over the KCs than in the flies ([the input-scaled KC threshold](#input-scaled-threshold)). The hard knees change both. With one, those KCs take a fifth to a quarter of the added responses, and the spread of the number of odors per KC comes down to the flies' or a little under it in both conditions (the two rows above the last of the table).

With half of the input passed below the knee both are where the fit has them, and the knee relative to the odor moves the release furthest toward the few-claw KCs while the spread stays the fit's. Selecting responders at the claw thus moves the release off the many-claw KCs, which the input-scaled KC threshold had done at a cost on the main target, but here only with the dead zone that silences the weak odors.

**Realism.** Every setting that held both response rates is inside all four realism bands, and so are both fitted knees, with the flies' responses counted in baseline-noise units, as the bands count now, and by the recordings' own criterion, as they did until 2026-11-10. The knee at 0.7 of the odor's largest bouton rate, which did not hold the response rate with APL off, is outside the band on the ratio, and nothing above rests on it.

What the hard knees cost lies in what the bands do not hold. ms and B-myr, already under the flies' response fractions in the fit, lose their responses. The largest spike count of a KC to one odor rises from {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_identity:max_count_on ~ .0f}} with APL on and {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_identity:max_count_off ~ .0f}} with APL off in the fit to {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_pp_knee130_g0:max_count_on ~ .0f}} and {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_pp_knee130_g0:max_count_off ~ .0f}} with the hard knee at 130 Hz at fixed scales: at unchanged response rates, a few KCs driven through a single claw fire much harder.

And the parameters are hard to defend. A knee at 100 to 130 Hz lies at {{E78/partA_scored.csv:thr100_rate0.068_aplboth_k2:knee_over_top_pn_rate ~ .2f}} to {{E78/partA_scored.csv:thr130_rate0.068_aplboth_k2:knee_over_top_pn_rate ~ .2f}} of the model's largest PN rate, so that a claw passing nothing below it is nearly all-or-none, where imaging of single claws shows each claw responding to its own PN input in a graded way and the KC summing several of them (Gruntman and Turner, 2013).

The somatic threshold falls from the fit's {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_identity:fixed_thr ~ .0f}} Hz to between {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_pp_knee130_g0:fixed_thr ~ .0f}} and {{E78/partA_scored.csv:thr100_rate0.068_aplboth_k2:fit_fixed_thr ~ .0f}} Hz with a hard knee at 100 Hz or above (last row of the table), and KC–KC inhibition is lowered with it. With half of the input passed below it the knee is mild, with a somatic threshold about half the fit's.

No setting is recommended, and the negative result does not depend on the bands, since nothing did what had been set beforehand inside them. As everywhere, the pairs with paa, euc and -aPine rest on [ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations).

**What follows.** The per-claw transfer is closed for this family on the main target. It had been closed for recruiting the weak odors (the section on the weak-input odors, further up), and a knee near the top of the PN rates does not lower the APL-effect loss in any form: as a hard knee it trades the ester group's error for the alcohol group's and for silent odors, and with input passed below it, or set relative to the odor, it does nothing for the six pairs.

Those pairs stay a target of their own, at about half the flies' APL effect and short mostly with APL on. What holds them apart in the flies is then not a transfer of this kind at the claw, nor a fixed change of the input ([above](#input-side)), nor the differences between flies in what reaches the KCs, which move these pairs apart with APL on and with APL off alike ([the ORN input as a population of flies](#input-population)); for inhibition that follows the calyx space that glomeruli share, the reading made with a static proxy is withheld with the connectome tables that it rests on ([above](#apl-calyx-maps)).

Read since against recordings of the stages before the somata, these pairs are the one case in which the model's step from claws to somata with APL on is too small in every reading, which keeps their shortfall where it had been placed ([the model's stages against the flies' stages](#model-stages)). What the hard knee did for the release with APL off is kept as a lead: whether responders can be selected at the claw without a dead zone that silences the weak odors is open. What is taken up from here is with the pending work at the end of the page.

### The flies' recording protocol in the model: the best families read as the flies were recorded, and what keeps the response with APL off at the odor's onset {#flies-protocol}

**Read as the flies were recorded, at their 2 s odor pulse and through their response window, the family with the firing ceiling loses part of its level on the main target at the adaptation it was fitted with: its APL-effect loss on raw spike counts rises by about a fifth with the indicator's kinetics as they have since been measured in the recordings, and by two fifths with the faster indicator that this subsection assumed, most of it in the mean part.** It has the level back once the adaptation outlasts the odor.

- An adaptation that decays over 1 s wears off within a 2 s odor, so that with APL off the KCs that it had held fire again late in the pulse; the assumed indicator gives those spikes the most weight in the flies' window, and the measured one weighs them like the others.
- With the adaptation decaying over 3 s, the fit, the literature setting on four wirings and a fit made at the flies' pulse all read what they read at the 0.5 s pulse. Mild depletion at the PN boutons does the same; a slower KC–KC inhibition and a slower APL do not, and a faster APL comes under the limit that had been set only with the measured kinetics.
- At the 0.5 s pulse itself the 3 s adaptation leaves the numbers of the family with the ceiling where they were, so that for it the short pulse with that setting stands in for the flies' protocol.
- The family without a ceiling keeps its match only under the calibrated readout, and a fit at the flies' pulse does not help it on raw counts.
- The error common to all wirings is made neither by the pulse nor by the window, and the time constant of APL's inhibition does not carry it.

[The flies' pulse in the model and the remaining candidates for the common error](#remaining-candidates) had left the raw-count numbers of the main target tied to the model's 0.5 s pulse, at parameters fitted with that pulse and with every spike counted alike. The flies' responses are neither: a response is the mean of a KC's calcium signal from 2 to 8 s after the onset of a 2 s pulse ([footnote](#fn-baseline-noise-units)), so that a spike late in the pulse counts for more than one at its onset, by how much depending on how fast the indicator's signal decays. The flies' recording protocol in the model read the models that way.

Each spike is weighted by the part of an indicator's response to it that falls inside the flies' window, for a response that rises over 0.5 s and decays over 3 s; rises of 0.2 to 1 s and decays of 1 to 5 s were read beside it, the kinetics of the indicator in these recordings not being on hand then. The weighted counts are scored raw and through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout), its half-saturation set again on them. Which KCs respond stays the two-spike criterion on the counts, so the response rates and the realism bands do not depend on the reading.

**The kinetics as measured (added 2026-11-11).** The indicator's kinetics in these recordings have since been measured from the frame-by-frame traces ([the time course of the APL effect in the flies' traces](#trace-time-course)), and they are several times slower than the slowest read here: a kernel fitted to the control flies' responses rises over {{E84/kernel_fits.csv:level=subset;subset=control flies;selection=resp;fit=free;drive=onset:rise ~ .2f}} s and decays over {{E84/kernel_fits.csv:level=subset;subset=control flies;selection=resp;fit=free;drive=onset:decay ~ .1f}} s if the KCs fire in a burst at the odor's onset, and decays over {{E84/kernel_fits.csv:level=subset;subset=control flies;selection=resp;fit=free;drive=steady:decay ~ .1f}} s if they fire evenly through the pulse.

With a decay that slow the flies' window weighs every spike of the pulse about alike, so that a model read as the flies were recorded reads what its spike counts at the 2 s pulse read: the first of the two values wherever the tables and the text below give two. The second values, through the assumed indicator, overstate what late firing costs.

Through the two measured kernels the fit with the ceiling at its 1 s adaptation reads {{E84/protocol_readings_measured_kernel.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;kernel=r1.29_d20.7:raw_loss ~ .3f}} and {{E84/protocol_readings_measured_kernel.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;kernel=r0.05_d21.9:raw_loss ~ .3f}} at the flies' pulse where the assumed kernel gave {{E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;kernel=r0.5_d3:raw_loss ~ .3f}}: {{diff:E84/protocol_readings_measured_kernel.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;kernel=r1.29_d20.7:raw_loss -- E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse0.5_fixed;kernel=counts:raw_loss ~ .3f}} to {{diff:E84/protocol_readings_measured_kernel.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;kernel=r0.05_d21.9:raw_loss -- E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse0.5_fixed;kernel=counts:raw_loss ~ .3f}} above the 0.5 s pulse in place of {{diff:E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;kernel=r0.5_d3:raw_loss -- E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse0.5_fixed;kernel=counts:raw_loss ~ .3f}}, about a fifth of its loss in place of two fifths, and a little more than one draw of the wiring moves the loss on raw counts in place of more than twice that. The mean over four wirings at the literature setting reads {{E84/protocol_populations_measured_kernel.csv:population=fc;pulse=2.0;kernel=r1.29_d20.7:raw_loss ~ .3f}} and {{E84/protocol_populations_measured_kernel.csv:population=fc;pulse=2.0;kernel=r0.05_d21.9:raw_loss ~ .3f}} for {{E82/protocol_populations.csv:population=fc;pulse=2.0;kernel=r0.5_d3:raw_loss ~ .3f}}, and the family without a ceiling {{E84/protocol_populations_measured_kernel.csv:population=b2;pulse=2.0;kernel=r1.29_d20.7:raw_loss ~ .3f}} and {{E84/protocol_populations_measured_kernel.csv:population=b2;pulse=2.0;kernel=r0.05_d21.9:raw_loss ~ .3f}} for {{E82/protocol_populations.csv:population=b2;pulse=2.0;kernel=r0.5_d3:raw_loss ~ .3f}}.

Where the adaptation outlasts the odor nothing changes ({{E84/protocol_readings_measured_kernel.csv:point_id=B2_fit0_tau3;kernel=r1.29_d20.7:raw_loss ~ .3f}} for the fit with the 3 s adaptation, through either kernel). One verdict on the settings changes: with APL's time constant at 0.01 s the fit with the ceiling reads {{E84/gate_measured_kernel.csv:measured_kernel=measured_onset;point_id=B5_fit0_taum0.01:raw_loss_primary ~ .4f}} and {{E84/gate_measured_kernel.csv:measured_kernel=measured_steady;point_id=B5_fit0_taum0.01:raw_loss_primary ~ .4f}} through the measured kernels, under the limit of {{E82/gate.csv:point_id=B2_fit0_tau3:pg_limit ~ .4f}}, where the assumed kernel gave {{E82/gate.csv:point_id=B5_fit0_taum0.01:raw_loss_primary ~ .4f}}; every other verdict stands, and no setting passes the test of the input side under any reading.

The paragraphs and tables below are as they were written with the assumed indicator and are to be read with this: the loss of level at the 1 s adaptation is about half as large as they give it, the case for an adaptation that outlasts the odor is weaker by as much, and the reading as the flies were recorded is, for practical purposes, the count of spikes at the flies' pulse.

Three things were done.

- Runs at the 2 s pulse, with both response rates held at each fit's own, were read this way: the breadth-2 APL-effect fit and the same family with the firing ceiling at its stronger setting on the real wiring (the two fits that the flies' pulse in the model was run on), and each family on four wirings (the real one, two claw permutations and one matched shuffle; the ceiling there at its literature setting), scored as the mean over the four.
- On the two fits, what could keep the response with APL off at the odor's onset was then varied at fixed scales, with both response rates held again: the time constant of the ceiling's adaptation (0.3, 3 and 10 s for its 1 s), depletion of the PN boutons' vesicles at two strengths, a KC–KC inhibition that lasts 0.2 or 1 s for its 0.05 s, and a time constant of APL of 0.01, 0.25 or 1 s for its 0.05 s. What a setting had to do had been set beforehand: bring the fit with the ceiling to a loss of {{E82/gate.csv:point_id=B2_fit0_tau3:pg_limit ~ .3f}} or less, on spike counts and through the flies' window, inside the realism bands and with spike counts no larger than at the 1 s adaptation.
- Last, both families were fitted again at the flies' pulse, the one with the ceiling with its adaptation at 3 s.

The breadth-2 APL-effect fit and the same family with the firing ceiling at its stronger setting, on the real wiring: at the model's 0.5 s pulse as fitted, at the flies' 2 s pulse with both response rates held and nothing fitted again, and fitted again at the 2 s pulse. In the first five rows two values are with every spike counted alike / read through the flies' window; in the family with the ceiling the calibrated readout runs to the upper end of its range, where it changes nothing. The eighth row is the model's prediction for the recorded traces: every spike of a responding KC × odor entry is given the indicator's response, the signal is averaged over the responding entries of each condition, and its mean with APL off is divided by its mean with APL on over three parts of the response

**At the adaptation it was fitted with, the ceiling loses its level at the flies' protocol.** At the 0.5 s pulse the fit with the ceiling scores on raw counts below what the breadth-2 fit scores through the calibrated readout, and the flies' window changes next to nothing there, since no spike comes late (fourth model column against the first).

At the flies' pulse and through their window its loss is two fifths higher and its mean APL effect a fifth lower, with the pattern part a little higher (fifth model column). That is {{diff:E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;kernel=r0.5_d3:raw_loss -- E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=C2_pulse2_held;kernel=r0.5_d3:cal_loss ~ .3f}} above the breadth-2 fit's loss through the readout, which hardly moves with the pulse, and still far below that fit's raw counts (second model column). The mean over four wirings at the literature setting rises by as much, more than twice what one draw of the wiring moves the loss on raw counts ({{E72/spread.csv:readout=raw:sd_single ~ .3f}}; table below). Late spikes with APL off make this.

With APL on nearly every spike of the fit falls in the first half second of the 2 s odor; with APL off a few in a hundred come later (sixth row), from {{E82/late_spikes.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;condition=off;by=total:n_kcs_late ~ .0f}} of the {{E82/late_spikes.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;condition=off;by=total:n_kcs_group ~ .0f}} KCs, and their number grows through the pulse, from {{E82/late_spikes.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;condition=off;by=bin;key=0.50-0.75:n_spikes ~ .0f}} in the quarter second after 0.5 s to {{E82/late_spikes.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;condition=off;by=bin;key=1.75-2.00:n_spikes ~ .0f}} in the last quarter second of the odor. The adaptation had been given its time constant of 1 s at a 0.5 s odor, which it outlasted; within a 2 s odor it wears off, and KCs that it had held fire again; with APL on, APL keeps them silent.

The flies' window adds to the weight of these spikes because it starts where the pulse ends: the faster the indicator is taken to decay, the higher the loss, from {{E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;kernel=r1_d5:raw_loss ~ .3f}} at the slowest kinetics read to {{E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;kernel=r0.2_d1:raw_loss ~ .3f}} at the fastest. With the APL-off spikes later than 0.5 s left out, nothing simulated again, the loss through the flies' window is {{E82/late_leave_out.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;kernel=r0.5_d3;left_out=all:raw_loss ~ .3f}}, the fit's own at the 0.5 s pulse.

Each family as a mean over four wirings (the real one, two claw permutations and one matched shuffle), every wiring with its own fit: the breadth-2 family and the same family with the firing ceiling at its literature setting. **An adaptation that outlasts the odor returns the numbers, and so does mild depletion at the boutons.** With the adaptation decaying over 3 s the late spikes with APL off are all but gone, and through the flies' window the fit reads within {{diff:E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=B2_fit0_tau3;kernel=r0.5_d3:raw_loss -- E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse0.5_fixed;kernel=counts:raw_loss ~ .3f}} of what it read at the 0.5 s pulse, with smaller largest spike counts (sixth model column of the first table). At 10 s it reads {{E82/gate.csv:point_id=B2_fit0_tau10:raw_loss_primary ~ .3f}}, and at 0.3 s, where the adaptation wears off sooner, {{E82/gate.csv:point_id=B2_fit0_tau0.3:raw_loss_primary ~ .3f}}. The reading no longer depends on the kinetics taken for the indicator ({{E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=B2_fit0_tau3;kernel=r0.2_d1:raw_loss ~ .3f}} at the fastest).

The literature setting on four wirings, run again with the 3 s adaptation, is back at its loss of the 0.5 s pulse (last column of the second table). The fit made at the flies' pulse with the 3 s adaptation, started from the fit at 0.5 s, ends {{diff:E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=B2_fit0_tau3;kernel=r0.5_d3:raw_loss -- E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t3000_k2_pulse2;kernel=r0.5_d3:raw_loss ~ .4f}} below the run with held response rates and at the numbers of the 0.5 s pulse in every row, on raw counts and through the readout alike (last column of the first table); having gained less than one draw of the wiring moves the loss, it was not repeated on re-drawn wirings.

Depletion of the PN boutons' vesicles does at its weaker strength what the longer adaptation does ({{E82/gate.csv:point_id=B3_fit0_ves0.01:raw_loss_primary ~ .3f}} through the flies' window, with largest spike counts of {{E82/gate.csv:point_id=B3_fit0_ves0.01:max_count_on ~ .0f}} with APL on and {{E82/gate.csv:point_id=B3_fit0_ves0.01:max_count_off ~ .0f}} with APL off); at the stronger the loss is {{E82/gate.csv:point_id=B3_fit0_ves0.03:raw_loss_primary ~ .3f}}. The other two do not.

- A KC–KC inhibition that lasts longer removes the late spikes as well, but raises the pattern part, to a loss of {{E82/gate.csv:point_id=B4_fit0_kckctau0.2:raw_loss_primary ~ .3f}} at 0.2 s and {{E82/gate.csv:point_id=B4_fit0_kckctau1:raw_loss_primary ~ .3f}} at 1 s.
- APL's own time constant leaves the spikes with APL off as they are, APL being removed there, and the loss stays between {{E82/gate.csv:point_id=B5_fit0_taum0.01:raw_loss_primary ~ .3f}} and {{E82/gate.csv:point_id=B5_fit0_taum1:raw_loss_primary ~ .3f}} (with the indicator's kinetics as measured since, the 0.01 s setting comes under the limit: the paragraph on the kinetics as measured, above).

**Without a ceiling only the readout holds.** The breadth-2 family has nothing that bounds the late firing. At the flies' pulse a third of its spikes with APL off come later than 0.5 s and its largest spike counts grow about threefold (sixth and seventh rows of the first table), and through the flies' window its loss on raw counts is two thirds higher than at the 0.5 s pulse on the real wiring and nearly twice as high as a mean over four wirings, with the mean APL effect at less than half. Through the calibrated readout, which takes away most of what the late spikes add to a KC's count, the same runs read within {{diff:E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=C2_pulse2_held;kernel=r0.5_d3:cal_loss -- E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=C2_pulse0.5_fixed;kernel=counts:cal_loss ~ .3f}} of the 0.5 s pulse, on the real wiring and as a mean over four wirings.

Fitted again at the flies' pulse, the family lowers its loss on raw counts through the flies' window by {{diff:E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=C2_pulse2_held;kernel=r0.5_d3:raw_loss -- E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=rate0.068_aplboth_k2_pulse2_cap3;kernel=r0.5_d3:raw_loss ~ .3f}} and leaves the readout's where it was (third model column): its KC–KC inhibition, free in the fit, does not bound the late firing. Of the settings tried on the fit at fixed scales, none brings the loss on raw counts through the flies' window below {{E82/gate.csv:point_id=B4_C2_kckctau1:raw_loss_primary ~ .3f}}, and the two that come nearest, the longest KC–KC inhibition and the stronger depletion, raise the loss through the readout (to {{E82/gate.csv:point_id=B4_C2_kckctau1:cal_loss_primary ~ .3f}} and {{E82/gate.csv:point_id=B3_C2_ves0.03:cal_loss_primary ~ .3f}}).

**The common error is made neither by the pulse nor by the window.** In the mean over four wirings of the breadth-2 family the pattern part through the readout is the same at the flies' protocol as at the 0.5 s pulse, and the two groups of the common error keep their signs and sizes: the model's APL effect stays too small among 2h, IaA, pa, eb, ep and ms and too large among 1-8ol, 1-5ol, 1-6ol and 6al (last two rows of the second table). On raw counts the pattern part rises with the pulse.

Each setting above was also put to the test of [the input side of the error common to all wirings](#input-side), against the same fit's run at the 2 s pulse, and none passes. The largest gain on the pattern part through the readout is {{E82/gate.csv:point_id=B3_fit0_ves0.01:pattern_gain ~ .4f}}, from the weaker depletion on the fit with the ceiling, where one draw of the wiring moves the loss by {{E72/spread.csv:readout=cal:sd_single ~ .3f}}. The transfer, the share of the common error's squared sum that a setting's change on the real wiring would remove if it were the same on every wiring, is negative at every setting (between {{E82/gate.csv:point_id=B5_fit0_taum0.25:transfer_all ~ +.2f}} and {{E82/gate.csv:point_id=B4_fit0_kckctau1:transfer_all ~ +.2f}}): each would add to the common error.

The time course of APL's inhibition was the last candidate that the input side had named on the model's side. As a time constant it is closed for this family; an APL that adapts was not run.

**Realism.** With the flies' responses counted in baseline-noise units, as the realism bands count now, every run of this experiment is inside all four bands: the response rates are held, and the number of odors per KC hardly moves with the pulse or the adaptation (lower rows of the first table). Counted by the recordings' own criterion, as until 2026-11-10, the two longer KC–KC inhibitions on the breadth-2 fit leave the band on the number of odors per KC with APL off ({{E82/runs.csv:point_id=B4_C2_kckctau0.2:opk_off_tv_zcrit ~ .3f}} and {{E82/runs.csv:point_id=B4_C2_kckctau1:opk_off_tv_zcrit ~ .3f}} against {{data:tnt_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .3f}}); everything else is inside, and nothing above rests on those two.

What the result asks to be defended lies outside the bands. It is a KC whose threshold stays raised for 3 s or longer after it has fired: no measurement of a KC's adaptation over seconds is on hand, and the whole-cell recordings from which the ceiling's strength was read used a 0.5 s odor ([footnote](#fn-firing-ceiling)).

Without a ceiling the spike counts at the flies' pulse are hard to defend, up to {{E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=rate0.068_aplboth_k2_pulse2_cap3;kernel=counts:max_count_on ~ .0f}} with APL on and {{E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=rate0.068_aplboth_k2_pulse2_cap3;kernel=counts:max_count_off ~ .0f}} with APL off for one KC and one odor in the fit made at 2 s, where the family with the ceiling and the 3 s adaptation stays at {{E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t3000_k2_pulse2;kernel=counts:max_count_on ~ .0f}} and {{E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t3000_k2_pulse2;kernel=counts:max_count_off ~ .0f}}. And in every model the response to a 2 s odor is almost all an onset burst: with APL on, {{E82/late_spikes.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;condition=on;by=total:share_first_bin ~ .1%}} of the spikes of the fit with the ceiling and {{E82/late_spikes.csv:point_id=C2_pulse2_held;condition=on;by=total:share_first_bin ~ .0%}} of the breadth-2 fit's fall in the first quarter second, and whether the flies' KCs fire through a 2 s odor is not in the data on hand.

The gain at the flies' protocol thus comes with the adaptation's time constant and costs nothing that the bands hold. As everywhere, the pairs with paa, euc and -aPine rest on [ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations); these three odors have {{E82/late_spikes.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;condition=off;by=odor;key=paa:n_late ~ .0f}}, {{E82/late_spikes.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;condition=off;by=odor;key=euc:n_late ~ .0f}} and {{E82/late_spikes.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;condition=off;by=odor;key=-aPine:n_late ~ .0f}} of the {{E82/late_spikes.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;condition=off;by=total:n_late ~ .0f}} late spikes of the fit with the ceiling.

**What follows.** The raw-count numbers that this page gives for the family with the firing ceiling hold as the flies were recorded on one condition, that the ceiling's adaptation outlasts the odor. The check that had been left open with the ceiling, whether its effect needs a time constant longer than the odor ([footnote](#fn-firing-ceiling)), is thereby answered: it does. For the family without a ceiling only the calibrated readout holds at either pulse.

Two things are then to be decided, and both are choices: whether the firing ceiling, with an adaptation that outlasts the odor, joins the base model, and which reading carries the model's side of the main target, raw counts read as the flies were recorded or the calibrated readout. With the ceiling and the 3 s adaptation the two readings give one number ({{E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t3000_k2_pulse2;kernel=r0.5_d3:raw_loss ~ .3f}} and {{E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t3000_k2_pulse2;kernel=r0.5_d3:cal_loss ~ .3f}} for the fit made at the flies' pulse), so the second choice weighs only if the ceiling stays out.

If the ceiling joins with that adaptation, later experiments can stay at the 0.5 s pulse, which takes fewer simulation steps, with each experiment's best fits read once as the flies were recorded. That rests on one more set of runs, the 3 s adaptation at the 0.5 s pulse itself with both response rates held, and they leave the family's numbers in place.

On raw counts, every spike counted alike, the fit at the stronger setting reads {{E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=B7_fit0_tau3;kernel=counts:raw_loss ~ .3f}} for {{E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse0.5_fixed;kernel=counts:raw_loss ~ .3f}} with its 1 s ({{E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=B7_fit0_tau10;kernel=counts:raw_loss ~ .3f}} with 10 s); the literature setting as a mean over four wirings reads {{E82/protocol_populations.csv:population=fc_tau3;pulse=0.5;kernel=counts:raw_loss ~ .3f}} for {{E82/protocol_populations.csv:population=fc;pulse=0.5;kernel=counts:raw_loss ~ .3f}}, and {{E82/protocol_populations.csv:population=fc_tau3;pulse=2.0;kernel=counts:raw_loss ~ .3f}} at the flies' pulse with the same adaptation ({{E82/protocol_populations.csv:population=fc_tau3;pulse=2.0;kernel=r0.5_d3:raw_loss ~ .3f}} through the flies' window); and the fit made at the flies' pulse reads {{E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=B7_D1_held;kernel=counts:raw_loss ~ .3f}} at the 0.5 s pulse for {{E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=I_B7_D1;kernel=counts:raw_loss ~ .3f}} at its own pulse. Each difference is less than one draw of the wiring moves the loss, the bound set before the runs for the fit and for the four wirings, and all of these runs are inside the realism bands.

For this family the 0.5 s pulse with the 3 s adaptation thus stands in for the flies' protocol, and nothing was fitted again. What has to be defended is the adaptation, and how long a KC's threshold stays raised after it has fired is the measurement to ask for; mild depletion at the boutons is the model's other way to the same numbers.

The model also gave its side of a question that waited on the recorded traces. With the ceiling and the 3 s adaptation the signal of the responding KCs with APL off is {{E82/predicted_ratios.csv:point_id=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t3000_k2_pulse2;kernel=r0.5_d3;signal=resp;t0=0.0:ratio_off_on ~ .2f}} times that with APL on during the pulse and {{E82/predicted_ratios.csv:point_id=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t3000_k2_pulse2;kernel=r0.5_d3;signal=resp;t0=4.0:ratio_off_on ~ .2f}} times at the end of the window; without a ceiling the ratio grows from {{E82/predicted_ratios.csv:point_id=C2_pulse2_held;kernel=r0.5_d3;signal=resp;t0=0.0:ratio_off_on ~ .2f}} to {{E82/predicted_ratios.csv:point_id=C2_pulse2_held;kernel=r0.5_d3;signal=resp;t0=4.0:ratio_off_on ~ .2f}} (eighth row of the first table). A ratio that grows after the pulse in the flies would say that their KCs go on firing through an odor when APL output is blocked, which an adaptation of this kind would not allow.

The traces have been read since: over all KC × odor entries the flies' ratio grows less than the family without a ceiling makes it grow, and among the responding entries it does not grow at all ([the time course of the APL effect in the flies' traces](#trace-time-course)). What is taken up from here is with the pending work at the end of the page.

### The flies' variability across the three repeats: what the odors of one repeat share, the noise correction it biases, and whether the models read through the trial noise stand {#repeat-structure}

%%% hover
same-repeat gap: The single-trial cosine distance between two different odors presented in different repeats of the panel minus the distance between the same two odors presented in the same repeat, averaged over odor pairs and recordings. It is positive when the odors of one repeat share part of their trial-to-trial variability.
estimate across repeats: A pair's distance without the trial noise, taken from single trials. One minus the cosine between trials of the two odors from different repeats, divided by the geometric mean of the two odors' cosines between their own trials across the same repeats. It assumes only that the noise of different repeats is independent.
re-specified noise: The model's trial noise set to the flies' two shares. A jitter of each KC's threshold that all odors of a trial share, at the level at which the model's same-repeat gap is the flies', plus a factor drawn independently for every KC, odor and trial that brings the distance between two presentations of one odor to the flies'.
%%%

**In the recordings, two different odors presented in the same repeat of the panel are more alike than the same two odors in different repeats: part of the flies' trial-to-trial variability is shared by the odors of a repeat, and that part is nearly three times larger with APL output blocked (TNT) than in control flies.** About three quarters of it follows the time between the two presentations, mostly a slow drift over the session, and the rest is tied to the repeat itself; neither the per-pair APL effect nor the error common to all wirings follows the order in which the odors were presented.

- Responses also run down over the session, faster in control flies, so that the ratio of the two response rates rises from the first repeat to the third.
- The correction for trial-to-trial noise that this page had used takes the noise of two odors to be independent, and it put the distances without noise too low; an estimate that needs only independence between repeats replaces it.
- The main target, the effect as measured, is not touched: the saved models keep their order against the effect without the noise, and the error common to all wirings is there from the first repeat.
- The model's trial noise has the wrong make-up, all of it shared between the odors of a trial, but set to the flies' shares it leaves the populations of wirings where they stood, and the firing ceiling's standing with them.
- What the model does not make is the asymmetry: its odors of one trial are hardly more alike with APL off than with APL on.

Every comparison of a model with the KC data as the data are made passes the model through [trial-to-trial noise](#fn-trial-noise) calibrated on one number, how far apart two presentations of one odor are, and every level quoted without the trial noise came from a correction that takes the noise of different odors to be independent. Each recording holds three repeats of the panel, so both can be checked against the flies. The flies' variability across the three repeats did that from the per-trial responses of the {{data:n_recordings_ctrl ~ .0f}} control recordings and the {{data:n_recordings_tnt ~ .0f}} with APL output blocked (TNT), with 90 % intervals from resampling the recordings. It then scored the saved models against the effect without the noise and read the best families again through a noise with the flies' make-up. No model was fitted.

![Single-trial cosine distances in the recordings' z-scored unit (z in the first panel's title). Left: the mean distance between two presentations of one odor in adjacent repeats and in the first and third repeat, and between two different odors in the same repeat and in different repeats (bars: 90 % intervals over recordings). Middle: the same-repeat gap of each recording, the distance between two odors in different repeats minus that in the same repeat, over all 120 pairs and over the six pairs with near-identical ORN input. Right: each pair's distance without the trial noise by the estimate across repeats against the same by the earlier correction (line: equality).](results/E81_repeat_structure/E81_distances_by_kind.png)

**The odors of one repeat share part of their variability, and more of it with APL output blocked.** The same-repeat gap is the distance between two different odors presented in different repeats minus the distance between the same two odors presented in the same repeat, both between single trials. If the variability of two odors' responses were independent it would be zero. It is positive in every recording, {{data:repeat_gap_ratio_tnt_ctrl ~ .1f}} times larger with APL output blocked (TNT) than in control flies (90 % interval {{data:repeat_gap_ratio_tnt_ctrl.lo ~ .1f}} to {{data:repeat_gap_ratio_tnt_ctrl.hi ~ .1f}}), and largest over the six pairs with near-identical ORN input (table below). The size of the responses does not make it: with every entry reduced to responding or not, the gap is about the same.

Of the trial-to-trial variance of a responding KC's response, the part common to that KC's odors within a repeat is {{E81/variance_parts.csv:units=z;genotype=TNT3c;level=genotype;cls=responders;statistic=share_shared:value ~ .0%}} in control flies and {{E81/variance_parts.csv:units=z;genotype=TNT;level=genotype;cls=responders;statistic=share_shared:value ~ .0%}} with APL output blocked (TNT). The variability also has a slow part: two presentations of one odor are further apart between the first and the third repeat than between adjacent repeats.

**Most of what the odors of a repeat share follows the time between presentations, and the order of the odors does not make the target.**

A repeat is one block of the session in which every odor is presented once, so two odors of one repeat are also closer in time than two odors of different repeats, and the order of the presentations tells the two apart: {{E81/order_gap_decomposition.csv:units=z;basis=positions;genotype=TNT3c;statistic=separation_share:value ~ .0%}} of the same-repeat gap in control flies and {{E81/order_gap_decomposition.csv:units=z;basis=positions;genotype=TNT;statistic=separation_share:value ~ .0%}} with APL output blocked (TNT) follows how many presentations apart the two were, and the rest is a step for the same repeat at equal separation (the two rows under the gap in the table above). Most of the first part is a slow drift over the session, two presentations growing less alike with the time between them up to the first repeat against the third (figure below), and both parts are larger with APL output blocked (TNT), by {{E81/order_gap_decomposition.csv:units=z;basis=positions;genotype=ratio;statistic=separation_part:value ~ .1f}} and {{E81/order_gap_decomposition.csv:units=z;basis=positions;genotype=ratio;statistic=block_part:value ~ .1f}} times.

Across the 120 pairs neither the per-pair APL effect nor the error common to all wirings (under the calibrated readout) follows how far apart the two odors of a pair were presented: their Spearman correlations with the pair's mean separation within a repeat, control flies minus APL output blocked (TNT), are {{E81/order_confound.csv:statistic=rho_effect_sep_diff:value ~ .2f}} and {{E81/order_confound.csv:statistic=rho_common_cal_sep_diff:value ~ .2f}}, where 90 % of orders drawn at random with the same reuse of orders give {{E81/order_confound.csv:statistic=rho_effect_sep_diff:null_lo ~ .2f}} to {{E81/order_confound.csv:statistic=rho_effect_sep_diff:null_hi ~ .2f}} and {{E81/order_confound.csv:statistic=rho_common_cal_sep_diff:null_lo ~ .2f}} to {{E81/order_confound.csv:statistic=rho_common_cal_sep_diff:null_hi ~ .2f}} (the strongest of the twelve such correlations, with the error also on raw counts and the separation also in each genotype alone and in all recordings, is {{E81/order_confound.csv:statistic=rho_common_raw_sep_tnt:value ~ .2f}}, at p = {{E81/order_confound.csv:statistic=rho_common_raw_sep_tnt:p_null ~ .2f}}, which the strongest of twelve often reaches by chance).

The shift of the per-pair effect that the separations predict has a root mean square of {{E81/order_confound.csv:statistic=confound_rms:value ~ .3f}}, against {{data:apl_effect_rmse_floor ~ .3f}} for the floor of the loss. The re-specified noise of the models (below) was matched to the gap as a whole, a jitter per repeat standing in for the drift, so what is concluded below about the models' noise stands.

**Responses run down over the session, and the ratio of the two response rates rises with them.** The response rate of single trials falls from the first repeat to the third in {{E81/rundown.csv:units=noise;criterion=bands;genotype=TNT3c;subset=all;level=genotype;statistic=n_recordings_r3_below_r1:value ~ .0f}} of the {{data:n_recordings_ctrl ~ .0f}} control recordings and in {{E81/rundown.csv:units=noise;criterion=bands;genotype=TNT;subset=all;level=genotype;statistic=n_recordings_r3_below_r1:value ~ .0f}} of the {{data:n_recordings_tnt ~ .0f}} with APL output blocked (TNT), and by more than twice as large a fraction in control flies (last row of the table).

The APL-off / APL-on response-rate ratio therefore depends on when in the session it is taken: {{data:repeat_rate_ratio_r1 ~ .2f}} in the first repeat (90 % interval {{data:repeat_rate_ratio_r1.lo ~ .2f}} to {{data:repeat_rate_ratio_r1.hi ~ .2f}}), {{data:repeat_rate_ratio_r2 ~ .2f}} in the second and {{data:repeat_rate_ratio_r3 ~ .2f}} in the third ({{data:repeat_rate_ratio_r3.lo ~ .2f}} to {{data:repeat_rate_ratio_r3.hi ~ .2f}}), {{data:repeat_rate_ratio_session ~ .2f}} over all single trials. The two recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) whose distances stand apart from the other six ([the data side of the main target](#data-side)) are the two that do not run down: from the first repeat to the third their response rate changes by {{E81/rundown.csv:units=noise;criterion=bands;genotype=TNT;subset=strong2;level=genotype;statistic=rate_change_r3_vs_r1:value ~ +.2f}} of its value in the first repeat, against {{E81/rundown.csv:units=noise;criterion=bands;genotype=TNT;subset=typical6;level=genotype;statistic=rate_change_r3_vs_r1:value ~ +.2f}} for the six.

![The run-down over the three repeats, with single trials counted above the realism bands' threshold in baseline-noise units (90 % intervals over recordings; thin lines: single recordings). Left: the response rate by repeat. Middle: the mean amplitude of the responding entries. Right: the APL-off / APL-on response-rate ratio by repeat, over all recordings and with only the six recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) that are alike, against the realism band on the ratio (grey).](results/E81_repeat_structure/E81_rundown.png)

**The earlier noise correction is biased, and the target is not.** The correction divided each pair's cosine by the two odors' signal norms, on the assumption that the noise adds nothing to the product of two different odors' responses. What the odors of a repeat share does add to that product, and the correction counted it as similarity between the odors. It therefore put the distances too low, most with APL output blocked (TNT), where the shared part is larger, and so the mean APL effect too high. The estimate across repeats uses only products of trials from different repeats, which that shared part does not enter: one minus the cosine between single trials of the two odors from different repeats, divided by the geometric mean of the two odors' cosines between their own trials across the same repeats.

The KC data as measured, by the earlier noise correction and without the trial noise by the estimate across repeats (the recordings' z-scored unit; 90 % intervals over recordings in parentheses)

| statistic | as measured, on the three-trial means (the main target's) | the earlier noise correction | without the trial noise, by the estimate across repeats |

| mean pair distance, control flies | {{data:ctrl_mean_dist ~ .3f}} | {{data:ctrl_mean_dist_noise_corrected ~ .3f}} | {{data:noise_free_mean_dist_ctrl ~ .3f}} ({{data:noise_free_mean_dist_ctrl.lo ~ .3f}} to {{data:noise_free_mean_dist_ctrl.hi ~ .3f}}) |
| mean pair distance, APL output blocked (TNT) | {{data:tnt_mean_dist ~ .3f}} | {{data:tnt_mean_dist_noise_corrected ~ .3f}} | {{data:noise_free_mean_dist_tnt ~ .3f}} ({{data:noise_free_mean_dist_tnt.lo ~ .3f}} to {{data:noise_free_mean_dist_tnt.hi ~ .3f}}) |
| mean APL effect over the 120 pairs | {{data:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}} | {{data:apl_effect_noise_corrected_mean ~ +.3f}} | {{data:noise_free_apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}} ({{data:noise_free_apl_effect_mean.lo ~ +.3f}} to {{data:noise_free_apl_effect_mean.hi ~ +.3f}}) |
| mean APL effect of the six pairs with near-identical ORN input | {{E81/noise_free_summary.csv:units=z;values=graded;side=effect;estimator=trial_mean;statistic=six_mean:value ~ +.3f}} | {{E81/noise_free_summary.csv:units=z;values=graded;side=effect;estimator=corrected;statistic=six_mean:value ~ +.3f}} | {{data:noise_free_apl_effect_six ~ +.3f}} ({{data:noise_free_apl_effect_six.lo ~ +.3f}} to {{data:noise_free_apl_effect_six.hi ~ +.3f}}) |
| fruity × small-ester block | {{data:block ~ +.3f}} | {{data:block_corrected ~ +.3f}} | {{data:noise_free_block ~ +.3f}} ({{data:noise_free_block.lo ~ +.3f}} to {{data:noise_free_block.hi ~ +.3f}}) |
| floor of the APL-effect loss | {{data:apl_effect_rmse_floor ~ .3f}} | {{E81/noise_free_summary.csv:units=z;values=graded;side=effect;estimator=corrected;statistic=rmse_floor:value ~ .3f}} | {{data:noise_free_apl_effect_rmse_floor ~ .3f}} |
| ceiling on ρ on the per-pair APL effect | {{data:apl_effect_rho_ceiling ~ .2f}} | {{E81/noise_free_summary.csv:units=z;values=graded;side=effect;estimator=corrected;statistic=rho_ceiling:value ~ .2f}} | {{data:noise_free_apl_effect_rho_ceiling ~ .2f}} |

Without the trial noise the per-pair APL effect is close to the effect as measured: across the 120 pairs the two have a Spearman correlation of {{data:noise_free_apl_effect_rho_measured ~ .2f}} and a root mean squared difference of {{E81/noise_free_summary.csv:units=z;values=graded;side=effect;estimator=noise_free;statistic=rms_diff_from_measured:value ~ .3f}}, well under the floor of the loss; its own floor is a little higher and its ceiling the same (last two rows of the table). The main target therefore stands as it is defined, on the three-trial means.

What changes is the level quoted for a model without noise. The mean distances are higher than the earlier correction gave, the mean effect is hardly above the measured one, and over the six pairs with near-identical ORN input the effect without the noise is smaller than as measured, not larger.

The estimate has a limit of its own. With APL output blocked (TNT) the mean distance estimated from adjacent repeats is {{E81/noise_free_summary.csv:units=z;values=graded;side=tnt;estimator=adjacent_minus_first_third;statistic=mean:value ~ .3f}} above the one estimated from the first against the third repeat ({{E81/noise_free_summary.csv:units=z;values=graded;side=tnt;estimator=adjacent_minus_first_third;statistic=mean:lo ~ .3f}} to {{E81/noise_free_summary.csv:units=z;values=graded;side=tnt;estimator=adjacent_minus_first_third;statistic=mean:hi ~ .3f}}; in control flies the two agree, {{E81/noise_free_summary.csv:units=z;values=graded;side=ctrl;estimator=adjacent_minus_first_third;statistic=mean:value ~ +.3f}}), so there the slow drift does not cancel completely.

**The saved models keep their order, and the error common to all wirings is there from the first repeat.** Scored against the effect without the noise, nearly every saved model's loss is a little higher and the order is the same: over the {{lit:1058 # results/E81_repeat_structure/comparison_table.md, section B1 (the number of variant rows of by_variant_noise_free.csv with both losses on raw counts)}} saved models the losses against the two effects have a Spearman correlation of {{lit:0.999 # results/E81_repeat_structure/comparison_table.md, section B1 (Spearman correlation of raw_measured_loss with raw_noise_free_loss over the variant rows of by_variant_noise_free.csv)}} on raw spike counts and {{lit:0.991 # results/E81_repeat_structure/comparison_table.md, section B1 (Spearman correlation of cal_measured_loss with cal_noise_free_loss over the variant rows of by_variant_noise_free.csv)}} under the calibrated readout, and the ten lowest are the same ten.

Nor does the session's history make the error common to all wirings. The per-pair APL effect taken within one repeat, from single trials of both genotypes, has the same mean in each repeat ({{data:repeat_apl_effect_mean_r1 ~ +.3f}}, {{data:repeat_apl_effect_mean_r2 ~ +.3f}} and {{data:repeat_apl_effect_mean_r3 ~ +.3f}}), and its Spearman correlation with the common error across the 120 pairs is as strong in the first repeat as in the third ({{E81/effect_by_repeat.csv:statistic=rho_common_cal;repeat=1:value ~ .2f}}, {{E81/effect_by_repeat.csv:statistic=rho_common_cal;repeat=2:value ~ .2f}} and {{E81/effect_by_repeat.csv:statistic=rho_common_cal;repeat=3:value ~ .2f}}; {{E81/effect_by_repeat.csv:statistic=rho_common_cal;repeat=session:value ~ .2f}} for the three-trial means; negative because the error is the model's effect minus the flies').

An error built up by the run-down would be weaker in the first repeat. The size of the effect's part along the error is {{E81/effect_by_repeat.csv:statistic=proj_common_cal_ratio_3_over_1;repeat=all:value ~ .2f}} times larger in the third repeat than in the first, with an interval that includes no change ({{E81/effect_by_repeat.csv:statistic=proj_common_cal_ratio_3_over_1;repeat=all:lo ~ .2f}} to {{E81/effect_by_repeat.csv:statistic=proj_common_cal_ratio_3_over_1;repeat=all:hi ~ .2f}}).

**With the flies' shares in the model's noise, the populations of wirings stay where they stood.** The trial noise put into the models is one draw per KC and trial, applied to the KC's threshold for all odors of the trial, so all of it is of the shared kind. At the level that matches the flies' distance between two presentations of one odor, the breadth-2 APL-effect fit has a same-repeat gap of {{E81/shared_state.csv:model=C2;condition=both:gap_on ~ .3f}} with APL on and {{E81/shared_state.csv:model=C2;condition=both:gap_off ~ .3f}} with APL off, where the flies have {{data:repeat_gap_ctrl ~ .3f}} and {{data:repeat_gap_tnt ~ .3f}}. The noise was therefore re-specified with the flies' two shares.

The shared jitter was lowered to the level at which the model's same-repeat gap is the flies' (for that fit a standard deviation of {{E81/mix_checks.csv:model=C2;readout=raw;unit=z;condition=on:sigma ~ .3f}} of the threshold with APL on and {{E81/mix_checks.csv:model=C2;readout=raw;unit=z;condition=acute_off:sigma ~ .3f}} with APL off, against {{E81/jitter_at_flies_gap.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;model=E67-rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3:sigma_matched_on ~ .3f}} in the pipeline), by interpolation between saved runs of the pipeline without noise, at half its matched jitter and at the matched level, and a factor drawn independently for every KC, odor and trial was added until the distance between two presentations of one odor was the flies' as well. The two populations of four wirings that had been read through the pipeline, the breadth-2 family without and with the firing ceiling at its literature setting ([above](#glomerulus-profile)), were scored again through this noise.

Through the re-specified noise the loss of the population without the ceiling moves by {{diff:E81/populations.csv:group=breadth-2 four;readout=raw;unit=z;kind=mix:loss -- E81/populations.csv:group=breadth-2 four;readout=raw;unit=z;kind=present_match_on:loss ~ +.3f}} and that of the population with it by {{diff:E81/populations.csv:group=firing-ceiling four;readout=raw;unit=z;kind=mix:loss -- E81/populations.csv:group=firing-ceiling four;readout=raw;unit=z;kind=present_match_on:loss ~ +.3f}}, both under half of what one draw of the wiring moves the loss on raw counts ({{E72/spread.csv:readout=raw:sd_single ~ .3f}}), and the ceiling's lead over the family without it stays inside that as well. Under the calibrated readout the two populations read {{E81/populations.csv:group=breadth-2 four;readout=cal;unit=z;kind=mix:loss ~ .3f}} and {{E81/populations.csv:group=firing-ceiling four;readout=cal;unit=z;kind=mix:loss ~ .3f}}, where through the pipeline they read {{E81/populations.csv:group=breadth-2 four;readout=cal;unit=z;kind=present_match_on:loss ~ .3f}} and {{E81/populations.csv:group=firing-ceiling four;readout=cal;unit=z;kind=present_match_on:loss ~ .3f}}: the two swap places, by less than one draw of the wiring moves the loss there ({{E72/spread.csv:readout=cal:sd_single ~ .3f}}). Against the flies' effect in baseline-noise units, where every model is short on the mean, the losses on raw counts are higher under either noise and in the same order ({{E81/populations.csv:group=breadth-2 four;readout=raw;unit=noise;kind=mix:loss ~ .3f}} and {{E81/populations.csv:group=firing-ceiling four;readout=raw;unit=noise;kind=mix:loss ~ .3f}} through the re-specified noise, {{E81/populations.csv:group=breadth-2 four;readout=raw;unit=noise;kind=present_match_on:loss ~ .3f}} and {{E81/populations.csv:group=firing-ceiling four;readout=raw;unit=noise;kind=present_match_on:loss ~ .3f}} through the pipeline).

The numbers read through the pipeline therefore stand, and with them the reading that the firing ceiling gives no clear gain on raw counts once flies and trials are both in the model. A second form of the independent part, a jitter of the threshold drawn anew for every presentation and run as simulations for the two fits on the real wiring, gives the same reading: {{E81/per_presentation.csv:group=C2;readout=raw;unit=z;kind=presentation:loss ~ .3f}} for the breadth-2 fit, where the factor gives {{E81/mix_scores.csv:name=E67-rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;readout=raw;unit=z;kind=mix:loss ~ .3f}}, and {{E81/per_presentation.csv:group=F1;readout=raw;unit=z;kind=presentation:loss ~ .3f}} and {{E81/mix_scores.csv:name=E69-rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2;readout=raw;unit=z;kind=mix:loss ~ .3f}} for the fit with the ceiling.

**Two statistics depend on the make-up of the noise more than the loss does.** One is the effect on the six pairs with near-identical ORN input. With the noise removed from both sides by the estimate across repeats, the population without the ceiling has an APL effect of {{E81/populations.csv:group=breadth-2 four;readout=raw;unit=z;kind=mix_noise_free:six_effect ~ +.3f}} on them and the population with it {{E81/populations.csv:group=firing-ceiling four;readout=raw;unit=z;kind=mix_noise_free:six_effect ~ +.3f}}, against the flies' {{data:noise_free_apl_effect_six ~ +.3f}} ({{data:noise_free_apl_effect_six.lo ~ +.3f}} to {{data:noise_free_apl_effect_six.hi ~ +.3f}}): a little under two thirds of the flies' effect, where the single fit has about half ([the high per-claw knee without a dead zone](#claw-knee)), so these pairs stay a target of their own.

The other is the block. The pipeline's jitter had cut the block of the reference family's fits by more than half ([above](#other-targets)). Read again through the re-specified noise, the same fits keep most of their block, and the fit that lost most through the pipeline keeps most (table below). For these three fits the shared jitter with APL on lies below the lowest saved level and is interpolated from the run without noise; their re-fits to a larger block, whose levels lie between saved runs, read {{E81/mix_scores.csv:name=E48-thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_block0.072_k2_cap3_exact;readout=raw;unit=z;kind=mix:block ~ +.3f}} to {{E81/mix_scores.csv:name=E48-thr70_gain1.5_rate0.068_block0.072_k2_cap3_exact;readout=raw;unit=z;kind=mix:block ~ +.3f}}.

The two populations, whose block is smaller to begin with, keep it through the shared jitter alone and lose part of it to the independent noise. In every row of the table the model's block stays below the flies'.
