**What the model does not make.** Two features of the flies' variability are in the model under no noise that was tried. The first is the asymmetry between the conditions. In the flies the same-repeat gap is {{data:repeat_gap_ratio_tnt_ctrl ~ .1f}} times larger with APL output blocked (TNT). In the model, a jitter per KC gives a gap with APL off that is {{E81/shared_state.csv:model=C2;condition=both:gap_ratio_off_on ~ .2f}} times the gap with APL on for the breadth-2 fit and {{E81/shared_state.csv:model=F1;condition=both:gap_ratio_off_on ~ .2f}} times for the fit with the ceiling, and the re-specified noise reaches the flies' two gaps only by taking a larger jitter with APL off than with APL on.

A slow change of the whole population does not make the asymmetry either. A factor on every KC's threshold of 0.8, 1 and 1.2 in three successive trials, a wider swing than the flies' run-down amounts to (for the fit with the ceiling the control flies' run-down corresponds to a threshold that rises by a factor of {{E81/rundown_axes.csv:unit=z;experiment=E69_kc_firing_ceiling;tag=rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2;repeat=0:thr_change_first_to_last ~ .2f}} from the first repeat to the third), leaves a same-repeat gap of {{E81/shared_state.csv:model=C2;triplet=0.8/1/1.2;readout=raw;condition=on:gap ~ .3f}} with APL on and {{E81/shared_state.csv:model=C2;triplet=0.8/1/1.2;readout=raw;condition=acute_off:gap ~ .3f}} with APL off in the breadth-2 fit.

The second is how alike the responders of one repeat are with APL off. With every entry reduced to responding or not, the same-repeat gap with APL off is {{E81/mix_checks.csv:model=C2;readout=raw;unit=z;condition=acute_off:bin_gap ~ .3f}} for the breadth-2 fit and {{E81/mix_checks.csv:model=F1;readout=raw;unit=z;condition=acute_off:bin_gap ~ .3f}} for the fit with the ceiling through the re-specified noise, against the flies' {{data:repeat_gap_binary_tnt ~ .3f}}, and the same with the jitter per presentation ({{E81/per_presentation_checks.csv:model=C2;readout=raw;unit=z;condition=acute_off:bin_gap ~ .3f}} and {{E81/per_presentation_checks.csv:model=F1;readout=raw;unit=z;condition=acute_off:bin_gap ~ .3f}}); with APL on it is close to the flies' ({{E81/mix_checks.csv:model=C2;readout=raw;unit=z;condition=on:bin_gap ~ .3f}} against {{data:repeat_gap_binary_ctrl ~ .3f}}). The shortfall is thus a property of which KCs the model has responding with APL off and not of how the noise is drawn: the flies' larger shared variability with APL output blocked (TNT) has no counterpart in the model.

**Realism.** No model is changed or fitted here, so every model stands in the realism bands where it stood; the re-specified noise asks less of a KC than the pipeline does (a threshold that differs between repeats with a standard deviation of {{E81/mix_checks.csv:model=C2;readout=raw;unit=z;condition=on:sigma ~ .0%}} of its value with APL on and {{E81/mix_checks.csv:model=C2;readout=raw;unit=z;condition=acute_off:sigma ~ .0%}} with APL off for the breadth-2 fit, against {{E81/jitter_at_flies_gap.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;model=E67-rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3:sigma_matched_on ~ .0%}} in the pipeline), and the flies' APL-off / APL-on response-rate ratio is inside its band in each of the three repeats, the band's reference value being a mean over a session that the model does not have.

All model numbers here are of the model's 0.5 s odor pulse ([the flies' recording protocol in the model](#flies-protocol)), and the model's pairs with paa, euc and -aPine rest on [ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations), as everywhere; the six pairs with near-identical ORN input include none of those odors, and the flies' side of this subsection uses no ORN input.

**What follows.** Where this page gives a level of the KC data without the trial noise, it is now the estimate across repeats, and the earlier correction is named where a result was made with it (the re-fits to the corrected block and one reading of the table of readings). The main target stays the effect as measured, with its floor and its ceiling.

The pipeline stays the way a model is read as the data are made: its noise is all shared between the odors of a trial where only part of the flies' is, but with the flies' shares no population of wirings moved by as much as one draw of the wiring moves the loss, so the numbers read through it stand. The block is the statistic for which the make-up of the noise matters, and a block read through the pipeline is a block under more shared jitter than the flies' repeats support.

The six pairs with near-identical ORN input stay a target of their own, at a little under two thirds of the flies' effect once the noise is removed from both sides. The order in which the odors were presented changes none of this: it does not make the target, and it shows most of what the odors of a repeat share to be a slow drift over the session.

One thing is open. A trial noise for the model that is right where the present one is not needs a source of shared variability that is larger without APL, most of it such a drift, so a slow change in a subset of the KCs or in the input; the same-repeat gap of the responders with APL off is the statistic to hold it to. It is with the pending work at the end of the page.

### The time course of the APL effect in the flies' traces: when in a response the effect is made, how slow the indicator is, and whether the recordings were measured alike {#trace-time-course}

%%% hover
onset-burst kernel: The indicator's response to a single spike, a rise with one time constant times a decay with another, fitted to the mean trace of the control flies' responding KCs on the assumption that the KCs fire in a brief burst at the odor's onset. One of the two limits between which the KCs' firing lies, and the one that fits the traces better.
steady-drive kernel: The indicator's response to a single spike fitted to the same trace on the assumption that the KCs fire evenly through the 2 s odor pulse, the other limit. Its rise goes to the lower bound of the fit, the pulse itself making the rise of the trace.
late-over-early ratio: The mean signal from 4 s after the odor's onset to the end of the target's window, divided by the mean signal during the 2 s pulse, over all KC × odor entries; here that quotient with APL output blocked (TNT) relative to the control flies', and for a model with APL off relative to APL on. It is above 1 where the signal with APL output blocked grows after the pulse relative to the control flies'.
%%%

**The flies' APL effect is there from the first second of the odor and is largest then: it falls through the response and does not build up in the window that the target is taken from.** The error common to all wirings is in every window of the response as well, so the time within a response is closed as its source on the data's side, as the pulse and the window had closed it on the model's.

The indicator is slow, its signal still near its peak when the target's window ends, so that a model read as the flies were recorded reads, to within about two thousandths of the loss, what its plain spike counts at the flies' 2 s pulse read; for the family with the firing ceiling, the faster indicator that had been assumed made late firing cost about twice what it does.

With APL output blocked (TNT) the flies' signal does not grow after the pulse as the firing of the breadth-2 family with APL off would make it grow: the traces exclude that family's late firing under the kernel that fits them better, and not under the other, and they exclude no setting of the firing ceiling. And the two recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) that carry the largest APL effect were not measured like the other recordings in some respect: their responses decay about three times faster, and the stimulus record of one of them says that APL was not labelled.

Every value of the KC data on this page is one number per KC and trial, the mean of the KC's signal from 2 to 8 s after the onset of a 2 s odor pulse ([footnote](#fn-baseline-noise-units)). The time course of the APL effect in the flies' traces read the frame-by-frame traces behind those numbers, for the {{data:n_recordings_ctrl ~ .0f}} control recordings and the {{data:n_recordings_tnt ~ .0f}} with APL output blocked (TNT) that make the target, and put four questions to them, each with its outcomes set beforehand: when in a response the per-pair APL effect and the common error are made; how fast the indicator rises and decays in these recordings, which [the flies' recording protocol in the model](#flies-protocol) had to assume, and what the models read through it; whether the signal with APL output blocked grows after the pulse relative to the control flies', as that subsection predicted for a model that cannot hold its late firing; and whether the recordings were all measured alike.

No model was changed or fitted. Recomputed from the traces, the target's window gives back the per-trial values and the two matrices of the target, so that the other windows differ from the target in the window alone. Windows are compared without the trial noise, by the estimate across repeats ([the flies' variability across the three repeats](#repeat-structure)), because the share of the noise in a response changes through the response and differs between the genotypes: as measured, the mean effect among 1-8ol, 1-5ol, 1-6ol and 6al in the first second reads {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=z;estimator=measured;window=0 to 1 s;statistic=effect_alcohol:value ~ +.3f}}, and without the noise {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=0 to 1 s;statistic=effect_alcohol:value ~ +.3f}}. Intervals are 90 % intervals from resampling the recordings.

The KC data by window of the response (the recordings' z-scored unit, means over recordings; the windows follow the imaging volumes, so that the target's window ends 8.1 s after the odor's onset). **The effect is there from the first second, and it falls through the response.** Without the trial noise the mean APL effect over the 120 pairs is {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=pulse;statistic=effect_mean:value ~ +.3f}} over the 2 s pulse, {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=target;statistic=effect_mean:value ~ +.3f}} in the target's window and {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=4-8.1;statistic=effect_mean:value ~ +.3f}} in the second part of that window, from 4 s on (third row of the table for the windows one by one). The pulse exceeds the second part of the window by {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=pulse;statistic=effect_mean_minus_late:value ~ +.3f}} ({{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=pulse;statistic=effect_mean_minus_late:lo_rec ~ +.3f}} to {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=pulse;statistic=effect_mean_minus_late:hi_rec ~ +.3f}}; {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=pulse;statistic=effect_mean_minus_late:lo_fly ~ +.3f}} to {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=pulse;statistic=effect_mean_minus_late:hi_fly ~ +.3f}} when flies are resampled in place of recordings), and past the window the effect goes on falling.

What changes is the distances with APL output blocked: there the odors start more alike than they end, their mean distance rising through the window and past it, while the control flies' rises little after the third second (first row). The effect is thus not something that a slow signal gathers; it is in the first frames of the response. Its pattern across the pairs is the target's from the second second on and least so in the first (sixth row).

In baseline-noise units the fall from the pulse to the second part of the window is smaller ({{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=noise;estimator=noise_free;window=pulse;statistic=effect_mean_minus_late:value ~ +.3f}}, {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=noise;estimator=noise_free;window=pulse;statistic=effect_mean_minus_late:lo_rec ~ +.3f}} to {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=noise;estimator=noise_free;window=pulse;statistic=effect_mean_minus_late:hi_rec ~ +.3f}}). It is there in the six recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) that are alike and in the two strongest, each set against the control flies: {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=six_typical;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=pulse;statistic=effect_mean:value ~ +.3f}}, {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=six_typical;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=2-4;statistic=effect_mean:value ~ +.3f}} and {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=six_typical;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=4-8.1;statistic=effect_mean:value ~ +.3f}} over the pulse, from 2 to 4 s and from 4 to 8 s with the six, and {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=two_strongest;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=pulse;statistic=effect_mean:value ~ +.3f}}, {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=two_strongest;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=2-4;statistic=effect_mean:value ~ +.3f}} and {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=two_strongest;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=4-8.1;statistic=effect_mean:value ~ +.3f}} with the two, so that no window makes the two like the six.

For the main target the window is therefore a choice on the data's side that moves the mean part and not the pattern. As measured, the mean effect is {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=z;estimator=measured;window=pulse;statistic=effect_mean:value ~ +.3f}} over the pulse, {{data:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}} in the target's window and {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=z;estimator=measured;window=4-8.1;statistic=effect_mean:value ~ +.3f}} in its second part, so a model scored against the pulse would be asked for a larger mean effect still. The saved models keep their order: scored against the effect of the pulse and against that of the second part of the window, the losses of the {{E84/variants_by_window_summary.csv:estimator=measured;window=pulse:n_variants ~ .0f}} saved models have Spearman correlations of {{E84/variants_by_window_summary.csv:estimator=measured;window=pulse:rho_with_present ~ .3f}} and {{E84/variants_by_window_summary.csv:estimator=measured;window=4-8.1:rho_with_present ~ .3f}} with their losses against the target.

**The common error is in every window.** The per-pair APL effect of the mean over the eight wirings of the breadth-2 family, under the calibrated readout ([the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population)), was set against the flies' effect of each window, without the trial noise.

In every window the model's effect is too small among 2h, IaA, pa, eb, ep and ms and too large among 1-8ol, 1-5ol, 1-6ol and 6al (last row of the table): by {{E84/common_error_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=4-8.1;population=eight;readout=cal;statistic=ester_error:hi_rec ~ +.3f}}) and {{E84/common_error_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=4-8.1;population=eight;readout=cal;statistic=alcohol_error:value ~ +.3f}} ({{E84/common_error_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=4-8.1;population=eight;readout=cal;statistic=alcohol_error:lo_rec ~ +.3f}} to {{E84/common_error_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=4-8.1;population=eight;readout=cal;statistic=alcohol_error:hi_rec ~ +.3f}}) in the second part of the window. Nor do the flies' own two groups part ways between those two windows: from the second part of the window to the pulse, the effect of the second group changes by {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=pulse;statistic=alcohol_minus_ester_change_from_late:value ~ +.3f}} more than that of the first ({{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=pulse;statistic=alcohol_minus_ester_change_from_late:lo_rec ~ +.3f}} to {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=pulse;statistic=alcohol_minus_ester_change_from_late:hi_rec ~ +.3f}}).

Among the 1 s windows from the second second to the end of the target's window, the lowest pattern error is {{E84/common_error_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=3 to 4 s;population=eight;readout=cal;statistic=pattern_minus_target:value ~ +.3f}} from the target window's, in the fourth second; the first second, where the pattern is least the target's, is {{E84/common_error_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=0 to 1 s;population=eight;readout=cal;statistic=pattern_minus_target:value ~ +.3f}} above it. This is the outcome that had been set as closing the question: the common error is not made by when in a response the flies' signal is read. The pulse and the window had closed it on the model's side ([the flies' recording protocol in the model](#flies-protocol)) and the repeats on the data's ([the flies' variability across the three repeats](#repeat-structure)), so time is closed as its source on both sides.

What is left of it is in the model's structure as it is fitted, the input, the wiring and APL's profile over the glomeruli, which have since been searched on several wirings at once: neither the fitted input nor the fitted profile passes its test, and one searched input, reduced, holds there ([the input and APL's glomerulus profile fitted on several wirings at once](#cross-wiring-fit), the next subsection), carrying a small part of the error that its controls confirm and that a second split of the flies does not repeat ([the controls and the replication of the reduced searched input](#reduced-input), the subsection after it).

Left: the mean trace of the responding KC × odor entries, chosen on two repeats and averaged on the third, each curve divided by its peak. Right: the mean over all KC × odor entries, each curve divided by its mean over the pulse. In both panels: the control flies, all eight recordings with APL output blocked (TNT), the six of them that are alike and the two with the largest APL effect (n: the number of entries).](results/E84_trace_time_course/E84_traces.png)

**The indicator is slow.** The mean trace of the responding KC × odor entries, chosen on two repeats and averaged on the third, peaks {{E84/kinetics_relations.csv:selection=resp;measure=peak_t:others_min ~ .1f}} to {{E84/kinetics_relations.csv:selection=resp;measure=peak_t:others_max ~ .1f}} s after the odor's onset in every recording but the two taken up below, more than a second after the pulse has ended, and when the target's window ends it is still at {{E84/kinetics_relations.csv:selection=resp;measure=v8.1_over_peak:others_min ~ .2f}} to {{E84/kinetics_relations.csv:selection=resp;measure=v8.1_over_peak:others_max ~ .2f}} of its peak (figure, left; table below).

A kernel for the indicator's response to a single spike, a rise with one time constant times a decay with another, was fitted to the control flies' trace under two limits of the firing, between which the KCs' firing lies. If the KCs fire in a burst at the odor's onset, the rise is {{E84/kernel_fits.csv:level=subset;subset=control flies;selection=resp;fit=free;drive=onset:rise ~ .2f}} s and the decay {{E84/kernel_fits.csv:level=subset;subset=control flies;selection=resp;fit=free;drive=onset:decay ~ .1f}} s (the onset-burst kernel). If they fire evenly through the pulse, the decay is {{E84/kernel_fits.csv:level=subset;subset=control flies;selection=resp;fit=free;drive=steady:decay ~ .1f}} s and the rise goes to the lower bound of the fit, the pulse making the rise of the trace (the steady-drive kernel).

The first fits better, with a root mean square misfit of {{E84/kernel_fits.csv:level=subset;subset=control flies;selection=resp;fit=free;drive=onset:rms ~ .3f}} against {{E84/kernel_fits.csv:level=subset;subset=control flies;selection=resp;fit=free;drive=steady:rms ~ .3f}} of a KC's baseline noise, and on synthetic traces with the recordings' volume rate and noise the fit tells firing that lasts 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1 or 2 s apart in every draw. But the fitted rise shortens as the firing is taken to last longer, so that what the traces leave open is the form of the kernel between the two limits, and both are carried below. Either way the decay is several times the 3 s that the reading of the models as the flies were recorded had assumed, and four times the slowest that it read beside it.

The control flies' responses also shorten as they run down over the session ([the flies' variability across the three repeats](#repeat-structure)): from the first repeat to the third the peak of their responders' trace falls from {{E84/kinetics_relations.csv:selection=resp;measure=by_repeat;genotype=TNT3c;repeat=1.0:peak_mean ~ .2f}} to {{E84/kinetics_relations.csv:selection=resp;measure=by_repeat;genotype=TNT3c;repeat=3.0:peak_mean ~ .2f}} times the baseline noise, and its mean signal from 4 to 8 s over its mean signal during the pulse from {{E84/kinetics_relations.csv:selection=resp;measure=by_repeat;genotype=TNT3c;repeat=1.0:late_over_early_mean ~ .2f}} to {{E84/kinetics_relations.csv:selection=resp;measure=by_repeat;genotype=TNT3c;repeat=3.0:late_over_early_mean ~ .2f}}.

**Through the measured kinetics, a model at the flies' protocol reads what its spike counts read.** With a decay that slow, a spike anywhere in the 2 s pulse leaves nearly the same share of its signal in the window from 2 to 8 s, so that the window weighs the spikes of the pulse about alike. The saved runs of the flies' recording protocol in the model were read again through both measured kernels, after the assumed kernel had given back that subsection's own numbers exactly.

In every row of the table below the two measured readings are within {{diff:E84/protocol_populations_measured_kernel.csv:population=b2;pulse=2.0;kernel=r0.05_d21.9:raw_loss -- E82/protocol_populations.csv:population=b2;pulse=2.0;kernel=counts:raw_loss ~ .3f}} of the loss with every spike counted alike, where the assumed indicator had put the loss {{diff:E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;kernel=r0.5_d3:raw_loss -- E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;kernel=counts:raw_loss ~ .3f}} above it for the fit with the firing ceiling at its 1 s adaptation and {{diff:E82/protocol_populations.csv:population=b2;pulse=2.0;kernel=r0.5_d3:raw_loss -- E82/protocol_populations.csv:population=b2;pulse=2.0;kernel=counts:raw_loss ~ .3f}} above it for the family without a ceiling. The reading of a model as the flies were recorded is thus, to that precision, its raw spike counts at the flies' 2 s pulse, and for the family with the ceiling the earlier reading overstated what late firing costs by about a factor of two.

The fit with the ceiling at its stronger setting and its 1 s adaptation stands at {{E84/protocol_readings_measured_kernel.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;kernel=r1.29_d20.7:raw_loss ~ .3f}} and {{E84/protocol_readings_measured_kernel.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;kernel=r0.05_d21.9:raw_loss ~ .3f}} at the flies' protocol, not at {{E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;kernel=r0.5_d3:raw_loss ~ .3f}}. That is {{diff:E84/protocol_readings_measured_kernel.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;kernel=r1.29_d20.7:raw_loss -- E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse0.5_fixed;kernel=counts:raw_loss ~ .3f}} to {{diff:E84/protocol_readings_measured_kernel.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;kernel=r0.05_d21.9:raw_loss -- E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse0.5_fixed;kernel=counts:raw_loss ~ .3f}} above its loss at the 0.5 s pulse in place of {{diff:E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;kernel=r0.5_d3:raw_loss -- E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse0.5_fixed;kernel=counts:raw_loss ~ .3f}}, about a fifth of the loss in place of two fifths, and a little more than one draw of the wiring moves the loss on raw counts ({{E72/spread.csv:readout=raw:sd_single ~ .3f}}) where it had been more than twice that.

The mean over four wirings at the literature setting rises by {{diff:E84/protocol_populations_measured_kernel.csv:population=fc;pulse=2.0;kernel=r1.29_d20.7:raw_loss -- E82/protocol_populations.csv:population=fc;pulse=0.5;kernel=counts:raw_loss ~ .3f}} to {{diff:E84/protocol_populations_measured_kernel.csv:population=fc;pulse=2.0;kernel=r0.05_d21.9:raw_loss -- E82/protocol_populations.csv:population=fc;pulse=0.5;kernel=counts:raw_loss ~ .3f}} in place of {{diff:E82/protocol_populations.csv:population=fc;pulse=2.0;kernel=r0.5_d3:raw_loss -- E82/protocol_populations.csv:population=fc;pulse=0.5;kernel=counts:raw_loss ~ .3f}}. With the adaptation at 3 s no spike comes late, and those rows read the same through every kernel. The family without a ceiling loses most of its match on raw counts at the flies' pulse with or without the kinetics.

One verdict on the settings that were tried with the 1 s adaptation changes. With APL's time constant at 0.01 s in place of 0.05 s, the fit with the ceiling reads {{E84/gate_measured_kernel.csv:measured_kernel=measured_onset;point_id=B5_fit0_taum0.01:raw_loss_primary ~ .4f}} and {{E84/gate_measured_kernel.csv:measured_kernel=measured_steady;point_id=B5_fit0_taum0.01:raw_loss_primary ~ .4f}} through the two measured kernels, under the limit of {{E82/gate.csv:point_id=B2_fit0_tau3:pg_limit ~ .4f}} that had been set beforehand; through the assumed kernel it had read {{E82/gate.csv:point_id=B5_fit0_taum0.01:raw_loss_primary ~ .4f}} and failed. Every other verdict stands, and no setting passes the test of [the input side of the error common to all wirings](#input-side) under any reading.

**With APL output blocked, the flies' signal does not grow after the pulse as the breadth-2 family's would.** The flies' recording protocol in the model had left a prediction for the traces: where nothing bounds the firing with APL off, the signal with APL off grows after the pulse relative to the signal with APL on, and where an adaptation holds the firing to the odor's onset it stays level.

The test set beforehand was the late-over-early ratio: the mean signal from 4 to 8 s over the mean signal during the pulse, with APL output blocked (TNT) relative to the control flies, over all KC × odor entries. For the models, the spikes with APL off and with APL on were passed through each measured kernel and the same ratio was taken. In the flies it is {{E84/trace_ratio_tests.csv:kind=flies;subset=APL output blocked (TNT), all eight;selection=all;ratio=4-8.1 over 0-2:value ~ .2f}} ({{E84/trace_ratio_tests.csv:kind=flies;subset=APL output blocked (TNT), all eight;selection=all;ratio=4-8.1 over 0-2:lo ~ .2f}} to {{E84/trace_ratio_tests.csv:kind=flies;subset=APL output blocked (TNT), all eight;selection=all;ratio=4-8.1 over 0-2:hi ~ .2f}}) with all eight recordings and {{E84/trace_ratio_tests.csv:kind=flies;subset=APL output blocked (TNT), the six typical;selection=all;ratio=4-8.1 over 0-2:value ~ .2f}} ({{E84/trace_ratio_tests.csv:kind=flies;subset=APL output blocked (TNT), the six typical;selection=all;ratio=4-8.1 over 0-2:lo ~ .2f}} to {{E84/trace_ratio_tests.csv:kind=flies;subset=APL output blocked (TNT), the six typical;selection=all;ratio=4-8.1 over 0-2:hi ~ .2f}}) with the six that are alike (table below).

Under the onset-burst kernel the breadth-2 family without a ceiling lies above both intervals on three of its four wirings and in its fit made at the flies' pulse, with the fourth wiring inside the upper end of the six's interval. Under the steady-drive kernel the same three wirings and that fit lie above the interval of all eight and inside that of the six. With the firing ceiling and an adaptation of 1 s or longer, every fit is inside the interval of all eight and just below that of the six.

On the traces alone, then, the flies' KCs do not go on firing through the odor with APL output blocked as the family without a bound has them fire, under the kernel that fits the traces better; under the other the test does not decide. That is evidence for some bound on the late firing with APL off, and the traces do not say which bound: they do not tell a 1 s adaptation from a 3 s one.

What growth the flies show is not in the responding entries, whose ratio is below one ({{E84/trace_ratio_tests.csv:kind=flies;subset=APL output blocked (TNT), the six typical;selection=resp;ratio=4-8.1 over 0-2:value ~ .2f}} with the six, {{E84/trace_ratio_tests.csv:kind=flies;subset=APL output blocked (TNT), the six typical;selection=resp;ratio=4-8.1 over 0-2:lo ~ .2f}} to {{E84/trace_ratio_tests.csv:kind=flies;subset=APL output blocked (TNT), the six typical;selection=resp;ratio=4-8.1 over 0-2:hi ~ .2f}}; {{E84/trace_ratio_tests.csv:kind=flies;subset=APL output blocked (TNT), all eight;selection=resp;ratio=4-8.1 over 0-2:value ~ .2f}} with all eight). It is in the entries below the response criterion, whose signal with APL output blocked rises slowly through the window and in the control flies stays near zero. The neuropil does not make it: with 0.5 or 0.9 of the surrounding neuropil's signal subtracted in place of 0.7, the ratio with the six is {{E84/neuropil_by_window.csv:neucoeff=0.5;window=signal 4-8.1 over 0-2;selection=all;tnt_subset=the six typical:tnt_over_ctrl ~ .2f}} and {{E84/neuropil_by_window.csv:neucoeff=0.9;window=signal 4-8.1 over 0-2;selection=all;tnt_subset=the six typical:tnt_over_ctrl ~ .2f}} for {{E84/neuropil_by_window.csv:neucoeff=0.7;window=signal 4-8.1 over 0-2;selection=all;tnt_subset=the six typical:tnt_over_ctrl ~ .2f}}.

**The two strongest recordings were not measured like the others.** The two recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) whose distances stand apart from the other six ([the data side of the main target](#data-side)), those of 2024-07-17 (fly 3) and of 2024-07-25 (fly 1), also stand apart in time. Their responders' traces peak about a second earlier and decay about three times faster than those of every other recording, with time constants of {{E84/kinetics_relations.csv:selection=resp;measure=decay_tau_from_8.1:strong_2024-07-17_fly_3_L ~ .1f}} and {{E84/kinetics_relations.csv:selection=resp;measure=decay_tau_from_8.1:strong_2024-07-25_fly_1_L ~ .1f}} s after the window where the others have {{E84/kinetics_relations.csv:selection=resp;measure=decay_tau_from_8.1:others_min ~ .1f}} to {{E84/kinetics_relations.csv:selection=resp;measure=decay_tau_from_8.1:others_max ~ .1f}} s (table of the traces' shape above; figure, left).

On seven of the eight measures of the trace's shape both lie outside the range of all the other recordings, the control flies' included, and on the eighth, the time to half the peak, one of them does. They stay outside when the responses compared are matched in amplitude, and no measure follows how bright a recording is or how noisy its baseline.

In the pattern of their distances the two had been found stronger and not different; in the time course of their responses they are different, in a way that the size of a response does not explain. Something in how these two were prepared or imaged differs from the rest, and the recordings' own records name one thing, for one of them: the stimulus record of the recording of 2024-07-17 says that APL was not labelled, which no other recording of the dataset with APL output blocked (TNT) says.

Among the control flies, flies that carry the active toxin and have no label in APL are controls ({{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=ctrl_TNT-nolabel_recorded;units=z;estimator=measured;window=target;statistic=effect_mean:n_ctrl ~ .0f}} of the {{data:n_recordings_ctrl ~ .0f}} control recordings are of that kind); by its record this recording is of that kind, and by its distances it is one of the two with the largest APL effect. Without it the mean APL effect of the target is {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=tnt_without_unlabeled;units=z;estimator=measured;window=target;statistic=effect_mean:value ~ +.3f}} as measured and {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=tnt_without_unlabeled;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=target;statistic=effect_mean:value ~ +.3f}} without the trial noise, where all eight give {{data:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}} and {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=target;statistic=effect_mean:value ~ +.3f}}; without both it is the six's, {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=six_typical;units=z;estimator=measured;window=target;statistic=effect_mean:value ~ +.3f}}.

The readings above rest little on the two: the kernels are fitted to the control flies, the effect falls through the response with the six as with all eight, and the late-over-early ratio is given with all eight and with the six. What was different about the two recordings, and whether APL was labelled in the first, are questions for the experimenter.

**Realism.** No model is changed or fitted here, so every model stands in the realism bands where it stood, and the readings through the measured kernels are of runs whose response rates were held. On the data's side the APL-off / APL-on response-rate ratio, with the flies' trial means counted by the bands' criterion in each window, is {{E84/rates_by_window.csv:subset=all;criterion=trialmean_fixed;window=pulse:ratio ~ .2f}} over the pulse, {{E84/rates_by_window.csv:subset=all;criterion=trialmean_fixed;window=2-4:ratio ~ .2f}} from 2 to 4 s, {{E84/rates_by_window.csv:subset=all;criterion=trialmean_fixed;window=4-8.1:ratio ~ .2f}} from 4 to 8 s and {{E84/rates_by_window.csv:subset=all;criterion=trialmean_fixed;window=target:ratio ~ .2f}} in the target's window, inside its band (1.6 to 2.9) throughout; outside the target's window the criterion is an approximation, the solvent having responders of its own.

What the experiment adds to realism is two measurements for the question that the flies' recording protocol in the model had raised, what holds the response with APL off to the odor's onset: the flies' own late-over-early ratio, which is lower than that of a model with no bound on its late firing, and the indicator's kinetics, which halve what the ceiling's 1 s adaptation costs at the flies' protocol.

Two checks bear on the flies' side. The tail of one presentation's response is still there when the next presentation starts. A model of that tail puts the largest bias it adds to a pair's APL effect at {{E84/carry_over_summary.csv:estimator=measured:max_abs_bias ~ .3f}}, and at {{E84/carry_over_summary.csv:estimator=measured:max_abs_bias_cal ~ .3f}} once the tail is calibrated on entries that are silent in their other repeats; it is a caveat and not a correction.

And the share of the neuropil's signal that is subtracted moves the levels and not the readings: the fall of the mean effect from the pulse to the second part of the window is {{diff:E84/neuropil_by_window.csv:neucoeff=0.5;window=pulse;estimator=noise_free:effect_mean -- E84/neuropil_by_window.csv:neucoeff=0.5;window=4-8.1;estimator=noise_free:effect_mean ~ +.3f}} and {{diff:E84/neuropil_by_window.csv:neucoeff=0.9;window=pulse;estimator=noise_free:effect_mean -- E84/neuropil_by_window.csv:neucoeff=0.9;window=4-8.1;estimator=noise_free:effect_mean ~ +.3f}} with 0.5 and 0.9 subtracted, for {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=pulse;statistic=effect_mean_minus_late:value ~ +.3f}} with 0.7. As everywhere, the model rows rest on [ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations) for the pairs with paa, euc and -aPine; the flies' side of this subsection uses no ORN input.

**What follows.** On the data's side the target's window stands. The pattern of the effect across the pairs is the same from the second second of the odor on, and what the window moves is the mean, by {{diff:E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=z;estimator=measured;window=pulse;statistic=effect_mean:value -- data:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}} if the pulse is taken and by {{diff:E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=z;estimator=measured;window=4-8.1;statistic=effect_mean:value -- data:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}} if the second part of the window is: a choice of the target beside the unit of the responses and the noise correction, and smaller than what the sample of flies leaves open.

The common error is closed in time on both sides. On the model's side, the reading of a model as the flies were recorded is its plain spike counts at the flies' 2 s pulse, so the choice of the reading that had been left open ([the flies' recording protocol in the model](#flies-protocol)) is between those counts and the calibrated readout.

The case for a firing ceiling whose adaptation outlasts the odor is weaker than it was: the 1 s adaptation raises the loss by {{diff:E84/protocol_readings_measured_kernel.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;kernel=r1.29_d20.7:raw_loss -- E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse0.5_fixed;kernel=counts:raw_loss ~ .3f}} to {{diff:E84/protocol_readings_measured_kernel.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;kernel=r0.05_d21.9:raw_loss -- E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse0.5_fixed;kernel=counts:raw_loss ~ .3f}} at the flies' protocol, a little more than one draw of the wiring moves it, and the 3 s adaptation by next to nothing, while the flies' traces ask only that the late firing with APL off be bounded, which the breadth-2 family without a ceiling does not do. Whether the ceiling joins the base model, with which adaptation, and which reading carries the model's side of the main target remain choices to be made.

The questions that came out of the recordings are for the experimenter: what was different about the two strongest recordings with APL output blocked (TNT), in the cross, the indicator, the age of the flies, the preparation or the imaging, and whether APL was labelled in the one whose record says that it was not. With the answer it is to be decided whether the target stays the mean over all eight recordings; until then every result that depends on it is given against all eight and against the six that are alike, as it is here.

The recordings of the panel that the target does not use were not read. They wait on the experimenter's check of their quality, and the reading of the traces and the measures of a response's time course are ready for them. What is taken up from here is with the pending work at the end of the page.

### The input and APL's glomerulus profile fitted on several wirings at once: whether either change holds on wirings and recordings it was not fitted to {#cross-wiring-fit}

**Searched on four wirings and one half of the recordings at once, neither a profile of APL's weight over the glomeruli nor an input changed glomerulus by glomerulus for each odor passes the test set for it on four other wirings and the other half of the recordings.** The profile carries a small part of its gain there, with a higher loss on raw counts and a smaller mean effect. The input search fits the half of the recordings it was run against, on wirings it never saw as well, and gains nothing against the other half.

One change does hold on both, by a little more than the test asks: the input that had been searched on the real wiring alone, reduced to 0.6 of its size. It was read here without its control. The control and a replication of its search have been run since: the controls hold, and the input carries a part of the common error that is smaller than the test asks ([the controls and the replication of the reduced searched input](#reduced-input), the next subsection).

[The glomerulus profile of APL inhibition](#glomerulus-profile) and [the input side of the error common to all wirings](#input-side) had each found, on the real wiring, a change that lowers the pattern part of the APL-effect loss there, and neither change had been shown to hold beyond that wiring. Both kinds were therefore searched in simulation on four wirings at once (the real one, two claw permutations and one matched shuffle), for the lowest pattern part of the mean over the four against one half of the recordings, once against each half: the 36 scores of a glomerulus profile at the cell site (a KC's APL weight multiplied once for each claw it has from a glomerulus), and, one odor after the other for the ten odors of the earlier search, a factor between one half and two on each glomerulus's ORN response.

Every wiring is at its own breadth-2 APL-effect fit ([above](#wiring-population)), the halves are those of the earlier search, split by fly with the two strongest recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) apart, and at every reading both response rates were set again. The test was fixed before any run. It is read on the mean over the four other wirings (two claw permutations and two matched shuffles), with each change at 0.6 of its size (its scores, or the logarithms of its factors, multiplied by 0.6), the share of one half's pattern that the other half reproduces.

Through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout), the pattern part against the half that a search had not seen had to fall by 0.003 or more for both halves' changes, and on six or more of the eight single wirings and halves; the loss on raw counts could rise by no more than 0.005, with the mean effect within 0.01 of the flies' and every point inside the realism bands; and the squared pattern error against all recordings had to fall by 15 % in the mean of the two halves' changes, and by half that against the six recordings that are alike.

A change that got that far was to be set against the same scores or factors permuted across the glomeruli. Before the searches, the changes that existed were read where they had never been run: the profiles of the earlier experiment on the seven re-drawn wirings, and the two inputs searched on the real wiring on the four held-out wirings, whole and at 0.6 of their size.

| mean APL effect (the test allows 0.01 either side of the flies') | {{data:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}} | {{E83/readings.csv:change=none;unit=T;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} | {{E83/readings.csv:change=DP_halfA_s0.6;unit=T;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} / {{E83/readings.csv:change=DP_halfB_s0.6;unit=T;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} | {{E83/readings.csv:change=DI_halfA_s0.6;unit=T;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} / {{E83/readings.csv:change=DI_halfB_s0.6;unit=T;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} | {{E83/readings.csv:change=A2_halfA_s0.6;unit=T;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} / {{E83/readings.csv:change=A2_halfB_s0.6;unit=T;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} |

**The input search fits its half of the recordings.** Against the half it was run against, the input searched on four wirings lowers the pattern part on the four held-out wirings too, by {{E83/two_by_two_DI.csv:searched_on=A;size=0.6;unit=T;against=searched:gain ~ .4f}} and {{E83/two_by_two_DI.csv:searched_on=B;size=0.6;unit=T;against=searched:gain ~ .4f}} for the two halves' inputs (fourth row), so what the search finds is not particular to the wirings it was run on. Against the half it did not see it gains nothing (first two rows), with {{E83/gate_DI.csv:searched_on=both:n_singles_lower ~ .0f}} of the eight single wirings and halves lower. Nor do the two halves ask for the same input: for each of the ten odors the correlation over the 36 glomeruli between the two halves' factors, on a log scale, lies between {{E83/agreement_I.csv:what=log factors over all glomeruli;odor=IaA:value ~ .2f}} and {{E83/agreement_I.csv:what=log factors over all glomeruli;odor=1-6ol:value ~ .2f}}, and what the two inputs do to the per-pair APL effect of the held-out wirings correlates at {{E83/agreement_I.csv:what=T's per-pair change of the APL effect, half A's change against half B's:value ~ .2f}} over the 120 pairs.

A search with a factor for every glomerulus of every odor thus fits what differs between the two halves of the recordings. With the {{data:n_recordings_tnt ~ .0f}} recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) split in two, the halves differ from each other about as much as the model differs from either, so it is the recordings and not the wirings that bound what a fitted input can be shown to carry.

**The profile carries a little, and costs more.** The profile searched on four wirings lowers the held-out wirings' pattern part against the half it did not see by {{E83/two_by_two_DP.csv:searched_on=A;size=0.6;unit=T;against=unseen:gain ~ .4f}} and {{E83/two_by_two_DP.csv:searched_on=B;size=0.6;unit=T;against=unseen:gain ~ .4f}}, a little over half of what the test asks, with {{E83/gate_DP.csv:searched_on=both:n_singles_lower ~ .0f}} of the eight single wirings and halves lower. It pays elsewhere: the loss on raw counts rises by {{E83/gate_DP.csv:searched_on=A:raw_loss_change ~ .4f}} and {{E83/gate_DP.csv:searched_on=B:raw_loss_change ~ .4f}}, the mean effect through the readout falls below the flies', and against the six recordings that are alike the pattern part does not fall (last three rows).

A second split of the flies had been kept for a verdict that hung on the gain against the unseen half alone, and with these other parts failed it was not run. The two halves' profiles agree in what they do and not in how they do it: their changes of the per-pair APL effect on the held-out wirings correlate at {{E83/agreement_P.csv:what=T's per-pair change of the APL effect, half A's change against half B's:value ~ .2f}}, their scores over the 36 glomeruli at {{E83/agreement_P.csv:what=scores over glomeruli:value ~ .2f}}, so many profiles move the same pairs and the glomeruli are not identified.

The earlier profile, built from single-glomerulus changes on the real wiring ([above](#glomerulus-profile)), does about as much where it had never been run: at half its scores it lowers the pattern part of the mean over the seven re-drawn wirings by {{E83/existing_changes.csv:change=A1_ridge_x0.5;unit=draws7:z8_gain ~ .4f}} against all recordings, on {{lit:six # results/E83_cross_wiring_fit/outcome_A.json, a1.n_draws_lower: 6 of the 7 re-drawn wirings have a lower pattern part}} of the seven, where the same scores permuted across the glomeruli raise it by {{diff:E83/existing_changes.csv:change=A1_ridge_perm1_x0.5;unit=draws7:z8_changed -- E83/existing_changes.csv:change=A1_ridge_perm1_x0.5;unit=draws7:z8_unchanged ~ .4f}}. A profile of APL's weight over the glomeruli thus removes a part of the common error that is real, on wirings and recordings it was not fitted to, and small.

**The input searched on the real wiring alone holds on both once it is reduced.** Whole, the two inputs of the earlier search gain {{E83/two_by_two_A2.csv:searched_on=A;size=1.0;unit=T;against=unseen:gain ~ .4f}} and {{E83/two_by_two_A2.csv:searched_on=B;size=1.0;unit=T;against=unseen:gain ~ .4f}} on the held-out wirings' pattern part against the half they did not see (the unchanged fits minus the change): nothing, as that experiment had found on the re-drawn wirings it read ([above](#input-side)). At 0.6 of their size they lower it by {{E83/two_by_two_A2.csv:searched_on=A;size=0.6;unit=T;against=unseen:gain ~ .4f}} and {{E83/two_by_two_A2.csv:searched_on=B;size=0.6;unit=T;against=unseen:gain ~ .4f}} (last column), on as many of the single wirings and halves as the test asks, with a loss on raw counts below the unchanged fits', the flies' mean effect, and more of the squared pattern error removed than the test asks, against all recordings and against the six that are alike.

The search had overshot: its input points the way that wirings and recordings it never saw ask, and goes too far. Read with the test's thresholds, the reduced input meets every part that was read. It was not one of the two changes that the test was set for, so the control with its factors permuted was not run on it here, and with two inputs chance was not excluded. Both have been taken up since: the controls hold, a second draw of the search carries as much, and a search on a second split of the flies does not ([the controls and the replication of the reduced searched input](#reduced-input), the next subsection).

Nor is it understood why a search on one wiring gives an input that holds when reduced and the same search on four wirings does not, the two having taken the half they were run against about equally far; only 0.6 and the whole were read, and 0.6, fixed beforehand, may be too large for the inputs searched on four wirings. What the reduced input removes is small beside what is left: against all recordings, one half of which each input has seen, the held-out wirings' pattern part falls from {{E83/readings.csv:change=none;unit=T;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .3f}} to {{E83/two_by_two_A2.csv:searched_on=A;size=0.6;unit=T;against=all:changed ~ .3f}} and {{E83/two_by_two_A2.csv:searched_on=B;size=0.6;unit=T;against=all:changed ~ .3f}}, where the floor is {{E66/data_floor_parts.csv:data=graded;stat=apl_effect_rmse_centered:mean ~ .3f}}.

**Realism.** Every point read here, on every wiring, is inside all four realism bands, with the flies' responses counted in baseline-noise units as the bands count now. Both response rates are held by construction, and the response rate ρ with APL on and the number of odors per KC, which a change can move, stay well inside their bands. Counted by the recordings' own criterion, as the bands counted until 2026-11-10, one point is just outside the band on the number of odors per KC with APL off, the second half's input searched on four wirings, on one matched shuffle ({{E83/runs.csv:DI_halfB_s0.6_M3:opk_off_tv_zcrit ~ .3f}} against {{data:tnt_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .3f}}); no reading above rests on it.

What the bands do not see is the family's own, and what the changes add to it. The reduced inputs raise the largest spike count with APL off, on the wiring where it is largest from {{E83/runs.csv:DP_halfA_s0.6_P3:max_count_off ~ .0f}} to {{E83/runs.csv:A2_halfA_s0.6_P3:max_count_off ~ .0f}} and {{E83/runs.csv:A2_halfB_s0.6_P3:max_count_off ~ .0f}} spikes per KC and odor, in a family that nothing bounds there ([the firing ceiling for the KCs](#firing-ceiling)). The profile needs an APL scale of up to {{E83/runs.csv:DP_halfB_s0.6_M1:apl_factor ~ .2f}} times the fit's at 0.6 of its scores. And the searched inputs are [oracle](#fn-oracle) inputs, each glomerulus's response between half and twice the recorded one, which no measurement supports and on which the two halves of the recordings do not agree.

As everywhere, the pairs with paa, euc and -aPine rest on [ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations); none of the three is among the ten odors searched. No gain here was bought with the bands; what the profile's gain costs is on raw counts and in the mean effect.

**What follows.** Fitted changes at the level of the glomeruli, of APL's weight or of the input, are closed as carriers of the common error as a whole: what holds on wirings and recordings that a change was not fitted to is a few thousandths of a pattern part of {{E72/population.csv:group=all:cal_pattern ~ .3f}} whose floor is {{E66/data_floor_parts.csv:data=graded;stat=apl_effect_rmse_centered:mean ~ .3f}}, less than one draw of the wiring moves the loss ({{E72/spread.csv:readout=cal:sd_single ~ .3f}}). The mean effect, which the family has at the flies' under the readout, is kept by the inputs and lowered a little by the profile.

Two things were left open. The reduced input was a candidate for a part of the error, and the control with its factors permuted was to decide whether it was more than chance. The control and a replication of the search have been run since ([the controls and the replication of the reduced searched input](#reduced-input), the next subsection): the controls hold, a second draw of the search carries as much, a search on a second split of the flies does not, and over the two splits the input gains {{E86/gate.csv:change=gate:g ~ .4f}} where this test asks 0.003, so that it carries a part of the error and does not pass.

The readings kept for an input that passes, in the family with the firing ceiling, at the flies' pulse and through the trial noise, were therefore not made. Its factors have been set against the fly-to-fly range of the ORN recordings: at 0.6 of its size the input changes a glomerulus's response by no more than flies differ from one another, in a direction not shown to be the flies' ([the ORN input as a population of flies](#input-population)). Hallem's receptor data neither support nor contradict it, and the few changes that six runs of the search share are named as a list that a measurement could test (the next subsection).

And the input search shows what limits any fitted pattern: with the recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) split in two, a flexible fit follows the split, so that more recordings would raise what a fit can be shown to carry. The profile is left as a description by the pairs it moves and not by its glomeruli, its comparison with the connectomes' APL synapses still to be made. What is taken up from here is with the pending work at the end of the page.

### The controls and the replication of the reduced searched input: whether the one change that held on wirings and recordings it was not fitted to carries a part of the error common to the wirings, and what that input is {#reduced-input}

**The reduced searched input carries a small part of the error common to all wirings, about half of what the test set for it asks, and at no cost elsewhere.** Its controls hold: on four wirings and the half of the recordings that its search never saw, the same factors permuted across each odor's glomeruli gain nothing on average and the factors inverted lose, so the gain depends on which glomerulus is given which factor.

A second draw of the search against the same halves of the recordings carries as much as the first, so the input was not the lucky draw of a short search. A search on a second split of the flies does not: one of its two inputs gains and the other loses. What a fitted input can be shown to carry thus depends on how the recordings are split, and it is the recordings, not the wirings or the search, that set the limit.

What the input is has been read from the six inputs that the search has now given. They move the same odor pairs, the way the recordings ask, and hardly agree on the glomeruli.

A few changes of a single glomerulus's response do recur in all six, more of them than chance gives, and are named as a list that a measurement could test, VM7d's response to eb, DM5's to 1-8ol and DM4's to ep lowered, DM1's to IaA raised and DP1m's lowered for ms, 6al and 2h first among them. Each is about as large as the difference between two ORN flies, and no data on hand show it to be what reaches the KCs of the recorded flies.

[The input and APL's glomerulus profile fitted on several wirings at once](#cross-wiring-fit) left one change that held where it had not been fitted: the input searched on the real wiring alone ([the input side of the error common to all wirings](#input-side)), at 0.6 of its size. It had been read without the control that the test keeps for a change that gets that far, and it was the better pair of four fitted inputs.

Everything here is read as there: the mean over the four held-out wirings, each at its own breadth-2 APL-effect fit, every input at 0.6 of its size with both response rates set again, through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout). An input's gain is the pattern part of the APL-effect loss of the unchanged fits minus that with the input, against the half of the recordings that its search did not see.

The input has two controls: each odor's factors permuted across its 36 glomeruli (four permutations of each half's input), and the factors inverted, each glomerulus's response divided where the search had multiplied it. And the search was run again on the real wiring: a second draw of its random steps against the same two halves, and once against each half of a second split of the flies, which keeps the two strongest recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) apart as the first does and has {{lit:four # recording_halves(0) against recording_halves(1) in experiments/E77_input_side_common_error.py: the second split's first half holds 8 of the 11 recordings of the first split's second half and 1 of the 8 of its first half, and its second half 7 of those 8 and 3 of the 11, so 4 of the 19 recordings (2 of control flies, 2 with APL output blocked) are on the other side}} of the recordings on the other side.

What would count was fixed before any run. The controls hold if no permuted input gains as much as the input, the first two of the four less than half of it and the four less than a quarter of it on average, and if the inverted input gains nothing.

The input passes if, in addition, the earlier test holds on the mean over the two splits (a gain of 0.003, 12 of the 16 single wirings and halves lower, and its limits on the loss on raw counts, the mean effect, the realism bands and the squared pattern error) and the four new inputs gain 0.002 on average with at least three gaining. It carries a part, short of a pass, if they gain 0.001 on average with at least three gaining, and it falls otherwise.

If the input passed or carried a part, what it is was to be read from the six inputs that the search had then given on the real wiring, two draws against each half of the first split and one against each half of the second: each on the seven re-drawn wirings, on none of which a search was run; their agreement with one another, in the pairs they move and in their factors; where the new ones lie in the spread between the ORN flies and against Hallem's receptor data, as the earlier ones had been set ([the ORN input as a population of flies](#input-population)); and the entries that recur.

An entry is one glomerulus's response to one odor, 360 of them for the ten odors searched. Those that at least five of the six inputs change in the same direction, and in the mean of the six by more than half of what the search allows on a log scale, were to be named as a list that a measurement could test if there were ten or more of them; with fewer, the input was to stay described by the pairs it moves.

The four held-out wirings as a mean over them: unchanged, and with each input at 0.6 of its size and both response rates set again, through the calibrated readout unless raw counts are named. Two values in a cell are for the input searched against the first half of its split of the recordings / against the second half, with the unchanged fits scored against the same half as the input beside them; the permuted column gives the permutation with the largest gain of the four; of all recordings, each search has seen one half

**The controls hold.** The reduced input gains {{E86/inputs.csv:change=cand_A:g ~ .4f}} and {{E86/inputs.csv:change=cand_B:g ~ .4f}} (second row). With the same factors permuted across each odor's glomeruli the best of four permutations gains {{E86/inputs.csv:change=B1_perm2_A:g ~ +.4f}} and {{E86/inputs.csv:change=B3_perm4_B:g ~ +.4f}}, under half of the input's gain, and the four gain {{lit:-0.0004733129370330814 # results/E86_reduced_input_candidate/verdict.json, controls.b3_rows.A.mean_g: the mean gain of the four inputs with the first half's factors permuted ~ +.4f}} and {{lit:-0.0017732826999318028 # results/E86_reduced_input_candidate/verdict.json, controls.b3_rows.B.mean_g: the mean gain of the four inputs with the second half's factors permuted ~ +.4f}} on average. With the factors inverted the gain is {{E86/inputs.csv:change=B2_inv_A:g ~ +.4f}} and {{E86/inputs.csv:change=B2_inv_B:g ~ +.4f}}, with a higher loss on raw counts and a lower ρ on the per-pair APL effect than the unchanged fits have. A change of the input of this size therefore does not lower the pattern part by being a change, as the shuffled deviations of the ORN flies do not either ([the ORN input as a population of flies](#input-population)): the gain is tied to which glomerulus is given which factor. That does not make the factors known, and which of them the searches agree on is read further down.

**A second draw of the search carries as much, and a search on a second split of the flies does not.** Run again with other random steps against the same two halves, the search gives inputs that gain {{E86/inputs.csv:change=C1_A:g ~ .4f}} and {{E86/inputs.csv:change=C1_B:g ~ .4f}}, each on {{E86/inputs.csv:change=C1_A:n_singles_lower ~ .0f}} of the four held-out wirings and with a lower loss on raw counts, as the first pair did: the first pair was not a lucky draw.

On the second split the search does not repeat. That split is the first with a few recordings moved across: its first half holds {{lit:eight of the eleven # recording_halves(0) against recording_halves(1) in experiments/E77_input_side_common_error.py: the second split's first half holds 8 of the 11 recordings of the first split's second half and 1 of the 8 of its first half, and its second half 7 of those 8 and 3 of the 11, so 4 of the 19 recordings (2 of control flies, 2 with APL output blocked) are on the other side}} recordings of the first split's second half and {{lit:one of the eight # recording_halves(0) against recording_halves(1) in experiments/E77_input_side_common_error.py: the second split's first half holds 8 of the 11 recordings of the first split's second half and 1 of the 8 of its first half, and its second half 7 of those 8 and 3 of the 11, so 4 of the 19 recordings (2 of control flies, 2 with APL output blocked) are on the other side}} of its first. The input searched against that half loses against the other (a gain of {{E86/inputs.csv:change=C2_C:g ~ +.4f}}), where the input searched against the first split's second half had gained {{E86/inputs.csv:change=cand_B:g ~ .4f}}, and the input searched against the second half gains ({{E86/inputs.csv:change=C2_D:g ~ +.4f}}).

The halves of one split differ from each other by more than any input moves the model: against the two halves of the second split the unchanged fits have pattern parts of {{E86/inputs.csv:change=C2_C:pattern_unseen_unchanged ~ .4f}} and {{E86/inputs.csv:change=C2_D:pattern_unseen_unchanged ~ .4f}} (first row). What a fitted input gains on recordings it has not seen is then in part a statement about which recordings were held out, the limit that the search on four wirings had met ([above](#cross-wiring-fit)), now for the search on one wiring.

**Over the two splits the input carries about half of what the test asks, and it costs nothing.** The four new inputs, none of them chosen for its gain as the first pair had been, gain {{E86/replication.csv:change=mean:g ~ .4f}} on average, {{E86/replication.csv:change=mean:n_positive ~ .0f}} of the four gaining: above the 0.001 set for an input that carries and below the 0.002 set for a pass.

On the mean over the two splits the earlier test fails on the size of the gain, {{E86/gate.csv:change=gate:g ~ .4f}} where it asks 0.003, and on the single wirings and halves, {{E86/gate.csv:change=gate:n_singles_lower ~ .0f}} of 16 lower where it asks 12. Its other parts hold: the loss on raw counts changes by {{E86/gate.csv:change=gate:raw_loss_change ~ +.4f}} (lower is better), the mean effect is {{E86/gate.csv:change=gate:mean_effect_cal ~ +.3f}} against the flies' {{data:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}}, and the squared pattern error against all recordings is {{E86/gate.csv:change=gate:sq_reduction_all ~ .0%}} lower.

The part carried is thus about what the first pair gained on the split it was found on, where the second draw repeats it, and nothing on the second split in the mean of its two searches. Over both splits it is about what the profile of APL's weight carried to the same wirings ({{E83/two_by_two_DP.csv:searched_on=A;size=0.6;unit=T;against=unseen:gain ~ .4f}} and {{E83/two_by_two_DP.csv:searched_on=B;size=0.6;unit=T;against=unseen:gain ~ .4f}}; [above](#cross-wiring-fit)), without that profile's cost on raw counts and in the mean effect. It does not bring the model to the data: against all recordings the six inputs searched on the real wiring leave a pattern part of {{E86/readings.csv:change=cand_B;unit=T;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .3f}} to {{E86/readings.csv:change=C2_C;unit=T;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .3f}}, where the unchanged fits have {{E86/readings.csv:change=none;unit=T;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .3f}} and the floor is {{E66/data_floor_parts.csv:data=graded;stat=apl_effect_rmse_centered:mean ~ .3f}} (fourth row).

The seven re-drawn wirings, on none of which a search was run, as a mean over them: unchanged, and with each of the six inputs searched on the real wiring at 0.6 of its size and both response rates set again, through the calibrated readout unless raw counts are named. Two values in a cell are for the input searched against the first half of its split of the recordings / against the second half; of all recordings, each search has seen one half

**On the wirings that no search has seen, the first split's inputs gain and the second split's do not.** Every search was run on the real wiring, so that all seven re-drawn wirings, the four held-out ones among them, are wirings that its inputs have not seen. As a mean over the seven, the first split's four inputs gain {{E86/partE_inputs.csv:input=C1_B:g_draws7 ~ .4f}} to {{E86/partE_inputs.csv:input=cand_A:g_draws7 ~ .4f}} against the half of the recordings that their search did not see, each on {{E86/partE_inputs.csv:input=cand_A:draws7_lower ~ .0f}} or {{E86/partE_inputs.csv:input=C1_A:draws7_lower ~ .0f}} of the seven single wirings, the second draw again near the first.

The second split's two inputs gain {{E86/partE_inputs.csv:input=C2_C:g_draws7 ~ +.4f}} and {{E86/partE_inputs.csv:input=C2_D:g_draws7 ~ +.4f}}, on {{E86/partE_inputs.csv:input=C2_C:draws7_lower ~ .0f}} and {{E86/partE_inputs.csv:input=C2_D:draws7_lower ~ .0f}} of the seven (first two rows of the second table). On the four held-out wirings one of these two had gained and the other lost; on the other four wirings, the real one among them, they change places ({{E86/partE_inputs.csv:input=C2_C:g_S ~ +.4f}} and {{E86/partE_inputs.csv:input=C2_D:g_S ~ +.4f}}), so that neither sign holds from one set of wirings to the next, and over the seven nothing is carried. Against all recordings, one half of which each search has seen, all six inputs lower the pattern part, and all six lower the loss on raw counts with the mean effect at the flies' or a little above it (last four rows).

**The six inputs move the same pairs and hardly agree on the glomeruli.** What two of the inputs do to the per-pair APL effect of the four held-out wirings correlates at {{lit:0.5113547106272736 # results/E86_reduced_input_candidate/part_e.json, agreement.changes_corr_T_mean: the mean of column changes_corr_T of partE_agreement.csv over the 15 pairs of inputs ~ .2f}} on average over the 15 pairs of inputs, and at {{E86/partE_agreement.csv:input_a=cand_A;input_b=C1_A:changes_corr_T ~ .2f}} and {{E86/partE_agreement.csv:input_a=cand_B;input_b=C1_B:changes_corr_T ~ .2f}} for the two pairs whose searches were run against the same half of the recordings. Their factors, on a log scale over the 360 entries, correlate at {{lit:0.10617695628055736 # results/E86_reduced_input_candidate/part_e.json, agreement.factors_corr_mean: the mean of column factors_corr of partE_agreement.csv over the 15 pairs of inputs ~ .2f}} on average, between {{E86/partE_agreement.csv:input_a=C2_C;input_b=C2_D:factors_corr ~ .2f}} and {{E86/partE_agreement.csv:input_a=cand_A;input_b=C2_D:factors_corr ~ .2f}}, and at {{E86/partE_agreement.csv:input_a=cand_A;input_b=C1_A:factors_corr ~ .2f}} and {{E86/partE_agreement.csv:input_a=cand_B;input_b=C1_B:factors_corr ~ .2f}} for the searches against the same half.

What the inputs share is a direction among the pairs, and it is the one the recordings ask for. The mean over the six of the change in each pair's APL effect correlates at {{lit:0.6544660754156494 # results/E86_reduced_input_candidate/part_e.json, pairs_moved.T.corr_mean_change_asked: over the 120 pairs on the four held-out wirings, the correlation of column mean_change with column asked of partE_pairs_moved.csv (unit T) ~ .2f}} with what all recordings ask of the unchanged fits, the flies' per-pair effect minus theirs with both means removed, and it goes about half of the way: the 15 pairs among 2h, IaA, pa, eb, ep and ms change by {{lit:0.03199478489463584 # results/E86_reduced_input_candidate/part_e.json, pairs_moved.T.groups.ester.mean_change: the mean of column mean_change of partE_pairs_moved.csv over the 15 rows with unit T and group ester ~ +.3f}} on average where the recordings ask {{lit:0.07008611930470161 # results/E86_reduced_input_candidate/part_e.json, pairs_moved.T.groups.ester.asked: the mean of column asked of partE_pairs_moved.csv over the 15 rows with unit T and group ester ~ +.3f}}, and the six pairs among 1-8ol, 1-5ol, 1-6ol and 6al by {{lit:-0.03307639817092301 # results/E86_reduced_input_candidate/part_e.json, pairs_moved.T.groups.alcohol.mean_change: the mean of column mean_change of partE_pairs_moved.csv over the 6 rows with unit T and group alcohol ~ +.3f}} where they ask {{lit:-0.07473925053813359 # results/E86_reduced_input_candidate/part_e.json, pairs_moved.T.groups.alcohol.asked: the mean of column asked of partE_pairs_moved.csv over the 6 rows with unit T and group alcohol ~ +.3f}}. Many inputs thus move the same pairs, as many profiles of APL's weight do ([above](#cross-wiring-fit)), and most of a single search's factors are its own draw.

The {{lit:eleven # results/E86_reduced_input_candidate/part_e.json, rule.n_meets_read: the rows of partE_five_of_six.csv with meets_read}} changes of a single glomerulus's response that recur at the size the input is read at, in the order of their mean factor. Factors are given as powers of two, so that the search's bounds, half and twice the recorded response, are −1 and +1; two values in a cell are for the search against the first half of its split of the recordings / against the second half. The spread between the ORN flies is the standard deviation over the flies of the logarithm of the entry's response. Hallem's response is given where the receptor data hold the entry
