**A few single changes recur in all six inputs, more of them than chance gives, and they are named.** {{lit:73 # results/E86_reduced_input_candidate/part_e.json, rule.n_meets: the entries with meets in partE_entries.csv, the rows of partE_five_of_six.csv}} of the 360 entries meet the rule that had been fixed: at least five of the six inputs change them in the same direction, and in the mean of the six by more than half of what the search allows. That is more than the ten set for naming a list.

How many such entries six unrelated inputs of this kind share was counted beside the rule, with each input's factors permuted across each odor's glomeruli: {{lit:38.385 # results/E86_reduced_input_candidate/part_e.json, rule.null_meets.null_mean: the mean of column n_meets of partE_null.csv over its 1000 draws ~ .0f}} on average, and in {{lit:none # results/E86_reduced_input_candidate/part_e.json, rule.null_meets.null_frac_ge is 0.0: no draw of partE_null.csv has an n_meets of 73 or more (the largest is 59)}} of 1,000 draws as many as the searches share. About half of the list is thus what searches that end at their bounds give by chance, and its length is not the result; its head is.

With the factors taken at 0.6 of their size, as the input is read, {{lit:11 # results/E86_reduced_input_candidate/part_e.json, rule.n_meets_read: the rows of partE_five_of_six.csv with meets_read}} entries still meet the rule, where the permuted factors give {{lit:2.011 # results/E86_reduced_input_candidate/part_e.json, rule.null_meets_read.null_mean: the mean of column n_meets_read of partE_null.csv over its 1000 draws ~ .0f}} on average and in {{lit:none # results/E86_reduced_input_candidate/part_e.json, rule.null_meets_read.null_frac_ge is 0.0: no draw of partE_null.csv has an n_meets_read of 11 or more (the largest is 8)}} of the draws as many, and on each of them all six inputs agree in direction (table above). {{lit:Nine # counted in results/E86_reduced_input_candidate/partE_five_of_six.csv: of the 11 rows with meets_read, those with sign -1}} lower a glomerulus's response and {{lit:two # counted in results/E86_reduced_input_candidate/partE_five_of_six.csv: of the 11 rows with meets_read, those with sign 1}} raise it.

VM7d's response to eb, which every search took to its bound, DM5's to 1-8ol and DM4's to ep are lowered, DM1's to IaA is raised, and DP1m's is lowered for three odors, ms, 6al and 2h; VL2p's response to 2h, DM2's to 6al and DM3's to IaA, lowered, and DC2's to 1-5ol, raised, complete the list. Over the whole list DP1m and DM5 are each lowered for {{lit:four # counted in results/E86_reduced_input_candidate/partE_five_of_six.csv: the rows with glomerulus DP1m (ms, 6al, 2h and 1-8ol), all with sign -1; the rows with glomerulus DM5 are four as well (1-8ol, 1-6ol, eb and IaA), all with sign -1}} of the ten odors, and VM7d is changed for {{lit:six # counted in results/E86_reduced_input_candidate/partE_five_of_six.csv: the rows with glomerulus VM7d (eb, 2h and pa with sign -1; 6al, 1-6ol and ep with sign 1)}}, lowered for three and raised for three.

**The changes are of the size by which flies differ, and nothing on hand shows them to be the flies'.** Read at 0.6 of its size, each of the {{lit:eleven # results/E86_reduced_input_candidate/part_e.json, rule.n_meets_read: the rows of partE_five_of_six.csv with meets_read}} changes a glomerulus's response by about one standard deviation of the spread between the ORN flies or less, and eb in VM7d by nearly two ({{E86/partE_five_of_six.csv:odor=eb;glomerulus=VM7d:read_in_flies_sd ~ +.1f}}; last column but one).

As whole inputs the four new ones are as the first two were ([the ORN input as a population of flies](#input-population)): {{E86/partE_vs_flies_summary.csv:e86_input=cand_A:within1_log2 ~ .0%}} to {{E86/partE_vs_flies_summary.csv:e86_input=C1_A:within1_log2 ~ .0%}} of the entries of each of the six are changed by less than one standard deviation of that spread, and the share of the squared size of an input's change that the nine flies' own deviations for the same odor can make up, {{E86/partE_vs_flies_summary.csv:e86_input=C1_B:span_share ~ .2f}} to {{E86/partE_vs_flies_summary.csv:e86_input=C2_C:span_share ~ .2f}} for the four new inputs, is about that of the same factors permuted across the glomeruli ({{E86/partE_vs_flies_summary.csv:e86_input=C1_B:span_share_perm_mean ~ .2f}} to {{E86/partE_vs_flies_summary.csv:e86_input=C2_C:span_share_perm_mean ~ .2f}}).

Hallem's receptor data hold two of the ten odors, 1-8ol and ms, at ten times the concentration of the KC recordings, and over their {{E86/partE_vs_flies_summary.csv:e86_input=C1_A:n_hallem ~ .0f}} entries the six inputs' changes correlate at {{E86/partE_vs_flies_summary.csv:e86_input=C2_C:hallem_corr ~ .2f}} to {{E86/partE_vs_flies_summary.csv:e86_input=C2_D:hallem_corr ~ .2f}} with Hallem's response relative to the lab's input. {{lit:Five # counted in results/E86_reduced_input_candidate/partE_five_of_six.csv: the rows with a value in hallem_log2_vs_lab (1-8ol in DM5, VM5d and VC3; ms in VA5 and DL1)}} of the {{lit:73 # results/E86_reduced_input_candidate/part_e.json, rule.n_meets: the entries with meets in partE_entries.csv, the rows of partE_five_of_six.csv}} listed entries are among them: {{lit:three # counted in results/E86_reduced_input_candidate/partE_five_of_six.csv: of the five rows with a value in hallem_log2_vs_lab, those whose mean_log2 has its sign (1-8ol in DM5, ms in VA5, 1-8ol in VM5d)}} are changed the way Hallem's data point, DM5's response to 1-8ol among them, and {{lit:two # counted in results/E86_reduced_input_candidate/partE_five_of_six.csv: of the five rows with a value in hallem_log2_vs_lab, those whose mean_log2 has the opposite sign (ms in DL1, 1-8ol in VC3)}} the other way.

The data on hand thus neither support the list nor contradict it. Nor does the gain on recordings not seen vouch for it: the second split's two inputs, which carry nothing there, agree with the other four on every one of the {{lit:eleven # results/E86_reduced_input_candidate/part_e.json, rule.n_meets_read: the rows of partE_five_of_six.csv with meets_read}}. The list is what a search for these pairs reaches for in this model, each change within what one fly differs from another by, and it becomes a statement about the flies only if a measurement bears it out.

**Realism.** No model was fitted and no parameter added: what is tested is an input, and both response rates are held at every reading. Every point of the controls and of the replication is inside all four realism bands, and so is each of the six inputs on each of the eight wirings, with the flies' responses counted in baseline-noise units, as the bands count now, and by the recordings' own criterion, as they counted until 2026-11-10. The response rate ρ with APL on moves most with the inverted input, to {{E86/runs.csv:B2_inv_A_P4:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}} at the lowest, where the band asks 0.37 or more.

What the bands do not see is as in the earlier reading. The largest spike count with APL off reaches {{E86/runs_E.csv:E_C1_A_real:max_count_off ~ .0f}} per KC and odor, in a family that nothing bounds there ([the firing ceiling for the KCs](#firing-ceiling)). And the inputs are [oracle](#fn-oracle) inputs, each glomerulus's response between half and twice the recorded one, with {{lit:0.3611111111111111 # counted in results/E86_reduced_input_candidate/partE_entries.csv: 130 of the 360 entries of column C2_D are at a bound of the search (a log2 factor of -1 or 1), the smallest share of the six inputs ~ .0%}} to {{lit:0.4444444444444444 # counted in results/E86_reduced_input_candidate/partE_entries.csv: 160 of the 360 entries of column C2_C are at a bound of the search (a log2 factor of -1 or 1), the largest share of the six inputs ~ .0%}} of the factors of each of the six searches at those bounds. No measurement supports them, and the entries named above are a list for a measurement, not measured values.

As everywhere, the pairs with paa, euc and -aPine rest on [ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations); none of the three is among the ten odors searched, whose ORN recordings are at the concentration of the KC recordings. The gain was not bought with the bands or on raw counts: with each of the six inputs searched on the real wiring the loss on raw counts is below the unchanged fits' and the mean effect is at the flies' or a little above it, on the four held-out wirings and on the seven re-drawn ones (last two rows of the first two tables).

**What follows.** The reduced searched input is no longer a candidate. It is a result, and a small one: its controls hold, a second draw of its search repeats it, and what it carries to wirings and recordings that it was not fitted to depends on the split of the flies, about half of what the test asked over two splits.

Fitted changes at the level of the glomeruli, of APL's weight or of the input, are thereby closed as carriers of more than a few thousandths of the pattern part with the present recordings, and the common error as a whole stays where it was ([above](#cross-wiring-fit)). Since the input did not pass, the readings kept for an input that passes, in the family with the firing ceiling, at the flies' 2 s pulse and through the trial noise, were not made: every number here is at the model's 0.5 s pulse, in the family without a ceiling and without trial noise.

What the input is has been read as far as six runs of the search allow. It is a direction among the odor pairs, the one the recordings ask for, which many inputs supply, and a short list of single glomeruli that all six runs change alike.

The list does not make the input a measured one: its entries are within the spread between flies, the data on hand neither support nor contradict them, and they are as much the second split's, which carries nothing, as the first's. It is what a measurement could test. The one reading that the data on hand allow has since been made, in recordings of the PN dendrites, and at the listed entries the dendrites do not depart from the ORNs in the searches' direction ([below](#missing-glomeruli)); what is left of the list is with the open measurement question at the end of the page.

What limits a fitted change is the recordings, and more of them would raise what one can be shown to carry; that too is with the pending work. The lead itself has moved since: read directly, the recordings place the models' shortfall in their KCs' responses without APL ([the form of APL's inhibition in the flies' own responses](#inhibition-form)), which a change of the input acts on as well, and what this subsection adds there is a size, the few thousandths that a fitted input can be shown to carry.

### The ORN input as a population of flies: whether the input averaged over the ORN flies stands for the inputs of the flies behind the KC data {#input-population}

**The input averaged over the ORN flies is a fair stand-in, on the main target, for the inputs of the flies behind the KC data.** With each of nine ORN flies' own input on each of the eight wirings, the mean over the 72 model flies has the pattern part of the APL-effect loss that the eight wirings have at the averaged input, and the flies' mean effect as before. Neither bound on how much of the spread between the ORN recordings is the flies' own changes this, nor does a control with each fly's deviations shuffled, nor letting the response rates differ between model flies.

Both distance matrices move a little toward the flies', and the odor pairs with near-identical ORN input move apart with APL on and with APL off alike, so that their APL effect stays at half the flies'. What the input flies add is spread: single model flies then differ from one another about as much as single recordings do.

Every model above takes as its input the average over the ORN flies of each glomerulus's response to each odor, the lab's input of the earlier subsections, while the KC data are averages over recordings of distances computed within a fly, and each of those flies had its own input. [The APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population) made the wiring a population of flies and left the input one averaged fly.

The ORN input as a population of flies gave the input its flies as well. Its main reading fits nothing to the KC data, so what limited [the input and APL's glomerulus profile fitted on several wirings at once](#cross-wiring-fit), that a fitted change is confirmed only in small part by recordings it has not seen, does not limit this reading.

The flies are those of the megamat ORN recordings: nine flies, three trials per odor, the 12 odors of that panel, and {{E85/flies.csv:fly=f1:n_gloms ~ .0f}} to {{E85/flies.csv:fly=f0:n_gloms ~ .0f}} of the model's 36 glomeruli in each fly. No fly has the averaged input: across the flies a response differs from the average by a factor of one and a half to nearly two (a standard deviation of {{lit:0.56 # results/E85_orn_fly_population/part_a.json, spread.median_sd_log2_above30: the median, over the glomerulus-by-odor entries whose mean response is above 30 % of the largest, of the SD across the nine flies of log2(fly / mean)}} for the strong responses and of {{lit:0.89 # results/E85_orn_fly_population/part_a.json, spread.median_sd_log2_all: the median over all glomerulus-by-odor entries of the SD across the nine flies of log2(fly / mean)}} over all, on a scale of logarithms to base 2), and per glomerulus a median of {{lit:0.91 # results/E85_orn_fly_population/part_a.json, reliability.r_g_median: the median over glomeruli of the share of the fly-to-fly variance that repeats across trials}} of that variance repeats across a fly's trials.

A model fly is one wiring with one ORN fly's input: the averaged input plus the fly's deviation from the average over the nine flies, for the 12 odors and the glomeruli measured in that fly, so that the average over the nine inputs is the averaged input exactly.

- In the main reading each deviation is multiplied by the share of its glomerulus's variance between flies that repeats across trials (the repeatable deviations).
- Two bounds stand beside it, because a difference between two flies' ORN recordings is in part a difference of the imaging and not of the fly's input: the deviations as measured, the upper bound, and the repeatable deviations with each fly's gain on each glomerulus divided out, so that a difference in brightness between flies cannot enter, the lower.
- The control has each fly's repeatable deviations shuffled over the glomeruli within each odor, which keeps their size and breaks their structure.

Every wiring is at its own breadth-2 APL-effect fit ([above](#wiring-population)); for each model fly the somatic threshold and the APL scale were set again until the numbers of responses with APL off and with APL on were the wiring's, and the main reading was also made with nothing set again. A population is read as the wirings were, the pair distances averaged over its model flies in each condition before the APL effect is taken. The main reading is on all eight wirings (72 model flies), the bounds and the control on four of them (the real wiring, two claw permutations and one matched shuffle).

What would count was fixed before any run, through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout) and against all recordings. The input flies move the target if the pattern part of the 72 model flies is lower than that of the eight wirings at the averaged input by 0.003 or more and lower on at least six of the eight wirings, each wiring's nine model flies set against the same wiring at the averaged input, with every population inside the realism bands. They do not move it if the change is below 0.0015 either way. And a shuffled control that gains half as much or more means that the size of the differences between flies does it, whatever their structure.

Right: the per-pair APL effect of the KC data (black), of the mean over the eight wirings at the averaged input (blue) and of the mean over the 72 model flies (orange), the 120 odor pairs in the order of the KC data's effect.](results/E85_orn_fly_population/E85_populations.png)

**The pattern part does not move.** The mean over the 72 model flies has a pattern part of {{E85/populations.csv:group=B1;unit=all;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} against {{E85/populations.csv:group=lab;unit=all;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} for the eight wirings at the averaged input, {{diff:E85/populations.csv:group=B1;unit=all;readout=cal:z8_pattern -- E85/populations.csv:group=lab;unit=all;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} higher, where a change of less than 0.0015 either way had been set as no move (the first two model columns of the table, and the right panel of the figure). The mean APL effect is {{E85/populations.csv:group=B1;unit=all;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}, still at the flies' {{data:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}}, and ρ on the per-pair APL effect, the pattern part against the six recordings that are alike and the loss on raw counts are where they were (third to sixth rows).

On the 66 pairs among the 12 odors whose input differs between model flies the pattern part is {{E85/populations.csv:group=B1;unit=all;readout=cal:z8_pattern_megamat ~ .4f}} against {{E85/populations.csv:group=lab;unit=all;readout=cal:z8_pattern_megamat ~ .4f}}. The other 54 pairs have paa, -aPine, euc or B-myr, which keep the averaged input in every model fly, since no fly was imaged with both ORN panels.

**Each wiring gains from its nine flies, and it is the gain that a mean over wirings already has.** On {{lit:seven # results/E85_orn_fly_population/verdict.json, B1.n_wirings_lower: 7 of the 8 wirings have a lower pattern part as the mean over their nine model flies than at the averaged input}} of the eight wirings the mean over the wiring's nine model flies has a lower pattern part than the same wiring at the averaged input, by up to {{E85/populations.csv:group=B1;unit=P4;readout=cal:gain_z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, and on the real wiring it is {{diff:E85/populations.csv:group=B1;unit=real;readout=cal:z8_pattern -- E85/populations.csv:group=B1;unit=real;readout=cal:lab_z8_pattern ~ .4f}} higher (the left panel of the figure). The count that had been set is thus met and the size is not, and the two fit together.

A single model fly is worse than its wiring at the averaged input, by {{E85/draw_terms.csv:readout=cal;effect=per-pair APL effect:mean_single_minus_lab ~ .4f}} on average: one wiring with one input carries an accident of that pairing, which a mean over the inputs removes, and which a mean over wirings removes as well. The eight wirings at the averaged input already have that gain (under the readout the loss is {{E72/spread.csv:readout=cal:median_single ~ .3f}} for the median single wiring and {{E72/population.csv:group=all:cal_loss ~ .3f}} for their mean), and the input flies add nothing to it.

**Neither bound, the shuffled control nor the reading with nothing set again moves it.** On the four wirings, whose mean at the averaged input has a pattern part of {{E85/populations.csv:group=lab;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, the repeatable deviations give {{E85/populations.csv:group=B1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, the deviations as measured {{E85/populations.csv:group=B2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} and those with each fly's glomerulus gains divided out {{E85/populations.csv:group=B3;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, each within 0.0015 of it (the last five columns). How much of the spread between the ORN recordings is the flies' own and how much the imaging's therefore does not bear on the reading.

The shuffled control gives {{E85/populations.csv:group=B4;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, a gain of {{E85/populations.csv:group=B4;unit=S;readout=cal:gain_z8_pattern ~ .4f}} that is inside the same margin, and since the repeatable deviations gain nothing there is nothing for it to be half of. With nothing set again the 72 model flies read {{E85/populations.csv:group=B5;unit=all;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} (third model column). Their response rates then differ from one model fly to the next, with APL on between {{E85/runs.csv:B5_repro_f6_M3:rate_on ~ .3f}} and {{E85/runs.csv:B5_repro_f1_M3:rate_on ~ .3f}} and with APL off between {{E85/runs.csv:B5_repro_f0_M1:ratio ~ .2f}} and {{E85/runs.csv:B5_repro_f3_P2:ratio ~ .2f}} times that, around the flies' {{data:noise_rate_ratio_fraction ~ .2f}} (90 % interval {{data:noise_rate_ratio_fraction.lo ~ .2f}} to {{data:noise_rate_ratio_fraction.hi ~ .2f}}), so holding the response rates is not what keeps the reading in place.

**The two matrices move, and the effect does not.** With input flies both mean distances rise toward the flies', from {{E85/populations.csv:group=lab;unit=all;readout=cal:mean_on ~ .3f}} to {{E85/populations.csv:group=B1;unit=all;readout=cal:mean_on ~ .3f}} with APL on and from {{E85/populations.csv:group=lab;unit=all;readout=cal:mean_off ~ .3f}} to {{E85/populations.csv:group=B1;unit=all;readout=cal:mean_off ~ .3f}} with APL off, where the control flies have {{data:ctrl_mean_dist ~ .3f}} and the flies with APL output blocked (TNT) {{data:tnt_mean_dist ~ .3f}}: a tenth to a seventh of what is missing, where a third had been set as the size that would matter for the matrices themselves. ρ on odor-odor distances does not change in either condition.

The four nearest of the pairs with near-identical ORN input ([above](#claw-knee)), 2h with IaA, 2h with pa, IaA with pa and eb with ep, move apart by {{diff:E85/populations.csv:group=B1;unit=all;readout=cal:nearest_on -- E85/populations.csv:group=lab;unit=all;readout=cal:nearest_on ~ .3f}} with APL on and by {{diff:E85/populations.csv:group=B1;unit=all;readout=cal:nearest_off -- E85/populations.csv:group=lab;unit=all;readout=cal:nearest_off ~ .3f}} with APL off, so that their APL effect is {{E85/populations.csv:group=B1;unit=all;readout=cal:nearest_effect ~ +.3f}} where it was {{E85/populations.csv:group=lab;unit=all;readout=cal:nearest_effect ~ +.3f}}, half the flies' {{E77/pair_kinds.csv:member=mean8;readout=cal;target=z8;kind=nearest:data_effect ~ +.3f}}, and the six pairs as a group behave the same. An input that differs from fly to fly makes two near-identical odors less alike with APL and without it by the same amount, and the difference between the two conditions, which is the target, is left where it was.

**Only the shuffled deviations lift the near pairs' APL effect, and a real fly's deviations are not of that kind.** In the shuffled control the four nearest pairs have an APL effect of {{E85/populations.csv:group=B4;unit=S;readout=cal:nearest_effect ~ +.3f}} against {{E85/populations.csv:group=lab;unit=S;readout=cal:nearest_effect ~ +.3f}} at the averaged input, about a seventh of what is missing, and the six pairs {{E85/populations.csv:group=B4;unit=S;readout=cal:six_effect ~ +.3f}} against {{E85/populations.csv:group=lab;unit=S;readout=cal:six_effect ~ +.3f}}. The reason is in the inputs (the row on the distance between the two odors' ORN inputs).

Deviations shuffled over the glomeruli are independent between odors, so they set the two odors of a near pair far apart, at {{lit:0.248 # mean of column distance over the nine flies and the four nearest ester pairs (2h with IaA, 2h with pa, IaA with pa, eb with ep), rows variant=permuted of results/E85_orn_fly_population/orn_distances_by_fly.csv}} on average for the four nearest pairs against {{lit:0.129 # mean of column lab_distance over the four nearest ester pairs (2h with IaA, 2h with pa, IaA with pa, eb with ep) in results/E85_orn_fly_population/orn_distances_by_fly.csv}} in the averaged input. A real fly's deviations are shared between similar odors, a glomerulus that responds more than the average to eb doing so to ep as well, and in each of their three forms they leave these pairs at {{lit:0.165 # mean of column distance over the nine flies and the four nearest ester pairs (2h with IaA, 2h with pa, IaA with pa, eb with ep), rows variant=gainfree of results/E85_orn_fly_population/orn_distances_by_fly.csv}} to {{lit:0.188 # mean of column distance over the nine flies and the four nearest ester pairs (2h with IaA, 2h with pa, IaA with pa, eb with ep), rows variant=measured of results/E85_orn_fly_population/orn_distances_by_fly.csv}}.

The model's APL effect on a near pair thus does grow with the distance between the two inputs, and the differences between flies do not supply that distance. What the KC data show on these pairs, a larger distance with APL than without it, then has to come from what APL does to near-identical input and not from the variability of that input.

**With input flies the model population has the flies' spread.** The flies behind the two conditions are different animals. APL on from one of the eight wirings at the averaged input with APL off from another has an APL-effect loss of {{E85/yardstick.csv:readout=cal:lab_two_wirings_loss_median ~ .3f}} at the median under the readout, where one control recording paired with one recording with APL output blocked (TNT), scored against the mean of the remaining recordings, has {{E71/partC_summary.csv:model=KC data (E70 yardstick):rmse_median ~ .3f}} ([the high-firing KCs that survive APL](#high-firing-kcs)): wirings alone leave model flies too alike.

APL on from one model fly with APL off from another of a different wiring and input fly has {{E85/yardstick.csv:readout=cal:loss_median ~ .3f}}, and {{E85/yardstick.csv:readout=raw:loss_median ~ .3f}} on raw counts. The recordings' value also holds trial and imaging noise, which these model flies do not have, so the match is, if anything, generous to the input's share.

One input fly moves a single model fly about as much as one draw of the wiring does. Of the variance of the per-pair APL effect over the 72 model flies under the readout, the wiring accounts for {{E85/draw_terms.csv:readout=cal;effect=per-pair APL effect:var_wiring ~ .5f}}, the input fly for {{E85/draw_terms.csv:readout=cal;effect=per-pair APL effect:var_fly ~ .5f}} and what is particular to their pairing for {{E85/draw_terms.csv:readout=cal;effect=per-pair APL effect:var_interaction ~ .5f}} (on raw counts the wiring's term is twice the input fly's), and the pattern part of a single model fly has a standard deviation of {{E85/draw_terms.csv:readout=cal;effect=per-pair APL effect:sd_single_pattern_within_wiring ~ .4f}} over the nine input flies of one wiring, where that of a wiring at the averaged input has {{E85/draw_terms.csv:readout=cal;effect=per-pair APL effect:sd_single_pattern_over_wirings_lab ~ .4f}} over the eight wirings. A comparison of two fits on one wiring at the averaged input therefore rests on one draw of each of two sources of that size.

**The flies' spread holds no input that the KC data prefer, and the searched inputs are of the flies' size without being shown to be of their kind.** A weighting of the nine input flies, non-negative weights that sum to one, was fitted on the four wirings of the bounds against one half of the recordings and scored on the other four wirings against the other half, once for each half (the halves are those of the earlier searches, split by fly).

Where it had not been fitted the weighting is worse than equal weights both times, by {{diff:E85/fly_mixture.csv:fitted_on=A:T_unseen_fitted -- E85/fly_mixture.csv:fitted_on=A:T_unseen_equal ~ .4f}} and {{diff:E85/fly_mixture.csv:fitted_on=B:T_unseen_fitted -- E85/fly_mixture.csv:fitted_on=B:T_unseen_equal ~ .4f}} in the pattern part, where a gain of 0.003 in both had been set as a pass, and the two fits do not give the flies the same weights. What the KC data ask of the input is therefore not among the nine flies, and a search restricted to what the ORN flies span is not a follow-up.

The ORN flies also give the yardstick that the searched inputs lacked ([the input side of the error common to all wirings](#input-side) and [the input and APL's glomerulus profile fitted on several wirings at once](#cross-wiring-fit)). At 0.6 of their size, the two inputs searched on the real wiring and the two searched on four wirings change a glomerulus's response by less than one standard deviation of the flies' spread in {{E85/searched_inputs_summary.csv:input=E77_halfA:within1_log2 ~ .0%}} to {{E85/searched_inputs_summary.csv:input=E77_halfB:within1_log2 ~ .0%}} of their entries: by size they are no more than the difference between two flies. By direction they are not shown to be the flies'.

Of the squared size of an input's change, the share that the nine flies' own deviations for the same odor can make up is {{E85/searched_inputs_summary.csv:input=E83_armI_halfA:span_share ~ .2f}} to {{E85/searched_inputs_summary.csv:input=E77_halfB:span_share ~ .2f}} for three of the four inputs, below that of the same factors permuted across the glomeruli ({{E85/searched_inputs_summary.csv:input=E83_armI_halfA:span_share_perm_mean ~ .2f}} to {{E85/searched_inputs_summary.csv:input=E77_halfB:span_share_perm_mean ~ .2f}}). For the fourth, the input searched on the real wiring against the first half of the recordings, it is {{E85/searched_inputs_summary.csv:input=E77_halfA:span_share ~ .2f}} against {{E85/searched_inputs_summary.csv:input=E77_halfA:span_share_perm_mean ~ .2f}}, and above the 95th percentile of the permutations for {{E85/searched_inputs_summary.csv:input=E77_halfA:n_odors_above_perm_p95 ~ .0f}} of the ten odors, pa and 1-5ol. The four inputs that the same search has given since on the real wiring are of the flies' size as well, and about as much inside the flies' span as permuted factors are ([above](#reduced-input)).

**Realism.** No population leaves a realism band: not the 72 model flies, not the mean over any wiring's nine model flies, and none of the populations of the bounds, the control or the reading with nothing set again, with the flies' responses counted in baseline-noise units, as the bands count now (the last four rows of the table), and by the recordings' own criterion, as they did until 2026-11-10. Both response rates are held by construction, and the two bands that an input can move, the response rate ρ with APL on and the number of odors per KC, stay well inside for every population.

Single model flies are another matter. In the main reading {{lit:7 # results/E85_orn_fly_population/verdict.json, B1.n_flagged_model_flies: the rows stage=B1S and B1T of runs.csv with a realism_flag}} of the 72 are below the band on the response rate ρ with APL on, down to {{E85/runs.csv:B1S_repro_f8_P1:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}}, five of them with one ORN fly's input and two with another's, since which odors drive many KCs depends on the input fly more than on the wiring; by the recordings' own criterion {{lit:19 # count of the rows stage=B1S and B1T of results/E85_orn_fly_population/runs.csv with a realism_flag_zcrit}} of the 72 are outside a band. The reading is judged on populations, as the KC data are means over recordings, and nothing above rests on a single model fly.

What the bands do not see is the family's own, with one addition: the largest spike count of a KC to one odor rises from {{lit:53 # the largest spike count per KC and odor with APL on over the eight wirings at the averaged input, Realism table of E85_orn_fly_population.md (the identity runs of results/E85_orn_fly_population)}} with APL on and {{lit:84 # the largest spike count per KC and odor with APL off over the eight wirings at the averaged input, Realism table of E85_orn_fly_population.md (the identity runs of results/E85_orn_fly_population)}} with APL off over the eight wirings at the averaged input to {{E85/runs.csv:B1T_repro_f0_P4:max_count_on ~ .0f}} and {{E85/runs.csv:B1S_repro_f7_real:max_count_off ~ .0f}} over the 72 model flies, in a family that nothing bounds there ([the firing ceiling for the KCs](#firing-ceiling)). The somatic threshold set again lies between {{E85/runs.csv:B1S_repro_f2_P2:thr_factor ~ .2f}} and {{E85/runs.csv:B1T_repro_f4_M3:thr_factor ~ .2f}} times the wiring's fitted one, and the APL scale between {{E85/runs.csv:B1T_repro_f4_M3:apl_factor ~ .2f}} and {{E85/runs.csv:B1S_repro_f0_M1:apl_factor ~ .2f}} times.

The inputs are measured ones, with two cautions: a difference between two flies' ORN recordings is in part the imaging's, which the two bounds bracket, and the average over these nine flies is not the model's input itself, a consensus over more flies and panels (an R² of {{lit:0.979 # results/E85_orn_fly_population/part_a.json, scaling.r2: the R² of the model's ORN input on the mean over the nine flies}} between the two), so that only the flies' deviations from their own average were used. As everywhere, the pairs with paa, euc and -aPine rest on [ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations), and these three and B-myr keep the averaged input in every model fly, so their 54 pairs get one odor's variability at most. The reading costs no realism at the level it is judged on, and it gains nothing.

**What follows.** The averaged input stays the input of the models on this page, and every population number above stands as given. Differences between flies in what reaches the KCs are closed, for this family, as a carrier of the common error and of the near pairs' shortfall, and since the two bounds agree, how much of the spread between the ORN recordings is the flies' own does not have to be settled for that.

The near pairs' shortfall stays with what happens between the claw and the soma, where a per-claw knee did not supply it either ([above](#claw-knee)): what is wanted there is a way for APL to hold near-identical inputs apart. The recordings have since been asked what does this in the flies.

An inhibition that all the KCs share, growing with the odor's response over all of them, gives the four nearest pairs nearly the flies' APL effect when it is applied to the flies' own responses with APL output blocked (TNT), and an inhibition among KCs of similar tuning overshoots it; the shared inhibition applied to the responses with APL off of the fits as they are gives these pairs less than the model's own APL does, so that the shortfall is, by that reading, in the model's responses without APL ([the form of APL's inhibition in the flies' own responses](#inhibition-form)). The result is that of one family, at the model's 0.5 s pulse and without trial noise; the family with the firing ceiling was to be read the same way only if the target moved, and was not read.

Two things are carried forward. Where single model flies are set against single recordings, or the spread between model flies serves as a yardstick, the model flies are to be drawn with input flies as well as wirings, since wirings alone vary too little. And for the reduced searched input, whose own controls have been run and hold ([above](#reduced-input)), the shuffled control here is a test of size without structure: deviations of the flies' size, shuffled, gain {{E85/populations.csv:group=B4;unit=S;readout=cal:gain_z8_pattern ~ .4f}} on four wirings, inside the margin of no move, so a change of the input of that size does not lower the pattern part merely by being a change. What is taken up from here is with the pending work at the end of the page.

### The form of APL's inhibition in the flies' own responses: whether an inhibition of a fly's responses without APL gives the flies' APL effect, and whether the models' error lies in their APL or in their responses without it {#inhibition-form}

**The pattern of the flies' APL effect can be read from their own responses without APL.**

- An inhibition that grows with the odor's response over all the KCs, and a little with how broadly the KC itself responds, applied to each recording with APL output blocked (TNT) with one constant set by the control flies' response rate, predicts the control flies' distances better than a uniform inhibition does on recordings it was not chosen on, and on all recordings it leaves a pattern part near the data's floor. The odor's strength is what carries it, and an inhibition among KCs of similar tuning is not what the recordings show.
- Applied to the models' responses with APL off, the same inhibition does no better than the models' own APL, and the models' APL effect among the esters stays too small under each inhibition of the kind that was read on them, so that by this reading the error common to the wirings lies in what the models' KCs do without APL and not in the form of their APL. Two results bound that reading.
  - It is a reading of spike counts: simulated in place of the model's APL, as a rise of each KC's threshold, the flies' form does worse than the model's own APL, and the simulations do not follow the reading pair by pair.
  - And it is the reading of a model that recruits in its own way. With how many KCs each odor recruits without APL set to the flies' on four wirings, the one respect of the responses that a saved handle can set, the model comes a third to a half of the way to what the flies' form does within a fly, the pattern of its own APL effect is no nearer the flies', and the flies' form applied to those responses does better than the model's own APL: a part of what is left is then read on the side of the model's APL. Simulated in place of APL on those responses, the form has since done far worse than the model's own APL ([below](#responder-sets)).
- What the form does within one fly is a target that needs no control flies and is known about twice as finely as the main target; it missed the test set for using it by a narrow margin, and by itself it is not a screen for the main target.

Every search for the common error has changed the model and read the model: APL's weight by glomerulus ([the glomerulus profile of APL inhibition](#glomerulus-profile)), what reaches the KCs ([the input side of the error common to all wirings](#input-side), [the input and APL's glomerulus profile fitted on several wirings at once](#cross-wiring-fit), [the controls and the replication of the reduced searched input](#reduced-input), [the ORN input as a population of flies](#input-population)), the transfer at the claw ([the high per-claw knee without a dead zone](#claw-knee)), where APL's inhibition falls in the calyx ([the APL calyx maps against the connectome](#apl-calyx-maps)) and the time course ([the flies' recording protocol in the model](#flies-protocol)). The form of APL's inhibition in the flies' own responses put the question to the recordings.

A recording with APL output blocked (TNT) holds a fly's KC responses without APL, KC by KC, which is what every model is asked to turn into its responses with APL. If a simple inhibition of those responses gives the control flies' distances, the pattern of the flies' effect is in their responses without APL, and the same inhibition applied to a model's responses with APL off says on which side the model's error lies: in the form of its APL, if the flies' inhibition brings the model nearer the flies' effect than the model's own APL does, or in its responses without APL, if it does not.

A recording's responses are its trial means, KC by odor. A response is a value above the recordings' criterion of 1 z, and values not above it are set to 0 on both sides, the convention closest to a model's spike counts ([the main target](#apl-effect)); the flies' mean effect is then {{data:apl_effect_thresholded_mean ~ +.3f}} and its standard deviation across the 120 pairs {{E87/forms.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;form=none:pattern ~ .3f}}.

A form of inhibition reduces each KC's response to each odor by a constant times a power of the odor's strength times a power of the KC's breadth. The odor's strength is its mean response over the recording's KCs, relative to the mean over the 16 odors. The KC's breadth is the number of odors it responds to, or its response summed over the odors, relative to the mean over the KCs that respond. Both are taken from the same recording, with APL output blocked (TNT).

The exponent on the strength was 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5 or 2 and the exponent on the breadth 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1 or 2, with either measure of breadth; the inhibition was either subtracted from the response or added to the criterion, the responses that stay above it keeping their values. That makes 90 forms, of which the one with both exponents at 0 is a uniform inhibition, the same amount off every response.

Two further inhibitions stand beside them. One is given a part of the answer: it sets each odor's response rate to the control flies' own, by keeping the odor's strongest responses, and shows what an inhibition that differs only by odor does once it has every odor's response rate right. The other, an inhibition from KCs of similar tuning, reduces each KC's response to an odor in proportion to the responses to it of the other KCs, weighted by how alike their tuning over the other 15 odors is to its own.

The one constant of a form is set so that the response rate over the recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) becomes the control flies' {{data:ctrl_frac ~ .3f}}, and nothing else is fitted. The predicted distances with APL are the mean over those recordings of the cosine distances of the reduced responses, and the predicted APL effect is that minus the same recordings' own distances. No wiring, no ORN input and no model enter, so [the substituted ORN concentrations](#fn-concentrations) do not bear on this part.

The forms were read as trial means, as the target is made, and with the trial noise removed (the form applied to the single trials of each repeat, at the criterion that gives the control flies' response rate on single trials, and the distances taken across repeats: [the flies' variability across the three repeats](#repeat-structure)), in the recordings' z and in [baseline-noise units](#fn-baseline-noise-units).

What would count was fixed before any run. A form was chosen, by the lowest pattern part, on one half of the recordings and scored on the other half, whose recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) then predict its own control recordings: for two splits of the flies into halves, each in both directions (the first split is that of the earlier searches, [above](#cross-wiring-fit)).

A form beyond a uniform inhibition holds if, in the recordings' z, the chosen form's pattern part on the unseen half is lower than the uniform inhibition's there by 0.005 or more in at least three of the four readings and in their mean, both as trial means and with the trial noise removed, and if the same form with the odors' strengths permuted over the odors gains less than half as much.

From the left: the flies' responses with APL output blocked (TNT) under a uniform inhibition; the same responses under the flies' chosen form; the mean over the eight wirings of the breadth-2 family with its own APL, on raw spike counts; the same wirings' responses with APL off under the flies' chosen form.](results/E87_inhibition_form/E87_forms.png)

**A form holds on recordings it was not chosen on.** On the half that it was not chosen on, the chosen form has a lower pattern part than the uniform inhibition in all four readings, by {{diff:E87/held_out.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;split=0;direction=B->A:uniform_pattern -- E87/held_out.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;split=0;direction=B->A:chosen_pattern ~ .3f}} to {{diff:E87/held_out.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;split=1;direction=B->A:uniform_pattern -- E87/held_out.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;split=1;direction=B->A:chosen_pattern ~ .3f}} as trial means ({{lit:0.013 # results/E87_inhibition_form/verdict_A.json, form_holds.by_reading.trial_means.mean_gain: the mean over the four held-out readings of the uniform inhibition's pattern part minus the chosen form's}} on average) and by {{diff:E87/held_out.csv:unit=z;reading=noise_free;split=0;direction=B->A:uniform_pattern -- E87/held_out.csv:unit=z;reading=noise_free;split=0;direction=B->A:chosen_pattern ~ .3f}} to {{diff:E87/held_out.csv:unit=z;reading=noise_free;split=1;direction=B->A:uniform_pattern -- E87/held_out.csv:unit=z;reading=noise_free;split=1;direction=B->A:chosen_pattern ~ .3f}} with the trial noise removed ({{lit:0.016 # results/E87_inhibition_form/verdict_A.json, form_holds.by_reading.noise_free.mean_gain: the mean over the four held-out readings of the uniform inhibition's pattern part minus the chosen form's}} on average), where 0.005 in three of the four had been set (second table). The same form with the odors' strengths permuted gains {{lit:0.001 # results/E87_inhibition_form/verdict_A.json, form_holds.by_reading.trial_means.perm_mean_gain: the mean over the four held-out readings of the uniform inhibition's pattern part minus that of the chosen form with the odors' strengths permuted (20 permutations each)}} and {{lit:0.005 # results/E87_inhibition_form/verdict_A.json, form_holds.by_reading.noise_free.perm_mean_gain: the mean over the four held-out readings of the uniform inhibition's pattern part minus that of the chosen form with the odors' strengths permuted (20 permutations each)}} on average, less than half as much.

Over 200 further random splits of the flies, each read in both directions as trial means, the chosen form has a pattern part of {{lit:0.042 # mean of column chosen_pattern over the 400 rows of results/E87_inhibition_form/held_out_random.csv}} on the unseen half against {{lit:0.053 # mean of column uniform_pattern over the 400 rows of results/E87_inhibition_form/held_out_random.csv}} for the uniform inhibition on average, and is lower by 0.005 or more in {{lit:97 % # results/E87_inhibition_form/held_out_random.csv: the share of its 400 rows (200 random splits of the flies, both directions; z, trial means) in which uniform_pattern minus chosen_pattern is 0.005 or more}} of the 400 readings. The readings agree on the form: {{lit:all four # results/E87_inhibition_form/held_out.csv: chosen_q is 1 and chosen_p is 0.25 in each of the four rows unit=z, reading=trial_means}} trial-mean readings choose an exponent of {{E87/held_out.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;split=0;direction=A->B:chosen_q ~ .0f}} on the odor's strength and of {{E87/held_out.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;split=0;direction=A->B:chosen_p ~ .2f}} on the KC's breadth, and with the trial noise removed the exponents are {{E87/held_out.csv:unit=z;reading=noise_free;split=0;direction=A->B:chosen_q ~ .1f}} or {{E87/held_out.csv:unit=z;reading=noise_free;split=1;direction=A->B:chosen_q ~ .0f}} on the strength and {{E87/held_out.csv:unit=z;reading=noise_free;split=0;direction=A->B:chosen_p ~ .2f}} or {{E87/held_out.csv:unit=z;reading=noise_free;split=0;direction=B->A:chosen_p ~ .1f}} on the breadth.

The form taken forward, the flies' chosen form below, is the one chosen most often with the trial noise removed: the odor's strength, at the exponent {{E87/held_out.csv:unit=z;reading=noise_free;split=1;direction=A->B:chosen_q ~ .0f}}, times the KC's summed response to the power {{E87/held_out.csv:unit=z;reading=noise_free;split=1;direction=A->B:chosen_p ~ .2f}}, subtracted from the response. On all recordings it leaves a pattern part of {{E87/forms.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;form=sub_q1_p0.25_summed:pattern ~ .3f}} as trial means, where the uniform inhibition leaves {{E87/forms.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;form=sub_q0_p0:pattern ~ .3f}} and the data's floor in this convention is {{E87/apl_free_target.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;form_label=chosen;subset=all:main_floor_pattern ~ .3f}}, and of {{E87/forms.csv:unit=z;reading=noise_free;form=sub_q1_p0.25_summed:pattern ~ .3f}} against {{E87/forms.csv:unit=z;reading=noise_free;form=sub_q0_p0:pattern ~ .3f}} and a floor of {{E87/apl_free_target.csv:unit=z;reading=noise_free;form_label=chosen;subset=all:main_floor_pattern ~ .3f}} with the trial noise removed (first table; the first two panels of the figure). The halves are small, five or six control recordings and three or five with APL output blocked (TNT), which is why the test asked for agreement over the four readings, and why the random splits are given beside them.

**The odor's strength carries the pattern.** An inhibition in proportion to the odor's strength alone, the same for every KC, already leaves {{E87/forms.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;form=sub_q1_p0:pattern ~ .3f}}, as little as the inhibition that is given each odor's response rate outright ({{E87/forms.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;form=per_odor_oracle_sub:pattern ~ .3f}}). With the strengths permuted over the odors the chosen form is back at {{lit:0.041 # mean of column pattern over the 20 rows unit=z, reading=trial_means, which=best, control=strengths of results/E87_inhibition_form/controls.csv (the chosen form on all recordings with the odors' strengths permuted)}} on all recordings. The KC's breadth alone, at the exponent of 2 that the best family's APL has, reaches {{E87/forms.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;form=sub_q0_p2_count:pattern ~ .3f}} and overshoots the mean effect ({{E87/forms.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;form=sub_q0_p2_count:mean ~ +.3f}} for the flies' {{data:apl_effect_thresholded_mean ~ +.3f}}).

A uniform inhibition, for its part, gives most of the flies' mean effect ({{E87/forms.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;form=sub_q0_p0:mean ~ +.3f}}) and little of its pattern: its effect varies too little from pair to pair (first panel of the figure). The mean is thus largely what bringing the response rate down to the control flies' does by itself, and the pattern is what the dependence on the odor adds. An inhibition in proportion to an odor's response over all the KCs is what a single APL that sums the KCs' activity and returns it to all of them would exert, and it is in kind what the models' APL does.

**A dependence on the KC's breadth is asked for in both units, weakly in the recordings' z and strongly in baseline-noise units.** In z the loss on the unseen halves is lower with the breadth dependence than with the best form that has none by {{lit:0.009 # results/E87_inhibition_form/verdict_A.json, breadth_needed.z.mean_gain: the mean over the four held-out readings (z, trial means) of the loss of the best form without a breadth dependence minus the loss of the chosen form}} on average over the four trial-mean readings, where 0.005 had been set, and with the breadths permuted over the KCs the form loses that gain (it is then {{lit:0.001 # results/E87_inhibition_form/verdict_A.json, breadth_needed.z.perm_mean_gain (sign reversed): with the breadths permuted over the responding KCs the chosen form's loss on the unseen halves is higher than that of the best form without a breadth dependence by this much on average}} worse than the form without breadth). In baseline-noise units the chosen exponents on breadth are {{E87/held_out.csv:unit=noise;reading=trial_means;split=1;direction=A->B:chosen_p ~ .2f}} to {{E87/held_out.csv:unit=noise;reading=trial_means;split=1;direction=B->A:chosen_p ~ .0f}} and the loss falls by {{lit:0.063 # results/E87_inhibition_form/verdict_A.json, breadth_needed.noise.mean_gain: the same in baseline-noise units}}.

The z-score divides the values of a KC that responds broadly by a larger standard deviation and so already holds a part of such a dependence; in fixed units the inhibition has to grow with breadth to give the flies' mean effect at all: {{data:noise_apl_effect_thresholded_mean ~ +.3f}} in the flies, {{E87/forms.csv:unit=noise;reading=trial_means;form=sub_q0_p0:mean ~ +.3f}} under a uniform inhibition and {{E87/forms.csv:unit=noise;reading=trial_means;form=sub_q1_p1_count:mean ~ +.3f}} with both exponents at 1. Breadth-weighted APL, which the best family has as an assumption with no measurement behind it, thus has some support in the KC data, at exponents on a KC's summed response or number of odors that are in most readings well below the 2 that the family has on a KC's spike total.

The six recordings that are alike, taken by themselves, choose the same exponents as all eight (pattern part {{E87/recordings.csv:unit=z;subset=six_typical:best_pattern ~ .3f}} against {{E87/recordings.csv:unit=z;subset=six_typical:uniform_pattern ~ .3f}} for the uniform inhibition). The two strongest recordings, together or each alone, choose a larger exponent on the breadth, {{E87/recordings.csv:unit=z;subset=alone_2024-07-17_3_L:best_p ~ .0f}} to {{E87/recordings.csv:unit=z;subset=two_strongest:best_p ~ .0f}}, and so do {{lit:two # results/E87_inhibition_form/recordings.csv: of the six rows unit=z, subset=alone_... of the recordings that are alike, those with best_p of 1 or more (2024-08-07_3_L and 2024-08-14_3_L)}} of the other six when taken alone; a form chosen on one or two recordings is chosen in sample, so this is noted and not tested.

**Inhibition among KCs of similar tuning is not what the recordings show.** It moves the odor pairs with near-identical ORN input apart far more than the flies do: the four nearest ester pairs get an APL effect of {{E87/forms.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;form=similar_pow1:near4 ~ +.3f}} where the flies have {{lit:+0.182 # mean of column effect over the four nearest ester pairs (2h with IaA, 2h with pa, IaA with pa, eb with ep), rows unit=z, reading=trial_means, form=data of results/E87_inhibition_form/forms_pairs.csv}} and the chosen form gives {{E87/forms.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;form=sub_q1_p0.25_summed:near4 ~ +.3f}}. Its pattern part on all recordings, {{E87/forms.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;form=similar_pow1:pattern ~ .3f}}, is no better than that of no inhibition at all ({{E87/forms.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;form=none:pattern ~ .3f}}), and on unseen halves it is {{lit:0.031 # results/E87_inhibition_form/verdict_A.json, similar_counts.mean_gain (sign reversed): the mean over the eight held-out readings in z (trial means and trial noise removed) of the similar-tuning form's pattern part minus the chosen form's}} worse than the chosen form on average, where 0.003 better had been set for it to count (last column of each half of the second table). What holds near-identical odors apart in the flies with APL is reproduced, in their own responses, by an inhibition that all KCs share, without one aimed at the KCs that respond alike.

**The models through the same inhibition.** The forms were then applied to the models' responses with APL off exactly as to the flies': the eight wirings of the breadth-2 family, each at its own APL-effect fit ([above](#wiring-population)), and the four wirings fitted with the firing ceiling at its literature setting, as raw spike counts (a response two or more spikes) and through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout), with the constant set so that the response rate becomes the model's own with APL on, and a family read as the mean over its wirings. With the model's own APL beside, this makes a two-by-two against the flies' effect with the trial noise removed, the reading that a model without trial noise is set against: whose responses, the flies' or the model's, by which inhibition (table below; the third and fourth panels of the figure).

The test had been fixed beforehand on the breadth-2 family's pattern part, under either reading of its counts. The error is in the model's responses without APL if the flies' chosen form on the model's responses is not lower than the model's own APL by 0.004 or more while the same form on the flies' own responses is lower than the model's own APL by 0.010 or more. It is in the form of the model's APL if the flies' chosen form on the model's responses is lower than the model's own APL by 0.006 or more for the family and on at least six of its eight wirings.

Whose responses and which inhibition: the per-pair APL effect of each combination against the flies' effect with the trial noise removed (the recordings' z, sub-threshold responses set to 0). A model is the mean over the wirings of its family; two values in a cell are on raw spike counts / through the calibrated readout. The flies' columns do not depend on the model and are repeated in the last two rows

| | | the flies' responses with APL output blocked (TNT) {span=2} | the model's responses with APL off {span=3} |

**By this reading the models' error is in their responses without APL.** On the flies' responses the flies' chosen form leaves a pattern part of {{E87/two_by_two.csv:family=b2;readout=raw;data_reading=noise_free;responses=flies;inhibition=chosen:pattern ~ .3f}}, against a floor of {{E87/apl_free_target.csv:unit=z;reading=noise_free;form_label=chosen;subset=all:main_floor_pattern ~ .3f}}. On the breadth-2 family's responses with APL off it leaves {{E87/two_by_two.csv:family=b2;readout=raw;data_reading=noise_free;responses=model;inhibition=chosen:pattern ~ .3f}} on raw counts and {{E87/two_by_two.csv:family=b2;readout=cal;data_reading=noise_free;responses=model;inhibition=chosen:pattern ~ .3f}} through the readout, where the family's own APL leaves {{E87/two_by_two.csv:family=b2;readout=raw;data_reading=noise_free;responses=model;inhibition=own:pattern ~ .3f}} and {{E87/two_by_two.csv:family=b2;readout=cal;data_reading=noise_free;responses=model;inhibition=own:pattern ~ .3f}}: {{diff:E87/two_by_two.csv:family=b2;readout=raw;data_reading=noise_free;responses=model;inhibition=own:pattern -- E87/two_by_two.csv:family=b2;readout=raw;data_reading=noise_free;responses=model;inhibition=chosen:pattern ~ .3f}} lower than the model's own APL on raw counts and {{diff:E87/two_by_two.csv:family=b2;readout=cal;data_reading=noise_free;responses=model;inhibition=chosen:pattern -- E87/two_by_two.csv:family=b2;readout=cal;data_reading=noise_free;responses=model;inhibition=own:pattern ~ .3f}} higher through the readout, while on the flies' own responses the form is {{diff:E87/two_by_two.csv:family=b2;readout=raw;data_reading=noise_free;responses=model;inhibition=own:pattern -- E87/two_by_two.csv:family=b2;readout=raw;data_reading=noise_free;responses=flies;inhibition=chosen:pattern ~ .3f}} and {{diff:E87/two_by_two.csv:family=b2;readout=cal;data_reading=noise_free;responses=model;inhibition=own:pattern -- E87/two_by_two.csv:family=b2;readout=cal;data_reading=noise_free;responses=flies;inhibition=chosen:pattern ~ .3f}} lower than the model's own APL. By the test the error is in the model's responses without APL, under both readings of the counts, and the family with the firing ceiling reads the same (last two rows).

The single wirings are less even. On raw counts the flies' chosen form is below the wiring's own APL on each of the eight, by more than the 0.006 set, {{diff:E87/model_forms.csv:family=b2;readout=raw;inhibition=own;unit=P2;data_reading=noise_free:pattern -- E87/model_forms.csv:family=b2;readout=raw;inhibition=chosen;unit=P2;data_reading=noise_free:pattern ~ .3f}} to {{diff:E87/model_forms.csv:family=b2;readout=raw;inhibition=own;unit=M3;data_reading=noise_free:pattern -- E87/model_forms.csv:family=b2;readout=raw;inhibition=chosen;unit=M3;data_reading=noise_free:pattern ~ .3f}}, a single wiring's own APL reading far worse in this convention than the mean over the wirings does ({{E87/model_forms.csv:family=b2;readout=raw;inhibition=own;unit=P2;data_reading=noise_free:pattern ~ .3f}} to {{E87/model_forms.csv:family=b2;readout=raw;inhibition=own;unit=real;data_reading=noise_free:pattern ~ .3f}} against {{E87/two_by_two.csv:family=b2;readout=raw;data_reading=noise_free;responses=model;inhibition=own:pattern ~ .3f}}); through the readout it is below, by 0.006 or more, on {{lit:five # results/E87_inhibition_form/verdict_B.json, by_readout.cal.n_wirings_chosen_lower: on 5 of the 8 wirings the pattern part of the flies' chosen form on the wiring's responses with APL off is lower than that of the wiring's own APL by 0.006 or more, through the calibrated readout}} of the eight. The part of the test on the wirings was thus met on raw counts and the part on the family was not, and the family is what the common error is defined on.

The verdict is that of the mean over the eight wirings and not of every subset: for the mean over the four wirings of the earlier searches alone, the flies' chosen form is {{diff:E87/two_by_two_D2.csv:arm=unchanged;readout=raw;unit=S;inhibition=own;data_reading=noise_free:pattern -- E87/two_by_two_D2.csv:arm=unchanged;readout=raw;unit=S;inhibition=chosen;data_reading=noise_free:pattern ~ .3f}} below the four wirings' own APL on raw counts, on {{lit:all four # results/E87_inhibition_form/verdict_B_D2.json, unchanged_raw.n_wirings_gain: on 4 of the 4 wirings the form is lower than the own APL by 0.006 or more}} of them, and {{diff:E87/two_by_two_D2.csv:arm=unchanged;readout=cal;unit=S;inhibition=chosen;data_reading=noise_free:pattern -- E87/two_by_two_D2.csv:arm=unchanged;readout=cal;unit=S;inhibition=own;data_reading=noise_free:pattern ~ .3f}} above it through the readout (the last rows of the table on those four wirings, further down).

**As far as one of these forms can stand in for it, the model's APL would do on the flies' responses nearly what the flies' chosen form does, through the readout only.** The model's APL is not one of these forms. The form whose result on the family's responses with APL off is nearest the family's own distances with APL on still differs from them by {{E87/two_by_two.csv:family=b2;readout=cal;data_reading=noise_free;responses=flies;inhibition=nearest_to_model:nearest_rms ~ .3f}} through the readout, as a root mean square over the pairs, which is of the size of the pattern parts themselves, so it stands in for the model's APL only loosely.

Through the readout that form has the exponents {{lit:1 # results/E87_inhibition_form/verdict_B.json, by_readout.cal.nearest_form: sub_q1_p0.5_count, the exponent on the odor's strength}} on the odor's strength and {{lit:0.5 # results/E87_inhibition_form/verdict_B.json, by_readout.cal.nearest_form: sub_q1_p0.5_count, the exponent on the number of odors the KC responds to}} on the KC's number of odors, close to the flies' chosen form, and applied to the flies' responses it leaves a pattern part of {{E87/two_by_two.csv:family=b2;readout=cal;data_reading=noise_free;responses=flies;inhibition=nearest_to_model:pattern ~ .3f}}. On raw counts the nearest form has the exponents {{lit:2 and 0.5 # results/E87_inhibition_form/verdict_B.json, by_readout.raw.nearest_form: sub_q2_p0.5_summed, the exponents on the odor's strength and on the summed response of the KC}}, is as far from the model's APL ({{E87/two_by_two.csv:family=b2;readout=raw;data_reading=noise_free;responses=flies;inhibition=nearest_to_model:nearest_rms ~ .3f}}) and leaves {{E87/two_by_two.csv:family=b2;readout=raw;data_reading=noise_free;responses=flies;inhibition=nearest_to_model:pattern ~ .3f}} on the flies' responses. This is weaker evidence than the two-by-two, and it points the same way through the readout and not on raw counts.

**The esters show where the responses differ.** Under each inhibition of this kind that was read on the models, their APL effect among 2h, IaA, pa, eb, ep and ms stays too small. Under the flies' chosen form the mean error over the 15 pairs is {{E87/two_by_two.csv:family=b2;readout=raw;data_reading=noise_free;responses=model;inhibition=chosen:err_ester ~ +.3f}} on the breadth-2 family's raw counts and {{E87/two_by_two.csv:family=b2;readout=cal;data_reading=noise_free;responses=model;inhibition=chosen:err_ester ~ +.3f}} through the readout, and {{E87/two_by_two.csv:family=fc;readout=raw;data_reading=noise_free;responses=model;inhibition=chosen:err_ester ~ +.3f}} in the family with the firing ceiling, where the same form on the flies' responses leaves {{E87/two_by_two.csv:family=b2;readout=raw;data_reading=noise_free;responses=flies;inhibition=chosen:err_ester ~ +.3f}}; on raw counts the model's own APL leaves less of this error ({{E87/two_by_two.csv:family=b2;readout=raw;data_reading=noise_free;responses=model;inhibition=own:err_ester ~ +.3f}}) than any of the forms read on the model.

Even the form of the grid that suits the breadth-2 family best, picked on the family against the flies' effect itself, leaves a pattern part of {{E87/two_by_two.csv:family=b2;readout=raw;data_reading=noise_free;responses=model;inhibition=best_grid:pattern ~ .3f}} on raw counts and {{E87/two_by_two.csv:family=b2;readout=cal;data_reading=noise_free;responses=model;inhibition=best_grid:pattern ~ .3f}} through the readout, with {{E87/two_by_two.csv:family=b2;readout=raw;data_reading=noise_free;responses=model;inhibition=best_grid:err_ester ~ +.3f}} and {{E87/two_by_two.csv:family=b2;readout=cal;data_reading=noise_free;responses=model;inhibition=best_grid:err_ester ~ +.3f}} of the error among the esters left. The four nearest ester pairs get an APL effect of {{E87/two_by_two.csv:family=b2;readout=raw;data_reading=noise_free;responses=model;inhibition=chosen:near4 ~ +.3f}} and {{E87/two_by_two.csv:family=b2;readout=cal;data_reading=noise_free;responses=model;inhibition=chosen:near4 ~ +.3f}} under the flies' chosen form on the model's responses and of {{E87/two_by_two.csv:family=b2;readout=raw;data_reading=noise_free;responses=flies;inhibition=chosen:near4 ~ +.3f}} on the flies', where the flies have {{lit:+0.181 # mean of column effect over the four nearest ester pairs (2h with IaA, 2h with pa, IaA with pa, eb with ep), rows unit=z, reading=noise_free, form=data of results/E87_inhibition_form/forms_pairs.csv}}. In the model, then, the KCs that the esters share respond with APL off in a way that no inhibition by the odor's strength and the KC's breadth that was tried separates, and in the flies they do not.

**Put into the model in place of its APL, the flies' form does worse than the model's own APL.** The two-by-two applies a form to a model's spike counts. To see what a form does as inhibition inside the model, five forms were simulated on the eight wirings of the breadth-2 family.

APL was removed, the KC–KC inhibition kept as fitted, and each KC's threshold for each odor multiplied by one plus a constant times the form, with the odor's strength and the KC's breadth taken from the wiring's own run with APL off and the constant searched until the number of responses was that of the wiring's fit with APL on, to within two responses; the run with APL off is the fit's own.

The forms were scored on the main target as measured, as the wirings' own fits are (table above). A form was to count as better than the family's APL if the pattern part of the mean over the eight wirings fell by 0.003 or more, on at least six of the wirings, inside the realism bands and without the loss on raw counts rising by more than 0.005, and as worse if the pattern part rose by 0.003 or more.

Every form is worse. The flies' chosen form comes nearest, with a pattern part of {{E87/readings_D.csv:form_label=chosen;readout=cal;unit=all8:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} against {{E87/readings_D.csv:form_label=chosen;readout=cal;unit=all8:unchanged_z8_pattern ~ .4f}} for the family's own APL, a mean effect of {{E87/readings_D.csv:form_label=chosen;readout=cal;unit=all8:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} against {{E87/readings_D.csv:form_label=chosen;readout=cal;unit=all8:unchanged_mean_effect ~ +.3f}} and a loss on raw counts of {{E87/readings_D.csv:form_label=chosen;readout=raw;unit=all8:z8_loss ~ .3f}} against {{E87/readings_D.csv:form_label=chosen;readout=raw;unit=all8:unchanged_z8_loss ~ .3f}}. A uniform rise of every threshold is the worst, and its per-pair effect is anti-correlated with the flies' (ρ on the per-pair APL effect {{E87/readings_D.csv:form_label=uniform;readout=cal;unit=all8:z8_rho ~ .2f}}).

Nor do the simulations follow the reading on the counts. For that reading to stand in for a simulation, the two per-pair effects of the family, both on raw counts, had to correlate at Pearson r 0.8 or more for each form; they correlate at {{lit:0.60 # results/E87_inhibition_form/verdict_D.json, chosen.proxy_r: the Pearson correlation over the 120 pairs between the simulated per-pair APL effect of the mean over the eight wirings on raw counts and the effect of the same form applied to their raw spike counts with APL off}} for the flies' chosen form, at {{lit:0.40 # results/E87_inhibition_form/verdict_D.json, q1_p1.proxy_r: the Pearson correlation over the 120 pairs between the simulated per-pair APL effect of the mean over the eight wirings on raw counts and the effect of the same form applied to their raw spike counts with APL off}} and {{lit:0.41 # results/E87_inhibition_form/verdict_D.json, q0_p2.proxy_r: the Pearson correlation over the 120 pairs between the simulated per-pair APL effect of the mean over the eight wirings on raw counts and the effect of the same form applied to their raw spike counts with APL off}} for the two forms with a larger exponent on breadth, and negatively for the two forms without breadth (last row).

A threshold raised in the model changes a KC's spikes through the network, the KC–KC inhibition staying in place, and is not a subtraction from its count. What the two-by-two shows is therefore what an inhibition of this kind does to the model's counts and not what a mechanism of this kind does in the model, and what the simulations add is that no static inhibition of this kind, the flies' own included, does better in the model than its feedback APL.

The inhibitions of this kind are those set by an odor's strength and a KC's breadth. One of another make has since been read, the family's own loss of drive for each KC given back as a fixed inhibition while APL is on: it does not do better than the feedback APL either, and it comes close, at {{E95/equal.csv:variant=C2_bcko:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} to {{E95/equal.csv:variant=C1_bck:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} above the family's pattern part through the calibrated readout on the four wirings of the earlier searches ([APL's inhibition as a static threshold raise per KC](#static-threshold)).

**A target that needs no APL.** What a form does within the flies with APL output blocked (TNT), the distances of their reduced responses minus their own, is itself a per-pair effect, and a model's responses with APL off can be scored against it by putting them through the same form. It is a comparison within each recording and needs no control flies, where the main target is a difference between two groups of flies. For the flies' chosen form the floor of its pattern part is about half the main target's in the same convention, two halves of the flies agree on it far better, and its ceiling is {{E87/apl_free_target.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;form_label=chosen;subset=all:ceiling ~ .2f}} against {{E87/apl_free_target.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;form_label=chosen;subset=all:main_ceiling ~ .2f}} (table above).

The test for using it as a target had been set as a floor of at most half the main target's and a ceiling of 0.90 or more, in both readings. As trial means the floor is {{E87/apl_free_target.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;form_label=chosen;subset=all:floor_pattern ~ .4f}} where the main target's is {{E87/apl_free_target.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;form_label=chosen;subset=all:main_floor_pattern ~ .4f}}, a little more than half, so the test is missed there by a narrow margin; it is passed with the trial noise removed and within the six recordings that are alike. The target is therefore reported and not adopted.

Against it the families are alike and further from its floor than they are from the main target's: the breadth-2 family reads {{E87/apl_free_models.csv:source=b2;readout=raw;unit=population;form_label=chosen;reading=noise_free:pattern ~ .3f}} on raw counts, two and a half times the floor, the family with the firing ceiling {{E87/apl_free_models.csv:source=fc;readout=raw;unit=population;form_label=chosen;reading=noise_free:pattern ~ .3f}}, and the 72 model flies that each have an ORN fly's own input ([above](#input-population)) {{E87/apl_free_models.csv:source=E85_model_flies;readout=raw;unit=population;form_label=chosen;reading=noise_free:pattern ~ .3f}}. Every saved model whose responses with APL off exist for the 16 odors was read against it as well, {{lit:1679 # count of the rows readout=raw of results/E87_inhibition_form/archive_scan.csv that were read without an error}} models of {{lit:75 # count of distinct folders among the rows readout=raw of results/E87_inhibition_form/archive_scan.csv that were read without an error}} experiments, each under both readings of its counts against the breadth-2 fit on the same wiring under the same reading.

A model was to stand out if it read lower than that fit by 0.008 or more, with a mean effect of at least two thirds of the flies' and inside the realism bands. On raw counts none does: the nearest is {{E87/archive_scan.csv:folder=E80_remaining_candidates;variant=C2_B3_throff_noise;readout=raw:gain ~ .3f}} lower. Through the readout {{lit:seven # results/E87_inhibition_form/verdict_C.json, n_standout: 7 rows of archive_scan.csv with standout true, all of them readout=cal}} do.

- {{lit:Six # results/E87_inhibition_form/verdict_C.json, standouts: the six variants C2_B3_... of E80_remaining_candidates, on the real wiring}} of them are the [oracle](#fn-oracle) runs of one handle, in which each odor's response rates were put on the flies' by a threshold for each odor on the real wiring ([the flies' pulse in the model and the remaining candidates for the common error](#remaining-candidates)): they read {{E87/archive_scan.csv:folder=E80_remaining_candidates;variant=C2_B3_thr_noise;readout=cal:noise_free_pattern ~ .3f}} to {{E87/archive_scan.csv:folder=E80_remaining_candidates;variant=C2_B3_throff_noise;readout=cal:noise_free_pattern ~ .3f}} against {{E87/archive_scan.csv:folder=E80_remaining_candidates;variant=C2_B3_thr_noise;readout=cal:b2_same_wiring_pattern ~ .3f}} for the breadth-2 fit there.
- The seventh is a fit from the replication of the structure-loss joint fits on re-drawn wiring, on one claw permutation ({{E87/archive_scan.csv:folder=E30_wiring_replication;variant=wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed2_k2;readout=cal:noise_free_pattern ~ .3f}} against {{E87/archive_scan.csv:folder=E30_wiring_replication;variant=wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed2_k2;readout=cal:b2_same_wiring_pattern ~ .3f}} for the breadth-2 fit on that wiring), a different fit and not a handle that can be put on the family.

How many KCs each odor recruits without APL is thus a part of what this target asks. How a saved model reads on the target says little about its own APL-effect loss (a Spearman correlation of {{lit:0.31 # Spearman correlation between columns noise_free_pattern and own_apl_loss over the 1489 rows readout=raw of results/E87_inhibition_form/archive_scan.csv that have both}} between the two over the saved models).
