**The one saved handle that stands out against the target without APL reaches that target and not the main one.** Because the stand-outs come from a handle that the model has, that handle was run, as had been fixed for that case, on the four wirings of the earlier searches (the real wiring, two claw permutations and one matched shuffle), each at its breadth-2 APL-effect fit.

The handle is an [oracle](#fn-oracle) for how many KCs each odor recruits: a threshold for each odor that puts the odor's response rate with APL off on that of the flies with APL output blocked (TNT), counted in baseline-noise units. It has three arms: the thresholds in both conditions, with the fit's APL; the thresholds with APL off only, the run with APL on being the fit's own; and the thresholds together with an APL scale for each odor that puts its response rate with APL on on the control flies'.

On the real wiring these are the runs of the earlier experiment, which they reproduce. They were read on the target without APL, and on the main target by the test that the fitted changes had been put to ([above](#cross-wiring-fit)), here against all recordings since nothing was searched on a half: the pattern part of the mean over the four wirings lower by 0.003 or more through the readout and lower on at least three of the four wirings; the loss on raw counts no more than 0.005 higher, the mean effect within 0.01 of the flies' and every run inside the realism bands; and 15 % of the squared pattern error removed (table above).

On the target without APL the handle does what the saved runs showed. The mean over the four wirings comes from {{E87/readings_D2.csv:arm=thr;readout=cal;unit=S:c1_unchanged_pattern ~ .3f}} to {{E87/readings_D2.csv:arm=thr;readout=cal;unit=S:c1_pattern ~ .3f}}, {{E87/readings_D2.csv:arm=throff;readout=cal;unit=S:c1_pattern ~ .3f}} and {{E87/readings_D2.csv:arm=thrapl;readout=cal;unit=S:c1_pattern ~ .3f}} through the readout in the three arms, and from {{E87/readings_D2.csv:arm=thr;readout=raw;unit=S:c1_unchanged_pattern ~ .3f}} to {{E87/readings_D2.csv:arm=thr;readout=raw;unit=S:c1_pattern ~ .3f}}, {{E87/readings_D2.csv:arm=throff;readout=raw;unit=S:c1_pattern ~ .3f}} and {{E87/readings_D2.csv:arm=thrapl;readout=raw;unit=S:c1_pattern ~ .3f}} on raw counts, where the floor is {{E87/apl_free_target.csv:unit=z;reading=noise_free;form_label=chosen;subset=all:floor_pattern ~ .3f}}. With the thresholds in both conditions each of the four wirings moves, by {{diff:E87/readings_D2.csv:arm=thr;readout=cal;unit=P1:c1_unchanged_pattern -- E87/readings_D2.csv:arm=thr;readout=cal;unit=P1:c1_pattern ~ .3f}} to {{diff:E87/readings_D2.csv:arm=thr;readout=cal;unit=real:c1_unchanged_pattern -- E87/readings_D2.csv:arm=thr;readout=cal;unit=real:c1_pattern ~ .3f}} through the readout. In the other two arms one claw permutation hardly moves through the readout ({{E87/readings_D2.csv:arm=throff;readout=cal;unit=P1:c1_pattern ~ .3f}} and {{E87/readings_D2.csv:arm=thrapl;readout=cal;unit=P1:c1_pattern ~ .3f}} for {{E87/readings_D2.csv:arm=thrapl;readout=cal;unit=P1:c1_unchanged_pattern ~ .3f}} unchanged) and the other three wirings fall; on raw counts {{lit:every wiring falls in every arm # results/E87_inhibition_form/readings_D2.csv: c1_pattern is below c1_unchanged_pattern in all 12 rows readout=raw of the single wirings real, P1, P2 and M1}}.

On the main target the test fails in every arm. The pattern part of the mean over the four wirings rises, from {{E87/readings_D2.csv:arm=thr;readout=cal;unit=S:unchanged_z8_pattern ~ .4f}} to {{E87/readings_D2.csv:arm=thr;readout=cal;unit=S:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, {{E87/readings_D2.csv:arm=throff;readout=cal;unit=S:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} and {{E87/readings_D2.csv:arm=thrapl;readout=cal;unit=S:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, it is lower on none of the four wirings in any arm, and the squared pattern error grows; on raw counts the pattern part falls by {{diff:E87/readings_D2.csv:arm=throff;readout=raw;unit=S:unchanged_z8_pattern -- E87/readings_D2.csv:arm=throff;readout=raw;unit=S:z8_pattern ~ .3f}} at most. In two of the arms the error among 2h, IaA, pa, eb, ep and ms is a little smaller than unchanged ({{E87/readings_D2.csv:arm=throff;readout=cal;unit=S:z8_err_ester ~ +.3f}} and {{E87/readings_D2.csv:arm=thrapl;readout=cal;unit=S:z8_err_ester ~ +.3f}} for {{E87/readings_D2.csv:arm=thr;readout=cal;unit=S:unchanged_z8_err_ester ~ +.3f}}) and the pattern part rises all the same, so that what the recruitment takes off the esters it adds on other pairs.

Only the third part of the test holds: the loss on raw counts falls a little, from {{E87/readings_D2.csv:arm=thr;readout=raw;unit=S:unchanged_z8_loss ~ .3f}} to {{E87/readings_D2.csv:arm=thr;readout=raw;unit=S:z8_loss ~ .3f}}, {{E87/readings_D2.csv:arm=throff;readout=raw;unit=S:z8_loss ~ .3f}} and {{E87/readings_D2.csv:arm=thrapl;readout=raw;unit=S:z8_loss ~ .3f}}, the mean effect stays at the flies' and every run is inside the realism bands. The earlier experiment had found on the real wiring that how many KCs each odor recruits when APL is removed is no lever on the main target; that now holds on four wirings.

**So the two targets part ways.** The flies' chosen form inhibits in proportion to each odor's response over all the KCs, so what it does within a fly depends first on how many KCs each odor recruits without APL. A model that is given that recruitment comes a third to a half of the way to the flies on the target without APL, and the pattern of its own APL effect is then no nearer the flies'. The target without APL thus measures the model's responses in one respect, which the main target does not reward in this family, and it is not a screen by itself: a change on the side of the responses has to be read on both targets, the one without APL for the responses and the main one for what the model's APL makes of them.

**With the flies' recruitment, a part of what is left is read on the side of the model's APL.** The two-by-two was read again on these four wirings, unchanged and with the recruitment set (last three rows of the table). With each odor's recruitment on the flies', the flies' chosen form on the model's responses with APL off leaves a pattern part of {{E87/two_by_two_D2.csv:arm=throff;readout=raw;unit=S;inhibition=chosen;data_reading=noise_free:pattern ~ .3f}} to {{E87/two_by_two_D2.csv:arm=thr;readout=raw;unit=S;inhibition=chosen;data_reading=noise_free:pattern ~ .3f}} on raw counts and of {{E87/two_by_two_D2.csv:arm=thr;readout=cal;unit=S;inhibition=chosen;data_reading=noise_free:pattern ~ .3f}} to {{E87/two_by_two_D2.csv:arm=throff;readout=cal;unit=S;inhibition=chosen;data_reading=noise_free:pattern ~ .3f}} through the readout in the three arms, where the model's own APL leaves {{E87/two_by_two_D2.csv:arm=throff;readout=raw;unit=S;inhibition=own;data_reading=noise_free:pattern ~ .3f}} to {{E87/two_by_two_D2.csv:arm=thrapl;readout=raw;unit=S;inhibition=own;data_reading=noise_free:pattern ~ .3f}}.

The form is lower than the model's own APL by {{diff:E87/two_by_two_D2.csv:arm=throff;readout=raw;unit=S;inhibition=own;data_reading=noise_free:pattern -- E87/two_by_two_D2.csv:arm=throff;readout=raw;unit=S;inhibition=chosen;data_reading=noise_free:pattern ~ .3f}} to {{diff:E87/two_by_two_D2.csv:arm=thrapl;readout=raw;unit=S;inhibition=own;data_reading=noise_free:pattern -- E87/two_by_two_D2.csv:arm=thrapl;readout=raw;unit=S;inhibition=chosen;data_reading=noise_free:pattern ~ .3f}} on raw counts and by {{diff:E87/two_by_two_D2.csv:arm=thrapl;readout=cal;unit=S;inhibition=own;data_reading=noise_free:pattern -- E87/two_by_two_D2.csv:arm=thrapl;readout=cal;unit=S;inhibition=chosen;data_reading=noise_free:pattern ~ .3f}} to {{diff:E87/two_by_two_D2.csv:arm=thr;readout=cal;unit=S;inhibition=own;data_reading=noise_free:pattern -- E87/two_by_two_D2.csv:arm=thr;readout=cal;unit=S;inhibition=chosen;data_reading=noise_free:pattern ~ .3f}} through the readout, more than the 0.006 of the test in every arm, on {{lit:all four # results/E87_inhibition_form/verdict_B_D2.json, thr_raw, throff_raw and thrapl_raw, n_wirings_gain: 4 of the 4 wirings in each arm}} wirings on raw counts and on {{lit:three # results/E87_inhibition_form/verdict_B_D2.json, thr_cal, throff_cal and thrapl_cal, n_wirings_gain: 3 of the 4 wirings in each arm}} of the four through the readout. It is still {{diff:E87/two_by_two_D2.csv:arm=thr;readout=cal;unit=S;inhibition=chosen;data_reading=noise_free:pattern -- E87/two_by_two.csv:family=b2;readout=raw;data_reading=noise_free;responses=flies;inhibition=chosen:pattern ~ .3f}} to {{diff:E87/two_by_two_D2.csv:arm=throff;readout=cal;unit=S;inhibition=chosen;data_reading=noise_free:pattern -- E87/two_by_two.csv:family=b2;readout=raw;data_reading=noise_free;responses=flies;inhibition=chosen:pattern ~ .3f}} above what the same form leaves on the flies' own responses ({{E87/two_by_two.csv:family=b2;readout=raw;data_reading=noise_free;responses=flies;inhibition=chosen:pattern ~ .3f}}).

On responses that recruit as the flies' do, then, the reading on the counts divides what is left: a part stays in the responses, in which KCs respond beyond how many, and a part of about the same size lies between the flies' form and the model's own APL, in what the model's APL makes of those responses. The verdict on the fits as they are, that the error is in the responses, is therefore the verdict for a model that recruits in its own way. It remains a reading on spike counts.

When it was made, the flies' form had been simulated in place of APL only on the fits as they are, where it did worse than the model's own APL; it has since been simulated on this base as well, where it does far worse than the model's own APL and the reading on the counts does not predict the simulation ([the common error split into who responds and how strongly](#responder-sets)).

**Realism.** The reading of the recordings fits nothing to a model and adds no parameter, so its realism is what a form predicts for the control flies beside what they have (last three rows of the first table).

The flies' chosen form gives the control flies' response rate by construction, their per-odor response rates (response rate ρ {{E87/forms.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;form=sub_q1_p0.25_summed:rate_rho ~ .2f}}) and their distribution of the number of odors per KC almost exactly: {{E87/forms.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;form=sub_q1_p0.25_summed:opk_tv ~ .3f}} from the control flies' mean distribution, where the uniform inhibition is at {{E87/forms.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;form=sub_q0_p0:opk_tv ~ .3f}}, the square of the KC's number of odors at {{E87/forms.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;form=sub_q0_p2_count:opk_tv ~ .3f}} and the most atypical control recording at {{data:ctrl_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .3f}} from the others. Its responders are a little weaker than the control flies' ({{E87/forms.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;form=sub_q1_p0.25_summed:amp_ratio ~ .2f}} of their mean response). The form that predicts the distances best is thus also the one that makes the control flies' spread of responses over the KCs from the responses with APL output blocked (TNT), with one constant.

What is hard to defend is the operation. The forms are static and act on time-averaged calcium signals; the flies with APL output blocked (TNT) are other animals than the control flies and have lived with the block, so that their responses need not be the control flies' responses without APL; a subtraction in z is not a subtraction of drive, which the divisive kind and the two units bracket; and while an inhibition in proportion to an odor's response over all the KCs is what a single APL that sums the KCs would give, the dependence on a KC's breadth has no measurement of APL behind it.

In the simulations both response rates are the fits' by construction. The ratio of the response rates ({{E87/runs_D.csv:D1_q0_p2_P4:ratio ~ .2f}} to {{E87/runs_D.csv:D1_uniform_P2:ratio ~ .2f}}) and the largest spike counts ({{E87/runs_D.csv:D1_chosen_M3:max_count_on ~ .0f}} to {{E87/runs_D.csv:D1_chosen_real:max_count_on ~ .0f}} per KC and odor with APL on) stay those of the family's fits, and the number of odors per KC stays inside its band, at the edge under the uniform rise ({{E87/runs_D.csv:D1_uniform_M3:opk_on_tv ~ .3f}} from the flies' distribution with APL on, against a band of {{data:noise_ctrl_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .3f}}).

{{lit:Eight # count of the 40 rows of results/E87_inhibition_form/runs_D.csv with a realism_flag (all of them the response rate ρ with APL on below 0.37)}} of the 40 runs fall below the band on the response rate ρ with APL on, down to {{E87/runs_D.csv:D1_q1_p1_M3:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}}: both exponents at 1 on four wirings, the flies' chosen form on three and the square of the number of odors on one. Counted by the recordings' own criterion, as the bands counted until 2026-11-10, {{lit:33 # count of the 40 rows of results/E87_inhibition_form/runs_D.csv with a realism_flag_zcrit}} of the 40 are outside a band.

Every one of these runs is worse than the family's APL on the main target, none is recommended for anything, and no mean over wirings was read on the bands. The rise of the thresholds is itself large: the uniform form raises every threshold by {{E87/runs_D.csv:D1_uniform_M2:c ~ .0%}} to {{E87/runs_D.csv:D1_uniform_P3:c ~ .0%}}, and where the breadth enters alone, as the square of the number of odors, the constant is up to {{E87/runs_D.csv:D1_q0_p2_P3:c ~ .1f}} on a factor that is 1 for a KC of mean breadth and 4 for one of twice that.

The runs with each odor's recruitment set are another matter: {{lit:all 12 # results/E87_inhibition_form/runs_D2.csv: none of its 12 rows has a realism_flag or a realism_flag_zcrit; results/E87_inhibition_form/verdict_D2.json, n_flagged 0 in each arm}} are inside the four realism bands, with the flies' responses counted in baseline-noise units and by the recordings' own criterion alike. The response rates with APL off are the flies' for each odor by construction, the response rate with APL on, which nothing holds where the thresholds act in both conditions, is {{E87/runs_D2.csv:D2_b3_thr_noise_P2:rate_on ~ .3f}} to {{E87/runs_D2.csv:D2_b3_thr_noise_M1:rate_on ~ .3f}} there, the ratio of the response rates is {{E87/runs_D2.csv:D2_b3_thr_noise_M1:ratio ~ .2f}} to {{E87/runs_D2.csv:D2_b3_thr_noise_P2:ratio ~ .2f}}, the response rate ρ with APL on is {{E87/runs_D2.csv:D2_b3_throff_noise_P1:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}} or more, and the number of odors per KC is at most {{E87/runs_D2.csv:D2_b3_thr_noise_P2:opk_on_tv ~ .3f}} from the flies' distribution with APL on and {{E87/runs_D2.csv:D2_b3_thr_noise_real:opk_off_tv ~ .3f}} with APL off. They are oracles all the same.

The thresholds differ between the odors by factors of {{E87/runs_D2.csv:D2_b3_thr_noise_M1:thr_min ~ .2f}} to {{E87/runs_D2.csv:D2_b3_thr_noise_P1:thr_max ~ .2f}}, set from the flies' response rates and from nothing in the model; where an APL scale is set for each odor it ranges from {{E87/runs_D2.csv:D2_b3_thrapl_noise_real:apl_min ~ .2f}} to {{E87/runs_D2.csv:D2_b3_thrapl_noise_M1:apl_max ~ .1f}} times the fit's, which no measurement supports; and with the thresholds in both conditions the largest spike count with APL on rises to {{E87/runs_D2.csv:D2_b3_thr_noise_P1:max_count_on ~ .0f}} on one wiring.

The parts on the models carry, as everywhere, paa, euc and -aPine at [ORN input of another concentration](#fn-concentrations). Nothing was gained on the main target in the model here, so nothing was bought with the bands; what the recruitment gains on the target without APL is an oracle's, inside the bands.

**What follows.** The common error is restated in part. On the spike counts of the fits as they are, the flies' APL effect is, to within what the recordings resolve, what an inhibition that grows with an odor's response over all the KCs makes of the flies' responses without APL, which is in kind what the models' APL does, and the same inhibition makes no more of the models' responses than their own APL does.

By that reading the models miss the effect first because their KCs' responses without APL are not the flies', among the esters above all, and the earlier reading that most of the common error lies in what APL does to particular pairs ([the input side of the error common to all wirings](#input-side)) is narrowed to which KCs respond without APL and how strongly, which the distances with APL off do not show. Three results bound the reading.

- It is an operation on spike counts, which the simulated forms do not follow pair by pair.
- It is the verdict of the mean over the eight wirings: on single wirings, and for the four wirings of the earlier searches as a mean, the flies' form does better than the model's own APL on raw counts.
- And it holds for a model that recruits in its own way: with each odor's recruitment without APL set to the flies', the pattern of the model's own APL effect is no nearer the flies', and the flies' form on those responses does better than the model's own APL, so that a part of what is left is then on the side of the model's APL.

The error is therefore not closed onto one side, and neither side alone has reached the main target here: not the flies' form in place of the model's APL on the model's own responses, and not the flies' recruitment with the model's own APL. The two together, the flies' form simulated on a base with the flies' recruitment, have since been run, and do far worse than the model's own APL does on either base ([below](#responder-sets)).

A mechanism that changes the responses without APL is read on both targets, the one without APL for the responses and the main one for what the model's APL makes of them. Changes on APL's side are not the lead on the fits as they are and are not excluded; where they are taken up, it is on a base with the flies' recruitment. The shortfall on the odor pairs with near-identical ORN input ([above](#input-population)) is of a piece with this: in the flies a shared inhibition holds those pairs apart, and an inhibition among KCs of similar tuning, the kind that would hold near-identical inputs apart in a model, is not what the recordings show.

Breadth-weighted APL keeps its place in the family, with some support from the KC data and at a smaller exponent than the family's; in the family itself a smaller exponent has since cost the main target, on the fits as they are and on a base with the flies' recruitment ([below](#breadth-weighting)); with APL's inhibition summed over a KC's claws, an exponent of 1 on that base has since read lower than the base's own family, by half of what the test set for it asks ([below](#summed-drive)).

The effect of the form within a fly is given beside the main target for later models; whether it is given a place in fits is not decided, and by itself it would reward the per-odor recruitment. What is taken up from here is with the pending work at the end of the page.

### The common error split into who responds and how strongly: whether the error lies in which KCs respond to each odor or in how strongly the shared responders respond, what the model's APL does to the responder sets, and whether the flies' form of inhibition does better once the model recruits as the flies do {#responder-sets}

%%% hover
co-response: Of two odors, how many times more often a KC responds to both than it would if the two odors' responders were independent of each other: the share of the KCs that respond to both, divided by the product of the two odors' response rates. It is 1 at chance. One of the three factors of a pair's similarity when responses below the criterion are set to 0; see the subsection on the common error split into who responds and how strongly.
amplitude factor: Of two odors, the similarity of their responses divided by the similarity of the same responses reduced to responding or not: the mean product of the shared responders' two responses, divided by the product of the root-mean-square responses of each odor's own responders. It is 1 when all responders respond equally strongly. One of the three factors of a pair's similarity when responses below the criterion are set to 0.
base with the flies' recruitment: The four wirings of the earlier searches, each at its breadth-2 APL-effect fit, with a threshold for each odor that puts the odor's response rate with APL off on that of the flies with APL output blocked (TNT), counted in baseline-noise units, and, where the model's own APL acts on it, an APL scale for each odor that puts the response rate with APL on on the control flies'. It stands in for a mechanism that would give the flies' recruitment, and is not one.
%%%

**With responses below the criterion set to 0, the similarity of two odors is exactly the product of three factors: how many KCs each odor recruits, how many times more often than chance a KC that responds to one odor responds to the other, and how strong the shared responders' responses are.** The first two say who responds, the third how strongly.

Putting the flies' factors into the models' product one at a time points to who responds: with the flies' responder sets and its own amplitudes the breadth-2 family has less than half of its pattern error left, and with the flies' amplitudes on its own responder sets it keeps most of it. By the test fixed beforehand this is not a verdict. On a model whose values without noise are known, the second factor is not estimated well enough through the trial noise, and against the six recordings that are alike the two readings disagree, so the split stands as a description. Four results stand beside it.

- In the model the two factors of who responds offset each other, each taken alone from the flies making the pattern worse, which would explain why setting each odor's recruitment to the flies' had moved nothing.
- The alcohols' responders that survive APL are shared more often than before in the flies, and less so in the models.
- The KCs that the model's APL removes although a cut by amplitude would keep them are the broadly responding KCs that its breadth weighting loads.
- And the flies' form of inhibition, simulated in place of APL on a base with the flies' recruitment, does far worse than the model's own APL, so that static inhibitions of this kind are closed on both bases.

The form of APL's inhibition in the flies' own responses had read the common error, on the spike counts of the fits as they are, as lying first in the models' responses without APL, and had left two things open ([above](#inhibition-form)). One was which respect of the responses carries the error. The other was a simulation: the flies' chosen form in place of APL on responses that recruit as the flies' do, since the readings on spike counts had not predicted the simulations on the fits as they are. The first question has an exact form, and it needs no simulation.

A response is a value above the criterion, and values not above it are set to 0, as in the readings of the flies' own responses above. The similarity of two odors, one minus the cosine distance of their responses over the KCs, is then exactly the product of three factors.

- The pair's recruitment is the geometric mean of the two odors' response rates.
- The co-response is how many times more often a KC responds to both odors than it would if the two odors' responders were independent of each other.
- The amplitude factor is the similarity of the responses divided by the similarity of the same responses reduced to responding or not; it says how strong the shared responders' two responses are against those of each odor's own responders.

Recruitment and co-response together are the responder sets, who responds, and the amplitude factor is how strongly. A pair's APL effect is its similarity with APL off minus its similarity with APL on, the fall of the product when APL acts.

The flies' factors were put into a model's product in place of the model's own, in both conditions: the two factors of who responds, the amplitude factor, the recruitment alone and the co-response alone. Each such combination was scored against the flies' per-pair APL effect as a model is, with the 15 pairs among 2h, IaA, pa, eb, ep and ms (the ester pairs below) and the 6 pairs among 1-8ol, 1-5ol, 1-6ol and 6al (the alcohol pairs below), the two groups of the common error, read beside the pattern part. A combination holds the flies' own factors, measured in the recordings that make the target, so it is an attribution and not a model, and it can read below the floor that a model is held to; its own floor comes from taking the flies' factors from resampled recordings.

The comparison is fair only if the model is read as the flies are, since trial noise changes which KCs count as responders. Three readings were used. As trial means, the flies' three-trial means at 1 z are set against the model under the per-KC reading, on ten simulated recordings of three trials for each wiring, with the measurement noise that the reading sets on the model's counts (the reading's own noise below).

The same reading was repeated with the model's noise raised until an odor's responder sets agree between two repeats as the flies' do: the mean cosine between the responder sets of two repeats of one odor is {{E88/members.csv:population=b2;wiring=real:mult_on_rel_target ~ .2f}} in the control flies and {{E88/members.csv:population=b2;wiring=real:mult_off_rel_target ~ .2f}} with APL output blocked (TNT), against {{E88/members.csv:population=b2;wiring=M2:mult_on_rel_r1 ~ .2f}} to {{E88/members.csv:population=b2;wiring=P4:mult_on_rel_r1 ~ .2f}} with APL on and {{E88/members.csv:population=b2;wiring=M2:mult_off_rel_r1 ~ .2f}} to {{E88/members.csv:population=b2;wiring=P3:mult_off_rel_r1 ~ .2f}} with APL off on the breadth-2 family's eight wirings at the reading's own noise, and the noise had to be multiplied by {{E88/members.csv:population=b2;wiring=M2:mult_on_mult ~ .1f}} to {{E88/members.csv:population=b2;wiring=P4:mult_on_mult ~ .1f}} with APL on and by {{E88/members.csv:population=b2;wiring=M2:mult_off_mult ~ .1f}} to {{E88/members.csv:population=b2;wiring=P3:mult_off_mult ~ .1f}} with APL off.

With the trial noise removed, the similarities are estimated across repeats in the same way on both sides ([the flies' variability across the three repeats](#repeat-structure)). The model without noise, on raw spike counts and through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout), is given beside them against the flies with the trial noise removed. The models were the breadth-2 family on its eight wirings ([above](#wiring-population)), the family with the firing ceiling on four, and the four wirings of the earlier searches, unchanged and on the base with the flies' recruitment ([above](#inhibition-form)).

What would count was fixed before any run. The model's values without noise are known, so each factor's estimate was first checked against them: a factor whose mean over a group of pairs is off by more than 0.03, in units of the similarity, is not read in that reading.

- The error is in who responds if the flies' responder sets lower the breadth-2 family's pattern part by 0.015 or more and the flies' amplitudes lower it by at most half as much, as trial means and with the trial noise removed alike; it is in how strongly in the reverse case, and in both otherwise.
- A group's error goes with recruitment if the flies' recruitment alone at least halves it and the flies' co-response alone does not, and with the co-response in the reverse case.
- Every verdict is repeated against the six recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) that are alike, and one that changes there is reported as depending on the two strongest recordings ([the data side of the main target](#data-side)).

The estimates checked on the breadth-2 family, whose values without noise are known: the estimate of each factor minus its value without noise, as the mean over a group's pairs that is furthest from 0 among five groups of pairs (the four nearest ester pairs, the six pairs with near-identical ORN input, the ester pairs, the alcohol pairs and the other 99 pairs) and the two conditions, in units of the similarity (0.03 had been set as the most a factor may be off and still be read)

| reading | recruitment | co-response | amplitude factor | similarity |

**The split cannot be read, because the co-response is not estimated well enough.**

Recruitment and the similarity itself are inside the tolerance in both readings that the verdict rests on. The co-response is not. As trial means it is read too low with APL on for the pairs that are nearest each other: its error is {{E88/estimator_check.csv:population=b2;reading=r1;condition=on;factor=L;group=six:err ~ +.3f}} for the six pairs with near-identical ORN input and {{E88/estimator_check.csv:population=b2;reading=r1;condition=on;factor=L;group=nearest4:err ~ +.3f}} for the four nearest ester pairs, while for the ester and the alcohol pairs themselves it is inside the tolerance ({{E88/estimator_check.csv:population=b2;reading=r1;condition=on;factor=L;group=ester:err ~ +.3f}} and {{E88/estimator_check.csv:population=b2;reading=r1;condition=on;factor=L;group=alcohol:err ~ +.3f}}). With the trial noise removed it is read too high in every group but the other 99 pairs, {{E88/estimator_check.csv:population=b2;reading=r2;condition=on;factor=L;group=ester:err ~ +.3f}} and {{E88/estimator_check.csv:population=b2;reading=r2;condition=on;factor=L;group=alcohol:err ~ +.3f}} for the ester and the alcohol pairs with APL on, and the amplitude factor is read too low ({{E88/estimator_check.csv:population=b2;reading=r2;condition=on;factor=G;group=ester:err ~ +.3f}} and {{E88/estimator_check.csv:population=b2;reading=r2;condition=on;factor=G;group=alcohol:err ~ +.3f}}).

At the flies' repeatability the trial-mean estimate of the co-response is off by as much as {{E88/estimator_check.csv:population=b2;reading=r1b;condition=off;factor=L;group=six:err ~ +.3f}}. The errors run opposite ways in the two readings, and they grow with the noise, so the flies' own co-response probably carries an error of this order, which cannot be checked on the flies. By the rule the split is therefore not read, and what follows in this subsection on the factors is description.

**Every reading through the trial noise points to who responds.** With the flies' responder sets and its own amplitudes, the breadth-2 family's pattern part is {{E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r1;subset=all;cell=sets:pattern ~ .3f}} as trial means and {{E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r2;subset=all;cell=sets:pattern ~ .3f}} with the trial noise removed, where its own is {{E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r1;subset=all;cell=own:pattern ~ .3f}} and {{E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r2;subset=all;cell=own:pattern ~ .3f}}; that is at the floor of the combination ({{E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r1;subset=all;cell=sets:floor_pattern ~ .3f}} and {{E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r2;subset=all;cell=sets:floor_pattern ~ .3f}}), so nothing that the recordings resolve is left (first two rows of the table; middle panels of the figure).

With the flies' amplitudes on its own responder sets the family keeps most of its error, {{E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r1;subset=all;cell=amp:pattern ~ .3f}} as trial means and {{E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r2;subset=all;cell=amp:pattern ~ .3f}} with the trial noise removed, against a floor of {{E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r1;subset=all;cell=amp:floor_pattern ~ .3f}} and {{E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r2;subset=all;cell=amp:floor_pattern ~ .3f}} for that combination. The responder sets thus take {{diff:E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r1;subset=all;cell=own:pattern -- E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r1;subset=all;cell=sets:pattern ~ .3f}} and {{diff:E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r2;subset=all;cell=own:pattern -- E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r2;subset=all;cell=sets:pattern ~ .3f}} off the pattern part and the amplitudes {{diff:E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r1;subset=all;cell=own:pattern -- E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r1;subset=all;cell=amp:pattern ~ .3f}} and {{diff:E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r2;subset=all;cell=own:pattern -- E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r2;subset=all;cell=amp:pattern ~ .3f}}, which by the thresholds is who responds in both readings. It is the same at the flies' repeatability, and in the family with the firing ceiling ({{E88/cells.csv:population=fc;reading=r1;subset=all;cell=sets:pattern ~ .3f}} with the flies' responder sets against its own {{E88/cells.csv:population=fc;reading=r1;subset=all;cell=own:pattern ~ .3f}}, trial means). ρ on the per-pair APL effect rises from {{E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r1;subset=all;cell=own:rho ~ .2f}} to {{E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r1;subset=all;cell=sets:rho ~ .2f}} with the flies' responder sets and to {{E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r1;subset=all;cell=amp:rho ~ .2f}} with the flies' amplitudes.

Two things qualify this beside the check on the estimates. On the model without noise the responder sets gain less, {{diff:E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r3raw;subset=all;cell=own:pattern -- E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r3raw;subset=all;cell=sets:pattern ~ .3f}} on raw counts and {{diff:E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r3cal;subset=all;cell=own:pattern -- E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r3cal;subset=all;cell=sets:pattern ~ .3f}} through the calibrated readout against {{diff:E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r3raw;subset=all;cell=own:pattern -- E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r3raw;subset=all;cell=amp:pattern ~ .3f}} and {{diff:E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r3cal;subset=all;cell=own:pattern -- E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r3cal;subset=all;cell=amp:pattern ~ .3f}} for the amplitudes, which by the thresholds is in both. And against the six recordings that are alike the trial means still say who responds ({{E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r1;subset=six;cell=sets:pattern ~ .3f}} against {{E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r1;subset=six;cell=own:pattern ~ .3f}}), while with the trial noise removed the amplitudes gain {{diff:E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r2;subset=six;cell=own:pattern -- E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r2;subset=six;cell=amp:pattern ~ .3f}}, more than half of the responder sets' {{diff:E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r2;subset=six;cell=own:pattern -- E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r2;subset=six;cell=sets:pattern ~ .3f}}, so that the two readings disagree there.

**In the model, recruitment and co-response offset each other.** Each taken alone from the flies makes the pattern part worse: {{E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r1;subset=all;cell=R:pattern ~ .3f}} with the flies' recruitment and {{E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r1;subset=all;cell=L:pattern ~ .3f}} with the flies' co-response, as trial means, against the model's own {{E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r1;subset=all;cell=own:pattern ~ .3f}}.

The two groups of the common error divide between the two factors (last two rows of the table). The flies' recruitment alone takes the ester pairs' error from {{E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r1;subset=all;cell=own:err_ester ~ +.3f}} to {{E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r1;subset=all;cell=R:err_ester ~ +.3f}} and leaves the alcohol pairs' where it was ({{E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r1;subset=all;cell=own:err_alcohol ~ +.3f}} and {{E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r1;subset=all;cell=R:err_alcohol ~ +.3f}}). The flies' co-response alone takes the alcohol pairs' error to {{E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r1;subset=all;cell=L:err_alcohol ~ +.3f}} and leaves the ester pairs' ({{E88/cells.csv:population=b2;reading=r1;subset=all;cell=L:err_ester ~ +.3f}}). By the thresholds the ester pairs' error goes with recruitment and the alcohol pairs' with the co-response, in both readings.

Against the six recordings that are alike the alcohol pairs' error still goes with the co-response; the ester pairs' goes with both factors as trial means and with recruitment with the trial noise removed, so its assignment depends on the two strongest recordings. Read plainly, the two assignments say that APL removes a larger share of the esters' responders in the flies than in the model, and that the alcohols' responders that remain under APL are shared more often in the flies than in the model. Both rest on the estimate of the co-response that the check does not pass.

**With the flies' recruitment given to the model, the co-response is what is left.** Setting each odor's recruitment without APL to the flies' had left the main target where it was ([the flies' pulse in the model and the remaining candidates for the common error](#remaining-candidates); [above](#inhibition-form)). Read by the factors it moves nothing either: as trial means the base with the flies' recruitment has a pattern part of {{E88/cells.csv:population=D2_thrapl;reading=r1;subset=all;cell=own:pattern ~ .3f}} where the unchanged fits of the same four wirings have {{E88/cells.csv:population=S_unchanged;reading=r1;subset=all;cell=own:pattern ~ .3f}}, and {{E88/cells.csv:population=D2_thrapl;reading=r2;subset=all;cell=own:pattern ~ .3f}} against {{E88/cells.csv:population=S_unchanged;reading=r2;subset=all;cell=own:pattern ~ .3f}} with the trial noise removed.

With the flies' co-response in place of its own, the base reads {{E88/cells.csv:population=D2_thrapl;reading=r1;subset=all;cell=L:pattern ~ .3f}} and {{E88/cells.csv:population=D2_thrapl;reading=r2;subset=all;cell=L:pattern ~ .3f}}, lower by {{diff:E88/cells.csv:population=D2_thrapl;reading=r1;subset=all;cell=own:pattern -- E88/cells.csv:population=D2_thrapl;reading=r1;subset=all;cell=L:pattern ~ .3f}} and {{diff:E88/cells.csv:population=D2_thrapl;reading=r2;subset=all;cell=own:pattern -- E88/cells.csv:population=D2_thrapl;reading=r2;subset=all;cell=L:pattern ~ .3f}} where 0.010 had been set, and by {{diff:E88/cells.csv:population=D2_thrapl;reading=r1;subset=six;cell=own:pattern -- E88/cells.csv:population=D2_thrapl;reading=r1;subset=six;cell=L:pattern ~ .3f}} and {{diff:E88/cells.csv:population=D2_thrapl;reading=r2;subset=six;cell=own:pattern -- E88/cells.csv:population=D2_thrapl;reading=r2;subset=six;cell=L:pattern ~ .3f}} against the six recordings that are alike. The oracle for the recruitment sets one of two factors that offset each other in the model, which would explain why it did not help: on the fits as they are the flies' co-response alone makes the pattern worse, and once the recruitment is the flies' it is what remains. This too rests on the estimate of the co-response.

What APL does to who responds: a factor with APL on divided by the same factor with APL off (KC data: the control flies over the flies with APL output blocked (TNT)), as the geometric mean over a group's pairs, read as trial means. A value above 1 for the co-response says that the responders that remain under APL are shared more often than the responders without it

**The alcohols' responders that survive APL are shared more often than before in the flies, and less so in the models.** What APL does to each factor can be read without putting one side's factors into the other's product (table above). In the flies and in the models alike APL cuts a pair's recruitment to about half, and the amplitude factor hardly changes (last five rows).

What differs is the co-response of the alcohol pairs. In the flies it is {{E88/changes.csv:source=flies;member=mean;subset=all;reading=r1;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} times as large with APL as without (90 % interval over resampled recordings {{lit:1.42 to 1.75 # the exponentials of columns lo and hi (log units) of results/E88_responder_sets/changes.csv, row source=flies, member=mean, subset=all, reading=r1, factor=L, group=alcohol}}): the alcohols' responders that remain under APL are shared more often than their responders without it. In the breadth-2 family the factor is {{E88/changes.csv:source=model;population=b2;member=population;reading=r1;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} at the reading's own noise and {{E88/changes.csv:source=model;population=b2;member=population;reading=r1b;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} at the flies' repeatability, in the family with the firing ceiling {{E88/changes.csv:source=model;population=fc;member=population;reading=r1;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} and {{E88/changes.csv:source=model;population=fc;member=population;reading=r1b;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}}, and on the base with the flies' recruitment {{E88/changes.csv:source=model;population=D2_thrapl;member=population;reading=r1;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} and {{E88/changes.csv:source=model;population=D2_thrapl;member=population;reading=r1b;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}}.

A model's change was to count as different from the flies' if it lay outside their interval and differed by a factor of 1.10 or more at both noise levels. It does so in all three, the breadth-2 family's value at the flies' repeatability lying just below the interval. Against the six recordings that are alike ({{E88/changes.csv:source=flies;member=mean;subset=six;reading=r1;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}}, interval {{lit:1.36 to 1.69 # the exponentials of columns lo and hi (log units) of results/E88_responder_sets/changes.csv, row source=flies, member=mean, subset=six, reading=r1, factor=L, group=alcohol}}) it does so only on the base with the flies' recruitment.

The ester pairs' co-response hardly changes under APL in the flies or in the models, and differs nowhere. The recruitment of the four nearest ester pairs, a factor that the check reads without bias, falls further under APL in the flies (to {{E88/changes.csv:source=flies;member=mean;subset=all;reading=r1;factor=R;group=nearest4:ratio ~ .2f}}, interval {{lit:0.38 to 0.51 # the exponentials of columns lo and hi (log units) of results/E88_responder_sets/changes.csv, row source=flies, member=mean, subset=all, reading=r1, factor=R, group=nearest4}}) than in the breadth-2 family ({{E88/changes.csv:source=model;population=b2;member=population;reading=r1;factor=R;group=nearest4:ratio ~ .2f}} and {{E88/changes.csv:source=model;population=b2;member=population;reading=r1b;factor=R;group=nearest4:ratio ~ .2f}}); that difference is not there against the six recordings that are alike, nor on the base with the flies' recruitment.

The size of the alcohols' difference carries the caveat of the estimate. Without noise the breadth-2 family's alcohol pairs have a co-response of {{E88/estimator_check.csv:population=b2;reading=r1;condition=on;factor=L;group=alcohol:truth ~ .2f}} with APL on and {{E88/estimator_check.csv:population=b2;reading=r1;condition=off;factor=L;group=alcohol:truth ~ .2f}} with APL off, a ratio of {{lit:1.33 # the quotient of column truth of results/E88_responder_sets/estimator_check.csv in rows population=b2, reading=r1, factor=L, group=alcohol, condition=on (4.687) and condition=off (3.528)}}, which the trial means read as less at the reading's own noise and as more at the flies' repeatability. If the flies' value is too high in the proportion in which the model's is at their repeatability, the difference between the flies and the model is smaller than the table shows, and it remains.

**On which side the alcohols' difference lies is not decided.** To ask whether the difference is in the responses without APL or in what APL does to them, each odor's responders without APL were cut by amplitude to the number that respond with APL, in the flies (the recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) cut to the control flies' response rates) and in the models (the responses with APL off cut to the model's response rates with APL on), and what the cut leaves of the co-response was set against what APL leaves (second row of the table).

If the cut leaves the same in the model as in the flies and APL does not, the difference is in what the model's APL does; if the cut already differs, it is in the responses. At the reading's own noise the cut leaves the breadth-2 family's alcohols nearly the flies' change ({{E88/cut.csv:source=model;population=b2;member=population;reading=r1;what=cut_own;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} against {{E88/cut.csv:source=flies;member=mean;subset=all;reading=r1;what=cut;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}}) while its APL leaves less ({{E88/changes.csv:source=model;population=b2;member=population;reading=r1;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} against {{E88/changes.csv:source=flies;member=mean;subset=all;reading=r1;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}}), which puts the difference on APL's side. At the flies' repeatability the cut itself leaves more than the flies' ({{E88/cut.csv:source=model;population=b2;member=population;reading=r1b;what=cut_own;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}}), which puts it on both sides. The two noise levels disagree, so by the rule the side is undecided, and the base with the flies' recruitment and the family with the firing ceiling read the same way.

At the reading's own noise the flies' chosen form applied to the model's responses gives the alcohols the co-response change that it gives on the flies' own responses ({{E88/cut.csv:source=model;population=b2;member=population;reading=r1;what=form;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} in the breadth-2 family and {{E88/cut.csv:source=model;population=D2_thrapl;member=population;reading=r1;what=form;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} on the base with the flies' recruitment, against {{E88/cut.csv:source=flies;member=mean;subset=all;reading=r1;what=form;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}}); at the flies' repeatability it gives more ({{E88/cut.csv:source=model;population=b2;member=population;reading=r1b;what=form;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} and {{E88/cut.csv:source=model;population=D2_thrapl;member=population;reading=r1b;what=form;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}}). The amplitudes of the shared responders say little on either side: the rank correlation between a shared responder's responses to the two odors of a pair is low in the flies ({{E88/shared_amplitudes.csv:source=flies;subset=all;reading=r1;condition=on;group=ester:rank_corr ~ .2f}} and {{E88/shared_amplitudes.csv:source=flies;subset=all;reading=r1;condition=on;group=alcohol:rank_corr ~ .2f}} for the ester and the alcohol pairs in the control flies, {{E88/shared_amplitudes.csv:source=flies;subset=all;reading=r1;condition=off;group=ester:rank_corr ~ .2f}} and {{E88/shared_amplitudes.csv:source=flies;subset=all;reading=r1;condition=off;group=alcohol:rank_corr ~ .2f}} with APL output blocked (TNT)) and in the breadth-2 family ({{E88/shared_amplitudes.csv:source=model;population=b2;reading=r1;condition=on;group=ester:rank_corr ~ .2f}} and {{E88/shared_amplitudes.csv:source=model;population=b2;reading=r1;condition=on;group=alcohol:rank_corr ~ .2f}} with APL on, {{E88/shared_amplitudes.csv:source=model;population=b2;reading=r1;condition=off;group=ester:rank_corr ~ .2f}} and {{E88/shared_amplitudes.csv:source=model;population=b2;reading=r1;condition=off;group=alcohol:rank_corr ~ .2f}} with APL off).

**The KCs that the model's APL removes although a cut by amplitude would keep them are the broad KCs that its breadth weighting loads.** For the side of APL there is a description that does not depend on the estimate of the co-response, because it is read on the model's spike counts without noise. The KCs that respond to both odors of a pair with APL off were divided into those that respond to both with APL on as well, those that the cut by amplitude would keep for both odors and the family's APL removes, and the rest (table above).

The second class is {{E88/shared_kcs.csv:population=b2;wiring=pooled;group=alcohol;kc_class=cut_kept_apl_removed:share_of_overlap ~ .2f}} of a pair's shared responders for the alcohol pairs and {{E88/shared_kcs.csv:population=b2;wiring=pooled;group=ester;kc_class=cut_kept_apl_removed:share_of_overlap ~ .2f}} for the ester pairs. Its KCs are among the strongest responders of both odors. They respond to {{E88/shared_kcs.csv:population=b2;wiring=pooled;group=alcohol;kc_class=cut_kept_apl_removed:n_odors_off ~ .1f}} and {{E88/shared_kcs.csv:population=b2;wiring=pooled;group=ester;kc_class=cut_kept_apl_removed:n_odors_off ~ .1f}} of the 16 odors without APL, where the KCs that still respond to both with APL on respond to {{E88/shared_kcs.csv:population=b2;wiring=pooled;group=alcohol;kc_class=survive:n_odors_off ~ .1f}} and {{E88/shared_kcs.csv:population=b2;wiring=pooled;group=ester;kc_class=survive:n_odors_off ~ .1f}}; they have more claws and are more often γ KCs; and they receive {{E88/shared_kcs.csv:population=b2;wiring=pooled;group=alcohol;kc_class=cut_kept_apl_removed:apl_weight ~ .1f}} and {{E88/shared_kcs.csv:population=b2;wiring=pooled;group=ester;kc_class=cut_kept_apl_removed:apl_weight ~ .1f}} times the mean APL→KC weight, where those that still respond receive {{E88/shared_kcs.csv:population=b2;wiring=pooled;group=alcohol;kc_class=survive:apl_weight ~ .1f}} and {{E88/shared_kcs.csv:population=b2;wiring=pooled;group=ester;kc_class=survive:apl_weight ~ .1f}} times the mean.

The family's APL scales each KC's APL→KC weight by the square of the KC's breadth, its spike total over the 16 odors with APL off. It had been fixed that the breadth weighting would be named as what removes a group's shared responders if at least two thirds of the KCs of the second class lie in the top quarter of the responding KCs' breadth weights. Counted once per KC and wiring, {{lit:84 % # results/E88_responder_sets/verdict_B.json, B4.b2.alcohol.share_top_quarter: of the KCs that the cut keeps and APL removes, counted once per KC and wiring over the eight wirings, the share in the top quarter of the responding KCs' breadth factors}} of them do for the alcohol pairs, {{lit:76 % # results/E88_responder_sets/verdict_B.json, B4.b2.ester.share_top_quarter: the same for the ester pairs}} for the ester pairs and {{lit:78 % # results/E88_responder_sets/verdict_B.json, B4.b2.nearest4.share_top_quarter: the same for the four nearest ester pairs}} for the four nearest ester pairs; for the 99 pairs outside the two groups the share is {{lit:66 % # results/E88_responder_sets/verdict_B.json, B4.b2.other.share_top_quarter: the same for the 99 pairs outside the ester and the alcohol pairs}}, just short of it, and on the base with the flies' recruitment the shares of the groups are {{lit:70 % # results/E88_responder_sets/verdict_B.json, B4.D2_thrapl.ester.share_top_quarter: the lowest of the shares for the four nearest ester pairs, the six pairs with near-identical ORN input, the ester pairs and the alcohol pairs on the base with the flies' recruitment}} to {{lit:81 % # results/E88_responder_sets/verdict_B.json, B4.D2_thrapl.alcohol.share_top_quarter: the highest of the same four shares}}.

The model's APL thus takes out of the alcohols' and the esters' overlap the strongly and broadly responding KCs that a cut by amplitude keeps. That fits the alcohols' difference lying on APL's side, as does the flies' form giving the model's alcohols the flies' change; the recordings ask for a much weaker dependence on breadth than the family has, an exponent of {{E87/held_out.csv:unit=z;reading=noise_free;split=1;direction=A->B:chosen_p ~ .2f}} on a KC's summed response in the flies' chosen form against 2 on its spike total ([above](#inhibition-form)). It does not settle the side.

**The saved models give no handle to take further.** Every saved model with responses in both conditions for the 16 odors was read by the same factors, {{lit:1684 # results/E88_responder_sets/verdict_C.json, n_variants (7 of them could not be read, n_errors)}} variants, as trial means and without noise, each against the breadth-2 fit on the same wiring. A variant was to stand out if, inside the realism bands and through a handle that the model has, its pattern part with the responses reduced to responding or not was lower than that fit's by 0.008 or more, or its alcohol pairs' co-response change came at least halfway from the fit's to the flies' with the ester pairs' no further from the flies'.

{{lit:79 # results/E88_responder_sets/verdict_C.json, standout_variants}} variants of {{lit:22 # results/E88_responder_sets/verdict_C.json, standout_handles: the number of experiments with a variant that stands out}} experiments pass, in {{lit:91 # results/E88_responder_sets/verdict_C.json, n_standout: rows of archive_scan.csv with standout true}} readings, and the rule proved too permissive to act on. Of the {{lit:68 # results/E88_responder_sets/verdict_C.json, n_standout_by: the readings that pass by the alcohol co-response change, 26 as trial means and 42 on raw counts}} readings that pass by the alcohols' co-response change, {{lit:55 # count of the rows of results/E88_responder_sets/archive_scan.csv with standout true and cand_by 'alcohol co-response change' whose bin_pattern is above base_bin_pattern}} have a higher pattern part than the fit they are compared with. Of the {{lit:23 # results/E88_responder_sets/verdict_C.json, n_standout_by: the readings that pass by the binarized pattern part, 3 as trial means and 20 on raw counts}} that pass by the pattern part, {{lit:17 # count of the rows of results/E88_responder_sets/archive_scan.csv with standout true, cand_by 'binarized pattern part' and wiring P2}} are on one claw permutation, whose breadth-2 fit is the weakest of the eight on that score on raw counts. And {{lit:70 # count of the folders of results/E88_responder_sets/archive_scan.csv whose rows have handle_in_code true}} of the {{lit:77 # count of the distinct folders of results/E88_responder_sets/archive_scan.csv}} experiments with saved models count as having a handle, the rule as coded having asked only that the experiment have a script. Since the split was not read, no handle was run, as had been fixed for that case.

**Simulated in place of APL on the base with the flies' recruitment, the flies' form does far worse than the model's own APL.**

The base is the four wirings of the earlier searches with each odor's response rate with APL off put on that of the flies with APL output blocked (TNT) by a threshold for each odor (factors of {{E88/runs_D1.csv:D1_chosen_M1:base_thr_min ~ .2f}} to {{E88/runs_D1.csv:D1_chosen_P1:base_thr_max ~ .2f}} on the fit's threshold); its runs with APL off reproduce the earlier ones exactly. On it APL was removed, the KC–KC inhibition kept as fitted, and each KC's threshold for each odor multiplied by one plus a constant times a form, with the odor's strength and the KC's breadth taken from the base's run with APL off and the constant searched until the number of responses was the one that the control flies' per-odor response rates give, to within two responses.

Three forms were run: the flies' chosen form, the odor's strength alone, and the same factor for every KC and odor. The test was that of the simulations on the fits as they are ([above](#inhibition-form)). A form does better than the unchanged fits if the pattern part of the mean over the four wirings, through the readout, is lower by 0.003 or more, on at least three of the wirings, inside the realism bands and with the loss on raw counts no more than 0.005 higher, and worse if the pattern part is higher by 0.003 or more.

Every form is worse (table above). The pattern part is {{E88/readings_D1.csv:form_label=chosen;readout=cal;unit=S:z8_pattern ~ .3f}} for the flies' chosen form, {{E88/readings_D1.csv:form_label=q1_p0;readout=cal;unit=S:z8_pattern ~ .3f}} for the odor's strength alone and {{E88/readings_D1.csv:form_label=uniform;readout=cal;unit=S:z8_pattern ~ .3f}} for the uniform rise, against {{E88/readings_D1.csv:form_label=chosen;readout=cal;unit=S:unchanged_z8_pattern ~ .3f}} for the unchanged fits and {{E88/main_target.csv:population=D2_thrapl;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .3f}} for the model's own APL on the same base. It is higher on every wiring ({{E88/readings_D1.csv:form_label=chosen;readout=cal;unit=M1:z8_pattern ~ .3f}} to {{E88/readings_D1.csv:form_label=chosen;readout=cal;unit=real:z8_pattern ~ .3f}} for the flies' chosen form against {{E88/readings_D1.csv:form_label=chosen;readout=cal;unit=P2:unchanged_z8_pattern ~ .3f}} to {{E88/readings_D1.csv:form_label=chosen;readout=cal;unit=P1:unchanged_z8_pattern ~ .3f}}), and the loss on raw counts is {{E88/readings_D1.csv:form_label=chosen;readout=raw;unit=S:z8_loss ~ .3f}} to {{E88/readings_D1.csv:form_label=q1_p0;readout=raw;unit=S:z8_loss ~ .3f}} against {{E88/readings_D1.csv:form_label=chosen;readout=raw;unit=S:unchanged_z8_loss ~ .3f}}.

The per-pair effect loses its pattern: ρ on the per-pair APL effect is {{E88/readings_D1.csv:form_label=chosen;readout=cal;unit=S:z8_rho ~ .2f}} for the flies' chosen form, {{E88/readings_D1.csv:form_label=q1_p0;readout=cal;unit=S:z8_rho ~ .2f}} for the odor's strength alone and {{E88/readings_D1.csv:form_label=uniform;readout=cal;unit=S:z8_rho ~ .2f}} for the uniform rise, against {{E88/readings_D1.csv:form_label=chosen;readout=cal;unit=S:unchanged_z8_rho ~ .2f}} for the unchanged fits. The ester pairs' shortfall deepens under every form ({{E88/readings_D1.csv:form_label=q1_p0;readout=cal;unit=S:z8_err_ester ~ +.3f}} to {{E88/readings_D1.csv:form_label=uniform;readout=cal;unit=S:z8_err_ester ~ +.3f}} against {{E88/readings_D1.csv:form_label=chosen;readout=cal;unit=S:unchanged_z8_err_ester ~ +.3f}}). The flies' chosen form nearly triples the alcohol pairs' excess ({{E88/readings_D1.csv:form_label=chosen;readout=cal;unit=S:z8_err_alcohol ~ +.3f}} against {{E88/readings_D1.csv:form_label=chosen;readout=cal;unit=S:unchanged_z8_err_alcohol ~ +.3f}}), and the odor's strength alone removes that excess ({{E88/readings_D1.csv:form_label=q1_p0;readout=cal;unit=S:z8_err_alcohol ~ +.3f}}) and leaves the esters short.

The forms also do worse here than on the fits as they are, where the flies' chosen form had read {{E87/readings_D.csv:form_label=chosen;readout=cal;unit=all8:z8_pattern ~ .3f}} against {{E87/readings_D.csv:form_label=chosen;readout=cal;unit=all8:unchanged_z8_pattern ~ .3f}} for the family's own APL on eight wirings. And the reading on the counts does not carry over. Applied to the base's spike counts with APL off, the flies' chosen form had read better than the model's own APL ([above](#inhibition-form)); the same forms applied to those counts correlate with the simulated per-pair effects at {{lit:0.40 # results/E88_responder_sets/verdict_D1.json, chosen.proxy_r}}, {{lit:0.04 # results/E88_responder_sets/verdict_D1.json, q1_p0.proxy_r}} and {{lit:0.09 # results/E88_responder_sets/verdict_D1.json, uniform.proxy_r}}, where 0.8 had been set (last row).

Static inhibitions of this kind are thus closed on both bases, the fits as they are and the base with the flies' recruitment. The readings on spike counts are no guide to what an inhibition does inside the model, and the model's own feedback APL remains the best inhibition tried on its responses.

**Realism.** The factors and the readings of what APL does fit nothing and add no parameter. They read saved responses, with the response rate with APL on held at the flies' in every reading (on the real wiring {{E88/members.csv:population=b2;wiring=real:r1_rate_on ~ .3f}} with APL on and {{E88/members.csv:population=b2;wiring=real:r1_rate_off ~ .3f}} with APL off, as trial means), and a combination that holds the flies' factors is not a model and is not read on the bands.

The twelve simulations are all inside the four realism bands. Both response rates are held by construction, at {{E88/runs_D1.csv:D1_chosen_real:rate_on ~ .3f}} and {{E88/runs_D1.csv:D1_chosen_real:rate_off ~ .3f}} on the real wiring (a ratio of {{E88/runs_D1.csv:D1_chosen_real:ratio ~ .2f}}), the side with APL off being the base itself. The response rate ρ with APL on is {{E88/runs_D1.csv:D1_chosen_P2:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}} to {{E88/runs_D1.csv:D1_chosen_real:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}} under the flies' chosen form, {{E88/runs_D1.csv:D1_uniform_M1:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}} to {{E88/runs_D1.csv:D1_uniform_real:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}} under the uniform rise and {{E88/runs_D1.csv:D1_q1_p0_P1:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}} to {{E88/runs_D1.csv:D1_q1_p0_M1:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}} under the odor's strength alone.

All three forms move the distribution of the number of odors per KC with APL on away from the flies': it is {{E88/runs_D1.csv:D1_chosen_M1:opk_on_tv ~ .3f}} to {{E88/runs_D1.csv:D1_chosen_real:opk_on_tv ~ .3f}} from the flies' distribution under the flies' chosen form and up to {{E88/runs_D1.csv:D1_uniform_M1:opk_on_tv ~ .3f}} under the uniform rise, against a band of {{data:noise_ctrl_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .3f}}. Counted by the recordings' own criterion, as the bands counted until 2026-11-10, {{lit:10 # count of the 12 rows of results/E88_responder_sets/runs_D1.csv with a realism_flag_zcrit (all of them the number of odors per KC with APL on); none of the 12 has a realism_flag}} of the 12 runs would be outside that band. The largest spike count per KC and odor with APL on is {{E88/runs_D1.csv:D1_q1_p0_M1:max_count_on ~ .0f}} to {{E88/runs_D1.csv:D1_chosen_P1:max_count_on ~ .0f}}. None of the runs is better than the unchanged fits, and none is recommended for anything.

Several things are hard to defend. A static rise of thresholds stands in for an inhibition and has no feedback, and the rise is large: {{E88/runs_D1.csv:D1_uniform_P2:c ~ .0%}} to {{E88/runs_D1.csv:D1_uniform_P1:c ~ .0%}} for every threshold under the uniform form. The base's threshold for each odor is an [oracle](#fn-oracle) for a mechanism of recruitment.

The flies' factors compare different animals across the two genotypes, and the flies with APL output blocked (TNT) have lived with the block. Raising the model's noise to the flies' repeatability, by the factors given above, is a property of the reading and not of the model. And the parts on the models carry, as everywhere, paa, euc and -aPine at [ORN input of another concentration](#fn-concentrations). No part improved the main target, so nothing was bought with the bands.

**What follows.** The common error keeps its two groups and gains a description of them that is not yet a verdict. Who responds is its likely address: the ester pairs' part with how large a share of an odor's responders APL removes, the alcohol pairs' part with whether the responders that survive APL are shared more often than before.

For that to be relied on, the co-response needs an estimate that passes the check on a model with known values, at the reading's own noise and at the flies' repeatability; the split is then read again, without new simulations. Until it is, the amplitudes, and with them the readouts, the bounds on firing and the indicator's kinetics, are not closed as carriers of the two groups' errors by this route, although none of them carried those errors when it was tried ([the compressive readout of the model's spike counts](#readout); [the firing ceiling for the KCs](#firing-ceiling); [the flies' recording protocol in the model](#flies-protocol); [the time course of the APL effect in the flies' traces](#trace-time-course)).

Two things are carried forward as they are. The alcohol pairs' co-response change under APL is given beside the main target for later mechanisms, on the fits as they are and on the base with the flies' recruitment: it is the difference between models and flies that shows at both noise levels and, on that base, against the six recordings that are alike as well. And on APL's side static forms are closed, so that what is pursued is the feedback APL's own weighting, with its breadth weighting first, since that weighting is what removes the shared responders that a cut by amplitude keeps.

The verdicts that change with the six recordings that are alike, which are the overall split, the ester pairs' assignment to recruitment and the alcohols' difference on the fits as they are, wait on the experimenter's answer about the two strongest recordings. Both steps have since been taken, and both close: no estimate of the co-response passes the check, and no other breadth weighting does better than the family's own ([below](#breadth-weighting)). What is taken up from here is with the pending work at the end of the page.

### The co-response read with a checked estimate and the breadth weighting inside the models' APL: whether any estimate of the co-response is good enough to read the split, and whether another breadth weighting of APL lowers the pattern part {#breadth-weighting}

**The two steps that the split of the common error had left both close.** No estimate of the co-response of two odors' responder sets passes the check on a model whose values without noise are known. The best of five, the geometric mean of the two earlier estimates, is inside the tolerance at the reading's own noise and at the flies' repeatability with the flies' share of noise common to the odors of a repeat; it is outside at one and a half times that share, and on the base with the flies' recruitment at the flies' share itself.

With three repeats a recording, the co-response of the pairs nearest each other cannot be read to the tolerance, so the split into who responds and how strongly stays a description. Read like for like with that estimate, the alcohol pairs' co-response still rises more under APL in the flies than in the models.

On the model's side, twelve other breadth weightings of APL, with a KC's breadth measured in three ways and exponents from 0 to 2, were run on the fits as they are and on the base with the flies' recruitment, and none has a lower pattern part than the family's own. A weaker weighting brings the alcohol pairs' co-response change to the flies' and removes those pairs' excess APL effect, and it deepens the ester pairs' shortfall and lowers the mean APL effect and ρ on the per-pair APL effect, so that the main target is worse wherever that change is the flies'. The family's mean APL effect rests on its weighting, its exponent of 2 stays, and for the breadth weighting APL's side is closed.

The common error split into who responds and how strongly had ended on two steps ([above](#responder-sets)). The first was an estimate of the co-response that passes the check on a model with known values, with which the split would be read again without simulation. The second was on APL's side, where static inhibitions were closed and the feedback APL's own breadth weighting was next: in the model that weighting removes from the alcohol and the ester pairs' overlap the broad KCs that a cut by amplitude keeps, and the recordings had asked for a much weaker dependence on a KC's breadth than the family has ([the form of APL's inhibition in the flies' own responses](#inhibition-form)).

Five estimates of the co-response were put to the check of the first reading. Two existed: from the trial means, which reads the co-response of the pairs nearest each other too low, and with the trial noise removed, which reads it too high. Three were new: the geometric mean of those two, an estimate that sorts each KC's mean response to an odor into classes after the trial noise has been taken out of the distribution of the responses, and a correction of the trial means by each odor's measured agreement between repeats.

Each is computed from a recording's three repeats, in the flies and in the models alike, and was checked on simulated recordings of the breadth-2 family's eight wirings and of the base with the flies' recruitment, with two seeds of the noise. The check was also made harder, with noise built as the flies' is ([the flies' variability across the three repeats](#repeat-structure)).

At the flies' repeatability a part of each KC's noise was shared by the odors of a repeat: the share at which two odors of the same repeat are closer than two odors of different repeats by as much as in the flies, counted on single trials with sub-threshold values set to 0, and half and one and a half times that share.

An estimate was to be used only if recruitment, the co-response and the similarity were each within 0.03 of their values without noise, in units of the similarity, as the mean over each of five groups of pairs, in both conditions and with both seeds, at the reading's own noise and at all three shares. The split itself was to be read only with an estimate whose amplitude factor passed as well.

The estimates of the co-response checked on models whose values without noise are known: the estimate minus the value without noise, as the mean over a group's pairs that is furthest from 0 among five groups of pairs (the four nearest ester pairs, the six pairs with near-identical ORN input, the ester pairs, the alcohol pairs and the other 99 pairs), the two conditions and the two seeds of the noise, in units of the similarity (0.03 is the most an estimate may be off and still be used)

**No estimate passes, so the split stays a description.** The trial means read the co-response too low and the estimate with the trial noise removed reads it too high, at every noise level (first two rows of the table), so that their geometric mean comes closest.

On the breadth-2 family it is inside the tolerance at the reading's own noise and with half and with the whole of the flies' share, where the two errors nearly cancel, and outside it at one and a half times that share ({{E89/estimator_check.csv:population=b2;seed=43;level=L3x;candidate=gm;condition=off;factor=L;group=nearest4:err ~ +.3f}}, for the four nearest ester pairs with APL off, with both seeds; the six pairs with near-identical ORN input and the alcohol pairs miss by nearly as much). Its amplitude factor is outside at half the flies' share as well ({{E89/estimator_check.csv:population=b2;seed=44;level=L3h;candidate=gm;condition=off;factor=G;group=six:err ~ +.3f}}), so that the split could not have been read with it in any case.

On the base with the flies' recruitment its co-response is outside the tolerance from the flies' share on, and there the similarity itself, which every estimate has in common, is off by {{E89/estimator_check.csv:population=base;seed=44;level=L3;candidate=gm;condition=on;factor=s;group=six:err ~ +.3f}} at the flies' repeatability, so that no estimate could have passed. The classes of response hold up to half the flies' share on the family and nowhere on the base, and the correction by the agreement between repeats is far outside everywhere.

By the rule fixed beforehand nothing is read with a new estimate and no further one is sought. With three repeats a recording, the co-response of the pairs nearest each other is not resolved to 0.03 at the flies' repeatability, and the earlier reading stands as it was left: it points to who responds and is not a verdict ([above](#responder-sets)).

One choice in the check was open and does not decide it. The flies' share was set on single trials with sub-threshold values set to 0; set on the graded values it would be smaller, between no shared part and half the share used. That level was not run, and with no shared part the geometric mean is outside the tolerance as well ({{E89/estimator_check.csv:population=b2;seed=44;level=L2;candidate=gm;condition=off;factor=L;group=nearest4:err ~ +.3f}}).

**Like for like, the alcohol pairs' co-response still rises more under APL in the flies than in the models.** Whatever becomes of the split, what APL does to the co-response can be given for the flies and for the models with one estimate, with that estimate's error on known values beside it.

Read with the geometric mean, the co-response of the alcohol pairs (the 6 pairs among 1-8ol, 1-5ol, 1-6ol and 6al) is {{E89/changes.csv:source=flies;candidate=gm;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} times as large with APL as without in the flies (90 % interval over resampled recordings {{lit:1.46 to 1.78 # the exponentials of columns lo and hi (log units) of results/E89_apl_breadth_weighting/changes.csv, row source=flies, candidate=gm, subset=all, factor=L, group=alcohol}}). In the breadth-2 family it is {{E89/changes.csv:source=model;candidate=gm;population=b2;level=L1;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} to {{E89/changes.csv:source=model;candidate=gm;population=b2;level=L3h;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} times as large over the four noise levels of the check, for a value without noise of {{E89/changes.csv:source=model;candidate=gm;population=b2;level=L1;factor=L;group=alcohol:truth_ratio ~ .2f}}, and on the base with the flies' recruitment {{E89/changes.csv:source=model;candidate=gm;population=base;level=L1;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} to {{E89/changes.csv:source=model;candidate=gm;population=base;level=L3h;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} for {{E89/changes.csv:source=model;candidate=gm;population=base;level=L1;factor=L;group=alcohol:truth_ratio ~ .2f}}.

A model's change counts as different from the flies' if it lies outside their interval and differs by a factor of 1.10 or more at every one of those noise levels. It does in both, and in the family with the firing ceiling and on the four wirings of the earlier searches as fitted. Against the six recordings that are alike ({{E89/changes.csv:source=flies;candidate=gm;subset=six;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}}, interval {{lit:1.42 to 1.72 # the exponentials of columns lo and hi (log units) of results/E89_apl_breadth_weighting/changes.csv, row source=flies, candidate=gm, subset=six, factor=L, group=alcohol}}) it does on the base and, by a narrow margin, on the breadth-2 family, where as trial means it had not.

At the flies' repeatability the estimate reads the models' change a few per cent above its value without noise; if the flies' value is too high in the same proportion, the flies remain {{lit:16 to 31 % # E89_apl_breadth_weighting.md, section A2, the rough correction: the flies' ratio divided by the estimate's bias on a model (columns ratio and truth_ratio of results/E89_apl_breadth_weighting/changes.csv, rows source=model, candidate=gm, factor=L, group=alcohol, levels L1 to L3x), against that model's truth_ratio: 16 to 24 % for population=b2 and 21 to 31 % for population=base}} above the models' values without noise. The difference is a firm one. The co-response of the ester pairs (the 15 pairs among 2h, IaA, pa, eb, ep and ms) hardly changes under APL on either side, and it does not differ at every noise level.

**The saved models gave no lead.** Before any run, the saved families in which only the weighting differs were read for whether the pattern part follows the alcohols' change: whether the member whose change is nearest the flies' has a pattern part lower than the member at an exponent of 2 by 0.003 or more, through the readout and on raw counts.

At the control flies' response rate {{lit:one # results/E89_apl_breadth_weighting/verdict_B.json, follows_any_at_the_flies_operating_point: one family, E66_thr40_gain1.5}} family of {{lit:four # results/E89_apl_breadth_weighting/verdict_B.json, families with operating_point 0.068: E66_thr40_gain1.5, E66_thr70_gain1.5, E66_thr70_gain1.25 and E67_C2}} does, and only as trial means: the current reference model with its weighting changed at otherwise fitted parameters ([above](#apl-effect-parts)). In it the pattern part through the readout falls with the exponent all the way down, from {{E89/weighting_archive.csv:family=E66_thr40_gain1.5;variant=C_thr40_gain1.5_spikes_k3:cal_z8_pattern ~ .3f}} at an exponent of 3 to {{E89/weighting_archive.csv:family=E66_thr40_gain1.5;variant=C_thr40_gain1.5_spikes_k0:cal_z8_pattern ~ .3f}} without the weighting, where the alcohols' change is {{lit:1.96 # the exponential of column r1_chg_L_alcohol (log units) of results/E89_apl_breadth_weighting/weighting_archive.csv, row family=E66_thr40_gain1.5, variant=C_thr40_gain1.5_spikes_k0}}, well above the flies'. What gains there is a weaker weighting, not the flies' co-response. The breadth-2 family's own fits at other exponents do not follow ([the APL-effect fits](#apl-effect-fits)).

What a weighting does depends on the rest of the model. In the reference model, and in most of the earlier grids at a response rate of 5 %, removing the weighting lowers a pattern part that is above the breadth-2 family's to begin with. In that family, whose exponent was fitted together with its other parameters, every step away from 2 costs, as the runs below show.

**None of twelve other weightings has a lower pattern part than the family's own.** The family multiplies each KC's APL→KC weight by a power of the KC's breadth relative to the mean over the KCs, with the breadth taken as the KC's spike total over the 16 odors without APL in a run of the bouton baseline, at another operating point than the fit's, and with an exponent of 2. Twelve other weightings were run.

- Three keep the measure, at exponents of 0.25, 0.5 and 1.
- Eight take the measure from the responses that APL acts on, each at 0.25, 0.5, 1 and 2: a KC's summed spike count over the odors it responds to in the model's own run without APL, which is the measure that the recordings chose, and the number of odors it responds to there.
- The last has no weighting.

Each was run on the four wirings of the earlier searches: on the fits as they are, with the APL scale set again to the fit's number of responses with APL on, and on the base with the flies' recruitment, with the APL scale for each odor set again to the control flies' response rate. The family's own weighting through the new code reproduces the saved runs exactly on both.

The weighting with the lowest pattern part of the mean over the four wirings, through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout) and against one half of the recordings, was to be read on the four other wirings against the other half, by the test that the fitted changes were put to ([above](#cross-wiring-fit)), if it was lower than the family's by 0.0015 or more. None was.

On the fits as they are the family's own weighting is the lowest against either half of the recordings and against either half of a second split of the flies, and against all recordings the other twelve are higher by {{diff:E89/readings_C.csv:arm=C1;weighting=S_k2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern -- E89/readings_C.csv:arm=C1;weighting=F_k2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .3f}} to {{diff:E89/readings_C.csv:arm=C1;weighting=none;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern -- E89/readings_C.csv:arm=C1;weighting=F_k2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .3f}}, where differences within 0.003 had been expected (table below, for the family's measure). On the base it is the lowest against three of those four halves; against the fourth the same measure at an exponent of 1 is lower by {{E89/choice_C.csv:arm=C2;half=A:gain ~ .4f}}.

The measures taken from the responses that APL acts on do no better than the family's. The best of them on the fits as they are, the summed response at an exponent of 2, has a pattern part of {{E89/readings_C.csv:arm=C1;weighting=S_k2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .3f}} against the family's {{E89/readings_C.csv:arm=C1;weighting=F_k2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .3f}}, and the best on the base, the summed response at an exponent of 1, {{E89/readings_C.csv:arm=C2;weighting=S_k1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .3f}} against {{E89/readings_C.csv:arm=C2;weighting=F_k2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .3f}}.

With the readout's constant kept at the fit's, the family's weighting is still the lowest on both against all recordings. Nothing therefore went to the four other wirings, and the result rests on the four that were searched.
