**The weighting moves the alcohol pairs' co-response and the main target in opposite directions.** As the weighting weakens, the alcohol pairs' co-response change under APL rises, on every measure (last row of the table, for the family's). As trial means at the reading's own noise it is below the flies' interval at the family's weighting and inside it at an exponent of 0.5. The alcohol pairs' excess APL effect goes with it, from {{E89/readings_C.csv:arm=C1;weighting=F_k2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_alcohol ~ +.3f}} to {{E89/readings_C.csv:arm=C1;weighting=none;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_alcohol ~ +.3f}} on the fits as they are and from {{E89/readings_C.csv:arm=C2;weighting=F_k2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_alcohol ~ +.3f}} to {{E89/readings_C.csv:arm=C2;weighting=none;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_alcohol ~ +.3f}} on the base, as the broad KCs that the weighting loads had suggested.

But the ester pairs' shortfall deepens, the mean APL effect falls from the flies' value to {{E89/readings_C.csv:arm=C1;weighting=none;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} and {{E89/readings_C.csv:arm=C2;weighting=none;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} without the weighting, and ρ on the per-pair APL effect falls with them. At the weightings where the alcohols' change differs from the flies' at neither noise level, the pattern part is higher than at the family's weighting by {{diff:E89/readings_C.csv:arm=C2;weighting=S_k0.5;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern -- E89/readings_C.csv:arm=C2;weighting=F_k2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .3f}} to {{diff:E89/readings_C.csv:arm=C1;weighting=S_k0.25;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern -- E89/readings_C.csv:arm=C1;weighting=F_k2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .3f}}. These changes are read as trial means, the estimate that the check does not pass, and their rise with a weaker weighting holds at both noise levels.

The weighting thus sets the alcohols' co-response under APL, and the common error is not there: what a weaker weighting gives the alcohol pairs it takes from the ester pairs and from the mean. The family's mean APL effect rests on its weighting. On raw counts the pattern part hardly moves, from {{E89/readings_C.csv:arm=C1;weighting=F_k2;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_pattern ~ .3f}} at the family's weighting to {{E89/readings_C.csv:arm=C1;weighting=none;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_pattern ~ .3f}} without it on the fits as they are, while the loss rises from {{E89/readings_C.csv:arm=C1;weighting=F_k2;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_loss ~ .3f}} to {{E89/readings_C.csv:arm=C1;weighting=none;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_loss ~ .3f}} with the falling mean.

**No weaker weighting is an equal, so the exponent stays.** The family's exponent is its hardest setting to defend. Among the KCs that respond without APL, the APL→KC weight at the 90th percentile is {{E89/runs_C1.csv:C1_F_k2_P2:fac_resp_p90_over_p10 ~ .0f}} to {{E89/runs_C1.csv:C1_F_k2_real:fac_resp_p90_over_p10 ~ .0f}} times that at the 10th on the four wirings, against {{E89/runs_C1.csv:C1_F_k1_P2:fac_resp_p90_over_p10 ~ .0f}} to {{E89/runs_C1.csv:C1_F_k1_real:fac_resp_p90_over_p10 ~ .0f}} times at an exponent of 1. A weighting with an exponent of 1 or less was therefore to be reported as the setting easier to defend if it was an equal: a pattern part within 0.003 of the family's against all recordings and against both halves, inside the realism bands, a loss on raw counts within 0.005 and a mean APL effect within 0.01. None is.

The nearest is the family's measure at an exponent of 1 on the base. Its pattern part is level ({{diff:E89/readings_C.csv:arm=C2;weighting=F_k1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern -- E89/readings_C.csv:arm=C2;weighting=F_k2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ +.4f}} against all recordings), but its mean APL effect is lower by {{diff:E89/readings_C.csv:arm=C2;weighting=F_k2;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect -- E89/readings_C.csv:arm=C2;weighting=F_k1;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ .3f}} and its loss on raw counts higher by {{diff:E89/readings_C.csv:arm=C2;weighting=F_k1;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_loss -- E89/readings_C.csv:arm=C2;weighting=F_k2;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_loss ~ .3f}}. On the fits as they are the same weighting is already {{diff:E89/readings_C.csv:arm=C1;weighting=F_k1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern -- E89/readings_C.csv:arm=C1;weighting=F_k2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} higher in the pattern part. No choice between exponents arises from these runs.

**Realism.** The estimates fit nothing and add no parameter, and a part of the noise shared by the odors of a repeat is a property of the reading, not of the model. All {{lit:104 # the rows of results/E89_apl_breadth_weighting/runs_C1.csv and runs_C2.csv, 52 each (13 weightings on four wirings); none has a realism_flag}} runs of the weightings are inside the four realism bands, with both response rates held by construction: on the fits as they are {{E89/runs_C1.csv:C1_F_k2_real:rate_on ~ .3f}} to {{E89/runs_C1.csv:C1_F_k2_P1:rate_on ~ .3f}} with APL on and {{E89/runs_C1.csv:C1_F_k2_M1:rate_off ~ .3f}} to {{E89/runs_C1.csv:C1_F_k2_P2:rate_off ~ .3f}} with APL off over the four wirings (a ratio of {{E89/runs_C1.csv:C1_F_k2_M1:ratio ~ .2f}} to {{E89/runs_C1.csv:C1_F_k2_P2:ratio ~ .2f}}), and on the base {{E89/runs_C2.csv:C2_F_k2_real:rate_on ~ .3f}} and {{E89/runs_C2.csv:C2_F_k2_real:rate_off ~ .3f}} (a ratio of {{E89/runs_C2.csv:C2_F_k2_real:ratio ~ .2f}}), the flies' response rates odor by odor. The response rate ρ with APL on is {{E89/runs_C1.csv:C1_S_k2_P2:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}} to {{E89/runs_C1.csv:C1_S_k2_real:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}} on the fits as they are.

The weaker weightings move the distribution of the number of odors per KC with APL on away from the flies': without the weighting it is up to {{E89/runs_C1.csv:C1_none_P2:opk_on_tv ~ .3f}} from the flies' distribution, against {{E89/runs_C1.csv:C1_F_k2_P1:opk_on_tv ~ .3f}} to {{E89/runs_C1.csv:C1_F_k2_real:opk_on_tv ~ .3f}} at the family's weighting and a band of {{data:noise_ctrl_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .3f}}. Counted by the recordings' own criterion, as the bands counted until 2026-11-10, {{lit:13 # count of the rows of results/E89_apl_breadth_weighting/runs_C1.csv (11) and runs_C2.csv (2) with a realism_flag_zcrit, all of them the number of odors per KC with APL on: no weighting (6), the family's measure at 0.25 (3), the number of odors at 0.25 (3) and at 0.5 (1); none of the 104 has a realism_flag}} of the runs would be outside that band, all at the weakest weightings. No weighting improved the main target, so nothing was bought with the bands, and the narrower weights of a weaker weighting do not come free.

Several things are hard to defend. The family's weighting spreads APL's weight over the responding KCs by the factors given above. The measures of breadth are taken from the model's own run without APL, to which no cell has access; they stand in for whatever makes APL's output larger onto broadly responding KCs, which the recordings support indirectly and do not measure.

The base's threshold for each odor (factors of {{E89/runs_C2.csv:C2_F_k2_M1:thr_min ~ .2f}} to {{E89/runs_C2.csv:C2_F_k2_P1:thr_max ~ .2f}} on the fit's) and its APL scale for each odor ({{E89/runs_C2.csv:C2_F_k2_real:apl_min ~ .2f}} to {{E89/runs_C2.csv:C2_F_k2_M1:apl_max ~ .2f}} times the fit's at the family's weighting) are [oracles](#fn-oracle) for a mechanism of recruitment. And the parts on the models carry, as everywhere, paa, euc and -aPine at [ORN input of another concentration](#fn-concentrations).

**What follows.** The common error keeps its two groups, and its split into who responds and how strongly stays a description. No further estimate of the co-response is sought, and the amplitudes are not closed as carriers of the two groups' errors by this route, although none of them carried those errors when it was tried ([above](#responder-sets)).

The alcohol pairs' co-response change under APL stays beside the main target for later mechanisms, read with the geometric mean of the two estimates and with that estimate's error on known values beside it. It is a firm difference between the models and the flies, and it is not a lead on APL's side: the weighting sets it, and the main target does not follow.

APL's side is thereby closed for the breadth weighting, as it is for static forms of inhibition ([above](#responder-sets)), for APL's profile over the glomeruli ([the glomerulus profile of APL inhibition](#glomerulus-profile); [the input and APL's glomerulus profile fitted on several wirings at once](#cross-wiring-fit)) and for its weights by KC type ([the flies' pulse in the model and the remaining candidates for the common error](#remaining-candidates)).

Of the inhibitions tried on the breadth-2 family's responses, its own feedback APL is the best. The place where that inhibition is summed, at each claw or over a KC's claws, has since been varied as well and does not carry the error either; summed over the claws, an exponent of 1 reads lower than the family's on the base with the flies' recruitment, short of the test set for it ([below](#summed-drive)).

The exponent stays at 2. The weighting is not fitted again with the family's other parameters free, nor read in the family with the firing ceiling, at the flies' pulse or through the trial noise; those steps were kept for a weighting that lowered the pattern part.

The lead goes to the responses that APL acts on: which KCs respond to both odors of a pair before APL does anything, with the description of the model's shared responders, broad, many-clawed and often γ KCs, as the brief for a mechanism between the claw and the soma. The stages before the somata have since been read against recordings of them: where the models leave the flies is not resolved, and whether the model's KCs without APL bring two odors closer than their claw input depends on which claws are read ([below](#model-stages)).

The verdicts that change with the six recordings that are alike wait, as before, on the experimenter's answer about the two strongest recordings. What is taken up from here is with the pending work at the end of the page.

### The model's stages against the flies' stages: whether the best family leaves the flies before the claws, at the step from claws to somata with APL on, or at that step without APL {#model-stages}

%%% hover
step from claws to somata: Of two odors, the distance between their responses across the KC somata minus the distance between their responses across the KC claws, each distance being one minus the Pearson correlation across the units of the stage. A positive step means that the somata hold the two odors further apart than the claws do. With APL the somata are those of wild-type flies, of the control flies or of a model with APL on; without APL they are those of the flies with APL output blocked (TNT) or of a model with APL off. The claws are those of wild-type flies, or of the model with APL on, for both steps.
settled level: The level of a unit of the model (a PN bouton, a KC claw, or APL) before the odor, taken as its mean over the last quarter of a second before the odor. The simulation starts the model's KCs, their claws and APL at zero half a second before the odor, and by the last quarter of a second they have settled; a mean over the whole half second reads the claws and the boutons high and APL low. A unit's response to an odor is its mean during the odor minus this level. See the footnote on the model's level before the odor.
%%%

**Read against recordings of the PN dendrites, the PN boutons and the KC claws of wild-type flies, the best family cannot be placed: by the rule fixed beforehand, where it leaves the flies is not resolved for the ester pairs, the alcohol pairs or the other pairs.**

- Whether the model's claws are more alike than the flies' depends on how much of a claw's signal is taken to come from its KC's spikes and on which claws are read, since a third of the wiring's glomeruli have no ORN input in the model; and how the model's steps from claws to somata compare with the flies' depends, beyond that, on how its somata are read and on the length of the odor pulse.
- What does not depend on a reading is mostly on the flies' side. In wild-type flies the step from claws to somata carries the pattern of the main target: with APL it is larger among the esters than among the alcohols, without APL it is not, and it passes, narrowly, the test set for a second reading of that pattern that uses no fly with APL output blocked (TNT).
- On the model's side one difference holds throughout: its step with APL on is too small for the six pairs with near-identical ORN input. For the ester pairs that step is the flies' when it is read from all claws and too small, in every reading of the somata and at either pulse, when it is read from the claws that the model's input drives. From those claws, which in the unit of the recordings read less alike than the flies', it is too small in every other group as well, so that the ester pairs' step with APL on is the lead which these readings leave, and one that hangs on which claws are read.
- Before the KCs, the model's antennal lobe evens out the odors' total drive, which the flies' PN dendrites do not, and its distances between odors are within 0.05 of the dendrites' once the noise between flies is removed.

Every test so far has held the models to the KC somata, and the search on APL's side had ended with the lead on the responses that APL acts on, with a mechanism between the claw and the soma as what is wanted ([the co-response read with a checked estimate and the breadth weighting inside the models' APL](#breadth-weighting)). For twelve of the panel's odors (2h, IaA, pa, 2-but, eb, ep, 6al, t2h, 1-8ol, 1-5ol, 1-6ol and ms) the stages before the somata have been recorded in wild-type flies: the ORNs and the PN dendrites glomerulus by glomerulus, and the PN boutons and the KC claws in the calyx, as the responses of imaged regions.

The 66 pairs of these odors hold all 15 ester pairs and all 6 alcohol pairs of the common error. No model had been read against these recordings stage by stage.

The model's stages against the flies' stages changed no model and fitted nothing, so that no number of the main target moved: through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout) the family's loss is all pattern, {{E72/population.csv:group=all:cal_pattern ~ .3f}} for the mean over its eight wirings against a floor of {{E66/data_floor_parts.csv:data=graded;stat=apl_effect_rmse_centered:mean ~ .3f}}, as before. It read the family's PNs, boutons and claws as the recordings were made and asked, for each group of pairs, whether the model differs from the flies at a stage before the somata, at the step from claws to somata with APL on, or at that step without APL. A model's error in a pair's APL effect is its error at the first step minus its error at the second, so that the two steps say on which side of APL a group's error is made.

The model is the breadth-2 family on its eight wirings, each at its own fit ([the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population)), run again at fixed parameters with the PN rates, the bouton rates and APL's activity kept. Every run reproduces its saved fit spike for spike, with APL on and with APL off, and a model value below is the mean over the eight wirings.

The distance between two odors is one minus the Pearson correlation of their responses across the units of a stage: glomeruli, imaged regions, or the model's boutons, claws or KCs. That is the measure in which the bouton and the claw recordings exist; it is not the cosine distance of the main target. It is given as the mean over the pairs of a group: the 15 pairs among 2h, IaA, pa, eb, ep and ms, the 6 pairs among 1-8ol, 1-5ol, 1-6ol and 6al, the 24 pairs of an ester with an alcohol, the 21 other pairs, and the six pairs with near-identical ORN input ([the high per-claw knee without a dead zone](#claw-knee)), which are counted in the other groups as well.

Noise makes two odors look less alike than they are, so the flies' values are given with it removed where the recordings allow. For the boutons and the claws, which were recorded in a unit scaled region by region and exist fly by fly only, the trial noise is removed within each fly: the correlation between two odors across blocks of trials is divided by how well each odor's own response repeats across blocks, and the flies are then averaged. For the ORNs and the PN dendrites, whose units are the same glomeruli in every fly, the values are those of the flies' mean pattern, with the noise between flies removed in the same way across halves of the flies, because the model's input is that mean.

A stage of the model was read in three ways: as changes of rate; in the unit of the recordings, with each bouton's or claw's signal divided by its own standard deviation over a simulated session of the 16 odors; and in that unit through measurement noise at the flies' repeatability, with the noise then removed as it is for the flies.

A bouton's or a claw's response to an odor is its mean during the odor minus its level before the odor, and every reading of the model's boutons, claws and steps in this subsection takes that level once the model's KCs and APL have settled, as the mean over the last quarter of a second before the odor ([why, and what that moved](#fn-preodor-startup)). On the model's known values the removal of the noise is right to within {{lit:0.004 # the largest absolute value of column error in results/E90_model_stages/settled_preodor/noise_check.csv over every stage, subset, claw version, condition, group and single wiring (0.0041; 0.0010 for the mean over the eight wirings; 0.0031 and 0.0012 in results/E90_model_stages/noise_check.csv, with the level before the odor taken over the whole half second)}} for every group, where 0.03 was allowed.

What a claw's calcium signal reports is not known, so each claw of the model was read in three versions: its drive after APL's inhibition alone, and with a quarter or a half of its signal taken from its KC's spikes. The boutons were read on the 28 glomeruli that the recordings of the PN dendrites share with the model's input, the bouton recordings having been made with the same PN driver line, and the claws on all claws.

The rule was fixed before any run. A stage or a step counts as different from the flies' if the model's value is 0.05 or more from the flies', lies outside their 90 % interval and has at least six of the eight wirings on the same side, in every reading and, for the claws and the steps, in every version of a claw. A group is then upstream if its boutons or its claws differ, at one of the two steps if only that step differs, and not resolved if the readings disagree. For the steps the rule read the model's somata through the calibrated readout.

The distance between two odors at each stage, as the mean over the pairs of a group. A row of flies gives the mean and, in parentheses, its 90 % interval over the flies or recordings; the rows beneath it give the model's mean over the eight wirings, and a model value below the flies' means that the model's two odors are more alike than the flies'. The model's boutons and claws are in the unit of the recordings unless changes of rate are named, with APL on and from their settled level before the odor, and its somata are read through the calibrated readout. Every stage is in the same measure, one minus the Pearson correlation, so that the somata's values differ from the cosine distances used elsewhere on this page

**Before the KCs the model evens out the odors' total drive, which the flies do not; in the distances between odors it is close to the flies once their noise is removed.**

The coefficient of variation, over the 12 odors, of the response summed over the 28 shared glomeruli is {{E90/pn_stage.csv:reading=change:cv_totals ~ .3f}} in the model's PNs, for {{E90/pn_stage.csv:reading=orn_input:cv_totals ~ .3f}} in its ORN input; in the flies it is {{E90/pn_stage.csv:reading=pn_dend:cv_totals ~ .3f}} in the PN dendrites (90 % interval {{E90/al_transfer.csv:section=summary;map=linear;stat=cv_total_pn:lo ~ .3f}} to {{E90/al_transfer.csv:section=summary;map=linear;stat=cv_total_pn:hi ~ .3f}}) and {{E90/pn_stage.csv:reading=orn_dff:cv_totals ~ .3f}} in the ORNs. The model's antennal lobe thus removes most of the differences between odors in total drive, as had been seen from the model's side ([the input side of the error common to all wirings](#input-side)), and the recordings of the PN dendrites do not show it.

The distances between odors are another matter, and they depend on how the flies are read. Taken fly by fly and averaged, the PN dendrites hold two odors further apart than the model's PNs do, by {{diff:E90/pn_stage_noise_removed.csv:key=pn_dend28;reading=per_fly;group=ester:mean -- E90/pn_stage_noise_removed.csv:key=pn_dend28;reading=per_fly;group=ester:model_change ~ .2f}} among the ester pairs and {{diff:E90/pn_stage_noise_removed.csv:key=pn_dend28;reading=per_fly;group=alcohol:mean -- E90/pn_stage_noise_removed.csv:key=pn_dend28;reading=per_fly;group=alcohol:model_change ~ .2f}} among the alcohol pairs (third row of the table), and by the rule the PN stage would differ for the alcohol pairs and for the six pairs with near-identical ORN input.

But a fly's own distances carry its trial noise and its own deviations from the mean over flies, and the model's PN stage has neither, since its input is that mean. Read on the flies' mean pattern with the noise between flies removed (first two rows), the dendrites are {{diff:E90/pn_stage_noise_removed.csv:key=pn_dend28;reading=across_flies_noise_removed;group=ester_alcohol:mean -- E90/pn_stage_noise_removed.csv:key=orn_pebbled28;reading=across_flies_noise_removed;group=ester_alcohol:mean ~ .2f}} to {{diff:E90/pn_stage_noise_removed.csv:key=pn_dend28;reading=across_flies_noise_removed;group=other:mean -- E90/pn_stage_noise_removed.csv:key=orn_pebbled28;reading=across_flies_noise_removed;group=other:mean ~ .2f}} less alike than the ORNs, the model's PNs keep the distances of the ORNs, and they are within 0.05 of the dendrites in every group, so that by the rule the PN stage does not differ.

At the boutons the answer depends on the unit. As changes of rate the model's boutons keep the PNs' distances and are more alike than the flies' in every group but the ester pairs. In the unit of the recordings they are the flies' in every group but one, though the alcohol pairs lie at the margin of the rule ({{E90/settled_preodor/stages_model.csv:stage=bouton;subset=shared;share=0.0;cond=on;reading=session_z;wiring=population:alcohol ~ .3f}} against the flies' {{E90/stages_flies.csv:key=bouton_noise_removed;group=alcohol:mean ~ .3f}}, less alike; of the two readings in this unit the one through the noise counts as a difference by the rule and the other does not): the six pairs with near-identical ORN input are {{E90/settled_preodor/stages_model.csv:stage=bouton;subset=shared;share=0.0;cond=on;reading=session_z;wiring=population:near ~ .2f}} apart in the model and {{E90/stages_flies.csv:key=bouton_noise_removed;group=near:mean ~ .2f}} in the flies (90 % interval {{E90/stages_flies.csv:key=bouton_noise_removed;group=near:lo ~ .2f}} to {{E90/stages_flies.csv:key=bouton_noise_removed;group=near:hi ~ .2f}}), and they are too close in all three readings, so that for these pairs the rule says "upstream". That verdict is not firm.

The flies' boutons can only be read fly by fly, each fly's boutons carrying that fly's own input, where the model's carry the input averaged over flies. At the PN dendrites, where both readings can be made, the six pairs are {{E90/pn_stage_noise_removed.csv:key=pn_dend28;reading=per_fly_trial_noise_removed;group=near:mean ~ .3f}} apart fly by fly with the trial noise removed and {{E90/pn_stage_noise_removed.csv:key=pn_dend28;reading=across_flies_noise_removed;group=near:mean ~ .3f}} for the flies' mean pattern, a difference nearly as large as the one at the boutons. The same reservation holds for every row of boutons and claws in the table: if a fly's own part is as large there as in the dendrites, the flies' values overstate the distances of the mean pattern, which is what the model is given.

**At the claws the answer turns on what is read.** With all claws and the drive alone, the model's claws are more alike than the flies' in every group, and by a wide margin in the four groups that make up the 66 pairs (the rows of the claws in the table). Two things qualify that.

The first is what a claw's signal reports. With half of it taken from the KC's spikes, the model's claws come within 0.05 of the flies' for the ester pairs and the alcohol pairs in the unit of the recordings ({{E90/settled_preodor/stages_model.csv:stage=claw;subset=all;share=0.5;cond=on;reading=session_z;wiring=population:ester ~ .3f}} and {{E90/settled_preodor/stages_model.csv:stage=claw;subset=all;share=0.5;cond=on;reading=session_z;wiring=population:alcohol ~ .3f}} against {{E90/stages_flies.csv:key=claw_noise_removed;group=ester:mean ~ .3f}} and {{E90/stages_flies.csv:key=claw_noise_removed;group=alcohol:mean ~ .3f}}), and for the ester, the alcohol and the other pairs as changes of rate. By the rule the claws thus differ in some versions and not in others, and only the pairs of an ester with an alcohol are more alike than the flies' in all nine.

The second is which claws are read. The model's ORN input covers 36 of the wiring's 54 glomeruli, and the other 18 have no input for any odor. Their PNs carry only the antennal lobe's lateral signal, about {{lit:5 Hz # E90_model_stages.md, Summary, the claw-reading caveat: the PNs of the 18 glomeruli without ORN input carry about 5 Hz during an odor}} during an odor, and their claws are {{lit:17 % # E90_model_stages.md, Summary, the claw-reading caveat: 1679 of the real wiring's 9867 claws belong to the 18 glomeruli without ORN input}} of all claws. In the unit of the recordings each of those claws is scaled by its own small variability, which turns the lateral signal into a pattern that every odor shares and pulls every pair together.

On the claws of the 36 glomeruli with ORN input, in the unit of the recordings and with the drive alone, the model's claws are less alike than the flies' for the ester pairs and the alcohol pairs ({{E90/settled_preodor/stages_model.csv:stage=claw;subset=input;share=0.0;cond=on;reading=session_z;wiring=population:ester ~ .3f}} and {{E90/settled_preodor/stages_model.csv:stage=claw;subset=input;share=0.0;cond=on;reading=session_z;wiring=population:alcohol ~ .3f}} against {{E90/stages_flies.csv:key=claw_noise_removed;group=ester:mean ~ .3f}} and {{E90/stages_flies.csv:key=claw_noise_removed;group=alcohol:mean ~ .3f}}), and by {{diff:E90/settled_preodor/stages_model.csv:stage=claw;subset=input;share=0.0;cond=on;reading=session_z;wiring=population:other -- E90/stages_flies.csv:key=claw_noise_removed;group=other:mean ~ .3f}} for the other pairs and {{diff:E90/settled_preodor/stages_model.csv:stage=claw;subset=input;share=0.0;cond=on;reading=session_z;wiring=population:near -- E90/stages_flies.csv:key=claw_noise_removed;group=near:mean ~ .3f}} for the six nearest pairs; only for the pairs of an ester with an alcohol are they the flies' ({{E90/settled_preodor/stages_model.csv:stage=claw;subset=input;share=0.0;cond=on;reading=session_z;wiring=population:ester_alcohol ~ .3f}} against {{E90/stages_flies.csv:key=claw_noise_removed;group=ester_alcohol:mean ~ .3f}}). As changes of rate those claws are more alike than the flies' for the alcohol pairs, the pairs of an ester with an alcohol and the other pairs: for the alcohol and the other pairs the two units thus differ in direction.

Which claws to read was chosen from how the recordings were made, all claws because a claw region is imaged whichever PN it receives from, after one wiring's readings had been seen and before the verdict. The reading on the 36 glomeruli was added after the verdict, as a check of how much it depends on that choice, and it is not the verdict.

By the rule, with all claws the ester pairs, the alcohol pairs and the other pairs are not resolved and the pairs of an ester with an alcohol are upstream; with the claws of the 36 glomeruli, or of the 28 shared ones, all four groups are not resolved. Where the two groups of the common error leave the flies is not decided by these recordings.

**In wild-type flies the step from claws to somata carries the pattern of the main target.** The flies' own steps need no model. With APL the somata hold two odors further apart than the claws do in every group, and more so among the ester pairs than among the alcohol pairs: the ester pairs' step exceeds the alcohol pairs' by {{E90/steps_flies_summary.csv:step=on_remy;claw=claw_noise_removed:ester_minus_alcohol ~ +.3f}} with the somata of wild-type flies (90 % interval {{E90/steps_flies_summary.csv:step=on_remy;claw=claw_noise_removed:ester_minus_alcohol_lo ~ +.2f}} to {{E90/steps_flies_summary.csv:step=on_remy;claw=claw_noise_removed:ester_minus_alcohol_hi ~ +.2f}}) and by {{E90/steps_flies_summary.csv:step=on_ctrl;claw=claw_noise_removed:ester_minus_alcohol ~ +.3f}} with those of the control flies ({{E90/steps_flies_summary.csv:step=on_ctrl;claw=claw_noise_removed:ester_minus_alcohol_lo ~ +.2f}} to {{E90/steps_flies_summary.csv:step=on_ctrl;claw=claw_noise_removed:ester_minus_alcohol_hi ~ +.2f}}), over the same four claw flies.

Without APL, with the somata of the flies with APL output blocked (TNT), the step is small, its interval reaching zero in three of the four groups, and the two groups do not differ ({{E90/steps_flies_summary.csv:step=off_tnt;claw=claw_noise_removed:ester_minus_alcohol ~ +.3f}}, {{E90/steps_flies_summary.csv:step=off_tnt;claw=claw_noise_removed:ester_minus_alcohol_lo ~ +.2f}} to {{E90/steps_flies_summary.csv:step=off_tnt;claw=claw_noise_removed:ester_minus_alcohol_hi ~ +.2f}}). In the flies, then, most of what the somata add to the claws' distances needs APL, and the difference between the esters and the alcohols that the models miss is made with APL on, in flies that share nothing with the recordings with APL output blocked (TNT).

Over the 66 pairs the step in wild-type flies follows the per-pair APL effect of the main target, with a Pearson correlation of {{E90/steps_flies_summary.csv:step=on_remy;claw=claw_noise_removed:r_effect ~ .2f}} with the trial noise removed from the claws and {{E90/steps_flies_summary.csv:step=on_remy;claw=claw_measured:r_effect ~ .2f}} with the claws as measured, and it runs against the common error ({{E90/steps_flies_summary.csv:step=on_remy;claw=claw_noise_removed:r_common_error ~ +.2f}}): the pairs on which the models' APL effect is too small are those with the larger step.

A rule fixed beforehand said when this step may be used as a second reading of the target's pattern. The two halves of the four claw flies had to agree on it at 0.6 or more, and its floor, the distance between a step from resampled flies and the measured one, had to be at most half of its standard deviation over the pairs. It passes in both readings of the claws, clearly on the first condition and by a hair on the second (second table below).

The step from claws to somata by group of pairs: the distance across the somata minus the distance across the claws, as the mean over a group's pairs. The flies' steps use the claws of wild-type flies with the trial noise removed and are given with the 90 % interval over resampled flies of both stages. The model's are the mean over the eight wirings, from its claws with APL on, the drive alone, in the unit of the recordings and from their settled level before the odor; the rule read its somata through the calibrated readout, and raw spike counts are given beside for the claws of the 36 glomeruli

The step from claws to somata in the flies, over the 66 pairs. The per-pair APL effect is the main target's (the control flies' cosine distance minus that with APL output blocked (TNT), all recordings); the steps of the control flies and of the flies with APL output blocked (TNT) share their somata with it, and the step of wild-type flies shares no fly with it. The rule for using the step in wild-type flies as a second reading of the target's pattern asked that the two halves of the four claw flies agree at 0.6 or more and that the floor be at most half of the standard deviation over the pairs, in both readings of the claws

**The model's steps depend first on the claws they start from; the step with APL on is too small for the nearest pairs throughout, and for the ester pairs it is the flies' from all claws and too small from the claws that the input drives.**

From all claws the model's step with APL on is the flies' for the ester pairs ({{E90/settled_preodor/steps_by_reading.csv:step=on;soma=cal_pearson;claws=all;group=ester:model ~ +.3f}} against the control flies' {{E90/settled_preodor/steps_by_reading.csv:step=on;soma=cal_pearson;claws=all;group=ester:flies ~ +.3f}}) and about twice the flies' for the alcohol pairs, the pairs of an ester with an alcohol and the other pairs (first of the two tables above). That excess is the other side of claws that read too alike, and it is partly made by the glomeruli without input.

From the claws of the 36 glomeruli with ORN input the step with APL on is too small in every group and in every reading of the somata. For the ester pairs it is {{E90/settled_preodor/steps_by_reading.csv:step=on;soma=cal_pearson;claws=input;group=ester:model ~ +.3f}} through the calibrated readout and {{E90/settled_preodor/steps_by_reading.csv:step=on;soma=raw_pearson;claws=input;group=ester:model ~ +.3f}} on raw spike counts against the control flies' {{E90/settled_preodor/steps_by_reading.csv:step=on;soma=cal_pearson;claws=input;group=ester:flies ~ +.3f}}, and {{E90/settled_preodor/steps_by_reading.csv:step=on;soma=cal_cosine;claws=input;group=ester:diff ~ +.2f}} and {{E90/settled_preodor/steps_by_reading.csv:step=on;soma=raw_cosine;claws=input;group=ester:diff ~ +.2f}} from the flies' with the somata's distances taken as cosine; for the alcohol pairs it is {{E90/settled_preodor/steps_by_reading.csv:step=on;soma=cal_pearson;claws=input;group=alcohol:model ~ +.3f}} and {{E90/settled_preodor/steps_by_reading.csv:step=on;soma=raw_pearson;claws=input;group=alcohol:model ~ +.3f}} against {{E90/settled_preodor/steps_by_reading.csv:step=on;soma=cal_pearson;claws=input;group=alcohol:flies ~ +.3f}}.

A part of that shortfall is in turn the other side of claws that read too far apart. For the alcohol pairs it is nearly all of it: their claws are {{diff:E90/settled_preodor/stages_model.csv:stage=claw;subset=input;share=0.0;cond=on;reading=session_z;wiring=population:alcohol -- E90/stages_flies.csv:key=claw_noise_removed;group=alcohol:mean ~ .3f}} less alike than the flies' and their step through the calibrated readout is {{diff:E90/settled_preodor/steps_by_reading.csv:step=on;soma=cal_pearson;claws=input;group=alcohol:flies -- E90/settled_preodor/steps_by_reading.csv:step=on;soma=cal_pearson;claws=input;group=alcohol:model ~ .3f}} smaller, the somata being the control flies' in that reading ({{E90/stages_model.csv:stage=soma;subset=all;share=0.0;cond=on;reading=cal_pearson;wiring=population:alcohol ~ .3f}} against {{E90/stages_flies.csv:key=soma_ctrl;group=alcohol:mean ~ .3f}}). For the ester pairs it is a third: their claws are {{diff:E90/settled_preodor/stages_model.csv:stage=claw;subset=input;share=0.0;cond=on;reading=session_z;wiring=population:ester -- E90/stages_flies.csv:key=claw_noise_removed;group=ester:mean ~ .3f}} less alike and their step {{diff:E90/settled_preodor/steps_by_reading.csv:step=on;soma=cal_pearson;claws=input;group=ester:flies -- E90/settled_preodor/steps_by_reading.csv:step=on;soma=cal_pearson;claws=input;group=ester:model ~ .3f}} smaller, and the rest is at the somata, which the model holds less far apart than the control flies' ({{E90/stages_model.csv:stage=soma;subset=all;share=0.0;cond=on;reading=cal_pearson;wiring=population:ester ~ .3f}} against {{E90/stages_flies.csv:key=soma_ctrl;group=ester:mean ~ .3f}}). For the six pairs with near-identical ORN input the step is too small in each of these readings and from either set of claws.

The step without APL depends on the claws in the same way. From the claws of the 36 glomeruli it is below the flies' and below zero for the ester pairs and the alcohol pairs in every reading of the somata: {{E90/settled_preodor/steps_by_reading.csv:step=off;soma=cal_pearson;claws=input;group=ester:model ~ +.3f}} and {{E90/settled_preodor/steps_by_reading.csv:step=off;soma=cal_pearson;claws=input;group=alcohol:model ~ +.3f}} through the calibrated readout, which the rule had named, and {{E90/settled_preodor/steps_by_reading.csv:step=off;soma=raw_pearson;claws=input;group=ester:model ~ +.3f}} and {{E90/settled_preodor/steps_by_reading.csv:step=off;soma=raw_pearson;claws=input;group=alcohol:model ~ +.3f}} on raw spike counts, against the flies' {{E90/settled_preodor/steps_by_reading.csv:step=off;soma=cal_pearson;claws=input;group=ester:flies ~ +.3f}} and {{E90/settled_preodor/steps_by_reading.csv:step=off;soma=cal_pearson;claws=input;group=alcohol:flies ~ +.3f}}; and {{E90/settled_preodor/steps_by_reading.csv:step=off;soma=raw_cosine;claws=input;group=ester:model ~ +.3f}} and {{E90/settled_preodor/steps_by_reading.csv:step=off;soma=raw_cosine;claws=input;group=alcohol:model ~ +.3f}} with those counts' distances taken as cosine, against {{E90/settled_preodor/steps_by_reading.csv:step=off;soma=raw_cosine;claws=input;group=ester:flies ~ +.3f}} and {{E90/settled_preodor/steps_by_reading.csv:step=off;soma=raw_cosine;claws=input;group=alcohol:flies ~ +.3f}}.

From these claws the model's somata with APL off are more alike than its claws, where the flies' are not. That is the opposite of the outcome that had been looked for, a model whose KCs separate their input without APL more than the flies' do. From all claws it does not hold: there the step without APL is below zero in no reading of the somata, and through the calibrated readout it is the flies' for the ester pairs and the alcohol pairs ({{E90/settled_preodor/steps_by_reading.csv:step=off;soma=cal_pearson;claws=all;group=ester:model ~ +.3f}} and {{E90/settled_preodor/steps_by_reading.csv:step=off;soma=cal_pearson;claws=all;group=alcohol:model ~ +.3f}}). That the model's KCs without APL bring two odors closer than their claw input therefore depends on which claws are read, and it is not a result.

Under the reading of the rule on the claws of the 36 glomeruli both groups fall short at both steps, the ester pairs by about as much at either and the alcohol pairs by more without APL, which is where their excess APL effect would then be made; from these claws each of the four shortfalls is found in every reading of the somata, and from all claws none is. What depends neither on the claws nor on the level from which they are read is the difference between a group's two steps, its error in the APL effect, since both steps start from the same claws.

The pulse does not lift the ester pairs' shortfall. At the flies' 2 s pulse, read on the real wiring with both response rates held again ([the flies' recording protocol in the model](#flies-protocol)), the PNs, the boutons as changes of rate, all claws and the somata move by {{lit:0.012 # the largest change from the 0.5 s to the 2 s pulse over the five groups in results/E90_model_stages/settled_preodor/stages_b5.csv (wiring=real against wiring=real_pulse2), rows with APL on for the PNs as changes of rate (0.009), the boutons of the shared glomeruli as changes of rate (0.012), all claws in the unit of the recordings (0.007) and the somata through the calibrated readout (0.006)}} at most with APL on.

The readings in the unit of the recordings on the glomeruli with input do move: among the ester pairs the boutons of the 28 shared glomeruli are {{diff:E90/settled_preodor/stages_b5.csv:stage=bouton;subset=shared;share=0.0;cond=on;reading=session_z;wiring=real:ester -- E90/settled_preodor/stages_b5.csv:stage=bouton;subset=shared;share=0.0;cond=on;reading=session_z;wiring=real_pulse2:ester ~ .3f}} more alike than at the family's 0.5 s pulse, and the claws of the 36 glomeruli {{diff:E90/settled_preodor/stages_b5.csv:stage=claw;subset=input;share=0.0;cond=on;reading=session_z;wiring=real:ester -- E90/settled_preodor/stages_b5.csv:stage=claw;subset=input;share=0.0;cond=on;reading=session_z;wiring=real_pulse2:ester ~ .3f}} more alike, at {{E90/settled_preodor/stages_b5.csv:stage=claw;subset=input;share=0.0;cond=on;reading=session_z;wiring=real_pulse2:ester ~ .3f}} against the flies' {{E90/stages_flies.csv:key=claw_noise_removed;group=ester:mean ~ .3f}}, so that at this pulse they are about as far apart as the flies'. The ester pairs' step with APL on from those claws is then {{diff:E90/settled_preodor/stages_b5.csv:stage=soma;subset=all;share=0.0;cond=on;reading=cal_pearson;wiring=real_pulse2:ester -- E90/settled_preodor/stages_b5.csv:stage=claw;subset=input;share=0.0;cond=on;reading=session_z;wiring=real_pulse2:ester ~ +.3f}} through the calibrated readout and {{diff:E90/settled_preodor/stages_b5.csv:stage=soma;subset=all;share=0.0;cond=on;reading=raw_pearson;wiring=real_pulse2:ester -- E90/settled_preodor/stages_b5.csv:stage=claw;subset=input;share=0.0;cond=on;reading=session_z;wiring=real_pulse2:ester ~ +.3f}} on raw counts, both still short of the flies' {{E90/settled_preodor/steps_by_reading.csv:step=on;soma=cal_pearson;claws=input;group=ester:flies ~ +.3f}}; for the six nearest pairs it stays too small in both ({{diff:E90/settled_preodor/stages_b5.csv:stage=soma;subset=all;share=0.0;cond=on;reading=cal_pearson;wiring=real_pulse2:near -- E90/settled_preodor/stages_b5.csv:stage=claw;subset=input;share=0.0;cond=on;reading=session_z;wiring=real_pulse2:near ~ +.3f}} and {{diff:E90/settled_preodor/stages_b5.csv:stage=soma;subset=all;share=0.0;cond=on;reading=raw_pearson;wiring=real_pulse2:near -- E90/settled_preodor/stages_b5.csv:stage=claw;subset=input;share=0.0;cond=on;reading=session_z;wiring=real_pulse2:near ~ +.3f}} against {{E90/settled_preodor/steps_by_reading.csv:step=on;soma=cal_pearson;claws=input;group=near:flies ~ +.3f}}). The reading from the 36 glomeruli was, besides, added after the verdict.

What the model's side leaves is one difference that holds throughout, the nearest pairs' step with APL on, and one lead, the ester pairs with APL on: the model's somata do not hold the esters as far apart as the flies' somata do, and whether its step from claws to somata is short for them depends on which claws are read.

**The family with the firing ceiling reads the same, and the one respect in which the antennal lobe differs from the recordings is one that the main target does not reward.** Two further readings had been made conditional.

Because the step in wild-type flies passed its test, the family with the firing ceiling was read in the same way on the four wirings on which it has been fitted ([the firing ceiling for the KCs](#firing-ceiling); [the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population)), beside the breadth-2 family on the same four. Its claws are the breadth-2 family's to within {{lit:0.03 # the largest absolute difference between families fc_S4 and C2_S4 over the five groups and the three sets of claws (all, input and shared), results/E90_model_stages/settled_preodor/d1_steps.csv, rows stage=claw, cond=on, share=0.0, reading=session_z (0.025; 0.021 in results/E90_model_stages/d1_steps.csv, with the level before the odor taken over the whole half second)}}, and its steps are a little smaller, by {{lit:0.01 to 0.04 # the breadth-2 family's step minus the firing-ceiling family's over the five groups and the two sets of claws, results/E90_model_stages/settled_preodor/d1_steps.csv, rows step=on, soma=cal_pearson, share=0.0, reading=session_z, subset=all and input (0.009 to 0.044)}} with APL on and {{lit:0.01 to 0.06 # the same for rows step=off of results/E90_model_stages/settled_preodor/d1_steps.csv (0.012 to 0.059)}} without; from the claws of the 36 glomeruli the ester pairs' step with APL on is {{E90/settled_preodor/d1_steps.csv:family=fc_S4;step=on;soma=cal_pearson;subset=input;share=0.0;reading=session_z:ester ~ +.3f}} against {{E90/settled_preodor/d1_steps.csv:family=C2_S4;step=on;soma=cal_pearson;subset=input;share=0.0;reading=session_z:ester ~ +.3f}}. The two families are as level on the steps as on the main target, where the pattern part through the calibrated readout is {{E72/partG_population.csv:family=40:cal_pattern ~ .4f}} with the ceiling and {{E72/partG_population.csv:family=none:cal_pattern ~ .4f}} without it on those wirings (lower is better; floor {{E66/data_floor_parts.csv:data=graded;stat=apl_effect_rmse_centered:mean ~ .3f}}).

The other reading set the antennal-lobe settings of the earlier screen ([the input side of the error common to all wirings](#input-side)) against the PN dendrites, beside the scores that those settings had on the main target on the real wiring with both response rates held. It had been made conditional on the PN stage differing from the recordings, which it does only with the dendrites read fly by fly, so that it stands as a description.

A weaker normalization, at the weakest of its four steps, raises the coefficient of variation of the odors' totals from {{E90/d2_pn_settings.csv:point_id=S1_identity:cv_totals ~ .3f}} to {{E90/d2_pn_settings.csv:point_id=S1_inhadd3141:cv_totals ~ .3f}}, half of the dendrites', and the pattern part rises with it from {{E90/d2_pn_settings.csv:point_id=S1_identity:cal_pattern ~ .3f}} to {{E90/d2_pn_settings.csv:point_id=S1_inhadd3141:cal_pattern ~ .3f}} (worse). The setting nearer the dendrites in the totals is thus not the one that the main target prefers, which is the model's own. The comparison of the settings by their distances between odors was made against the dendrites read fly by fly and is not read here.

**Realism.** Nothing was fitted and no parameter was added. Every run is a saved fit run again with its internal rates kept, and each reproduces its saved spike counts exactly, so that the runs are inside the four realism bands as their fits are: response rates of {{E90/variants.csv:real:rate_on ~ .3f}} to {{E90/variants.csv:P3:rate_on ~ .3f}} with APL on and {{E90/variants.csv:P4:rate_acute_off ~ .3f}} to {{E90/variants.csv:P2:rate_acute_off ~ .3f}} with APL off over the eight wirings (the flies' {{data:noise_ctrl_frac ~ .3f}} and {{data:noise_tnt_frac ~ .3f}}), and likewise the fit at the flies' 2 s pulse and the four fits with the firing ceiling.

The experiment is itself a reading of the base model's realism below the somata, and what it finds is above: an antennal lobe that evens out the odors' total drive; a third of the wiring's glomeruli without ORN input, whose claws, a sixth of all, carry only a lateral signal; boutons that match the flies' in the unit of the recordings in every group but the nearest pairs, the alcohol pairs lying at the margin of the rule; and somata that with APL on are more alike than the control flies' among the ester pairs ({{E90/stages_model.csv:stage=soma;subset=all;share=0.0;cond=on;reading=cal_pearson;wiring=population:ester ~ .3f}} through the calibrated readout and {{E90/stages_model.csv:stage=soma;subset=all;share=0.0;cond=on;reading=raw_pearson;wiring=population:ester ~ .3f}} on raw counts against {{E90/stages_flies.csv:key=soma_ctrl;group=ester:mean ~ .3f}} in this measure).

At the 2 s pulse the family without a firing ceiling fires up to {{lit:124 # results/E90_model_stages/b5_realism.json, pulse2.max_count_on}} spikes per KC and odor with APL on and {{lit:236 # results/E90_model_stages/b5_realism.json, pulse2.max_count_off}} with APL off, far more than a KC has been recorded to fire, and the fits with the ceiling stay at {{lit:9 to 15 # E90_model_stages.md, Realism table: the largest spike count per KC and odor with APL on over the four firing-ceiling fits}} and {{lit:21 to 29 # E90_model_stages.md, Realism table: the largest spike count per KC and odor with APL off over the four firing-ceiling fits}}. What is hard to defend lies in the comparison more than in the model.

The signal of the PN dendrites is calcium in the dendrites, not the PNs' output, and it saturates for the strongest responses; passed through a saturating map that bounds this, the dendrites' totals spread further still (a coefficient of variation of {{E90/al_transfer.csv:section=summary;map=saturating;stat=cv_total_pn:value ~ .2f}}). The dendrites and the boutons were recorded with a driver line that labels about seven PNs in ten. An imaged region is not one bouton or one claw: a claw region holds about {{lit:14 # notes/remy-summary.md, cited in E90_model_stages.md, Realism: a claw region averages about 14 claws of 14 KCs}} claws of as many KCs, where the model's units are single. A claw's signal may carry its KC's spikes.

A fly's boutons and claws carry that fly's own input, and the model's the mean over flies. There are four claw flies and five bouton flies. And the stage recordings are of wild-type flies at 3 s pulses, the KC recordings of the main target of flies after three days at 31 °C at 2 s pulses, and the model's readings of a 0.5 s pulse. The stage recordings hold twelve odors, so that no pair of paa, euc, -aPine or B-myr is in any number of this subsection but those of the main target, and their [ORN input of another concentration](#fn-concentrations) enters the stage readings only through the calibrated readout's constant, which is set on all 16 odors.

**What follows.** Where along the pathway the common error is made is not decided by these recordings, and the model's side of this subsection is a set of readings, not a verdict. What would decide it is on the flies' side: the responses of the imaged bouton and claw regions odor by odor and trial by trial, where only distances between odors are on hand, and the outline of the claw regions. With them the claws can be read on the regions that the model's input reaches, the share of a claw's signal that comes from its KC's spikes can be estimated from the claws' own time course, and a fly's own part can be told from the mean pattern, as it was for the PN dendrites. They are asked of the experimenter who made the recordings.

Meanwhile four things are carried forward. The step from claws to somata in wild-type flies is given beside the main target for every later mechanism, with its floor: it reads the target's pattern on flies that share nothing with the recordings with APL output blocked (TNT), and whether it is also kept out of fits as a test is a choice still to be made.

The step with APL on joins the brief of the mechanism between the claw and the soma that the lead asks for ([above](#breadth-weighting)): for the nearest pairs in every reading, and for the ester pairs as a lead, their step being too small from the claws that the input drives and the flies' from all claws. A change at that step that leaves the responses without APL as they are, APL's inhibition summed over a KC's claws in place of clipped at each claw, has since been run and is level on the main target ([below](#summed-drive)).

The step without APL does not join it as a result: that the model's KCs without APL bring two odors closer than their claw input holds from the claws that the input drives, in every reading of the somata, and not from all claws, so that a family which would not do so is read from both sets of claws, on raw counts and through the readout alike.

The somata of both sides have since been read alike, the flies' with their trial noise removed and the model's as the recordings are normalized ([below](#steps-like-for-like)). With APL on the model's ester pairs are then too alike and its alcohol pairs too far apart in every reading. Without APL the model's somata are the flies' if a KC's signal is taken to saturate with its firing and too far apart if it is not, and in no such reading are the alcohol pairs too alike: the reading in which their excess is made at the step without APL, by somata that are too alike there, holds only with the calibrated readout set against the flies' trial means.

The antennal lobe's evening-out of the odors' totals stands as a difference between the base model and the flies; a fit of that stage to the PN dendrites had been kept for a verdict that names the PN stage alone, which has not come, and the settings tried say that the main target would not reward it at fixed scales.

And before the stages are read again, the 18 glomeruli without ORN input are given input or left out of the claws that are read, and the PN dendrites and the ORNs are read on the flies' mean pattern. The first has since been done for the ten of the 18 for which responses to the panel's odors have been measured, and the reading of the claws moves to the margin of the rule: with all claws the pairs of an ester with an alcohol, upstream with the lab's input, are narrowly not resolved with the fuller input, and on the claws of the glomeruli with input the four groups that make up the 66 pairs are not resolved ([below](#missing-glomeruli)). What is taken up from here is with the pending work at the end of the page.

### APL's inhibition on the KC's summed drive: whether an inhibition summed over a KC's claws, in place of one clipped at each claw, lowers the pattern part {#summed-drive}

%%% hover
summed form: In a model, APL's inhibition of a KC charged to the sum of the KC's claws: the inhibition that a claw cannot absorb, because it exceeds the claw's own input, is taken from the KC's other claws, all of it unless a share is named. In every other model on this page a claw loses to APL no more than its own input, the clipping at each claw. Off in every model except those of the subsection on APL's inhibition on the KC's summed drive.
%%%

**In every model so far APL's inhibition of a KC is taken from each claw separately, and a claw can lose no more than its own input.** Charging the inhibition that a claw cannot absorb to the KC's other claws, so that APL acts on the KC's summed drive, does not lower the pattern part. On the fits as they are it is level at the family's breadth weighting, at an exponent of 1 it gives back about a quarter of what the weaker weighting loses and at weaker weightings nothing, and against no half of the recordings is a setting with the summed form the best. The family fitted again with the summed form is level as well.

Only on the base with the flies' recruitment does the summed form gain: there a weighting with an exponent of 1 reads lower than the base's own family, on the four wirings of the earlier searches and, against recordings that it was not chosen on, on the four others. That gain is half of what the test asks, an inhibition that is the same for every odor gives more than half of it, and it makes up about what that base costs against the fits as they are.

What the clipping holds back sits in the many-clawed, broadly responding KCs that the family's weighting already loads, so that the summed form acts as a second breadth weighting. For the feedback APL's subtraction from the KCs, the weighting and now the place where it is summed are closed on the fits as they are; what was left on APL's side in this family, a gain on each claw's drive in place of the subtraction and the form of APL's inhibition of the boutons, has been run since, in the subsection that follows this one.

The search on APL's side had left one property of the feedback APL's inhibition of the KCs that nothing had varied ([above](#breadth-weighting)): the place where it is subtracted. In the model a claw's drive is its PN input minus APL's inhibition of that claw, and a drive below zero is set to zero before the KC sums its claws. A KC that an odor drives through one or two strong claws therefore loses little to APL, however many claws it has, while a KC driven through many weak claws loses most of its drive.

If the inhibition acts on the sum instead, every claw's inhibition is charged whether the odor drives that claw or not, and APL removes the KCs with many undriven claws. That is a selection of responders made between the claw and the soma, with the responses without APL left exactly as they are. The KCs it would remove are of the kind that the model's APL had been found to remove among the shared responders, broad and many-clawed ([the common error split into who responds and how strongly](#responder-sets)), so that the summed form might have done the work of the family's weighting without weights as unequal as the family's.

The summed form adds to a KC's sum a share of the inhibition that its claws could not absorb: none of it in every model so far, half of it, or all of it, at which a KC sums its claws' inhibition as it sums their excitation. What is saved of each claw, and what drives APL, stays clipped; the responses with APL off do not change; and nothing is fitted. With no share the new code reproduces the saved fits spike for spike, and with APL off it does so with the whole share as well.

The breadth-2 family was run on the four wirings of the earlier searches, each at its own fit ([the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population)), in three parts. The first changed no model: for every KC and odor of the fits as they are, the inhibition that the claws do not absorb was set against the KC's summed drive, and from it the responders that the whole share would remove were predicted.

The second ran the share at a half and in full on the fits as they are, at the family's weighting (the family's measure of a KC's breadth at an exponent of 2), at exponents of 1 and 0.5 and without a weighting, with the APL scale set again to the fit's number of responses with APL on; and the share in full on the base with the flies' recruitment (each odor's response fraction without APL set to the flies' by a threshold for the odor, an [oracle](#fn-oracle)), at exponents of 2 and 1 and without a weighting, with the APL scale for each odor set again to the control flies' response rate.

The references with the clipping are the runs of the breadth weightings ([above](#breadth-weighting)). On each base the setting with the lowest pattern part of the mean over the four wirings, through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout) and against one half of the recordings, was to be read on the four other wirings against the other half, by the test that the fitted changes were put to ([above](#cross-wiring-fit)), if it was lower than the base's own family by 0.0015 or more; the halves were those of two splits of the flies.

A setting that got that far was set against a control: the clipped form with a fixed inhibition added at each KC's soma with APL on, equal for every odor to the mean of what the summed form takes from that KC. The control keeps how strongly each KC is inhibited and removes the dependence on which claws an odor drives, and it had to gain less than half as much as the setting. The third part fitted the family again with the whole share, from each wiring's own fit and with the same free parameters, so that the two families are compared like for like.

**What the clipping holds back is in the KCs that the family's weighting already loads.** In the fits as they are, the inhibition that a responding KC's claws do not absorb is {{E91/unabsorbed.csv:unit=S;kind=responders;cls=with APL on:U_over_D_mean ~ .2f}} of its summed drive, as the mean over the KC × odor entries that respond with APL on, on the four wirings and over the odor pulse. It is spread very unevenly. By quarter of the family's breadth weights it is {{E91/unabsorbed.csv:unit=S;kind=breadth_quartile;cls=Q4:U_over_D_mean ~ .2f}} of the drive in the top quarter, {{E91/unabsorbed.csv:unit=S;kind=breadth_quartile;cls=Q3:U_over_D_mean ~ .2f}} in the third and at most {{E91/unabsorbed.csv:unit=S;kind=breadth_quartile;cls=Q2:U_over_D_mean ~ .3f}} in the lower half; by number of claws it is {{E91/unabsorbed.csv:unit=S;kind=n_claws;cls=4:U_over_D_mean ~ .2f}} for a KC with four claws and {{E91/unabsorbed.csv:unit=S;kind=n_claws;cls=9:U_over_D_mean ~ .2f}} for one with nine.

Half of a responder's drive comes through {{E91/unabsorbed.csv:unit=S;kind=responders;cls=with APL on:n_half_on_median ~ .0f}} of its claws at the median, so that the more claws a KC has, the more of its claws' inhibition goes unabsorbed. The summed form therefore charges the broad, many-clawed KCs, the same that the weighting charges. For the shared responders of the ester pairs that survive APL it is {{E91/unabsorbed.csv:unit=S;kind=ester_shared;cls=survive:U_over_D_mean ~ .2f}} of the drive, and for those of the alcohol pairs {{E91/unabsorbed.csv:unit=S;kind=alcohol_shared;cls=survive:U_over_D_mean ~ .2f}}.

The prediction made from these numbers was no guide. Taking as removed the responders whose drive, less the inhibition that their claws do not absorb, falls below threshold, the predicted change of the per-pair APL effect correlates with the simulated one at {{lit:0.50 # results/E91_summed_drive_inhibition/prediction.json, units, entry removed:S:cal, r_reheld (0.503): the Pearson correlation over the 120 pairs between the predicted and the simulated change of the per-pair APL effect, the rows of prediction.csv with readout=cal, unit=S, prediction=removed and sim=reheld}} over the 120 pairs (Pearson correlation; the mean over the four wirings through the calibrated readout), where 0.8 had been asked before the prediction would be relied on. As with the static forms of inhibition ([above](#responder-sets)), what a change of APL does to the per-pair effect is read from simulations only.

APL's inhibition summed over a KC's claws against the same inhibition clipped at each claw: the mean over the four wirings of the earlier searches against the main target as measured, all recordings, through the calibrated readout. The squares of the amplitude part and the shape part add up to the squared pattern part, and a spread below one means that APL moves the model's pairs apart more evenly than the flies'; no setting is chosen by a correlation ([why](#fn-pattern-split)). **On the fits as they are the summed form is level.** At the family's weighting the whole share reads a pattern part of {{E91/spread.csv:variant=B1_F_k2_s1;unit=S;readout=cal;target=z8:pattern ~ .4f}} and the half share {{E91/readings.csv:variant=B1_F_k2_s0.5;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, for the unchanged fits' {{E91/spread.csv:variant=B1_F_k2;unit=S;readout=cal;target=z8:pattern ~ .4f}}: higher by {{diff:E91/readings.csv:variant=B1_F_k2_s1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern -- E91/readings.csv:variant=B1_F_k2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} and {{diff:E91/readings.csv:variant=B1_F_k2_s0.5;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern -- E91/readings.csv:variant=B1_F_k2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, where a change within 0.003 either way had been expected (first rows of the table).

The spread of the model's effect comes toward the flies' and its shape part rises, and the second outweighs the first. The two groups of pairs trade against each other, as they did when the weighting was changed ([above](#breadth-weighting)): the ester pairs' shortfall shrinks by {{diff:E91/readings.csv:variant=B1_F_k2_s1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_ester -- E91/readings.csv:variant=B1_F_k2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_ester ~ .3f}} and the alcohol pairs' excess grows by {{diff:E91/readings.csv:variant=B1_F_k2_s1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_alcohol -- E91/readings.csv:variant=B1_F_k2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_alcohol ~ .3f}}.

At an exponent of 1 the whole share gives back {{diff:E91/readings.csv:variant=B1_F_k1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern -- E91/readings.csv:variant=B1_F_k1_s1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} of the {{diff:E91/readings.csv:variant=B1_F_k1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern -- E91/readings.csv:variant=B1_F_k2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} that the weaker weighting costs, in the shape part, just under the 0.002 to 0.008 that had been expected; at an exponent of 0.5 and without a weighting it changes the pattern part by {{diff:E91/readings.csv:variant=B1_F_k0.5_s1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern -- E91/readings.csv:variant=B1_F_k0.5;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ +.4f}} and {{diff:E91/readings.csv:variant=B1_none_s1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern -- E91/readings.csv:variant=B1_none;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ +.4f}}. No weaker weighting with the summed form is therefore an equal of the family's, as that was defined for the weightings ([above](#breadth-weighting)): the nearest, an exponent of 1 with the whole share, is {{E91/equal.csv:B1_F_k1_s1:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} higher, where an equal had to be within 0.003.

Against each of the four halves of the recordings the setting with the lowest pattern part is the unchanged fits' own, so that nothing went to the four other wirings. The other readings agree. On raw counts the loss with the whole share at the family's weighting is {{E91/readings.csv:variant=B1_F_k2_s1;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_loss ~ .4f}} for {{E91/readings.csv:variant=B1_F_k2;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_loss ~ .4f}}, and against the six recordings that are alike the pattern part is {{E91/readings.csv:variant=B1_F_k2_s1;unit=S;readout=cal:z6_pattern ~ .4f}} for {{E91/readings.csv:variant=B1_F_k2;unit=S;readout=cal:z6_pattern ~ .4f}}. The alcohol pairs' co-response change under APL, as trial means at the reading's own noise, is {{E91/coresponse.csv:variant=B1_F_k2_s1;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} with the whole share for {{E91/coresponse.csv:variant=B1_F_k2;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} with the clipping, against the flies' {{E91/coresponse.csv:variant=B1_F_k2;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:flies_ratio ~ .2f}} ({{E91/coresponse.csv:variant=B1_F_k2;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:flies_lo ~ .2f}} to {{E91/coresponse.csv:variant=B1_F_k2;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:flies_hi ~ .2f}}): the summed form does not move it.

One further step that the model's code allows was run at the family's weighting, the clipping lifted altogether, so that a claw inhibited beyond its input also lowers what APL itself receives from that claw (the fourth row of the table). Its pattern part is within {{diff:E91/readings.csv:variant=B1_F_k2_s1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern -- E91/readings.csv:variant=B3_F_k2_net;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} of the summed form's, with the spread of its effect nearly the flies'.

On raw counts its loss is lower than the unchanged fits', {{E91/readings.csv:variant=B3_F_k2_net;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_loss ~ .4f}} for {{E91/readings.csv:variant=B1_F_k2;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_loss ~ .4f}}, through a larger mean effect ({{E91/readings.csv:variant=B3_F_k2_net;unit=S;readout=raw:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} for {{E91/readings.csv:variant=B1_F_k2;unit=S;readout=raw:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}) at a higher pattern part ({{E91/readings.csv:variant=B3_F_k2_net;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} for {{E91/readings.csv:variant=B1_F_k2;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}). Two of its four runs reached the limit set for the APL scale, one of them with a response rate with APL on of {{E91/runs_B3.csv:B3_F_k2_net_P1:rate_on ~ .3f}}, so that this reading on raw counts is a description and not a comparison at matched response rates.

**On the base with the flies' recruitment a weaker weighting gains with the summed form, short of the test.** With the clipping, an exponent of 1 on this base had been level with the base's own family in the pattern part ([above](#breadth-weighting)). With the whole share it has the lowest pattern part against all four halves of the recordings, by {{E91/choice.csv:arm=B2;half=D:gain ~ .4f}} to {{E91/choice.csv:arm=B2;half=C:gain ~ .4f}} below the base's own family, and against all recordings it reads {{E91/spread.csv:variant=B2_F_k1_s1;unit=S;readout=cal;target=z8:pattern ~ .4f}} for the base's own family's {{E91/spread.csv:variant=B2_F_k2;unit=S;readout=cal;target=z8:pattern ~ .4f}} and for {{E91/spread.csv:variant=B2_F_k1;unit=S;readout=cal;target=z8:pattern ~ .4f}} at the same exponent with the clipping. Its gain is in the shape part, at a spread near the flies' (the table), and both groups' errors shrink: the ester pairs' from {{E91/readings.csv:variant=B2_F_k2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_ester ~ +.3f}} to {{E91/readings.csv:variant=B2_F_k1_s1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_ester ~ +.3f}} and the alcohol pairs' from {{E91/readings.csv:variant=B2_F_k2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_alcohol ~ +.3f}} to {{E91/readings.csv:variant=B2_F_k1_s1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_alcohol ~ +.3f}}.

Two readings do not go with it on these four wirings. On raw counts its loss is higher than the base's own family's, {{E91/readings.csv:variant=B2_F_k1_s1;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_loss ~ .4f}} for {{E91/readings.csv:variant=B2_F_k2;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_loss ~ .4f}}, and its mean APL effect through the readout is lower by {{diff:E91/readings.csv:variant=B2_F_k2;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect -- E91/readings.csv:variant=B2_F_k1_s1;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ .3f}}, so that by the rule for an equal it counts as better than the base's own family in the pattern part and not as its equal. And against the six recordings that are alike it is level with the base's own family ({{E91/readings.csv:variant=B2_F_k1_s1;unit=S;readout=cal:z6_pattern ~ .4f}} for {{E91/readings.csv:variant=B2_F_k2;unit=S;readout=cal:z6_pattern ~ .4f}}). Its gain reached 0.0015 against one half of each split of the flies, and for those two halves it was read on the four other wirings against the other half.

The setting chosen on the base with the flies' recruitment, on the four other wirings: the mean over those wirings through the calibrated readout.
