**There it gains on the base's own family in both directions that were read, by half of what the test asks once all four are counted, and a fixed inhibition of each KC gives more than half of the gain.** Against the half that it was not chosen on, the setting is {{E91/gate.csv:arm=B2;searched_on=A;reference_kind=own:g ~ .4f}} and {{E91/gate.csv:arm=B2;searched_on=C;reference_kind=own:g ~ .4f}} below the base's own family on the four other wirings, with {{E91/gate.csv:arm=B2;searched_on=A;reference_kind=own:n_singles_lower ~ .0f}} and {{E91/gate.csv:arm=B2;searched_on=C;reference_kind=own:n_singles_lower ~ .0f}} of the four single wirings lower (first two columns of the table).

The test asked for a mean gain of 0.003 over the two halves of both splits, with 12 of the 16 single wirings and halves lower, and a half for which the setting had not been confirmed counts as no gain. Over the four the mean gain is {{lit:0.0015 # results/E91_summed_drive_inhibition/verdict.json, arms.B2.gate.own.g_mean (0.00150): the mean of column g over the four rows of gate.csv with arm=B2 and reference_kind=own}} and {{lit:7 # results/E91_summed_drive_inhibition/verdict.json, arms.B2.gate.own.n_singles_lower, of n_singles 16: the sum of column n_singles_lower over the rows of gate.csv with arm=B2 and reference_kind=own}} of the 16 are lower. The squared pattern error against all recordings is {{E91/gate.csv:arm=B2;searched_on=A;reference_kind=own:sq_reduction_all ~ .1%}} lower with the setting, which counts as half of that over the four, where 15 % was asked. The loss on raw counts ({{E91/readings.csv:variant=B2_F_k1_s1;unit=T;readout=raw:z8_loss ~ .4f}} for {{E91/readings.csv:variant=B2_F_k2;unit=T;readout=raw:z8_loss ~ .4f}} on these wirings), the mean APL effect and the realism bands hold.

The control gains {{diff:E91/readings.csv:variant=B2_F_k2;unit=T;readout=cal:halfB_pattern -- E91/readings.csv:variant=B2_F_k1_s1_ctrl;unit=T;readout=cal:halfB_pattern ~ .4f}} and {{diff:E91/readings.csv:variant=B2_F_k2;unit=T;readout=cal:halfD_pattern -- E91/readings.csv:variant=B2_F_k1_s1_ctrl;unit=T;readout=cal:halfD_pattern ~ .4f}} in the same two directions, more than half of the setting's gain, where it had to stay under half. Most of the gain therefore comes from how strongly each KC is inhibited and not from which of its claws each odor drives: a KC's undriven claws work here as one more measure of its breadth, which is described and not adopted.

Nor does the gain carry beyond the base. Against the fits as they are on the same four wirings the setting is lower by {{E91/gate.csv:arm=B2;searched_on=A;reference_kind=unchanged:g ~ .4f}} against one unseen half and higher by {{diff:E91/gate.csv:arm=B2;searched_on=C;reference_kind=unchanged:pattern -- E91/gate.csv:arm=B2;searched_on=C;reference_kind=unchanged:ref_pattern ~ .4f}} against the other; against all recordings it reads {{E91/spread.csv:variant=B2_F_k1_s1;unit=T;readout=cal;target=z8:pattern ~ .4f}} for the unchanged fits' {{E91/spread.csv:variant=B1_F_k2;unit=T;readout=cal;target=z8:pattern ~ .4f}} (the table), and against the six recordings that are alike {{E91/readings.csv:variant=B2_F_k1_s1;unit=T;readout=cal:z6_pattern ~ .4f}} for {{E91/readings.csv:variant=B1_F_k2;unit=T;readout=cal:z6_pattern ~ .4f}}.

The base with the flies' recruitment costs about what the summed form gains on it. What the result says is about APL's side once recruitment is the flies': there, with the inhibition summed over the claws, a weaker weighting reads lower in the pattern part than the family's, where with the clipping the two were level.

**Fitted again with the summed form, the family is level.** As a population the four refits read {{E91/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all ~ .4f}} for the unchanged fits' {{E91/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}} (last row of the first table), with {{E91/d_scores.csv:unit=S:n_lower ~ .0f}} of the four wirings lower and single wirings moving by {{diff:E91/d_scores.csv:unit=P1:pattern_all -- E91/d_scores.csv:unit=P1:pattern_all_unchanged ~ +.4f}} to {{diff:E91/d_scores.csv:unit=real:pattern_all -- E91/d_scores.csv:unit=real:pattern_all_unchanged ~ +.4f}}. Fits on the four other wirings had been made conditional on a population lower by 0.0015 and were not run. What the refit gains is in the spread of its effect, which comes toward the flies' at an unchanged shape part.

The loss on raw counts is the same ({{E91/d_scores.csv:unit=S:raw_loss ~ .4f}} for {{E91/d_scores.csv:unit=S:raw_loss_unchanged ~ .4f}}), the mean APL effect stays the flies' ({{E91/d_scores.csv:unit=S:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}), and against the six recordings that are alike the pattern part is {{E91/spread.csv:variant=D_S2;unit=S;readout=cal;target=z6:pattern ~ .4f}} for {{E91/spread.csv:variant=D_S2_unchanged;unit=S;readout=cal;target=z6:pattern ~ .4f}}. The fit moves a little of APL's inhibition from the boutons to the KCs: the APL→bouton scale falls on every wiring, to between {{E91/d_scores.csv:unit=P2:wAPLPN_scale ~ .2f}} and {{E91/d_scores.csv:unit=real:wAPLPN_scale ~ .2f}} from between {{E72/stats_variants.csv:wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed2_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3:wAPLPN_scale ~ .2f}} and {{E72/stats_variants.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3:wAPLPN_scale ~ .2f}} in the unchanged fits, while the somatic threshold, the APL→KC scale and KC–KC inhibition stay near their values.

**Realism.** The summed form adds no fitted parameter. Its share is set at a half or at one, and with the whole share a KC sums its claws' inhibition as it sums their excitation, as the near-linear summation of a KC's claw inputs would have it (Gruntman and Turner, 2013).

All {{lit:72 # the rows of results/E91_summed_drive_inhibition/runs_B1.csv (36), runs_B2.csv (12), runs_B3.csv (4) and runs_C.csv (16) and the four refits of d_scores.csv; none has a realism_flag}} runs and refits are inside the four realism bands. On the real wiring the whole share at the family's weighting has response rates of {{E91/runs_B1.csv:B1_F_k2_s1_real:rate_on ~ .3f}} with APL on and {{E91/runs_B1.csv:B1_F_k2_s1_real:rate_off ~ .3f}} with APL off (a ratio of {{E91/runs_B1.csv:B1_F_k2_s1_real:ratio ~ .2f}}), the fit's own by construction, and the setting chosen on the base {{E91/runs_B2.csv:B2_F_k1_s1_real:rate_on ~ .3f}} and {{E91/runs_B2.csv:B2_F_k1_s1_real:rate_off ~ .3f}} ({{E91/runs_B2.csv:B2_F_k1_s1_real:ratio ~ .2f}}), the flies' response rates odor by odor; the four refits have {{E91/d_scores.csv:unit=real:rate_on ~ .3f}} to {{E91/d_scores.csv:unit=M1:rate_on ~ .3f}} and {{E91/d_scores.csv:unit=real:rate_off ~ .3f}} to {{E91/d_scores.csv:unit=P2:rate_off ~ .3f}} (ratios of {{E91/d_scores.csv:unit=M1:ratio ~ .2f}} to {{E91/d_scores.csv:unit=P2:ratio ~ .2f}}), against the flies' {{data:noise_ctrl_frac ~ .3f}} and {{data:noise_tnt_frac ~ .3f}} ({{data:noise_rate_ratio_fraction ~ .2f}}).

Over all the runs the response rate with APL on is {{E91/runs_B1.csv:B1_F_k2_s1_fixed_P2:rate_on ~ .3f}} to {{E91/runs_B3.csv:B3_F_k2_net_P1:rate_on ~ .3f}} and the ratio {{E91/runs_B3.csv:B3_F_k2_net_P1:ratio ~ .2f}} to {{E91/runs_B1.csv:B1_F_k2_s1_fixed_P2:ratio ~ .2f}}, the ends being the runs in which the APL scale was not set again or reached its limit; the response rate ρ with APL on is {{E91/runs_B1.csv:B1_F_k2_s0.5_P2:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}} or more; and the distribution of the number of odors per KC is at most {{E91/runs_B1.csv:B1_none_s0.5_P2:opk_on_tv ~ .3f}} from the flies' with APL on, without a weighting (band {{data:noise_ctrl_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .3f}}), and {{E91/runs_C.csv:B2_F_k2_M3:opk_off_tv ~ .3f}} with APL off (band {{data:noise_tnt_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .3f}}).

Counted by the recordings' own criterion, as the bands counted until 2026-11-10, {{lit:11 # count of the rows of results/E91_summed_drive_inhibition/runs_B1.csv (8) and runs_B2.csv (3) with a realism_flag_zcrit, all without a breadth weighting and all the number of odors per KC with APL on; none of the 72 runs and refits has a realism_flag}} of the runs would be outside the band on odors per KC with APL on, all without a weighting, as such runs are with the clipping. Nothing was bought with the bands: no run was left out of a choice by them, and the small gains came at no cost in them.

Two things qualify the one gain. The base's threshold for each odor and its APL scale for each odor are [oracles](#fn-oracle) for a mechanism of recruitment. And the setting chosen there is the easier one to defend only so far: among the KCs that respond without APL, its APL→KC weight at the 90th percentile is {{E91/runs_B2.csv:B2_F_k1_s1_P2:fac_resp_p90_over_p10 ~ .0f}} to {{E91/runs_B2.csv:B2_F_k1_s1_real:fac_resp_p90_over_p10 ~ .0f}} times that at the 10th on the four wirings, for {{E91/runs_B2.csv:B2_F_k2_s1_P2:fac_resp_p90_over_p10 ~ .0f}} to {{E91/runs_B2.csv:B2_F_k2_s1_real:fac_resp_p90_over_p10 ~ .0f}} times at the family's exponent, but it holds under the oracle only and did not pass its test. The runs carry, as everywhere, paa, euc and -aPine at [ORN input of another concentration](#fn-concentrations).

**What follows.** The place where APL's inhibition is summed does not limit the family: the clipping at each claw holds back inhibition in the KCs that the weighting already loads, and lifting it does there what the weighting has done. After the static forms of inhibition and the flies' form simulated in place of APL ([the form of APL's inhibition in the flies' own responses](#inhibition-form); [the common error split into who responds and how strongly](#responder-sets)), and after the breadth weighting ([above](#breadth-weighting)), the feedback APL's subtraction from the KCs is closed in the place where it is summed as well, on the fits as they are and at the model's 0.5 s pulse.

Two things were left on APL's side in this family: a gain on each claw's drive in place of the subtraction, and the form of APL's inhibition of the boutons. A divisive inhibition at either site had been run on an early model only, where it left the per-odor suppression as selective as it was ([what drives APL](#apl-drive)).

Both have been run since, with the family with the clipping at each claw as their reference ([the claw-to-soma steps read like for like and APL's inhibition as a gain at the claw](#steps-like-for-like)): the gain at the claw is worse at the family's weighting and at an exponent of 1 and is the best setting against no half of the recordings, and a divisive inhibition at the boutons is worse on the main target at fixed scales. The strength of APL's inhibition of the boutons has been varied since as well, and the fitted one is the best ([the PN boutons' share of APL's inhibition](#bouton-share)).

The base with the flies' recruitment adds one statement and changes no base: once recruitment is the flies', a weighting with an exponent of 1 reads lower in the pattern part than the family's when the inhibition is summed over the claws, with weights far less unequal, short of the test and under the oracle only. If a mechanism later gives the model the flies' recruitment without the oracle, that setting is the first to be read on it.

The count-level reading of a change on APL's side has failed again, as it did for the static forms, so that such changes are simulated. The two groups of pairs trade against each other under the summed form as under the weighting, and the alcohol pairs' co-response change under APL stays where it was: nothing on APL's side has so far brought it toward the flies' while keeping the ester pairs'.

For the mechanism between the claw and the soma that the lead asks for, the result is a boundary. The summed form re-weights which KCs APL inhibits, toward the broad and many-clawed, and leaves the responses without APL as they are; it is not that mechanism.

The stages of its runs have been read since as the stages were ([above](#model-stages)): its somata, its claws and its steps from claws to somata are those of the family with the clipping ([below](#steps-like-for-like)). Every reading here is of the model's 0.5 s pulse without trial noise; the readings at the flies' pulse, through the trial noise and with the firing ceiling had been kept for a setting that passed, and were not made.

### The claw-to-soma steps read like for like and APL's inhibition as a gain at the claw: whether the model's KC somata differ from the flies' once both are read the same way, where the saved versions of the model lie when APL's inhibition is changed, and whether a gain on each claw's drive in place of the subtraction lowers the pattern part {#steps-like-for-like}

%%% hover
weightings' line: For a model, the mean cosine distance with APL on over the 15 ester pairs minus the mean over all 120 pairs, set against the same difference for the 6 alcohol pairs. The 13 breadth weightings of APL on the fits as they are, each as the mean over the four wirings of the earlier searches, fall close to one straight line in that plane. A model's distance from the line is its ester pairs' value minus the line's value at its alcohol pairs', and the control flies lie on the positive side. Defined in the subsection on the claw-to-soma steps read like for like.
%%%

**Read the same way on both sides, the model's KC somata differ from the flies' with APL on in every reading, and in opposite directions for the two groups of the common error: the ester pairs are too alike and the alcohol pairs too far apart.**

Without APL the verdict turns on one assumption of the reading. If a KC's signal is taken to saturate with its firing, the model's somata without APL are the flies' in every group of pairs but the four ester pairs with near-identical ORN input; if it is taken to grow in proportion to its firing, they are too far apart. In no such reading are the alcohol pairs too alike without APL, which is how the earlier comparison of the stages had read them through the calibrated readout. The two steps from claws to somata say no more than the somata, because both start from claws that read more alike than the flies'.

Over the breadth weightings of APL the ester pairs' and the alcohol pairs' distances with APL on move together, along one line, and the control flies lie far off it. Of the saved changes of APL's inhibition that treat every glomerulus alike, none leaves that line toward the flies by more than about a thousandth; what leaves it are changes made glomerulus by glomerulus or odor by odor, to the input or to APL's weight, fitted to the recordings or taken from single flies.

The one form of APL's inhibition of the KCs that the family had not run, a gain on each claw's drive in place of the subtraction, is worse at the family's weighting and at an exponent of 1, and better by one to three thousandths only at the weakest weightings, which stay far above the family; against no half of the recordings is a setting with the gain the best, and none is an equal.

A divisive inhibition at the boutons, run for the record, is the only form on APL's side that moves the model clearly off the line toward the flies and brings the alcohol pairs' co-response change under APL to the flies'; at fixed scales it pays for both in the pattern part and in the mean APL effect. The summed form reads as the family with the clipping in its somata, its claws and its steps, and it lies on the line.

The feedback APL's inhibition of the KCs is thereby closed in its form, after its weighting and the place where it is summed. What a mechanism between the claw and the soma has to do can now be said on the somata themselves: with APL on, hold the ester pairs further apart and the alcohol pairs closer together, both at once.

[The model's stages against the flies' stages](#model-stages) had set the model's steps from claws to somata beside the flies' and had left a lead and a reading that, as the claws were then read, hung on the readout: the ester pairs' step with APL on was too small from the claws that the model's input drives, and through the calibrated readout the model's KCs without APL brought two odors closer together than the flies' do, which would place the alcohol pairs' excess at the step without APL.

At the somata that comparison had not treated the two sides alike. The flies' somata were trial means in the recordings' own unit, which carry the trial noise and each KC's own normalization, and the model's were spike counts without noise, or the calibrated readout of them. On APL's side two things had been left as well ([APL's inhibition on the KC's summed drive](#summed-drive)): a gain on each claw's drive in place of the subtraction, and the form of APL's inhibition of the boutons.

The claw-to-soma steps read like for like and APL's inhibition as a gain at the claw took these up in three parts: a reading of saved runs that simulated nothing, the gain at fixed scales, and the runs with the summed form read as the first part reads the family. The reference throughout is the breadth-2 family with the subtraction clipped at each claw, whose pattern part through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout) is {{E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} on the four wirings of the earlier searches, for a floor of {{data:apl_effect_pattern_floor ~ .4f}}.

The first part reads the somata of both sides in the same unit and with the same treatment of the noise. On the flies' side, for every recording of the control flies and of the flies with APL output blocked (TNT), the distance between two odors was taken as the trial means give it and with the trial noise removed, by the estimate across repeats ([the flies' variability across the three repeats](#repeat-structure)); in the recordings' own unit, each KC's trace z-scored over its recording, and in [baseline-noise units](#fn-baseline-noise-units); and as one minus the Pearson correlation across the KCs, the measure of the stage recordings, and as cosine distance, the measure of the main target. A value is the mean over the recordings, with a 90 % interval over resampled recordings.

The estimate was checked where the truth is known. Applied to simulated recordings of the model, of three trials each and at four levels of noise, it returns the model's noise-free distances of every group to within {{lit:0.013 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/estimate_check.json, largest_population_error: the largest absolute error of the estimate with the trial noise removed against the model's noise-free group distance, for the mean over the eight wirings, over the groups, the two conditions, the four noise levels, the two measures and the two units (0.0129)}} for the mean over the eight wirings, where 0.03 was allowed and where the trial means are off by up to {{lit:0.18 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/estimate_check.csv, rows wiring=population: the largest absolute value of column error_trial_mean (0.177)}}.

On the model's side the saved runs of the breadth-2 family on its eight wirings, each at its own fit ([the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population)), were read as the recordings are normalized, under the per-KC reading ([the per-KC normalization of the recordings](#per-kc-normalization)) set on each run's counts with APL on. That reading passes a KC's spike counts through a saturating map before it places them in a simulated recording. It was made with that map and with a linear map in its place, because whether a KC's calcium signal saturates over the range of its firing is not known.

Each of the two was read in the reading's z against the flies in the recordings' own unit and in baseline-noise units against the flies in those units; without noise against the flies' values with the trial noise removed and through the reading's measurement noise against the flies' trial means; and as Pearson and as cosine. That makes 16 readings in which the two sides are treated alike. Raw spike counts and the calibrated readout were read beside them, against the flies in baseline-noise units.

The groups of pairs and the rule are those of the stages comparison: a group differs from the flies' if the model's mean over the eight wirings is 0.05 or more from the flies' value, lies outside their 90 % interval and has at least six of the eight wirings on the same side. Of the six pairs with near-identical ORN input ([the high per-claw knee without a dead zone](#claw-knee)), the four ester pairs, eb with ep, IaA with pa, 2h with pa and 2h with IaA, are read together, and the other two singly and as leads. The two steps from claws to somata were then read with the claws of the stages comparison on both sides, the model's as all claws with the drive alone, from their settled level before the odor ([footnote](#fn-preodor-startup)).

The same part asks what a change on APL's side can do to the two groups at once. For a model, the mean cosine distance with APL on over the 15 ester pairs, minus the mean over all 120 pairs, says how far apart APL leaves the ester pairs relative to the mean pair, and the same difference for the 6 alcohol pairs says it for them.

For the 13 breadth weightings of APL on the fits as they are ([the co-response read with a checked estimate and the breadth weighting inside the models' APL](#breadth-weighting)), each as the mean over the four wirings of the earlier searches, the two numbers fall close to a straight line, the weightings' line. Every saved variant of the family was placed against it, on raw spike counts and through the calibrated readout: {{lit:286 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, n_variants}} variants from {{lit:757 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, n_runs}} runs of ten earlier experiments, {{lit:265 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, n_in_bands}} of them inside the realism bands.

A variant counts as off the line toward the flies if its distance from the line, on the side on which the control flies lie, is larger than the largest distance among the 13 weightings themselves, with the flies' point taken from either half of the recordings. A single run, or a mean over the four held-out wirings, is measured from the unchanged family on the same wirings.

The second part runs the one form of the feedback APL's inhibition of the KCs that the family had not been given. In every model so far a claw's drive is its PN input minus APL's inhibition of that claw. With the gain, the PN input is divided by one plus that inhibition, so that APL scales a claw's drive down and never removes it.

The gain was run at fixed scales on the four wirings of the earlier searches, on the fits as they are: at the family's weighting (the family's measure of a KC's breadth at an exponent of 2), at exponents of 1 and 0.5 and without a weighting, with the APL scale set again until the number of responses with APL on was the fit's. The responses with APL off are the fit's own, so that both response rates are held.

The references are the runs with the subtraction at the same weightings ([above](#breadth-weighting)). For the record, and not as candidates, a divisive inhibition of the boutons was run in the same way: at the family's weighting with the subtraction at the claws, and with the gain at the claws at the family's weighting and at an exponent of 1.

What would count had been fixed as it was for the summed form. The setting with the lowest pattern part against one half of the recordings, for the mean over the four wirings through the calibrated readout, was to be read on the four held-out wirings against the other half, by the test that the fitted changes were put to ([above](#cross-wiring-fit)), if it was lower than the family by 0.0015 or more; the halves were those of two splits of the flies.

A setting with the gain at an exponent of 1 or below was an equal of the family if its pattern part stayed within 0.003 of the family's, with limits on the loss on raw counts, on the mean APL effect and on the realism bands. The family was to be fitted again with the gain only on a choice or an equal. The third part read the runs with the summed form as the first part reads the family, on the fits as they are, in the family fitted again with it and at the setting chosen on the base with the flies' recruitment, and ran the refits and the chosen setting once more with every stage saved.

**With APL on the model's somata differ from the flies' in every reading, the ester pairs too alike and the alcohol pairs too far apart.** Over the 16 readings the model's ester pairs lie {{E92/verdict_rows_A.csv:element=soma;set=like_for_like;cond=on;reading=linear_z_none_pearson;group=ester:diff ~ +.3f}} to {{E92/verdict_rows_A.csv:element=soma;set=like_for_like;cond=on;reading=saturating_z_none_cosine;group=ester:diff ~ +.3f}} from the flies' (the model's value minus the flies', so that a negative difference means pairs that are more alike). By the rule the group differs in {{lit:15 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/verdict_A.json, somata.ester.on.n_differ, of n_readings 16}} of the 16, the one that does not falling just short of the rule's 0.05. The alcohol pairs lie {{E92/verdict_rows_A.csv:element=soma;set=like_for_like;cond=on;reading=saturating_z_expected_cosine;group=alcohol:diff ~ +.3f}} to {{E92/verdict_rows_A.csv:element=soma;set=like_for_like;cond=on;reading=linear_z_none_pearson;group=alcohol:diff ~ +.3f}} from the flies', further apart in all 16, and differ by the rule in {{lit:14 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/verdict_A.json, somata.alcohol.on.n_differ, of n_readings 16}}.

The four ester pairs with near-identical ORN input are too alike in all 16, lying {{E92/verdict_rows_A.csv:element=soma;set=like_for_like;cond=on;reading=linear_z_none_pearson;group=near_ester:diff ~ +.3f}} to {{E92/verdict_rows_A.csv:element=soma;set=like_for_like;cond=on;reading=saturating_z_none_cosine;group=near_ester:diff ~ +.3f}} from the flies'; the pairs of an ester with an alcohol are too alike in {{lit:11 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/verdict_A.json, somata.ester_alcohol.on.n_differ, of n_readings 16}}; and the other pairs differ in none (the first six rows of the table, for one of the readings, and the upper panels of the figure). One single pair goes with the alcohol pairs: 1-5ol with 1-6ol is too far apart in the model in all 16 readings, with APL on and without, and a single pair is a lead and no more.

It is the removal of the flies' trial noise that brings the alcohol pairs out. Trial noise makes two odors look less alike than they are, and it does so most for the alcohol pairs: the control flies' trial means put them {{diff:E92/somata_flies.csv:genotype=ctrl;units=z;reading=trial_mean;measure=pearson;group=alcohol:mean -- E92/somata_flies.csv:genotype=ctrl;units=z;reading=noise_removed;measure=pearson;group=alcohol:mean ~ .2f}} further apart than the estimate without the noise does, for {{diff:E92/somata_flies.csv:genotype=ctrl;units=z;reading=trial_mean;measure=pearson;group=ester_alcohol:mean -- E92/somata_flies.csv:genotype=ctrl;units=z;reading=noise_removed;measure=pearson;group=ester_alcohol:mean ~ .2f}} to {{diff:E92/somata_flies.csv:genotype=ctrl;units=z;reading=trial_mean;measure=pearson;group=ester:mean -- E92/somata_flies.csv:genotype=ctrl;units=z;reading=noise_removed;measure=pearson;group=ester:mean ~ .2f}} in the three other groups.

Against the trial means the calibrated readout had read the model's alcohol pairs with APL on as the flies', {{E92/somata_model.csv:run=all8;cond=on;reading=cal_pearson:alcohol ~ .3f}} for {{E92/somata_flies.csv:genotype=ctrl;units=z;reading=trial_mean;measure=pearson;group=alcohol:mean ~ .3f}}. Read alike, they are {{E92/somata_model.csv:run=all8;cond=on;reading=saturating_z_none_pearson:alcohol ~ .3f}} with the saturating map and {{E92/somata_model.csv:run=all8;cond=on;reading=linear_z_none_pearson:alcohol ~ .3f}} with the linear one, for the flies' {{E92/somata_flies.csv:genotype=ctrl;units=z;reading=noise_removed;measure=pearson;group=alcohol:mean ~ .3f}}. The two groups' differences at the somata have the signs of their errors in the main target, an APL effect too small for the ester pairs and too large for the alcohol pairs, so that the two-signed part of the common error is seen at the somata with APL on, in every reading.

**Without APL the verdict turns on whether a KC's signal saturates with its firing.** With the saturating map of the per-KC reading the model's somata without APL are the flies'. Over its eight readings the four groups lie between {{E92/verdict_rows_A.csv:element=soma;set=like_for_like;cond=off;reading=saturating_z_expected_pearson;group=ester_alcohol:diff ~ +.3f}} and {{E92/verdict_rows_A.csv:element=soma;set=like_for_like;cond=off;reading=saturating_noise_none_cosine;group=other:diff ~ +.3f}} of the flies', none differs by the rule but the other pairs in {{lit:one # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/verdict_A.json, by_map.saturating.somata_off.other.n_differ: 1 of n_readings 8, and 0 of 8 for ester, alcohol and ester_alcohol}}, and only the four ester pairs with near-identical ORN input are too alike, in {{lit:six # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/verdict_A.json, by_map.saturating.somata_off.near_ester.n_differ: 6 of n_readings 8}} of the eight.

With the linear map the ester pairs, the alcohol pairs and the other pairs are too far apart, by {{E92/verdict_rows_A.csv:element=soma;set=like_for_like;cond=off;reading=linear_noise_expected_pearson;group=ester:diff ~ +.3f}} to {{E92/verdict_rows_A.csv:element=soma;set=like_for_like;cond=off;reading=linear_z_none_cosine;group=alcohol:diff ~ +.3f}}, in {{lit:6 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/verdict_A.json, by_map.linear.somata_off.ester.n_differ, of n_readings 8}}, {{lit:7 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/verdict_A.json, by_map.linear.somata_off.alcohol.n_differ, of n_readings 8}} and {{lit:8 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/verdict_A.json, by_map.linear.somata_off.other.n_differ, of n_readings 8}} of its eight readings (the last six rows of the table, and the lower panels of the figure). The two maps part here and not with APL on because the saturating map compresses a KC's large responses, and without APL the KCs respond to more odors and more strongly.

Beside the 16, against the flies in baseline-noise units, raw spike counts are too far apart as well, by up to {{E92/verdict_rows_A.csv:element=soma;set=beside;cond=off;reading=raw_cosine;flies_reading=noise_removed;group=other:diff ~ +.3f}}, and the calibrated readout lies between {{E92/verdict_rows_A.csv:element=soma;set=beside;cond=off;reading=cal_cosine;flies_reading=trial_mean;group=alcohol:diff ~ +.3f}} and {{E92/verdict_rows_A.csv:element=soma;set=beside;cond=off;reading=cal_pearson;flies_reading=noise_removed;group=other:diff ~ +.3f}} of the flies' for the ester, the alcohol and the other pairs. For the alcohol pairs this corrects the earlier comparison of the stages. There the model's somata without APL had read as too alike, which placed the alcohol pairs' excess APL effect at the step without APL; that reading set the calibrated readout against the flies' trial means in the recordings' own unit (in the table, {{E92/somata_model.csv:run=all8;cond=off;reading=cal_pearson:alcohol ~ .3f}} for {{E92/somata_flies.csv:genotype=tnt;units=z;reading=trial_mean;measure=pearson;group=alcohol:mean ~ .3f}}).

In none of the 16 readings are the alcohol pairs too alike without APL. With the saturating map they are within {{E92/verdict_rows_A.csv:element=soma;set=like_for_like;cond=off;reading=saturating_noise_none_cosine;group=alcohol:diff ~ .2f}} of the flies', and with the linear map they lie {{E92/verdict_rows_A.csv:element=soma;set=like_for_like;cond=off;reading=linear_noise_expected_pearson;group=alcohol:diff ~ +.3f}} to {{E92/verdict_rows_A.csv:element=soma;set=like_for_like;cond=off;reading=linear_z_none_cosine;group=alcohol:diff ~ +.3f}} from them, too far apart, which is the opposite sign. Which map is right is a question about the recordings and the indicator, whether a KC's calcium signal saturates over the range of the KC's firing, and not one about the model; these readings cannot answer it.

**The steps from claws to somata say no more than the somata.** With all claws read and the drive alone, the model's claws are more alike than the flies' by {{diff:E90/stages_flies.csv:key=claw_noise_removed;group=ester:mean -- E90/settled_preodor/stages_model.csv:stage=claw;subset=all;share=0.0;cond=on;reading=session_z;wiring=population:ester ~ .2f}} among the ester pairs and by {{diff:E90/stages_flies.csv:key=claw_noise_removed;group=alcohol:mean -- E90/settled_preodor/stages_model.csv:stage=claw;subset=all;share=0.0;cond=on;reading=session_z;wiring=population:alcohol ~ .2f}} among the alcohol pairs ([the model's stages against the flies' stages](#model-stages)), and both steps start from those claws. The model's step is then larger than the flies' in all 16 readings for the alcohol pairs, the pairs of an ester with an alcohol and the other pairs, with APL on and without, and for the ester pairs without APL; for the ester pairs with APL on it is larger by the rule in {{lit:10 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/settled_F.json, cells_a3.new.ester.on (10/16, the model's step the larger), from the rows element=step, cond=on, group=ester of results/E92_steps_like_for_like/steps_like_for_like_settled.csv; 15 in results/E92_steps_like_for_like/verdict_A.json, steps.ester.on.n_differ, with the claws' level before the odor taken over the whole half second}} of the 16.

A step that is too large from claws that are too alike is one difference counted twice. Part of it belongs to the claws of the glomeruli without ORN input, which the reading of all claws includes: on the claws that the input drives, the earlier comparison finds the ester and the alcohol pairs' claws less alike than the flies', and not more alike. The steps are therefore not read further here, and the verdict rests on the somata.

![The weightings' line. For each model, the ester pairs' mean cosine distance with APL on minus the mean over all 120 pairs (vertical) against the same difference for the alcohol pairs (horizontal), on raw spike counts (left) and through the calibrated readout (right). Blue: the 13 breadth weightings of APL on the fits as they are, with the line fitted through them and, shaded, the band of their largest distance from it. Grey: the other saved versions of the family that are means over the four wirings of the earlier searches, those outside the realism bands in a lighter shade. Circled in magenta: the versions off the line toward the flies. Stars: the control flies as trial means; crosses: the control flies with the trial noise removed; the small symbols beside each are the two halves of the recordings.](results/E92_steps_like_for_like/E92_line.png)

**Over the breadth weightings of APL the two groups move together, and the flies lie off the line.** Through the calibrated readout the 13 weightings hold the ester pairs at {{E92/line_points.csv:readout=cal;line=S;weighting=N_k1:ester ~ +.3f}} to {{E92/line_points.csv:readout=cal;line=S;weighting=F_k2:ester ~ +.3f}} relative to the mean pair, a negative value meaning closer together than the mean pair, and the alcohol pairs at {{E92/line_points.csv:readout=cal;line=S;weighting=none:alcohol ~ +.3f}} to {{E92/line_points.csv:readout=cal;line=S;weighting=S_k2:alcohol ~ +.3f}}, and the two go together.

Along the weightings' line the ester pairs' value rises by {{lit:0.2652096271904637 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, lines.cal.S.slope ~ .2f}} for each unit of the alcohol pairs' (by {{lit:0.5714606526999498 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, lines.raw.S.slope ~ .2f}} on raw counts; Pearson correlations of {{lit:0.7356313615496841 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, lines.cal.S.r ~ .2f}} and {{lit:0.7482071151708288 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, lines.raw.S.r ~ .2f}} over the 13), and no weighting lies further than {{lit:0.009911938135506365 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, lines.cal.S.max_abs_resid ~ .3f}} from it ({{lit:0.017628248730717194 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, lines.raw.S.max_abs_resid ~ .3f}} on raw counts). A weighting that holds the ester pairs further apart, relative to the mean pair, holds the alcohol pairs further apart as well. That is the trade which the weightings had shown in the two groups' errors ([above](#breadth-weighting)), read here on the distances themselves.

The control flies are not on the line. With APL on their ester pairs are nearly as far apart as the mean pair, at {{lit:-0.05065745385046694 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, lines.cal.S.flies.trial_mean_all.ester ~ +.3f}} relative to it, for alcohol pairs at {{lit:-0.23140154814614666 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, lines.cal.S.flies.trial_mean_all.alcohol ~ +.3f}}. That puts the flies {{lit:0.09866993033793536 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, lines.cal.S.flies.trial_mean_all.resid ~ +.3f}} from the line through the readout and {{lit:0.10701777447779079 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, lines.raw.S.flies.trial_mean_all.resid ~ +.3f}} on raw counts, about ten and six times the weightings' largest distance, and {{lit:0.11029610987169114 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, lines.cal.S.flies.noise_removed_all.resid ~ +.3f}} and {{lit:0.1328880364474679 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, lines.raw.S.flies.noise_removed_all.resid ~ +.3f}} with the trial noise removed from the flies' distances. The family itself lies at {{E92/beside_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2:line_cal_resid ~ +.3f}} and {{E92/beside_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2:line_raw_resid ~ +.3f}}, at the edge of the weightings' own scatter.

**The saved changes of APL's inhibition that treat every glomerulus alike stay on the line.** Of the variants inside the realism bands, none of those saved by the experiments on the form of APL's inhibition, on the responder sets, on the remaining candidates on the model's side and on the flies' protocol is off the line toward the flies, through the readout or on raw counts (the first four rows of the table). On the base with the flies' recruitment two of the weaker weightings are just past it, by about a thousandth, one of them through the readout as well, and one run with a high per-claw knee is off it at a pattern part of {{E92/line.csv:folder=E78_claw_knee;family=knee100_g0;population=real;readout=cal:pattern ~ .3f}}, far above the family's.

The rest of what leaves the line toward the flies comes from the four experiments that changed the model glomerulus by glomerulus or odor by odor (the last four rows): settings of the input stage and inputs searched against the recordings, single ORN flies as the input, the reduced searched input with its replications and controls, and, where both were fitted on several wirings at once, APL's weight by glomerulus as well as the input.

The fitted ones among these were read on wirings and recordings that they had not been fitted to, and none passed that test; the one that carries a part of the common error there, the reduced searched input, carries a few thousandths of the pattern part ([above](#reduced-input)). Leaving the line is therefore not the same as carrying the common error, and controls leave it too: {{lit:seven # counted in results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.csv, rows folder=E86_reduced_input_candidate, readout=cal, in_bands True, families B1_perm1_A, B1_perm2_A, B1_perm1_B, B1_perm2_B, B2_inv_A, B2_inv_B, B3_perm3_A, B3_perm4_A, B3_perm3_B and B3_perm4_B: 7 of the 10 have off_toward_flies True}} of the ten versions of the reduced searched input with its factors permuted over the glomeruli or inverted, and {{lit:six # counted in results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.csv, rows folder=E85_orn_fly_population, readout=cal, in_bands True, families B4_permuted_f0 to B4_permuted_f8: 6 of the 9 have off_toward_flies True}} of the nine model flies whose deviations from the mean input were permuted over the glomeruli.

What the plane does show is a tendency. Over the {{lit:140 # counted in results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.csv: the rows with readout=cal, population S or T and in_bands True}} means over four wirings that are inside the bands, the further a version of the model lies toward the flies' side of the line, the lower its pattern part, at a Pearson correlation of {{lit:-0.6011595419282887 # computed from results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.csv: the Pearson correlation between columns resid and pattern over the 140 rows with readout=cal, population S or T and in_bands True ~ .2f}} through the readout and {{lit:-0.5895737661178715 # computed from results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.csv: the Pearson correlation between columns resid and pattern over the 140 rows with readout=raw, population S or T and in_bands True ~ .2f}} on raw counts. Input that was measured does not act as input that was fitted: with the fuller input the family lies at {{E93/line.csv:input=F;unit=S;readout=cal:resid ~ +.3f}} from the line through the readout, for {{E93/line.csv:input=I0;unit=S;readout=cal:resid ~ +.3f}} with the lab's input, on the four wirings of the earlier searches ([below](#missing-glomeruli)).

APL's inhibition as a gain at the claw, and a divisive inhibition at the boutons, against the subtraction clipped at each claw: the mean over the four wirings of the earlier searches, on the fits as they are with the APL scale set again, against the main target as measured, all recordings, through the calibrated readout. The squares of the amplitude part and the shape part add up to the squared pattern part, and a spread below one means that APL moves the model's pairs apart more evenly than the flies'; no setting is chosen by a correlation ([why](#fn-pattern-split)). The mean error of a group is the model's per-pair APL effect minus the flies', each side's mean removed, over the 15 ester pairs and over the 6 alcohol pairs. The distance from the weightings' line is positive on the flies' side, and the co-response change is read as trial means at the reading's own noise; in the row of the KC data these two cells are the flies' own, the second with its 90 % interval. **A gain at the claw is worse at the family's weighting and at an exponent of 1, and no setting with it is chosen.** At the family's weighting the gain reads a pattern part of {{E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2_div;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} for the subtraction's {{E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, higher by {{diff:E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2_div;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern -- E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} against all recordings and by {{diff:E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2_div;unit=S;readout=cal:halfA_pattern -- E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2;unit=S;readout=cal:halfA_pattern ~ .4f}} and {{diff:E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2_div;unit=S;readout=cal:halfB_pattern -- E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2;unit=S;readout=cal:halfB_pattern ~ .4f}} against the two halves of the first split of the flies (the first rows of the table). Nearly all of it is in the shape part, which rises from {{E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_shape ~ .4f}} to {{E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2_div;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_shape ~ .4f}} while the spread of the effect hardly moves, and Pearson r on the per-pair APL effect falls from {{E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pearson ~ .2f}} to {{E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2_div;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pearson ~ .2f}}.

It is the alcohol pairs that pay. Their excess grows from {{E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_alcohol ~ +.3f}} to {{E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2_div;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_alcohol ~ +.3f}} with the ester pairs' shortfall where it was ({{E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_ester ~ +.3f}} and {{E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2_div;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_ester ~ +.3f}}), and their co-response change under APL moves away from the flies', to {{E92/coresponse_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2_div;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} from {{E92/coresponse_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} for the flies' {{E92/coresponse_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:flies_ratio ~ .2f}}. A gain scales a broad KC's response down where the subtraction removes it, which had been thought likely to help the alcohol pairs if it helped anything; it does the opposite.

At an exponent of 1 the gain reads {{E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k1_div;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} for the subtraction's {{E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}. Only at the weakest weightings is it the lower of the two, by {{diff:E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k0.5;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern -- E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k0.5_div;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} at an exponent of 0.5 and by {{diff:E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_none;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern -- E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_none_div;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} without a weighting, where 0.002 to 0.006 had been expected, and those two settings remain {{E92/equal.csv:variant=B_F_k0.5_div:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} and {{E92/equal.csv:variant=B_none_div:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} above the family. At every weighting the gain lowers the mean APL effect, by {{diff:E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect -- E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2_div;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ .3f}} to {{diff:E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_none;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect -- E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_none_div;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ .3f}} against the subtraction at the same weighting, and at the two stronger weightings it moves the model away from the flies' side of the weightings' line (the last column but one).

Against each of the four halves of the recordings the setting with the lowest pattern part is the family's own, whether or not the two settings of the gain that have a run outside the realism bands are counted, so that nothing went to the four held-out wirings and no control was run. No setting with the gain is an equal either: the nearest at an exponent of 1 or below is {{E92/equal.csv:variant=B_F_k1_div:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} above the family, where 0.003 was allowed.

On raw counts the order is the same. At the family's weighting the loss is {{E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2_div;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_loss ~ .4f}} for {{E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_loss ~ .4f}}, through a smaller mean effect ({{E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2_div;unit=S;readout=raw:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} for {{E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2;unit=S;readout=raw:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}) and at a higher pattern part ({{E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2_div;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} for {{E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}). The family was not fitted again with the gain, a refit having been kept for a choice or an equal.

**A divisive inhibition at the boutons leaves the line toward the flies, and pays for it.** With APL's inhibition of the boutons made divisive, with the subtraction or with the gain at the claws, the model lies {{E92/beside_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2_bdiv:line_cal_resid ~ +.3f}}, {{E92/beside_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2_both:line_cal_resid ~ +.3f}} and {{E92/beside_B.csv:variant=B_F_k1_both:line_cal_resid ~ +.3f}} from the weightings' line through the readout (the last three rows of the table) and {{E92/beside_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2_bdiv:line_raw_resid ~ +.3f}}, {{E92/beside_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2_both:line_raw_resid ~ +.3f}} and {{E92/beside_B.csv:variant=B_F_k1_both:line_raw_resid ~ +.3f}} on raw counts. Both are past the weightings' largest distance, where the family is at {{E92/beside_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2:line_cal_resid ~ +.3f}} and {{E92/beside_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2:line_raw_resid ~ +.3f}} and the flies at {{lit:0.09866993033793536 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, lines.cal.S.flies.trial_mean_all.resid ~ +.3f}} and {{lit:0.10701777447779079 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, lines.raw.S.flies.trial_mean_all.resid ~ +.3f}}. Of the changes of the form of APL's inhibition that have been run, it is the only one that moves the model this far.

The alcohol pairs' excess falls to between {{E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2_bdiv;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_alcohol ~ +.3f}} and {{E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2_both;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_alcohol ~ +.3f}}, from the family's {{E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_alcohol ~ +.3f}}, while the ester pairs' shortfall does not grow ({{E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k1_both;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_ester ~ +.3f}} to {{E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2_both;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_ester ~ +.3f}} for {{E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_ester ~ +.3f}}), which no weighting had done; and the alcohol pairs' co-response change under APL comes inside the flies' interval, at {{E92/coresponse_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2_both;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} to {{E92/coresponse_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2_bdiv;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}}. The main target does not follow. The pattern part is {{diff:E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2_both;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern -- E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} to {{diff:E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2_bdiv;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern -- E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} above the family's, in the shape part, and the mean APL effect falls to between {{E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2_bdiv;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} and {{E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2_both;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}, for the flies' {{data:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}}.

These runs were made for the record at fixed scales, with only the APL scale set again, and none was a candidate for the choice. Whether the cost belongs to the fixed scales or to the form would take a fit of the family with it, which this experiment did not make. A gain at the boutons has since been run as a candidate at weaker strengths, from a fiftieth to about a seventh of the fitted weight, and it costs at each of them ([below](#bouton-share)); a fit of the family with it was again kept for a choice or an equal, and was not made.

**The summed form reads as the family with the clipping, and it lies on the line.** The runs with the summed form ([above](#summed-drive)) were read as the family was. On the fits as they are and in the family fitted again with it, the somata's group means are within {{lit:0.01 # computed from results/E92_steps_like_for_like/somata_F_means.csv, rows kind=population, wiring=S: the largest absolute difference from family C2 of families E91_B1_k2_s1 (0.0074) and E91_refit (0.0094) over the 16 like-for-like readings, both conditions and the groups ester, alcohol, ester_alcohol and other}} of the family's in each of the 16 readings, with APL on and without, for the four groups; the claws are within {{lit:0.003 # computed from results/E92_steps_like_for_like/claws_F_settled.csv: the largest absolute difference between families E91_refit and C2 in the mean over the four wirings, over the two claw readings and the groups ester, alcohol, ester_alcohol and other (0.0030; 0.0023 in results/E92_steps_like_for_like/claws_F.csv, with the level before the odor taken over the whole half second)}} and the two steps within {{lit:0.01 # computed from results/E92_steps_like_for_like/steps_F_settled.csv, rows population=S: the largest absolute difference in column model between families E91_refit and C2 over the 16 like-for-like readings, both conditions and the groups ester, alcohol, ester_alcohol and other (0.0096; 0.0089 in results/E92_steps_like_for_like/steps_F.csv, with the level before the odor taken over the whole half second)}}, and they differ from the flies' in the same readings and in the same direction.

Against the weightings' line the summed form moves the fits as they are by {{diff:E92/line_F.csv:family=B1_F_k2_s1;population=S;readout=cal:resid -- E92/line_F.csv:family=C2_unchanged;population=S;readout=cal:resid ~ +.3f}} through the readout and {{diff:E92/line_F.csv:family=B1_F_k2_s1;population=S;readout=raw:resid -- E92/line_F.csv:family=C2_unchanged;population=S;readout=raw:resid ~ +.3f}} on raw counts at the family's weighting, and the family fitted again by {{diff:E92/line_F.csv:family=E91_refit;population=S;readout=cal:resid -- E92/line_F.csv:family=C2_unchanged;population=S;readout=cal:resid ~ +.3f}} and {{diff:E92/line_F.csv:family=E91_refit;population=S;readout=raw:resid -- E92/line_F.csv:family=C2_unchanged;population=S;readout=raw:resid ~ +.3f}}, where the flies are {{lit:0.09866993033793536 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, lines.cal.S.flies.trial_mean_all.resid ~ +.3f}} and {{lit:0.10701777447779079 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, lines.raw.S.flies.trial_mean_all.resid ~ +.3f}} away. The summed form is one more weighting on the line.

The one shift beyond the weightings' scatter is on the base with the flies' recruitment, an [oracle](#fn-oracle). There the summed form moves the model toward the flies' side by {{diff:E92/line_F.csv:family=B2_F_k2_s1;population=S;readout=cal:resid -- E92/line_F.csv:family=C2_F_k2;population=S;readout=cal:resid ~ +.3f}} and {{diff:E92/line_F.csv:family=B2_F_k1_s1;population=S;readout=cal:resid -- E92/line_F.csv:family=C2_F_k1;population=S;readout=cal:resid ~ +.3f}} through the readout at exponents of 2 and 1, and by {{diff:E92/line_F.csv:family=B2_F_k2_s1;population=S;readout=raw:resid -- E92/line_F.csv:family=C2_F_k2;population=S;readout=raw:resid ~ +.3f}} and {{diff:E92/line_F.csv:family=B2_F_k1_s1;population=S;readout=raw:resid -- E92/line_F.csv:family=C2_F_k1;population=S;readout=raw:resid ~ +.3f}} on raw counts, a tenth to a fifth of the way to the flies. The larger of the two is the setting that had been chosen there, at an exponent of 1, for which both groups' errors shrink ([above](#summed-drive)); on the four held-out wirings it lies {{diff:E92/line_F.csv:family=B2_F_k1_s1;population=T;readout=cal:resid -- E92/line_F.csv:family=B2_F_k2;population=T;readout=cal:resid ~ +.3f}} beyond its base through the readout. Its control, a fixed inhibition of each KC that is the same for every odor, moves {{diff:E92/line_F.csv:family=B2_F_k1_s1_ctrl;population=S;readout=cal:resid -- E92/line_F.csv:family=C2_F_k1;population=S;readout=cal:resid ~ +.3f}} on the wirings of the earlier searches, less than half as far, although on the main target the control had gained more than half of what the setting gains.

On that base the place against the line and the pattern part do not move together, and the setting stays what it was, a lead under an oracle. Run again with every stage saved, the four refits and the chosen setting on the four wirings reproduce their saved runs without one differing spike count, with APL on and with APL off.

**Realism.** The first and the third part change no model: they read saved runs that are inside the four realism bands, and the stage runs of the third part reproduce their fits.

The second part adds no fitted parameter. A gain or a divisive form replaces the subtraction, and the APL scale is set again so that the response rate with APL on is the fit's; the responses with APL off are the fit's own. Its {{lit:28 # the 16 rows of results/E92_steps_like_for_like/runs_B1.csv and the 12 rows of results/E92_steps_like_for_like/runs_B2.csv}} runs therefore have the fits' response rates, {{E92/runs_B1.csv:B_F_k2_div_real:rate_on ~ .3f}} to {{E92/runs_B1.csv:B_F_k2_div_P1:rate_on ~ .3f}} with APL on and {{E92/runs_B1.csv:B_F_k2_div_M1:rate_off ~ .3f}} to {{E92/runs_B1.csv:B_F_k2_div_P2:rate_off ~ .3f}} with APL off (ratios of {{E92/runs_B1.csv:B_F_k2_div_M1:ratio ~ .2f}} to {{E92/runs_B1.csv:B_F_k2_div_P2:ratio ~ .2f}}), for the flies' {{data:noise_ctrl_frac ~ .3f}} and {{data:noise_tnt_frac ~ .3f}} ({{data:noise_rate_ratio_fraction ~ .2f}}). {{lit:Four # the rows with a realism_flag in results/E92_steps_like_for_like/runs_B1.csv (B_F_k2_div_real, B_none_div_real, B_none_div_P2 and B_none_div_M1), none in runs_B2.csv; the same four in results/E92_steps_like_for_like/verdict_B.json, flagged_runs}} of them are outside a band, all with the gain at the claw.

At the family's weighting on the real wiring the response rate ρ with APL on falls to {{E92/runs_B1.csv:B_F_k2_div_real:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}}, from the unchanged fit's {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}} and where the band asks 0.37 or more; on the three other wirings it is {{E92/runs_B1.csv:B_F_k2_div_M1:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}} to {{E92/runs_B1.csv:B_F_k2_div_P2:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}}. Without a weighting the distribution of the number of odors per KC with APL on is {{E92/runs_B1.csv:B_none_div_M1:opk_on_tv ~ .3f}} to {{E92/runs_B1.csv:B_none_div_P2:opk_on_tv ~ .3f}} from the flies' on three of the four wirings (band {{data:noise_ctrl_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .3f}}).

The gain at the family's weighting is the divisive setting with the lowest APL-effect loss, so that what it reads comes, on one wiring, with a per-odor pattern of response rates unlike the flies'. Counted by the recordings' own criterion, as the bands counted until 2026-11-10, {{lit:13 # the rows of results/E92_steps_like_for_like/runs_B1.csv (2: B_none_div_P1 and B_F_k0.5_div_P2) and runs_B2.csv (11) with a realism_flag_zcrit and no realism_flag}} more runs would be outside the band on odors per KC with APL on, eleven of them among the twelve runs with the divisive inhibition at the boutons.

What is hard to defend is the size of the gain. At the family's weighting the divisor on a responding KC's claw is {{E92/runs_B1.csv:B_F_k2_div_real:divisor_kc_p50 ~ .2f}} at the median and {{E92/runs_B1.csv:B_F_k2_div_M1:divisor_kc_p90 ~ .2f}} to {{E92/runs_B1.csv:B_F_k2_div_P2:divisor_kc_p90 ~ .2f}} at the 90th percentile, but it reaches {{E92/runs_B1.csv:B_F_k2_div_P2:divisor_kc_max ~ .0f}} to {{E92/runs_B1.csv:B_F_k2_div_real:divisor_kc_max ~ .0f}}, and {{E92/runs_B1.csv:B_F_k2_div_M1:divisor_kc_share_above10 ~ .1%}} to {{E92/runs_B1.csv:B_F_k2_div_real:divisor_kc_share_above10 ~ .1%}} of the responders' claws are divided by more than ten during the odor. Those are the claws of the KCs with the largest breadth weights: among the KCs that respond without APL, the family's APL→KC weight at the 90th percentile is {{E92/runs_B1.csv:B_F_k2_div_P2:fac_resp_p90_over_p10 ~ .0f}} to {{E92/runs_B1.csv:B_F_k2_div_real:fac_resp_p90_over_p10 ~ .0f}} times that at the 10th, and a gain carries that spread into the claw.

A shunt that divides a claw's input by more than about ten is hard to defend, and one that divides it by hundreds more so. At an exponent of 1 the largest divisor is {{E92/runs_B1.csv:B_F_k1_div_P2:divisor_kc_max ~ .0f}} to {{E92/runs_B1.csv:B_F_k1_div_real:divisor_kc_max ~ .0f}}, and without a weighting {{E92/runs_B1.csv:B_none_div_real:divisor_kc_max ~ .1f}} to {{E92/runs_B1.csv:B_none_div_P1:divisor_kc_max ~ .1f}}. At the boutons the divisor is {{E92/runs_B2.csv:B_F_k2_both_M1:divisor_bouton_p50 ~ .2f}} to {{E92/runs_B2.csv:B_F_k2_bdiv_P1:divisor_bouton_p50 ~ .2f}} at the median and {{E92/runs_B2.csv:B_F_k2_both_M1:divisor_bouton_max ~ .1f}} to {{E92/runs_B2.csv:B_F_k2_bdiv_P1:divisor_bouton_max ~ .1f}} at the most, which a shunt could do. The APL scale set again is {{E92/runs_B1.csv:B_F_k1_div_P2:apl_factor ~ .2f}} to {{E92/runs_B1.csv:B_F_k2_div_P1:apl_factor ~ .2f}} times the fit's with the gain at the claws and {{E92/runs_B2.csv:B_F_k2_both_P1:apl_factor ~ .3f}} to {{E92/runs_B2.csv:B_F_k2_bdiv_M1:apl_factor ~ .3f}} times with the divisive inhibition at the boutons, a change of units more than of strength, and no run is at a limit of the search.

Nothing was bought with the bands: the settings with the gain are level or worse on the main target with or without the flagged runs. The like-for-like readings of the somata hold the 66 pairs among the twelve megamat odors, so that no pair of paa, euc, -aPine or B-myr enters them; the line and the main target use all 120 pairs, with paa, euc and -aPine at [ORN input of another concentration](#fn-concentrations).

**What follows.** The feedback APL's inhibition of the KCs is closed in its form. A subtraction clipped at each claw, a subtraction summed over the claws and a gain at the claw read the same or worse on the main target at every weighting, on the fits as they are and at the model's 0.5 s pulse, and the reference stays the family with the clipping at each claw.

With the static forms and the flies' form simulated in place of APL ([the form of APL's inhibition in the flies' own responses](#inhibition-form); [the common error split into who responds and how strongly](#responder-sets)), the breadth weighting ([above](#breadth-weighting)) and the place where the inhibition is summed ([above](#summed-drive)), nothing is left to vary in how APL inhibits the KCs in this family.

Two descriptions stay on APL's side, and neither changes a base. A divisive inhibition at the boutons is the one form that moves the model clearly off the weightings' line toward the flies and gives the alcohol pairs the flies' co-response change without taking from the ester pairs, at a cost in the pattern part and in the mean APL effect at fixed scales; it was not fitted. And on the base with the flies' recruitment the summed form moves the model a tenth to a fifth of the way to the flies' side of the line, under an oracle.

APL's other path, the inhibition of the PN boutons, was then still open in its strength and in its form. It has been run since ([below](#bouton-share)): the fitted strength is the best, less or more of the inhibition at the boutons costs, and a gain there costs at every strength, so that APL's side of this family is closed at both of its sites.

For the mechanism between the claw and the soma that the lead asks for ([above](#responder-sets)), the brief is now stated on the somata. With APL on it has to hold the ester pairs further apart and the alcohol pairs closer together, by the amounts above, in every reading that treats the two sides alike; this is the two-signed part of the common error. The weightings' line says why no re-weighting, summation or gain of APL's inhibition has done it: whatever holds one group further apart, relative to the mean pair, holds the other further apart too.

From here a mechanism is placed against the line, beside the main target and beside the step from claws to somata in wild-type flies, and a change that moves the model along the line is read as one more weighting. Leaving the line toward the flies is asked of a mechanism and does not suffice, controls having left it.

The earlier comparison of the stages ([above](#model-stages)) is qualified in two respects. Its lead on the ester pairs is now a difference at the somata in every like-for-like reading, with APL on. Its reading of the alcohol pairs, an excess made at the step without APL by somata that are too alike there, holds only with the calibrated readout set against the flies' trial means: read alike, the alcohol pairs are too far apart with APL on in every reading, and without APL they are the flies' or too far apart, never too alike.

Whether anything is asked of the side without APL then depends on whether a KC's calcium signal saturates with the KC's firing, a question about the recordings that is with the pending work at the end of the page. The steps from claws to somata are not read again from all claws: what would let them place the error is still the stage recordings asked of the experimenter.

On the input, what leaves the line toward the flies is made glomerulus by glomerulus or odor by odor, fitted to the recordings or taken from single flies, and the rows that have been measured for the glomeruli without input do not leave it ([below](#missing-glomeruli)); what such changes stand for in the flies' input or antennal lobe is open. Every reading here is of the model's 0.5 s pulse without trial noise, in the family without a firing ceiling; the readings at the flies' pulse, through the trial noise and with the ceiling had been kept for a setting that passed, and were not made.

### The PN boutons' share of APL's inhibition: whether the best family's match depends on how much of APL's inhibition is made at the PN boutons, whether less or more of it there or a gain in place of the subtraction lowers the pattern part, and what the connectome's share costs {#bouton-share}

%%% hover
bouton share: Of the drive that APL removes from a model's KC claws over the odor pulse, the fraction that is already removed at the PN boutons, before the claws. A claw's loss is its drive without APL minus what is left of it with APL on, and the part made at the boutons is the fall of the bouton rates that reach the claw. Summed over the claws and the odors, from the simulator's own claw-by-bouton weights. Defined in the subsection on the PN boutons' share of APL's inhibition.
fitted dose: The APL→bouton scale of a wiring's own fit of the breadth-2 family, the scale of APL's inhibition of the PN boutons. In the subsection on the PN boutons' share of APL's inhibition the strength of that inhibition is given as a dose, a multiple of the fitted scale, so that a dose of 1 is the fit as it is and a dose of 0 a model without the inhibition.
%%%

**The best family's APL acts on two paths: on the KCs, at each claw, and on the PN boutons, before the claws.** The first had been varied in its weighting, in the place where it is summed and in its form; the second had stayed at the scale that the family was fitted with, under a bound set for an earlier family. In the fits as they are the second path is the larger one.

About seven tenths of the drive that APL takes from the claws is taken at the boutons, as a subtraction that is nearly the same for every odor, where the connectome puts about a tenth of APL's calyx synapses on PN boutons. The fitted strength of that path is the best of those tried, from none of it to four times as much.

With less of the inhibition at the boutons the pattern part rises, by five to six thousandths at a quarter of the fitted strength and below; with more, above the bound, it rises as well; a gain at the boutons in place of the subtraction costs at every strength; and more inhibition at the boutons does not make up for a weaker breadth weighting. Against no half of the recordings is a setting other than the unchanged fits the best, so that nothing was read on held-out wirings, and half the fitted strength is the one equal.

Fitted again with the bouton path held at the strength nearest the connectome's share, the family is worse by about nine thousandths, with no single wiring lower and every half of the recordings worse: the refit recovers most of the size and all of the spread of the effect by moving APL's weight to the KCs, and loses in its shape. More inhibition at the boutons shrinks the alcohol pairs' excess and deepens the ester pairs' shortfall, so that the two groups trade under this path as under every other change on APL's side.

APL's inhibition is thereby closed at both of its sites in this family, in strength and in form. What stays is a statement about the family and its price: its match to the per-pair APL effect rests in part on an offset at the boutons whose share of APL's action is several times APL's share of synapses there, and holding the path near the connectome's share costs about five thousandths of the pattern part at fixed scales and about nine after a refit.

[The claw-to-soma steps read like for like and APL's inhibition as a gain at the claw](#steps-like-for-like) had closed the feedback APL's inhibition of the KCs in its form and had left APL's other path. In the model APL also subtracts from the rate of every PN bouton, in proportion to the connectome's APL→bouton weights and to one fitted scale, and every claw on the bouton receives the lowered rate.

In the eight fits of the breadth-2 family ([the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population)) that scale lies between {{E94/a1_path.csv:wiring=P2:aplpn_fit_multiple ~ .1f}} and {{E94/a1_path.csv:wiring=real:aplpn_fit_multiple ~ .1f}} times the baseline's. It had stayed under a bound of three times the baseline's, which had been set for the reference model, an earlier family under an earlier loss, and nothing had varied it since. A divisive inhibition at the boutons had been run at the fitted weight only, for the record, and had cost the pattern part ([above](#steps-like-for-like)). Whether the family needs the path at its fitted strength, whether the bound holds it back, and whether a weaker divisive inhibition would do better were therefore not known.

The PN boutons' share of APL's inhibition was run on the breadth-2 family, each wiring at its own fit and with the lab's input throughout, in three parts. The first simulated nothing. From the saved stages of the eight fits and the simulator's own claw-by-bouton weights it computed how much of the claws' summed drive APL removes over the odor pulse and how much of that loss is made at the boutons, the bouton share, and it counted, in the connectome tables that the model reads, how many of APL's synapses in the calyx are onto PN boutons.

The second ran the bouton path at other strengths on the four wirings of the earlier searches, on the fits as they are. A dose multiplies a wiring's fitted APL→bouton scale and nothing else. The family ties its other APL weights (APL→KC, KC→APL and bouton→APL) to one scale, and that tied scale was then set again until the number of responses with APL on was the fit's; the somatic threshold and the KC–KC scale stayed the fit's, and the responses with APL off are the fit's own, so that both response rates are held.

The subtraction was run at the family's weighting (the family's measure of a KC's breadth at an exponent of 2) at doses of 0, which is no inhibition of the boutons, and of 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 2 and 4; at an exponent of 1 at doses of 2 and 4, to see whether more inhibition at the boutons makes up for a weaker weighting; and as a gain, a bouton's rate divided by one plus APL's inhibition of it, at 0.02, 0.05 and 0.15 of the fitted weight, the gain at the fitted weight being the run of the earlier subsection. The references are the unchanged fits and the family at an exponent of 1 ([above](#breadth-weighting)).

Before any run was scored the new code was checked: at a dose of 1 it reproduces the saved fits on all eight wirings without one differing spike count, with APL on and with APL off, at a dose of 0 a model built without the path, and with the gain at the fitted weight the earlier run. What would count had been fixed as it was for the summed form and for the gain at the claw.

- The setting with the lowest pattern part against one half of the recordings, for the mean over the four wirings through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout), was to be read on the four held-out wirings against the other half, by the test that the fitted changes were put to ([above](#cross-wiring-fit)), if it was lower than the unchanged fits by 0.0015 or more; the halves were those of two splits of the flies.
- A setting that got that far was to be set against a control in which each KC's mean loss of drive under the setting is given as an inhibition that is the same for every odor.
- A setting with a lower bouton share, with the weaker weighting or with the gain was an equal of the family if its pattern part stayed within 0.003 of the family's against all recordings and against both halves of the first split, with limits on the loss on raw counts, on the mean APL effect and on the realism bands.

The third part fitted the family again with less at the boutons. Of the doses 0.1, 0.25 and 0.5, the one whose bouton share on the four wirings is nearest the connectome's share was held, and the family's other parameters were fitted from the run at that dose, with the family's own loss, on the four wirings of the earlier searches. Refits on the four held-out wirings, a fit above the bound and a fit with the gain had been kept for a choice or an equal.

**In the fits as they are, about seven tenths of what APL takes from the claws is taken at the boutons.** Over the odor pulse APL removes {{E94/a1_path.csv:wiring=M2:drive_removed ~ .2f}} to {{E94/a1_path.csv:wiring=P3:drive_removed ~ .2f}} of the claws' summed drive on the eight wirings, and {{E94/a1_path.csv:wiring=P2:bouton_share ~ .2f}} to {{E94/a1_path.csv:wiring=real:bouton_share ~ .2f}} of that loss is already made at the boutons, before the feedback inhibition at the claws acts.

This bouton share is largest for the KCs with few claws: {{E94/a1_path.csv:wiring=real:bouton_share_1-4 ~ .2f}} to {{E94/a1_path.csv:wiring=M3:bouton_share_1-4 ~ .2f}} for KCs with one to four claws, {{E94/a1_path.csv:wiring=P2:bouton_share_5-8 ~ .2f}} to {{E94/a1_path.csv:wiring=real:bouton_share_5-8 ~ .2f}} for those with five to eight and {{E94/a1_path.csv:wiring=P2:bouton_share_9+ ~ .2f}} to {{E94/a1_path.csv:wiring=real:bouton_share_9+ ~ .2f}} for those with nine or more, the KCs that the breadth weighting loads at the claws. It hardly depends on the odor, lying between {{E94/a1_by_odor.csv:wiring=P2;odor=1-5ol:bouton_share ~ .2f}} and {{E94/a1_by_odor.csv:wiring=real;odor=euc:bouton_share ~ .2f}} over the 16 odors and the eight wirings, because the subtraction itself hardly does.

APL takes {{E94/a1_path.csv:wiring=M2:bouton_sub_p50 ~ .1f}} to {{E94/a1_path.csv:wiring=P3:bouton_sub_p50 ~ .1f}} Hz from the median bouton, {{E94/a1_path.csv:wiring=M2:bouton_share_removed ~ .2f}} to {{E94/a1_path.csv:wiring=P3:bouton_share_removed ~ .2f}} of the boutons' summed rate, and at the median bouton that amount varies over the 16 odors by {{E94/a1_path.csv:wiring=P2:sub_cv_over_odors_median_bouton ~ .1%}} to {{E94/a1_path.csv:wiring=real:sub_cv_over_odors_median_bouton ~ .1%}} of its mean (its standard deviation over the odors as a fraction of the mean). APL's inhibition of the boutons therefore works as an offset. Every claw's input is lowered by about the same amount whatever the odor, and a KC loses in proportion to its number of claws, in effect a threshold that APL raises with a KC's claw count.

The connectome does not suggest a path of that size: a fraction of {{E94/a2_connectome.csv:set=calyx, all:share_pn ~ .3f}} to {{E94/a2_connectome.csv:set=calyx, assigned, KCs with a type:share_pn ~ .3f}} of APL's output synapses in the calyx is onto PN boutons and the rest onto KCs, according to which synapses are counted. A share of synapses is not a share of inhibition, since nothing says that a synapse onto a bouton and one onto a claw inhibit alike, so that the two numbers are set side by side as a description.

At the bouton stage alone the subtraction acts in the direction that the two-signed part of the common error asks for. With APL's activity as saved, it adds {{E94/a3_summary.csv:form=sub;dose=1.0;measure=cosine;signal=evoked;group=ester:change ~ +.3f}} to the cosine distance between the evoked bouton patterns of two ester odors and {{E94/a3_summary.csv:form=sub;dose=1.0;measure=cosine;signal=evoked;group=alcohol:change ~ +.3f}} to that of two alcohol odors at the fitted dose (the mean over the eight wirings), and more for the esters than for the alcohols at every dose and with the gain as well. More inhibition at the boutons had therefore been thought likely to raise the ester pairs' APL effect relative to the alcohol pairs'.

![Left: the pattern part of the APL-effect loss, for the mean over the four wirings of the earlier searches through the calibrated readout, against the dose of APL's inhibition of the PN boutons, the APL→bouton scale as a multiple of each wiring's fitted scale (logarithmic axis, with a dose of 0 placed at the left; the tick labels to the left of it are an artefact of the axis). Black: against all recordings; red and blue: against the two halves of the first split of the flies. Solid lines and circles: the subtraction at the family's breadth weighting (exponent 2); dashed lines and squares: the subtraction at an exponent of 1; dotted lines and triangles: a gain at the boutons at the family's weighting. Dashed horizontal lines: the unchanged fits; hollow markers: a setting with a run outside the realism bands. Right: the bouton share, the share of the claws' loss of drive that is made at the boutons, for the same settings as the mean over the four wirings, with the share of APL's calyx synapses that the connectome puts on PN boutons as the green band.](results/E94_bouton_share/E94_dose.png)

APL's inhibition of the PN boutons at other doses and as a gain, against the unchanged fits: the mean over the four wirings of the earlier searches, on the fits as they are with the tied APL scale set again, against the main target as measured, all recordings, through the calibrated readout. The bouton share is given as its range over the four wirings.

The squares of the amplitude part and the shape part add up to the squared pattern part, and a spread below one means that APL moves the model's pairs apart more evenly than the flies'; no setting is chosen by a correlation ([why](#fn-pattern-split)). The mean error of a group is the model's per-pair APL effect minus the flies', each side's mean removed, over the 15 ester pairs and over the 6 alcohol pairs.

The distance from the weightings' line is positive on the flies' side, and the co-response change is read as trial means at the reading's own noise; in the row of the KC data these two cells are the flies' own, the second with its 90 % interval. The first model row is the reference, and the last row is the family fitted again, for which the last two readings were not made
