**The fitted dose is the best, and less inhibition at the boutons costs.** Against all recordings the unchanged fits read a pattern part of {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, for a floor of {{data:apl_effect_pattern_floor ~ .4f}}. Without the bouton path the family reads {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d0;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, at a tenth and at a quarter of the fitted dose {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d0.1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} and {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d0.25;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, and at half of it {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d0.5;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} (the figure, and the first rows of the table); a cost of up to 0.008 had been expected.

The tied APL scale makes up the response rate, at {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d0_P2:apl_factor ~ .1f}} to {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d0_real:apl_factor ~ .1f}} times the fit's without the bouton path, and it does not make up the effect. Without the path the mean APL effect through the readout is {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d0;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}, for the fits' {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} and the flies' {{data:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}}; the spread of the per-pair effect falls to {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d0;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_sd_ratio ~ .2f}} of the flies' from {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_sd_ratio ~ .2f}}, so that the amplitude part rises from {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_amplitude ~ .4f}} to {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d0;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_amplitude ~ .4f}}; and the loss on raw counts rises from {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d1;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_loss ~ .4f}} to {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d0;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_loss ~ .4f}}.

A tenth or a quarter of the fitted dose brings most of the size and the spread back, and the cost then sits in the shape part ({{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d0.1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_shape ~ .4f}} and {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d0.25;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_shape ~ .4f}} for the fits' {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_shape ~ .4f}}). It is the alcohol pairs that pay for a smaller part at the boutons: their excess grows from {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_alcohol ~ +.3f}} to {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d0;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_alcohol ~ +.3f}} without the path, with the ester pairs' shortfall where it was ({{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_ester ~ +.3f}} and {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d0;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_ester ~ +.3f}}).

Against each of the four halves of the recordings the setting with the lowest pattern part is the unchanged fits' own, among the settings of all three kinds and whether or not the two with a run outside the realism bands are counted, so that nothing went to the four held-out wirings and no control was run. One setting is an equal, half the fitted dose. Its pattern part is {{E94/equal.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d0.5:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} above the family's against all recordings and {{E94/equal.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d0.5:d_pattern_halfA ~ .4f}} and {{E94/equal.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d0.5:d_pattern_halfB ~ .4f}} above it against the two halves of the first split, inside the 0.003 allowed; its loss on raw counts is {{E94/equal.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d0.5:d_raw_loss ~ .4f}} higher, where 0.005 was allowed; its mean APL effect is {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d0.5;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}; and its four runs are inside the bands, with a bouton share of {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d0.5_P2:bouton_share ~ .2f}} to {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d0.5_real:bouton_share ~ .2f}}.

Its steps from claws to somata, read like for like ([above](#steps-like-for-like)), are within {{lit:0.03 # computed from results/preodor_startup_check_viki/E94_bouton_share_steps_equal_vs_C2.csv (the steps at the settled pre-odor level, 2026-11-15): the largest absolute settled_equal_minus_C2, families B_sub_k2_d0.5 and C2, over the 16 like-for-like readings, both conditions and every group of pairs (0.0300, the four ester near pairs with APL on, linear_noise_none_pearson; over E90's start-up window, results/E94_bouton_share/steps.csv, it was 0.025)}} of the family's in every group of pairs, so that the reading of the steps is unchanged. The family could thus make a somewhat smaller part of its inhibition at the boutons at no cost that the recordings resolve, and no less than that: at a quarter of the fitted dose, with a bouton share of {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d0.25_P2:bouton_share ~ .2f}} to {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d0.25_real:bouton_share ~ .2f}}, the pattern part is {{E94/equal.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d0.25:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} higher.

**More inhibition at the boutons costs as well, and does not make up for a weaker weighting.** At twice and at four times the fitted dose the APL→bouton scale is {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d2_P2:aplpn_multiple ~ .1f}} to {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d2_real:aplpn_multiple ~ .1f}} and {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d4_P2:aplpn_multiple ~ .1f}} to {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d4_real:aplpn_multiple ~ .1f}} times the baseline's, above the bound of three, and the bouton share {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d2_P2:bouton_share ~ .2f}} to {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d2_real:bouton_share ~ .2f}} and {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d4_M1:bouton_share ~ .2f}} to {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d4_real:bouton_share ~ .2f}}. APL then acts almost wholly before the claws, and the tied APL scale falls to {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d4_P1:apl_factor ~ .2f}} to {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d4_M1:apl_factor ~ .2f}} of the fit's at four times.

The pattern part is {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} and {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d4;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, higher than the fits' in the shape part ({{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_shape ~ .4f}} and {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d4;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_shape ~ .4f}} for {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_shape ~ .4f}}), where a change within 0.004 either way had been expected. As far as runs at fixed scales can say, the bound is therefore not what holds the family back.

The two groups part. The alcohol pairs' excess shrinks from {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_alcohol ~ +.3f}} to {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_alcohol ~ +.3f}} and {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d4;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_alcohol ~ +.3f}}, and the ester pairs' shortfall deepens from {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_ester ~ +.3f}} to {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_ester ~ +.3f}} and {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d4;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_ester ~ +.3f}}. The reading of the bouton stage had predicted the opposite for the ester pairs: what the subtraction adds to their distance at the boutons is lost again on the way to the KCs' responses, and what a change of APL does to the per-pair effect is once more read from simulations only.

Against the weightings' line the two settings stay close to the family's place, at {{E94/line.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:resid ~ +.3f}} and {{E94/line.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d4;unit=S;readout=cal:resid ~ +.3f}} for the family's {{E94/line.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:resid ~ +.3f}} and the flies' {{lit:0.09866993033793536 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, lines.cal.S.flies.trial_mean_all.resid ~ +.3f}}. The alcohol pairs' co-response change under APL rises to {{E94/coresponse.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d2;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} and {{E94/coresponse.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d4;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} from {{E94/coresponse.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d1;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}}, and at four times the fitted dose it is inside the flies' interval ({{E94/coresponse.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d1;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:flies_lo ~ .2f}} to {{E94/coresponse.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d1;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:flies_hi ~ .2f}}), at a cost of {{E94/equal.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d4:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} in the pattern part.

At an exponent of 1 more inhibition at the boutons makes the weaker weighting worse: {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k1_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} and {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k1_d4;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} at twice and at four times the dose, for {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k1_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} at the fitted dose. An offset at the boutons is no substitute for the weighting at the claws.

**A gain at the boutons costs at every strength.** With a bouton's rate divided by one plus APL's inhibition of it, the pattern part is {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_gain_k2_d0.02;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_gain_k2_d0.05;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} and {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_gain_k2_d0.15;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} at 0.02, 0.05 and 0.15 of the fitted weight, for {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_gain_k2_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} at the fitted weight ([above](#steps-like-for-like)) and for the subtraction's {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}. The weakest is the nearest, {{E94/equal.csv:variant=B_gain_k2_d0.02:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} above the family where an equal had to be within 0.003, and the cost grows with the strength, as the mean APL effect falls ({{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_gain_k2_d0.02;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}, {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_gain_k2_d0.05;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} and {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_gain_k2_d0.15;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}, and {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_gain_k2_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} at the fitted weight). The cost of the gain is therefore not one of the strength at which it had first been run.

The gain puts the spread of the per-pair effect at the flies' ({{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_gain_k2_d0.02;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_sd_ratio ~ .2f}} and {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_gain_k2_d0.05;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_sd_ratio ~ .2f}} times at the two weaker strengths, with amplitude parts of {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_gain_k2_d0.02;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_amplitude ~ .4f}} and {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_gain_k2_d0.05;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_amplitude ~ .4f}}), and it loses that and more in the shape part ({{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_gain_k2_d0.02;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_shape ~ .4f}} and {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_gain_k2_d0.05;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_shape ~ .4f}} for the fits' {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_shape ~ .4f}}). It does for the two groups what the subtraction does not. The ester pairs' shortfall shrinks a little, to between {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_gain_k2_d0.02;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_ester ~ +.3f}} and {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_gain_k2_d0.15;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_ester ~ +.3f}} from {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_ester ~ +.3f}}, and the alcohol pairs' excess falls with the strength, from {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_gain_k2_d0.02;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_alcohol ~ +.3f}} at the weakest, a little above the family's {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_alcohol ~ +.3f}}, to {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_gain_k2_d0.15;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_alcohol ~ +.3f}} at the strongest.

The model leaves the weightings' line toward the flies at every strength, at {{E94/line.csv:variant=B_gain_k2_d0.02;unit=S;readout=cal:resid ~ +.3f}}, {{E94/line.csv:variant=B_gain_k2_d0.05;unit=S;readout=cal:resid ~ +.3f}} and {{E94/line.csv:variant=B_gain_k2_d0.15;unit=S;readout=cal:resid ~ +.3f}} for the family's {{E94/line.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:resid ~ +.3f}}, as it had at the fitted weight ({{E94/line.csv:variant=B_gain_k2_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:resid ~ +.3f}}), and at the strongest of the three the alcohol pairs' co-response change under APL is inside the flies' interval, at {{E94/coresponse.csv:variant=B_gain_k2_d0.15;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}}. None of these settings gets further than a third of the way to the flies' place against the line ({{lit:0.09866993033793536 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, lines.cal.S.flies.trial_mean_all.resid ~ +.3f}}), and each step toward it is paid for in the shape of the effect.

Weak as these gains are, they make most of the claws' loss at the boutons, their bouton share being {{E94/runs_B3.csv:B_gain_k2_d0.02_P2:bouton_share ~ .2f}} to {{E94/runs_B3.csv:B_gain_k2_d0.15_real:bouton_share ~ .2f}}. The family was not fitted with the gain, such a fit having been kept for a choice or an equal.

**Fitted again with the bouton path near the connectome's share, the family is worse.** Of the three lower doses, a tenth of the fitted dose has the bouton share nearest the connectome's, {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d0.1_P2:bouton_share ~ .2f}} to {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d0.1_real:bouton_share ~ .2f}} on the four wirings, which is still more than twice the connectome's share of synapses. With the APL→bouton scale held there, at {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d0.1_P2:aplpn_multiple ~ .2f}} to {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d0.1_real:aplpn_multiple ~ .2f}} times the baseline's, and the family's other parameters fitted again, the population reads a pattern part of {{E94/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all ~ .4f}}, for the unchanged fits' {{E94/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}} and for {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d0.1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} at the same dose with the scales fixed (the last row of the table).

No single wiring is lower, the four moving by {{diff:E94/d_scores.csv:unit=P1:pattern_all -- E94/d_scores.csv:unit=P1:pattern_all_unchanged ~ +.4f}} to {{diff:E94/d_scores.csv:unit=real:pattern_all -- E94/d_scores.csv:unit=real:pattern_all_unchanged ~ +.4f}}, and against the two halves of the first split the refits read {{E94/d_scores.csv:unit=S:halfA ~ .4f}} and {{E94/d_scores.csv:unit=S:halfB ~ .4f}} for {{E94/d_scores.csv:unit=S:halfA_unchanged ~ .4f}} and {{E94/d_scores.csv:unit=S:halfB_unchanged ~ .4f}}; an equal at the connectome's share had been thought about as likely as not after a refit. The fit, whose loss holds the mean effect and both definitions of the model's side, brings the mean APL effect back to {{E94/d_scores.csv:unit=S:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} from {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d0.1;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} and the spread of the effect to the flies' ({{E94/d_scores.csv:unit=S:sd_ratio ~ .2f}} times, an amplitude part of {{E94/d_scores.csv:unit=S:amplitude ~ .4f}}), and it pays in the shape part ({{E94/d_scores.csv:unit=S:shape ~ .4f}}), with the alcohol pairs' excess at {{E94/d_scores.csv:unit=S:err_alcohol ~ +.3f}}, twice the family's {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_alcohol ~ +.3f}}. It does so by moving APL's weight to the KCs.

On three wirings the APL→KC scale ends at {{E94/fits.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_aplpnhold_k2_d1:apl_factor_vs_e3 ~ .1f}} to {{E94/fits.csv:wiring-curveball_within_type_matched-seed1_rate0.068_aplboth_aplpnhold_k2_d1:apl_factor_vs_e3 ~ .1f}} times the baseline's, from {{E72/stats_variants.csv:wiring_label=real:apl_factor_vs_e3 ~ .1f}} to {{E72/stats_variants.csv:wiring_label=P1:apl_factor_vs_e3 ~ .1f}} in the unchanged fits, and on the fourth the fit leaves the family's region, with a somatic threshold of {{E94/fits.csv:wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed2_rate0.068_aplboth_aplpnhold_k2_d1:thr_factor ~ .2f}} of the baseline's from {{E72/stats_variants.csv:wiring_label=P2:thr_factor ~ .2f}} and a KC–KC scale of {{E94/fits.csv:wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed2_rate0.068_aplboth_aplpnhold_k2_d1:kc_kc_inh ~ .0f}} from {{E72/stats_variants.csv:wiring_label=P2:kc_kc_inh ~ .0f}}, as one refit with the fuller input did ([below](#missing-glomeruli)); the population's direction does not rest on that fit, all four being worse.

The loss on raw counts is higher as well, {{E94/d_scores.csv:unit=S:raw_loss ~ .4f}} for {{E94/d_scores.csv:unit=S:raw_loss_unchanged ~ .4f}}. The breadth-weighted inhibition at the claws thus replaces the size of what the boutons' offset does and not its pattern. The refits on the four held-out wirings had been kept for an equal and were not run. The dose that was held is an upper reading of the connectome's share, and the run without the path, at fixed scales, says which way a lower one would go.

**Realism.** No parameter was added. A scale that the family already has was multiplied, or the subtraction at the boutons was replaced by a gain, and both response rates were held, the one with APL on by the tied APL scale and the one with APL off by the fit's own run. The {{lit:44 # the 24 rows of results/E94_bouton_share/runs_B1.csv, the 8 of runs_B2.csv and the 12 of runs_B3.csv}} runs have response rates of {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d0.5_real:rate_on ~ .3f}} to {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d2_P1:rate_on ~ .3f}} with APL on and {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d0.5_M1:rate_off ~ .3f}} to {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d0.5_P2:rate_off ~ .3f}} with APL off (ratios of {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d0.5_M1:ratio ~ .2f}} to {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d2_P2:ratio ~ .2f}}), and the four refits {{E94/d_scores.csv:unit=P2:rate_on ~ .3f}} to {{E94/d_scores.csv:unit=real:rate_on ~ .3f}} and {{E94/d_scores.csv:unit=real:rate_off ~ .3f}} to {{E94/d_scores.csv:unit=P1:rate_off ~ .3f}} ({{E94/d_scores.csv:unit=real:ratio ~ .2f}} to {{E94/d_scores.csv:unit=P1:ratio ~ .2f}}), for the flies' {{data:noise_ctrl_frac ~ .3f}} and {{data:noise_tnt_frac ~ .3f}} ({{data:noise_rate_ratio_fraction ~ .2f}}).

{{lit:Two # the rows with a realism_flag in results/E94_bouton_share/runs_B1.csv (B_sub_k2_d0_real and B_sub_k2_d0.1_real); none in runs_B2.csv, runs_B3.csv or d_scores.csv; the same two in results/E94_bouton_share/verdict.json, flagged_runs}} runs are outside a band, both on the real wiring and both on the response rate ρ with APL on. Without the bouton path it falls to {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d0_real:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}}, from the unchanged fit's {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}}, and at a tenth of the fitted dose it is {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d0.1_real:rate_rho_on ~ .3f}}, just under the 0.37 that the band asks; on the three other wirings it is {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d0_M1:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}} to {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d0_P1:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}} without the path. On the real wiring the per-odor pattern of response rates thus needs the boutons' offset as well. Neither setting is a chosen one or the equal, and the choice comes out the same with and without them.

Every other run and the four refits are inside the four bands, with a response rate ρ with APL on of {{E94/d_scores.csv:unit=real:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}} or more and a distribution of the number of odors per KC that is at most {{E94/runs_B3.csv:B_gain_k2_d0.15_M1:opk_on_tv ~ .3f}} from the flies' with APL on (band {{data:noise_ctrl_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .3f}}) and {{E94/d_scores.csv:unit=P2:opk_off_tv ~ .3f}} with APL off (band {{data:noise_tnt_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .3f}}). Counted by the recordings' own criterion, as the bands counted until 2026-11-10, {{lit:six # the rows of results/E94_bouton_share/runs_B2.csv (B_sub_k1_d4_real, B_sub_k1_d4_P2 and B_sub_k1_d4_M1) and runs_B3.csv (B_gain_k2_d0.15_real, B_gain_k2_d0.15_P2 and B_gain_k2_d0.15_M1) with a realism_flag_zcrit and no realism_flag}} more runs would be outside the band on odors per KC with APL on: the exponent of 1 at four times the dose and the gain at 0.15 of the fitted weight, on three wirings each.

The largest spike count of a KC to one odor with APL on is {{E94/runs_B3.csv:B_gain_k2_d0.02_P2:max_count_on ~ .0f}} to {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d0_P1:max_count_on ~ .0f}} over the runs, in a family that nothing bounds there ([the firing ceiling for the KCs](#firing-ceiling)). Three things bear on what can be defended.

- The doses above the fitted one put the APL→bouton scale at {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d2_P2:aplpn_multiple ~ .1f}} to {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d4_real:aplpn_multiple ~ .1f}} times the baseline's, above the bound of three, and they read worse; they do not silence the boutons, the share of bouton-by-odor entries at zero staying at {{E94/runs_B2.csv:B_sub_k1_d4_P2:bouton_zero_share ~ .1%}} or less in every run, where the estimate at APL's saved activity had put it at {{E94/a3_summary.csv:form=sub;dose=2.0;measure=cosine;signal=evoked;group=ester:zero_share ~ .0%}} and {{E94/a3_summary.csv:form=sub;dose=4.0;measure=cosine;signal=evoked;group=ester:zero_share ~ .0%}} at twice and at four times, because the tied APL scale and APL's own activity fall as the dose rises.
- The gain's divisor at the boutons is small, {{E94/runs_B3.csv:B_gain_k2_d0.02_M1:divisor_bouton_p50 ~ .2f}} to {{E94/runs_B3.csv:B_gain_k2_d0.15_P1:divisor_bouton_p50 ~ .2f}} at the median bouton and {{E94/runs_B3.csv:B_gain_k2_d0.02_M1:divisor_bouton_max ~ .1f}} to {{E94/runs_B3.csv:B_gain_k2_d0.15_P1:divisor_bouton_max ~ .1f}} at the most, which a shunt could do; the form that is easy to defend reads worse.
- And the family as fitted makes about seven tenths of APL's action on the claws' drive at the boutons, as an offset that hardly depends on the odor, where about a tenth of APL's calyx synapses are. That a synapse onto a bouton and one onto a claw inhibit alike is an assumption and not a measurement, and the model's share is of drive and not of synapses, so that this is reported beside the bands and is not one of them.

The verdict was not bought with the bands or bent by them: the two runs outside a band are of settings that read worse in any case. As everywhere, the pairs with paa, euc and -aPine rest on [ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations).

**What follows.** APL's side of the breadth-2 family is closed at both of its sites: at the KCs in the weighting ([above](#breadth-weighting)), in the place where the inhibition is summed ([above](#summed-drive)) and in its form ([above](#steps-like-for-like)), and at the boutons in strength and in form, on the fits as they are, in a refit near the connectome's share and at the model's 0.5 s pulse. The reference stays the family as fitted, and no base and no bound is changed. Two things are carried from here.

The first is a statement about the best family, with its price. Its match to the per-pair APL effect rests in part on an offset at the boutons that the anatomy does not suggest: about seven tenths of APL's action on the claws' drive, nearly the same for every odor, where about a tenth of APL's calyx synapses are. Holding the bouton path at the dose nearest the connectome's share costs {{E94/equal.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d0.1:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} of the pattern part at fixed scales and {{diff:E94/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E94/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}} after a refit, and half the fitted dose costs nothing that the recordings resolve.

A third price has since been read: with a part of the APL→KC weights that is the same on every claw, the refit at that dose costs {{diff:E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}}, with weights that the connectome does not have ([APL's inhibition as a static threshold raise per KC](#static-threshold)). A fourth has been read with weights that it has, the synapses that APL makes on the KCs outside their claws: the refit at that dose then costs {{diff:E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}}, and a part of the mean APL effect with it ([below](#offclaw-synapses)).

This is given beside the best models, at the head of this section. Whether a limit on the bouton share is to replace the bound on the APL→bouton scale, and at which of these prices, is a choice still to be made; the bound itself costs nothing at fixed scales, the family reading worse above it.

The second is a lead, and nothing rests on it. What the boutons' offset does for a KC is to raise its threshold, with APL on only, in proportion to its number of claws and alike for every odor, which removes many-clawed and weakly driven KCs evenly across the odors, and the breadth-weighted inhibition at the claws does not replace it.

The static forms of inhibition that have been tried ([the form of APL's inhibition in the flies' own responses](#inhibition-form); [the common error split into who responds and how strongly](#responder-sets)) did not include such a threshold, [the input-scaled KC threshold](#input-scaled-threshold) acted with APL on and with APL off alike, and the control that would have tested it here was written and not run, nothing having been chosen. A proposal that takes it up starts with that control.

The control has since been run, with the whole APL given in the same way, and the lead is read ([below](#static-threshold)): as a fixed inhibition of each KC that is present only with APL on, the bouton path reads as the family does, an equal with each KC's loss for each odor and a hair outside the margin with one amount per KC.

The two groups of the common error trade under the bouton path as under every other change on APL's side. More of the subtraction takes from the alcohol pairs' excess and adds to the ester pairs' shortfall, and the gain, which eases both a little, loses more in the shape of the effect than it gains; nothing on APL's side has moved the model off the weightings' line toward the flies without a cost in the pattern part.

With the input closed in its entries, in its spread between flies and in its coverage ([below](#missing-glomeruli)), what is left is not among APL's parameters. It is the mechanism between the claw and the soma that the lead asks for ([above](#responder-sets)), the side without APL, which turns on whether a KC's calcium signal saturates with its firing ([above](#steps-like-for-like)), and the recordings themselves; these are with the pending work at the end of the page. Every reading here is of the model's 0.5 s pulse without trial noise, in the family without a firing ceiling; the readings at the flies' pulse, through the trial noise and with the ceiling had been kept for a setting that passed, and were not made.

### The measured input for the glomeruli without ORN input: whether the responses that have been measured for ten of the glomeruli that the model's input leaves at zero lower the pattern part, and whether the PN dendrites bear out the list that the searches of the input left {#missing-glomeruli}

%%% hover
fuller input: The lab's input, the 36 glomeruli that both ORN panels hold, with ten more rows of measured responses: VA4 and VL1 from the megamat ORN recordings, VM4 and DL4 from the ORN recordings of the validation2 panel, and DA4l, DA3, DA4m, DL3, VA1d and VA1v (and DL4 for the megamat odors) from Hallem's receptor data, each odor's values scaled to the units of the ORN recordings. An input of this subsection only: every other model on this page has the lab's input, in which these rows are zero.
%%%

**The model's input leaves a third of the wiring's glomeruli at zero, and for ten of them responses to the panel's odors have been measured.** Put into the input, the measured rows do not lower the pattern part. With the fits at their own scales and both response rates set again, the fuller input reads a little higher than the lab's input on the four wirings of the earlier searches, on the four held-out wirings and on all eight, against all recordings and against every half of them, with no single wiring lower, and it stays inside the margin that had been set for an equal.

The same rows moved to other glomeruli cost as much, the rows with their values shuffled over the odors gain about what the measured rows cost, and no reduced version of the fuller input does better. Fitted again with the fuller input, the family gives back about a quarter of the cost and stays above the unchanged fits.

The rows do change which KCs respond, as the receptors predict: KCs with a claw on VA4 respond to 2h, IaA and pa, and KCs with a claw on DA4l or DA3 to 1-5ol and 1-6ol, about two to three times as often as with the lab's input. The per-pair APL effect does not follow, and the errors of the ester pairs and of the alcohol pairs both grow a little. Two readings were made beside the main one.

- At the entries on which the searches of the input agree, the PN dendrites do not depart from the ORNs in the searches' direction, and if anything in the other, so that the list which the searches left is what a search reaches for in this model and has no support in the antennal lobe as recorded.
- And with ten more glomeruli driven, the model's claws move toward the flies' for the pairs of an ester with an alcohol when all claws are read: the difference there, which the rule resolves with the lab's input, falls just short of the rule with the fuller input, so that whether it is that of the claws without input is not decided.

The coverage of the input is thereby closed as a carrier of the common error, after its fitted entries and its spread between flies. The fuller input is the easier of the two to defend in what it holds, measured responses where there were zeros; it costs about two thousandths of the pattern part, and whether it becomes the input of the base model is a choice still to be made.

Every model above takes as its input the 36 glomeruli that both of the lab's ORN panels hold, the lab's input, while the wiring has 54 ([the model's stages against the flies' stages](#model-stages)). The other 18 are filled with zeros: their PNs carry a spontaneous rate and the antennal lobe's lateral signal, and their claws, a sixth of all, nothing of the odor.

No search of the input could reach these rows, since every search multiplied recorded responses by factors and a zero stays zero ([the input side of the error common to all wirings](#input-side); [the input and APL's glomerulus profile fitted on several wirings at once](#cross-wiring-fit); [the controls and the replication of the reduced searched input](#reduced-input)), and the ORN flies as inputs had the same 36 glomeruli ([the ORN input as a population of flies](#input-population)).

In the fits as they are the zeros decide which KCs can respond. Over the eight wirings, the KCs with more than four tenths of their claws on glomeruli without input, {{E93/who_responds.csv:unit=pooled;input=I0;kind=zero_filled_share;cls=above 0.4:n_kcs ~ .0f}} of {{lit:13856 # the sum of column n_kcs over the four rows unit=pooled, input=I0, kind=zero_filled_share of results/E93_missing_glomeruli_input/who_responds.csv: the KCs of the eight wirings, 1732 each}}, have a response rate of {{E93/who_responds.csv:unit=pooled;input=I0;kind=zero_filled_share;cls=above 0.4:rate_on ~ .3f}} with APL on, where the KCs with no such claw have {{E93/who_responds.csv:unit=pooled;input=I0;kind=zero_filled_share;cls=none:rate_on ~ .3f}}. [The common error split into who responds and how strongly](#responder-sets) had pointed to which KCs respond, and the measured rows were the one part of the input that is known and that nothing had tried.

For ten of the 18 glomeruli, responses to the panel's odors exist. VA4 and VL1 are in the megamat ORN recordings, for 12 of the odors, and VM4 and DL4 in the ORN recordings of the validation2 panel, for paa, -aPine, euc and B-myr; these are in the units of the other rows. DA4l, DA3, DA4m, DL3, VA1d and VA1v, and DL4 for the megamat odors, are in [Hallem's receptor data](#hallem-input), recorded at 10^-2: each odor's values were brought to the concentrations and units of the lab's recordings by the slope of the lab's input on Hallem's over the 16 glomeruli that both hold, between {{E93/hallem_scaling.csv:odor=ms:slope ~ .2f}} for ms and {{E93/hallem_scaling.csv:odor=-aPine:slope ~ .2f}} for -aPine.

The fuller input is the lab's input with these ten rows, its 36 other rows unchanged, and it was fixed before any run. {{lit:26 # results/E93_missing_glomeruli_input/part_a1.json, n_measured: 134 of the 160 added entries (ten glomeruli by 16 odors) are measured, so that 26 are not}} of its 160 added entries were measured by nobody and stay at zero: VA4 and VL1 for the four odors of the validation2 panel, VM4 for the megamat odors and the six rows that come from Hallem's data alone for euc. The other eight glomeruli, which serve pheromones, carbon dioxide, amines, temperature and humidity, have no recording of the panel's odors and stay at zero as well.

The ten rows drive {{lit:841 # results/E93_missing_glomeruli_input/part_a1.json, claws_real.on_ten: the claws of the real wiring on the ten glomeruli that the fuller input adds, of 1679 on the 18 glomeruli without ORN input and 9867 in all}} more claws, half of those that were without input, and add up to {{E93/input_shares.csv:odor=2h:F ~ .1%}} of an odor's input summed over the claws, most for 2h, pa, 1-6ol and IaA. They are not equally well measured. VA4, which the lab's input lacks only because the validation2 panel does not hold it, has large responses to 2h, IaA and pa, and its profile over the 12 odors agrees between halves of the ORN flies at a correlation of {{E93/a1_reliability.csv:glomerulus=VA4;source=olfdb dataset 1 (megamat):half_r ~ .2f}} and with the profile of the PN dendrites at {{E93/a1_reliability.csv:glomerulus=VA4;source=ORNs (pebbled) against PN dendrites (GH146), fly means:r_orn_pn ~ .2f}}; VL1's small responses agree between halves at {{E93/a1_reliability.csv:glomerulus=VL1;source=olfdb dataset 1 (megamat):half_r ~ .2f}}.

The reading is that of the earlier changes of the input, with one difference. The family is the breadth-2 APL-effect fit on its eight wirings, each at its own fit ([the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population)); for each wiring and input the somatic threshold and the APL scale were set again until the numbers of responses with APL off and with APL on were the fit's, and a population is the mean over its wirings, read through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout). The lab's input with the ten rows written out as zeros reproduced every saved run without one differing spike count, so that naming more glomeruli in the input changes nothing by itself.

The difference is that the fuller input is measured and was not fitted to the KC recordings. All recordings and all eight wirings therefore test it, and the limit that the halves of the recordings set on a fitted input ([above](#reduced-input)) does not apply. What would count was fixed before any run, on the four held-out wirings.

- The fuller input passes if the pattern part of the APL-effect loss falls by 0.003 or more against all recordings and as the mean over four halves of the recordings, the halves of the two splits of the flies used before; if at least 12 of the 16 single wirings and halves are lower; if every run is inside the realism bands, the loss on raw counts no more than 0.005 higher and the mean APL effect within 0.01 of the flies'; if 15 % of the squared pattern error is removed against all recordings and half that against the six recordings that are alike; if two controls gain less than half as much; and if the pattern part is lower as well on the 66 pairs among the megamat odors, for which VA4 was recorded.
- It is an equal if it stays within 0.003 of the lab's input on the four held-out wirings and on the four wirings of the earlier searches, against all recordings and each half, with the same limits on raw counts, the mean effect and the bands.
- The controls are the fuller input with the ten rows moved to other glomeruli among the ten, none left in place, and with each added row's values shuffled over the odors; one draw of each was to be run unless the fuller input moved the held-out population by 0.0015 or more.
- Three reduced versions were read on the four wirings of the earlier searches: the four rows from the lab's own recordings alone, the fuller input with Hallem's values as recorded and not scaled, and VA4's row alone. One of them was to be preferred to the fuller input only by the rule for fitted changes, 0.0015 lower against one half of the recordings and then read on the held-out wirings against the other.
- On a pass or an equal the family was to be fitted again with the fuller input on the four wirings of the earlier searches, and on the four others only if that population came out 0.0015 or more below the unchanged fits.

![Left: the pattern part of the APL-effect loss through the calibrated readout and against all recordings (lower is better), for each of the eight wirings (real, P1, P2 and M1 are the four wirings of the earlier searches and S their mean; P3, P4, M2 and M3 are the four held-out wirings and T their mean; all8 is the mean over the eight): with the lab's input (I0, black), with the fuller input at the fits' scales (F), with the two controls on the held-out wirings (PL1, the ten rows moved to other glomeruli; PO1, each row's values shuffled over the odors) and with the three reduced versions on the wirings of the earlier searches (L, the four rows from the lab's own recordings; U, Hallem's values not scaled; V, VA4's row alone). Right: the per-pair APL effect of the KC data (black), of the mean over the eight wirings with the lab's input (grey) and with the fuller input (red), the 120 odor pairs in the order of the KC data's effect.](results/E93_missing_glomeruli_input/E93_readings.png)

Except in the third model column the fits are at their own scales, with both response rates set again. The squares of the amplitude part and the shape part add up to the squared pattern part, and a spread below one means that APL moves the model's pairs apart more evenly than the flies'; no input is chosen by a correlation ([why](#fn-pattern-split)).
