**At the fits' scales the fuller input is an equal, and a little worse everywhere.** On the four held-out wirings the pattern part is {{E93/readings.csv:input=F;unit=T;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} with the fuller input for {{E93/readings.csv:input=I0;unit=T;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} with the lab's input, on the four wirings of the earlier searches {{E93/readings.csv:input=F;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} for {{E93/readings.csv:input=I0;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, and on all eight {{E93/readings.csv:input=F;unit=all8;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} for {{E93/readings.csv:input=I0;unit=all8;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, where the floor is {{data:apl_effect_pattern_floor ~ .4f}} (first row of the table, and the left panel of the figure). It is lower on {{E93/gate.csv:input=F:n_wirings_lower ~ .0f}} of the eight single wirings, and in {{E93/gate.csv:input=F:n_cells_lower ~ .0f}} of the 16 combinations of a held-out wiring with a half of the recordings, where the test asked for 12.

Where the test asked for a gain of 0.003 on the held-out wirings, the gain is {{E93/gate.csv:input=F:gain_all ~ +.4f}} against all recordings and {{E93/gate.csv:input=F:gain_halves_mean ~ +.4f}} as the mean over the four halves, a loss in both. On the 66 pairs among the megamat odors it is {{E93/gate.csv:input=F:gain_all_66 ~ +.4f}}, so that the cost does not come from the entries that nobody measured, and of the squared pattern error nothing is removed (a reduction of {{E93/gate.csv:input=F:sq_reduction_all ~ +.0%}}, where 15 % was asked). The fuller input is worse as well against the six recordings that are alike, under the per-KC reading and on raw counts (the table).

What holds is the part of the test that guards against a cost elsewhere: every run is inside the realism bands, the loss on raw counts is {{E93/gate.csv:input=F:raw_loss_change ~ .4f}} higher on the held-out wirings, where 0.005 was allowed, and the mean APL effect is {{E93/gate.csv:input=F:mean_effect_cal ~ +.3f}} for the flies' {{data:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}}. By the rule for an equal the fuller input is one: on both sets of wirings its pattern part is within {{E93/equal.csv:input=F:max_abs_d_pattern ~ .4f}} of the lab's input against all recordings and against each of the four halves, where 0.003 was allowed. It is better in none of these readings.

The cost is in the shape part, which rises from {{E93/spread.csv:input=I0;unit=S;readout=cal;pairs=all;target=z8:shape ~ .4f}} to {{E93/spread.csv:input=F;unit=S;readout=cal;pairs=all;target=z8:shape ~ .4f}} on the wirings of the earlier searches and from {{E93/spread.csv:input=I0;unit=T;readout=cal;pairs=all;target=z8:shape ~ .4f}} to {{E93/spread.csv:input=F;unit=T;readout=cal;pairs=all;target=z8:shape ~ .4f}} on the held-out ones (second row). The amplitude part does not rise with it: the spread of the model's effect stays at {{E93/spread.csv:input=F;unit=S;readout=cal;pairs=all;target=z8:sd_ratio ~ .2f}} of the flies' on the first set and comes from {{E93/spread.csv:input=I0;unit=T;readout=cal;pairs=all;target=z8:sd_ratio ~ .2f}} to {{E93/spread.csv:input=F;unit=T;readout=cal;pairs=all;target=z8:sd_ratio ~ .2f}} on the second, and Pearson r on the per-pair APL effect falls a little on both.

**Rows of this size move the pattern part by about two thousandths either way, and no reduced version does better.** With the ten rows moved to other glomeruli the held-out wirings read {{E93/readings.csv:input=PL1;unit=T;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, as they do with the rows in place; with each row's values shuffled over the odors they read {{E93/readings.csv:input=PO1;unit=T;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, {{diff:E93/readings.csv:input=I0;unit=T;readout=cal:z8_pattern -- E93/readings.csv:input=PO1;unit=T;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} below the lab's input (last two columns of the table). One draw of each control was run, as had been fixed for a change of the held-out population below 0.0015, and the two draws differ by {{diff:E93/readings.csv:input=PL1;unit=T;readout=cal:z8_pattern -- E93/readings.csv:input=PO1;unit=T;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}.

The control that keeps each row's profile over the odors and moves it to another glomerulus thus costs what the measured rows cost, and the control that breaks the profiles gains about as much; on one draw of each this is a lead and not a result. What the controls do establish is the scale: ten added rows of this size scatter the pattern part by about two thousandths, the fuller input lies at the upper end of that scatter, and the test's condition on the controls cannot be met by an input that gains nothing.

Of the reduced versions, on the four wirings of the earlier searches the four rows from the lab's own recordings read {{E93/readings.csv:input=L;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, the fuller input with Hallem's values not scaled {{E93/readings.csv:input=U;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} and VA4's row alone {{E93/readings.csv:input=V;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, for {{E93/readings.csv:input=F;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} with the fuller input and {{E93/readings.csv:input=I0;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} with the lab's. Against three of the four halves of the recordings VA4's row alone is the lowest of these, by {{E93/bounds.csv:half=A:gain_over_F ~ .4f}} to {{E93/bounds.csv:half=D:gain_over_F ~ .4f}} below the fuller input, where 0.0015 was needed, and none was read on the held-out wirings. Two things follow from them.

- The unscaled values read as the scaled ones do, so that the result does not rest on how Hallem's data were brought to the lab's units.
- And VA4's row alone, the best measured of the ten, costs nearly what the ten cost together.

**Fitted again with the fuller input, the family stays above the unchanged fits.** The four fits on the wirings of the earlier searches were each started from the wiring's own fit with the threshold and the APL scale set again for the fuller input, and ran for up to 150 evaluations. As a population they read {{E93/e_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all ~ .4f}}, where the unchanged fits have {{E93/e_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_I0 ~ .4f}} and the fuller input at the fits' scales {{E93/readings.csv:input=F;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} (third model column of the table): the refit gives back about a quarter of the cost, and {{E93/e_scores.csv:unit=S:n_lower ~ .0f}} of the four wirings is lower than with the lab's input.

What comes back is in the spread of the effect and not in its shape. The amplitude part falls from {{E93/spread.csv:input=F;unit=S;readout=cal;pairs=all;target=z8:amplitude ~ .4f}} to {{E93/e_readings.csv:fit=refit;unit=S;readout=cal;pairs=all:amplitude ~ .4f}}, and the shape part from {{E93/spread.csv:input=F;unit=S;readout=cal;pairs=all;target=z8:shape ~ .4f}} to {{E93/e_readings.csv:fit=refit;unit=S;readout=cal;pairs=all:shape ~ .4f}}, for {{E93/spread.csv:input=I0;unit=S;readout=cal;pairs=all;target=z8:shape ~ .4f}} in the unchanged fits. The loss on raw counts is below that of the unchanged fits, {{E93/e_scores.csv:unit=S:raw_loss ~ .4f}} for {{E93/e_scores.csv:unit=S:raw_loss_I0 ~ .4f}}, through a larger mean effect on raw counts ({{E93/e_readings.csv:fit=refit;unit=S;readout=raw;pairs=all:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} for {{E93/readings.csv:input=I0;unit=S;readout=raw:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}) and with a higher pattern part there ({{E93/e_readings.csv:fit=refit;unit=S;readout=raw;pairs=all:pattern ~ .4f}} for {{E93/readings.csv:input=I0;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}), so that it is not a gain in the pattern.

One of the four fits decides the direction of the population. On one claw permutation the fit left the region that the family's fits occupy, its somatic threshold going from {{E93/runs_B.csv:B_F_P2:fixed_thr ~ .0f}} to {{E93/e_scores.csv:unit=P2:fixed_thr ~ .0f}}, its KC–KC inhibition from {{E93/runs_B.csv:B_F_P2:wKCKC_scale ~ .0f}} to {{E93/e_scores.csv:unit=P2:kc_kc_inh ~ .0f}} and its APL→KC scale from {{E93/runs_B.csv:B_F_P2:wAPLKC_scale ~ .2f}} to {{E93/e_scores.csv:unit=P2:wAPLKC_scale ~ .2f}}, and its pattern part is {{E93/e_scores.csv:unit=P2:pattern_all ~ .4f}} where the same wiring's unchanged fit has {{E93/e_scores.csv:unit=P2:pattern_all_I0 ~ .4f}}. The other three end within {{diff:E93/e_scores.csv:unit=real:pattern_all -- E93/e_scores.csv:unit=real:pattern_all_I0 ~ .4f}} of their unchanged fits, one of them lower. With 150 evaluations a refit is a local search, and a second start was not run, the stopping point having been fixed: fits on the four held-out wirings had been made conditional on a population 0.0015 or more below the unchanged fits, and were not run.

**The rows change which KCs respond, and the per-pair APL effect does not follow.** With the fuller input, over the eight wirings and with APL on, the KCs with a claw on VA4 have response rates of {{E93/who_responds_runs.csv:unit=pooled;input=F;kind=VA4_claw;cls=True:rate_2h_on ~ .3f}}, {{E93/who_responds_runs.csv:unit=pooled;input=F;kind=VA4_claw;cls=True:rate_IaA_on ~ .3f}} and {{E93/who_responds_runs.csv:unit=pooled;input=F;kind=VA4_claw;cls=True:rate_pa_on ~ .3f}} to 2h, IaA and pa, where with the lab's input they had {{E93/who_responds_runs.csv:unit=pooled;input=I0;kind=VA4_claw;cls=True:rate_2h_on ~ .3f}}, {{E93/who_responds_runs.csv:unit=pooled;input=I0;kind=VA4_claw;cls=True:rate_IaA_on ~ .3f}} and {{E93/who_responds_runs.csv:unit=pooled;input=I0;kind=VA4_claw;cls=True:rate_pa_on ~ .3f}} and where the other KCs now have {{E93/who_responds_runs.csv:unit=pooled;input=F;kind=VA4_claw;cls=False:rate_2h_on ~ .3f}}, {{E93/who_responds_runs.csv:unit=pooled;input=F;kind=VA4_claw;cls=False:rate_IaA_on ~ .3f}} and {{E93/who_responds_runs.csv:unit=pooled;input=F;kind=VA4_claw;cls=False:rate_pa_on ~ .3f}}. The KCs with a claw on DA4l or DA3 have {{E93/who_responds_runs.csv:unit=pooled;input=F;kind=DA4l_or_DA3_claw;cls=True:rate_1-5ol_on ~ .3f}} and {{E93/who_responds_runs.csv:unit=pooled;input=F;kind=DA4l_or_DA3_claw;cls=True:rate_1-6ol_on ~ .3f}} to 1-5ol and 1-6ol, for {{E93/who_responds_runs.csv:unit=pooled;input=I0;kind=DA4l_or_DA3_claw;cls=True:rate_1-5ol_on ~ .3f}} and {{E93/who_responds_runs.csv:unit=pooled;input=I0;kind=DA4l_or_DA3_claw;cls=True:rate_1-6ol_on ~ .3f}}. These are the odors that the receptors of those glomeruli respond to most.

Of the KCs with more than four tenths of their claws on the ten glomeruli, {{E93/who_responds_runs.csv:unit=pooled;input=I0;kind=ten_share;cls=above 0.4:silent_share_on ~ .0%}} responded to no odor with APL on and {{E93/who_responds_runs.csv:unit=pooled;input=F;kind=ten_share;cls=above 0.4:silent_share_on ~ .0%}} do now. The KCs with more than four tenths of their claws on any of the 18 glomeruli stay nearly silent, at a response rate of {{E93/who_responds_runs.csv:unit=pooled;input=F;kind=zero_filled_share;cls=above 0.4:rate_on ~ .3f}} for {{E93/who_responds_runs.csv:unit=pooled;input=I0;kind=zero_filled_share;cls=above 0.4:rate_on ~ .3f}} with APL on, since eight glomeruli keep no input. How many KCs respond to each of these five odors hardly changes, by {{lit:0.01 # E93_missing_glomeruli_input.md, Realism: the response fractions of 2h, IaA, pa, 1-5ol and 1-6ol with APL on (columns frac_2h_on to frac_1-6ol_on of results/E93_missing_glomeruli_input/runs_B.csv) stay within 0.01 of those of the unchanged fits on every wiring}} of the KCs at most on any wiring, both response rates being held: the rows change which KCs respond and not how many.

The main target does not gain from it. At the input the rows make the odors a little more alike, most of all within the two groups of pairs that carry the common error: the distance between two odors' inputs over the claws, as a mean over the pairs, falls from {{E93/input_distances.csv:input=I0;weighting=claw-weighted:ester ~ .3f}} to {{E93/input_distances.csv:input=F;weighting=claw-weighted:ester ~ .3f}} among the ester pairs and from {{E93/input_distances.csv:input=I0;weighting=claw-weighted:alcohol ~ .3f}} to {{E93/input_distances.csv:input=F;weighting=claw-weighted:alcohol ~ .3f}} among the alcohol pairs.

In the model the errors of both groups then grow, over the eight wirings from {{E93/readings.csv:input=I0;unit=all8;readout=cal:z8_err_ester ~ +.3f}} to {{E93/readings.csv:input=F;unit=all8;readout=cal:z8_err_ester ~ +.3f}} for the ester pairs, whose APL effect is too small, and from {{E93/readings.csv:input=I0;unit=all8;readout=cal:z8_err_alcohol ~ +.3f}} to {{E93/readings.csv:input=F;unit=all8;readout=cal:z8_err_alcohol ~ +.3f}} for the alcohol pairs, whose effect is too large (last row but one of the table, for the two sets of wirings). The control with the rows' values shuffled over the odors does not do this (last column of the same row), and it is in these two groups that it differs from the measured rows: input that the odors of a group share is added to pairs whose APL effect the model already misplaces. With one draw of the control this is a description.

One pair had been named beforehand, 1-5ol with 1-6ol, the two odors that DA4l and DA3 respond to most. Its APL effect moves away from the flies', from {{E93/readings.csv:input=I0;unit=all8;readout=cal:effect_15ol_16ol ~ +.3f}} to {{E93/readings.csv:input=F;unit=all8;readout=cal:effect_15ol_16ol ~ +.3f}} over the eight wirings for the flies' {{lit:0.1134560353229199 # results/E93_missing_glomeruli_input/verdict.json, pair_15ol_16ol.data: the KC data's APL effect of 1-5ol with 1-6ol, all recordings ~ +.3f}}; a single pair is a lead and no more.

Two statistics that are given beside the main target for a change of the responses without APL do not gain either. The target without APL ([the form of APL's inhibition in the flies' own responses](#inhibition-form)) changes by less than 0.0015 in every population, {{E93/apl_free.csv:input=F;unit=all8;readout=raw;reading=noise_free:pattern ~ .4f}} for {{E93/apl_free.csv:input=I0;unit=all8;readout=raw;reading=noise_free:pattern ~ .4f}} on raw counts over the eight wirings. The alcohol pairs' co-response change under APL, as trial means at the reading's own noise, moves away from the flies': {{E93/coresponse.csv:input=F;unit=S;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} for {{E93/coresponse.csv:input=I0;unit=S;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} on the four wirings of the earlier searches and {{E93/coresponse.csv:input=F;unit=T;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} for {{E93/coresponse.csv:input=I0;unit=T;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} on the held-out ones, against the flies' {{E93/coresponse.csv:input=I0;unit=S;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:flies_ratio ~ .2f}} ({{E93/coresponse.csv:input=I0;unit=S;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:flies_lo ~ .2f}} to {{E93/coresponse.csv:input=I0;unit=S;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:flies_hi ~ .2f}}).

**The PN dendrites do not bear out the list that the searches of the input left.** The six inputs that the search has given on the real wiring agree on few single entries, and those were named as a list that a measurement could test ([above](#reduced-input)). The recordings of the PN dendrites ([the model's stages against the flies' stages](#model-stages)) allow a first reading of it without a new measurement: whether, at the listed entries, what the antennal lobe makes of the ORNs' responses goes the way the searches changed them.

Of the {{lit:73 # results/E86_reduced_input_candidate/part_e.json, rule.n_meets: the entries with meets in partE_entries.csv, the rows of partE_five_of_six.csv}} entries that at least five of the six runs change alike, {{lit:60 # results/E93_missing_glomeruli_input/dendrite_reading.json, subsets.glom.meets.n: the entries with meets of E86's partE_entries.csv that lie in the 28 glomeruli which the PN-dendrite table, the ORN table beside it and the model's input share}} lie in the 28 glomeruli that the recordings of the PN dendrites, the ORN recordings beside them and the model's input share, among them all {{lit:eleven # results/E93_missing_glomeruli_input/dendrite_reading.json, subsets.glom.meets_read.n: 11, the entries with meets_read}} that recur at the size the input is read at. At each entry the departure of the dendrites from the ORNs is the logarithm of the dendrites' response over the ORNs', each side's responses first taken relative to its others in one of three ways: within the glomerulus over the 12 odors, within the odor over the glomeruli, and with the model's own PN stage in place of the ORNs.

The departures were set against the mean factor of the six searches at the same entries, by the share of entries at which the two have the same sign and by their rank correlation, with the departures permuted within each odor as the level of chance. The rule had been fixed: the dendrites go in the list's direction if that share is above the 95th percentile of chance in at least two of the three ways, opposite if it is below the 5th percentile in at least two, and neither otherwise.

The share is {{lit:0.43333333333333335 # results/E93_missing_glomeruli_input/dendrite_reading.json, subsets.glom.meets.agree: the share of the 60 entries at which the dendrites' departure from the ORNs, normalized within a glomerulus, has the sign of the searches' mean factor ~ .2f}} within a glomerulus, where chance gives {{lit:0.43333333333333335 # results/E93_missing_glomeruli_input/dendrite_reading.json, subsets.glom.meets.null_p5: the 5th percentile of the share over 2000 permutations of the departures within each odor ~ .2f}} to {{lit:0.6333333333333333 # results/E93_missing_glomeruli_input/dendrite_reading.json, subsets.glom.meets.null_p95: the 95th percentile of the share over 2000 permutations of the departures within each odor ~ .2f}}; {{lit:0.36666666666666664 # results/E93_missing_glomeruli_input/dendrite_reading.json, subsets.odor.meets.agree: the share of the 60 entries at which the dendrites' departure from the ORNs, normalized within an odor, has the sign of the searches' mean factor ~ .2f}} within an odor, where chance gives {{lit:0.4166666666666667 # results/E93_missing_glomeruli_input/dendrite_reading.json, subsets.odor.meets.null_p5 ~ .2f}} to {{lit:0.6166666666666667 # results/E93_missing_glomeruli_input/dendrite_reading.json, subsets.odor.meets.null_p95 ~ .2f}}; and {{lit:0.45 # results/E93_missing_glomeruli_input/dendrite_reading.json, subsets.model_pn.meets.agree: the share of the 60 entries at which the dendrites' departure from the model's own PN stage has the sign of the searches' mean factor ~ .2f}} against the model's PN stage, where chance gives {{lit:0.4 # results/E93_missing_glomeruli_input/dendrite_reading.json, subsets.model_pn.meets.null_p5 ~ .2f}} to {{lit:0.6 # results/E93_missing_glomeruli_input/dendrite_reading.json, subsets.model_pn.meets.null_p95 ~ .2f}}. It is below a half in all three ways, below the 5th percentile of chance in one and at it in a second. By the rule the reading is neither, and it leans to opposite: the rank correlation between the departures and the searches' factors is negative in all three ways, {{lit:-0.298638510697416 # results/E93_missing_glomeruli_input/dendrite_reading.json, subsets.glom.meets.rho: the rank correlation over the 60 entries between the dendrites' departure, normalized within a glomerulus, and the searches' mean factor ~ .2f}}, {{lit:-0.26201722700750213 # results/E93_missing_glomeruli_input/dendrite_reading.json, subsets.odor.meets.rho ~ .2f}} and {{lit:-0.16733355588805737 # results/E93_missing_glomeruli_input/dendrite_reading.json, subsets.model_pn.meets.rho ~ .2f}}.

For the eleven entries alone the shares are {{lit:0.36363636363636365 # results/E93_missing_glomeruli_input/dendrite_reading.json, subsets.glom.meets_read.agree ~ .2f}}, {{lit:0.6363636363636364 # results/E93_missing_glomeruli_input/dendrite_reading.json, subsets.odor.meets_read.agree ~ .2f}} and {{lit:0.5454545454545454 # results/E93_missing_glomeruli_input/dendrite_reading.json, subsets.model_pn.meets_read.agree ~ .2f}}, none of them outside chance for so few. The departures themselves are measured moderately well, two halves of the dendrite flies agreeing on them at correlations of {{lit:0.38213887376510786 # results/E93_missing_glomeruli_input/dendrite_reading.json, subsets.glom.halves_r: the correlation of the departures, normalized within a glomerulus, between halves of the flies, mean over 200 splits ~ .2f}} to {{lit:0.5963972179005359 # results/E93_missing_glomeruli_input/dendrite_reading.json, subsets.odor.halves_r: the correlation of the departures, normalized within an odor, between halves of the flies, mean over 200 splits ~ .2f}}. An input that carries the dendrites' departures had been kept for the case that they went in the list's direction, and was not run.

The list is therefore what a search for these pairs reaches for in this model. It is not what the antennal lobe, as the dendrites record it, makes of the ORNs' responses.

**With ten more glomeruli driven, the claws' difference for the pairs of an ester with an alcohol narrows to the margin of the rule and is no longer resolved.**

The eight wirings were run again with the fuller input and every stage saved, each run reproducing its spike counts, and the claws were read against the flies' by the same rule and, as there, from their settled level before the odor ([the model's stages against the flies' stages](#model-stages); [footnote](#fn-preodor-startup)): the model's claws and APL start from rest half a second before the odor, so that a level taken over that whole half second reads the claws high and APL low. No spike count and no number of the main target depends on it.

With all claws read, the model's claws are more alike than the flies' for the pairs of an ester with an alcohol in every version of the claw reading, by {{diff:E93/d_verdict_rows_settled.csv:element=claw;group=ester_alcohol;model_reading=noisy_nr;subset=all;share=0.5:flies -- E93/d_verdict_rows_settled.csv:element=claw;group=ester_alcohol;model_reading=noisy_nr;subset=all;share=0.5:model ~ .2f}} to {{diff:E93/d_verdict_rows_settled.csv:element=claw;group=ester_alcohol;model_reading=rate;subset=all;share=0.0:flies -- E93/d_verdict_rows_settled.csv:element=claw;group=ester_alcohol;model_reading=rate;subset=all;share=0.0:model ~ .2f}}, where the lab's input read the same way gives {{diff:E93/d_verdict_rows_lab_input_settled.csv:element=claw;group=ester_alcohol;model_reading=rate;subset=all;share=0.5:flies -- E93/d_verdict_rows_lab_input_settled.csv:element=claw;group=ester_alcohol;model_reading=rate;subset=all;share=0.5:model ~ .2f}} to {{diff:E93/d_verdict_rows_lab_input_settled.csv:element=claw;group=ester_alcohol;model_reading=session_z;subset=all;share=0.0:flies -- E93/d_verdict_rows_lab_input_settled.csv:element=claw;group=ester_alcohol;model_reading=session_z;subset=all;share=0.0:model ~ .2f}}. By the rule {{lit:seven # results/E93_missing_glomeruli_input/d_verdict_settled.json, readings.all.ester_alcohol.elements.claw: n_differ 7 of n_readings 9}} of the nine versions differ with the fuller input, where all {{lit:nine # results/E93_missing_glomeruli_input/d_verdict.json, readings.all.ester_alcohol.elements.claw: n_differ 9 of n_readings 9}} had with the level taken over the whole half second, and all {{lit:nine # results/E93_missing_glomeruli_input/d_verdict_lab_input_settled.json, readings.all.ester_alcohol.elements.claw: n_differ 9 of n_readings 9}} with the lab's input; in the other two the model's value is {{E93/d_verdict_rows_settled.csv:element=claw;group=ester_alcohol;model_reading=session_z;subset=all;share=0.5:model ~ .3f}}, where the flies' interval begins at {{E93/d_verdict_rows_settled.csv:element=claw;group=ester_alcohol;model_reading=session_z;subset=all;share=0.5:lo ~ .3f}}. These pairs are thus not resolved with the fuller input and upstream with the lab's input, in this experiment's own scoring and in the stage comparison's own verdict at the same level.

On the claws of the 46 glomeruli that now have input, and on those of the 36, {{lit:three # results/E93_missing_glomeruli_input/d_verdict_settled.json, readings.input46.ester_alcohol.elements.claw: n_differ 3 of n_readings 9}} and {{lit:six # results/E93_missing_glomeruli_input/d_verdict_settled.json, readings.input36.ester_alcohol.elements.claw: n_differ 6 of n_readings 9}} of the nine versions differ and the group is not resolved, as on the claws of the 36 with the lab's input. The ester pairs, the alcohol pairs and the other pairs are not resolved in any of the three readings, and the six pairs with near-identical ORN input are upstream in all three, as before. Whether the difference for the pairs of an ester with an alcohol is made by the claws without input is therefore not decided: it still depends on which claws are read, and {{lit:838 # results/E93_missing_glomeruli_input/part_a1.json, claws_real: zero_filled (1679) minus on_ten (841), the claws of the real wiring on the eight glomeruli that stay without input}} claws of eight glomeruli remain without input.

**Realism.** No parameter was added, and in the main reading nothing was fitted to the KC recordings: an input was exchanged, and both response rates were held at every run. All {{lit:32 # the 28 rows of results/E93_missing_glomeruli_input/runs_B.csv and the four refits of e_scores.csv; none has a realism_flag or a realism_flag_zcrit}} runs and refits are inside the four realism bands, with the flies' responses counted in baseline-noise units, as the bands count now, and by the recordings' own criterion, as they counted until 2026-11-10.

The response rate with APL on is {{E93/e_scores.csv:unit=P2:rate_on ~ .3f}} to {{E93/runs_B.csv:B_F_P3:rate_on ~ .3f}} and the response rate with APL off {{E93/runs_B.csv:B_F_P4:ratio ~ .2f}} to {{E93/runs_B.csv:B_F_P2:ratio ~ .2f}} times that, for the flies' {{data:noise_ctrl_frac ~ .3f}} and {{data:noise_rate_ratio_fraction ~ .2f}} (90 % interval {{data:noise_rate_ratio_fraction.lo ~ .2f}} to {{data:noise_rate_ratio_fraction.hi ~ .2f}}); the distribution of the number of odors per KC is at most {{E93/e_scores.csv:unit=P2:opk_on_tv ~ .3f}} from the flies' with APL on (band {{data:noise_ctrl_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .3f}}) and {{E93/e_scores.csv:unit=P2:opk_off_tv ~ .3f}} with APL off (band {{data:noise_tnt_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .3f}}).

The band that an input can move is the response rate ρ with APL on, and the fuller input lowers it on every wiring at the fits' scales. It is {{E93/runs_B.csv:B_F_P1:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}} to {{E93/runs_B.csv:B_F_M1:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}} over the eight wirings, where the unchanged fits have {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;tag=wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed1_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}} to {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;tag=wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed4_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}}, lower by {{diff:apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;tag=wiring-curveball_within_type_matched-seed1_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3:rate_rho_on -- E93/runs_B.csv:B_F_M1:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}} to {{diff:apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;tag=wiring-curveball_within_type_matched-seed2_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3:rate_rho_on -- E93/runs_B.csv:B_F_M2:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}} on a wiring; the lowest of any run is {{E93/runs_B.csv:B_U_P1:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}}, with Hallem's values not scaled on one claw permutation, where the band asks 0.37 or more. The refits bring it back to {{E93/e_scores.csv:unit=P1:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}} to {{E93/e_scores.csv:unit=M1:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}}. At scales fitted for 36 rows the measured rows thus put the per-odor response rates a little further from the flies', and a refit recovers that where it does not recover the pattern part.

The somatic threshold set again for the fuller input is {{E93/runs_B.csv:B_F_P1:thr_factor ~ .2f}} to {{E93/runs_B.csv:B_F_P2:thr_factor ~ .2f}} times the fitted one, and the APL scale {{E93/runs_B.csv:B_F_real:apl_factor ~ .2f}} to {{E93/runs_B.csv:B_F_P1:apl_factor ~ .2f}} times. What the bands do not see is the family's own: the largest spike count of a KC to one odor is {{E93/runs_B.csv:B_F_P1:max_count_on ~ .0f}} with APL on and {{E93/runs_B.csv:B_F_P4:max_count_off ~ .0f}} with APL off with the fuller input, in a family that nothing bounds there ([the firing ceiling for the KCs](#firing-ceiling)). The refit that left the family's region is inside the bands and has the lowest such counts of all, {{E93/e_scores.csv:unit=P2:max_count_on ~ .0f}} and {{E93/e_scores.csv:unit=P2:max_count_off ~ .0f}}, at a somatic threshold well above those of the family's other fits.

The fuller input is the more realistic of the two in what it holds, with three cautions. Hallem's rows are recordings from single sensilla at 10^-2, brought to the concentrations and units of the lab's recordings by one slope for each odor over 16 glomeruli, at correlations of {{E93/hallem_scaling.csv:odor=-aPine:r ~ .2f}} to {{E93/hallem_scaling.csv:odor=pa:r ~ .2f}}; the unscaled values read the same. {{lit:26 # results/E93_missing_glomeruli_input/part_a1.json, n_measured: 134 of the 160 added entries (ten glomeruli by 16 odors) are measured, so that 26 are not}} of the 160 added entries are zeros that nobody measured, and eight glomeruli keep no input at all. And as everywhere, the pairs with paa, euc and -aPine rest on [ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations). The verdict was not bought with the bands or bent by them: no run was left out of a comparison, and what the fuller input costs is in the pattern part and, at the fits' scales, in the response rate ρ with APL on.

**What follows.** The coverage of the input does not limit the family. With the fitted inputs ([the input side of the error common to all wirings](#input-side); [the input and APL's glomerulus profile fitted on several wirings at once](#cross-wiring-fit); [the controls and the replication of the reduced searched input](#reduced-input)) and the ORN flies as inputs ([the ORN input as a population of flies](#input-population)), the ORN side of the common error is now closed in its entries, in its spread between flies and in its coverage. The glomeruli without input leave the list of leads, and no measurement is asked for them: the responses of VA4 to the four odors of the validation2 panel, and of the six glomeruli of Hallem's data at the lab's concentrations, had been kept for a pass.

The lab's input stays the input of the models on this page, and every number above stands. Whether the fuller input replaces it in the base model is a choice still to be made, and it is one of realism against a small cost. For it, measured responses stand where there were zeros, and KCs with claws on VA4, DA4l or DA3 respond to the odors of their receptors. Against it stand about two thousandths of the pattern part, at the fits' scales and after a refit, which is inside the margin of an equal, and by which every later comparison would shift. If the fuller input is taken, the family is fitted again with it on the four held-out wirings as well, so that the reference population is the fuller input's.

The list that the searches of the input left is no longer a request for a measurement, and the open measurement question at the end of the page keeps, of the searches' entries, only those where a search and Hallem's data point opposite ways. The reading of the claws for the pairs of an ester with an alcohol is on the margin of the rule: with all claws read it is a difference with the lab's input and, narrowly, not resolved with the fuller input, on the claws with input the rule resolves none, and what would decide it is still the stage recordings asked of the experimenter.

One lead is noted, and nothing rests on it. The control with the rows' values shuffled over the odors gained about what the measured rows cost, and both run through how alike the inputs of the ester odors and of the alcohol odors are; this rests on one draw, and a proposal that would use it first repeats the draw and reads it against halves of the recordings.

Every reading here is of the model's 0.5 s pulse, without trial noise and in the family without a firing ceiling; the readings at the flies' pulse, through the trial noise and with the ceiling had been kept for a pass, and were not made. The lead stays where the earlier subsections left it, with a mechanism between the claw and the soma that changes which KCs respond to both odors of a pair without APL ([the common error split into who responds and how strongly](#responder-sets)): the measured rows changed which KCs respond to single odors, and neither the main target nor the alcohol pairs' co-response followed.

### APL's inhibition as a static threshold raise per KC: whether a fixed inhibition of each KC, present only with APL on, reads as the best family's APL does, at the PN boutons and for the whole APL, and whether the boutons' offset can be made at the KCs with the bouton path near the connectome's share {#static-threshold}

%%% hover
unweighted component: A part added to the APL→KC weight of every claw, the same for every claw and not multiplied by the family's breadth weighting. Its size is given in units of what the bouton path took per claw in a wiring's own fit, the wiring's mean loss of drive per claw at the boutons, so that a size of 1 restores on average what the bouton path took. A setting of the subsection on APL's inhibition as a static threshold raise per KC only: the connectome's own APL→KC weights are not the same for every claw, and for three tenths of the real wiring's claws the tables hold no APL synapse.
%%%

**For a KC, the best family's APL is close to a fixed raise of the KC's threshold while APL is on.** What its APL takes from a KC's drive is nearly the same for every odor, at the PN boutons almost wholly and at the claws for the most part; at the boutons it goes with the KC's number of claws, and at the claws with the breadth weighting.

Replaced by a fixed inhibition of each KC that is present only with APL on, the bouton path reads as it did: with each KC's own loss for each odor it is an equal of the family, and with one amount per KC it misses the margin of an equal by a hair, against one half of the recordings. The whole APL replaced in the same way reads three to five thousandths of the pattern part higher through the calibrated readout and, with one amount per KC, no higher on raw counts. The feedback, an inhibition that follows what each odor drives, thus adds little to the family's match, and adds it only through the readout.

The number of claws alone can stand in for the bouton path, at a cost of about four thousandths, and cannot stand in for the whole APL. Against no half of the recordings is a setting other than the unchanged fits the best, so that nothing was read on held-out wirings.

The offset that the boutons make can be made at the KCs instead. With the bouton path held at a tenth of its fitted strength, a part of the APL→KC weights that is the same on every claw brings back the mean APL effect that the family loses without it, and the family fitted again in that way reads about three thousandths above the unchanged fits, where the refit without that part had read about nine above them. That is just outside the margin of an equal, and such weights are not the connectome's, whose own weights per claw, put in the same place, lose the mean effect.

Nothing is gained on the main target, and no base, bound or reference is changed. What is added is a description of the family and a third price. The family's match to the per-pair APL effect rests on a threshold difference per KC between the two conditions, where in the flies' own responses the inhibition grows with an odor's response over all KCs; and about two thirds of what the connectome's bouton share cost after a refit belongs to how the family's APL weights the KCs, and not to the site.

[The PN boutons' share of APL's inhibition](#bouton-share) had left a lead and a price. The lead was that the boutons' offset does for a KC what a higher threshold would do, with APL on only and in proportion to the KC's number of claws. None of the static forms of inhibition tried before had been of that make ([the form of APL's inhibition in the flies' own responses](#inhibition-form); [the common error split into who responds and how strongly](#responder-sets)), and the control written for it had not been run.

The price was that of holding the bouton path near the connectome's share. Whether it belongs to the site, the boutons themselves being needed, or to the family's weighting of the KCs, which loads the broad KCs and leaves most KCs nearly untouched at the claws, was not known.

APL's inhibition as a static threshold raise per KC was run on the breadth-2 family, each wiring at its own fit ([the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population)) and with the lab's input throughout, in four parts and a refit. The first simulated nothing. From the saved stages of the eight fits it took, for every KC and odor, the drive that APL removes at the boutons and at the claws, and split each into an amount per KC, an amount per odor and a rest.

The second replaced the bouton path by a static inhibition, on the four wirings of the earlier searches. The APL→bouton scale was set to zero, the feedback inhibition at the claws was kept with the family's weights, and each KC was given a fixed amount that is subtracted from its input while the odor is on, with APL on, and nothing with APL off. The amount was the KC's own mean loss at the boutons in its fit; that loss for each odor; a multiple of the KC's number of claws, or of a power of that number between 0 and 2; and, as controls, the KCs' own mean losses permuted among the KCs with the same number of claws and over all KCs.

The third replaced the whole APL. Every APL scale was set to zero and each KC was given the sum of its losses at the boutons and at the claws: as one amount per KC, for each odor, by the number of claws alone, with the bouton part by the number of claws and the claw part the KC's own, and permuted over all KCs as a control; the claw path alone was also made static, with the bouton path left as it is.

The fourth kept the feedback APL and made the boutons' offset at the KCs. The bouton path was held at a tenth of its fitted strength, the setting nearest the connectome's share ([above](#bouton-share)), and the unweighted component, a part that is the same for every claw, was added to the APL→KC weights at sizes of 0.5, 1 and 2, a size of 1 restoring on average what the bouton path took from a claw. In the component's place the connectome's own APL→KC weights per claw, not multiplied by the breadth weighting, were added at the same sizes, and the component was run once with no bouton path at all.

In every run one factor was set again until the number of responses with APL on was the fit's, the tied APL scale or, where no APL was left, the size of the static inhibition; the somatic threshold and the KC–KC scale stayed the fit's and the responses with APL off are the fit's own, so that both response rates are held.

Before any run was scored the new code was checked. On all eight wirings a static inhibition of zero reproduces the saved run with APL on, and every APL scale at zero the saved run with APL off, without one differing spike count, and on the real wiring the fourth part without the component reproduces the earlier run at a tenth of the fitted dose.

What would count had been fixed as it was for the bouton path. The setting with the lowest pattern part against one half of the recordings, for the mean over the four wirings through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout), was to be read on the four held-out wirings against the other half, by the test that the fitted changes were put to ([above](#cross-wiring-fit)), if it was lower than the unchanged fits by 0.0015 or more; the halves were those of two splits of the flies.

A setting was an equal of the family if its pattern part stayed within 0.003 of the family's against all recordings and against both halves of the first split, with its loss on raw counts no more than 0.005 higher, its mean APL effect within 0.01 of the family's and its runs inside the realism bands. And if the best setting of the component came within 0.008 of the unchanged fits, the family was to be fitted again on the four wirings of the earlier searches, with the bouton path held at a tenth, the size of the component free beside the family's other parameters, and each wiring starting from its own best run with the component. Refits on the four held-out wirings had been kept for an equal.

**In the fits, what APL takes from a KC is close to one amount per KC.** Of the variance, over KCs and odors, of the drive that APL removes at the boutons, {{E95/a1_split.csv:wiring=P3;site=boutons;kcs=all:share_kc ~ .3f}} to {{E95/a1_split.csv:wiring=M3;site=boutons;kcs=all:share_kc ~ .3f}} on the eight wirings is an amount per KC that is the same for every odor, and {{E95/a1_split.csv:wiring=P4;site=boutons;kcs=all:share_odor ~ .3f}} to {{E95/a1_split.csv:wiring=M2;site=boutons;kcs=all:share_odor ~ .3f}} an amount per odor that is the same for every KC; of what it removes at the claws, the amount per KC holds {{E95/a1_split.csv:wiring=P3;site=claws;kcs=all:share_kc ~ .3f}} to {{E95/a1_split.csv:wiring=P1;site=claws;kcs=all:share_kc ~ .3f}}.

The bouton part is in proportion to the KC's number of claws, with a slope of {{E95/a2_per_kc.csv:wiring=P2:loglog_slope ~ .2f}} to {{E95/a2_per_kc.csv:wiring=real:loglog_slope ~ .2f}} on logarithmic axes, and what the number of claws leaves follows the APL→bouton weights of the boutons that the KC samples, at a correlation of {{E95/a2_per_kc.csv:wiring=P3:pearson_resid_bouton_apl ~ .2f}} to {{E95/a2_per_kc.csv:wiring=M3:pearson_resid_bouton_apl ~ .2f}}. The claw part follows the family's breadth weighting, at a rank correlation of {{E95/a2_per_kc.csv:wiring=P1:spearman_c_factor ~ .2f}} to {{E95/a2_per_kc.csv:wiring=real:spearman_c_factor ~ .2f}} with the KC's breadth factor; it is near zero for most KCs and large for the broad ones. Set against the KC's own threshold as the simulator sets it, the fitted somatic threshold plus twice the KC's spontaneous input, the bouton part is {{E95/a3_sizes.csv:wiring=M2;quantity=b:over_thr_p50 ~ .2f}} to {{E95/a3_sizes.csv:wiring=P3;quantity=b:over_thr_p50 ~ .2f}} of the threshold at the median KC, and both parts together {{E95/a3_sizes.csv:wiring=M2;quantity=b+c:over_thr_p50 ~ .2f}} to {{E95/a3_sizes.csv:wiring=P3;quantity=b+c:over_thr_p50 ~ .2f}}.

APL's own activity varies over the 16 odors by {{E95/a4_apl.csv:wiring=P2;source=fit:apl_win_cv ~ .1%}} to {{E95/a4_apl.csv:wiring=real;source=fit:apl_win_cv ~ .1%}} of its mean, and {{E95/a4_apl.csv:wiring=P3;source=fit:apl_pre_over_win ~ .0%}} to {{E95/a4_apl.csv:wiring=real;source=fit:apl_pre_over_win ~ .0%}} of its mean during the odor is there before the odor arrives (that mean before the odor includes the start of the simulation and reads low; against the level that APL holds during a blank the share is {{E98/a4_profile_carrying.csv:wiring=P3:a0_share ~ .0%}} to {{E98/a4_profile_carrying.csv:wiring=real:a0_share ~ .0%}}: [the strength of APL's response in the flies against the model's APL](#apl-strength)). For a KC the family's APL is therefore close to a threshold that is higher while APL is on, and the runs ask whether that is all that the main target needs of it.
