**The bouton path is a static inhibition per KC.** Against all recordings the unchanged fits read a pattern part of {{E95/readings.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, for a floor of {{data:apl_effect_pattern_floor ~ .4f}} (the figure, and the table). With the bouton path replaced by each KC's own loss for each odor, the population reads {{E95/equal.csv:variant=B5_bko:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} higher against all recordings and {{E95/equal.csv:variant=B5_bko:d_pattern_halfA ~ .4f}} and {{E95/equal.csv:variant=B5_bko:d_pattern_halfB ~ .4f}} higher against the two halves, inside the 0.003 allowed; its loss on raw counts is {{E95/equal.csv:variant=B5_bko:d_raw_loss ~ .4f}} higher, where 0.005 was allowed, its mean APL effect is {{E95/readings.csv:variant=B5_bko;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} for the fits' {{E95/readings.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}, and its four runs are inside the bands. It is the one equal.

With one amount per KC, the KC's mean loss over the odors, the pattern part is {{E95/equal.csv:variant=B1_bk:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} higher against all recordings and {{E95/equal.csv:variant=B1_bk:d_pattern_halfA ~ .4f}} higher against one of the halves, a hair outside the margin; what the odor adds to the bouton path is at the edge of what the recordings resolve. The number of claws alone does a little less well, at {{E95/equal.csv:variant=B2_nk:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} above the fits, and of the powers of that number the proportional one is the best, the others reading {{E95/equal.csv:variant=B3_nk0.5:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} to {{E95/equal.csv:variant=B3_nk2:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} above the fits.

The two controls say what a rule by the number of claws lacks. With the KCs' own amounts permuted among the KCs with the same number of claws, one draw on each wiring, the pattern part is as low as with each KC's own, {{E95/readings.csv:variant=B4_bk_permclaw1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} for {{E95/readings.csv:variant=B1_bk;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, while the mean APL effect falls to {{E95/readings.csv:variant=B4_bk_permclaw1;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} and the loss on raw counts rises to {{E95/readings.csv:variant=B4_bk_permclaw1;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_loss ~ .4f}} from {{E95/readings.csv:variant=B1_bk;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_loss ~ .4f}}; permuted over all KCs the pattern part is {{E95/readings.csv:variant=B4_bk_permall1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}. For the pattern of the effect it therefore does not matter which boutons a KC samples, beyond how many claws it has; what a rule by the number of claws lacks is that KCs with the same number of claws are not all raised by the same amount.

The static forms of the bouton path leave the alcohol pairs' excess a little larger, {{E95/readings.csv:variant=B5_bko;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_alcohol ~ +.3f}} for the equal where the fits have {{E95/readings.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_alcohol ~ +.3f}}. Against each of the four halves of the recordings the lowest pattern part is the unchanged fits' own, among the {{E95/choice.csv:half=A:n_eligible ~ .0f}} settings that could be chosen in this part and the two that follow, the unchanged fits among them, so that nothing went to the four held-out wirings.

**The whole APL is close to a static inhibition per KC, and what the feedback adds shows only through the readout.** With every APL scale at zero and each KC given one amount, the sum of its mean losses at the boutons and at the claws, the pattern part through the calibrated readout is {{E95/equal.csv:variant=C1_bck:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} above the fits. On raw counts nothing is lost: the loss is {{E95/readings.csv:variant=C1_bck;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_loss ~ .4f}} for the fits' {{E95/readings.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_loss ~ .4f}}, and the pattern part {{E95/readings.csv:variant=C1_bck;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} for {{E95/readings.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}.

With each KC's loss for each odor the pattern part is {{E95/equal.csv:variant=C2_bcko:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} above the fits through the readout, and {{E95/equal.csv:variant=C2_bcko:d_pattern_halfA ~ .4f}} and {{E95/equal.csv:variant=C2_bcko:d_pattern_halfB ~ .4f}} against the two halves; its loss on raw counts is {{E95/equal.csv:variant=C2_bcko:d_raw_loss ~ .4f}} higher, the mean effect on raw counts being smaller, so that it is not an equal, by a hair on the pattern part and by more on raw counts. The cost of the static forms sits in the shape part ({{E95/readings.csv:variant=C1_bck;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_shape ~ .4f}} and {{E95/readings.csv:variant=C2_bcko;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_shape ~ .4f}} for the fits' {{E95/readings.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_shape ~ .4f}}), the spread of the effect staying the family's.

With the claw path alone made static and the bouton path left as it is, the pattern part is {{E95/equal.csv:variant=C6_ck:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} above the fits, about what the whole APL costs. What the feedback adds to a fixed threshold difference per KC between the two conditions, an inhibition that follows what each odor drives, is therefore three to five thousandths of the pattern part through the readout, and for the pattern nothing that raw counts show.

The number of claws alone fails here. With the whole APL given by it the pattern part is {{E95/readings.csv:variant=C3_nk;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, the ρ on the per-pair APL effect {{E95/readings.csv:variant=C3_nk;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_rho ~ .2f}} and the mean APL effect {{E95/readings.csv:variant=C3_nk;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}, and with only the bouton part given by it and the claw part each KC's own the pattern part is still {{E95/equal.csv:variant=C4_nkck:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} above the fits: the number of claws carries the bouton part and cannot replace the breadth weighting at the claws. The control with the KCs' amounts permuted over all KCs loses the mean effect ({{E95/readings.csv:variant=C5_bck_permall1;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}) and is outside the realism bands on all four wirings.

The static inhibitions that had been simulated in place of APL before were set by an odor's strength and a KC's breadth. Read on the same four wirings, they are at {{E95/a5_archive.csv:source=E87_D;form=sub_q1_p0.25_summed;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} to {{E95/a5_archive.csv:source=E87_D;form=sub_q0_p0;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} on the fits as they are ([the form of APL's inhibition in the flies' own responses](#inhibition-form)) and at {{E95/a5_archive.csv:source=E88_D1;form=sub_q1_p0;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} to {{E95/a5_archive.csv:source=E88_D1;form=sub_q0_p0;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} on the base with the flies' recruitment ([the common error split into who responds and how strongly](#responder-sets)). That no static inhibition does better in the model than its feedback APL still holds, and it is narrowed: a static inhibition made of the family's own loss per KC comes within three to five thousandths of it.

**At the KCs, a part of the weights that is the same on every claw brings the mean effect back, and the connectome's own weights per claw do not.** With the bouton path at a tenth of its fitted strength and nothing in its place, the mean APL effect is {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D0;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} and the loss on raw counts {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D0;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_loss ~ .4f}} ([above](#bouton-share)). With the unweighted component the mean effect is {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D1_uniform_d0.5;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} to {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D1_uniform_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} over the three sizes, the flies' being {{data:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}}, and the loss on raw counts {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D1_uniform_d2;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_loss ~ .4f}} to {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D1_uniform_d0.5;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_loss ~ .4f}}, for the unchanged fits' {{E95/readings.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_loss ~ .4f}}.

The pattern part is {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D1_uniform_d0.5;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} to {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D1_uniform_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, for {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D0;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} without the component and the fits' {{E95/readings.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}; the best of the three is {{E95/equal.csv:variant=D1_uniform_d0.5:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} above the fits against all recordings and {{E95/equal.csv:variant=D1_uniform_d0.5:d_pattern_halfB ~ .4f}} against one half, so that none is an equal. In these runs the bouton share is {{E95/runs_D.csv:D1_uniform_d0.5_P2:bouton_share ~ .3f}} to {{E95/runs_D.csv:D1_uniform_d0.5_real:bouton_share ~ .3f}} at the smallest size and {{E95/runs_D.csv:D1_uniform_d2_M1:bouton_share ~ .3f}} to {{E95/runs_D.csv:D1_uniform_d2_real:bouton_share ~ .3f}} at the largest, at and below the fraction of {{E94/a2_connectome.csv:set=calyx, all:share_pn ~ .3f}} to {{E94/a2_connectome.csv:set=calyx, assigned, KCs with a type:share_pn ~ .3f}} of APL's calyx synapses that the connectome puts on PN boutons. Without any bouton path the component at a size of 1 reads {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D3_uniform_d1_dose0;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}: the offset does not have to be made before the claws.

The connectome's own APL→KC weights per claw, added in the component's place, read alike on the pattern part, {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D2_connectome_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} to {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D2_connectome_d0.5;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, and lose what the component restores. Their mean APL effect is {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D2_connectome_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} to {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D2_connectome_d0.5;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}, the spread of the effect {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D2_connectome_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_sd_ratio ~ .2f}} to {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D2_connectome_d0.5;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_sd_ratio ~ .2f}} of the flies', and the loss on raw counts {{E95/equal.csv:variant=D2_connectome_d0.5:d_raw_loss ~ .4f}} to {{E95/equal.csv:variant=D2_connectome_d2:d_raw_loss ~ .4f}} higher than the fits'.

Those weights are far from the same on every claw: for {{E95/a4_weights.csv:wiring=real:zero_share ~ .0%}} of the real wiring's claws the tables hold no APL synapse, and over the claws the weights vary with a standard deviation as large as their mean ({{E95/a4_weights.csv:wiring=real:cv_claws ~ .2f}} times it). Most of that unevenness is not what loses the mean, as has since been read ([below](#weight-evenness)): about three quarters of the variance lies within KCs, in how a KC's synapses are divided over its own claws, and through the calibrated readout it carries little of the loss, most of which goes with the unequal amounts per KC.

**Fitted again with the component and the bouton path at a tenth, the family misses an equal narrowly, and gets back two thirds of what the refit without the component had lost.** The condition for the refit held, the best setting of the component being {{E95/equal.csv:variant=D1_uniform_d0.5:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} above the fits where 0.008 was allowed, and each wiring started from its own best run, which was the largest size on all four.

The population reads a pattern part of {{E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all ~ .4f}}, for the unchanged fits' {{E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}} and for the {{E94/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all ~ .4f}} of the refit with the bouton path held at the same strength and no component ([above](#bouton-share); the last two rows of the table). That is {{diff:E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}} above the fits against all recordings, and {{diff:E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:halfA -- E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:halfA_unchanged ~ .4f}} and {{diff:E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:halfB -- E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:halfB_unchanged ~ .4f}} against the two halves, where an equal had to stay within 0.003 against all three. The loss on raw counts is lower than the fits', {{E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:raw_loss ~ .4f}} for {{E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:raw_loss_unchanged ~ .4f}}, the mean APL effect is the fits' ({{E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}), and all four fits are inside the bands.

Where the refit without the component had put the spread of the effect at the flies' and lost in its shape ({{E94/d_scores.csv:unit=S:shape ~ .4f}}), this one keeps the family's spread ({{E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:sd_ratio ~ .2f}} for {{E95/readings.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_sd_ratio ~ .2f}}) and has a shape part of {{E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:shape ~ .4f}}, for the fits' {{E95/readings.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_shape ~ .4f}}. By wiring the refit is lower than the unchanged fit on one claw permutation, level on the other and higher on the real wiring and on the matched shuffle, the four moving by {{diff:E95/f_scores.csv:unit=P2:pattern_all -- E95/f_scores.csv:unit=P2:pattern_all_unchanged ~ +.4f}} to {{diff:E95/f_scores.csv:unit=M1:pattern_all -- E95/f_scores.csv:unit=M1:pattern_all_unchanged ~ +.4f}}; on raw counts it is lower on all four.

The fitted size of the component is {{E95/f_scores.csv:unit=P1:aplkc_flat_size ~ .2f}} to {{E95/f_scores.csv:unit=P2:aplkc_flat_size ~ .2f}}, so that every claw's APL→KC weight carries, beside its breadth-weighted part, about twice what the bouton path took from a claw, on the claws without an APL synapse as on the others. The search moved little from its start, which read {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D1_uniform_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} at fixed scales.

Of the {{diff:E94/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E94/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}} that the bouton path near the connectome's share cost after a refit, {{diff:E94/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all ~ .4f}} is thus got back when APL's weights at the KCs reach every claw alike, as the boutons' offset did, and {{diff:E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}} remains. What remains is at the margin's line, inside it against one half of the recordings and outside it against the other, so that the rule and not a clear difference decides that the refit is not an equal. The refits on the four held-out wirings had been kept for an equal and were not run, and a refit with the connectome's own weights per claw had been kept for an equal of those weights at fixed scales.

**Realism.** No mechanism was added to the base. An inhibition that the fits already make was given back as a fixed amount per KC, or a part was added to the APL→KC weights, and both response rates were held, the one with APL on by one factor in every run and the one with APL off by the fit's own run. The {{lit:88 # the 36 rows of results/E95_static_apl/runs_B.csv, the 24 of runs_C.csv and the 28 of runs_D.csv}} runs have response rates of {{E95/runs_B.csv:B1_bk_real:rate_on ~ .3f}} to {{E95/runs_C.csv:C4_nkck_P1:rate_on ~ .3f}} with APL on and {{E95/runs_B.csv:B1_bk_M1:rate_off ~ .3f}} to {{E95/runs_B.csv:B1_bk_P2:rate_off ~ .3f}} with APL off (ratios of {{E95/runs_D.csv:D2_connectome_d2_M1:ratio ~ .2f}} to {{E95/runs_B.csv:B1_bk_P2:ratio ~ .2f}}), and the four refits {{E95/f_scores.csv:unit=real:rate_on ~ .3f}} to {{E95/f_scores.csv:unit=P2:rate_on ~ .3f}} and {{E95/f_scores.csv:unit=real:rate_off ~ .3f}} to {{E95/f_scores.csv:unit=P2:rate_off ~ .3f}} ({{E95/f_scores.csv:unit=real:ratio ~ .2f}} to {{E95/f_scores.csv:unit=P2:ratio ~ .2f}}), for the flies' {{data:noise_ctrl_frac ~ .3f}} and {{data:noise_tnt_frac ~ .3f}} ({{data:noise_rate_ratio_fraction ~ .2f}}).

{{lit:Four # the rows with a realism_flag in results/E95_static_apl/runs_C.csv (C5_bck_permall1_real, C5_bck_permall1_P1, C5_bck_permall1_P2 and C5_bck_permall1_M1); none in runs_B.csv, runs_D.csv or f_scores.csv; the same four in results/E95_static_apl/verdict.json, flagged_runs}} runs are outside a band, and they are one control on the four wirings. With the whole APL's static amounts permuted over all KCs, the distribution of the number of odors per KC with APL on is {{E95/runs_C.csv:C5_bck_permall1_P1:opk_on_tv ~ .3f}} to {{E95/runs_C.csv:C5_bck_permall1_M1:opk_on_tv ~ .3f}} from the flies' (band {{data:noise_ctrl_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .3f}}), {{E95/runs_C.csv:C5_bck_permall1_M1:static_over_max_drive ~ .0%}} to {{E95/runs_C.csv:C5_bck_permall1_P1:static_over_max_drive ~ .0%}} of the KCs being given more inhibition than their largest drive. It is neither a chosen setting nor an equal. Every other run and the four refits are inside the four bands, with a response rate ρ with APL on of {{E95/runs_B.csv:B4_bk_permall1_real:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}} or more and a distribution of the number of odors per KC that is at most {{E95/runs_C.csv:C3_nk_M1:opk_on_tv ~ .3f}} from the flies' with APL on and {{E95/f_scores.csv:unit=real:opk_off_tv ~ .3f}} with APL off (band {{data:noise_tnt_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .3f}}).

Counted by the recordings' own criterion, as the bands counted until 2026-11-10, {{lit:six # the rows of results/E95_static_apl/runs_C.csv (C3_nk_real, C3_nk_P1, C3_nk_P2 and C3_nk_M1) and runs_D.csv (D2_connectome_d2_real and D2_connectome_d2_P2) with a realism_flag_zcrit and no realism_flag}} more runs would be outside the band on odors per KC with APL on: the whole APL by the number of claws alone on all four wirings, and the connectome's own weights per claw at the largest size on two. The largest spike count of a KC to one odor with APL on is {{E95/runs_B.csv:B3_nk0_P2:max_count_on ~ .0f}} to {{E95/runs_D.csv:D2_connectome_d2_P1:max_count_on ~ .0f}} over the runs, in a family that nothing bounds there ([the firing ceiling for the KCs](#firing-ceiling)).

Three things bear on what can be defended. As a static inhibition the whole APL asks more than a KC's own threshold of the KCs that it inhibits most: with one amount per KC, {{E95/runs_C.csv:C1_bck_P2:static_over_thr_max ~ .1f}} to {{E95/runs_C.csv:C1_bck_P1:static_over_thr_max ~ .1f}} times the threshold at the most and {{E95/runs_C.csv:C1_bck_M1:static_over_thr_p50 ~ .2f}} to {{E95/runs_C.csv:C1_bck_P1:static_over_thr_p50 ~ .2f}} at the median KC, where the bouton path's static form stays at {{E95/runs_B.csv:B1_bk_P1:static_over_thr_max ~ .2f}} of the threshold or less.

The unweighted component is not in the connectome. It puts APL→KC weight on every claw alike, on the claws without an APL synapse as on the others, and the connectome's own weights per claw, which could be defended, lose the mean effect.

And the equal is further from the flies at the step from claws to somata. Read like for like with the saturating map ([above](#steps-like-for-like)), with the claws taken from their settled level before the odor ([footnote](#fn-preodor-startup)), its step with APL on over the 66 pairs of the stage recordings is {{preodor_startup_check_viki/E95_static_apl_steps_settled.csv:family=B5_bko;cond=on;reading=saturating_z_none_pearson;group=all66:model_settled ~ .2f}}, where the family's is {{preodor_startup_check_viki/E95_static_apl_steps_settled.csv:family=C2;cond=on;reading=saturating_z_none_pearson;group=all66:model_settled ~ .2f}} and the flies' {{E95/steps.csv:family=C2;cond=on;reading=saturating_z_none_pearson;group=all66:flies ~ .2f}}: the static form inhibits the KC and not its boutons, and its claws read more alike ({{preodor_startup_check_viki/E95_static_apl_steps_settled.csv:family=B5_bko;cond=on;reading=saturating_z_none_pearson;group=all66:claw_model_settled ~ .2f}} for {{preodor_startup_check_viki/E95_static_apl_steps_settled.csv:family=C2;cond=on;reading=saturating_z_none_pearson;group=all66:claw_model_settled ~ .2f}}). This is a description of the one equal, and no other setting was read there.

The verdict was not bought with the bands or bent by them: the only runs outside a band are a control's. As everywhere, the pairs with paa, euc and -aPine rest on [ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations).

**What follows.** Nothing is gained on the main target. The reference stays the family as fitted, no base and no bound is changed, and the static forms and the component are readings and not candidates.

Three things are carried from here. The first is a description of the family. For the main target its APL is close to a table of thresholds: a fixed raise per KC that is present only with APL on, set at the boutons by the KC's number of claws and at the claws by the breadth weighting. What the feedback adds to that is three to five thousandths of the pattern part through the calibrated readout, and on raw counts nothing for the pattern.

The flies' inhibition is not of that kind. In their own responses it grows with an odor's response over all KCs, and with its strengths permuted over the odors the gain is gone ([the form of APL's inhibition in the flies' own responses](#inhibition-form)). A change on APL's side that is to move the main target would therefore have to change which KCs' thresholds rise with APL on, or make the inhibition depend on the odor as the family's does not; none is proposed here. That the feedback's part shows only through the readout also bears on the choice, still to be made, of the reading that carries the model's side of the main target (the pending work at the end of the page).

The second is a third price for the connectome's bouton share, beside the two already given ([above](#bouton-share)). Holding the bouton path at a tenth of its fitted strength costs {{E94/equal.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d0.1:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} of the pattern part at fixed scales and {{diff:E94/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E94/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}} after a refit with the family's weights, and {{diff:E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}} after a refit in which a part of the APL→KC weights reaches every claw alike. The connectome's weights do not do that, and its own weights per claw, at fixed scales, lose the mean effect. Whether a limit on the bouton share replaces the bound on the APL→bouton scale, and at which of these prices, is still a choice to be made, and nothing here makes it.

The third narrows an earlier statement. That no static inhibition does better in the model than its feedback APL holds, and one made of the family's own loss per KC comes within a few thousandths of it, as the earlier ones, set by an odor's strength and a KC's breadth, did not ([above](#inhibition-form); [above](#responder-sets)).

Two readings are left for planning, and neither has been run: the family fitted with a static inhibition per KC and no feedback, which would say whether the feedback is needed at all for the main target, and APL→KC weights that reach every claw from the anatomy and not uniformly, which would say whether the three thousandths that remain at the connectome's bouton share are got back with weights that the connectome has (the pending work at the end of the page). The second has since been run ([below](#offclaw-synapses)): with the synapses that APL makes on the KCs outside their claws as such weights, the refit reads {{diff:E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}} above the fits, so that the three thousandths are not got back, and a part of the mean APL effect is lost besides.

The two groups of the common error are where they were. Against the weightings' line ([above](#steps-like-for-like)) every setting but the permuted control of the whole APL stays at the family's place or a little further from the flies, between {{E95/line.csv:variant=C4_nkck;unit=S;readout=cal:resid ~ +.3f}} and {{E95/line.csv:variant=B5_bko;unit=S;readout=cal:resid ~ +.3f}} for the family's {{E95/line.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=cal:resid ~ +.3f}} and the flies' {{lit:0.09866993033793536 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, lines.cal.S.flies.trial_mean_all.resid ~ +.3f}}. The alcohol pairs' co-response change under APL stays below the flies' interval ({{E95/coresponse.csv:variant=ref;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:flies_lo ~ .2f}} to {{E95/coresponse.csv:variant=ref;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:flies_hi ~ .2f}}) in every setting that holds the mean APL effect, the family's being {{E95/coresponse.csv:variant=ref;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}}; it enters the interval only for the whole APL by the number of claws alone and for the connectome's own weights per claw at the two larger sizes, which lose the mean effect.

The limits of these readings are those of runs at fixed scales. The second, third and fourth parts set one factor again on four wirings and left every other parameter at the fit's, and only the refit moved the others, by one search from one start on each wiring. The static amounts are the fits' own losses, so that they say what the fitted APL does and are not a mechanism with a source of its own, and a family fitted without feedback was not run.

The margin of an equal is a line, and three settings lie within a few ten-thousandths of it on one side or the other: the bouton path with one amount per KC, the whole APL with each KC's loss for each odor, and the refit. Every reading here is of the model's 0.5 s pulse without trial noise, in the family without a firing ceiling; the readings with the ceiling, at the flies' pulse and through the trial noise had been kept for a setting that passed, and a reading at the flies' pulse of the whole APL's static form for an equal of it, and none was made.

### APL's synapses on the KCs outside the claws: whether the synapses that APL makes on a KC off its claws, which the model's weights leave out, can make the boutons' offset at the KCs with the bouton path near the connectome's share, at fixed scales and in a refit {#offclaw-synapses}

%%% hover
off-claw component: A part added to the APL→KC weights that is made of the synapses that APL makes on each KC outside the KC's claws, which the model's weights leave out. A KC's count of such synapses is divided evenly over the KC's claws and is not multiplied by the family's breadth weighting. Over all claws the part has a mean of 1, and its size is given in the unit of the unweighted component, so that a size of 1 takes on average what the bouton path took from a claw. With the calyx alone, the count is of APL's synapses in the calyx that lie on none of the KC's claws; with the peduncle's, APL's synapses onto the KC in the peduncle are added. A setting of the subsection on APL's synapses on the KCs outside the claws only.
%%%

**The model's APL→KC weights count the synapses that APL makes on the claws that the wiring keeps, and no others.** About two fifths of APL's synapses onto the model's KCs in the calyx lie elsewhere, most of them on the dendrite outside the claws, and nearly as many again lie in the peduncle.

The synapses outside the claws reach nearly every KC and grow with a KC's number of claws, though less than in proportion. Given to the model as a part of the APL→KC weights, with the bouton path held at a tenth of its fitted strength, they read on the pattern part as the part that is the same on every claw had read, at fixed scales and after a refit, and they do not hold the mean APL effect as that part did. Fitted again with them, the family reads about four thousandths above the unchanged fits: one above the refit with the uniform part and five below the refit with nothing in the boutons' place, with a mean APL effect about a hundredth short of the fits' and of the flies'.

The counts read no better than the same counts permuted among the KCs, and what loses the mean effect is not isolated by any run. No setting is an equal, and against no half of the recordings is a setting lower than the unchanged fits by an amount that could be confirmed, so that nothing was read on held-out wirings.

Nothing is gained on the main target, and no base, bound or reference is changed. What is added is a fourth price for the connectome's bouton share, the first with weights that the connectome has: about four thousandths of the pattern part, and a part of the mean effect with it.

[APL's inhibition as a static threshold raise per KC](#static-threshold) had left a third price for the connectome's bouton share and a reading for planning. With the bouton path held at a tenth of its fitted strength, the unweighted component had brought the refit to about three thousandths above the unchanged fits. But it puts APL→KC weight on every claw alike, as the connectome does not, and the connectome's own weights per claw, put in the same place, had lost the mean APL effect.

Those weights are not all of APL's synapses onto a KC, however. The model reads a synapse into its weights only if it lies on a claw that the wiring keeps, and whether the boutons' offset had been standing in for the synapses that are left out was not known.

APL's synapses on the KCs outside the claws was run on the breadth-2 family, each wiring at its own fit ([the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population)) and with the lab's input throughout, in three parts. The first simulated nothing. In the connectome table that the model's weights are read from, and with the same filters, it split APL's synapses onto each of the model's KCs into those on a claw that the wiring keeps, those on a claw that it drops, those in the calyx on no claw and those in the peduncle, and set the counts against the KC's number of claws and against what the bouton path takes from the KC in its fit; in tables derived from four connectomes in separate work it also read how many of APL's calyx synapses onto KCs lie away from the KC's claws, a reading that is withheld here, the use of those tables being on hold ([footnote](#fn-derived-tables)).

The second ran at fixed scales on the four wirings of the earlier searches. The bouton path was held at a tenth of its fitted strength, the setting nearest the connectome's share ([above](#bouton-share)), and the off-claw component was added to the APL→KC weights where the unweighted component had been ([above](#static-threshold)), with the calyx alone and with the peduncle's, each at sizes of 0.5, 1 and 2. Beside them the component with the peduncle's was run in the summed form ([APL's inhibition on the KC's summed drive](#summed-drive)) at the three sizes, with the summed form without a component as the reference of those runs; at a size of 1 with its counts permuted among the KCs with the same number of claws and over all KCs, as controls; and at a size of 1 with no bouton path at all.

All of APL's counted synapses were also given without the breadth weighting, each kept claw with its own count and the KC's synapses outside the claws spread over its claws, in the proportion in which they are counted, at the three sizes. In every run the tied APL scale was set again until the number of responses with APL on was the fit's; the somatic threshold and the KC–KC scale stayed the fit's and the responses with APL off are the fit's own, so that both response rates are held.

Before any run was scored the new code was checked. On the real wiring it reproduces three earlier runs without one differing spike count: with a component of size zero, the run at a tenth of the fitted dose; with the component made uniform, the run with the unweighted component; and with the summed form and no component, the earlier run of that form. On all eight wirings its counts on the kept claws are the model's weights, claw by claw.

What would count had been fixed as it was for the unweighted component ([above](#static-threshold)). A setting was to be read on the four held-out wirings, against the other half of the recordings, if its pattern part through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout) was the lowest against one half and lower than the unchanged fits' by 0.0015 or more, with the unweighted component at the same size as its control. A setting was an equal of the family if its pattern part stayed within 0.003 of the family's against all recordings and against both halves of the first split of the flies, with its loss on raw counts no more than 0.005 higher, its mean APL effect within 0.01 of the family's and its runs inside the realism bands.

And if the best setting of the off-claw component came within 0.008 of the unchanged fits, the family was to be fitted again on the four wirings of the earlier searches, with the bouton path held at a tenth and the size of the component free beside the family's other parameters: with the calyx alone unless the component with the peduncle's had read lower by more than 0.0005, and from two starts on each wiring, the wiring's own best run with the component and its refit with the unweighted component, the one component exchanged for the other at the same size.

Of a wiring's two fits the one that ended at the lower value of the fit's own loss was to be kept, and the refit was to count as reading as well as the one with the unweighted component if it came within 0.0015 of it. Refits on the four held-out wirings had been kept for an equal.

**Two fifths of APL's calyx synapses onto the model's KCs are not in the model's weights, and nearly every KC has some of them.** Of the {{E96/a2_distances.csv:kind=all;to=any_claw:n ~ ,.0f}} synapses that APL makes on the model's KCs in the calyx, the weights hold {{E96/a1_counts.csv:kind=kept:synapses ~ ,.0f}}, or {{E96/a1_counts.csv:kind=kept:share_of_calyx ~ .1%}}; {{E96/a1_counts.csv:kind=no_claw:synapses ~ ,.0f}} lie on no claw and {{E96/a1_counts.csv:kind=dropped_claw:synapses ~ ,.0f}} on claws that the wiring drops, and {{E96/a1_counts.csv:kind=peduncle:synapses ~ ,.0f}} more lie in the peduncle.

The synapses on no claw are not strays at a claw's edge. They lie a median of {{E96/a2_distances.csv:kind=no_claw;to=any_claw:d_p50 ~ .1f}} µm from the KC's nearest PN→KC synapse on a claw, where those on the kept claws lie {{E96/a2_distances.csv:kind=kept;to=any_claw:d_p50 ~ .1f}} µm from it. They are spread over nearly all KCs: {{E96/a1_counts.csv:kind=no_claw:kcs_none_share ~ .1%}} of the KCs have none in the calyx and {{E96/a1_counts.csv:kind=no_claw+peduncle:kcs_none_share ~ .1%}} none in the calyx or the peduncle, so that as a part of the weights they leave {{E96/a1_per_claw.csv:quantity=comp_offclaw:zero_share ~ .1%}} of the claws without any with the calyx alone and {{E96/a1_per_claw.csv:quantity=comp_offclaw_ped:zero_share ~ .1%}} with the peduncle's, where the connectome's own weights per claw leave {{E95/a4_weights.csv:wiring=real:zero_share ~ .0%}}. And they grow with a KC's number of claws, less than in proportion.

KCs with 1 to 4, with 5 to 8 and with 9 or more claws have a mean of {{E96/a1_by_type_class.csv:by=claw_class;group=1-4:no_claw_mean ~ .1f}}, {{E96/a1_by_type_class.csv:by=claw_class;group=5-8:no_claw_mean ~ .1f}} and {{E96/a1_by_type_class.csv:by=claw_class;group=9+:no_claw_mean ~ .1f}} of them in the calyx, and of {{E96/a1_by_type_class.csv:by=claw_class;group=1-4:no_claw+peduncle_mean ~ .1f}}, {{E96/a1_by_type_class.csv:by=claw_class;group=5-8:no_claw+peduncle_mean ~ .1f}} and {{E96/a1_by_type_class.csv:by=claw_class;group=9+:no_claw+peduncle_mean ~ .1f}} with the peduncle's. On logarithmic axes the slopes are {{E96/a1_counts.csv:kind=no_claw:loglog_slope_n ~ .2f}} and {{E96/a1_counts.csv:kind=no_claw+peduncle:loglog_slope_n ~ .2f}}, where the synapses on the kept claws have {{E96/a1_counts.csv:kind=kept:loglog_slope_n ~ .2f}}, what the bouton path takes from a KC in its fit {{E96/a1_counts.csv:kind=b:loglog_slope_n ~ .2f}} and the unweighted component, by its make, 1.

Among KCs with the same number of claws the counts in the calyx have a coefficient of variation of {{E96/a1_counts.csv:kind=no_claw:within_cv_min ~ .2f}} to {{E96/a1_counts.csv:kind=no_claw:within_cv_max ~ .2f}}, of the order of that of what the bouton path takes ({{E96/a1_counts.csv:kind=b:within_cv_min ~ .2f}} to {{E96/a1_counts.csv:kind=b:within_cv_max ~ .2f}}), and they do not follow it, the median correlation being {{E96/a1_counts.csv:kind=no_claw:within_r_b_median ~ .2f}}. Counted in synapses, those on no claw in the calyx are {{E96/runs_B.csv:B1_offclaw_d0.5_real:synapse_share ~ .2f}} of what a KC then receives from APL, on its kept claws and outside them, and with the peduncle's {{E96/runs_B.csv:B2_offclawped_d0.5_real:synapse_share ~ .2f}}.

The counts are those of one connectome, the hemibrain, in the tables that the model reads. In tables derived from four connectomes in separate work, with a synapse taken as outside the claws when it lies more than 2 µm from the KC's nearest claw, it was also read what share of APL's calyx synapses onto KCs lies outside the claws and how their number per KC goes with the KC's number of claws. The use of those tables is on hold, and both readings are withheld ([footnote](#fn-derived-tables)); no run, component, refit or verdict of this subsection used them.

The synapses that APL makes on the KCs outside the claws as a part of the APL→KC weights, against the unchanged fits and against the parts that had been put in the same place: the mean over the four wirings of the earlier searches, with the bouton path at a tenth of its fitted strength and the response rate with APL on set again to each wiring's fit, against the main target as measured, all recordings, through the calibrated readout unless raw counts are named. The settings at fixed scales are all at a size of 1; the halves are those of the first split of the flies.

The squares of the amplitude part and the shape part add up to the squared pattern part, and a spread below one means that APL moves the model's pairs apart more evenly than the flies'; no setting is chosen by a correlation ([why](#fn-pattern-split)). The first model row is the reference, the rows marked as controls could not be chosen, the two rows marked as earlier runs are for comparison ([above](#static-threshold)), and the last three rows are the family fitted again.

**At fixed scales the off-claw component reads on the pattern part as the unweighted component did, and it does not hold the mean APL effect.** Against all recordings the unchanged fits read a pattern part of {{E96/readings.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, for a floor of {{data:apl_effect_pattern_floor ~ .4f}}, and the bouton path at a tenth with nothing in its place {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D0;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} (the table).

With the off-claw component the pattern part is {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B1_offclaw_d0.5;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} to {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B1_offclaw_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} over the three sizes with the calyx alone and {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B2_offclawped_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} to {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B2_offclawped_d0.5;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} with the peduncle's, where the unweighted component had read {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D1_uniform_d0.5;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} to {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D1_uniform_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}. Size for size the two differ by {{E96/vs_uniform.csv:B2_offclawped_d1:d_pattern_z8 ~ +.4f}} to {{E96/vs_uniform.csv:B2_offclawped_d0.5:d_pattern_z8 ~ +.4f}}. On the pattern of the effect the synapses outside the claws thus do what the uniform part did. At fixed scales that is little: neither part moves the pattern part far from the run with nothing in the boutons' place, and every setting that could be chosen stays {{E96/equal.csv:variant=B6_allsyn_d2:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} to {{E96/equal.csv:variant=B2_offclawped_d0.5:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} above the fits. On the mean they do not do it.

The mean APL effect is {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B1_offclaw_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} to {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B1_offclaw_d0.5;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} with the calyx alone and {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B2_offclawped_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} to {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B2_offclawped_d0.5;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} with the peduncle's, falling as the component grows, where the unweighted component had held {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D1_uniform_d0.5;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} to {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D1_uniform_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}, the fits have {{E96/readings.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} and the flies {{data:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}}. With nothing in the boutons' place it is {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D0;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}, so that the component with the peduncle's brings back about half of the lost mean at the most, and the calyx alone, at the two larger sizes, none of it.

With the off-claw component the loss on raw counts is {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B2_offclawped_d0.5;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_loss ~ .4f}} to {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B1_offclaw_d2;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_loss ~ .4f}}, for the fits' {{E96/readings.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_loss ~ .4f}} and the unweighted component's {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D1_uniform_d2;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_loss ~ .4f}} to {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D1_uniform_d0.5;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_loss ~ .4f}}. What the off-claw component has for itself is the spread of the effect, {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B2_offclawped_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_sd_ratio ~ .2f}} to {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B1_offclaw_d0.5;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_sd_ratio ~ .2f}} of the flies' for the fits' {{E96/readings.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_sd_ratio ~ .2f}} and the unweighted component's {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D1_uniform_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_sd_ratio ~ .2f}} to {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D1_uniform_d0.5;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_sd_ratio ~ .2f}}; its cost against the fits is in the shape part ({{E96/readings.csv:variant=B2_offclawped_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_shape ~ .4f}} to {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B2_offclawped_d0.5;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_shape ~ .4f}} for {{E96/readings.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_shape ~ .4f}}).

No setting is an equal. Two are inside the 0.003 on the pattern part against all recordings and both halves, all of APL's counted synapses and the summed form with the component, each at the largest size, and every setting misses on the other two counts: the mean APL effect moves by {{E96/equal.csv:variant=B2_offclawped_d0.5:d_mean_effect ~ +.3f}} to {{E96/equal.csv:variant=B1_offclaw_d2:d_mean_effect ~ +.3f}} from the fits', where 0.01 either way was allowed, and the loss on raw counts is {{E96/equal.csv:variant=B3_offclawped_d0.5_pool1:d_raw_loss ~ .4f}} to {{E96/equal.csv:variant=B1_offclaw_d2:d_raw_loss ~ .4f}} higher, where 0.005 was.

Against three of the four halves of the recordings the lowest pattern part among the {{E96/choice.csv:half=A:n_eligible ~ .0f}} settings that could be chosen, the unchanged fits among them, is the fits' own. Against the fourth, all of APL's counted synapses at the largest size are lower by {{E96/choice.csv:half=D:gain ~ .5f}}, where 0.0015 had been asked for a reading on the held-out wirings, so that nothing went to them.

**Which KCs the synapses outside the claws are on carries nothing that a shuffle loses, and what loses the mean is not isolated.** With the counts of the component with the peduncle's permuted among the KCs with the same number of claws, one draw on each wiring, the pattern part is {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B4_offclawped_d1_permclaw1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} for the {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B2_offclawped_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} of the counts themselves, and the mean APL effect {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B4_offclawped_d1_permclaw1;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} for {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B2_offclawped_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}. Permuted over all KCs, which removes their relation to the number of claws as well, they read {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B4_offclawped_d1_permall1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} and {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B4_offclawped_d1_permall1;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}.

The result does not rest on the other choices either. Without any bouton path the component reads {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B5_offclawped_d1_dose0;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, as it does with a tenth of it. In the summed form it reads {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B3_offclawped_d2_pool1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} to {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B3_offclawped_d1_pool1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, nowhere the 0.0015 below the clipped form that had been asked for a fit of its own; the summed form without a component, the reference of those runs, has the lowest pattern part of all, {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B3_pool1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, and loses the mean effect ({{E96/readings.csv:variant=B3_pool1;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}) and, on the real wiring, the per-odor pattern of the response rates (the paragraph on realism).

With all of APL's counted synapses the pattern part is {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B6_allsyn_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} to {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B6_allsyn_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} and the mean APL effect {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B6_allsyn_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} to {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B6_allsyn_d0.5;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}, where the connectome's own weights per claw had given {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D2_connectome_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} to {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D2_connectome_d0.5;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} ([above](#static-threshold)): a part of the mean that those weights had lost comes back with the synapses that were missing, and size for size the mean is still {{E96/vs_uniform.csv:B6_allsyn_d0.5:d_mean_effect ~ +.3f}} to {{E96/vs_uniform.csv:B6_allsyn_d2:d_mean_effect ~ +.3f}} from the unweighted component's. What the unweighted component did for the mean is therefore not done by reaching nearly every KC. The off-claw component differs from it in two respects.

A KC's total grows with its number of claws less than in proportion, and the weight is not the same from claw to claw. No run separates the two. As a description, at each of the three sizes the mean effect falls in the order of the second and not of the first (the table below), and the counts permuted over all KCs, which have no relation to the number of claws left, keep the mean of the counts themselves. The runs that separate the two have since been made ([below](#weight-evenness)): the first carries none of the loss, and of the second what carries it is the inequality of the amounts among KCs with the same number of claws.

The parts that have been put in the boutons' place, in the order of how unequal each is from claw to claw: the coefficient of variation of the part's weight per claw over the claws of the real wiring, the slope of a KC's total on its number of claws on logarithmic axes, and the mean APL effect at the three sizes, for the mean over the four wirings of the earlier searches through the calibrated readout. A description and not a test: no run of this subsection varies one of the two properties with the other held, and the runs that do are [below](#weight-evenness).

**Fitted again with the off-claw component and the bouton path at a tenth, the family reads about four thousandths above the unchanged fits: as the refit with the unweighted component on the pattern part, and not on the mean.** The condition for the refit held, the best setting of the component, the calyx alone at the smallest size, being {{E96/equal.csv:variant=B1_offclaw_d0.5:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} above the fits where 0.008 was allowed.

At their best sizes the calyx alone and the component with the peduncle's were within 0.0005 of each other ({{E96/readings.csv:variant=B1_offclaw_d0.5;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} and {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B2_offclawped_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}), so that the calyx alone was fitted, the form that does not rest on where in a KC the peduncle's synapses act; the summed form and all of APL's counted synapses had not met the conditions for fits of their own.

The population of the four kept fits reads a pattern part of {{E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all ~ .4f}}, for the unchanged fits' {{E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}} (the last three rows of the table). That is {{diff:E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}} above the fits against all recordings, and {{diff:E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:halfA -- E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:halfA_unchanged ~ .4f}} and {{diff:E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:halfB -- E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:halfB_unchanged ~ .4f}} against the two halves, where an equal had to stay within 0.003 against all three. It is {{diff:E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all ~ .4f}} above the refit with the unweighted component ({{E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all ~ .4f}}), inside the 0.0015 that had been fixed for reading as well as it, and {{diff:E94/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all ~ .4f}} below the refit with nothing in the boutons' place ({{E94/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all ~ .4f}}). On the mean and on raw counts it does not read as the refit with the unweighted component. Its mean APL effect is {{E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}, for {{E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} there, the fits' {{E96/readings.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} and the flies' {{data:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}}, and its loss on raw counts {{E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:raw_loss ~ .4f}}, for {{E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:raw_loss ~ .4f}} there and the fits' {{E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:raw_loss_unchanged ~ .4f}}.

The spread of the effect is nearer the flies' than the fits' is ({{E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:sd_ratio ~ .2f}} for {{E96/readings.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_sd_ratio ~ .2f}}), and the cost is in the shape part ({{E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:shape ~ .4f}} for {{E96/readings.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_shape ~ .4f}}). By wiring the kept refit is lower than the unchanged fit on one claw permutation and higher on the other, on the real wiring and on the matched shuffle, the four moving by {{diff:E96/d_scores.csv:unit=P1;picked=True:pattern_all -- E96/d_scores.csv:unit=P1;picked=True:pattern_all_unchanged ~ +.4f}} to {{diff:E96/d_scores.csv:unit=P2;picked=True:pattern_all -- E96/d_scores.csv:unit=P2;picked=True:pattern_all_unchanged ~ +.4f}}.

The fitted size of the component is {{E96/d_scores.csv:unit=M1;picked=True:aplkc_flat_size ~ .2f}} to {{E96/d_scores.csv:unit=P1;picked=True:aplkc_flat_size ~ .2f}}. The two starts of a wiring did not end in the same place, and the fit that was kept, the one with the lower value of its own loss, is not on every wiring the one with the lower pattern part: on the matched shuffle the kept fit reads {{E96/d_scores.csv:unit=M1;picked=True:pattern_all ~ .4f}} and the other {{E96/d_scores.csv:unit=M1;start=own:pattern_all ~ .4f}}. The refits on the four held-out wirings had been kept for an equal and were not run.

**Realism.** No mechanism was added to the base. Synapses that the connectome holds and the model's weights had left out were added to the APL→KC weights, and both response rates were held, the one with APL on by the tied APL scale in every run and the one with APL off by the fit's own run. The {{lit:64 # the rows of results/E96_offclaw_apl/runs_B.csv}} runs at fixed scales have response rates of {{E96/runs_B.csv:B1_offclaw_d0.5_real:rate_on ~ .3f}} to {{E96/runs_B.csv:B1_offclaw_d0.5_P1:rate_on ~ .3f}} with APL on and {{E96/runs_B.csv:B1_offclaw_d0.5_M1:rate_off ~ .3f}} to {{E96/runs_B.csv:B1_offclaw_d0.5_P2:rate_off ~ .3f}} with APL off (ratios of {{E96/runs_B.csv:B2_offclawped_d2_M1:ratio ~ .2f}} to {{E96/runs_B.csv:B3_offclawped_d1_pool1_P2:ratio ~ .2f}}), and the {{lit:eight # the rows of results/E96_offclaw_apl/d_scores.csv with a start (own and e95 for each of real, P1, P2 and M1)}} refits, two on each wiring, {{E96/d_scores.csv:unit=P2;start=own:rate_on ~ .3f}} to {{E96/d_scores.csv:unit=real;start=e95:rate_on ~ .3f}} and {{E96/d_scores.csv:unit=P1;start=e95:rate_off ~ .3f}} to {{E96/d_scores.csv:unit=P2;start=e95:rate_off ~ .3f}} ({{E96/d_scores.csv:unit=P1;start=e95:ratio ~ .2f}} to {{E96/d_scores.csv:unit=P2;start=e95:ratio ~ .2f}}), for the flies' {{data:noise_ctrl_frac ~ .3f}} and {{data:noise_tnt_frac ~ .3f}} ({{data:noise_rate_ratio_fraction ~ .2f}}).

{{lit:One # the one row with a realism_flag in results/E96_offclaw_apl/runs_B.csv (B3_pool1_real); none in d_scores.csv; the same one in results/E96_offclaw_apl/verdict.json, flagged_runs}} run is outside a band: the summed form without a component, on the real wiring, where the response rate ρ with APL on is {{E96/runs_B.csv:B3_pool1_real:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}} for the 0.37 that the band asks. It is the reference of its runs and could be neither chosen nor an equal. Every other run and the eight refits are inside the four bands, with a response rate ρ with APL on of {{E96/runs_B.csv:B1_offclaw_d0.5_real:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}} or more and a distribution of the number of odors per KC that is at most {{E96/runs_B.csv:B1_offclaw_d2_P1:opk_on_tv ~ .3f}} from the flies' with APL on (band {{data:noise_ctrl_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .3f}}) and {{E96/d_scores.csv:unit=M1;start=e95:opk_off_tv ~ .3f}} with APL off (band {{data:noise_tnt_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .3f}}).

Counted by the recordings' own criterion, as the bands counted until 2026-11-10, the same run and no other is outside a band. On the real wiring the off-claw component brings the per-odor pattern of the response rates back inside its band: with the bouton path at a tenth and nothing in its place the response rate ρ with APL on had been {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d0.1_real:rate_rho_on ~ .3f}}, just under it ([above](#bouton-share)).

The largest spike count of a KC to one odor with APL on is {{E96/runs_B.csv:B3_pool1_M1:max_count_on ~ .0f}} to {{E96/runs_B.csv:B4_offclawped_d1_permclaw1_P1:max_count_on ~ .0f}} over the runs and {{E96/d_scores.csv:unit=P2;start=own:max_count_on ~ .0f}} to {{E96/d_scores.csv:unit=P1;start=e95:max_count_on ~ .0f}} in the refits, in a family that nothing bounds there ([the firing ceiling for the KCs](#firing-ceiling)). In the runs with the off-claw component the bouton share is {{E96/runs_B.csv:B1_offclaw_d0.5_P2:bouton_share ~ .3f}} to {{E96/runs_B.csv:B2_offclawped_d0.5_real:bouton_share ~ .3f}} at the smallest size and {{E96/runs_B.csv:B1_offclaw_d2_M1:bouton_share ~ .3f}} to {{E96/runs_B.csv:B2_offclawped_d2_real:bouton_share ~ .3f}} at the largest, at and below the fraction of {{E94/a2_connectome.csv:set=calyx, all:share_pn ~ .3f}} to {{E94/a2_connectome.csv:set=calyx, assigned, KCs with a type:share_pn ~ .3f}} of APL's calyx synapses that the connectome puts on PN boutons, and the component makes {{E96/runs_B.csv:B2_offclawped_d0.5_P2:comp_share ~ .2f}} to {{E96/runs_B.csv:B1_offclaw_d0.5_real:comp_share ~ .2f}} of what APL takes from the claws' drive at the smallest size and {{E96/runs_B.csv:B2_offclawped_d2_P1:comp_share ~ .2f}} to {{E96/runs_B.csv:B1_offclaw_d2_real:comp_share ~ .2f}} at the largest.

Four things bear on what can be defended. The refits move two parameters away from the fits'. The kept refits have a somatic threshold of {{E96/d_scores.csv:unit=P1;picked=True:fixed_thr ~ .0f}} to {{E96/d_scores.csv:unit=P2;picked=True:fixed_thr ~ .0f}}, for the fits' {{E96/runs_B.csv:B1_offclaw_d0.5_P1:fixed_thr ~ .0f}} to {{E96/runs_B.csv:B1_offclaw_d0.5_M1:fixed_thr ~ .0f}}, and a KC–KC scale of {{E96/d_scores.csv:unit=P2;picked=True:kc_kc_inh ~ .1f}} to {{E96/d_scores.csv:unit=P1;picked=True:kc_kc_inh ~ .1f}}, for the fits' {{E96/runs_B.csv:B1_offclaw_d0.5_P2:wKCKC_scale ~ .1f}} to {{E96/runs_B.csv:B1_offclaw_d0.5_P1:wKCKC_scale ~ .1f}}.

The off-claw component is the connectome's in its counts and not in its placement. A KC's count is spread evenly over the KC's claws, where on the dendrite a synapse lies not being modelled, and the weights on the claws keep the family's breadth weighting.

The settings with the peduncle's synapses take them to act on a KC's drive, which holds only if they lie before the place where the KC's spikes start; the component with the calyx alone, the one that was fitted, does not rest on that. And the counts are one hemibrain's: how the number of such synapses on a KC goes with its number of claws in other connectomes is among the readings that are withheld ([footnote](#fn-derived-tables)).

The verdict was not bought with the bands or bent by them, the only run outside a band being a reference that could not be chosen. As everywhere, the pairs with paa, euc and -aPine rest on [ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations).

**What follows.** Nothing is gained on the main target. The reference stays the family as fitted, no base and no bound is changed, and the off-claw component is a reading and not a candidate.

Three things are carried from here. The first is a fourth price for the connectome's bouton share, and the first with weights that the connectome has.

Holding the bouton path at a tenth of its fitted strength costs {{E94/equal.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d0.1:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} of the pattern part at fixed scales. After a refit it costs {{diff:E94/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E94/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}} with the family's weights, {{diff:E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}} with the unweighted component, which the connectome does not have, and {{diff:E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}} with the off-claw component, which it has. The last comes with a mean APL effect of {{E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} for the flies' {{data:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}}, with a loss on raw counts {{diff:E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:raw_loss -- E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:raw_loss_unchanged ~ .4f}} above the fits', and with somatic thresholds and KC–KC scales away from the fits'. Whether a limit on the bouton share replaces the bound on the APL→bouton scale, and at which of these prices, is still a choice to be made, and nothing here makes it.

The second is what the boutons' offset stands in for. For the pattern of the effect, the synapses that the model's weights had left out do at the KCs what the uniform part did, so that the three to four thousandths that stay with the connectome's bouton share are not a matter of reaching every claw. For the mean APL effect they do not, and which property of the uniform part held the mean is open: a KC's total in proportion to its number of claws, or a weight that is the same from claw to claw.

The third is three leads for planning, and none has been run. One is the pair of runs that would separate those two properties: the off-claw counts rescaled so that a KC's total grows in proportion to its number of claws, against the same amounts per KC made unequal from claw to claw. Another is the same reading with the counts of another connectome, which needs that connectome's wiring in the model's format. The last is where on the dendrite the synapses outside the claws lie, relative to the claws that an odor drives, which the model does not represent. The first of the three has since been run ([below](#weight-evenness)), and the question above is closed: the uniform part held the mean by giving KCs with the same number of claws equal amounts, and not by a total in proportion to the number of claws.

The two groups of the common error are where they were. Against the weightings' line ([above](#steps-like-for-like)) every setting with a component stays at the family's place or a little further from the flies, between {{E96/line.csv:variant=B6_allsyn_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:resid ~ +.3f}} and {{E96/line.csv:variant=B3_offclawped_d0.5_pool1;unit=S;readout=cal:resid ~ +.3f}} for the family's {{E96/line.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=cal:resid ~ +.3f}} and the flies' {{lit:0.09866993033793536 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, lines.cal.S.flies.trial_mean_all.resid ~ +.3f}}, and the alcohol pairs' co-response change under APL stays below the flies' interval ({{E96/coresponse.csv:variant=ref;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:flies_lo ~ .2f}} to {{E96/coresponse.csv:variant=ref;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:flies_hi ~ .2f}}) in every setting, at {{E96/coresponse.csv:variant=B2_offclawped_d0.5;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} to {{E96/coresponse.csv:variant=B1_offclaw_d2;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} for the family's {{E96/coresponse.csv:variant=ref;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}}.

The limits are those of runs at fixed scales and of local searches. The second part set one factor again on four wirings and left every other parameter at the fit's. The refits are one search from each of two starts on a wiring, of {{E96/d_scores.csv:unit=P1;start=e95:n_evals ~ .0f}} to {{E96/d_scores.csv:unit=P2;start=own:n_evals ~ .0f}} evaluations, and the rule that kept one of the two was the fit's own loss and not the pattern part.

The margins are lines: the refit lies {{diff:E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all ~ .4f}} from the refit with the unweighted component, where 0.0015 was allowed, and {{diff:E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}} from the fits, where 0.003 was. Nothing here was read on the four held-out wirings.

The counts are one connectome's as the model's loader reads it, and what the counts of other connectomes are like is among the readings that are withheld ([footnote](#fn-derived-tables)); the run in which a KC's count no longer follows its number of claws is the shuffle over all KCs, which read as the counts themselves did. Every reading here is of the model's 0.5 s pulse without trial noise, in the family without a firing ceiling; the readings with the ceiling, at the flies' pulse and through the trial noise had been kept for a setting that passed, and none was made.

### The evenness of APL's weights among KCs and over a KC's claws: which property of APL's counted synapses loses the mean APL effect when they are put in the bouton path's place at the KCs, how a KC's amount grows with its number of claws, how unequal the amounts are among KCs with the same number of claws, or how unevenly the synapses lie over a KC's claws {#weight-evenness}

**With the bouton path near the connectome's share, what loses the mean APL effect when APL's counted synapses are put in the bouton path's place is that KCs with the same number of claws get unequal amounts.** That a KC's amount grows with its number of claws less than in proportion loses none of it.

With the inequality removed and the slope kept, the synapses outside the claws hold the mean as the part that is the same on every claw does; with the slope removed and the inequality kept, they lose what they had lost. For the connectome's own weights on the claws the amounts per KC carry most of the loss through the calibrated readout and how the synapses lie over a KC's claws little of it; on raw counts the two share it.

Half the inequality of the counts outside the claws already loses about a hundredth of the mean, and every part made of each KC's counted synapses is more unequal than that, so that none holds the mean however it is spread, and the family was not fitted again. The bouton path of the best family is not equal among such KCs either: it holds the mean in the other way, by following what each KC loses.

The pattern part stays where it was in every setting. Nothing is gained on the main target, and no base, bound or reference is changed. What is added is the reason for the lost mean that goes with the fourth price of the connectome's bouton share. [APL's synapses on the KCs outside the claws](#offclaw-synapses) had left that reason open.

With the bouton path held at a tenth of its fitted strength, the unweighted component holds the mean APL effect, and the parts made of APL's counted synapses lose some of it: the off-claw component, all of APL's counted synapses and, most of all, the connectome's own weights per claw ([above](#static-threshold)). The counted parts differ from the unweighted component in three ways that no run had separated.

- A KC's amount, the sum of the part's weights over the KC's claws, grows with the KC's number of claws less than in proportion (the slope).
- KCs with the same number of claws get unequal amounts (the inequality).
- And where the synapses are on the claws, they lie unevenly over a KC's claws (the placement).

The experiment on the evenness of APL's weights among KCs and over a KC's claws was run on the breadth-2 family as the two before it were ([above](#static-threshold); [above](#offclaw-synapses)): on the four wirings of the earlier searches, each at its own fit ([the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population)) and with the lab's input, with the bouton path at a tenth of its fitted strength and a part added to the family's APL→KC weights, its size in the unit of the unweighted component. In every run the tied APL scale was set again until the number of responses with APL on was the fit's; the somatic threshold and the KC–KC scale stayed the fit's and the responses with APL off are the fit's own, so that both response rates are held.

Each new part changes one of the three properties of a counted part and keeps the others. Four were made from the counts outside the claws in the calyx, the off-claw component's.

- With the slope removed, every group of KCs with the same number of claws has the same amount per claw and each KC keeps its count relative to its group's mean.
- With the inequality removed, every KC has its group's mean.
- With half the inequality, each KC lies halfway between its own count and its group's mean.
- As presence alone, every KC that has such a synapse has the same amount per claw and the others none.

The first two were run also at a size of 2 and with the peduncle's synapses. Two were made from the connectome's own weights on the claws: each KC's amount kept and spread evenly over its claws, and every KC given the same amount per claw, placed over its claws as its synapses lie.

And each KC's count of all of APL's synapses, on the claws that the wiring keeps and outside the claws, was spread evenly over the KC's claws, with the peduncle's and without, at sizes of 0.5, 1 and 2. These last, and the amounts on the claws spread evenly, are counts as counted; the others are rearrangements that no connectome holds, made to isolate one property. A group with fewer than 20 KCs was joined to the group with the next lower number of claws.

Before any run was scored the new code was checked. On the real wiring it reproduces four earlier runs without one differing spike count, those with the unweighted component, with the connectome's own weights per claw, with the off-claw component and with all of APL's counted synapses, and on each of the four wirings the two parts made from a count multiply back to it, claw by claw.

What would count had been fixed beforehand. The loss of a counted part is the gap between its mean APL effect and the unweighted component's at the same size, for the mean over the four wirings through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout).

A property carries the loss if removing it alone brings back 0.6 of the gap or more while removing the other brings back less than 0.25, and the reading holds by wiring if three of the four wirings give it from their own values. The family was to be fitted again with all counted synapses spread evenly, the bouton path held at a tenth, only if that part held a mean APL effect of +0.168 or more, within 0.01 of the flies', with a pattern part within 0.0015 of the unweighted component's at the same size.

Only the counts as counted could be chosen against a half of the recordings or be an equal, by the rules of the two experiments before. And two descriptions of the seven means that had been saved, the mean APL effect falling with the variance of a part's weight per claw as a whole, or with its parts among KCs and within KCs separately, were written down with their predictions for every new setting before the first run.

![The mean APL effect (left) and the pattern part of the APL-effect loss (right, lower is better) for every setting, as the mean over the four wirings of the earlier searches (S in the figure's title) through the calibrated readout, with the bouton path at a tenth of its fitted strength. Left: the dotted line is the flies' mean APL effect, and the dashed lines are the unweighted component (D1_uniform_d1) and the off-claw component with the calyx alone (B1_offclaw_d1), both at a size of 1. Right: black, against all recordings; red and blue, against the two halves of the first split of the flies; dashed lines, the unchanged fits. Hollow marker: a setting with a run outside the realism bands or at a limit of the search for the APL scale. The new settings: the counts outside the claws with the slope removed (K1), with the inequality removed (K2), with half the inequality (K3) and as presence alone (K4), from the calyx's counts (offclaw) or with the peduncle's (offclawped); the weights on the claws with each KC's amount spread evenly over its claws (W1) and with every KC the same amount per claw, placed as its synapses lie (W2); all of APL's counted synapses spread evenly over each KC's claws, with the peduncle's (T1) and without (T2); d0.5, d1 and d2 give the size. The earlier runs: the unweighted component (D1_uniform), the connectome's own weights per claw (D2_connectome), the off-claw component with the calyx alone (B1_offclaw) and with the peduncle's (B2_offclawped), its counts permuted among KCs with the same number of claws (B4, permclaw1) and over all KCs (B4, permall1), all of APL's counted synapses with those on the claws where they lie (B6_allsyn), and the bouton path at a tenth with nothing in its place (D0).](results/E99_apl_weight_evenness/E99_settings.png)

The parts that have been put in the bouton path's place, with one property of the counts changed at a time: the mean over the four wirings of the earlier searches at a size of 1, with the bouton path at a tenth of its fitted strength and the response rate with APL on set again to each wiring's fit, against the main target as measured, all recordings, through the calibrated readout unless raw counts are named.

The first three columns describe the part itself and are the same on the four wirings: the slope of a KC's amount on its number of claws on logarithmic axes, where 1 is in proportion; the coefficient of variation of the amount among KCs with the same number of claws, as the median over the numbers of claws from 2 to 10; and the variance of the weight per claw that lies within KCs, in how a KC's amount is divided over its own claws, in units of the squared mean weight.

The squares of the amplitude part and the shape part add up to the squared pattern part, and a spread below one means that APL moves the model's pairs apart more evenly than the flies'; no setting is chosen by a correlation ([why](#fn-pattern-split)). The rows marked as earlier runs are for comparison ([above](#static-threshold); [above](#offclaw-synapses)). Of the new rows only those in which counts are spread evenly as counted could be chosen; the others are constructions.
