**Between KCs, the inequality carries the loss and the slope none of it.** At a size of 1 the unweighted component holds a mean APL effect of {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D1_uniform_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} and the off-claw component with the calyx alone {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B1_offclaw_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}, a gap of {{E99/c_shares.csv:kind=between;case=calyx_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:gap ~ .3f}}; the flies' mean is {{data:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}} (the table).

With the slope removed and the inequality kept the mean is {{E99/readings.csv:variant=K1_offclaw_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}. A KC's amount then grows in proportion to its number of claws, as the unweighted component's does, and what was lost stays lost. With the inequality removed and the slope kept it is {{E99/readings.csv:variant=K2_offclaw_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}. The amounts then still grow with the number of claws as weakly as the counts do, with a slope of {{E99/a1_shapes.csv:wiring=real;setting=K2:loglog_slope_n ~ .2f}} on logarithmic axes, and the mean is the unweighted component's. Removing the inequality thus brings back {{E99/c_shares.csv:kind=between;case=calyx_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:ineq_share ~ .2f}} of the gap and removing the slope {{E99/c_shares.csv:kind=between;case=calyx_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:slope_share ~ .2f}}.

The reading is the same at a size of 2 ({{E99/c_shares.csv:kind=between;case=calyx_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:ineq_share ~ .2f}} and {{E99/c_shares.csv:kind=between;case=calyx_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:slope_share ~ .2f}} of a gap of {{E99/c_shares.csv:kind=between;case=calyx_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:gap ~ .3f}}) and with the peduncle's synapses ({{E99/c_shares.csv:kind=between;case=peduncle_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:ineq_share ~ .2f}} and {{E99/c_shares.csv:kind=between;case=peduncle_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:slope_share ~ .2f}} of {{E99/c_shares.csv:kind=between;case=peduncle_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:gap ~ .3f}}). It holds on each of the four wirings taken by itself, where the inequality's share is {{E99/c_shares.csv:kind=between;case=calyx_d1;unit=real;readout=cal:ineq_share ~ .2f}} to {{E99/c_shares.csv:kind=between;case=calyx_d1;unit=M1;readout=cal:ineq_share ~ .2f}} and the slope's {{E99/c_shares.csv:kind=between;case=calyx_d1;unit=P1;readout=cal:slope_share ~ .2f}} to {{E99/c_shares.csv:kind=between;case=calyx_d1;unit=M1;readout=cal:slope_share ~ .2f}}, and on raw counts ({{E99/c_shares.csv:kind=between;case=calyx_d1;unit=S;readout=raw:ineq_share ~ .2f}} and {{E99/c_shares.csv:kind=between;case=calyx_d1;unit=S;readout=raw:slope_share ~ .2f}}). Beforehand the inequality had been thought the more likely of the two, at about three in five.

What the inequality does shows in which KCs respond. With the off-claw component, the fifth of the KCs that have the fewest synapses outside the claws for their number of claws makes {{E99/b_fifths.csv:variant=B1_offclaw_d1;unit=S;by=fifth_offclaw;group=1:share_on ~ .0%}} of all responses with APL on, and the fifth that has the most {{E99/b_fifths.csv:variant=B1_offclaw_d1;unit=S;by=fifth_offclaw;group=5:share_on ~ .0%}}; with the unweighted component the same two fifths make {{E99/b_fifths.csv:variant=D1_uniform_d1;unit=S;by=fifth_offclaw;group=1:share_on ~ .0%}} and {{E99/b_fifths.csv:variant=D1_uniform_d1;unit=S;by=fifth_offclaw;group=5:share_on ~ .0%}}. Removing the inequality evens them ({{E99/b_fifths.csv:variant=K2_offclaw_d1;unit=S;by=fifth_offclaw;group=1:share_on ~ .0%}} and {{E99/b_fifths.csv:variant=K2_offclaw_d1;unit=S;by=fifth_offclaw;group=5:share_on ~ .0%}}), and removing the slope alone leaves them as the counts had them ({{E99/b_fifths.csv:variant=K1_offclaw_d1;unit=S;by=fifth_offclaw;group=1:share_on ~ .0%}} and {{E99/b_fifths.csv:variant=K1_offclaw_d1;unit=S;by=fifth_offclaw;group=5:share_on ~ .0%}}).

Among KCs with the same number of claws, those that the part inhibits least take over the responses with APL on, and the mean APL effect falls. The two shuffles of the earlier experiment had pointed the same way ([above](#offclaw-synapses)): permuted among KCs with the same number of claws, which keeps the inequality and the slope, and over all KCs, which keeps the inequality and takes the slope away altogether, the counts with the peduncle's had held the mean of the counts themselves.

**Within the connectome's own weights on the claws, the amounts per KC carry most of the loss through the calibrated readout, and the placement little.** The connectome's own weights per claw lose the most of the mean, {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D2_connectome_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} for the unweighted component's {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D1_uniform_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}, a gap of {{E99/c_shares.csv:kind=within;case=d1;unit=S;readout=cal:gap ~ .3f}}.

In units of the squared mean weight, the variance of those weights from claw to claw is {{E99/a1_shapes.csv:wiring=real;setting=connectome:within ~ .2f}} within KCs, in how a KC's synapses are divided over its own claws, {{E99/a1_shapes.csv:wiring=real;setting=connectome:among ~ .2f}} among KCs with the same number of claws and {{E99/a1_shapes.csv:wiring=real;setting=connectome:between ~ .2f}} between the numbers of claws, so that the placement is the largest part of their unevenness. It is not the part that loses most of the mean.

With each KC's amount kept and spread evenly over its claws the mean is {{E99/readings.csv:variant=W1_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}, as with the weights where they lie. With every KC given the same amount per claw, placed as its synapses lie, it is {{E99/readings.csv:variant=W2_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}. Equal amounts thus bring back {{E99/c_shares.csv:kind=within;case=d1;unit=S;readout=cal:amounts_share ~ .2f}} of the gap and an even placement {{E99/c_shares.csv:kind=within;case=d1;unit=S;readout=cal:placement_share ~ .2f}}, and the amounts carry the loss by the rule on each of the four wirings, with shares of {{E99/c_shares.csv:kind=within;case=d1;unit=real;readout=cal:amounts_share ~ .2f}} to {{E99/c_shares.csv:kind=within;case=d1;unit=P2;readout=cal:amounts_share ~ .2f}} for the amounts and {{E99/c_shares.csv:kind=within;case=d1;unit=P1;readout=cal:placement_share ~ .2f}} to {{E99/c_shares.csv:kind=within;case=d1;unit=M1;readout=cal:placement_share ~ .2f}} for the placement.

The placement as counted is not free, however. The two shares do not add up to the whole: with the amounts equal, the uneven placement still leaves the mean {{diff:E95/readings.csv:variant=D1_uniform_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect -- E99/readings.csv:variant=W2_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ .3f}} short of the unweighted component's, a cost that it hardly adds once the amounts are unequal.

And on raw counts neither carries the loss alone by the rule. Equal amounts there bring back {{E99/c_shares.csv:kind=within;case=d1;unit=S;readout=raw:amounts_share ~ .2f}} of the gap, short of the 0.6 that had been fixed for carrying it, and an even placement {{E99/c_shares.csv:kind=within;case=d1;unit=S;readout=raw:placement_share ~ .2f}}, and with the amounts equal the mean on raw counts stays {{diff:E95/readings.csv:variant=D1_uniform_d1;unit=S;readout=raw:mean_effect -- E99/readings.csv:variant=W2_d1;unit=S;readout=raw:mean_effect ~ .3f}} short; by wiring the rule there gives the amounts on two of the four wirings and neither alone on the other two. That the amounts carry it is thus the calibrated readout's reading, the one for which the rule had been fixed.

Both descriptions written down beforehand had put this loss on the placement, which had been thought as likely as not to carry it where the amounts had been given about one chance in six, and both descriptions were wrong in that. All of APL's counted synapses show the same: with the part on the claws spread evenly in place of lying where it is counted, the mean moves by {{diff:E99/readings.csv:variant=T1_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect -- E96/readings.csv:variant=B6_allsyn_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} at a size of 1.

**The counted amounts are more unequal than the mean bears, and no part made of counted synapses holds it.** Among KCs with the same number of claws the counts outside the claws in the calyx have a coefficient of variation of {{E99/a1_shapes.csv:wiring=real;setting=offclaw:within_cv_median ~ .2f}}. With half the inequality, a coefficient of {{E99/a1_shapes.csv:wiring=real;setting=K3:within_cv_median ~ .2f}}, the mean APL effect is {{E99/readings.csv:variant=K3_offclaw_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}, {{diff:E95/readings.csv:variant=D1_uniform_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect -- E99/readings.csv:variant=K3_offclaw_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ .3f}} below the unweighted component's, and with all of it {{E99/c_shares.csv:kind=between;case=calyx_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:gap ~ .3f}} below. A power law through the two puts the loss of a hundredth of the mean at a coefficient of variation of about {{lit:0.287911369497319 # results/E99_apl_weight_evenness/c_verdicts.json, bound.cv_at_loss ~ .2f}}, half of what the counts have.

Presence alone, the same amount per claw for every KC that has a synapse outside its claws and none for the {{E96/a1_counts.csv:kind=no_claw:kcs_none_share ~ .1%}} of the KCs that have none, gives {{E99/readings.csv:variant=K4_offclaw_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}. That is {{diff:E95/readings.csv:variant=D1_uniform_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect -- E99/readings.csv:variant=K4_offclaw_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ .3f}} below the unweighted component's, about two fifths of the gap, so that the KCs without such a synapse are a part of the loss and not the whole of it.

Every counted part is more unequal than that bound: the coefficient of variation is {{E99/a1_shapes.csv:wiring=real;setting=connectome:within_cv_median ~ .2f}} for the amounts on the claws, {{E99/a1_shapes.csv:wiring=real;setting=T1:within_cv_median ~ .2f}} for all of APL's counted synapses and {{E99/a1_shapes.csv:wiring=real;setting=T2:within_cv_median ~ .2f}} for them without the peduncle's (the table). The bound is a line through two settings of one kind of count and not a rule for every kind: the amounts on the claws lose more of the mean at a like coefficient. It is also a bound for amounts that do not follow what a KC loses, as the paragraph on what follows sets out.

Each KC's count of all of APL's synapses, spread evenly over its claws, was the part that could have held the mean with weights that the connectome has, and had been thought as likely as not to hold it. Its mean APL effect is {{E99/readings.csv:variant=T1_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} to {{E99/readings.csv:variant=T1_d0.5;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} over the three sizes with the peduncle's and {{E99/readings.csv:variant=T2_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} to {{E99/readings.csv:variant=T2_d0.5;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} without, falling as the part grows, for the +0.168 that had been asked. The family was therefore not fitted again, and the price of the connectome's bouton share with counted weights stays the one already read ([above](#offclaw-synapses)).

**The pattern part does not separate the settings.** Against all recordings the new settings read a pattern part of {{E99/readings.csv:variant=T2_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} to {{E99/readings.csv:variant=W2_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, for the unchanged fits' {{E99/readings.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, the unweighted component's {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D1_uniform_d0.5;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} to {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D1_uniform_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} and a floor of {{data:apl_effect_pattern_floor ~ .4f}}; the amplitude part, the shape part and the spread of the effect are in the table.

Against three of the four halves of the recordings the lowest pattern part among the {{E99/choice.csv:half=A:n_eligible ~ .0f}} settings that could be chosen, the unchanged fits among them, is the fits' own. Against the fourth, all of APL's counted synapses without the peduncle's at the largest size are lower by {{E99/choice.csv:half=D:gain ~ .4f}}, where 0.0015 had been asked for a reading on the held-out wirings, so that nothing went to them. No setting is an equal either: the mean APL effect moves by {{E99/equal.csv:variant=T1_d0.5:d_mean_effect ~ +.3f}} to {{E99/equal.csv:variant=W1_d1:d_mean_effect ~ +.3f}} from the fits', where 0.01 either way was allowed, and the loss on raw counts is {{E99/equal.csv:variant=T1_d0.5:d_raw_loss ~ .4f}} to {{E99/equal.csv:variant=W1_d1:d_raw_loss ~ .4f}} higher, where 0.005 was.

The two groups of the common error are where they were. Against the weightings' line ([above](#steps-like-for-like)) every new setting stays at the family's place or a little further from the flies, between {{E99/line.csv:variant=W2_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:resid ~ +.3f}} and {{E99/line.csv:variant=W1_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:resid ~ +.3f}} for the family's {{E99/line.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=cal:resid ~ +.3f}} and the flies' {{lit:0.09866993033793536 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, lines.cal.S.flies.trial_mean_all.resid ~ +.3f}}. The alcohol pairs' co-response change under APL is {{E99/coresponse.csv:variant=K2_offclawped_d1;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} to {{E99/coresponse.csv:variant=T2_d2;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} over the new settings, for the family's {{E99/coresponse.csv:variant=ref;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} and the flies' interval of {{E99/coresponse.csv:variant=ref;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:flies_lo ~ .2f}} to {{E99/coresponse.csv:variant=ref;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:flies_hi ~ .2f}}. It stays below the interval in every new setting but one, all of APL's counted synapses without the peduncle's at the largest size, which reaches the interval's lower edge and holds the least of the mean among the parts of all counted synapses.

**Realism.** No mechanism was added to the base. Counted synapses were rearranged within a part of the APL→KC weights, and both response rates were held, the one with APL on by the tied APL scale in every run and the one with APL off by the fit's own run.

The {{lit:64 # the rows of results/E99_apl_weight_evenness/runs_B.csv}} runs have response rates of {{E99/runs_B.csv:T2_d1_real:rate_on ~ .3f}} to {{E99/runs_B.csv:T1_d0.5_P1:rate_on ~ .3f}} with APL on and {{E99/runs_B.csv:K1_offclaw_d1_M1:rate_off ~ .3f}} to {{E99/runs_B.csv:K1_offclaw_d1_P2:rate_off ~ .3f}} with APL off (ratios of {{E99/runs_B.csv:K1_offclaw_d1_M1:ratio ~ .2f}} to {{E99/runs_B.csv:K2_offclaw_d2_P2:ratio ~ .2f}}), for the flies' {{data:noise_ctrl_frac ~ .3f}} and {{data:noise_tnt_frac ~ .3f}} ({{data:noise_rate_ratio_fraction ~ .2f}}). All of them are inside the four bands, with a response rate ρ with APL on of {{E99/runs_B.csv:K2_offclaw_d2_P1:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}} or more and a distribution of the number of odors per KC that is at most {{E99/runs_B.csv:W1_d1_P2:opk_on_tv ~ .3f}} from the flies' with APL on (band {{data:noise_ctrl_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .3f}}) and {{E99/runs_B.csv:K1_offclaw_d1_real:opk_off_tv ~ .3f}} with APL off (band {{data:noise_tnt_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .3f}}). Counted by the recordings' own criterion, as the bands counted until 2026-11-10, none is outside a band either, and no run ended at a limit of the search for the APL scale.

The largest spike count of a KC to one odor with APL on is {{E99/runs_B.csv:K2_offclaw_d2_P2:max_count_on ~ .0f}} to {{E99/runs_B.csv:W1_d1_P1:max_count_on ~ .0f}} over the runs, in a family that nothing bounds there ([the firing ceiling for the KCs](#firing-ceiling)), and the bouton share is {{E99/runs_B.csv:T2_d2_M1:bouton_share ~ .3f}} to {{E99/runs_B.csv:T1_d0.5_real:bouton_share ~ .3f}}, at and below the fraction of {{E94/a2_connectome.csv:set=calyx, all:share_pn ~ .3f}} to {{E94/a2_connectome.csv:set=calyx, assigned, KCs with a type:share_pn ~ .3f}} of APL's calyx synapses that the connectome puts on PN boutons.

What cannot be defended as anatomy is the constructions themselves. The parts with the slope removed, with the inequality removed or halved, as presence alone and with equal amounts are rearrangements of counted synapses made to isolate one property, and no connectome holds them. The parts in which a KC's count is spread evenly over its claws are the connectome's in their counts and not in their placement, and those with the peduncle's synapses take them to act on a KC's drive. That the mean APL effect comes back with the inequality removed is therefore a reading of what the mean needs of such a part, and not a model that has it; it came at no cost on the bands.

The counts are one hemibrain's, in the tables that the model reads. How unequal the counts of other connectomes are among KCs with the same number of claws was to be read from connectome tables whose use is on hold, and is not given here ([footnote](#fn-derived-tables)); no construction, run or verdict of this subsection used them. As everywhere, the pairs with paa, euc and -aPine rest on [ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations).

**What follows.** Nothing is gained on the main target. The reference stays the family as fitted, no base and no bound is changed, and the constructions are readings and not candidates.

Three things are carried from here. The first closes the question that the synapses outside the claws had left ([above](#offclaw-synapses)). With the bouton path near the connectome's share, what a part of the APL→KC weights made of counted synapses lacks for holding the mean APL effect is amounts that are nearly equal among KCs with the same number of claws.

How a KC's amount grows with its number of claws carries none of the loss in these runs, and how the amount lies over the KC's claws carries little of it through the calibrated readout, a part of it on raw counts. The earlier description, which had ordered the loss by how unequal a part is from claw to claw, had mixed the inequality among KCs with the unevenness within them.

The second is what this says of the best family, and it is not that the family's bouton path is equal among such KCs. What the bouton path takes from a KC in its fit varies among KCs with the same number of claws with a coefficient of variation of {{E96/a1_counts.csv:kind=b:within_cv_min ~ .2f}} to {{E96/a1_counts.csv:kind=b:within_cv_max ~ .2f}} over the numbers of claws from 2 to 10, above the bound read here at every number of claws up to 8 ([above](#offclaw-synapses)). It holds the mean by following each KC's own loss.

Given as a static inhibition with each KC's own mean loss, the bouton path holds a mean APL effect of {{E95/readings.csv:variant=B1_bk;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}, and with the same amounts permuted among KCs with the same number of claws {{E95/readings.csv:variant=B4_bk_permclaw1;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}, {{diff:E95/readings.csv:variant=B1_bk;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect -- E95/readings.csv:variant=B4_bk_permclaw1;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ .3f}} less ([above](#static-threshold)). Two ways of holding the mean have thus been shown, amounts that are nearly equal among KCs with the same number of claws and amounts that follow what each KC loses of its drive, and the bound on the inequality is a bound for amounts of the first kind. The counted synapses are of neither kind: among such KCs the counts outside the claws do not go with what the bouton path takes, the median correlation being {{E96/a1_counts.csv:kind=no_claw:within_r_b_median ~ .2f}}.

For the choice, still to be made, of whether a limit on the bouton share replaces the bound on the APL→bouton scale, no price is changed. With counted weights it stays {{diff:E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}} of the pattern part after a refit, with a mean APL effect of {{E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} for the flies' {{data:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}} ([above](#offclaw-synapses)); what is added is why the mean goes with it, and nothing here makes the choice.

The third is two leads for planning, and neither has been run. One is whether a quantity that the anatomy defines for each KC gives an inhibition that is nearly equal among KCs with the same number of claws, or that follows the KC's own input, as a count of APL's synapses does not: the KC's total input, for one, or where APL's synapses lie relative to the place where the KC's spikes start, which the model does not represent. The other is the same readings with the counts of another connectome, which is now the male CNS alone ([footnote](#fn-derived-tables)); what its tables allow is said with the pending work at the end of the page.

The limits are those of runs at fixed scales. One factor was set again on four wirings and every other parameter left at the fit's; no setting met the condition for a refit, so that none was made, and nothing was read on the four held-out wirings. The shares are of the mean over four wirings, and the verdict on the weights on the claws is the calibrated readout's and not that of raw counts.

The bound on the inequality is a line through two settings of one kind of count. And the two descriptions that were written down beforehand had been fitted to seven saved means, five of them from one family of parts, so that their failure on the weights on the claws is a finding about those descriptions and not about the runs. Every reading here is of the model's 0.5 s pulse without trial noise, in the family without a firing ceiling.

### The flies' APL against their KC claws in the dual-colour recordings: whether APL's response is one function of the claws' response, how APL and the claws change across three odors and along concentration against the best family, and whether APL's calcium follows the claws place by place {#apl-vs-claws}

**In the only recordings in which APL and the KCs' dendrites in the calyx, their claws, were imaged together, the two channels hold what they were taken to hold, and what the recordings were read for is not decided.** A little of APL's green signal appears in the red channel of the KCs, and the size of that leak, measured in the two flies in which only APL carried an indicator, does not carry from one of them to the other.

By the rule fixed beforehand, every reading of the KC channel with the leak taken out is then not decided, and with it whether APL's response is one function of the claws' response and whether APL's calcium follows the claws place by place; what is reported is how strongly the APL channel responds. There the flies' APL responds several times as strongly to pa as to ms, where the best family's APL responds about a quarter more strongly to pa than to ms.

By the rule fixed beforehand the family is still inside the flies' interval, which is wide, through the steepest readings of the indicator and one estimate of ms's input; read in proportion it is flatter than the flies under every estimate. On the model's side that flatness is not made by APL. The family's APL follows the summed input to its claws, with APL on and with APL off, and the claws follow the PNs' summed response, which is nearly the same for pa and ms with the lab's input; with Hallem's receptor data as the input the same fits separate the two odors two to three times.

Within a fly, APL rises faster than the KC channel from ms to pa and along concentration, and in five of the seven flies APL's map follows the KC channel's place by place, as recorded and with the leak taken out; both are leads and not results, since both rest on the KC channel. The experimenter who made the recordings has not yet checked their quality. No model is changed, and nothing is scored on the main target.

The best family assumes two things about APL that a recording of APL alone cannot test: that APL is driven by the summed input to the KCs' claws, and that one APL variable serves the whole calyx. In its fits APL's activity is nearly the same for every odor of the panel ([APL's inhibition as a static threshold raise per KC](#static-threshold)).

Of two comparisons of that activity with the flies' own APL, one has since found the model's APL flatter than the flies' along concentration ([the strength of APL's response in the flies against the model's APL](#apl-strength), the next subsection) and one, at weak odors, has since read inside the flies' interval by its rule and flatter when read in proportion ([the flies' APL at the weak odors and at the panel's concentrations](#apl-weak-odors), at the end of this section).

For a model's APL that is flatter than the flies', two repairs stand open that those comparisons cannot tell apart: a drive of APL by the KCs' spikes ([what drives APL](#apl-drive)), or a weaker normalization in the antennal lobe ([the input side of the error common to all wirings](#input-side)). Under the first the flies' APL departs from the summed response of their claws; under the second it follows the claws, and it is the claws' own response that the model makes too even. The dual-colour recordings are the only ones that hold both sides: calcium in APL through a green indicator and in the KCs' claws through a red one, in the same plane of the same fly, with pa, paa and ms as concentration series.

The claws' own map also stands where a prediction from the wiring would: whether APL's calcium follows the activity around it had been asked only through maps predicted from where the PN boutons lie ([the APL calyx maps against the connectome](#apl-calyx-maps)), which rest on connectome tables whose use is on hold and are withheld ([footnote](#fn-derived-tables)), and here it could be asked of the flies without a connectome. The experiment changes no model and scores nothing on the main target, so that [the APL-effect loss](#apl-effect), its mean part and its pattern part stay where they are.

**What was read, and by which rules.** The verdicts rest on {{E101/a1_groups.csv:group=L:recordings ~ .0f}} recordings from {{E101/a1_groups.csv:group=L:flies ~ .0f}} flies, those that the experimenter listed as the dual-colour data; {{E101/a1_groups.csv:group=V0:recordings ~ .0f}} earlier recordings of the same kind, from {{E101/a1_groups.csv:group=V0:flies ~ .0f}} flies, are read beside them as a repetition and decide nothing.

A response is the change in fluorescence over its baseline around its peak, averaged inside the outline of the calyx, as the mean over a stimulus's presentations with the response to the solvent in the same recording subtracted. Flies are the units, a ratio of two responses is the geometric mean over the flies, and its interval is the one in which nine in ten resamplings of the flies fall. Three things were asked, each with a verdict fixed before any map was read.

- The first needs no model: whether, within a fly, APL's response is one function of the claws' summed response whatever the odor. It is read as the difference between two odors' APL responses at a matched response of the claws, and granted if the flies' interval stays within a factor of one and a half for all three pairs of odors.
- The second sets the best family against the flies in three ratios, pa over ms and paa over ms near the panel's concentration and paa one log unit below the concentration of its input over paa at that concentration, each for APL, for the claws and for APL's ratio over the claws' ratio in the same fly.
  - The model's side is the fits of the eight wirings run as they are, with nothing set again ([the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population)): its APL and the summed input to its claws, the stage that was read against recordings of claws before ([the model's stages against the flies' stages](#model-stages)), each taken as its mean during the odor minus its mean during a blank in the same run, and each read through a family of indicator nonlinearities, from one in proportion to one about as steep as the reported cooperativity of the indicator.
  - A wiring is inside a ratio if any of its readings lies in the flies' interval, for the two ratios over ms under any of the estimates of ms's input from the lab's recording sessions, and a ratio is classed when at least six of the eight wirings agree.
- The third is whether APL's calcium follows the claws place by place. The calyx is divided into squares four micrometres wide; the part of APL's map that is particular to a stimulus is taken from two of its presentations and correlated over the squares with the same part of the claws' map from its other two, which gives the agreement of the two maps as a Pearson r; and that agreement is set against what the claws' maps of other odors give.

The two colours are not perfectly separate, and that governs how all of it is read. A little of the green signal appears in the red channel, with APL's own pattern. Its size is given by {{E101/a1_groups.csv:group=G:recordings ~ .0f}} recordings from {{E101/a1_groups.csv:group=G:flies ~ .0f}} flies in which only APL carried an indicator while both channels were recorded, as the slope of the red channel on the green one. Every reading of the claws is made as recorded and again with that much of APL's map taken out, and a class counts only if both give it.

One check was fixed with it: the red channel of each of these flies, corrected with the slope of the other, has to keep no more agreement with APL's map than other odors' maps give. If one keeps more, the leak is not known well enough to be taken out: every reading of the claws with the leak taken out and the test place by place are then not decided, and only the strengths of the APL channel are reported. The model's side, which reads no recording, was made before the recordings were read.

**The channels hold what they were taken to hold.** Which channel holds which indicator had been inferred from the files and not confirmed by the experimenter, so that the controls were read for it first. In each of the {{E101/a1_groups.csv:group=G:flies ~ .0f}} flies with only APL labelled, the channel taken for APL responds, its fluorescence changing by {{lit:0.5207986505808657 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/channel_check.csv (the table opens with a caveat line, which the filler does not read, so the value is entered by hand): group G, smallest expected_response ~ .2f}} to {{lit:1.327142068371888 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/channel_check.csv (the table opens with a caveat line, which the filler does not read, so the value is entered by hand): group G, largest expected_response ~ .2f}} of its baseline at a recording's strongest stimulus, and the other channel shows {{lit:0.0180976610881667 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/channel_check.csv (the table opens with a caveat line, which the filler does not read, so the value is entered by hand): group G, smallest expected_other_fraction ~ .3f}} to {{lit:0.0437910611500149 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/channel_check.csv (the table opens with a caveat line, which the filler does not read, so the value is entered by hand): group G, largest expected_other_fraction ~ .3f}} of that response. In the {{E101/a1_groups.csv:group=R:flies ~ .0f}} flies with only the KCs labelled, the channel taken for the KCs responds, and the channel taken for APL stays under the limit set for it in {{lit:8 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/channel_check.csv (the table opens with a caveat line, which the filler does not read, so the value is entered by hand): group R, recordings classed as inferred}} of the {{lit:9 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/channel_check.csv (the table opens with a caveat line, which the filler does not read, so the value is entered by hand): group R, recordings with both channels processed}} recordings that could be evaluated and a little over it in the other. The check passed. The experimenter's own confirmation is still asked for.

**The leak does not carry from one fly to the other.** In the flies with only APL labelled the red channel holds no indicator, and what it shows is the leak. It rises with the green channel by {{lit:0.031764148858911836 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/b_leak.json: b_G_per_fly, fly 20221005_1 ~ .3f}} of it in one fly and by {{lit:0.024193122084705743 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/b_leak.json: b_G_per_fly, fly 20221217_6 ~ .3f}} in the other, {{lit:0.028261733324614166 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/b_leak.json: b_G ~ .3f}} over both. Before any correction that empty channel agrees with APL's map place by place, at {{lit:0.28621140548953733 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/b1_cross_check.csv (the table opens with a caveat line, which the filler does not read, so the value is entered by hand): fly 20221005_1, rows with b_mult 0, mean of A over its 3 recordings ~ .2f}} and {{lit:0.4710561240466492 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/b1_cross_check.csv (the table opens with a caveat line, which the filler does not read, so the value is entered by hand): fly 20221217_6, rows with b_mult 0, mean of A over its 1 recordings ~ .2f}}, about as well as the red channel of the dual-colour flies does ({{lit:0.2973878349480683 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/score_x3_flies.csv (the table opens with a caveat line, which the filler does not read, so the value is entered by hand): reading carrying, b_mult 0, smallest A over the 7 flies ~ .2f}} to {{lit:0.4894939422072601 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/score_x3_flies.csv (the table opens with a caveat line, which the filler does not read, so the value is entered by hand): reading carrying, b_mult 0, largest A over the 7 flies ~ .2f}} over the {{lit:7 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/verdict.json: X3, by_reading, carrying, n_flies}} flies). An agreement between the two channels therefore shows nothing by itself, and how much of it is the claws rests on the size of the leak.

Corrected with the larger slope, the red channel of the fly with the smaller one keeps no agreement ({{lit:-0.0873379079123435 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/b1_cross_check.csv (the table opens with a caveat line, which the filler does not read, so the value is entered by hand): fly 20221217_6, rows with the other fly slope, mean of A over 1 recordings ~ .3f}}, against the {{lit:0.0634420292654498 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/b1_cross_check.csv (the table opens with a caveat line, which the filler does not read, so the value is entered by hand): fly 20221217_6, rows with the other fly slope, mean of null_pct over 1 recordings ~ .3f}} that other odors' maps give, from its one recording that could be evaluated). Corrected with the smaller slope, that of the fly with the larger one keeps {{lit:0.07047761440449977 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/b1_cross_check.csv (the table opens with a caveat line, which the filler does not read, so the value is entered by hand): fly 20221005_1, rows with the other fly slope, mean of A over 3 recordings ~ .3f}} against {{lit:0.02908519708058523 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/b1_cross_check.csv (the table opens with a caveat line, which the filler does not read, so the value is entered by hand): fly 20221005_1, rows with the other fly slope, mean of null_pct over 3 recordings ~ .3f}}, a remainder with APL's pattern.

The slope that two flies give thus does not carry between them, and by the rule the leak cannot be taken out of the dual-colour flies' red channel with it. That channel does hold more than the leak: its own slope on the APL channel is {{lit:0.10654276093148012 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/b_leak.json: set_l_median_slope ~ .3f}} at the median fly, well above the leak's. How much of one of its maps is the claws and how much is APL cannot be said from these recordings.

**What the rule leaves undecided.** Whether APL is one function of the claws is not decided: as recorded, the flies' interval for pa against ms crosses the bound of a factor of one and a half, and with the leak taken out the rule applies.

Of the three ratios, the family's claws are inside the flies' intervals on all three as recorded, and its ratio of APL over the claws on two of them, being more even than the flies' on the third; with the leak taken out neither is decided, by the rule. APL's own ratios do not depend on the KC channel and are taken up next.

Place by place, {{lit:5 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/verdict.json: X3, by_reading, carrying, n_pass_0_bg}} of the {{lit:7 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/verdict.json: X3, by_reading, carrying, n_flies}} flies pass both as recorded and with the leak taken out, all of the flies whose maps had not been opened when the rules were fixed among them, and none fails. That would have read as APL following the claws but for the failed check, and it would not have been held in any case: under the two other ways of taking a response that the rule asks to agree, against the solvent of the same block and from the first two presentations alone, {{lit:2 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/verdict.json: X3, by_reading, block, n_pass_0_bg}} and {{lit:4 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/verdict.json: X3, by_reading, first_two, n_pass_0_bg}} flies pass. These readings are leads.

**How strongly the flies' APL responds, which is what stands.** The APL channel is not touched by the leak.

The APL channel's three ratios in the flies and in the best family. Flies: the geometric mean over the flies of the dual-colour recordings, with the interval over resampled flies and the number of flies in parentheses; pa over ms is given for the two concentrations of pa that were imaged within one log unit of the panel's, 10^-3.8 and 10^-2, and paa over ms for paa at 10^-4 and at 10^-3, with ms read at 10^-3 between its two imaged neighbours and one interval spanning both. With the lab's input and the indicator read in proportion, the family's APL responds {{E101/a3_x2_summary.csv:wiring=M2;ratio_id=r1;estimate=ms;baseline=blank:apl_linear ~ .2f}} to {{E101/a3_x2_summary.csv:wiring=real;ratio_id=r1;estimate=ms;baseline=blank:apl_linear ~ .2f}} times as strongly to pa as to ms on the eight wirings, and {{E101/a3_x2_summary.csv:wiring=M2;ratio_id=r1;estimate=ms [kiwi-control/control] @ -3;baseline=blank:apl_linear ~ .2f}} to {{E101/a3_x2_summary.csv:wiring=real;ratio_id=r1;estimate=ms [kiwi-control/diag] @ -3;baseline=blank:apl_linear ~ .2f}} times over every estimate of ms's input, below the flies' interval in each case.

The rule fixed beforehand is more lenient, and by it the family is inside the flies' interval on all three ratios, in every reading of the flies' side. For pa over ms it is inside through the steepest readings of the indicator and under one session's estimate of ms's input; with the input that the model uses, {{lit:4 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/verdict.json: X2, lines, APL, the carrying reading, r1 with the panel ms input, wirings inside}} of the eight wirings are inside and {{lit:4 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/verdict.json: X2, lines, APL, the carrying reading, r1 with the panel ms input, wirings flatter}} flatter. What stands is a description and not a class. In these flies APL separates pa from ms several times, and a model whose APL separates them by about a quarter matches that only through an indicator that exaggerates differences: with the input that the model uses, only at about the steepest reading that the indicator's cooperativity allows, and then on half of the wirings. The description is of flies recorded in 2022, and each of its ratios comes from one pair of vials a day.

Two series of 2021 have since been read for pa against ms, one of them held out from every rule: there the flies' APL responds {{E103/b_x1.csv:series_reading=carrying;ratio_id=Q1:ratio_ref ~ .2f}} to {{E103/b_x1.csv:series_reading=carrying;ratio_id=Q2:ratio ~ .2f}} times as strongly to pa as to ms, at lower concentrations, and two vials of one odor differ by enough that a ratio between two odors read from one pair of vials is known to no better than a factor of about one and a half. The recordings of 2021 and of 2022 differ about ms by more than that, which is a question for the experimenter ([the flies' APL across odors in the held-out vial series](#apl-held-out)).

**In the family the flatness is made before APL.** On the model's side the question that the recordings were read for has an answer. Over the odors of the panel the family's APL is one function of the summed input to its claws: on logarithmic axes the line of APL's response on the claws' has a slope of {{E101/a2_blank_lines.csv:wiring=P2;level=blank;subset=input;share=0.0;odor=pa:slope_rma ~ .2f}} to {{E101/a2_blank_lines.csv:wiring=real;level=blank;subset=input;share=0.0;odor=pa:slope_rma ~ .2f}} and a Pearson r of {{E101/a2_blank_lines.csv:wiring=M2;level=blank;subset=input;share=0.0;odor=pa:r ~ .2f}} to {{E101/a2_blank_lines.csv:wiring=M3;level=blank;subset=input;share=0.0;odor=pa:r ~ .2f}} on the eight wirings.

How far the best family's APL, the summed input to its claws and its PNs separate two stimuli, with the flies' two channels beside. Family: the ratio of the responses to the two stimuli, each taken against the blank of the same run and read in proportion, as the range over the eight wirings; the PNs' summed response is the same on every wiring. The family's APL separates two stimuli as its claws do and no further: APL's ratio over the claws' ratio stays near one in every row of the model. It does so with APL off as well, each run read against its own blank, so that it is not APL's own inhibition that makes the claws even.

The claws in turn follow the PNs' summed response, which the model's antennal lobe returns nearly equal for pa and ms with the lab's input, although the ORN inputs of the two odors differ widely in total; over the odors of the stage recordings the coefficient of variation of the PNs' summed response, its standard deviation as a share of its mean, is {{E90/pn_stage.csv:reading=change:cv_totals ~ .3f}} in the model and {{E90/pn_stage.csv:reading=pn_dend:cv_totals ~ .3f}} in the flies' PN dendrites ([the model's stages against the flies' stages](#model-stages)). With Hallem's receptor data for the two odors as the input, through the same antennal lobe and the same fits, the PNs' summed responses differ more than threefold, and the family's APL separates pa from ms {{E101/c4_hallem_ratios.csv:wiring=M1;series=pa over ms;log10_conc=-4.0;cond=on;quantity=APL:linear ~ .2f}} to {{E101/c4_hallem_ratios.csv:wiring=real;series=pa over ms;log10_conc=-2.0;cond=on;quantity=APL:linear ~ .2f}} times, inside the interval of the flies' APL channel when read in proportion.

The family's flat APL is thus set by what the model is given at its claws, in the input and in the antennal lobe, and no change in what drives APL is needed to make it less flat. Hallem's data come from another laboratory's odor delivery at nominal dilutions and cover a part of the model's glomeruli, so that this shows where the flatness is set and is not an estimate of the flies' input ([Hallem's receptor data as the weak odors' input](#hallem-input)).

**Leads, not results.** Three readings rest on the KC channel and stay leads until the leak is measured. Within a fly, APL rises faster than the KC channel. From ms to pa, APL's ratio over the KC channel's is {{lit:2.38 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/c_x2_flies.csv (the table opens with a caveat line, which the filler does not read, so the value is entered by hand): row flies=L, reading=carrying, b_mult=0, ratio_id=r1, quantity=Q; column readings, the point estimate at pa @ -2, as printed there ~ .2f}} to {{lit:2.41 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/c_x2_flies.csv (the table opens with a caveat line, which the filler does not read, so the value is entered by hand): row flies=L, reading=carrying, b_mult=0, ratio_id=r1, quantity=Q; column readings, the point estimate at pa @ -3.806, as printed there ~ .2f}} as recorded ({{lit:1.2606260584921656 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/c_x2_flies.csv (the table opens with a caveat line, which the filler does not read, so the value is entered by hand): row flies=L, reading=carrying, b_mult=0, ratio_id=r1, quantity=Q; column lo ~ .2f}} to {{lit:4.592505322190588 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/c_x2_flies.csv (the table opens with a caveat line, which the filler does not read, so the value is entered by hand): row flies=L, reading=carrying, b_mult=0, ratio_id=r1, quantity=Q; column hi ~ .2f}}; {{lit:6 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/c_x2_flies.csv (the table opens with a caveat line, which the filler does not read, so the value is entered by hand): row flies=L, reading=carrying, b_mult=0, ratio_id=r1, quantity=Q; column n_flies}} flies), where the family's is {{E101/c4_apl_off.csv:wiring=P2;ratio_id=r1;estimate=ms;cond=on;quantity=Q;subset=input:linear ~ .2f}} to {{E101/c4_apl_off.csv:wiring=real;ratio_id=r1;estimate=ms;cond=on;quantity=Q;subset=input:linear ~ .2f}}. Over the log unit of paa it is {{lit:0.602 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/c_x2_flies.csv (the table opens with a caveat line, which the filler does not read, so the value is entered by hand): row flies=L, reading=carrying, b_mult=0, ratio_id=r3, quantity=Q; column readings, the point estimate at paa @ -5, as printed there ~ .2f}} as recorded ({{lit:0.5481817388689122 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/c_x2_flies.csv (the table opens with a caveat line, which the filler does not read, so the value is entered by hand): row flies=L, reading=carrying, b_mult=0, ratio_id=r3, quantity=Q; column lo ~ .2f}} to {{lit:0.6600076165019609 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/c_x2_flies.csv (the table opens with a caveat line, which the filler does not read, so the value is entered by hand): row flies=L, reading=carrying, b_mult=0, ratio_id=r3, quantity=Q; column hi ~ .2f}}; {{lit:4 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/c_x2_flies.csv (the table opens with a caveat line, which the filler does not read, so the value is entered by hand): row flies=L, reading=carrying, b_mult=0, ratio_id=r3, quantity=Q; column n_flies}} flies) and {{lit:0.563 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/c_x2_flies.csv (the table opens with a caveat line, which the filler does not read, so the value is entered by hand): row flies=L, reading=carrying, b_mult=1, ratio_id=r3, quantity=Q; column readings, the point estimate at paa @ -5, as printed there ~ .2f}} with the leak taken out, where the family's is {{E101/c4_apl_off.csv:wiring=P3;ratio_id=r3;estimate=paa [validation2/diag] @ -5;cond=on;quantity=Q;subset=input:linear ~ .2f}} to {{E101/c4_apl_off.csv:wiring=real;ratio_id=r3;estimate=paa [validation2/diag] @ -5;cond=on;quantity=Q;subset=input:linear ~ .2f}}, more even than the flies' on all eight wirings as recorded.

A leak of APL into the KC channel can only pull the two channels' ratios together, so that these departures would be underestimates if the leak were all that the red channel holds besides the claws; what else it holds is not known. If they stand once the leak is measured, the flies' APL is steeper than their own claws, which would point to what drives APL, towards the KCs' spikes, and not only to the input.

Place by place, the agreement between the two channels is {{lit:0.2858914440974773 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/score_x3_flies.csv (the table opens with a caveat line, which the filler does not read, so the value is entered by hand): reading carrying, b_mult 1, smallest A over the 7 flies ~ .2f}} to {{lit:0.4216921593350377 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/score_x3_flies.csv (the table opens with a caveat line, which the filler does not read, so the value is entered by hand): reading carrying, b_mult 1, largest A over the 7 flies ~ .2f}} over the {{lit:7 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/verdict.json: X3, by_reading, carrying, n_flies}} flies with the leak taken out, and {{lit:4 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/verdict.json: X3, by_reading, carrying, n_pass_0_bg_2bg}} of the flies that pass still pass with twice the leak taken out. And as recorded, the question of one function has its intervals within the bound for two of the three pairs of odors.

**Limits.**

- The quality of the recordings has not been checked by the experimenter who made them, and no recording was left out.
- Which channel holds which indicator is inferred and borne out by the controls, not confirmed.
- The size of the leak rests on {{E101/a1_groups.csv:group=G:flies ~ .0f}} flies and {{E101/a1_groups.csv:group=G:recordings ~ .0f}} recordings.
- Whether the red channel is aligned with the green one pixel for pixel is not confirmed, which bears on the test place by place and not on the strengths.
- The concentrations are nominal dilutions, delivered by another olfactometer than that of the ORN recordings.
- paa enters the model with ORN input one log unit below the flies' concentration, as everywhere ([ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations)), which affects the two ratios with paa.
- The concentrations rose through each recording, so that a ratio along concentration is also one of earlier over later presentations.
- A square of a map is not a claw, one plane holds a part of the claws, and what calcium in one plane of APL is of the model's single APL variable is not known.

**Realism.** No model was changed or fitted. The fits of the eight wirings are read as saved, every run giving its saved spike counts again, and all eight are inside the four realism bands.

What the experiment adds is a description of that family beside the bands: read in proportion, its APL is more even across pa and ms than the flies' APL channel, while its KCs are less even than the flies' KCs. With APL on, {{E101/a3_family.csv:wiring=real;cond=on;stimulus=pa:kc_rate ~ .3f}} to {{E101/a3_family.csv:wiring=P1;cond=on;stimulus=pa:kc_rate ~ .3f}} of the family's KCs respond to pa and {{E101/a3_family.csv:wiring=P2;cond=on;stimulus=ms:kc_rate ~ .3f}} to {{E101/a3_family.csv:wiring=P4;cond=on;stimulus=ms:kc_rate ~ .3f}} to ms, where {{data:noise_ctrl_frac_pa ~ .3f}} and {{data:noise_ctrl_frac_ms ~ .3f}} of the control flies' KCs do: too few of the model's KCs respond to ms, one of the weak-input odors.

**What follows.** Nothing is gained or lost on the main target, and no base, bound or reference family is changed. Four things are carried from here.

- The first is a request and not an experiment. The experimenter who made the recordings is asked for images of the baseline of both channels in each recording, from which each recording's own leak between the colours is measured, for the confirmation of which channel holds which indicator and of the alignment of the two channels, and for the check of the recordings' quality. With a leak measured for each recording, every reading of the KC channel and the three verdicts are made again by the rules already fixed.
- The second is for the two comparisons of APL's strength, both of which have been completed since ([the next subsection](#apl-strength); [the flies' APL at the weak odors and at the panel's concentrations](#apl-weak-odors)): in other flies than theirs, and with pa within one log unit of the model's input, the flies' APL separates pa from ms several times and falls further over the log unit of paa than the family's read in proportion, and the family comes inside the flies' intervals through the indicator family or through another session's estimate of the input. Their verdicts are their own and are not anticipated here.
- The third concerns the two repairs of a flat APL. On the model's side the flatness is set before APL, so that a less even input, or a weaker normalization in the antennal lobe, would carry through to the family's APL with no change in what drives it. On the flies' side the leads say that their APL is also steeper than their own KC channel, which would ask for a change in what drives APL as well. Which of the two the flies' steeper APL asks for is what the leak leaves open, and neither is proposed here.
- The fourth is that whether a part of APL's activity is local stays open: the test against the claws' own map, the one test of it that needs no connectome, is not decided, and the readings against maps predicted from the derived connectome tables stay withheld ([footnote](#fn-derived-tables)). The same test made again on three calyces of the hemibrain and the male CNS reads on no pair of odors, the calyces not predicting one another's maps well enough for a single plane ([the flies' APL at the weak odors and at the panel's concentrations](#apl-weak-odors)).
  - What such a test is about has since been measured in recordings of APL alone: the part of APL's map that is a stimulus's own returns with another vial of the same odor in another block of presentations, and not with another odor, so that it is the odor's and not the block's ([the flies' APL across odors in the held-out vial series](#apl-held-out)).

**Read since, in flies without the leak.** Which repair the flies' steeper APL asks for has been put to flies of 2022 in which the KCs alone carry an indicator ([the flies' KCs beside their APL along concentration](#kc-calyx-vs-apl)). There APL falls further with concentration than the KCs' calyx signal on every fall read, by less than in the dual-colour flies, and by the rules fixed beforehand that is not decided. Across odors the KCs separate pa from ms as far as the APL of that year does. Over the log unit of paa their signal falls about as far as the APL of the strength comparison.

### The strength of APL's response in the flies against the model's APL: whether the best family's APL responds as the flies' APL does along concentration and across odors, and which recordings would tell a nearly even APL from one that follows the KCs' response {#apl-strength}

**Along concentration the best family's APL is flatter than the flies' APL.** From paa at 10^-4 to paa at 10^-5 the flies' APL falls to about half of its response, and the family's falls by about a tenth. The family is flatter on all eight wirings, under every reading that the measurement leaves open, and whether the concentrations rose through a recording or came in shuffled order.

Across odors near the panel's concentration, for paa against ms, the flies' APL responds about equally to the two and the family's, with the ms input that the model uses, a fifth to a third more strongly to paa. There the class turns on which of five estimates of ms's ORN input the model is given, and by the rule fixed beforehand, under which one estimate suffices, the family is inside.

Of the changes read beside the verdict on the real wiring, only a weaker normalization in the model's antennal lobe moves the fall along concentration towards the flies', and it moves the family away from the flies across odors. In further recordings of the same series, whose quality the experimenter who made them has not checked, the verdict along concentration is repeated at the two deeper planes and rests on how steep the indicator is taken to be elsewhere.

A later series of the same genotype, held out from every rule and read since, responds more strongly to paa than to ms and holds the family inside its flies' interval under every estimate of ms's input, so that across odors the reading depends on the series ([the flies' APL across odors in the held-out vial series](#apl-held-out)). No model is changed, and nothing is scored on the main target.

**Read since, in recordings of the KCs alone.** The verdict along concentration stands, and three things change how it is read ([the flies' KCs beside their APL along concentration](#kc-calyx-vs-apl)). The calyx signal of the flies' KCs falls to {{E104/a2_falls.csv:reading=carrying;fall=G1:kc ~ .2f}} over the same step, as far as the APL of these recordings, so that the fall is not shown to be APL's own. The family's claws are too flat as its APL is, read in proportion under each of the three estimates of paa's input at 10^-5. And at three weak odors the flies' KCs do not ask for an APL weaker than the family's.

In the best family's fits APL's own activity is nearly the same for every odor of the panel, and a large part of it is there without an odor. On the eight wirings on which the family has been fitted ([the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population)) it varies over the 16 odors by {{E98/a4_profile_carrying.csv:wiring=P2:a_cv ~ .1%}} to {{E98/a4_profile_carrying.csv:wiring=real:a_cv ~ .1%}} of its mean; {{E98/a4_profile_carrying.csv:wiring=P3:a0_share ~ .0%}} to {{E98/a4_profile_carrying.csv:wiring=real:a0_share ~ .0%}} of its mean during an odor is the level that it holds during a blank; and what an odor adds to that level varies by {{E98/a4_profile_carrying.csv:wiring=P2:evoked_cv ~ .1%}} to {{E98/a4_profile_carrying.csv:wiring=real:evoked_cv ~ .1%}}, with ms adding the least on every wiring, {{E98/a4_profile_carrying.csv:wiring=real:ms_over_mean ~ .2f}} to {{E98/a4_profile_carrying.csv:wiring=M1:ms_over_mean ~ .2f}} of the mean over the odors.

For the main target such an APL is close to a fixed raise of each KC's threshold ([APL's inhibition as a static threshold raise per KC](#static-threshold)), where the flies' own KC responses ask for an inhibition that grows with an odor's response over all KCs ([the form of APL's inhibition in the flies' own responses](#inhibition-form)), and the evenness is made before APL, by an antennal lobe that returns the odors' total drive nearly equal ([the model's stages against the flies' stages](#model-stages)).

APL's activity is the one variable of the model's inhibition that has been imaged directly, as calcium in APL in one plane through the calyx: {{E98/a3_ratios.csv:ratio_id=V2;reading=order_matched;subset=all:n_recordings ~ .0f}} recordings from {{E98/a3_ratios.csv:ratio_id=V2;reading=order_matched;subset=all:n_flies ~ .0f}} flies, each with pa, paa and ms as concentration series. Those maps had been read for where APL responds ([the APL calyx maps against the connectome](#apl-calyx-maps)); here they are read for how strongly. The experiment changes no model and scores nothing on the main target, so that [the APL-effect loss](#apl-effect), its mean part and its pattern part stay where they are.

**What was read, and by which rules.** On the flies' side a response is the change in fluorescence over its baseline around its peak, averaged inside the outline of the calyx, with each presentation taken against the presentation of the solvent at the same place in its block, as the mean of a stimulus's two presentations.

Two stimuli are compared as a ratio within a recording. The flies' ratio is the geometric mean over the flies, a fly's recordings averaged first, with the interval in which nine in ten resamplings of the flies fall, and a concentration that was not imaged is read between its two imaged neighbours on the logarithm of the concentration, inside the recording's imaged range.

On the model's side the fits of the eight wirings are run again as they are, with nothing set again, on a longer list of stimuli, and every run gives its saved spike counts on the panel's odors again without one differing. The model's response is APL's mean activity while the odor is on minus its mean during a blank in the same run, the counterpart of what a change in fluorescence leaves out.

The indicator need not report APL's activity in proportion, so that the model's ratio is read through a family of indicator nonlinearities, from one in proportion to one about as steep as the reported cooperativity of the indicator, each in two forms: with the level without an odor inside the indicator's baseline, and with only what the odor adds seen.

A wiring is inside a comparison if any of its readings lies in the flies' interval, flatter if all of them are nearer to one than the interval or on the other side of one, and steeper if all lie beyond the interval's far end. A comparison takes a class when at least six of the eight wirings agree, and the class is held only if every reading that the measurement leaves open gives it, among them another way of taking the baseline from the solvent presentations, the recordings without three that had been set apart, and the model read against its level just before the odor in place of the blank's.

Two comparisons carry the verdict, both fixed beforehand and both with the lab's input. Along concentration it is paa at 10^-5 over paa at 10^-4, the concentration of paa's ORN input, with the input at 10^-5 taken from the ORN recordings of the flies in which the input at 10^-4 was recorded.

Across odors it is paa over ms at 10^-3. There the flies' interval spans both readings of paa's concentration, the 10^-4 at which its ORN input was recorded and the maps' concentration nearest the 10^-3 of the KC recordings, for which that input stands in ([ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations)), and the model is read under each estimate of ms's input that the lab's ORN recordings hold. Those recordings were made in three sessions, each in its own flies: that of the megamat panel, from which the model's ms input comes, that of the validation2 panel, from which its paa input comes, and one of two mixture panels.

Each session also recorded a set of diagnostic odors, among them ms at 10^-3 and paa at 10^-5, and the control panel of the mixture session holds ms at 10^-3 as well, which gives five estimates of ms's input and three of paa's input at 10^-5. Across odors the family counts as inside if inside is held under any of the five, and as outside only if flatter or steeper is held under all of them.

Ratios of APL's response to two stimuli in the flies and in the best family. Flies: the geometric mean over the flies, with the interval over resampled flies and the number of flies in parentheses; for paa over ms the two means are for paa at 10^-4 and for paa at the maps' concentration nearest 10^-3, and the one interval spans both. Family: the range over the eight wirings with the indicator read in proportion, the range over every reading of the indicator, and how many of the eight wirings are inside the flies' interval, flatter and steeper.

The first row carries the verdict along concentration. The second is its check on the order of the concentrations, in recordings whose quality the experimenter who made them has not checked. The third and fourth take paa's input at 10^-5 from the other two sessions and decide nothing. The last five carry the verdict across odors

**Along concentration the family is flatter, in both orders.** The flies' APL grows with concentration in all three odors, by a factor of {{E98/a2_fly_summary.csv:odor=ms;reading=order_matched:fold_per_log_unit ~ .2f}} per log unit for ms, {{E98/a2_fly_summary.csv:odor=pa;reading=order_matched:fold_per_log_unit ~ .2f}} for pa and {{E98/a2_fly_summary.csv:odor=paa;reading=order_matched:fold_per_log_unit ~ .2f}} for paa over the imaged ranges. From paa at 10^-4 to paa at 10^-5 it falls to {{E98/a3_ratios.csv:ratio_id=V2;reading=order_matched;subset=all:ratio ~ .2f}} of its response, where the family's APL falls to {{E98/comparison_table.csv:comparison=V2, paa at 10^-5 from validation2/diag:model_linear_min ~ .2f}} to {{E98/comparison_table.csv:comparison=V2, paa at 10^-5 from validation2/diag:model_linear_max ~ .2f}} read in proportion; through the steepest reading of the indicator on the steepest wiring it reaches {{E98/comparison_table.csv:comparison=V2, paa at 10^-5 from validation2/diag:model_min ~ .2f}}, still above the flies' interval, which ends at {{E98/comparison_table.csv:comparison=V2, paa at 10^-5 from validation2/diag:flies_hi90 ~ .2f}}. All eight wirings are flatter under every reading of the flies' side and of the model's level without an odor, so that the class is held.

In all but one of the verdict's recordings the concentrations rose through the recording, so that the ratio is also one of an earlier over a later presentation. That order does not make the flies' fall.

In {{E98/d1_v2r.csv:reading=carrying:n_recordings ~ .0f}} further recordings, from {{E98/d1_v2r.csv:reading=carrying:n_flies ~ .0f}} flies, the concentrations came in shuffled order, and there the flies' APL falls further (second row); the family is flatter on all eight wirings again, and stays so with each of those flies left out in turn (the flies' ratio is then {{E98/d1_v2r.csv:reading=carrying, without 2021-08-23_fly4:ratio ~ .2f}} to {{E98/d1_v2r.csv:reading=carrying, without 2021-07-16_fly1:ratio ~ .2f}}). Within the flies that were recorded in both orders, a lower concentration that comes later gives a slightly lower ratio, so that the rising order, if anything, hides a little of the fall.

The recordings at the model's pulse length and those at twice that length differ in neither comparison by more than splits of the flies at random commonly give. Other flies give a fall of the same size or larger: in the dual-colour recordings the interval of the same ratio is {{E101/c_x2_flies.csv:flies=L;reading=carrying;b_mult=0.0;ratio_id=r3;quantity=APL:lo ~ .2f}} to {{E101/c_x2_flies.csv:flies=L;reading=carrying;b_mult=0.0;ratio_id=r3;quantity=APL:hi ~ .2f}} ({{E101/c_x2_flies.csv:flies=L;reading=carrying;b_mult=0.0;ratio_id=r3;quantity=APL:n_flies ~ .0f}} flies) and in the earlier recordings of that kind {{E101/c_x2_flies.csv:flies=V0;reading=carrying;b_mult=0.0;ratio_id=r3;quantity=APL:lo ~ .2f}} to {{E101/c_x2_flies.csv:flies=V0;reading=carrying;b_mult=0.0;ratio_id=r3;quantity=APL:hi ~ .2f}} ({{E101/c_x2_flies.csv:flies=V0;reading=carrying;b_mult=0.0;ratio_id=r3;quantity=APL:n_flies ~ .0f}} flies), and the family read in proportion lies above both ([above](#apl-vs-claws)).

The verdict rests on one session's estimate of paa's input at 10^-5, the one from the flies in which paa's input at 10^-4 was recorded. With the other two sessions' estimates (third and fourth rows) the family's APL falls further: it is inside the flies' interval through the steeper readings of the indicator, and still flatter when read in proportion.

**Across odors the class turns on the estimate of ms's input.** Near the panel's concentration the flies' APL responds about equally to paa and to ms: the ratio is {{E98/a3_ratios.csv:ratio_id=V1_paa-4;reading=order_matched;subset=all:ratio ~ .2f}} ({{E98/a3_ratios.csv:ratio_id=V1_paa-4;reading=order_matched;subset=all:lo90 ~ .2f}} to {{E98/a3_ratios.csv:ratio_id=V1_paa-4;reading=order_matched;subset=all:hi90 ~ .2f}}) for paa at 10^-4 and {{E98/a3_ratios.csv:ratio_id=V1_paa-2.954;reading=order_matched;subset=all:ratio ~ .2f}} ({{E98/a3_ratios.csv:ratio_id=V1_paa-2.954;reading=order_matched;subset=all:lo90 ~ .2f}} to {{E98/a3_ratios.csv:ratio_id=V1_paa-2.954;reading=order_matched;subset=all:hi90 ~ .2f}}) for paa at the maps' concentration nearest 10^-3.

With the ms input that the model uses, the family's APL responds {{E98/comparison_table.csv:numerator=paa;denominator=ms:model_linear_min ~ .2f}} to {{E98/comparison_table.csv:numerator=paa;denominator=ms:model_linear_max ~ .2f}} times as strongly to paa as to ms when read in proportion, which is at the upper end of the flies' interval: {{E98/comparison_table.csv:numerator=paa;denominator=ms:n_inside ~ .0f}} wirings are inside and {{E98/comparison_table.csv:numerator=paa;denominator=ms:n_steeper ~ .0f}} steeper, the eight lying within {{E98/comparison_table.csv:numerator=paa;denominator=ms:M1_linear_minus_nearer_end ~ +.2f}} to {{E98/comparison_table.csv:numerator=paa;denominator=ms:real_linear_minus_nearer_end ~ +.2f}} of that end, and the other readings of the flies' side move single wirings across it. Nothing is decided there, nor with the estimates from the diagnostic odors of the megamat and the validation2 sessions.

The five estimates of ms's input differ more than twofold in their total over the glomeruli, from {{lit:501 # data/model_outputs/E98_apl_response_strength/B/B1/b1_stimuli.csv (the model-output archive, which the filler does not read): input_total of the stimulus ms [kiwi-control/diag] @ -3, 500.82}} to {{lit:1177 # data/model_outputs/E98_apl_response_strength/B/B1/b1_stimuli.csv (the model-output archive, which the filler does not read): input_total of the stimulus ms [kiwi-control/control] @ -3, 1177.36}} in the units of the model's input, where the one that the model uses has {{lit:747 # data/model_outputs/E98_apl_response_strength/B/B1/b1_stimuli.csv (the model-output archive, which the filler does not read): input_total of the stimulus ms, the megamat panel's, 747.19}}. With the largest, from the control panel of the mixture session, the family is inside on all eight wirings and under every reading; with the smallest, from that session's diagnostic odors, it is steeper on all eight. By the rule fixed beforehand the family is therefore inside across odors. That class says more about the input than about APL, and it joins the choice of the base model's input, which is still to be made ([the measured input for the glomeruli without ORN input](#missing-glomeruli)).

On the flies' side the comparison has since been read again, in a held-out series of the same genotype ([the flies' APL across odors in the held-out vial series](#apl-held-out)). There paa at 10^-4 evokes {{E103/b_x1.csv:series_reading=carrying;ratio_id=P1:ratio ~ .2f}} times the response to ms at 10^-3 ({{E103/b_x1.csv:series_reading=carrying;ratio_id=P1:lo90 ~ .2f}} to {{E103/b_x1.csv:series_reading=carrying;ratio_id=P1:hi90 ~ .2f}}), the family is inside the flies' interval on all eight wirings under each of the five estimates, and the difference between the two series is within what two vials of one odor make.

![Every comparison of the verdict and those read beside it: the flies' interval (grey bar), the best family's ratio read in proportion on each of the eight wirings (dots) and its range over every reading of the indicator (line), with the class at the right and, for the comparisons that decide, the held class in parentheses. Top, the lab's input: paa over ms near 10^-3 under each estimate of ms's input (megamat/megamat is the megamat panel, the input that the model uses; diag stands for a session's diagnostic odors, kiwi-control for the mixture session and kiwi-control/control for its control panel), then paa at 10^-5 over paa at 10^-4 with the validation2 session's estimate of the input at 10^-5, which carries the verdict, and with the other two sessions' estimates. Bottom, Hallem's receptor data as the input, which decide nothing: ms and pa along concentration and the odors against each other at equal concentration, with the flies' values taken at the nearest imaged concentration where one was not imaged.](results/E98_apl_response_strength/E98_verdict.png)

**With Hallem's receptor data as the input the family's APL is not flat.** Beside the verdict, and deciding nothing, the same fits were run on the concentration series of pa and ms in [Hallem's receptor data](#hallem-input). There the family's ratios fall on both sides of the flies' (figure, bottom).

- From pa at 10^-4 to pa at 10^-6, where Hallem's input falls to {{lit:0.17 # data/model_outputs/E98_apl_response_strength/B/B1/b1_stimuli.csv (the model-output archive, which the filler does not read): input_total of pa [hallem] @ -6 over that of pa [hallem] @ -4, 111 / 665 = 0.167}} of its total, the family's APL falls to {{E98/comparison_table.csv:numerator=pa [hallem] @ -6;denominator=pa [hallem] @ -4:model_linear_min ~ .2f}} to {{E98/comparison_table.csv:numerator=pa [hallem] @ -6;denominator=pa [hallem] @ -4:model_linear_max ~ .2f}} of its response read in proportion, further than the flies' {{E98/comparison_table.csv:numerator=pa [hallem] @ -6;denominator=pa [hallem] @ -4:flies_lo90 ~ .2f}} to {{E98/comparison_table.csv:numerator=pa [hallem] @ -6;denominator=pa [hallem] @ -4:flies_hi90 ~ .2f}}.
- From ms at 10^-2 to ms at 10^-6, where the input falls to {{lit:0.29 # data/model_outputs/E98_apl_response_strength/B/B1/b1_stimuli.csv (the model-output archive, which the filler does not read): input_total of ms [hallem] @ -6 over that of ms [hallem] @ -2, 101 / 346 = 0.292}}, the family's APL falls to {{E98/comparison_table.csv:numerator=ms [hallem] @ -6;denominator=ms [hallem] @ -2:model_linear_min ~ .2f}} to {{E98/comparison_table.csv:numerator=ms [hallem] @ -6;denominator=ms [hallem] @ -2:model_linear_max ~ .2f}}, less far than the flies' {{E98/comparison_table.csv:numerator=ms [hallem] @ -6;denominator=ms [hallem] @ -2:flies_lo90 ~ .2f}} to {{E98/comparison_table.csv:numerator=ms [hallem] @ -6;denominator=ms [hallem] @ -2:flies_hi90 ~ .2f}}.

The family's APL is thus not fixed. It follows the input that it is given, through an antennal lobe and a claw stage that compress it, as the dual-colour recordings showed for pa against ms ([above](#apl-vs-claws)). Hallem's data come from another laboratory's odor delivery at nominal dilutions and cover a part of the model's glomeruli, so that these ratios say how far the family's APL follows its input and are not an estimate of the flies' input.

**What does not scale with the input.** Over the log unit of paa the lab's ORN input falls to {{lit:0.54 # data/model_outputs/E98_apl_response_strength/B/B1/b1_stimuli.csv (the model-output archive, which the filler does not read): input_total of paa [validation2/diag] @ -5 over that of paa, 608.57 / 1133.26 = 0.537}} of its total over the glomeruli, which is about the fall of the flies' APL. In the model the PNs' summed response falls only to {{E101/c4_apl_off.csv:wiring=real;ratio_id=r3;estimate=paa [validation2/diag] @ -5;cond=on;quantity=PN total:linear ~ .2f}} of its size, the summed input to the claws follows the PNs, and APL follows the claws ([the table of the dual-colour recordings](#apl-vs-claws)). The halving of the input has become a fall of about a tenth by the time it reaches the family's APL, and most of that change is made between the ORN input and the PNs, in the model's antennal lobe.

Across odors the flies' APL does not follow the input's total: with the input that the model uses, paa's total is {{E98/a5_alternatives.csv:source=input;ratio_id=paa_over_ms:ratio ~ .2f}} times ms's, where the flies' APL responds about equally to the two. An APL in proportion to the input's total would thus be inside the flies' interval along concentration and steeper than the flies across odors, and the family is flatter along concentration and at the edge of the interval across odors: neither does both.

An APL in proportion to the KC data's response rates would give {{E98/a5_alternatives.csv:kind=in proportion to the KCs' response rates, control flies (noise);ratio_id=paa_over_ms:ratio ~ .2f}} for paa over ms by the rates of the control flies and {{E98/a5_alternatives.csv:kind=in proportion to the KCs' response rates, APL output blocked (TNT) (noise);ratio_id=paa_over_ms:ratio ~ .2f}} by those with APL output blocked (TNT), inside the flies' interval. That is a lead towards a drive that follows the KCs' response, and it cannot be tested along concentration, since no recordings of the KCs' somata exist at paa at 10^-5. The KCs' signal in the calyx has since been read along that step, and falls as far as the APL of these recordings ([below](#kc-calyx-vs-apl)).

Beside the verdict, and deciding nothing: the best family on the real wiring under other settings, each run read against its own blank. Flies: the interval over resampled flies. Model: the ratio read in proportion, for the fall along concentration with the range over every reading of the indicator in parentheses. The pulse twice as long is read as the mean over that pulse
