| a weaker normalization in the antennal lobe, the third of the four steps of the earlier screen | {{E98/comparison_table_b_points.csv:point=E77_inhadd1000;comparison=V2;window=win:ratio_linear ~ .2f}} ({{E98/comparison_table_b_points.csv:point=E77_inhadd1000;comparison=V2;window=win:ratio_min ~ .2f}} to {{E98/comparison_table_b_points.csv:point=E77_inhadd1000;comparison=V2;window=win:ratio_max ~ .2f}}) | {{E98/comparison_table_b_points.csv:point=E77_inhadd1000;comparison=V1, the panel ms;window=win:ratio_linear ~ .2f}} | {{E98/comparison_table_b_points.csv:point=E77_inhadd1000;comparison=V1, kiwi-control/control ms;window=win:ratio_linear ~ .2f}} |
| a weaker normalization in the antennal lobe, the last step | {{E98/comparison_table_b_points.csv:point=E77_inhadd3141;comparison=V2;window=win:ratio_linear ~ .2f}} ({{E98/comparison_table_b_points.csv:point=E77_inhadd3141;comparison=V2;window=win:ratio_min ~ .2f}} to {{E98/comparison_table_b_points.csv:point=E77_inhadd3141;comparison=V2;window=win:ratio_max ~ .2f}}) | {{E98/comparison_table_b_points.csv:point=E77_inhadd3141;comparison=V1, the panel ms;window=win:ratio_linear ~ .2f}} | {{E98/comparison_table_b_points.csv:point=E77_inhadd3141;comparison=V1, kiwi-control/control ms;window=win:ratio_linear ~ .2f}} |

Only the weaker normalization moves the family's fall towards the flies'. Read in proportion the ratio goes from {{E98/comparison_table_b_points.csv:point=real;comparison=V2;window=win:ratio_linear ~ .2f}} to {{E98/comparison_table_b_points.csv:point=E77_inhadd1000;comparison=V2;window=win:ratio_linear ~ .2f}} and {{E98/comparison_table_b_points.csv:point=E77_inhadd3141;comparison=V2;window=win:ratio_linear ~ .2f}} at the two steps, which is still above the flies' interval; through the steeper readings of the indicator both steps are inside it. The same steps move the family away from the flies across odors: with the ms input that the model uses the ratio rises from {{E98/comparison_table_b_points.csv:point=real;comparison=V1, the panel ms;window=win:ratio_linear ~ .2f}} to {{E98/comparison_table_b_points.csv:point=E77_inhadd1000;comparison=V1, the panel ms;window=win:ratio_linear ~ .2f}} and {{E98/comparison_table_b_points.csv:point=E77_inhadd3141;comparison=V1, the panel ms;window=win:ratio_linear ~ .2f}}, against an interval that ends at {{E98/comparison_table_b_points.csv:point=real;comparison=V1, the panel ms;window=win:flies_hi90 ~ .2f}}, and with the control panel's it stays inside. Both steps are settings of the earlier screen of the input ([the input side of the error common to all wirings](#input-side)), where they raised the pattern part of the APL-effect loss.

A pulse twice as long ([the flies' pulse in the model and the remaining candidates for the common error](#remaining-candidates)), the fuller input ([the measured input for the glomeruli without ORN input](#missing-glomeruli)) and the refit near the connectome's bouton share ([APL's inhibition as a static threshold raise per KC](#static-threshold)) leave the family as flat along concentration as it was and where it was across odors.

The two earlier bases in which the KCs' spikes drive APL ([what drives APL](#apl-drive)) are as flat along concentration as the family, and with the ms input that the model uses they are steeper than the flies across odors, as the family is on this wiring. These recordings therefore do not tell a drive by the summed input to the claws from a drive by the KCs' spikes, and those bases have the same antennal lobe.

**Further recordings of the same series.** The verdict's recordings are one run of each calyx. {{E98/d2_replication.csv:set=all21;comparison=V2:n_recordings ~ .0f}} further recordings with rising concentrations, of the verdict's flies and one more, at other depths of the imaged plane and as repeated runs, were read by the same rules after the verdict had been written, and the experimenter who made them has not checked their quality. Over all of them the flies' APL falls to {{E98/d2_replication.csv:set=all21;comparison=V2:V2 ~ .2f}} of its response over the log unit of paa ({{E98/d2_replication.csv:set=all21;comparison=V2:flies_lo90 ~ .2f}} to {{E98/d2_replication.csv:set=all21;comparison=V2:flies_hi90 ~ .2f}}; {{E98/d2_replication.csv:set=all21;comparison=V2:n_flies_V2 ~ .0f}} flies), a smaller fall than in the verdict's recordings.

The family is flatter again in the recordings at 21 µm ({{E98/d2_replication.csv:set=21 um;comparison=V2:V2 ~ .2f}}, {{E98/d2_replication.csv:set=21 um;comparison=V2:flies_lo90 ~ .2f}} to {{E98/d2_replication.csv:set=21 um;comparison=V2:flies_hi90 ~ .2f}}; {{E98/d2_replication.csv:set=21 um;comparison=V2:n_flies_V2 ~ .0f}} flies) and in the one fly at 24 µm ({{E98/d2_replication.csv:set=24 um;comparison=V2:V2 ~ .2f}}). It is not in those at 15 µm ({{E98/d2_replication.csv:set=15 um;comparison=V2:V2 ~ .2f}}, {{E98/d2_replication.csv:set=15 um;comparison=V2:flies_lo90 ~ .2f}} to {{E98/d2_replication.csv:set=15 um;comparison=V2:flies_hi90 ~ .2f}}; {{E98/d2_replication.csv:set=15 um;comparison=V2:n_flies_V2 ~ .0f}} flies), nor in the repeated runs at 18 µm, the depth of the verdict's recordings ({{E98/d2_replication.csv:set=18 um;comparison=V2:V2 ~ .2f}}, {{E98/d2_replication.csv:set=18 um;comparison=V2:flies_lo90 ~ .2f}} to {{E98/d2_replication.csv:set=18 um;comparison=V2:flies_hi90 ~ .2f}}; {{E98/d2_replication.csv:set=18 um;comparison=V2:n_flies_V2 ~ .0f}} flies), nor over all of them: there the flies' interval reaches the family's steepest readings of the indicator, and the family counts as inside or the comparison is not decided.

Read in proportion the family lies above every one of these intervals except that of the repeated runs at 18 µm. Outside the verdict's recordings the class thus rests on how steep the indicator is taken to be, and what stands everywhere but in those few repeated runs is that the family is flatter when read in proportion.

Across odors the further recordings show a dependence on depth: paa at 10^-4 over ms is higher at 15 µm than at 18 µm in {{E98/d2_plane_pairs.csv:recording=(summary);plane_um=15;ratio_id=V1_paa-4:n_positive ~ .0f}} of the {{E98/d2_plane_pairs.csv:recording=(summary);plane_um=15;ratio_id=V1_paa-4:n_calyces ~ .0f}} calyces imaged at both. Each depth is another run of the day, so that this could have been the plane or the time. It was of the runs and not of the plane: in a held-out series in which every calyx was imaged at both depths, the ratio is higher at 15 µm in {{lit:3 # results/E103_apl_across_odors_heldout/e_summary.json: z, P1, n_higher_15}} of the {{lit:8 # results/E103_apl_across_odors_heldout/e_summary.json: z, P1, n_calyces}} calyces ([the flies' APL across odors in the held-out vial series](#apl-held-out)), so that the dependence does not return and says nothing against one APL variable for the whole calyx.

**Realism.** No model was changed or fitted. The fits of the eight wirings are read as saved, and all eight are inside the four realism bands. The settings read beside the verdict are saved points of their own subsections, inside the bands except the base with the KCs' spikes alone driving APL, which lies below the band on the response rate ρ with APL on. A blank evokes no response in the model's KCs, with APL on or with APL off, where {{lit:0.012 # results/E98_apl_response_strength/verdict.json: flies_solvent_rate, ctrl (0.01206), by the recordings' own response criterion}} of the control flies' KCs and {{lit:0.007 # results/E98_apl_response_strength/verdict.json: flies_solvent_rate, tnt (0.00696), by the recordings' own response criterion}} of the KCs with APL output blocked (TNT) respond to the solvent.

What the experiment adds is a description of the family beside the bands. Read in proportion, its APL falls by about a tenth over a step of concentration at which the flies' APL halves, while its own KCs lose more: with APL on, their response rate to paa at 10^-5 is {{E101/c4_apl_off.csv:wiring=M2;ratio_id=r3;estimate=paa [validation2/diag] @ -5;cond=on;quantity=KC response rate:linear ~ .2f}} to {{E101/c4_apl_off.csv:wiring=P3;ratio_id=r3;estimate=paa [validation2/diag] @ -5;cond=on;quantity=KC response rate:linear ~ .2f}} of that to paa at 10^-4 on the eight wirings. The family's APL is thus more even than the flies' APL and more even than the family's own KCs.

**Limits.**

- The verdict along concentration rests on one estimate of paa's ORN input at 10^-5, and the class across odors on which estimate of ms's input is taken.
- paa enters the model with ORN input recorded at 10^-4, one log unit below the concentration of the KC recordings, as everywhere ([ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations)), and the concentrations are nominal dilutions, in the imaged flies as in the ORN recordings.
- No map of pa lies within one log unit of the model's pa input, so that pa is compared only with Hallem's data here; the dual-colour recordings hold it ([above](#apl-vs-claws)).
- The quality of the recordings in shuffled order and of the further recordings with rising concentrations has not been checked by the experimenter who made them.
- What calcium in one plane of APL is of the model's single APL variable is not known; the dependence on depth, which had seemed one sign of that, does not return in the held-out series ([the flies' APL across odors in the held-out vial series](#apl-held-out)).
- The reading of the flies' side and the model's level without an odor were fixed after first tables had been read, and the protection is the rule that a class counts only if every reading gives it: along concentration every reading gives the same class, and across odors with the model's ms input they do not, which is why nothing is decided there.
- The model's level without an odor is taken from a blank because the simulation starts its KCs and its APL from zero half a second before the odor, so that a mean over that half second reads low; against that mean, {{lit:6 # results/E98_apl_response_strength/verdict.json: V1_lines, megamat/megamat (the panel), the model under the earlier pre-odor level, inside (6 of 8)}} of the eight wirings would have been inside across odors with the model's ms input, in place of {{E98/comparison_table.csv:numerator=paa;denominator=ms:n_inside ~ .0f}}, and the class along concentration is the same.

**What follows.** Nothing is gained or lost on the main target, and no base, bound or reference family is changed. Four things are carried from here.

- The first is an experiment that has since been run, the antennal lobe's normalization at the strength the flies' APL asks for ([below](#al-normalization)). It took the one change that moved the family's fall towards the flies' to the eight wirings and to a refit. At the mildest strength that brings the fall inside the flies' interval through the steeper readings of the indicator, the family fitted again pays a small price on the pattern part of the APL-effect loss; the comparison across odors moves the wrong way with the ms input that the model uses, and fewer KCs respond at low concentration.
  - The other places at which the scaling could be lost stay open: an input that scales more than the one session's estimate at the lower concentration, and a drive of APL by the KCs' spikes, which did not scale in the saved bases either and whose test in the flies waits on the leak between the two colours of the dual-colour recordings ([above](#apl-vs-claws)).
- The second is the flies' APL at the weak odors and at the panel's concentrations, a comparison in other recordings of APL that has since been run ([at the end of this section](#apl-weak-odors)). At six weak odors the family is inside the flies' interval by the rule fixed beforehand, through the steeper readings of the indicator and one session's estimate of the input, and flatter than the flies when read in proportion. Across odors at the panel's concentration too few flies hold the comparison for a verdict.
- The third is a table for the experimenter who imaged APL. The three odors imaged cannot tell a nearly even APL from one that follows the KCs' response, since the KC data's response rates to them lie close together. For every pair of the panel's odors the table gives the ratio of the family's APL, the ratio of an APL in proportion to the KCs' response rates with APL output blocked (TNT) and, from the spread between flies in the maps, the number of flies that would tell the two apart.
  - Among the pairs whose ORN input is at the concentration of the KC recordings, those that set eb, 1-6ol, 2h, ep or 2-but against 1-8ol separate the two most: the family's APL gives {{E98/a6_power_carrying.csv:numerator=2-but;denominator=1-8ol:family_min ~ .2f}} to {{E98/a6_power_carrying.csv:numerator=2h;denominator=1-8ol:family_max ~ .2f}} there and the proportional one {{E98/a6_power_carrying.csv:numerator=2-but;denominator=1-8ol:proportional_tnt ~ .2f}} to {{E98/a6_power_carrying.csv:numerator=1-6ol;denominator=1-8ol:proportional_tnt ~ .2f}}, which about {{E98/a6_power_carrying.csv:numerator=1-6ol;denominator=1-8ol:flies_needed_sd_median ~ .0f}} flies would tell apart for each pair. Against -aPine the two lie further apart ({{E98/a6_power_carrying.csv:numerator=2-but;denominator=-aPine:proportional_tnt ~ .2f}} to {{E98/a6_power_carrying.csv:numerator=1-6ol;denominator=-aPine:proportional_tnt ~ .2f}} for the proportional one), but -aPine's ORN input was recorded at another concentration than that of the KC recordings. {{lit:67 # results/E98_apl_response_strength/a6_power_carrying.csv: the pairs whose flies_needed_sd_median is 3 or less, counted from the table's 120 rows}} of the 120 pairs need three flies or fewer at the median spread between flies, and the request goes with the data asked for at the end of the page.
- The fourth are two leads.
  - KC recordings of a panel odor at a second concentration, paa at 10^-5 first, would say whether the flies' APL follows their KCs along concentration, as the response rates suggest that it may across odors. The KCs' signal in the calyx has since been read at both concentrations ([below](#kc-calyx-vs-apl)); recordings of the KCs' somata at the second concentration are still missing.
  - And the dependence of paa over ms on the depth of the plane seemed to belong with the question of a spatially local APL ([the APL calyx maps against the connectome](#apl-calyx-maps)). Both the comparison across odors and that dependence on depth have since been read again in a further series of the same experimenter's recordings, held out from every rule fixed here ([the flies' APL across odors in the held-out vial series](#apl-held-out), the next subsection). The dependence on depth does not return there, so that this lead is closed.
  - Across odors the held-out flies lie between these recordings and flies recorded in 2022 and hold the family inside their interval under every estimate of ms's input; and two vials of one odor differ there by enough that a ratio between two odors read from one pair of vials is known to no better than a factor of about one and a half, with which the comparison across odors made here and the numbers of flies in the table for the experimenter are to be read.

### The flies' APL across odors in the held-out vial series: which of two disagreeing readings of how strongly APL responds to ms a series held out from every rule sides with, where the best family stands against its flies, what two vials of one odor differ by in strength and in the map, and whether the dependence on the depth of the plane returns {#apl-held-out}

**The readings of the flies' APL disagreed about ms.** In the recordings of the strength comparison APL responds to ms about as strongly as to paa, and in flies recorded a year later paa evokes two to three times as much as ms. A further series by the same experimenter, with the genotype of the first and made as a control with three vials of one odor in every recording, was read by rules fixed before any of it was opened.

Its flies lie between the two. Their APL responds a third to three quarters more strongly to paa than to ms, more than in the first series by about what five flies against eight can just show, and on pa against ms and on ms's own fall with concentration they are as the first series, far from the flies of the later year. Which side they are on changes with the reading, so that by the rule nothing is decided and no interval is pooled over the two series.

The best family, whose ratio lies above that of the first series at the concentration of paa's input, is inside the held-out flies' interval under every estimate of ms's input. Two vials of one odor at one concentration differ persistently by more than had been expected, so that a ratio between two odors read from one pair of vials is known to no better than a factor of about one and a half; the difference between the two years is larger than that, and the difference between the two series of one year is not.

The part of APL's map that is a stimulus's own returns with another vial of the same odor and not with another odor, so that it is the odor's. The dependence of paa over ms on the depth of the plane does not return.

The experimenter who made the recordings has not checked their quality. No model is changed, and nothing is scored on the main target.

How strongly the flies' APL responds to one odor against another had been read in three sets of recordings, and they disagree about ms.

- In the {{E98/a3_ratios.csv:ratio_id=V2;reading=order_matched;subset=all:n_recordings ~ .0f}} recordings of [the strength of APL's response in the flies against the model's APL](#apl-strength), made from July to September 2021 in {{E98/a3_ratios.csv:ratio_id=V2;reading=order_matched;subset=all:n_flies ~ .0f}} flies and called the summer recordings here, paa at 10^-4, the concentration of its ORN input, evokes {{E103/a_ratios_12.csv:reading_12=carrying;ratio_id=P1:ratio ~ .2f}} of the response to ms at 10^-3 ({{E103/a_ratios_12.csv:reading_12=carrying;ratio_id=P1:lo90 ~ .2f}} to {{E103/a_ratios_12.csv:reading_12=carrying;ratio_id=P1:hi90 ~ .2f}}, the interval over resampled flies).
- In {{E100/b_ratios.csv:set=S;subset=all;calyx_response=yang_table;reading=order_matched;numerator=paa @ -3;denominator=pa @ -3:n_flies ~ .0f}} flies recorded in 2022 with whole log steps of concentration, {{E100/b_ratios.csv:set=S;subset=all;calyx_response=yang_table;reading=order_matched;numerator=ms @ -3;denominator=pa @ -3:n_flies ~ .0f}} of them with ms and called the flies of 2022 here, paa evokes about {{E103/a_ratios_12.csv:reading_12=carrying;ratio_id=P1:set_s_lo ~ .1f}} times as much as ms, and pa about {{E103/a_ratios_12.csv:reading_12=carrying;ratio_id=Q1:set_s_lo ~ .1f}} to {{E103/a_ratios_12.csv:reading_12=carrying;ratio_id=Q2:set_s_lo ~ .1f}} times as much, where the summer recordings give {{E103/a_ratios_12.csv:reading_12=carrying;ratio_id=Q1:ratio ~ .2f}} to {{E103/a_ratios_12.csv:reading_12=carrying;ratio_id=Q2:ratio ~ .2f}} for pa. Those values are first estimates from the experimenter's own table of calyx responses, fixed before the new series was opened; the flies themselves have since been read in [the flies' APL at the weak odors and at the panel's concentrations](#apl-weak-odors), where they are too few for the verdict that had been fixed for them.
- In the dual-colour recordings, also of 2022, APL responds several times as strongly to pa as to ms ([the flies' APL against their KC claws in the dual-colour recordings](#apl-vs-claws)).

The best family lies between. With the ms input that the model uses, its APL responds {{E98/comparison_table.csv:numerator=paa;denominator=ms:model_linear_min ~ .2f}} to {{E98/comparison_table.csv:numerator=paa;denominator=ms:model_linear_max ~ .2f}} times as strongly to paa as to ms on the eight wirings when read in proportion, and {{E98/comparison_table.csv:denominator=ms [kiwi-control/control] @ -3:model_linear_min ~ .2f}} to {{E98/comparison_table.csv:denominator=ms [kiwi-control/diag] @ -3:model_linear_max ~ .2f}} times over the five estimates of ms's input: above the summer recordings' ratio and below that of the flies of 2022. Whether the family's APL favours paa over ms too much or too little thus depended on which flies were read, and [the antennal lobe's normalization at the strength the flies' APL asks for](#al-normalization) (the next subsection) reads that ratio beside the main target.

One series of recordings of APL alone by the same experimenter had not been read for this work: {{lit:30 # results/E103_apl_across_odors_heldout/p0_identity.json: eligibility, n_series (the processed recordings of the series of October and November 2021)}} processed recordings from {{E103/d_m.csv:blur_px=5.0;variant=carrying:n_flies ~ .0f}} flies and {{E103/d_m.csv:blur_px=5.0;variant=carrying:n_calyces ~ .0f}} calyces, made in October and November 2021, with the genotype of the summer recordings, the pulse length of the model and, by the experimenter's notes, another olfactometer. It was made as a control. Every recording holds ms, paa and pa at three concentrations each and, at the same three concentrations, two further vials of pa or of paa, so that one odor is delivered from three vials within a recording.

No reading of the flies' APL had had a measure of what the same odor from another vial gives, in strength or in the map, and every calyx was imaged at 15 µm and at 18 µm. The experiment changes no model and scores nothing on the main target, so that [the APL-effect loss](#apl-effect), its mean part and its pattern part stay where they are.

**What was read, and by which rules.** The series was held out. Every rule was written from its stimulus files and the experimenter's notes, the values of the summer recordings at the series' own stimuli were tabulated and fixed, and only then was any of its maps opened.

Responses, ratios and intervals are read as in the strength comparison and at its depth, 18 µm, where {{E103/b_x1.csv:series_reading=carrying;ratio_id=P1:n_recordings ~ .0f}} recordings of the {{E103/b_x1.csv:series_reading=carrying;ratio_id=P1:n_flies ~ .0f}} flies carry the reading: a response is the change in fluorescence over its baseline around its peak, averaged inside the outline of the calyx, each presentation taken against the presentation of the solvent at the same place in its block, as the mean of a stimulus's first two presentations, the main reading in what follows; a ratio is the geometric mean over the flies; and its interval is the one in which nine in ten resamplings of the flies fall.

Eight ratios were fixed: six with ms (paa over ms and pa over ms at several concentrations, and ms's own fall over two log units) and two without it (the fall of paa and of pa with concentration), the check that the two sets of flies can be compared at all. Two sets of flies differ on a ratio if fewer than one in ten of the ways of dividing all their flies into sets of the same sizes give a difference as large.

The held-out flies are on the side of the summer recordings if at most one of the six ratios with ms differs from them; on the side of the flies of 2022 if at least four differ, each in the direction of those flies and each nearer on the logarithmic scale to their value than to that of the summer recordings; and between the two otherwise.

The best family is read from the saved fits of the eight wirings ([the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population)), with no simulation and by the rule of the strength comparison: a wiring is inside if any of its readings through the family of indicator nonlinearities lies in the flies' interval and above if all of them lie above it, and a comparison takes a class when at least six of the eight wirings agree.

A class counts only if every reading that the measurement leaves open gives it, among them another way of taking the baseline from the solvent presentations, every presentation in place of the first two, the recordings without the five that the experimenter's notes mark, each fly left out in turn and, for the family, an interval from Student's t in place of the resampled one, which five flies make too narrow.

Before the series was opened, the least difference that five flies against eight can show by the rule on the splits was worked out from the spread between the summer flies: a factor of {{E103/a_least_detectable.csv:ratio_id=Q1:factor_up ~ .2f}} to {{E103/a_least_detectable.csv:ratio_id=P2:factor_up ~ .2f}} on the six ratios with ms, where the summer recordings and the flies of 2022 differ by a factor of two or more. The checks fixed for the start all passed: the reader, extended to this series' blocks of presentations, gives the responses of the summer recordings again to the last digit, and the list of recordings rebuilt from the stimulus files equals the list fixed beforehand.

Ratios of APL's response to two stimuli in the three sets of flies. Summer recordings and held-out flies: the geometric mean over the flies with the interval over resampled flies in parentheses, at 18 µm and under the main reading; a concentration that was not imaged is read between its imaged neighbours. Flies of 2022: the first estimates, as a range where the concentration of paa lies between two of theirs. Last column: the share of the ways of dividing the thirteen flies of 2021 into sets of five and eight that give a difference between the sets as large as the one found, the two sets differing on a ratio where it is below one in ten. The first six rows are the ratios with ms, which decide the side; the last two are the check without ms

| statistic | the summer recordings | the held-out flies | the flies of 2022 | share of the splits<br>with a difference as large |

**The held-out flies lie between the two earlier sets, and the side changes with the reading.** On the three ratios of paa over ms the held-out flies are higher than the summer recordings (first three rows), each in the direction of the flies of 2022, by a factor of {{lit:1.6062 # results/E103_apl_across_odors_heldout/b_x1.csv: row series_reading=carrying, ratio_id=P1, ratio over ratio_ref, 1.30672 / 0.81353 = 1.6062 (the smallest of P1, P2 and P3) ~ .1f}} to {{lit:1.6618 # results/E103_apl_across_odors_heldout/b_x1.csv: row series_reading=carrying, ratio_id=P2, ratio over ratio_ref, 1.48469 / 0.89341 = 1.6618 (the largest of P1, P2 and P3) ~ .1f}}. That is about what five flies against eight can just show: {{E103/b_x1.csv:series_reading=carrying;ratio_id=P3:split_share ~ .3f}} to {{E103/b_x1.csv:series_reading=carrying;ratio_id=P2:split_share ~ .3f}} of the splits give as much. On pa over ms and on ms's fall with concentration the held-out flies are as the summer recordings (fourth to sixth rows), far from the flies of 2022.

Of the six ratios with ms, {{lit:3 # results/E103_apl_across_odors_heldout/b_x1.csv: rows series_reading=carrying, of the six ratios with ms (in_x1 True) those with differ True, counted (P1, P2 and P3)}} differ, where the side of the summer recordings allows one and the side of the flies of 2022 asks for four, and {{lit:2 # results/E103_apl_across_odors_heldout/b_x1.csv: rows series_reading=carrying with differ True (P1, P2 and P3), those with nearer_s False, counted (P1 and P3)}} of the three that differ lie nearer to the summer recordings than to the flies of 2022. Under the main reading the held-out flies are therefore between the two. That class is not held. In {{lit:4 # results/E103_apl_across_odors_heldout/b_summary.json: sides_per_reading, the readings on the side of the summer recordings, counted (without_marked, without 2021-10-22_fly1, without 2021-10-29_fly3, without 2021-11-09_fly5)}} of the {{lit:9 # results/E103_apl_across_odors_heldout/b_summary.json: sides_per_reading, the readings, counted}} readings, without the recordings that the notes mark and with each of three of the flies left out, one ratio or none differs, which is the side of the summer recordings.

By the rule nothing is decided: the ratios stand one by one, and no interval pooled over the two series is formed. The two ratios without ms do not differ (last two rows), so that the two sets of flies can be compared. What moved between the two series of 2021 is paa against ms and not pa against ms: the other olfactometer did not by itself make ms weak, since with it flies of the summer recordings' genotype respond to pa against ms as the summer flies do.

Beside, and deciding nothing: against the {{E103/b_beside.csv:set=18 um against the 12's 0.5 s flies;ratio_id=P1:n_flies_ref ~ .0f}} summer flies that were recorded at the model's pulse length, in which paa at 10^-4 over ms at 10^-3 is {{E103/b_beside.csv:set=18 um against the 12's 0.5 s flies;ratio_id=P1:ratio_ref ~ .2f}}, the held-out flies differ on no ratio ({{E103/b_beside.csv:set=18 um against the 12's 0.5 s flies;ratio_id=P1:split_share ~ .2f}} of the splits for that ratio), and neither do their recordings at 15 µm against the further recordings of the strength comparison at that depth.

**The best family is inside the held-out flies' interval.** Against the summer recordings, read at the series' own stimuli, the family lies above. For paa at 10^-4 it is above on all eight wirings under every estimate, and every reading gives that. Against the span over both concentrations of paa it is above under four of the five estimates, and with the largest estimate of ms's input, the control panel's, the readings do not agree. Neither was the rule of the strength comparison, whose interval spanned paa at 10^-4 and the maps' concentration nearest 10^-3 ({{E98/comparison_table.csv:numerator=paa;denominator=ms:flies_lo90 ~ .2f}} to {{E98/comparison_table.csv:numerator=paa;denominator=ms:flies_hi90 ~ .2f}}) and under which one estimate sufficed, and its verdict stands as written.

Against the held-out flies the family is inside on all eight wirings under every estimate, in both comparisons, and over the estimates both classes are held. One class under a single estimate is not: with ms's input from the diagnostic odors of the mixture session, under which the family's ratio is largest, the family is above the interval for paa at 10^-4 on all eight wirings once one of the flies is left out (the interval then ends at {{E103/c_classes.csv:x=X3;estimate=kiwi-control/diag;reading=without 2021-10-29_fly3:flies_hi90 ~ .2f}}).

The held-out flies' intervals are wide, and their width is what holds the family: with five flies paa at 10^-4 over ms at 10^-3 lies anywhere from {{E103/c_classes.csv:x=X3;estimate=megamat/megamat (the panel);reading=carrying:flies_lo90 ~ .2f}} to {{E103/c_classes.csv:x=X3;estimate=megamat/megamat (the panel);reading=carrying:flies_hi90 ~ .2f}}. The weaker normalization of the antennal-lobe experiment raises the family's ratio on the real wiring from {{E98/comparison_table_b_points.csv:point=real;comparison=V1, the panel ms;window=win:ratio_linear ~ .2f}} to {{E98/comparison_table_b_points.csv:point=E77_inhadd1000;comparison=V1, the panel ms;window=win:ratio_linear ~ .2f}} and {{E98/comparison_table_b_points.csv:point=E77_inhadd3141;comparison=V1, the panel ms;window=win:ratio_linear ~ .2f}} at the last two steps of the earlier screen, further above the summer recordings and still inside the held-out flies' intervals. Whether the family's APL favours paa over ms too much thus depends on which series of 2021 is read.

With Hallem's receptor data as the input, beside and deciding nothing, the family's pa over ms at 10^-4 is {{E103/e_hallem.csv:set=held-out flies (18 um, carrying);ratio_id=Q2:model_linear_min ~ .2f}} to {{E103/e_hallem.csv:set=held-out flies (18 um, carrying);ratio_id=Q2:model_linear_max ~ .2f}}, above both sets of flies of 2021 on all eight wirings and below the flies of 2022, and its fall of ms from 10^-2 to 10^-4, to {{E103/e_hallem.csv:set=held-out flies (18 um, carrying);ratio_id=F1:model_linear_min ~ .2f}} to {{E103/e_hallem.csv:set=held-out flies (18 um, carrying);ratio_id=F1:model_linear_max ~ .2f}} of the response, is inside both sets' intervals through the family of indicator nonlinearities.

**Two vials of one odor differ by more than had been expected.** Within a recording, the ratio of the responses to two vials of one odor at one concentration has a standard deviation of {{lit:0.5049972172330608 # results/E103_apl_across_odors_heldout/d_summary.json: y1, carrying, all, sd_single ~ .2f}} in its base-two logarithm over single recordings ({{lit:196 # results/E103_apl_across_odors_heldout/d_summary.json: y1, carrying, all, n_values}} ratios), where {{lit:0.15 # experiment_priorities.md in the shared directory, the entry of this experiment, Expected (Y1): the lower end of the expected SD of the log2 ratio of two vials within a recording, written before any response of the series was read}} to {{lit:0.35 # experiment_priorities.md in the shared directory, the entry of this experiment, Expected (Y1): the upper end of the expected SD of the log2 ratio of two vials within a recording, written before any response of the series was read}} had been expected.

The part of that spread that persists over a day's recordings, the spread of the day's means for one odor, concentration and pair of vials with the scatter of single recordings about them removed, is {{E103/c_widened_classes.csv:x=X2;estimate=megamat/megamat (the panel);reading=carrying:widened_by_log2 ~ .2f}}, a factor of {{lit:1.3764 # two to the power of the persistent spread, results/E103_apl_across_odors_heldout/d_summary.json: y1, carrying, all, persistent_sd (0.46092), 2^0.46092 = 1.3764 ~ .2f}} per standard deviation, where less than {{lit:0.2 # experiment_priorities.md in the shared directory, the entry of this experiment, Expected (Y1): the bound below which the persistent part was expected at about two in three, written before any response of the series was read}} had been expected and {{lit:0.3 # experiment_priorities.md in the shared directory, the entry of this experiment, outcome (e): the bound on the persistent SD of the log2 ratio of two vials above which no ratio between two odors from one pair of vials counts as known to better than a factor of about one and a half, fixed before any response of the series was read}} was the bound fixed for what follows. It is not a drift through the recording, since the spread does not grow steadily with the number of blocks between the two vials.

A ratio between two odors reads one vial of each. A ratio read from one pair of vials is therefore known to no better than a factor of about one and a half, however many flies it has, unless the vials are made anew from day to day and the days are averaged. That holds for the readings across odors of the strength comparison ([above](#apl-strength)), of the dual-colour recordings ([above](#apl-vs-claws)) and of the flies of 2022, each of which had one pair of vials a day.

By the yardstick fixed beforehand, a difference between two series in a ratio between two odors is beyond the vials if its base-two logarithm exceeds {{lit:2.8 # results/E103_apl_across_odors_heldout/d_summary.json: rules, y1_yardstick; fixed in the entry of this experiment before any response of the series was read}} times the persistent spread, here a factor of {{lit:2.446276457587244 # results/E103_apl_across_odors_heldout/d_summary.json: y1, carrying, all, yardstick_factor ~ .2f}}. The summer recordings and the flies of 2022 differ by more than that on {{lit:4 # E103_apl_across_odors_heldout.md in the shared directory, part D, the differences between the series against the yardstick of 1.29 in log2: of the five ratios between odors (P1, P2, P3, Q1, Q2) those whose log2 of set S over the summer recordings exceeds it, counted (P1 1.44, P2 1.30 to 1.84, P3 1.61, Q2 2.03; not Q1 1.22); from set_s_lo, set_s_hi and ratio in results/E103_apl_across_odors_heldout/a_ratios_12.csv, rows reading_12=carrying}} of the {{lit:5 # results/E103_apl_across_odors_heldout/a_ratios_12.csv: rows reading_12=carrying, the ratios between two odors, counted (P1, P2, P3, Q1, Q2)}} ratios between odors, on one of them only just, and the held-out flies differ from the summer recordings by less on every one.

The difference between the two years is thus more than the vials of one series make. It is one between the recordings of 2021 and of 2022, in the odor stocks, the delivery of ms, the longer pulse and whole log steps of the later series or an indicator near saturation, and it goes to the experimenter as a question. The difference between the two series of 2021 is within what the vials make.

**The part of APL's map that is a stimulus's own is the odor's.** In the earlier maps most of a recording was one pattern common to all of its stimuli, and what was left of a stimulus's map, the remainder, repeated between its presentations ([the APL calyx maps against the connectome](#apl-calyx-maps)). Those presentations lay in one block, so that the remainder could have belonged to the block, to a drift of the plane or to the state of the fly, as well as to the odor. Three vials of one odor in separate blocks tell these apart.

The pattern common to a recording is taken from the nine stimuli of ms and of the first vials of paa and pa and removed from every map, and the remainders, smoothed over 5 pixels, are correlated over the pixels inside the outline, in the recordings of every depth. Between the two halves of a stimulus's presentations in its block the Pearson r is {{E103/d_m_calyces.csv:calyx=2021-10-29_fly3_L;blur_px=5.0;variant=carrying:r_rep ~ .2f}} to {{E103/d_m_calyces.csv:calyx=2021-11-09_fly5_R;blur_px=5.0;variant=carrying:r_rep ~ .2f}} over the {{E103/d_m.csv:blur_px=5.0;variant=carrying:n_calyces ~ .0f}} calyces; between the second and the third vial of one odor at one concentration, which lie in different blocks, it is {{E103/d_m_calyces.csv:calyx=2021-11-07_fly1_L;blur_px=5.0;variant=carrying:r_vial ~ .2f}} to {{E103/d_m_calyces.csv:calyx=2021-11-07_fly1_R;blur_px=5.0;variant=carrying:r_vial ~ .2f}}; and between such a vial and another odor at the same rank of concentration it is {{E103/d_m_calyces.csv:calyx=2021-10-22_fly1_L;blur_px=5.0;variant=carrying:r_odor ~ .2f}} to {{E103/d_m_calyces.csv:calyx=2021-10-29_fly3_L;blur_px=5.0;variant=carrying:r_odor ~ .2f}}.

As a share of what repeats within a block, from none of it to all of it, what returns with another vial of the same odor is {{E103/d_m.csv:blur_px=5.0;variant=carrying:share ~ .2f}} ({{E103/d_m.csv:blur_px=5.0;variant=carrying:lo90 ~ .2f}} to {{E103/d_m.csv:blur_px=5.0;variant=carrying:hi90 ~ .2f}}, the interval over resampled flies), and the same odor agrees better than another odor in {{E103/d_m.csv:blur_px=5.0;variant=carrying:n_vial_over_odor ~ .0f}} of the {{E103/d_m.csv:blur_px=5.0;variant=carrying:n_calyces ~ .0f}} calyces, where the rule asked for an interval above one half and for seven calyces. At the three other smoothings the share is {{E103/d_m.csv:blur_px=20.0;variant=carrying:share ~ .2f}} to {{E103/d_m.csv:blur_px=2.0;variant=carrying:share ~ .2f}}, and the class is the same before the common pattern is removed.

The share exceeds one because the agreement within a block is between halves of a block's presentations, which noise lowers more than it lowers the agreement between whole blocks; the class does not rest on that. The correlation with another odor is mostly below zero because removing one common pattern from the maps of three odors leaves their remainders opposed. An odor-specific map of the flies' APL thus exists against the control that it had lacked, and with a size.

**The dependence on the depth of the plane does not return.** In the further recordings of the strength comparison paa at 10^-4 over ms had been higher at 15 µm than at 18 µm in {{E98/d2_plane_pairs.csv:recording=(summary);plane_um=15;ratio_id=V1_paa-4:n_positive ~ .0f}} of the {{E98/d2_plane_pairs.csv:recording=(summary);plane_um=15;ratio_id=V1_paa-4:n_calyces ~ .0f}} calyces imaged at both, each depth being another run of the day. In the held-out series it is higher at 15 µm in {{lit:3 # results/E103_apl_across_odors_heldout/e_summary.json: z, P1, n_higher_15}} of the {{lit:8 # results/E103_apl_across_odors_heldout/e_summary.json: z, P1, n_calyces}} calyces, and the mean factor over the flies is {{lit:0.8293160983223142 # results/E103_apl_across_odors_heldout/e_summary.json: z, P1, factor ~ .2f}} ({{lit:0.6925660604590419 # results/E103_apl_across_odors_heldout/e_summary.json: z, P1, lo90 ~ .2f}} to {{lit:0.9736328375577523 # results/E103_apl_across_odors_heldout/e_summary.json: z, P1, hi90 ~ .2f}}), the other way if anything; the rule asked for seven of the eight and an interval that excludes one for a replication, and for four or fewer for none. In the four calyces whose planes alternate from run to run, the ratio is lower at 15 µm whichever of two neighbouring runs came first. The earlier dependence was thus of the runs and not of the plane.

**Limits.**

- Further recordings of the series that exist only as movies, {{lit:13 # results/E103_apl_across_odors_heldout/p0_identity.json: eligibility, n_raw_only_listed}} of them, were not read.
- Five flies are few, and it is the width of their intervals that holds the family.
- The values for the flies of 2022 are first estimates, from another table, a pulse twice as long and few flies, so that the comparisons with them and with the yardstick are approximate.
- paa at 10^-4 and ms at 10^-3 lie between imaged concentrations in every recording of the series and are read between their neighbours on the logarithm of the concentration.
- paa was not imaged at 10^-5, so that the fall along concentration that carries the verdict of the strength comparison cannot be read here, and the highest concentration of pa is more than one log unit below the model's pa input, so that pa is set against the family only with [Hallem's receptor data](#hallem-input).
- paa enters the model with ORN input recorded at 10^-4, one log unit below the concentration of the KC recordings, so that the comparison at the series' concentration nearest the panel's rests on [ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations) and the comparison at 10^-4 does not; euc and -aPine are not involved.
- Within a block the response to paa grows from the first presentation to the second by a factor of {{lit:1.1418117122038776 # results/E103_apl_across_odors_heldout/e_summary.json: y3, factor (paa's second presentation over its first, relative to the same for ms; mean over the 5 flies) ~ .2f}} more than the response to ms does, of which the mean of the first two presentations carries about half into paa over ms.
- Whether the vials were made anew on each of the series' five days is not known, and one class under a single estimate rests on it: with every interval widened at each end by the persistent spread between two vials, as if one pair of vials had served all five days, the family is inside under every estimate and every reading.
- The concentrations are nominal dilutions, on another olfactometer than that of the ORN recordings, and what calcium in one plane of APL is of the model's single APL variable is not known.

**Realism.** No model was changed or fitted. The fits of the eight wirings are read as saved, and all eight are inside the four realism bands.

What the experiment adds is how far the flies' APL can at present judge the family's across odors. The family's paa over ms lies above one series of 2021, inside another of the same genotype made a month later, and below the flies of 2022, and the vials of one series alone move a ratio between two odors by a factor of {{lit:1.3764 # two to the power of the persistent spread, results/E103_apl_across_odors_heldout/d_summary.json: y1, carrying, all, persistent_sd (0.46092), 2^0.46092 = 1.3764 ~ .2f}} per standard deviation.

From these recordings the family's APL can be called neither too even across odors nor too uneven. Along concentration the verdict of the strength comparison, that the family's APL is flatter than the flies', is a fall within one odor and is not touched; there the two series of 2021 do not differ in the falls of paa, of pa or of ms (last three rows of the first table).

The family's own KCs are less even over the three odors than the flies' KCs. With APL on, {{E101/a3_family.csv:wiring=real;cond=on;stimulus=pa:kc_rate ~ .3f}} to {{E101/a3_family.csv:wiring=P1;cond=on;stimulus=pa:kc_rate ~ .3f}} of them respond to pa, {{E101/a3_family.csv:wiring=P2;cond=on;stimulus=ms:kc_rate ~ .3f}} to {{E101/a3_family.csv:wiring=P4;cond=on;stimulus=ms:kc_rate ~ .3f}} to ms and {{E101/a3_family.csv:wiring=M3;cond=on;stimulus=paa:kc_rate ~ .3f}} to {{E101/a3_family.csv:wiring=P4;cond=on;stimulus=paa:kc_rate ~ .3f}} to paa on the eight wirings, where {{data:noise_ctrl_frac_pa ~ .3f}}, {{data:noise_ctrl_frac_ms ~ .3f}} and {{data:noise_ctrl_frac_paa ~ .3f}} of the control flies' KCs do: ms is the odor whose KC response the family undershoots.

**What follows.** Nothing is gained or lost on the main target, and no base, bound or reference family is changed. Five things are carried from here.

The first is how the family's APL is read across odors. Near the panel's concentration the flies' APL does not at present constrain it: every reading of paa over ms or of pa over ms against the family is given with the series that it comes from, and the family is called neither too even nor too uneven across odors while the series disagree. The verdict of the strength comparison stands as written ([above](#apl-strength)), and its class across odors, inside, is found again in flies on which no rule had been fixed, at the series' own concentrations and under every estimate of ms's input.

The second is for [the antennal lobe's normalization at the strength the flies' APL asks for](#al-normalization) (the next subsection), which has since been run. No interval pooled over the two series of 2021 went to it, the interval fixed for its ratio between odors stood, and the held-out flies' intervals are a record beside that interval, inside which the family's ratio stays once the family is fitted again with the weaker normalization.

The third is the vials. A ratio between two odors that has to be known to better than a factor of about one and a half needs vials made anew on several days, with the days averaged; that bears on the table of pairs left for the experimenter, whose numbers of flies take the spread between flies as the only uncertainty ([above](#apl-strength)), and on the comparison of ms with pa at the panel's concentrations in the flies of 2022, which has since been read and is described only, the flies being too few ([the flies' APL at the weak odors and at the panel's concentrations](#apl-weak-odors)).

The fourth is a set of questions to the experimenter, which hold nothing meanwhile: whether the vials of the held-out series were made anew each day and diluted separately; whether ms's stock, its vials or its delivery differed between 2021 and 2022, which decides which flies' ms to trust and so whether the family's paa over ms is judged against the flies of 2021 or against those of 2022; and whether a note against one block in two of the recordings excludes the block or the recording. Until the second is answered, a change of ms's input as a handle on the main target is not proposed.

The fifth concerns a spatially local APL. Its premise from the maps now has a measured object, the part of APL's map that is the odor's, with a size and with its control.

The readings against maps predicted from the derived connectome tables stay withheld ([footnote](#fn-derived-tables)), the same test made again on three calyces of the hemibrain and the male CNS reads on no pair of odors ([the flies' APL at the weak odors and at the panel's concentrations](#apl-weak-odors)), and the test place by place against the claws stays undecided ([the flies' APL against their KC claws in the dual-colour recordings](#apl-vs-claws)), so that no local APL is fitted; and the dependence on depth that had pointed the same way is closed, so that verdicts on responses averaged over the calyx need no restriction to one depth.

One lead is left for the planning of further readings: recordings of the KCs' claws alone in the calyx, in other flies, would give the claws' side of the same ratios across odors without the leak between the two colours.

**That lead has since been taken.** In flies of 2022 in which the KCs alone carry an indicator ([the flies' KCs beside their APL along concentration](#kc-calyx-vs-apl)), the KCs' calyx signal is {{E104/a5_beside.csv:part=across odors, K6F;fall=pa_over_ms:apl ~ .2f}} times as large for pa as for ms at 10^-3 and {{E104/a5_beside.csv:part=across odors, K6F;fall=paa_over_ms:apl ~ .2f}} times for paa. The APL flies of that year give {{E104/a5_beside.csv:part=across odors, S;fall=pa_over_ms:apl ~ .2f}} to {{E104/a5_beside.csv:part=across odors, L;fall=pa_over_ms:apl ~ .2f}} and {{E104/a5_beside.csv:part=across odors, S;fall=paa_over_ms:apl ~ .2f}} to {{E104/a5_beside.csv:part=across odors, L;fall=paa_over_ms:apl ~ .2f}}. Each of these is a ratio between two odors, and so known to no better than a factor of about one and a half.

### The antennal lobe's normalization at the strength the flies' APL asks for: what an antennal lobe under which the best family's APL falls with concentration as the flies' APL does costs on the pattern part, at fixed scales and after a refit, and what it does to the KCs at low concentration {#al-normalization}

%%% hover
picked step: Of the six steps by which the normalization in the model's antennal lobe is weakened, the mildest at which the best family's APL falls over the log unit of paa as the flies' APL does. The fall has to be inside the flies' interval on at least six of the eight wirings by the rule of the strength comparison, under every reading that the measurement leaves open. It is the third step, and it was named by the flies' APL, not by the main target. Defined in the subsection on the antennal lobe's normalization at the strength the flies' APL asks for.
%%%

**The goal was to measure what the best family pays on the main target for an antennal lobe under which its APL falls with concentration as the flies' does.** Over a log unit of paa the flies' APL loses about half of its response and the family's about a tenth ([the strength of APL's response in the flies against the model's APL](#apl-strength)). That flatness is made before APL, by an antennal lobe that returns the odors' totals nearly equal ([the model's stages against the flies' stages](#model-stages)). Unlike those comparisons, this experiment changes the model and is scored on [the APL-effect loss](#apl-effect).

**The family pays a small price.** Fitted again at the mildest normalization that brings its APL's fall inside the flies' interval, it reads slightly worse on the pattern part than the unchanged fits. As fitted the difference is smaller than had been expected, and by the rule fixed beforehand it is a price and not an equal. With the fits' response rates matched it is a range that reaches the lower end of what had been expected. The change brings the mean APL effect on raw counts close to the flies' and costs KCs at low concentration, where the family already recruits too few. Read like for like since, that cost at low concentration holds against some of the flies' sets of recordings and reverses against others ([the KCs' response rates at the weak odors read like for like](#weak-odor-rates)).

**What was changed.** In the model's antennal lobe a PN's gain is divided by a term that grows with the ORNs' mean activity and stands for lateral inhibition. A constant was added to that divisor in six steps, with the gain at a typical odor kept: the larger the constant, the less the gain depends on how much of the antennal lobe is active. The last step fixes the gain. Every step was run on the eight wirings, each at its own fit ([the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population)), with the lab's input and with both response rates set again.

**How the strength was chosen.** The strength was named by the flies' APL through rules fixed beforehand, not by the main target and not by a correlation. The picked step is the mildest at which the family's fall over the log unit of paa is inside the flies' interval on at least six of the eight wirings, by the rule of the strength comparison. At that step the family was fitted again under the APL-effect loss on the four wirings of the earlier searches. The four held-out wirings were to be fitted only if that refit came out an equal or better.

The best family as fitted, at the picked step at fixed scales and fitted again there, beside the flies. Model columns: the mean over the four wirings of the earlier searches against the main target as measured, all recordings, through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout) unless raw counts are named; a range is over those four wirings, and a median is theirs. The flies' column holds the KC data and, in the rows on APL and on the PNs, the flies' APL and their PN dendrites

**At fixed scales the pattern part rises at every step.** On the four wirings of the earlier searches it goes from {{E102/b_steps.csv:step=identity:pattern_S ~ .4f}} as fitted to {{E102/b_steps.csv:step=inhadd100:pattern_S ~ .4f}} at the first step, the only step inside the margin of an equal, and to {{E102/b_steps.csv:step=gain_fixed:pattern_S ~ .4f}} at the last (worse; the floor is {{data:apl_effect_pattern_floor ~ .4f}}). At the picked step every single wiring is worse, and the mean over all eight reads {{E102/b_readings.csv:change=inhadd1000;unit=all8;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} for {{E102/b_readings.csv:change=identity;unit=all8;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}. Nearly all of the rise is in the shape part ([how the pattern part is split](#fn-pattern-split)). The amplitude part falls at first, as the spread of the model's per-pair effect comes nearer to the flies'.

**On raw counts the same change helps.** The mean APL effect on raw counts rises towards the flies', and the loss on raw counts falls with it (the table). Through the readout the mean effect is the flies' already, so that the loss there follows the pattern part. The pattern part through the readout is what decides, and the gain on raw counts is a description beside it.

**The flies' APL picks the third step.** From the third step on, the family's fall over the log unit of paa is inside the flies' interval on all {{E102/b_e98.csv:comparison=V2, paa at 10^-5 from validation2/diag;reading_set=carrying;step=inhadd1000:n_inside ~ .0f}} wirings, through the steeper readings of the indicator. It is the mildest step that does so, and the one at which the family was fitted again.

**No step short of a fixed gain reaches the flies' fall read in proportion.** Read in proportion the family stays flatter than the flies at every step but the last, a fixed gain. That step is no candidate: on one wiring no KC responds to B-myr with APL on there, and a rule added after the scores had been seen excludes a step at which an odor is silent.

**The antennal lobe makes most of the flattening, and not all of it.** Over the log unit of paa the lab's ORN input falls to {{E102/a1_ratios.csv:setting=C2;ratio_id=V2:input_total_ratio ~ .2f}} of its total. The flies' APL falls about in proportion to it, a power-law exponent of {{E102/a1_ratios.csv:setting=C2;ratio_id=V2:exponent_flies ~ .2f}}, where the family's APL on the real wiring follows the input with an exponent of {{E102/a1_ratios.csv:setting=C2;ratio_id=V2:exponent_model ~ .2f}}. Of that flattening the antennal lobe makes {{E102/a1_ratios.csv:setting=C2;ratio_id=V2:al_share ~ .0%}}, and the mushroom body the rest. At the picked step the exponent is {{E102/a1_ratios.csv:setting=inhadd1000;ratio_id=V2:exponent_model ~ .2f}} and the antennal lobe's share still {{E102/a1_ratios.csv:setting=inhadd1000;ratio_id=V2:al_share ~ .0%}}.

**Fitted again, the family takes back most of the cost.** The refit's pattern part lies between the unchanged fits' and that at fixed scales, nearer to the first (the table). Each of the four wirings is still worse than its unchanged fit, by {{diff:E102/d_compare_inhadd1000.csv:unit=real;row=refit at inhadd1000:cal_z8_pattern -- E102/d_compare_inhadd1000.csv:unit=real;row=unchanged fits:cal_z8_pattern ~ .3f}} to {{diff:E102/d_compare_inhadd1000.csv:unit=P1;row=refit at inhadd1000:cal_z8_pattern -- E102/d_compare_inhadd1000.csv:unit=P1;row=unchanged fits:cal_z8_pattern ~ .3f}}, and better than at fixed scales. The mean over the four moves less than any one of them, and less than the {{lit:0.003 # experiment_priorities.md in the shared directory, the entry of this experiment, Why, and how it moves the APL-effect loss: refitted at the strength the flies' APL asks for, the expected price is 0.003 to 0.012 on the pattern part of the four searched wirings' mean; written before any run (the lower end)}} to {{lit:0.012 # experiment_priorities.md in the shared directory, the entry of this experiment, Why, and how it moves the APL-effect loss: refitted at the strength the flies' APL asks for, the expected price is 0.003 to 0.012 on the pattern part of the four searched wirings' mean; written before any run (the upper end)}} that had been expected. The refits raise the somatic threshold on all four wirings, and no parameter is at a bound.

The class of the refit by the rule fixed beforehand: the family fitted again at the picked step minus the unchanged fits, for the mean over the four wirings of the earlier searches, and the change that an equal allows in either direction. A negative change of the pattern part or of the loss is an improvement

**A price, by one half of the recordings.** An equal had to stay within the margin against all recordings and against both halves of the first split of the flies, with its four fits inside the realism bands. Against all recordings the refit is inside the margin, and against one half it is lower than the unchanged fits; against the other half it is higher by more than the margin, which makes it a price. Better would have needed a pattern part lower by the margin against all recordings. The four held-out wirings were therefore not fitted.

**The rule's clause on raw counts.** The rule for an equal also limits how far the loss on raw counts may move, in either direction ([the PN boutons' share of APL's inhibition](#bouton-share)). An improvement beyond the limit thus fails an equal as a worsening would. Here the loss on raw counts improved by several times the limit, so that the refit fails that clause as well. The class does not rest on it, since one half of the recordings decides. The rule was applied as written, and whether an improvement is meant to fail an equal is still to be decided.

**What the price buys.** Fitted again, the family's fall over the log unit of paa stays inside the flies' interval on all four wirings through the steeper readings of the indicator, and flatter read in proportion. The mean APL effect on raw counts stays close to the flies', and the loss on raw counts is the lowest of the three columns. The PNs' totals become less even over the odors, and stay far more even than the flies' PN dendrites.

**At the weak odors the family's APL comes nearer to the flies' as well.** Six weak stimuli carry the verdict of another comparison, the flies' APL at the weak odors and at the panel's concentrations ([at the end of this section](#apl-weak-odors)). On the real wiring, {{E102/e_table_inhadd1000.csv:point=unchanged_none:W1 ratios inside under some estimate}} of their ratios are inside the flies' interval under some estimate of the input as fitted, and {{E102/e_table_inhadd1000.csv:point=refit_D:W1 ratios inside under some estimate}} after the refit. Read in proportion, the two that turn stay flatter than the flies.

**What it costs beside the pattern part.** To ma at 10^-7 fewer KCs respond, with APL on and with APL off, which is further from the flies in both conditions (the table). The refit recovers little of that. With both response rates held, a weaker normalization raises the somatic threshold, and a weak input gains least from the change. In this family the flies' steep APL and their KCs' responses at the weakest inputs thus pull the antennal lobe's normalization in opposite directions.

**Across odors nothing is decided.** With the ms input that the model uses, the family's paa over ms becomes steeper than the flies of the strength comparison on all four wirings (the table); with the largest estimate of ms's input it stays inside their interval. It also stays inside the held-out flies' intervals, which span {{E103/c_classes.csv:x=X2;estimate=megamat/megamat (the panel);reading=carrying:flies_lo90 ~ .2f}} to {{E103/c_classes.csv:x=X2;estimate=megamat/megamat (the panel);reading=carrying:flies_hi90 ~ .2f}} ([the flies' APL across odors in the held-out vial series](#apl-held-out)). The move is smaller than what two vials of one odor differ by in that series. These recordings therefore cannot show it as a cost.

From the third row on, both response rates are set again to the unchanged fit's, so that on the refit's side the second row is the reference and on the unchanged fit's side the first. **Read beside on the real wiring, only the bouton path near the connectome's share helps the refit.** Three settings of earlier subsections were put on both fits: the fuller input ([the measured input for the glomeruli without ORN input](#missing-glomeruli)), the bouton path near the connectome's share with the unweighted component in its place ([APL's inhibition as a static threshold raise per KC](#static-threshold)), and a pulse twice as long ([the flies' pulse in the model and the remaining candidates for the common error](#remaining-candidates)). On the unchanged fit all three cost. On the refit the fuller input and the longer pulse cost as well.

**What the bouton path does there.** Against its reference it lowers the refit's pattern part by {{diff:E102/e_table_inhadd1000.csv:point=refit_none:cal_z8_pattern -- E102/e_table_inhadd1000.csv:point=refit_b:cal_z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, in the shape part, and it does so against each half of two splits of the flies. It also brings the mean APL effect on raw counts closest to the flies' of the settings in the table. It stays above the refit as fitted and above the unchanged fit. The family fitted again near the connectome's bouton share does not carry over either: moved to the picked step, it reads {{E102/e_table_inhadd1000.csv:point=E95f1_level:cal_z8_pattern ~ .4f}} for its {{E102/e_table_inhadd1000.csv:point=E95_f1:cal_z8_pattern ~ .4f}} at the default normalization.

**None of the three undoes what the normalization did beside the main target.** APL's fall over the log unit of paa, read in proportion, stays where the normalization puts it under every setting, flatter than the flies on both fits. The response rates to ma at 10^-7 stay where the normalization puts them as well.

**On the real wiring the refit loses its recovery when its response rates are set again.** Setting the response rates again is itself a change for the refit, whose response rate with APL on is {{E102/e_table_inhadd1000.csv:point=refit_D:rate_on ~ .3f}} as fitted for the unchanged fit's {{E102/e_table_inhadd1000.csv:point=unchanged_none:rate_on ~ .3f}}, both inside the bands. Set to the unchanged fit's, the refit on the real wiring reads near the {{E102/d_compare_inhadd1000.csv:unit=real;row=fixed scales at inhadd1000 (part B):cal_z8_pattern ~ .4f}} of the fixed scales there, not near its own value as fitted (the table above). Either the recovery belongs to the refit's response rates, or a fit reads worse when it is held away from those at which it was fitted.

**The four refits were therefore read at matched response rates, in both directions.** Each refit was held to the response rates of its own wiring's unchanged fit, and each unchanged fit to those of its refit. Nothing was fitted: the somatic threshold and the APL scale were set again until the numbers of responses with APL off and with APL on were the other fit's. What each outcome would mean, and the form of the price under it, had been fixed before the runs.

The fits read at matched response rates, beside the fits as fitted. Under each spanning header the fits have the same response rates on every wiring, with APL on and with APL off.
